nodes.description: A group with no relations among generators; SO(3) contains a free subgroup on two generators.

nodes.name: free_product
nodes.description: The group G * H formed by alternating words from G and H with no additional relations.

nodes.name: amalgamated_free_product
nodes.description: The group G *_A H formed by identifying a common subgroup A in G and H.

nodes.name: hnn_extension
nodes.description: The group G*_A = <G, t.

nodes.name: quasi_isometry
nodes.function_signature: (Metric space X, Metric space Y) → (Quasi-isometry f: X→Y)
nodes.description: A map between metric spaces that distorts distances by at most multiplicative and additive constants; boundary maps from q.i.'s are key to Mostow's proof.

nodes.name: quasi_isometry_invariant
nodes.description: A property of groups preserved under quasi-isometry, hence independent of generating set.

nodes.name: dehn_function
nodes.description: The function delta(n) giving the maximum area needed to fill a loop of length n in the Cayley complex, measuring difficulty of the word problem.

nodes.name: hyperbolic_group
nodes.description: A finitely generated group whose Cayley graph is delta-hyperbolic (triangles are delta-thin) in the sense of Gromov.

nodes.name: boundary_at_infinity
nodes.description: The Gromov boundary of a hyperbolic group, consisting of equivalence classes of geodesic rays.

nodes.name: cat_0_space
nodes.description: A geodesic metric space where triangles are at least as thin as comparison triangles in Euclidean space.

nodes.name: cat_0_group
nodes.description: A group acting properly and cocompactly on a CAT(0) space by isometries.

nodes.name: amenable_group
nodes.description: A group admitting a finitely additive left-invariant probability measure on all subsets.

nodes.name: residually_finite_group
nodes.description: A group where for every nontrivial element g, there exists a finite quotient in which g maps nontrivially.

nodes.name: linear_group
nodes.description: A group admitting a faithful representation into GL_n(k) for some field k.

nodes.name: automatic_group
nodes.description: A group with a regular language of normal forms and synchronous fellow-traveling for multiplication by generators.

nodes.name: growth_rate
nodes.description: The exponential growth rate lim_{n->infty} gamma_G(n)^{1/n}, distinguishing polynomial, intermediate, and exponential growth.

nodes.name: ends_of_group
nodes.description: The number of ends of the Cayley graph, a quasi-isometry invariant taking values 0, 1, 2, or infinity.

nodes.name: dehn_presentation
nodes.description: A presentation where the Dehn algorithm (greedy relator replacement) solves the word problem in linear time.

nodes.name: rips_complex
nodes.description: The simplicial complex R_d(G,S) with a simplex for each subset of diameter at most d in the Cayley graph.

nodes.name: hyperbolic_dehn_function_is_linear
nodes.description: Hyperbolic groups have linear Dehn function: delta(n) is O(n), and conversely (Gromov)

nodes.name: milnor_svarc_lemma
nodes.description: If G acts properly and cocompactly by isometries on a geodesic metric space X, then G is quasi-isometric to X (Milnor, Svarc)

nodes.name: flat_torus_theorem
nodes.description: A CAT(0) group containing Z^n contains a flat: an isometrically embedded copy of R^n (Bridson-Haefliger)

nodes.name: quasi_isometric_classification
nodes.function_signature: (Finitely generated group G) → (QI-invariants: growth, ends, hyperbolicity)
nodes.description: Classifying groups up to quasi-isometry using invariants like growth, ends, hyperbolicity, and asymptotic dimension.

nodes.name: van_kampen_diagram
nodes.function_signature: (Word w in generators of G) → (Planar diagram proving w=1 in G)
nodes.description: A planar diagram whose boundary represents a word equal to 1, with 2-cells labeled by relators, used to bound Dehn functions.

nodes.name: small_cancellation_theory
nodes.function_signature: (Group presentation with small overlap) → (Structural properties of G)
nodes.description: Studying groups given by presentations where relators have small overlap, yielding hyperbolic groups and solvable word problems.

nodes.name: geometric_group_actions
nodes.function_signature: (Group G, Metric space X) → (Algebraic properties of G from action)
nodes.description: Studying algebraic properties of groups via their isometric actions on metric spaces, trees, buildings, and CAT(0) complexes.

nodes.name: christoffel_symbols
nodes.description: The coefficients Gamma^k_{ij} expressing the Levi-Civita connection in local coordinates.

nodes.name: exponential_map_diff_geom
nodes.description: The map exp_p: T_pM -> M sending v to gamma_v(1) where gamma_v is the geodesic with initial velocity v.

nodes.name: parallel_transport
nodes.description: Moving a vector along a curve while keeping it "constant" with respect to the connection: nabla_{gamma'} V = 0.

nodes.name: covariant_derivative
nodes.description: The operator nabla_X Y giving the derivative of a vector field Y in the direction X using a connection.

nodes.name: differential_form
nodes.description: A section of the exterior power Lambda^k T^*M, the natural objects for integration on manifolds.

nodes.name: de_rham_cohomology
nodes.description: The cohomology H^k_{dR}(M) = ker d / im d of the exterior derivative complex.

nodes.name: connection_form
nodes.description: The 1-form omega on a principal bundle encoding the connection, valued in the Lie algebra of the structure group.

nodes.name: curvature_form
nodes.description: The 2-form Omega = d omega + omega wedge omega on a principal bundle, measuring the connection's curvature.

nodes.name: todd_class
nodes.description: The Todd class Td(E) of a complex vector bundle, a characteristic class appearing in index formulas.

nodes.name: cut_locus
nodes.description: The set of points where geodesics from a given point p cease to be minimizing.

nodes.name: volume_form
nodes.description: The canonical n-form on an oriented Riemannian manifold vol_g = sqrt(det g) dx^1 wedge ... wedge dx^n.

nodes.name: laplacian_on_manifold
nodes.description: The Laplace-Beltrami operator Delta f = div(grad f) on functions, or the Hodge Laplacian on forms.

nodes.name: harmonic_form
nodes.description: A differential form alpha with Delta alpha = 0, representing a de Rham cohomology class.

nodes.name: einstein_metric
nodes.description: A Riemannian metric satisfying Ric = lambda g for a constant lambda, the vacuum field equation of general relativity.

nodes.name: kahler_metric
nodes.description: A Riemannian metric on a complex manifold that is simultaneously Hermitian and symplectic, with parallel complex structure.

nodes.name: bochner_weitzenboeck_formula
nodes.description: Delta alpha = nabla^* nabla alpha + curvature terms, relating the Hodge Laplacian to the connection Laplacian and curvature.

nodes.name: berger_classification
nodes.description: The possible holonomy groups of irreducible simply connected non-symmetric Riemannian manifolds: SO(n), U(n), SU(n), Sp(n), Sp(n)Sp(1), G_2, Spin(7) (Berger)

nodes.name: hamilton_three_manifolds
nodes.description: A compact 3-manifold with positive Ricci curvature converges under Ricci flow to a space of constant positive curvature (Hamilton)

nodes.name: comparison_geometry
nodes.function_signature: (Manifold with curvature bounds) → (Comparison with model spaces)
nodes.description: Using sectional or Ricci curvature bounds to compare a manifold's geometry with model spaces of constant curvature.

nodes.name: bochner_technique
nodes.function_signature: (Manifold with curvature condition) → (Vanishing of harmonic forms)
nodes.description: Using the Bochner-Weitzenbock formula to deduce vanishing of harmonic forms from curvature positivity.

nodes.name: moving_frames_method
nodes.function_signature: (Submanifold with adapted frame) → (Curvature and connection forms)
nodes.description: Cartan's method of choosing adapted frames to compute curvature and connection forms efficiently.

nodes.name: trigonometric system
nodes.description: The orthonormal system {e^{2πinx} : n ∈ Z} on the circle.

nodes.name: L^p space on the circle
nodes.description: Space of measurable functions with finite p-th power integral on T.

nodes.name: Dirichlet kernel
nodes.description: D_N(x) = sum_{.

nodes.name: Fejér kernel
nodes.description: F_N(x) = (1/N) sum_{k=0}^{N-1} D_k(x), averaging kernel for Cesàro means.

nodes.name: maximal partial sum operator
nodes.description: S* f(x) = sup_N.

nodes.name: Riesz transform
nodes.description: R_j f(x) = c_n p.v. integral (x_j - y_j)/.

nodes.name: multiplier operator
nodes.description: T_m f = (m · f-hat)^∨ for a bounded function m (Fourier multiplier)

nodes.name: stationary phase point
nodes.description: A point x_0 where ∇φ(x_0) = 0, dominating oscillatory integral asymptotics.

nodes.name: Kakeya set
nodes.description: A compact set in R^n containing a unit line segment in every direction.

nodes.name: BMO space
nodes.description: Space of functions of bounded mean oscillation,.

nodes.name: A_p weight
nodes.description: A nonnegative locally integrable function w satisfying the Muckenhoupt A_p condition.

nodes.name: stationary phase method
nodes.description: Asymptotic expansion I(λ) ~ λ^{-n/2} sum a_k λ^{-k} when phase has nondegenerate critical point.

nodes.name: van der Corput lemma
nodes.description: Bounds on oscillatory integrals in one dimension:.

nodes.name: H^1-BMO duality
nodes.description: (H^1)* = BMO, the dual of the real Hardy space H^1 is the space of bounded mean oscillation.

nodes.name: Kakeya conjecture
nodes.description: Kakeya sets in R^n have Hausdorff dimension n (known for n=2, open for n ≥ 3)

nodes.name: TT* method
nodes.function_signature: (Prove L^p → L^q bounds by analyzing the self-adjoint operator TT* instead of T directly.) → (Result)
nodes.description: Prove L^p → L^q bounds by analyzing the self-adjoint operator TT* instead of T directly.

nodes.name: weak derivative
nodes.description: A locally integrable function g such that integral f ∂φ = -integral g φ for all test functions φ.

nodes.name: Neumann problem
nodes.description: Find u with Δu = f in Ω and ∂u/∂n = g on ∂Ω.

nodes.name: conservation law
nodes.description: ∂u/∂t + div F(u) = 0, a first-order hyperbolic system from physics.

nodes.name: shock wave
nodes.description: A discontinuous weak solution of a conservation law across a hypersurface.

nodes.name: Rankine-Hugoniot condition
nodes.description: Jump condition [F(u)]·n = s[u] relating shock speed s to jumps in u and F(u)

nodes.name: characteristics of a PDE
nodes.description: Curves or surfaces along which information propagates for first-order or hyperbolic equations.

nodes.name: Riemann problem
nodes.description: An initial value problem for a conservation law with piecewise constant initial data.

nodes.name: Leray existence of weak solutions for Navier-Stokes
nodes.description: For any L^2 initial data there exists a global weak solution of 3D Navier-Stokes.

nodes.name: Hopf maximum principle / boundary point lemma
nodes.description: If Lu ≥ 0, u achieves its max on the boundary, and at that boundary point the outward normal derivative is strictly positive.

nodes.name: energy method for PDE
nodes.function_signature: (PDE, Solution u) → (A priori estimates on u)
nodes.description: Multiply the PDE by u or its derivatives, integrate by parts to obtain a priori estimates.

nodes.name: method of characteristics
nodes.function_signature: (First-order PDE) → (Solution along characteristic curves)
nodes.description: Solve a first-order PDE by following characteristic curves along which the PDE becomes an ODE.

nodes.name: Galerkin approximation
nodes.function_signature: (Weak formulation of PDE) → (Approximate solutions in finite-dimensional subspaces)
nodes.description: Approximate weak solutions in finite-dimensional subspaces and pass to the limit using compactness.

nodes.name: stress-energy tensor
nodes.description: A symmetric (0,2)-tensor T_{μν} describing the density and flux of energy-momentum in spacetime.

nodes.name: causal structure
nodes.description: The partition of tangent vectors into timelike, null, and spacelike types determined by the Lorentzian metric.

nodes.name: Einstein tensor
nodes.description: G_{μν} = R_{μν} - (1/2)Rg_{μν}, the divergence-free combination entering the field equations.

nodes.name: Schwarzschild solution
nodes.description: The unique spherically symmetric vacuum solution ds² = -(1-2M/r)dt² + (1-2M/r)^{-1}dr² + r²dΩ².

nodes.name: Kerr solution
nodes.description: The rotating black hole solution, a stationary axisymmetric vacuum spacetime parametrized by mass M and angular momentum a.

nodes.name: Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker metric
nodes.description: Homogeneous isotropic cosmological solutions ds² = -dt² + a(t)²[dr²/(1-kr²) + r²dΩ²].

nodes.name: event horizon
nodes.description: A null hypersurface in spacetime beyond which events cannot send signals to infinity.

nodes.name: singularity in spacetime
nodes.description: A geodesic incompleteness: timelike or null geodesics that cannot be extended to infinite affine parameter.

nodes.name: Penrose diagram
nodes.description: A conformal compactification of spacetime mapping the causal structure to a bounded region.

nodes.name: ADM mass
nodes.description: The total mass-energy of an asymptotically flat spacetime measured at spatial infinity.

nodes.name: Bondi mass
nodes.description: Mass measured at null infinity, accounting for energy lost to gravitational radiation.

nodes.name: Cauchy surface
nodes.description: A spacelike hypersurface intersected exactly once by every inextendible timelike curve — an initial data surface.

nodes.name: Weyl tensor
nodes.description: C_{μνρσ}, the trace-free part of the Riemann tensor, encoding gravitational radiation.

nodes.name: Penrose inequality
nodes.description: The ADM mass M ≥ sqrt(A/16π) where A is the area of the outermost apparent horizon.

nodes.name: orbit of a point
nodes.description: {f^n(x) : n ≥ 0} for a discrete system, or {φ_t(x) : t ∈ R} for a flow.

nodes.name: attractor
nodes.description: A compact invariant set A that attracts all nearby orbits: d(f^n(x), A) → 0.

nodes.name: strange attractor
nodes.description: An attractor with sensitive dependence on initial conditions and fractal structure.

nodes.name: basin of attraction
nodes.description: The set of all initial conditions whose orbits converge to a given attractor.

nodes.name: sensitive dependence on initial conditions
nodes.description: Nearby orbits diverge exponentially: the hallmark of chaos, quantified by positive Lyapunov exponents.

nodes.name: symbolic dynamics
nodes.description: Representing orbits as sequences in a shift space {0,1,...,k-1}^Z with the shift map σ.

nodes.name: hyperbolic set
nodes.description: A compact f-invariant set Λ where the tangent bundle splits TΛ M = E^s ⊕ E^u with exponential contraction on E^s and expansion on E^u.

nodes.name: Fatou set
nodes.description: The complement of the Julia set: the maximal open set where iterates form a normal family.

nodes.name: bifurcation
nodes.description: A qualitative change in the dynamics (e.g., creation/destruction of fixed points) as a parameter varies.

nodes.name: logistic map
nodes.description: f(x) = rx(1-x) on [0,1], the simplest model exhibiting period-doubling cascade to chaos.

nodes.name: Hénon map
nodes.description: (x,y) ↦ (1-ax² + y, bx), a two-dimensional map exhibiting a strange attractor.

nodes.name: Lorenz attractor
nodes.description: The strange attractor of the Lorenz system dx/dt = σ(y-x), dy/dt = rx-y-xz, dz/dt = xy-bz.

nodes.name: KAM torus
nodes.description: An invariant torus in a nearly integrable Hamiltonian system surviving small perturbation (Diophantine frequency)

nodes.name: Jakobson's theorem
nodes.description: For a positive measure set of parameters, the logistic map has an absolutely continuous invariant measure.

nodes.name: Poincaré section
nodes.function_signature: (Continuous flow) → (Discrete return map on transversal)
nodes.description: Reduce a flow to a discrete map by recording intersections with a transversal hypersurface.

nodes.name: involution on an algebra
nodes.description: An antilinear map a ↦ a* satisfying (ab)* = b*a* and (a*)* = a.

nodes.name: spectrum of an element
nodes.description: σ(a) = {λ ∈ C : a - λ1 is not invertible}, the set of spectral values.

nodes.name: GNS representation
nodes.description: The *-representation π_φ: A → B(H_φ) on a Hilbert space H_φ constructed from a state φ via the GNS construction.

nodes.name: factor
nodes.description: A von Neumann algebra M whose center Z(M) = M ∩ M' consists only of scalar multiples of the identity.

nodes.name: Type I factor
nodes.description: A factor isomorphic to B(H) for some Hilbert space H.

nodes.name: Type II_1 factor
nodes.description: An infinite-dimensional factor admitting a faithful normal tracial state (unique up to scalar)

nodes.name: Type II_∞ factor
nodes.description: A factor isomorphic to a Type II_1 factor tensored with B(H) for infinite-dimensional H.

nodes.name: Type III factor
nodes.description: A factor with no nonzero finite projections (all nonzero projections are Murray-von Neumann equivalent)

nodes.name: hyperfinite II_1 factor R
nodes.description: The unique (up to isomorphism) approximately finite-dimensional Type II_1 factor.

nodes.name: KMS condition
nodes.description: A state φ is KMS at inverse temperature β if for all a,b ∈ M the function F_{a,b}(t) = φ(a σ_t(b)) extends analytically with F(t+iβ) = φ(σ_t(b)a)

nodes.name: subfactor
nodes.description: An inclusion N ⊂ M of Type II_1 factors.

nodes.name: Jones index [M:N]
nodes.description: A real number ≥ 1 measuring the relative size of a subfactor inclusion N ⊂ M.

nodes.name: standard invariant of a subfactor
nodes.description: The tower of relative commutants (the Bratteli diagram / paragroup / planar algebra) capturing the combinatorial data of N ⊂ M.

nodes.name: K_0 group of a C*-algebra
nodes.description: The Grothendieck group of Murray-von Neumann equivalence classes of projections in matrix algebras over A.

nodes.name: K_1 group of a C*-algebra
nodes.description: The group of connected components of the unitary group of the stabilization of A.

nodes.name: GNS theorem
nodes.description: Every state on a C*-algebra arises from a cyclic vector in a *-representation; the GNS representation is unique up to unitary equivalence.

nodes.name: Jones index theorem
nodes.description: The index [M:N] for a subfactor N ⊂ M takes values in {4cos²(π/n) : n ≥ 3} ∪ [4,∞)

nodes.name: Elliott classification of AF algebras
nodes.description: Approximately finite-dimensional C*-algebras are classified up to isomorphism by their ordered K_0 group with distinguished order unit.

nodes.name: Takesaki duality theorem
nodes.description: For a crossed product M ⋊_α G, the double crossed product (M ⋊_α G) ⋊_{α-hat} G-hat is isomorphic to M ⊗ B(L²(G))

nodes.name: GNS construction method
nodes.function_signature: (C*-algebra A, State φ) → (Hilbert space H, Representation π)
nodes.description: Construct a Hilbert space representation from a state by quotienting out the null space and completing.

nodes.name: Jones basic construction
nodes.function_signature: (Subfactor N⊂M) → (Tower of factors M_k with Jones projections)
nodes.description: From N ⊂ M, construct M_1 = <M, e_N> where e_N is the Jones projection onto L²(N), iterating to build the Jones tower.

nodes.name: string theory compactification
nodes.description: In string theory, extra dimensions are compactified on a Calabi-Yau 3-fold to produce a 4D effective theory.

nodes.name: Hodge numbers h^{p,q}
nodes.description: Dimensions of Dolbeault cohomology H^{p,q}(X) = H^q(X, Ω^p), refined Betti numbers of a Kähler manifold.

nodes.name: Hodge diamond
nodes.description: The array of Hodge numbers h^{p,q} arranged symmetrically, encoding the cohomological structure of a Kähler manifold.

nodes.name: period integral
nodes.description: integral_γ Ω for a holomorphic n-form Ω and a cycle γ ∈ H_n(X), encoding variation of complex structure.

nodes.name: Yukawa coupling
nodes.description: A three-point function on the moduli space computed from a cubic form on cohomology, with physical meaning as a coupling constant.

nodes.name: Gromov-Witten invariant
nodes.description: A virtual count of holomorphic curves of genus g and degree β in a target manifold X.

nodes.name: quantum cohomology
nodes.description: A deformation of the ordinary cohomology ring of X where the product is corrected by Gromov-Witten invariants.

nodes.name: prepotential
nodes.description: The generating function F(t) = sum_{β} N_β e^{2πi<β,t>} encoding genus-0 Gromov-Witten invariants (instanton corrections)

nodes.name: Fukaya category
nodes.description: An A_∞-category whose objects are Lagrangian submanifolds of a symplectic manifold with morphisms given by Floer cohomology.

nodes.name: A-model
nodes.description: The topological sigma model capturing symplectic geometry (Gromov-Witten invariants and the Fukaya category)

nodes.name: B-model
nodes.description: The topological sigma model capturing complex geometry (variations of Hodge structure and derived category of coherent sheaves)

nodes.name: Picard-Fuchs equation
nodes.description: An ODE satisfied by period integrals as the complex structure varies, encoding monodromy of the variation of Hodge structure.

nodes.name: mirror symmetry for the quintic (Candelas-de la Ossa-Green-Parkes)
nodes.description: The genus-0 Gromov-Witten invariants of the quintic 3-fold can be computed from the periods of its mirror via the Picard-Fuchs equation.

nodes.name: Kontsevich homological mirror symmetry conjecture
nodes.description: For a mirror pair (X, X̌), the derived Fukaya category of X is equivalent to the derived category of coherent sheaves on X̌.

nodes.name: SYZ conjecture (Strominger-Yau-Zaslow)
nodes.description: Mirror Calabi-Yau manifolds are T-dual special Lagrangian torus fibrations over the same base.

nodes.name: Batyrev mirror construction
nodes.description: For a Calabi-Yau hypersurface in a toric variety associated to a reflexive polytope Δ, the mirror is the CY hypersurface of the dual polytope Δ*.

nodes.name: localization on moduli spaces
nodes.function_signature: (Moduli space with torus action) → (Gromov-Witten invariants)
nodes.description: Use torus actions and virtual localization to compute Gromov-Witten invariants.

nodes.name: vertex algebra
nodes.description: A vector space V with a vacuum vector, a translation operator T, and a vertex operator map Y: V → End(V)[[z,z^{-1}]] satisfying locality.

nodes.name: vertex operator
nodes.description: Y(a,z) = sum a_{(n)} z^{-n-1}, a formal Laurent series of operators associated to a state a ∈ V.

nodes.name: Virasoro algebra
nodes.description: The infinite-dimensional Lie algebra spanned by {L_n}_{n ∈ Z} and central element c, with [L_m,L_n] = (m-n)L_{m+n} + (c/12)(m³-m)δ_{m+n,0}.

nodes.name: conformal vertex algebra
nodes.description: A vertex algebra with a Virasoro element ω ∈ V such that Y(ω,z) = sum L_n z^{-n-2} gives V a grading by L_0-eigenvalues.

nodes.name: monster group M
nodes.description: The largest sporadic finite simple group, of order ~8 × 10^53.

nodes.name: moonshine module V^♮
nodes.description: A vertex operator algebra of central charge 24 whose automorphism group is the monster group M.

nodes.name: j-function
nodes.description: The modular invariant j(τ) = q^{-1} + 744 + 196884q + ··· whose Fourier coefficients are related to representations of the monster.

nodes.name: McKay-Thompson series
nodes.description: T_g(τ) = sum_{n} Tr(g.

nodes.name: monstrous moonshine
nodes.description: The observation that Fourier coefficients of the j-function are sums of dimensions of irreducible representations of the monster group.

nodes.name: affine Lie algebra (Kac-Moody)
nodes.description: The central extension of the loop algebra g ⊗ C[t,t^{-1}], an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra.

nodes.name: WZW model
nodes.description: The Wess-Zumino-Witten conformal field theory associated to a compact Lie group and a level k.

nodes.name: rational vertex algebra
nodes.description: A vertex algebra with finitely many irreducible modules and complete reducibility (semisimple representation theory)

nodes.name: conformal field theory (2D)
nodes.description: A quantum field theory on a surface invariant under conformal transformations, axiomatized by vertex algebras.

nodes.name: operator product expansion
nodes.description: The expansion Y(a,z)Y(b,w) ~ sum c_k (z-w)^{-k-1} encoding singular behavior as z → w.

nodes.name: modular tensor category
nodes.description: A braided tensor category arising from the representation category of a rational vertex algebra, yielding a modular functor.

nodes.name: Borcherds' theorem (monstrous moonshine conjecture)
nodes.description: The McKay-Thompson series T_g(τ) for each g ∈ M is a principal modulus (Hauptmodul) for a genus-zero subgroup of SL_2(R)

nodes.name: Frenkel-Lepowsky-Meurman construction
nodes.description: The moonshine module V^♮ is constructed as an orbifold of the Leech lattice vertex algebra, proving the monster acts on it.

nodes.name: Goddard-Kent-Olive coset construction
nodes.description: Given a vertex subalgebra W ⊂ V, the commutant (coset) C(V,W) is again a vertex algebra, providing new conformal field theories.

nodes.name: singular homology H_n(X;Z)
nodes.description: H_n(X) = ker ∂_n / im ∂_{n+1}, the n-th homology group of the singular chain complex.

nodes.name: singular cohomology H^n(X;R)
nodes.description: H^n(X;R) = Hom(H_n(X), R) (approximately), dual to homology, with a ring structure via cup product.

nodes.name: cup product
nodes.description: A graded ring structure on H*(X;R): α ∪ β ∈ H^{p+q}(X;R) for α ∈ H^p and β ∈ H^q.

nodes.name: relative homology H_n(X,A)
nodes.description: Homology of the quotient complex C_*(X)/C_*(A), measuring the topology of X relative to a subspace A.

nodes.name: excision in homology
nodes.description: H_n(X,A) ≅ H_n(X\U, A\U) when the closure of U is contained in the interior of A.

nodes.name: reduced K-theory K̃(X)
nodes.description: K̃(X) = ker(K(X) → K(pt)), the reduced K-theory group.

nodes.name: cobordism group Ω_n
nodes.description: The group of closed n-manifolds up to cobordism equivalence (M ~ N if there exists W with ∂W = M ⊔ N)

nodes.name: Thom spectrum
nodes.description: The spectrum MO (or MU, MSO, etc.) whose homotopy groups are cobordism groups.

nodes.name: splitting principle
nodes.description: To prove an identity about characteristic classes of vector bundles, it suffices to prove it for direct sums of line bundles.

nodes.name: smooth map
nodes.description: A map between smooth manifolds that is infinitely differentiable in local coordinates.

nodes.name: smooth structure
nodes.description: An equivalence class of smooth atlases on a topological manifold, not always unique.

nodes.name: surgery on a manifold
nodes.description: Removing S^k × D^{n-k} from an n-manifold and replacing it with D^{k+1} × S^{n-k-1}, changing the topology.

nodes.name: connected sum
nodes.description: M₁ # M₂: remove a small ball from each manifold and glue along the resulting boundary spheres.

nodes.name: exotic sphere
nodes.description: A smooth manifold homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to the standard sphere S^n.

nodes.name: Milnor's exotic spheres
nodes.description: There exist smooth structures on S^7 not diffeomorphic to the standard one; specifically.

nodes.name: Kervaire-Milnor classification
nodes.description: The group Θ_n of exotic spheres is finite for n ≥ 5 and computable via the surgery exact sequence.

nodes.name: exotic R^4
nodes.description: There exist uncountably many pairwise non-diffeomorphic smooth structures on R^4.

nodes.name: Rohlin's theorem
nodes.description: The signature of a smooth closed spin 4-manifold is divisible by 16.

nodes.name: surgery theory
nodes.function_signature: (Manifold M, Normal map) → (Modified manifold with desired homotopy type)
nodes.description: Systematically modify manifolds by cutting and pasting handles to achieve desired homotopy type.

nodes.name: Deligne-Mumford compactification M̄_g
nodes.description: The compactification of M_g by stable curves (nodal curves with finite automorphism groups)

nodes.name: stable curve
nodes.description: A connected nodal curve of arithmetic genus g with only nodes as singularities and finite automorphism group.

nodes.name: Teichmüller space T_g
nodes.description: The universal covering of M_g, parametrizing marked Riemann surfaces (a complex manifold diffeomorphic to R^{6g-6})

nodes.name: moduli of vector bundles on a curve
nodes.description: The moduli space M(r,d) parametrizing semistable vector bundles of rank r and degree d on a fixed curve.

nodes.name: S-equivalence
nodes.description: Two semistable bundles are S-equivalent if they have the same associated graded object; points of the moduli space represent S-equivalence classes.

nodes.name: period matrix
nodes.description: A g × 2g matrix of integrals of holomorphic 1-forms over cycles, mapping a curve to its Jacobian in A_g.

nodes.name: Torelli map
nodes.description: The map M_g → A_g sending a curve C to its Jacobian variety Jac(C)

nodes.name: stability in GIT
nodes.description: A point x is stable if its orbit is closed in the semistable locus and its stabilizer is finite.

nodes.name: algebraic stack
nodes.description: A generalization of a scheme allowing objects with nontrivial automorphisms to be parametrized, e.g. [X/G].

nodes.name: Deligne-Mumford stack
nodes.description: An algebraic stack with finite, reduced automorphism groups at every point.

nodes.name: tautological classes on M̄_g
nodes.description: The classes ψ_i, κ_j, λ ∈ H*(M̄_{g,n}) generating the tautological ring.

nodes.name: Mumford's GIT construction
nodes.description: For a reductive group G acting on a projective variety X with linearization, the GIT quotient X//G exists as a projective variety.

nodes.name: Narasimhan-Seshadri theorem
nodes.description: Stable vector bundles on a Riemann surface of degree 0 correspond to irreducible unitary representations of the fundamental group.

nodes.name: Harer stability
nodes.description: H_k(Mod_g; Z) is independent of g for g >> k; the homology of the mapping class group stabilizes.

nodes.name: Witten conjecture (Kontsevich's theorem)
nodes.description: The generating function for intersection numbers of ψ-classes on M̄_{g,n} satisfies the KdV hierarchy.

nodes.name: partition of an integer
nodes.description: A way of writing n as an unordered sum of positive integers: n = λ_1 + λ_2 + ··· + λ_k with λ_1 ≥ ··· ≥ λ_k ≥ 1.

nodes.name: Young diagram
nodes.description: A left-justified array of boxes with λ_i boxes in row i, the visual representation of a partition λ.

nodes.name: symmetric function
nodes.description: A formal power series f(x_1,x_2,...) invariant under all permutations of the variables.

nodes.name: Schur polynomial s_λ
nodes.description: The symmetric function s_λ = sum_T x^T summed over semistandard Young tableaux of shape λ.

nodes.name: Kostka number K_{λ,μ}
nodes.description: The number of semistandard Young tableaux of shape λ and weight μ; the transition matrix between Schur and monomial symmetric functions.

nodes.name: Littlewood-Richardson coefficient c^ν_{λ,μ}
nodes.description: The structure constant s_λ · s_μ = sum c^ν_{λ,μ} s_ν for multiplication of Schur polynomials.

nodes.name: Littlewood-Richardson rule
nodes.description: c^ν_{λ,μ} counts the number of LR tableaux (skew SSYT of shape ν/λ and weight μ satisfying the lattice word condition)

nodes.name: Robinson-Schensted correspondence
nodes.description: A bijection between permutations of {1,...,n} and pairs (P,Q) of standard Young tableaux of the same shape.

nodes.name: Möbius function of a poset
nodes.description: μ: P × P → Z defined by sum_{z: x≤z≤y} μ(x,z) = δ_{x,y}, the combinatorial analogue of inclusion-exclusion.

nodes.name: Möbius inversion on posets
nodes.description: If g(x) = sum_{y≤x} f(y), then f(x) = sum_{y≤x} μ(y,x)g(y)

nodes.name: zeta polynomial of a poset
nodes.description: Z(P,n) = number of multichains x_0 ≤ x_1 ≤ ··· ≤ x_n in P, a polynomial in n.

nodes.name: incidence algebra of a poset
nodes.description: The algebra of functions f: {(x,y) : x ≤ y} → k with convolution product (f*g)(x,y) = sum_{x≤z≤y} f(x,z)g(z,y)

nodes.name: P-partition
nodes.description: An order-preserving map σ: P → {1,2,...} from a labeled poset P to the positive integers.

nodes.name: Jacobi-Trudi formula
nodes.description: s_λ = det(h_{λ_i - i + j})_{1≤i,j≤k}, expressing Schur functions as determinants of complete homogeneous symmetric functions.

nodes.name: dual Jacobi-Trudi formula
nodes.description: s_λ = det(e_{λ'_i - i + j}), expressing Schur functions via elementary symmetric functions and the conjugate partition.

nodes.name: Cauchy identity
nodes.description: sum_λ s_λ(x) s_λ(y) = prod_{i,j} 1/(1 - x_i y_j), a fundamental identity for Schur functions.

nodes.name: Pieri's rule
nodes.description: s_λ · h_k = sum s_μ summed over μ obtained from λ by adding k boxes with no two in the same column.

nodes.name: Frobenius characteristic map
nodes.description: A ring isomorphism from the representation ring of all symmetric groups to the ring of symmetric functions, sending irreps to Schur functions.

nodes.name: Cauchy identity proof and generalizations
nodes.description: The Cauchy identity and its dual encode the RSK correspondence bijectively and underlie much of symmetric function theory.

nodes.name: simple graph
nodes.description: A graph G = (V,E) with no loops or multiple edges.

nodes.name: Turán graph T(n,r)
nodes.description: The complete r-partite graph on n vertices with part sizes as equal as possible, the extremal graph for K_{r+1}-free graphs.

nodes.name: graph density
nodes.description: The ratio.

nodes.name: clique number ω(G)
nodes.description: The size of the largest complete subgraph of G.

nodes.name: independence number α(G)
nodes.description: The size of the largest independent set (no two adjacent) in G.

nodes.name: regularity partition
nodes.description: A partition of V(G) into clusters such that most pairs of clusters have edge density close to the overall density (ε-regular)

nodes.name: ε-regular pair
nodes.description: A pair (A,B) of vertex sets where for all large subsets A' ⊂ A, B' ⊂ B, the edge density d(A',B') ≈ d(A,B)

nodes.name: arithmetic progression of length k
nodes.description: A set {a, a+d, a+2d, ..., a+(k-1)d} in the integers.

nodes.name: graph Ramsey theory
nodes.description: The study of which monochromatic substructures must appear in any coloring of a large complete graph.

nodes.name: sunflower (Δ-system)
nodes.description: A family of sets {A_1,...,A_k} whose pairwise intersections are all equal: A_i ∩ A_j = K for all i ≠ j.

nodes.name: extremal number ex(n,H)
nodes.description: The maximum number of edges in an H-free graph on n vertices.

nodes.name: Sunflower lemma (Erdős-Ko)
nodes.description: A family of more than (p-1)^k k! sets of size k contains a sunflower with p petals.

nodes.name: probabilistic method
nodes.function_signature: (Probability space on structures) → (Existence of structure with desired properties)
nodes.description: Prove existence of combinatorial structures by showing a random object has the desired property with positive probability.

nodes.name: regularity method
nodes.function_signature: (Dense graph G) → (Regular partition, Embedded substructures)
nodes.description: Apply Szemerédi regularity lemma then counting/embedding lemma to find substructures in dense graphs.

nodes.name: alteration method
nodes.function_signature: (Random structure with violations) → (Deterministic fix of violations)
nodes.description: Start with a random structure, then deterministically fix a small number of violations.

nodes.name: alphabet and strings
nodes.description: A finite alphabet Σ and the set Σ* of all finite strings over Σ.

nodes.name: Boolean circuit
nodes.description: A directed acyclic graph of AND, OR, NOT gates computing a Boolean function.

nodes.name: decision problem / language
nodes.description: A subset L ⊂ Σ* to be decided (accepted or rejected) by a computational model.

nodes.name: complexity class P
nodes.description: The class of decision problems solvable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.

nodes.name: complexity class NP
nodes.description: The class of decision problems for which a YES certificate can be verified in polynomial time.

nodes.name: NP-completeness
nodes.description: A language L is NP-complete if L ∈ NP and every NP problem reduces to L in polynomial time.

nodes.name: SAT (Boolean satisfiability)
nodes.description: Given a Boolean formula, is there a truth assignment making it true? The canonical NP-complete problem.

nodes.name: 3-SAT
nodes.description: SAT restricted to CNF formulas with exactly 3 literals per clause, still NP-complete.

nodes.name: complexity class coNP
nodes.description: The class of languages whose complements are in NP.

nodes.name: complexity class PSPACE
nodes.description: Problems solvable using polynomial space (regardless of time)

nodes.name: complexity class L (logspace)
nodes.description: Problems solvable using O(log n) bits of working memory.

nodes.name: complexity class NL (nondeterministic logspace)
nodes.description: Problems solvable by a nondeterministic TM using O(log n) space.

nodes.name: complexity class BPP
nodes.description: Problems solvable by a randomized TM in polynomial time with error probability < 1/3.

nodes.name: complexity class RP
nodes.description: Problems solvable by a randomized TM in polynomial time: no-instances always rejected, yes-instances accepted with probability ≥ 1/2.

nodes.name: complexity class IP
nodes.description: Problems solvable by an interactive proof system: a polynomial-time verifier interacting with an all-powerful prover.

nodes.name: circuit complexity
nodes.description: The minimum size (number of gates) of a Boolean circuit computing a given function.

nodes.name: circuit class NC
nodes.description: Problems solvable by polylog-depth polynomial-size circuits (efficiently parallelizable problems)

nodes.name: circuit class AC^0
nodes.description: Problems solvable by constant-depth polynomial-size circuits with unbounded fan-in AND/OR gates.

nodes.name: polynomial hierarchy PH
nodes.description: PH = ∪_k Σ^P_k, the hierarchy of alternating quantifier classes generalizing NP and coNP.

nodes.name: space complexity class
nodes.description: DSPACE(f(n)) and NSPACE(f(n)): problems solvable in deterministic/nondeterministic f(n) space.

nodes.name: approximation algorithm
nodes.description: An algorithm that finds a solution within a guaranteed factor of the optimal for an NP-hard optimization problem.

nodes.name: PCP verifier
nodes.description: A probabilistic verifier that checks a proof by reading only O(1) random bits and O(1) proof bits.

nodes.name: P ≠ NP conjecture
nodes.description: The (unresolved) conjecture that not every problem with polynomial-time verifiable solutions has a polynomial-time algorithm.

nodes.name: IP = PSPACE
nodes.description: Every PSPACE language has an interactive proof, and conversely every IP language is in PSPACE.

nodes.name: PCP theorem and inapproximability
nodes.description: The PCP theorem implies that MAX-3SAT cannot be approximated within a factor better than 7/8 unless P = NP.

nodes.name: NP-completeness of 3-SAT
nodes.description: Reduction from SAT to 3-SAT proving that the restriction remains NP-complete.

nodes.name: Baker-Gill-Solovay relativization barrier
nodes.description: There exist oracles A,B such that P^A = NP^A and P^B ≠ NP^B, so P vs NP cannot be resolved by relativizing techniques.

nodes.name: diagonalization
nodes.function_signature: (Enumeration of machines) → (Language not in the class)
nodes.description: Construct a language differing from every machine in a list on at least one input, proving hierarchy separations.

nodes.name: arithmetization
nodes.function_signature: (Boolean formula) → (Polynomial over finite field for interactive proofs)
nodes.description: Convert a Boolean formula to a polynomial over a finite field to design interactive proofs.

nodes.name: floating-point number system
nodes.description: A finite subset F ⊂ R representing real numbers as ±d × β^e with precision t and exponent range.

nodes.name: mesh / grid
nodes.description: A discretization of a domain Ω into finitely many elements (triangles, rectangles, tetrahedra)

nodes.name: interpolation
nodes.description: Constructing a function p from a finite-dimensional space that matches given data values at specified nodes.

nodes.name: polynomial interpolation
nodes.description: Finding the unique polynomial of degree ≤ n passing through n+1 given data points.

nodes.name: Lagrange interpolation
nodes.description: The polynomial p(x) = sum f(x_i) L_i(x) where L_i are the Lagrange basis polynomials.

nodes.name: Newton interpolation
nodes.description: Interpolation using the Newton divided-difference form with the forward-difference table.

nodes.name: spline interpolation
nodes.description: Piecewise polynomial interpolation with specified smoothness at the knots.

nodes.name: numerical quadrature
nodes.description: Approximating integral_a^b f(x) dx by a weighted sum sum w_i f(x_i)

nodes.name: Gaussian quadrature
nodes.description: Quadrature with nodes and weights chosen to be exact for polynomials of degree ≤ 2n-1 using n nodes.

nodes.name: Newton-Cotes formula
nodes.description: Quadrature using equally spaced nodes (trapezoidal rule, Simpson's rule, etc.)

nodes.name: finite element space
nodes.description: A space of piecewise polynomial functions on a triangulation, e.g. continuous piecewise linear (P1) functions.

nodes.name: stiffness matrix
nodes.description: The matrix K_{ij} = a(φ_j, φ_i) arising from the bilinear form of a finite element discretization.

nodes.name: spectral method
nodes.description: Approximating a PDE solution by a truncated expansion in orthogonal polynomials or Fourier modes.

nodes.name: linear multistep method
nodes.description: An ODE solver using a linear combination of previous steps: sum a_j y_{n-j} = h sum b_j f_{n-j}.

nodes.name: truncation error
nodes.description: The difference between the exact and numerical operator applied to the exact solution, measuring discretization quality.

nodes.name: stability of a numerical method
nodes.description: The property that small perturbations in data produce small perturbations in the numerical solution.

nodes.name: convergence of a numerical method
nodes.description: The numerical solution approaches the exact solution as the mesh is refined (h → 0)

nodes.name: CFL condition
nodes.description: Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy condition: Δt/Δx ≤ C for stability of explicit time-stepping for hyperbolic PDEs.

nodes.name: conjugate gradient method
nodes.description: An iterative method for symmetric positive definite systems achieving the minimum error in the A-norm over Krylov subspaces.

nodes.name: multigrid method
nodes.description: An iterative method using a hierarchy of grids: smooth the error on a fine grid, restrict to a coarse grid, solve, and interpolate back.

nodes.name: Krylov subspace
nodes.description: K_k(A,b) = span{b, Ab, A²b, ..., A^{k-1}b}, the subspace explored by iterative methods like CG and GMRES.

nodes.name: Céa's lemma
nodes.description: The finite element solution u_h satisfies.

nodes.name: Bramble-Hilbert lemma
nodes.description: An approximation theory result bounding the error of polynomial interpolation on a reference element.

nodes.name: Runge phenomenon
nodes.description: Polynomial interpolation on equally spaced nodes can diverge for smooth functions as the degree increases.

nodes.name: Lax-Richtmyer theorem
nodes.description: A consistent numerical scheme is convergent if and only if it is stable (for well-posed linear initial value problems)

nodes.name: Dahlquist barrier theorems
nodes.description: No linear multistep method of order > 2 is A-stable (second Dahlquist barrier); stable methods have order ≤ p+2 where p is the number of steps.

nodes.name: Richardson extrapolation
nodes.function_signature: (Approximations at step sizes h, h/2) → (Higher-order approximation)
nodes.description: Combine numerical solutions at different step sizes to cancel leading error terms and obtain higher-order accuracy.

nodes.name: adaptive mesh refinement
nodes.function_signature: (PDE domain, Error estimator) → (Locally refined mesh)
nodes.description: Locally refine the mesh where the estimated error is large, achieving efficiency for problems with varying regularity.

nodes.name: axiom of extensionality
nodes.description: Two sets are equal iff they have the same elements: ∀x(x∈A ↔ x∈B) → A=B.

nodes.name: axiom of infinity
nodes.description: There exists an infinite set (containing ∅ and closed under successor)

nodes.name: axiom of replacement
nodes.description: The image of a set under a definable function is a set.

nodes.name: axiom of power set
nodes.description: For any set A, the collection P(A) of all subsets of A is a set.

nodes.name: axiom of regularity / foundation
nodes.description: Every nonempty set x contains an element y with x ∩ y = ∅ (no infinite descending ∈-chains)

nodes.name: successor ordinal
nodes.description: An ordinal of the form α + 1 = α ∪ {α}.

nodes.name: limit ordinal
nodes.description: An ordinal that is neither 0 nor a successor, e.g. ω, the first infinite ordinal.

nodes.name: aleph numbers ℵ_α
nodes.description: The α-th infinite cardinal: ℵ_0 =.

nodes.name: V = L (axiom of constructibility)
nodes.description: The assertion that every set is constructible, a restrictive axiom implying GCH and many combinatorial principles.

nodes.name: forcing
nodes.description: Cohen's technique for constructing models of set theory by adding generic filters over a poset to a ground model.

nodes.name: generic filter
nodes.description: A filter G on a partial order P meeting every dense set in the ground model, used in forcing extensions.

nodes.name: forcing extension M[G]
nodes.description: The smallest model of ZFC containing M and the generic filter G, where new sets are interpreted via names.

nodes.name: Boolean-valued model
nodes.description: A model of set theory where truth values come from a complete Boolean algebra rather than {0,1}.

nodes.name: large cardinal
nodes.description: A cardinal number whose existence transcends ZFC provability, providing a hierarchy of consistency strength.

nodes.name: supercompact cardinal
nodes.description: A cardinal κ such that for every λ ≥ κ there is an elementary embedding j: V → M with critical point κ and M^λ ⊂ M.

nodes.name: Woodin cardinal
nodes.description: A cardinal δ such that for every A ⊂ V_δ there exists an elementary embedding with critical point below δ.

nodes.name: determinacy (AD)
nodes.description: Every two-player infinite game on ω with a Borel (or more complex) payoff set is determined.

nodes.name: Borel set
nodes.description: A set in the σ-algebra generated by open sets in a topological space.

nodes.name: analytic / Σ^1_1 set
nodes.description: The continuous image of a Borel set, first level of the projective hierarchy.

nodes.name: descriptive set theory
nodes.description: The study of definable subsets of Polish spaces (Borel, analytic, projective sets) using set-theoretic methods.

nodes.name: Gödel's consistency of CH
nodes.description: The continuum hypothesis and the axiom of choice hold in the constructible universe L, so Con(ZFC) → Con(ZFC + CH)

nodes.name: Cohen's independence of CH
nodes.description: By forcing, there exists a model of ZFC where CH fails, so CH is independent of ZFC.

nodes.name: large cardinal consistency hierarchy
nodes.description: The consistency strength ordering: inaccessible < measurable < Woodin < supercompact < ...

nodes.name: forcing technique
nodes.function_signature: (Model M of ZFC, Partial order P) → (Generic extension M[G])
nodes.description: Add a generic object to a model of ZFC by choosing an appropriate partial order and interpreting names.

nodes.name: iterated forcing
nodes.function_signature: (Model M, Ordinal-length iteration) → (Iterated generic extension)
nodes.description: Perform forcing at successive stages along an ordinal, supporting at limit stages with direct/inverse limits.

nodes.name: model of a theory
nodes.description: A structure M satisfying all sentences in T, written M ⊨ T.

nodes.name: complete theory
nodes.description: A consistent theory T such that for every sentence φ, either T ⊢ φ or T ⊢ ¬φ.

nodes.name: type over A
nodes.description: A maximal consistent collection of formulas in variables x with parameters from A, an element of the Stone space S_n(A)

nodes.name: definable set
nodes.description: A subset of M^n defined by a first-order formula: {a ∈ M^n : M ⊨ φ(a)}.

nodes.name: ultrafilter
nodes.description: A maximal proper filter on a Boolean algebra (or index set), used to form ultraproducts.

nodes.name: ultraproduct
nodes.description: ∏_I M_i / U, the quotient of a product of structures by an ultrafilter U with Łoś's theorem determining truth.

nodes.name: saturated model
nodes.description: A model M that realizes every type over every subset A ⊂ M of cardinality <.

nodes.name: homogeneous model
nodes.description: A model where every elementary map between small subsets extends to an automorphism.

nodes.name: model completeness
nodes.description: A theory T such that every embedding between models is elementary.

nodes.name: Morley rank
nodes.description: An ordinal-valued rank on definable sets in an ω-stable theory, generalizing dimension.

nodes.name: o-minimal structure
nodes.description: An ordered structure (M, <, ...) where every definable subset of M is a finite union of intervals and points.

nodes.name: categoricity in power κ
nodes.description: A theory T is κ-categorical if all models of T of cardinality κ are isomorphic.

nodes.name: Baldwin-Lachlan theorem
nodes.description: An uncountably categorical theory that is not totally categorical has exactly two countable models (up to isomorphism)

nodes.name: Shelah's classification theory
nodes.description: A complete theory is classifiable (its models are determined by cardinal invariants) iff it is superstable with NDOP and NOTOP.

nodes.name: ultraproduct construction
nodes.function_signature: (Form new models by taking products modulo an ultrafilter) → (Result)
nodes.description: Form new models by taking products modulo an ultrafilter, transferring first-order properties.

nodes.name: back-and-forth method
nodes.function_signature: (Construct isomorphisms or elementary maps between countable structures by alternately extending partial maps.) → (Result)
nodes.description: Construct isomorphisms or elementary maps between countable structures by alternately extending partial maps.

nodes.name: filtration {F_t}
nodes.description: An increasing family of σ-algebras F_s ⊂ F_t for s ≤ t, representing information available at time t.

nodes.name: adapted process
nodes.description: A stochastic process X_t where X_t is F_t-measurable for each t.

nodes.name: stationary distribution
nodes.description: A probability vector π with πP = π, the long-run distribution of an ergodic Markov chain.

nodes.name: supermartingale
nodes.description: An adapted process with E[X_t.

nodes.name: Itô integral
nodes.description: integral_0^t H_s dW_s for adapted processes H, extending integration to Brownian motion as integrator.

nodes.name: Itô process
nodes.description: X_t = X_0 + integral_0^t μ_s ds + integral_0^t σ_s dW_s, a process driven by drift and Brownian noise.

nodes.name: Itô's formula
nodes.description: d f(X_t) = f'(X_t) dX_t + (1/2) f''(X_t) (dX_t)² with (dW_t)² = dt, the chain rule of stochastic calculus.

nodes.name: Gaussian free field
nodes.description: The canonical Gaussian process indexed by functions on a domain, with covariance given by the Green's function.

nodes.name: percolation model
nodes.description: On Z^d or another lattice, each edge (bond) or vertex (site) is open with probability p, independently.

nodes.name: critical probability p_c
nodes.description: The threshold p_c such that an infinite open cluster exists a.s. for p > p_c and not for p < p_c.

nodes.name: Harris-FKG inequality
nodes.description: For increasing events A, B on a product probability space, P(A ∩ B) ≥ P(A)P(B)

nodes.name: coupling of Markov chains
nodes.function_signature: (Two Markov chains on same space) → (Meeting time bounds, Mixing time)
nodes.description: Construct two chains on the same probability space so they meet, bounding mixing times and distances between distributions.

nodes.name: Lévy's lemma on the sphere
nodes.description: A 1-Lipschitz function on S^{n-1} is within ε of its median except on a set of measure ≤ C e^{-cεn}.

nodes.name: Johnson-Lindenstrauss projection
nodes.description: A random linear projection from R^n to R^k with k = O(ε^{-2} log N) preserves pairwise distances of N points within (1±ε)

nodes.name: Rademacher average
nodes.description: E.

nodes.name: volume ratio
nodes.description: vr(K) = (vol(K)/vol(E))^{1/n} where E is the maximal volume ellipsoid in K, measuring roundness.

nodes.name: entropy and covering numbers
nodes.description: N(K,εB) = the minimum number of translates of εB needed to cover K, measuring metric complexity.

nodes.name: Sudakov minoration
nodes.description: For a Gaussian process indexed by T ⊂ S^{n-1}: E sup_{t∈T} <g,t> ≥ c ε √(log N(T,ε))

nodes.name: restricted invertibility
nodes.description: Given vectors in a high-dimensional space, one can find a proportional-size subset on which the associated operator is well-conditioned.

nodes.name: Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma
nodes.description: For any ε > 0 and N points in R^n, there exists a linear map into R^k with k = O(ε^{-2} log N) preserving all pairwise distances within (1±ε)

nodes.name: Gaussian isoperimetric theorem (Borell, Sudakov-Tsirelson)
nodes.description: Half-spaces are the isoperimetric extremizers for Gaussian measure: they minimize boundary measure for given Gaussian volume.

nodes.name: Bourgain-Milman inverse Santaló inequality
nodes.description: vol(K) · vol(K°) ≥ c^n vol(B_2^n)² for centrally symmetric convex bodies K.

nodes.name: Talagrand's majorizing measures theorem
nodes.description: E sup_{t∈T} X_t ~ γ_2(T,d) where γ_2 is the generic chaining functional, characterizing the expected supremum of a Gaussian process.

nodes.name: Schechtman's theorem on random sections
nodes.description: A random k-dimensional section of ℓ_1^n is (1+ε)-Euclidean for k ≤ c ε² n / log n.

nodes.name: Bourgain-Tzafriri restricted invertibility theorem
nodes.description: Given vectors v_1,...,v_n with.

nodes.name: random projection / sketching
nodes.function_signature: (Project high-dimensional data onto a random low-dimensional subspace to approximately preserve geometry.) → (Result)
nodes.description: Project high-dimensional data onto a random low-dimensional subspace to approximately preserve geometry.

nodes.name: generic chaining
nodes.function_signature: (Stochastic process) → (Bound on E[sup X_t] via entropy integral)
nodes.description: Bound the supremum of a stochastic process by a multi-scale entropy integral summing over dyadic scales.

nodes.name: radical_of_integer
nodes.description: The radical rad(n) of a positive integer n is the product of the distinct prime factors of n.

nodes.name: abc_triple
nodes.description: A triple (a,b,c) of coprime positive integers satisfying a + b = c.

nodes.name: abc_conjecture
nodes.description: For every ε > 0 there exist finitely many abc-triples with c > rad(abc)^(1+ε)

nodes.name: quality_of_abc_triple
nodes.description: The quality q(a,b,c) = log(c)/log(rad(abc)) measuring how exceptional an abc-triple is.

nodes.name: mason_stothers_theorem
nodes.description: For coprime polynomials a(t)+b(t)=c(t), max(deg a, deg b, deg c) ≤ deg(rad(abc)) - 1; the polynomial analogue of ABC.

nodes.name: szpiros_conjecture
nodes.description: For elliptic curves E/ℚ with conductor N and minimal discriminant Δ,.

nodes.name: halls_conjecture
nodes.description: If x³ − y² ≠ 0 for integers x,y then.

nodes.name: erdos_woods_conjecture_consequence
nodes.description: ABC implies that for large enough k, there is no pair m < n with rad(m+i) = rad(n+i) for i=0,…,k.

nodes.name: weak_abc_conjecture
nodes.description: There exists a constant C > 0 such that c < rad(abc)^C for all abc-triples.

nodes.name: abc_implies_fermat_asymptotic
nodes.description: The ABC conjecture implies FLT for sufficiently large exponents.

nodes.name: abc_implies_mordell
nodes.description: ABC conjecture implies Mordell conjecture (Faltings' theorem) via Elkies' result.

nodes.name: langevin_result
nodes.description: Effective bounds on number of solutions to S-unit equations follow from ABC.

nodes.name: analytic_index
nodes.description: The analytic index of an elliptic operator D is dim ker D − dim coker D.

nodes.name: k_theory
nodes.description: The Grothendieck group K(X) of vector bundles on X, the natural home for the index.

nodes.name: k_theory_proof
nodes.function_signature: (Elliptic operator D) → (Index via K-theory and cobordism)
nodes.description: Atiyah-Singer's original proof via cobordism invariance and K-theory.

nodes.name: families_index_theorem
nodes.description: A generalization of the index theorem to continuous families of elliptic operators, yielding a K-theory class.

nodes.name: eta_invariant
nodes.description: A spectral invariant measuring the asymmetry of the spectrum of a self-adjoint elliptic operator on the boundary.

nodes.name: hausdorff_paradox
nodes.description: The sphere S² minus countably many points is paradoxical under rotations; precursor to Banach-Tarski.

nodes.name: tarski_alternative
nodes.description: A group G is non-amenable if and only if it is paradoxical.

nodes.name: finitely_additive_measure
nodes.description: A measure where μ(A ∪ B) = μ(A) + μ(B) for disjoint sets, but not necessarily for countable unions.

nodes.name: von_neumann_conjecture
nodes.description: A group is non-amenable if and only if it contains a free subgroup of rank 2 (now known to be false)

nodes.name: no_paradox_in_plane
nodes.description: The Banach-Tarski paradox does not occur in ℝ¹ or ℝ², because the isometry groups are amenable (solvable)

nodes.name: equidecomposable
nodes.description: Two sets A,B are equidecomposable if A can be partitioned into pieces rearranged by group elements to form B.

nodes.name: algebraic_rank
nodes.description: The rank of the Mordell-Weil group E(ℚ), i.e., the number of independent points of infinite order.

nodes.name: analytic_rank
nodes.description: The order of vanishing of L(E,s) at s = 1.

nodes.name: bsd_conjecture
nodes.description: The algebraic rank of E equals the analytic rank of L(E,s), plus an exact formula for the leading coefficient.

nodes.name: bsd_leading_coefficient
nodes.description: The leading term of L(E,s) at s=1 involves Ш, the regulator, Tamagawa numbers, and the torsion.

nodes.name: neron_tate_height_pairing
nodes.description: A canonical quadratic form on E(ℚ) used to define the regulator appearing in BSD.

nodes.name: carlesons_theorem
nodes.description: The Fourier series of every L² function converges pointwise almost everywhere.

nodes.name: carleson_operator
nodes.description: The maximal operator C*f(x) = sup_N.

nodes.name: time_frequency_analysis
nodes.function_signature: (Function f) → (Time-frequency decomposition)
nodes.description: Decomposition of functions simultaneously in time and frequency, underlying modern proofs of Carleson's theorem.

nodes.name: luzin_conjecture
nodes.description: Carleson's theorem resolved Luzin's 1915 conjecture that L² Fourier series converge a.e.

nodes.name: du_bois_reymond_example
nodes.description: A continuous function whose Fourier series diverges at a point; shows continuity alone is insufficient.

nodes.name: normal_distribution
nodes.description: The Gaussian distribution N(μ,σ²) with density (2πσ²)^{-1/2} exp(−(x−μ)²/(2σ²))

nodes.name: lindeberg_clt
nodes.description: CLT holds for independent (non-identically distributed) variables if Lindeberg's condition is satisfied.

nodes.name: lindeberg_condition
nodes.description: For each ε > 0, the sum of truncated variances is negligible relative to total variance; sufficient for CLT.

nodes.name: lyapunov_clt
nodes.description: CLT holds if a Lyapunov condition on moments of order 2+δ is satisfied; implies Lindeberg.

nodes.name: multivariate_clt
nodes.description: The CLT extends to random vectors, with convergence to a multivariate normal distribution.

nodes.name: simple_group
nodes.description: A group G ≠ {e} with no proper normal subgroups; the atoms of group theory.

nodes.name: alternating_group
nodes.description: The group A_n of even permutations on n letters, simple for n ≥ 5.

nodes.name: groups_of_lie_type
nodes.description: Finite analogues of simple Lie groups, including classical groups (PSL, PSp, PSO, PSU) and exceptional types.

nodes.name: chevalley_groups
nodes.description: Groups of Lie type over finite fields constructed by Chevalley's uniform method.

nodes.name: sporadic_groups
nodes.description: The 26 finite simple groups that do not belong to any infinite family.

nodes.name: monster_group
nodes.description: The largest sporadic simple group, of order approximately 8 × 10⁵³.

nodes.name: mathieu_groups
nodes.description: Five sporadic simple groups M₁₁, M₁₂, M₂₂, M₂₃, M₂₄ discovered by Mathieu; the first sporadic groups.

nodes.name: baby_monster
nodes.description: The second-largest sporadic group, a subquotient of the Monster.

nodes.name: thompson_classification
nodes.description: Thompson's classification of minimal simple groups (simple groups all of whose proper subgroups are solvable)

nodes.name: bn_pair
nodes.description: A pair of subgroups (B,N) in a group G satisfying Tits' axioms; the structural basis for groups of Lie type.

nodes.name: local_analysis
nodes.function_signature: (Finite group G, Prime p) → (Structure of p-local subgroups)
nodes.description: Studying a finite group via the structure of normalizers of p-subgroups.

nodes.name: character_theory_in_cfsg
nodes.function_signature: (Finite group G) → (Character-theoretic constraints on structure)
nodes.description: Use of ordinary and modular character theory to constrain the structure of simple groups.

nodes.name: quasithin_groups
nodes.description: Simple groups of characteristic-2 type with e(G) ≤ 2; the last major case completed by Aschbacher-Smith.

nodes.name: monstrous_moonshine
nodes.description: Unexpected connection between the Monster group and modular functions (j-invariant)

nodes.name: griess_construction
nodes.description: Construction of the Monster group as the automorphism group of a 196884-dimensional commutative algebra.

nodes.name: arithmetic_progression
nodes.description: A sequence a, a+d, a+2d, … with gcd(a,d)=1.

nodes.name: non_vanishing_of_l1_chi
nodes.description: L(1,χ) ≠ 0 for all non-principal Dirichlet characters χ; the key step in Dirichlet's proof.

nodes.name: orthogonality_of_characters
nodes.function_signature: (Dirichlet characters mod q) → (Isolation of primes in arithmetic progressions)
nodes.description: The relation Σ_χ χ(n) = φ(d) if n ≡ 1 mod d, 0 otherwise; used to isolate primes in a progression.

nodes.name: dirichlet_density
nodes.description: The Dirichlet density of a set S of primes is lim_{s→1+} Σ_{p∈S} p^{−s} / log(1/(s−1))

nodes.name: equidistribution_of_primes
nodes.description: Primes are equidistributed among the φ(d) residue classes coprime to d, each having Dirichlet density 1/φ(d)

nodes.name: logarithmic_derivative_of_l
nodes.function_signature: (L-function L(s,χ)) → (Connection between primes and zeros)
nodes.description: Using −L'/L(s,χ) = Σ Λ(n)χ(n)n^{−s} to connect primes to L-functions.

nodes.name: furstenberg_correspondence_principle
nodes.description: Any set of integers with positive upper density corresponds to a set in an ergodic system, translating combinatorial problems to dynamics.

nodes.name: furstenberg_szemeredi
nodes.description: Ergodic-theoretic proof that sets of positive upper density contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions (Szemerédi's theorem)

nodes.name: mixing_transformation
nodes.description: A measure-preserving T where μ(A ∩ T⁻ⁿB) → μ(A)μ(B); stronger than ergodicity.

nodes.name: upper_density
nodes.description: The upper density d*(A) = lim sup.

nodes.name: ribets_theorem
nodes.description: The Frey curve (if it exists) is not modular; proved by Ribet, reducing FLT to the modularity conjecture.

nodes.name: taniyama_shimura_conjecture
nodes.description: Every elliptic curve over ℚ is modular (now the modularity theorem); the key conjecture linking FLT to modular forms.

nodes.name: hecke_algebra
nodes.description: The algebra T of Hecke operators acting on modular forms; the modular deformation ring.

nodes.name: r_equals_t
nodes.description: Wiles proved R = T (deformation ring equals Hecke algebra) for semistable curves, establishing modularity.

nodes.name: langlands_tunnell
nodes.description: The modularity of GL₂ Galois representations with solvable image, providing the base case for Wiles' induction.

nodes.name: contraction_mapping
nodes.description: A map T on a metric space with d(Tx,Ty) ≤ c·d(x,y) for some c < 1.

nodes.name: picard_iteration
nodes.function_signature: (Contraction map T, Initial x₀) → (Unique fixed point x*)
nodes.description: The iterative scheme x_{n+1} = T(x_n) converging to the unique fixed point of a contraction.

nodes.name: knaster_tarski
nodes.description: Every monotone function on a complete lattice has a least and greatest fixed point.

nodes.name: poincare_birkhoff
nodes.description: An area-preserving twist map of an annulus has at least two fixed points.

nodes.name: discharging_method
nodes.function_signature: (Planar graph G) → (Structural properties via charge redistribution)
nodes.description: Assigning charges to vertices/faces and redistributing to derive structural properties of minimal counterexamples.

nodes.name: unavoidable_set
nodes.description: A set of configurations such that every planar graph must contain at least one; combined with reducibility.

nodes.name: fundamental_theorem_of_algebra
nodes.description: Every non-constant polynomial with complex coefficients has at least one root in ℂ.

nodes.name: fta_topological_proof
nodes.description: Proof of FTA using the fact that a polynomial map ℂ → ℂ of degree n has topological degree n, hence is surjective.

nodes.name: fta_analytic_proof
nodes.description: Proof using Liouville's theorem: if p has no root, then 1/p is entire and bounded, hence constant.

nodes.name: splitting_of_polynomials
nodes.description: Over ℂ, every degree-n polynomial factors completely as c(z−α₁)⋯(z−αₙ)

nodes.name: fta_algebraic_proof
nodes.description: Proof using Galois theory and the fact that ℝ has no odd-degree extensions, plus every element of ℂ has a square root.

nodes.name: euclids_lemma
nodes.description: If a prime p divides ab then p divides a or p divides b; the key step for uniqueness.

nodes.name: bezouts_identity
nodes.description: For integers a,b, there exist x,y with ax + by = gcd(a,b)

nodes.name: formal_system
nodes.description: A system of axioms and inference rules for deriving theorems in a formal language.

nodes.name: goedel_numbering
nodes.description: An encoding of formulas and proofs as natural numbers, allowing self-reference within arithmetic.

nodes.name: omega_consistency
nodes.description: A stronger condition than consistency: the system does not prove ∃x¬P(x) while proving P(0), P(1), P(2),….

nodes.name: rossers_theorem
nodes.description: Strengthening of Gödel's first theorem: simple consistency (not ω-consistency) suffices.

nodes.name: diagonalization_in_arithmetic
nodes.function_signature: (Formal system F) → (Self-referential sentence G unprovable in F)
nodes.description: Constructing a sentence G that asserts "G is not provable," the self-referential heart of Gödel's proof.

nodes.name: primitive_recursive_function
nodes.description: A function computable by bounded recursion; the provability predicate is primitive recursive.

nodes.name: representability
nodes.description: A formal system S represents a function f if for each n, S proves f(n̄) = f(n)̄; ensures arithmetic encodes its own proof theory.

nodes.name: consistency_statement
nodes.description: The arithmetic sentence Con(S) formalizing "S does not prove 0=1".

nodes.name: bass_guivarch_formula
nodes.description: For a finitely generated nilpotent group, the degree of polynomial growth is Σ i·rank(Gᵢ/Gᵢ₊₁)

nodes.name: montgomery_zippin
nodes.description: A locally compact group that is a topological manifold is a Lie group; used in Gromov's proof.

nodes.name: vanishing_ideal
nodes.description: The ideal I(V) of all polynomials vanishing on a variety V.

nodes.name: weak_nullstellensatz
nodes.description: If I is a proper ideal in k[x₁,…,xₙ] (k algebraically closed), then V(I) ≠ ∅.

nodes.name: strong_nullstellensatz
nodes.description: I(V(J)) = √J for any ideal J in k[x₁,…,xₙ] (k algebraically closed); a polynomial vanishing on V(J) has a power in J.

nodes.name: radical_ideal
nodes.description: The radical √I = {f : fⁿ ∈ I for some n}; the Nullstellensatz says vanishing ideals are always radical.

nodes.name: rabinowitsch_trick
nodes.function_signature: (Strong Nullstellensatz statement) → (Reduction to weak Nullstellensatz)
nodes.description: Introducing a new variable to reduce the strong Nullstellensatz to the weak form: if fg = 0 on V(I) use I + (1−yg)

nodes.name: zariski_correspondence
nodes.description: The bijection between radical ideals in k[x₁,…,xₙ] and algebraic subsets of kⁿ via V and I.

nodes.name: maximal_ideals_are_points
nodes.description: Under the Nullstellensatz, the maximal ideals of k[x₁,…,xₙ] are exactly (x₁−a₁,…,xₙ−aₙ) for (a₁,…,aₙ) ∈ kⁿ.

nodes.name: zfc_axioms
nodes.description: Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory with the Axiom of Choice; the standard axioms of set theory.

nodes.name: goedel_constructibility
nodes.description: GCH holds in L; hence if ZFC is consistent, so is ZFC + GCH.

nodes.name: generic_filter
nodes.description: A filter meeting all dense sets in a partial order; the object adjoined in forcing constructions.

nodes.name: cohen_independence_of_ch
nodes.description: CH is independent of ZFC: Cohen constructed a model where CH fails by adding ℵ₂ many reals via forcing.

nodes.name: partial_order_for_forcing
nodes.description: A poset (P,≤) whose conditions approximate the generic object; the structure driving a forcing extension.

nodes.name: boolean_valued_models
nodes.description: An alternative formulation of forcing using complete Boolean algebras instead of partial orders.

nodes.name: large_cardinal_axioms
nodes.description: Axioms asserting the existence of very large infinite cardinals; often interact with CH and forcing.

nodes.name: am_gm_inequality
nodes.description: The arithmetic mean is at least the geometric mean: (Σaᵢ)/n ≥ (∏aᵢ)^{1/n} for non-negative reals.

nodes.name: holders_inequality
nodes.description: ‖fg‖₁ ≤ ‖f‖_p ‖g‖_q for 1/p + 1/q = 1; generalizes Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: minkowskis_inequality
nodes.description: ‖f+g‖_p ≤ ‖f‖_p + ‖g‖_p for p ≥ 1; the triangle inequality for Lᵖ spaces.

nodes.name: jensens_inequality
nodes.description: For a convex function φ, φ(E[X]) ≤ E[φ(X)]; underlies AM-GM and many other inequalities.

nodes.name: gronwalls_inequality
nodes.description: If u'(t) ≤ β(t)u(t), then u(t) ≤ u(0)exp(∫β); key for uniqueness and stability in ODEs.

nodes.name: schur_inequality
nodes.description: For non-negative reals and t > 0: xᵗ(x−y)(x−z) + yᵗ(y−x)(y−z) + zᵗ(z−x)(z−y) ≥ 0.

nodes.name: poincare_inequality
nodes.description: ‖f − f̄‖_{L²} ≤ C‖∇f‖_{L²} on a bounded domain; controls oscillation by gradient.

nodes.name: halting_problem
nodes.description: The problem of determining whether a given Turing machine halts on a given input.

nodes.name: diagonalization_argument
nodes.function_signature: (Hypothetical halting decider) → (Contradiction)
nodes.description: Assuming a halting decider exists leads to a contradiction by constructing a machine that does the opposite of what is predicted.

nodes.name: decidable_set
nodes.description: A set (language) for which there is a Turing machine that always halts and correctly accepts/rejects.

nodes.name: computably_enumerable_set
nodes.description: A set for which there is a Turing machine that halts and accepts exactly the elements of the set (may not halt on non-elements)

nodes.name: rices_theorem
nodes.description: Every non-trivial semantic property of programs (partial functions) is undecidable.

nodes.name: reduction_between_problems
nodes.function_signature: (Undecidable problem A) → (Undecidability of problem B)
nodes.description: Showing problem A is undecidable by constructing a computable transformation taking instances of the halting problem to instances of A.

nodes.name: halting_not_co_ce
nodes.description: The complement of the halting set is not computably enumerable; the halting set is c.e. but not decidable.

nodes.name: polynomial_equation_by_radicals
nodes.description: Expressing the roots of a polynomial using only +, −, ×, ÷ and nth roots applied to the coefficients.

nodes.name: galois_criterion
nodes.description: A polynomial is solvable by radicals if and only if its Galois group is a solvable group.

nodes.name: sn_not_solvable
nodes.description: The symmetric group S_n is not solvable for n ≥ 5 because A_n is simple and non-abelian.

nodes.name: quadratic_cubic_quartic_formulas
nodes.description: Polynomials of degree 2, 3, 4 are solvable by radicals because S₂, S₃, S₄ are solvable groups.

nodes.name: transcendental_number
nodes.description: A complex number that is not algebraic; e.g., e and π.

nodes.name: liouville_number
nodes.description: A real number with extraordinarily good rational approximations; specifically, for each n there exist p,q with.

nodes.name: liouville_transcendence
nodes.description: Liouville numbers are transcendental, providing the first explicit examples of transcendental numbers.

nodes.name: irrationality_measure
nodes.description: The infimum μ of exponents w such that.

nodes.name: thue_siegel_method
nodes.function_signature: (Algebraic number α, Approximation p/q) → (Lower bound on |α-p/q|)
nodes.description: A method using auxiliary polynomials and the pigeonhole principle, refined through Thue, Siegel, and Roth.

nodes.name: lattice_in_lie_group
nodes.description: A discrete subgroup Γ of a Lie group G with finite covolume G/Γ.

nodes.name: margulis_superrigidity
nodes.description: For lattices in higher-rank semisimple groups, homomorphisms to algebraic groups extend to the ambient group; generalizes Mostow.

nodes.name: no_rigidity_in_dimension_2
nodes.description: Closed surfaces of genus g ≥ 2 have a (6g−6)-dimensional moduli space of hyperbolic metrics; rigidity fails in dimension 2.

nodes.name: complexity_class_p
nodes.description: The class of decision problems solvable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.

nodes.name: complexity_class_np
nodes.description: The class of decision problems for which a YES answer has a polynomial-time verifiable certificate.

nodes.name: p_vs_np_problem
nodes.description: The open question of whether P = NP; one of the Clay Millennium Problems.

nodes.name: boolean_satisfiability
nodes.description: The problem of determining whether a Boolean formula in CNF has a satisfying assignment.

nodes.name: np_hard
nodes.description: A problem to which every NP problem reduces in polynomial time (may or may not be in NP)

nodes.name: co_np
nodes.description: The class of problems whose complement is in NP; if P ≠ NP then NP ≠ co-NP.

nodes.name: ladners_theorem
nodes.description: If P ≠ NP then there exist NP-intermediate problems (in NP but neither in P nor NP-complete)

nodes.name: three_sat
nodes.description: The satisfiability problem restricted to clauses of size 3; still NP-complete.

nodes.name: traveling_salesman_problem
nodes.description: Given cities and distances, find the shortest tour visiting all cities; NP-hard optimization problem.

nodes.name: graph_isomorphism
nodes.description: Determining whether two graphs are isomorphic; in NP, not known to be NP-complete or in P.

nodes.name: poincare_conjecture_statement
nodes.description: Every simply connected closed 3-manifold is homeomorphic to S³.

nodes.name: poincare_conjecture
nodes.description: Perelman's proof (2003) that every simply connected closed 3-manifold is homeomorphic to S³, via Ricci flow.

nodes.name: hamiltons_program
nodes.function_signature: (Riemannian 3-manifold) → (Geometric decomposition via Ricci flow)
nodes.description: Hamilton's strategy of using Ricci flow to deform a 3-manifold metric toward constant curvature.

nodes.name: perelman_geometrization
nodes.description: Perelman proved the full Thurston geometrization conjecture using Ricci flow with surgery.

nodes.name: neckpinch_singularity
nodes.description: A singularity in Ricci flow where the manifold develops a long thin neck approaching a cylinder.

nodes.name: freedman_4d_poincare
nodes.description: The topological Poincaré conjecture in dimension 4, proved by Freedman (1982)

nodes.name: non_trivial_zeros
nodes.description: The zeros of ζ(s) in the critical strip, as opposed to the trivial zeros at s = −2, −4, −6, ….

nodes.name: logarithmic_integral
nodes.description: Li(x) = ∫₂ˣ dt/ln(t); the better approximation to π(x) in the PNT.

nodes.name: goldbach_conjecture
nodes.description: Every even integer greater than 2 is the sum of two primes (unproven)

nodes.name: schnirelmann_density
nodes.description: The density σ(A) = inf_{n≥1} A(n)/n of a set A of non-negative integers, where A(n) =.

nodes.name: sumset
nodes.description: The sumset A + B = {a + b : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} of two sets of integers.

nodes.name: freimans_theorem
nodes.description: A finite set A with.

nodes.name: szemeredis_theorem
nodes.description: Every subset of ℤ with positive upper density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.

nodes.name: goldbach_weak_conjecture
nodes.description: Every odd integer greater than 5 is the sum of three primes; proved by Helfgott (2013)

nodes.name: conductor_of_abelian_extension
nodes.description: The modulus measuring the ramification of an abelian extension; determines which primes ramify.

nodes.name: langlands_program
nodes.description: A vast generalization of class field theory to non-abelian extensions, relating automorphic forms to Galois representations.

nodes.name: mordell_conjecture_statement
nodes.description: A curve of genus ≥ 2 over a number field has only finitely many rational points (conjecture)

nodes.name: chabauty_method
nodes.function_signature: (Curve C/ℚ with rank < genus) → (Finite set of rational points)
nodes.description: A p-adic method for determining rational points on curves of genus g when the Mordell-Weil rank is less than g.

nodes.name: heights_in_number_theory
nodes.function_signature: (Rational point on variety) → (Arithmetic complexity measure)
