nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} (ω(n) − log log x)² = O(x log log x), giving the variance bound that implies the Hardy–Ramanujan normal order result.

nodes.name: Legendre sieve formula
nodes.description: S(A,z) = ∑_{d|P(z)} μ(d)|A_d|, the inclusion-exclusion identity counting elements of A not divisible by primes below z, where P(z) = ∏_{p<z} p.

nodes.name: Twin prime sieve estimate
nodes.description: |{n ≤ x : n and n+2 both prime}| ≪ x/(log x)² by Selberg's or Brun's sieve, consistent with the Hardy–Littlewood conjecture up to the constant.

nodes.name: Additive character mod q
nodes.description: The function e_q(a) = e^{2πia/q} for a ∈ ℤ/qℤ, forming the character group of (ℤ/qℤ, +).

nodes.name: Orthogonality of additive characters
nodes.description: ∑_{a=0}^{q−1} e_q(na) = q if q|n and 0 otherwise, the discrete Fourier orthogonality for ℤ/qℤ.

nodes.name: Truncated Perron formula
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} aₙ = (1/2πi) ∫_{c−iT}^{c+iT} F(s)xˢ/s ds + O(xᶜ/(T·min(1,‖x‖))), the effective version of Perron's formula with explicit error from truncation.

nodes.name: Cesàro summability and Riesz means
nodes.description: The Riesz mean of order δ of a Dirichlet series: (1/Γ(δ+1)) ∑_{n≤x} aₙ(1−n/x)^δ, a smoothed partial sum that improves convergence properties.

nodes.name: Landau's formula for Dirichlet series coefficients
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} aₙ = (1/2πi) ∮ F(s)xˢ/s ds with the sum over residues giving the main terms, relating singularities of F(s) to the average behavior of aₙ.

nodes.name: 3-4-1 trigonometric inequality
nodes.description: 3 + 4cos θ + cos 2θ ≥ 0 for all real θ, the key inequality used to prove ζ(1+it) ≠ 0 via |ζ(σ)³ ζ(σ+it)⁴ ζ(σ+2it)| ≥ 1.

nodes.name: y-smooth integer (friable number)
nodes.description: A positive integer n is y-smooth if all its prime factors satisfy p ≤ y; Ψ(x,y) = |{n ≤ x : P⁺(n) ≤ y}| counts them.

nodes.name: Dickman rho function ρ(u)
nodes.description: The continuous function satisfying ρ(u) = 1 for 0 ≤ u ≤ 1 and uρ′(u) = −ρ(u−1) for u > 1, governing the density of smooth numbers: Ψ(x, x^{1/u}) ∼ ρ(u)x.

nodes.name: Smooth number asymptotic (de Bruijn / Hildebrand–Tenenbaum)
nodes.description: Ψ(x,y) ∼ xρ(u) uniformly for u = log x/log y in a wide range, with Hildebrand's refinement extending this to exp((log y)^{3/5−ε}) ≤ y ≤ x.

nodes.name: Buchstab function ω(u)
nodes.description: The continuous function with ω(u) = 1/u for 1 ≤ u ≤ 2 and (uω(u))′ = ω(u−1) for u > 2, arising in the Buchstab identity for Φ(x,y) = |{n ≤ x : P⁻(n) > y}|.

nodes.name: Primes in short intervals
nodes.description: π(x+h) − π(x) ∼ h/log x for h = x^θ with θ > 7/12 (Huxley), showing primes exist in intervals [x, x + x^θ].

nodes.name: Sathe–Selberg theorem on integers with k prime factors
nodes.description: |{n ≤ x : ω(n) = k}| ∼ (x/log x)(log log x)^{k−1}/((k−1)!) uniformly for 1 ≤ k ≤ (2−ε)log log x.

nodes.name: Beurling generalized primes
nodes.description: A sequence 1 < p₁ ≤ p₂ ≤ ⋯ of reals (generalized primes) generating by multiplicative closure a set of generalized integers; the framework for studying PNT-type results axiomatically.

nodes.name: Beurling PNT for generalized primes
nodes.description: If N(x) = Ax + O(x/(log x)^γ) with γ > 3/2 for the counting function of Beurling integers, then π_P(x) ∼ x/log x.

nodes.name: Induced Dirichlet character
nodes.description: Given χ a character mod q and q|Q, the character χ* mod Q defined by χ*(n) = χ(n) if gcd(n,Q) = 1 and 0 otherwise; every character is induced from a unique primitive character.

nodes.name: Quadratic Dirichlet character
nodes.description: A real-valued Dirichlet character of order 2, given by the Kronecker symbol χ_D(n) = (D/n) for a fundamental discriminant D.

nodes.name: Riemann hypothesis
nodes.description: All nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2; equivalently ψ(x) = x + O(x^{1/2+ε}) for every ε > 0.

nodes.name: Generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH)
nodes.description: All nontrivial zeros of every Dirichlet L-function L(s,χ) lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2.

nodes.name: Hadamard product for ξ(s)
nodes.description: ξ(s) = ξ(0) ∏_ρ (1 − s/ρ), the product over nontrivial zeros ρ of ζ(s), obtained by applying the Hadamard factorization theorem to the entire function ξ(s) of order 1.

nodes.name: Zero-counting function N(T)
nodes.description: N(T) = |{ρ : ζ(ρ) = 0, 0 < Im(ρ) ≤ T}| = (T/2π)log(T/2πe) + O(log T), counting nontrivial zeros of ζ up to height T.

nodes.name: Classical zero-free region for L-functions
nodes.description: L(s,χ) ≠ 0 for σ > 1 − c/log(q(|t|+2)) with at most one exceptional real zero for real χ, extending de la Vallée Poussin's region to Dirichlet L-functions.

nodes.name: Siegel's theorem on L(1,χ)
nodes.description: For every ε > 0 there exists c(ε) > 0 (ineffective) such that L(1,χ) > c(ε)q^{−ε} for real primitive χ mod q, ruling out Siegel zeros in an ineffective sense.

nodes.name: Page's theorem
nodes.description: Among all real primitive characters χ mod q with q ≤ Q, at most one L(s,χ) can have a real zero β > 1 − c/log Q, and that exceptional modulus q₁ satisfies q₁ > Q^δ for some δ > 0.

nodes.name: Prime number theorem for arithmetic progressions
nodes.description: π(x;q,a) ∼ Li(x)/φ(q) for fixed q with gcd(a,q) = 1, with an error term depending on the zero-free region for L-functions mod q.

nodes.name: Siegel–Walfisz theorem
nodes.description: For any A > 0, ψ(x;q,a) = x/φ(q) + O(x exp(−c√(log x))) uniformly for q ≤ (log x)^A with gcd(a,q) = 1, using Siegel's ineffective zero-free region.

nodes.name: Vaughan's identity
nodes.description: Decomposes Λ(n) into Type I and Type II sums via Λ = μ_{≤U} ∗ log + μ_{≤U} ∗ Λ_{>V} ∗ 1 + remainder, enabling bilinear sum estimates in the Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem and other applications.

nodes.name: Explicit formula for ψ(x;q,a)
nodes.description: ψ(x;q,a) = x/φ(q) − (1/φ(q)) ∑_χ ∑_ρ x^ρ/ρ + lower order terms, where ρ runs over nontrivial zeros of L(s,χ) for all χ mod q.

nodes.name: Weil's explicit formula
nodes.description: ∑_ρ h(ρ) = h(1) + h(0) − ∑_p ∑_k (log p / p^{k/2}) ĝ(k log p) + integral terms, relating a test function h evaluated at zeros of ζ to sums over primes.

nodes.name: Guinand–Weil explicit formula
nodes.description: A distributional identity ∑_ρ ĥ(γ_ρ) = ĥ(i/2) + ĥ(−i/2) − ∑_p log p ∑_k p^{−k/2}(h(k log p) + h(−k log p)) + integral terms, the symmetric form of Weil's explicit formula.

nodes.name: Von Koch's theorem: RH implies sharp prime counting
nodes.description: Under RH, π(x) = Li(x) + O(√x log x), equivalently ψ(x) = x + O(x^{1/2} log²x), the best possible error term up to logarithmic factors.

nodes.name: RH implies sharp error in arithmetic progressions
nodes.description: Under GRH, ψ(x;q,a) = x/φ(q) + O(x^{1/2} log²x) uniformly in q, giving the conditional analogue of von Koch's theorem for primes in AP.

nodes.name: Lindelöf hypothesis
nodes.description: ζ(1/2 + it) = O(|t|^ε) for every ε > 0, equivalent to μ(1/2) = 0 where μ(σ) is the infimum of exponents bounding |ζ(σ+it)|; implied by RH.

nodes.name: Conditional bounds on ζ(s) under RH
nodes.description: Under RH, |ζ(σ+it)| ≪ |t|^{(1−σ)/2+ε} for σ ≥ 1/2 and log|ζ(1/2+it)| ≪ log t/log log t, improving the unconditional convexity bound.

nodes.name: Conditional estimate for M(x) under RH
nodes.description: Under RH, M(x) = ∑_{n≤x} μ(n) = O(x^{1/2+ε}) for every ε > 0, the best conditional bound on the Mertens function.

nodes.name: Conditional bounds on gaps between primes under RH
nodes.description: Under RH, p_{n+1} − p_n ≪ √p_n log p_n, showing that consecutive prime gaps are O(√p log p).

nodes.name: Conditional estimate for π(x;q,a) with large q under GRH
nodes.description: Under GRH, π(x;q,a) = Li(x)/φ(q) + O(√x log x) for q ≤ x, effective for much larger moduli than unconditional results.

nodes.name: Zero density estimate N(σ,T)
nodes.description: N(σ,T) = |{ρ = β+iγ : L(ρ,χ) = 0, β ≥ σ, |γ| ≤ T}| ≪ T^{A(σ)(1−σ)+ε} for σ > 1/2, bounding zeros of L-functions away from the critical line.

nodes.name: Ingham density estimate
nodes.description: N(σ,T) ≪ T^{3(1−σ)/(2−σ)+ε} for 1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1, Ingham's classical zero density estimate for the Riemann zeta function.

nodes.name: Hardy's theorem on zeros on the critical line
nodes.description: ζ(s) has infinitely many zeros on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2 (Hardy, 1914).

nodes.name: Positive proportion of zeros on the critical line
nodes.description: At least 41.05% of nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) lie on the critical line (Conrey, 1989), improving Selberg's result that a positive proportion do.

nodes.name: Density hypothesis
nodes.description: N(σ,T) ≪ T^{2(1−σ)+ε} for σ ≥ 1/2, a conjecture on the optimal exponent in zero density estimates, weaker than RH but sufficient for many applications.

nodes.name: Landau's oscillation theorem
nodes.description: If a Dirichlet series F(s) = ∑ aₙ/nˢ (aₙ real) has a singularity on the real axis at its abscissa of convergence σ_c, then ∑_{n≤x} aₙ oscillates in sign.

nodes.name: Ω₊/Ω₋ notation for oscillation
nodes.description: f(x) = Ω₊(g(x)) means lim sup f(x)/g(x) > 0; f(x) = Ω₋(g(x)) means lim inf f(x)/g(x) < 0; f(x) = Ω±(g(x)) means both hold.

nodes.name: Littlewood's omega theorem for π(x) − Li(x)
nodes.description: π(x) − Li(x) = Ω±(√x log log log x / log x), proving that Li(x) is not always an overestimate of π(x), despite being so for all computationally accessible x.

nodes.name: Oscillation of ψ(x) − x
nodes.description: ψ(x) − x = Ω±(√x), i.e. ψ(x) − x changes sign infinitely often and achieves magnitude at least c√x for some c > 0.

nodes.name: Omega result for M(x)
nodes.description: M(x) = Ω±(x^{1/2}), the Mertens function oscillates with amplitude at least c√x infinitely often.

nodes.name: Ingham's theorem on omega results from zeros
nodes.description: A general method producing Ω-results for summatory functions from knowledge of zeros of the associated Dirichlet series on the critical line.

nodes.name: Skewes number and sign changes of π(x) − Li(x)
nodes.description: The first x where π(x) > Li(x) exists (Littlewood); Skewes gave the first explicit upper bound, later improved to around e^{727.95} unconditionally.

nodes.name: Riemann–Stieltjes integral
nodes.description: ∫ₐᵇ f dα = lim ∑ f(tₖ)(α(xₖ) − α(xₖ₋₁)), generalizing the Riemann integral by integrating against a monotone or BV function α.

nodes.name: Integration by parts for Stieltjes integrals
nodes.description: ∫ₐᵇ f dα = fα|ₐᵇ − ∫ₐᵇ α df, the analogue of integration by parts for Riemann–Stieltjes integrals, fundamental for partial summation.

nodes.name: Values of ζ(s) at positive even integers
Weierstrass product for 1/Γ(z)
nodes.description: 1/Γ(z) = ze^{γz} ∏_{n=1}^∞ (1 + z/n)e^{−z/n}, the infinite product representation showing 1/Γ is entire of order 1.

nodes.name: Theta function (number-theoretic)
nodes.description: ϑ(t) = ∑_{n=−∞}^{∞} e^{−πn²t} for t > 0, equal to θ₃(0, e^{−πt}) in Jacobi notation, central to the proof of the functional equation of ζ(s).

nodes.name: Theta function transformation formula
nodes.description: ϑ(1/t) = √t · ϑ(t) for t > 0, a consequence of Poisson summation, used to derive the functional equation of the Riemann zeta function.

nodes.name: Rankin's trick
nodes.description: Bounding a counting function ∑_{n≤x} aₙ by (x/y)^δ ∑_{n≤y} aₙ(n/y)^{−δ} for a free parameter δ > 0, converting a sharp cutoff into a smooth weight.

nodes.name: Dirichlet's divisor problem
nodes.description: Determine the infimum α such that ∑_{n≤x} d(n) = x log x + (2γ−1)x + O(x^α); conjectured α = 1/4, best known α ≈ 0.314 (Kolesnik, Huxley).

nodes.name: Selberg class
nodes.description: An axiomatic class S of Dirichlet series satisfying: (i) analytic continuation, (ii) Ramanujan bound on coefficients, (iii) functional equation, (iv) Euler product; conjectured to coincide with automorphic L-functions.

nodes.name: Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free region
nodes.description: ζ(σ+it) ≠ 0 for σ > 1 − c/(log|t|)^{2/3}(log log|t|)^{1/3}, a wider zero-free region than de la Vallée Poussin's, obtained via exponential sum estimates.

nodes.name: Mertens conjecture (disproved)
nodes.description: |M(x)| < √x for all x > 1 was conjectured by Mertens; disproved by Odlyzko and te Riele (1985) using computations of zeros of ζ(s).

nodes.name: Twin prime conjecture
nodes.description: There are infinitely many primes p such that p+2 is also prime; unproven, though Zhang (2013) proved bounded gaps between primes.

nodes.name: Hardy–Littlewood twin prime conjecture
nodes.description: |{p ≤ x : p+2 prime}| ∼ 2C₂ x/(log x)² where C₂ = ∏_{p≥3}(1−1/(p−1)²) ≈ 0.6602 is the twin prime constant.

nodes.name: Dirichlet series for the Liouville function
nodes.description: ∑_{n=1}^∞ λ(n)/nˢ = ζ(2s)/ζ(s) for Re(s) > 1, expressing the Dirichlet series of Liouville's function via zeta.

nodes.name: Ramanujan's sum formula for σ_s(n)
nodes.description: σ_s(n)/n^s = ζ(s+1) ∑_{q=1}^∞ c_q(n)/q^{s+1}, expressing the divisor function as an absolutely convergent series of Ramanujan sums.

nodes.name: Vinogradov–Korobov error term in PNT
nodes.description: ψ(x) = x + O(x exp(−c(log x)^{3/5}(log log x)^{−1/5})), the best known unconditional error term in the PNT.

nodes.name: Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture
nodes.description: The pair correlation of normalized spacings of nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) follows 1 − (sin πu/(πu))² (GUE statistics), connecting zeros of zeta to random matrix theory.

nodes.name: Explicit formula with general test function
nodes.description: A general identity ∑_ρ h(ρ) = δ + ∫ h·K − ∑_p ∑_k g(k log p) log p / p^{k/2} for suitable test functions h with Fourier transform g, unifying various explicit formulas.

nodes.name: Halász's theorem
nodes.description: For multiplicative f with |f(n)| ≤ 1, (1/x)∑_{n≤x} f(n) = O(exp(−c min_|t|≤T ∑_{p≤x}(1−Re f(p)p^{−it})/p)) + O(1/T), characterizing when mean values of multiplicative functions are small.

nodes.name: Generalized von Mangoldt function Λ_k
nodes.description: Λ_k = μ ∗ log^k, the k-fold Dirichlet convolution giving Λ₁ = Λ and Λ_k(n) supported on integers with at most k prime factors; −ζ^(k)(s)/ζ(s) = ∑ Λ_k(n)/nˢ.

nodes.name: Grand Riemann hypothesis
nodes.description: All nontrivial zeros of all automorphic L-functions lie on Re(s) = 1/2, the strongest form of RH encompassing Dedekind zeta, Artin L-functions, and all automorphic L-functions.

nodes.name: Effective vs ineffective constants
nodes.description: A constant is effective if it can in principle be computed; ineffective if its existence is proved indirectly (e.g., via Siegel's theorem). The distinction is central to the gap between Siegel–Walfisz and Bombieri–Vinogradov.

nodes.name: Riemann–Stieltjes partial summation technique
nodes.description: Converting ∑_{n≤x} f(n)g(n) into ∫₁ˣ g(t) dA(t) where A(t) = ∑_{n≤t} f(n), then integrating by parts to separate smooth and arithmetic parts.

nodes.name: Dirichlet series multiplication theorem
nodes.description: If F(s) = ∑ f(n)/nˢ and G(s) = ∑ g(n)/nˢ converge absolutely, then F(s)G(s) = ∑ (f∗g)(n)/nˢ where f∗g is the Dirichlet convolution.

nodes.name: Explicit zero-free region constant improvements
nodes.description: Numerical improvements to the classical zero-free region σ > 1 − 1/(R log t) for ζ(s), with the best explicit R values due to Ford, Kadiri, and others.

nodes.name: Completely additive function
nodes.description: An arithmetic function f satisfying f(mn) = f(m) + f(n) for all m, n ≥ 1; equivalently f(p^a) = a·f(p), e.g. Ω(n) and log n.

nodes.name: Generalized divisor function τ_k(n)
nodes.description: τ_k(n) = ∑_{n=n₁⋯nₖ} 1, the number of ordered k-fold factorizations of n; its Dirichlet series is ζ(s)^k.

nodes.name: Selberg–Delange method
nodes.function_signature: (Dirichlet series behaving like ζ(s)^z near s=1) → (asymptotic ∑_{n≤x} a_n ~ Cx(log x)^{z-1}/Γ(z))
nodes.description: Obtains asymptotics for partial sums of Dirichlet series behaving like ζ(s)^z near s = 1 via contour integration around a Hankel contour.

nodes.name: Smoothed Perron formula
nodes.description: A variant of Perron's formula using a smooth weight function to replace the sharp cutoff, yielding faster-decaying error terms via rapid decay of the Mellin transform of the weight.

nodes.name: Dyadic decomposition
nodes.function_signature: (sum over [1,X]) → (O(log X) sums over dyadic blocks (N, 2N])
nodes.description: Partitioning a sum over [1, X] into O(log X) blocks of the form (N, 2N], reducing estimates to those uniform in a parameter N.

nodes.name: Smooth partition of unity
nodes.function_signature: (sharp cutoff) → (sum of smooth bumps with ∑ψ_j ≡ 1)
nodes.description: A collection of smooth bump functions {ψ_j} with ∑_j ψ_j ≡ 1, used to decompose sums into pieces with controlled Mellin or Fourier transforms.

nodes.name: Heath-Brown's identity
nodes.function_signature: (Λ(n) for n ≤ x) → (O(k²) multilinear Type I/II sums)
nodes.description: Decomposes the von Mangoldt function into O(k) multilinear sums using k-fold applications of an identity involving μ and log, yielding flexible Type I and Type II sums.

nodes.name: Linnik's identity
nodes.function_signature: (Λ(n)) → (alternating series of higher-order convolutions)
nodes.description: Expresses Λ(n) as Λ = ∑_{k≥1} (−1)^{k−1}/k · (1∗⋯∗1 − ε)^{∗k} · log, converting prime sums into iterated convolution sums.

nodes.name: Type I sum
nodes.description: A sum of the form ∑_{m≤M} a_m ∑_{n: mn∈A} 1 where a_m are general coefficients and the inner sum is over a well-understood sequence.

nodes.name: Type II sum
nodes.description: A bilinear sum ∑_m ∑_n a_m b_n c(mn) where both variables carry nontrivial coefficients, requiring Cauchy–Schwarz or bilinear form techniques.

nodes.name: Wirsing's theorem
nodes.description: For nonnegative multiplicative f with ∑_p f(p)/p ~ κ log log x, gives ∑_{n≤x} f(n) ~ Ce^{-γκ}/Γ(κ) · x(log x)^{κ-1} ∏_p(1+f(p)/p+⋯)(1-1/p)^κ.

nodes.name: Shiu's bound
nodes.description: For multiplicative f with 0 ≤ f(n) ≤ τ(n)^A, gives ∑_{x<n≤x+y, n≡a(q)} f(n) ≪ (y/φ(q))exp(∑_{p≤x} f(p)/p) for y ≥ x^{1/2+ε}.

nodes.name: General L-function (Iwaniec–Kowalski framework)
nodes.description: An L-function satisfying: Euler product of degree d, analytic continuation, functional equation Λ(s) = εΛ̄(1−s) with gamma factors, and the Ramanujan bound |a(p)| ≤ d.

nodes.name: Completed L-function
nodes.description: Λ(s, π) = q^{s/2} ∏_j Γ_ℝ(s + μ_j) · L(s, π) incorporating conductor q and gamma factors, satisfying Λ(s) = ε Λ̄(1−s).

nodes.name: Root number
nodes.description: The complex number ε of absolute value 1 in the functional equation Λ(s) = εΛ̄(1−s); for self-dual L-functions ε = ±1, governing vanishing at the central point.

nodes.name: Gamma factors in functional equations
nodes.description: The archimedean part γ(s) = ∏_j Γ_ℝ(s + μ_j) of a completed L-function, where Γ_ℝ(s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2), encoding the archimedean local factors.

nodes.name: Conductor of an L-function
nodes.description: The positive integer q(π) in the functional equation measuring arithmetic ramification; equals ∏_p p^{f_p} with f_p the local conductor exponents.

nodes.name: Analytic conductor
nodes.description: C(π) = q(π)∏_j(|μ_j|+3), the quantity governing convexity bounds, zero-free regions, and approximate functional equations of an L-function.

nodes.name: Degree of an L-function
nodes.description: The number d of Γ_ℝ-factors in the completed L-function; equals n for GL(n) automorphic L-functions, governing the growth rate and density of zeros.

nodes.name: Convexity bound for L-functions
nodes.description: For an L-function of analytic conductor C, L(1/2+it) ≪ C(t)^{1/4+ε}, obtained from the Phragmén–Lindelöf principle applied to the functional equation.

nodes.name: Subconvexity bound
nodes.description: Any bound L(1/2, π) ≪ C(π)^{1/4−δ} for some δ > 0 breaking the convexity barrier; has applications to equidistribution and mass transfer.

nodes.name: Grand Lindelöf hypothesis
nodes.description: The conjecture that L(1/2+it, π) ≪ C(π, t)^ε for every ε > 0 and every automorphic L-function; generalizes the Lindelöf hypothesis.

nodes.name: Approximate functional equation
nodes.description: L(s) = ∑_{n≤x} a_n n^{−s} V(n/x) + ε(s)∑_{n≤y} ā_n n^{s−1} W(n/y) + remainder, expressing L(s) on the critical line as two finite sums of length ~√(q|t|).

nodes.name: Mean value theorem for Dirichlet polynomials
nodes.description: ∫_0^T |∑_{n≤N} a_n n^{−it}|² dt = (T + O(N))∑|a_n|², the Montgomery–Vaughan form equating the L² norm over t to the sum of squared coefficients.

nodes.name: Montgomery's mean value theorem for large values
nodes.description: Bounds the number R of well-spaced t-values where |∑ a_n n^{−it}| ≥ V: R ≪ (N+T)(∑|a_n|²)/V², controlling large values of Dirichlet polynomials.

nodes.name: Huxley–Jutila large values estimate
nodes.description: Refined bounds on the measure of t-values where a Dirichlet polynomial is large, improving Montgomery's estimate via mean-square and fourth-power moment methods.

nodes.name: Fourth moment of the Riemann zeta function
nodes.description: ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|⁴ dt ~ (2π²)⁻¹ T(log T)⁴, proved by Ingham (1926); the highest moment of ζ(1/2+it) for which an asymptotic is known.

nodes.name: Second moment of L-functions over characters
nodes.description: ∑_{χ mod q} |L(1/2, χ)|² ~ (φ(q)/q)·q log q, the mean-square for central values of Dirichlet L-functions averaged over characters mod q.

nodes.name: Moments of L-functions (conjectural asymptotics)
nodes.description: The conjecture that ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} dt ~ c_k T(log T)^{k²} with c_k predicted by random matrix theory (Keating–Snaith).

nodes.name: Hecke L-function
nodes.description: L(s, λ) = ∑_𝔞 λ(𝔞)N(𝔞)^{−s} attached to a Hecke Grössencharakter λ of a number field, admitting Euler product, analytic continuation, and functional equation.

nodes.name: Rankin–Selberg L-function
nodes.description: L(s, π × π') = ∏_p det(I − A_π(p) ⊗ A_{π'}(p) p^{−s})^{−1}, a degree-mn L-function for GL(m)×GL(n) forms with analytic continuation and functional equation.

nodes.name: Kronecker's limit formula
nodes.description: The Laurent expansion of the Epstein zeta function at s = 1 has constant term involving −π(γ + log 2 − log(√y|η(τ)|²)), connecting Eisenstein series to the Dedekind eta function.

nodes.name: Sifting function S(A, P, z)
nodes.description: S(A, P, z) = |{a ∈ A : gcd(a, P(z)) = 1}| where P(z) = ∏_{p<z, p∈P} p, counting elements not divisible by any sifting prime below z.

nodes.name: Sieve dimension
nodes.description: The parameter κ such that ∑_{w≤p<z} g(p)log p = κ log(z/w) + O(1), governing sifting prime density; κ = 1 for the linear sieve, κ = 1/2 for binary quadratic forms.

nodes.name: Buchstab's identity
nodes.description: S(A, P, z) = S(A, P, w) − ∑_{w≤p<z} S(A_p, P, p), recursively expressing the sifting function at level z in terms of lower levels.

nodes.name: Linear sieve (Iwaniec's formulation)
nodes.description: For sieve dimension κ = 1, S(A,P,z) = X·W(z){f(s)+O((log D)^{-1/3})} with s = log D/log z, where f and F solve the linear sieve differential-delay equations.

nodes.name: Sieve upper/lower bound functions F_κ(s), f_κ(s)
nodes.description: Continuous functions satisfying differential-delay equations giving best possible sieve bounds: f_κ(s)XV(z) ≤ S ≤ F_κ(s)XV(z) + remainder.

nodes.name: Rosser–Iwaniec sieve (β-sieve)
nodes.function_signature: (sifting function S(A,P,z), level D) → (optimal upper/lower bounds)
nodes.description: A combinatorial sieve using Rosser's alternating truncation combined with Iwaniec's bilinear remainder estimates, achieving optimal bounds for the linear sieve.

nodes.name: Parity problem in sieve theory
nodes.description: The obstruction that classical sieve methods cannot distinguish integers with even vs odd number of prime factors, preventing sieves from detecting primes in the main term.

nodes.name: Semilinear sieve (κ = 1/2)
nodes.function_signature: (sieve problem of dimension 1/2) → (upper/lower bounds without parity obstruction)
nodes.description: The sieve of dimension κ = 1/2, applicable to primes represented by binary quadratic forms; the lower bound becomes positive for s > 1.

nodes.name: Bombieri's asymptotic sieve
nodes.function_signature: (sifting function with strong remainder estimates) → (asymptotic formula for primes)
nodes.description: A sieve producing asymptotic formulas for sifting functions under strong equidistribution hypotheses, overcoming the parity problem.

nodes.name: Asymptotic sieve for primes (Bombieri–Friedlander–Iwaniec)
nodes.function_signature: (sequence A with bilinear remainder control) → (asymptotic for #{primes in A})
nodes.description: Combines Bombieri's asymptotic sieve with bilinear form estimates to produce asymptotic formulas for primes in sequences, circumventing the parity problem.

nodes.name: Level of distribution
nodes.description: The supremum ϑ such that ∑_{q≤x^ϑ-ε} max_{(a,q)=1} |A(x;q,a) − A(x)/φ(q)| ≪ A(x)/(log x)^B; the primes have ϑ = 1/2 by Bombieri–Vinogradov.

nodes.name: Well-factorable function
nodes.description: A function λ(d) is well-factorable of level D if for every D = D₁D₂ there exist λ₁, λ₂ with λ = λ₁∗λ₂, |λ_i| ≤ 1, and support at scale D_i; key to Iwaniec's bilinear sieve.

nodes.name: Switching principle in sieve theory
nodes.function_signature: (upper bound sieve result) → (lower bound for primes)
nodes.description: Reversing roles of sifted set and sifting primes via Buchstab decomposition, exploiting different distributional properties to convert upper into lower bounds.

nodes.name: Van der Corput's A-process
nodes.function_signature: (exponential sum with |f''| ≍ λ) → (bound O(Nλ^{1/2} + λ^{-1/2}))
nodes.description: The second derivative test: if f'' is monotone and |f''(x)| ≍ λ, then ∑ e(f(n)) ≪ Nλ^{1/2} + λ^{-1/2}.
aliases: van der Corput second derivative test

nodes.name: Van der Corput's B-process
nodes.function_signature: (exponential sum ∑ e(f(n))) → (dual sum via Poisson summation)
nodes.description: Transforms ∑ e(f(n)) into a dual sum via Poisson summation, converting information about f' into a shorter dual sum.

nodes.name: Method of exponent pairs
nodes.function_signature: (A- and B-processes iterated) → (family of admissible exponent pairs (k,ℓ))
nodes.description: A framework for bounding exponential sums by iterating A-process (k,ℓ)→(k/(2k+2),(k+ℓ+1)/(2k+2)) and B-process (k,ℓ)→(ℓ-1/2,k+1/2).

nodes.name: Exponent pair (k, ℓ)
nodes.description: A pair (k,ℓ) such that ∑_{n~N} e(f(n)) ≪ N^ℓ λ^k when |f^(j)| ≍ λ/N^j; the trivial pair is (0,1) and (1/2,1/2) from van der Corput.

nodes.name: Vinogradov's method of exponential sums
nodes.function_signature: (exponential sum with polynomial phase of degree k) → (bound via iterated Weyl differencing + Vinogradov mean value theorem)
nodes.description: Bounds exponential sums using iterated Weyl differencing followed by Hölder's inequality and mean value estimates, producing the Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free region.

nodes.name: Salié sum
nodes.description: S*(a,b;c) = ∑_{x mod c, (x,c)=1} (x/c)e((ax+bx̄)/c), the Kloosterman sum twisted by the Legendre symbol; evaluable in terms of Gauss sums when c is prime.

nodes.name: Hyper-Kloosterman sum
nodes.description: Kl_k(a;q) = ∑_{x₁⋯x_k ≡ a(q)} e((x₁+⋯+x_k)/q), the k-variable Kloosterman sum satisfying Deligne's bound |Kl_k(a;p)| ≤ k·p^{(k-1)/2}.

nodes.name: Stepanov's method
nodes.function_signature: (curve C/𝔽_q) → (bound |C(𝔽_q)| via auxiliary polynomial)
nodes.description: An elementary method bounding rational points on curves over finite fields by constructing an auxiliary polynomial vanishing to high order at each rational point.

nodes.name: Bombieri's proof of RH for curves
nodes.description: A simplified proof of the Riemann hypothesis for curves over finite fields using Stepanov's method and Riemann-Roch, avoiding Weil's algebraic geometry.

nodes.name: Square sieve (Heath-Brown)
nodes.function_signature: (sequence S) → (bound on #{n ∈ S : n = □} via character sums)
nodes.description: Detects perfect squares in sequences via n is a square iff (n/p) = 1 for all primes p, applying Legendre symbols and the large sieve.

nodes.name: Bombieri–Iwaniec method
nodes.function_signature: (exponential sum ∑ e(f(n))) → (improved bound via lattice point/large sieve)
nodes.description: Bounds exponential sums by converting to a lattice point counting problem near a curve, then applying the large sieve to detect coincidences; yields exponent pair (9/56, 1/2+9/56).

nodes.name: Duality principle for bilinear forms
nodes.description: The operator norm of a bilinear form equals its transpose norm; in the large sieve, interchanges the roles of the sequence and test points.

nodes.name: Dual large sieve inequality
nodes.description: ∑_n |∑_r b_r e(nα_r)|² ≤ (N + δ⁻¹)∑|b_r|² for δ-spaced α_r; the dual form of the large sieve.
aliases: dual form of the large sieve

nodes.name: Large sieve inequality for Dirichlet characters
nodes.description: ∑_{q≤Q} ∑*_{χ mod q} |∑_{n≤N} a_n χ(n)|² ≤ (N + Q² − 1)∑|a_n|², bounding mean squares of character sums over primitive characters.

nodes.name: Deshouillers–Iwaniec method
nodes.function_signature: (sums of Kloosterman sums) → (bounds via spectral theory + Kuznetsov formula)
nodes.description: Combines Kloosterman sum estimates, spectral theory, and the Kuznetsov trace formula to bound bilinear forms in Kloosterman sums.

nodes.name: Linnik's dispersion method
nodes.function_signature: (sum over arithmetic progression) → (variance estimate via Cauchy-Schwarz)
nodes.description: Estimates ∑_q(∑_{n≡a(q)} f(n) − main)² by expanding the square and exchanging summation, reducing to bilinear sums.

nodes.name: Halász–Montgomery inequality
nodes.description: For R well-spaced t_r: ∑_r |∑_n a_n n^{-it_r}|² ≤ (N + RT)(∑|a_n|²), a discrete mean value theorem for Dirichlet polynomials.

nodes.name: Motohashi's formula
nodes.description: An exact identity relating the fourth moment of ζ(1/2+it) to a spectral sum over Maass forms, expressing ∫|ζ|⁴ in terms of Hecke eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Gallagher's larger sieve
nodes.description: If S ⊂ [1,N] reduces to at most ν_p residue classes mod p for each p ∈ P, then |S| ≤ N(∑ log p)/(∑ ν_p log p/(p−ν_p+1)) − corrections.

nodes.name: Barban–Davenport–Halberstam theorem
nodes.description: ∑_{q≤Q} ∑_{(a,q)=1} |ψ(x;q,a) − x/φ(q)|² ≪ xQ log x for Q ≤ x, an L² average bound on PNT errors in arithmetic progressions.

nodes.name: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture
nodes.description: The conjecture that primes have level of distribution ϑ = 1 − ε; implies bounded gaps between primes by the Goldston–Pintz–Yıldırım method.

nodes.name: Modular group SL₂(ℤ)
nodes.description: The group of 2×2 integer matrices with determinant 1, acting on the upper half-plane by Möbius transformations; the fundamental discrete symmetry group of modular forms.

nodes.name: Congruence subgroup Γ₀(N)
nodes.description: The subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) consisting of matrices whose lower-left entry is divisible by N, the standard level structure for Hecke theory.

nodes.name: Congruence subgroup Γ₁(N)
nodes.description: The subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) with lower-left entry ≡ 0 mod N and diagonal entries ≡ 1 mod N, parametrizing modular forms with Nebentypus.

nodes.name: Principal congruence subgroup Γ(N)
nodes.description: The kernel of SL₂(ℤ) → SL₂(ℤ/Nℤ); a subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) is a congruence subgroup iff it contains some Γ(N).

nodes.name: Nebentypus character
nodes.description: A Dirichlet character χ mod N in the transformation law f(γz) = χ(d)(cz+d)^k f(z) for forms on Γ₁(N), refining the level structure.

nodes.name: Fundamental domain for SL₂(ℤ)
nodes.description: The region F = {z ∈ H : |Re(z)| ≤ 1/2, |z| ≥ 1} for the action of SL₂(ℤ) on H, with hyperbolic area π/3.

nodes.name: Cusps of a congruence subgroup
nodes.description: The Γ-equivalence classes in ℙ¹(ℚ) = ℚ ∪ {∞}, forming the boundary points where Γ\H is compactified to a Riemann surface.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic Laplacian on H
nodes.description: The Laplace-Beltrami operator Δ = −y²(∂²/∂x² + ∂²/∂y²) on the upper half-plane with Poincaré metric, commuting with SL₂(ℝ).

nodes.name: Cusp form
nodes.description: A modular form of weight k and level N that vanishes at all cusps, spanning the subspace S_k(Γ) ⊂ M_k(Γ).

nodes.name: Slash operator |_k
nodes.description: The weight-k right action (f|_k γ)(z) = (cz+d)^{-k} f(γz) of GL₂⁺(ℝ) on functions on H, encoding the modular transformation law.

nodes.name: Poincaré series P_m(z, k, Γ)
nodes.description: P_m(z) = ∑_{γ ∈ Γ_∞\Γ} e^{2πimγz}(cz+d)^{-k}, spanning cusp forms and satisfying ⟨f, P_m⟩ = c·a_f(m) for cusp forms f.

nodes.name: Petersson inner product
nodes.description: ⟨f,g⟩ = ∫_{Γ\H} f(z)ḡ(z) y^k dμ(z) on cusp forms, making S_k(Γ) a Hilbert space with Hecke operators self-adjoint.

nodes.name: Fourier expansion at cusps
nodes.description: The q-expansion f(z) = ∑_{n≥0} a_f(n)e^{2πinz/w} of a modular form at a cusp of width w; the expansion at each cusp determines the form.

nodes.name: Atkin-Lehner theory
nodes.description: S_k(Γ₀(N)) = S_k^{old} ⊕ S_k^{new} with multiplicity-one for newforms, decomposing cusp forms into oldforms from lower levels and primitive newforms.

nodes.name: Atkin-Lehner involution W_Q
nodes.description: For Q || N, an involution on S_k(Γ₀(N)) normalizing Γ₀(N); newforms are eigenforms for all W_Q with eigenvalue ±1.

nodes.name: Fricke involution W_N
nodes.description: The Atkin-Lehner involution z ↦ −1/(Nz) relating the functional equation of L(f,s) to its Fricke eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Oldform
nodes.description: A form in S_k(Γ₀(N)) arising from lower level M | N via f(z) ↦ f(dz) for d | (N/M), spanning the old subspace.

nodes.name: Conductor of a modular form
nodes.description: The minimal level N such that a newform lives in S_k(Γ₀(N), χ), encoding the precise ramification data of the associated automorphic representation.

nodes.name: Dimension formula for M_k(SL₂(ℤ))
nodes.description: dim M_k(SL₂(ℤ)) = ⌊k/12⌋ + 1 for even k ≥ 2 (with correction for k ≡ 2 mod 12), from the Riemann-Roch theorem on the genus-0 modular curve.
aliases: dimension of modular forms for SL₂(ℤ)

nodes.name: Dimension formula for S_k(Γ₀(N))
nodes.description: dim S_k(Γ₀(N)) = (k−1)(g−1) + corrections from elliptic and parabolic elements, where g is the genus of X₀(N).
aliases: Riemann-Roch dimension formula for cusp forms

nodes.name: Theta function of a quadratic form
nodes.description: θ_Q(z) = ∑_{n ∈ ℤ^m} e^{2πiQ(n)z} for a positive definite quadratic form Q in m variables; a modular form of weight m/2 whose coefficients count representations by Q.

nodes.name: Maass form
nodes.description: A smooth Γ-automorphic eigenfunction of the hyperbolic Laplacian Δf = λf on H with at most polynomial growth at cusps.

nodes.name: Maass cusp form
nodes.description: A Maass form that decays exponentially at all cusps, belonging to the discrete cuspidal spectrum of the Laplacian on L²(Γ\H).

nodes.name: Spectral parameter r
nodes.description: The parameter r such that a Maass form has eigenvalue λ = 1/4 + r²; the Selberg conjecture asserts r ∈ ℝ for congruence subgroups.

nodes.name: Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture
nodes.description: For holomorphic cuspidal newforms of weight k, |a_p(f)| ≤ 2p^{(k−1)/2} (Deligne); for Maass forms, |a_p| ≤ 2p^{1/2} (open, best bound from Kim-Sarnak).

nodes.name: Real-analytic Eisenstein series E(z,s)
nodes.description: E(z,s) = ∑_{γ ∈ Γ_∞\Γ}(Im γz)^s for Re(s) > 1, continued meromorphically to all s, spanning the continuous spectrum of the Laplacian.

nodes.name: Scattering matrix for Γ\H
nodes.description: The matrix Φ(s) relating constant terms of Eisenstein series at different cusps, satisfying Φ(s)Φ(1−s) = I, whose poles give the residual spectrum.

nodes.name: Spectral decomposition of L²(Γ\H)
nodes.description: L²(Γ\H) = ℂ ⊕ V_cusp ⊕ V_res ⊕ V_cont, with V_cusp from Maass cusp forms, V_res from residues of Eisenstein series, and V_cont the continuous Eisenstein spectrum.

nodes.name: Discrete spectrum of Γ\H
nodes.description: The subspace of L²(Γ\H) spanned by eigenfunctions with isolated eigenvalues: constants, Maass cusp forms, and residual Eisenstein contributions.

nodes.name: Continuous spectrum of Γ\H
nodes.description: The absolutely continuous part of the Laplacian spectrum on L²(Γ\H), parametrized by Eisenstein series E(z, 1/2+it) for t ∈ ℝ, occupying [1/4, ∞).

nodes.name: Pre-trace formula
nodes.description: ∑_j h(r_j)|u_j(z)|² + (cont. part) = ∑_{γ ∈ Γ} k(u(z,γz)), the spectral expansion of an automorphic kernel, preceding the Selberg trace formula.

nodes.name: Selberg zeta function Z_Γ(s)
nodes.description: Z_Γ(s) = ∏_{γ₀} ∏_{k≥0}(1 − N(γ₀)^{−s−k}) over primitive hyperbolic classes, an entire function whose zeros encode eigenvalues of Δ on Γ\H.

nodes.name: Maass-Selberg relations
nodes.description: Inner product formulas for truncated Eisenstein series in terms of the scattering matrix, controlling the continuous spectrum contribution.

nodes.name: Petersson trace formula
nodes.description: ∑_f ā_f(m)a_f(n)/⟨f,f⟩ = δ_{m,n} + 2πi^{-k}∑_{c≡0(N)} c^{-1}S(m,n;c)J_{k-1}(4π√(mn)/c), relating Fourier coefficients to Kloosterman sums.

nodes.name: Eichler-Selberg trace formula
nodes.description: An explicit formula for tr(T_n | S_k(Γ₀(N))) as a sum over conjugacy classes involving class numbers, totient values, and cusp/elliptic contributions.
aliases: Selberg trace formula for Hecke operators

nodes.name: Kuznetsov trace formula
nodes.description: A sum formula relating spectral sums over Maass/holomorphic forms weighted by Fourier coefficients to geometric sums of Kloosterman sums via Bessel transforms.

nodes.name: Voronoi summation formula (GL(2))
nodes.description: Transforms ∑_n a_f(n)e(nα/q)g(n) for a GL(2) form into a dual sum with Kloosterman twists and Bessel integral transforms; the automorphic Poisson summation.

nodes.name: L-function of a modular form
nodes.description: L(f,s) = ∑ a_f(n)n^{-s} for a Hecke eigenform f, admitting analytic continuation and functional equation Λ(f,s) = ε·Λ(f,k−s).

nodes.name: Euler product for Hecke eigenform L-function
nodes.description: L(f,s) = ∏_p(1 − a_p p^{-s} + χ(p)p^{k-1-2s})^{-1} for (p,N) = 1, with modified local factors at primes dividing the level.

nodes.name: Rankin-Selberg method
nodes.function_signature: (cusp form f, Eisenstein series E(z,s)) → (Rankin-Selberg L-function L(f⊗ḡ,s))
nodes.description: Unfolds ∫_{Γ\H} f(z)ḡ(z)E(z,s)y^k dμ to obtain L(f⊗g,s), yielding analytic continuation and bounds for convolution L-functions.

nodes.name: Symmetric square L-function L(sym²f, s)
nodes.description: The degree-3 L-function ∏_p(1−α²_p p^{-s})^{-1}(1−α_p β_p p^{-s})^{-1}(1−β²_p p^{-s})^{-1} whose analytic properties yield bounds toward Ramanujan.

nodes.name: Jacquet-Langlands correspondence
nodes.description: A bijection between automorphic representations of GL₂(𝔸) and those of quaternion algebra D×(𝔸) that are not one-dimensional, preserving L-functions.

nodes.name: Gelbart-Jacquet lift
nodes.description: The functorial lift GL(2)→GL(3) corresponding to the symmetric square, proving L(sym²f,s) is automorphic on GL(3).

nodes.name: GL(n) automorphic form
nodes.description: A smooth function on GL_n(ℚ)\GL_n(𝔸) satisfying moderate growth, K-finiteness, and Z(g_∞)-finiteness, generalizing classical modular forms.

nodes.name: Kirillov model
nodes.description: A realization of a generic representation of GL₂(F) on functions on F×, obtained by restricting the Whittaker model to the diagonal torus.

nodes.name: Strong multiplicity one for GL(2)
nodes.description: Two cuspidal automorphic representations of GL(2) with isomorphic local components at all but finitely many places are globally isomorphic.

nodes.name: Twisted L-function L(f⊗χ, s)
nodes.description: L(f⊗χ,s) = ∑ a_f(n)χ(n)n^{-s} for a Hecke eigenform f and Dirichlet character χ, with functional equation involving the conductor of χ.

nodes.name: Satake parameters
nodes.description: The pair (α_p, β_p) with α_p + β_p = a_f(p) and α_p β_p = χ(p)p^{k-1} parametrizing the unramified local factor at prime p via the Satake isomorphism.

nodes.name: Hecke multiplicativity relations
nodes.description: a(m)a(n) = ∑_{d|(m,n)} χ(d)d^{k-1} a(mn/d²) for a Hecke eigenform, encoding the ring structure of Hecke operators.

nodes.name: Amplification method
nodes.function_signature: (target form f₀ in spectral family) → (subconvexity bound for L(f₀, 1/2))
nodes.description: Constructs an amplifier large on a target form, applies spectral mean-value estimates to convert spectral information into pointwise L-function bounds.

nodes.name: Spectral large sieve inequality
nodes.description: ∑_j |∑_n a_n ρ_j(n)|² ≤ (N + T²)∑|a_n|², bounding bilinear forms in Fourier coefficients of Maass forms, the spectral analogue of the classical large sieve.

nodes.name: Subconvexity for GL(2) L-functions
nodes.description: L(f, 1/2) ≪ C(f)^{1/4−δ} for some δ > 0, breaking the convexity bound; proved in various aspects by Iwaniec, Duke-Friedlander-Iwaniec, and Michel-Venkatesh.

nodes.name: Mean value estimates via spectral methods
nodes.function_signature: (spectral family of L-functions) → (moment asymptotics via Kuznetsov formula)
nodes.description: Uses the spectral decomposition and Kuznetsov formula to evaluate moments of L-functions over spectral families.

nodes.name: Spectral reciprocity formula
nodes.description: An identity relating moments of L-functions over one spectral family to moments over a dual family, transferring subconvexity between aspects.

nodes.name: Nonvanishing results for central L-values
nodes.description: L(f,1/2) ≠ 0 or L(f⊗χ,1/2) ≠ 0 for a positive proportion of forms/characters in a family, proved via mollified moments.

nodes.name: Singular integral (circle method)
nodes.description: The archimedean factor J(n) = ∫ δ(x₁^k+…+x_s^k − n) dx in the circle method asymptotic, measuring the real-analytic solution density.

nodes.name: Hua's inequality
nodes.description: ∫₀¹ |∑_{n≤N} e(αn^k)|^{2^k} dα ≪ N^{2^k − k + ε}, a mean value estimate for Weyl sums fundamental to the minor arc analysis in Waring's problem.

nodes.name: Hardy-Littlewood asymptotic for Waring's problem
nodes.description: R_{s,k}(n) = 𝔖(n)·J(n)·n^{s/k−1} + o(n^{s/k−1}) for s sufficiently large, where 𝔖 is the singular series and J the singular integral.

nodes.name: Farey dissection
nodes.function_signature: ([0,1)) → (Farey arcs centered at a/q with q ≤ Q)
nodes.description: Partition of [0,1) into arcs centered at Farey fractions of order Q, providing finer major/minor arc decomposition than the standard Hardy-Littlewood dissection.

nodes.name: Kloosterman refinement (HLK method)
nodes.function_signature: (major arc contributions) → (sums of Kloosterman sums S(m,n;c))
nodes.description: The Hardy-Littlewood-Kloosterman method: major arc contributions yield Kloosterman sums whose cancellation (Weil bound) improves the error term.

nodes.name: Delta method (Duke-Friedlander-Iwaniec)
nodes.function_signature: (binary additive equation n = m) → (smooth delta detection via Kloosterman sums)
nodes.description: Replaces the circle method's major/minor arc dissection with a smooth delta symbol built from Kloosterman sums, effective for binary problems.

nodes.name: Huxley's zero density estimate
nodes.description: N(σ,T) ≪ T^{12(1−σ)/5+ε} for σ ≥ 1/2, improving Ingham's estimate and implying primes in short intervals [x, x + x^{7/12+ε}].

nodes.name: Jutila's zero density estimate
nodes.description: Improved zero density bounds for Dirichlet L-functions uniform in the conductor q, with applications to primes in arithmetic progressions.

nodes.name: Log-free zero density estimate
nodes.description: ∑_{χ mod q} N(σ,T,χ) ≪ (qT)^{A(1−σ)} without logarithmic factors, critical for the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem.

nodes.name: Zero-detecting polynomial
nodes.function_signature: (zeros of L(s,χ)) → (mean value estimate for Dirichlet polynomial M(s)·L(s,χ))
nodes.description: A Dirichlet polynomial M(s) chosen so M(s)L(s,χ) ≈ 1 near zeros, converting zero-counting into mean value estimates.

nodes.name: Turán's power sum method
nodes.function_signature: (power sums of reciprocal zeros) → (lower bound detecting zeros)
nodes.description: Bounds max_{1≤ν≤N} |∑ b_j z_j^ν| from below for |z_j| ≥ 1, applied to detect zeros of zeta functions via power sum analysis.

nodes.name: Halász-Montgomery method
nodes.function_signature: (Dirichlet polynomials near zeros) → (zero density estimates)
nodes.description: Combines Halász's theorem on mean values with Montgomery's zero-detection, exploiting duality between zeros and prime distribution.

nodes.name: GUE hypothesis for ζ(s) zeros
nodes.description: The conjecture that all local statistics of normalized zeros of ζ(s) match those of eigenvalues of large random matrices from the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble.

nodes.name: Mollifier method
nodes.function_signature: (ζ(s) on critical line) → (lower bound for proportion of zeros at Re(s)=1/2)
nodes.description: Multiplies ζ(s) by M(s) ≈ 1/ζ(s) to smooth zeros, then analyzes moments of ζ·M on Re(s)=1/2 to bound zeros on the critical line.

nodes.name: Levinson's method
nodes.function_signature: (mollifier involving ζ'(s)) → (≥1/3 of zeros on critical line)
nodes.description: A refinement of the mollifier method using ζ'/ζ to prove that at least 1/3 of nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) lie on the critical line.

nodes.name: Deuring-Heilbronn repulsion phenomenon
nodes.description: A real zero β₁ of L(s,χ₁) near 1 forces all other L-functions to have enlarged zero-free regions near 1, with explicit repulsion depending on 1 − β₁.

nodes.name: Linnik's constant
nodes.description: The infimum L such that the least prime p ≡ a mod q satisfies p ≪ q^L; currently known L ≤ 5 (Xylouris, 2011), and L = 2+ε under GRH.

nodes.name: Fouvry's theorem
nodes.description: A Bombieri-Vinogradov type result with level of distribution beyond x^{1/2}: for a positive proportion of moduli q ≤ x^{4/7−ε}, the PNT error satisfies strong average bounds.

nodes.name: Duke's theorem (equidistribution of CM points)
nodes.description: CM points of discriminant −D and closed geodesics of discriminant D become equidistributed on SL₂(ℤ)\H as D → ∞, proved via subconvexity for half-integral weight L-functions.

nodes.name: Subconvexity implies equidistribution
nodes.description: Subconvexity L(f⊗χ_D, 1/2) ≪ D^{1/4−δ} implies equidistribution of associated arithmetic objects via Weyl's criterion applied to spectral test functions.

nodes.name: Erdős-Turán inequality
nodes.description: D_N ≤ C(1/H + ∑_{h=1}^H (1/h)|∑_{n≤N} e(hω_n)|/N) for any H ≥ 1, bounding discrepancy by exponential sums.

nodes.name: Discrepancy of a sequence
nodes.description: D_N = sup_{[a,b)} |#{n ≤ N : ω_n ∈ [a,b)}/N − (b−a)|, the quantitative deviation from uniform distribution.

nodes.name: Friedlander-Iwaniec theorem
nodes.description: There are infinitely many primes of the form a² + b⁴, proved using the half-dimensional sieve, bilinear forms, and automorphic techniques.

nodes.name: Iwaniec's half-dimensional sieve
nodes.function_signature: (thin sequence with κ=1/2 sieve dimension) → (prime detection via bilinear structure)
nodes.description: A sieve achieving dimension κ = 1/2 by exploiting bilinear structure in error terms, detecting primes where the linear sieve has parity obstruction.

nodes.name: Shifted convolution sums
nodes.description: Sums ∑_n a_f(n)a_g(n+h) for automorphic coefficients, estimated via spectral methods or the delta method with applications to subconvexity.

nodes.name: Additive divisor problem
nodes.description: The estimation of ∑_{n≤x} d(n)d(n+h), a prototype shifted convolution sum controlled by spectral theory of automorphic forms.

nodes.name: Hecke's converse theorem
nodes.description: A Dirichlet series with Euler product and the standard functional equation Λ(s) = εΛ(k−s) necessarily arises from a modular form of weight k for SL₂(ℤ).

nodes.name: Weil's converse theorem
nodes.description: If L(s,χ) = ∑ a_n χ(n)n^{-s} satisfies functional equations for sufficiently many twists χ, then ∑ a_n q^n is a modular form of the predicted level and character.

nodes.name: Holomorphic modular form (weight k, level N)
nodes.description: A holomorphic f: H → ℂ with f|_k γ = χ(d)f for all γ ∈ Γ₀(N) and holomorphic at all cusps; M_k(Γ₀(N),χ) is finite-dimensional.

nodes.name: Eisenstein series with Nebentypus
nodes.description: Eisenstein series E_k(z,χ,ψ) = ∑ χ(c)ψ(d)(cz+d)^{-k} for characters χ,ψ with χψ(-1) = (-1)^k, spanning the Eisenstein subspace of M_k(Γ₁(N)).

nodes.name: Ramanujan conjecture for GL(2)
nodes.description: The conjecture that for a cuspidal π of GL(2)/ℚ, all unramified local components are tempered; equivalently |α_p| = |β_p| = 1 at Satake parameters.

nodes.name: Extremal order of an arithmetic function
nodes.description: The maximal (resp. minimal) order of f(n) is a function g(n) bounding f from above (resp. below) up to (1+o(1)) factor, achieved along some subsequence.

nodes.name: Highly composite number
nodes.description: An integer n such that d(m) < d(n) for all m < n; has the form ∏ p_i^{a_i} with a_1 ≥ a_2 ≥ … ≥ 1 (Ramanujan).

nodes.name: Largest prime factor P⁺(n)
nodes.description: P⁺(n) = max{p : p | n} for n ≥ 2, with P⁺(1) = 1 by convention; central to the study of smooth/friable integers.

nodes.name: Smallest prime factor P⁻(n)
nodes.description: P⁻(n) = min{p : p | n} for n ≥ 2, with P⁻(1) = +∞ by convention; central to the study of rough integers.

nodes.name: Rough integers Φ(x, y)
nodes.description: Φ(x, y) = #{n ≤ x : P⁻(n) > y}, counting integers up to x whose smallest prime factor exceeds y.

nodes.name: Natural density (asymptotic density)
nodes.description: d(A) = lim_{x→∞} |A ∩ [1,x]| / x for a set A ⊆ ℤ_{>0}, when the limit exists.

nodes.name: Logarithmic density
nodes.description: δ(A) = lim_{x→∞} (1/log x) ∑_{n≤x, n∈A} 1/n; if natural density d(A) exists then δ(A) = d(A), but the converse fails.

nodes.name: Slowly varying function
nodes.description: A measurable function L: [1,∞) → (0,∞) with L(tx)/L(x) → 1 for every t > 0 as x → ∞; examples include log x, log log x, constants.

nodes.name: Generalized divisor function d_z(n)
nodes.description: For z ∈ ℂ, d_z(n) is the n-th Dirichlet coefficient of ζ(s)^z; multiplicative with d_z(p^k) = z(z+1)⋯(z+k−1)/k!.

nodes.name: Local zeta function ζ(s, y)
nodes.description: ζ(s, y) = ∏_{p≤y}(1 − p^{−s})^{−1} = ∑_{P⁺(n)≤y} n^{−s}, the truncated Euler product restricted to y-smooth integers.

nodes.name: Pretentious distance D(f, g; x)
nodes.description: D(f, g; x)² = ∑_{p≤x} (1 − Re(f(p)g̅(p)))/p, measuring proximity between multiplicative functions f, g of modulus ≤ 1 on primes.

nodes.name: Hooley's Δ-function
nodes.description: Δ(n) = max_{u∈ℝ} #{d | n : e^u < d ≤ e^{u+1}}, measuring the maximum concentration of divisors of n in a dyadic interval.

nodes.name: Distribution function of an arithmetic function
nodes.description: F_N(t) = (1/N)#{n ≤ N : f(n) ≤ t}, the empirical cumulative distribution function of f evaluated at the first N integers.

nodes.name: Limiting distribution of an arithmetic function
nodes.description: An arithmetic function f has limiting distribution F if F_N(t) → F(t) at all continuity points of F as N → ∞.

nodes.name: Summatory Liouville function L(x)
nodes.description: L(x) = ∑_{n≤x} λ(n); the PNT is equivalent to L(x) = o(x), and the RH to L(x) = O(x^{1/2+ε}).

nodes.name: Dickman function differential-delay equation
nodes.description: ρ satisfies uρ′(u) = −ρ(u−1) for u > 1 with ρ(u) = 1 for 0 ≤ u ≤ 1; ρ(u) decreases super-exponentially as u → ∞.

nodes.name: Buchstab function differential-delay equation
nodes.description: (uω(u))′ = ω(u−1) for u > 2 with uω(u) = 1 for 1 ≤ u ≤ 2; ω(u) → e^{−γ} as u → ∞.

nodes.name: Saddle-point parameter α(x, y)
nodes.description: The unique positive solution α to ∑_{p≤y} (log p)/(p^α − 1) = log x, the saddle point in the Hildebrand–Tenenbaum estimate for Ψ(x, y).

nodes.name: Robin's inequality
nodes.description: σ(n) < e^γ n log log n for all n ≥ 5041; equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (Robin, 1984).

nodes.name: Mertens' first theorem
nodes.description: ∑_{p≤x} (log p)/p = log x + O(1).

nodes.name: Mertens' second theorem
nodes.description: ∑_{p≤x} 1/p = log log x + M + O(1/log x), where M is the Meissel–Mertens constant.

nodes.name: Mertens' third theorem
nodes.description: ∏_{p≤x}(1 − 1/p) = e^{−γ}/log x · (1 + O(1/log x)), where γ is the Euler–Mascheroni constant.

nodes.name: Average order of ω(n)
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} ω(n) = x log log x + M₁x + O(x/log x), where M₁ is a constant related to the Meissel–Mertens constant.

nodes.name: Average order of Ω(n)
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} Ω(n) = x log log x + M₂x + O(x/log x), with M₂ = M₁ + ∑_p 1/(p(p−1)).

nodes.name: Squarefree counting asymptotic
nodes.description: Q(x) = ∑_{n≤x} μ(n)² = (6/π²)x + O(√x), counting squarefree integers up to x.

nodes.name: Maximal order of d(n)
nodes.description: lim sup_{n→∞} log d(n) · log log n / log n = log 2; equivalently d(n) ≤ 2^{(1+o(1)) log n / log log n} with equality along highly composite numbers.

nodes.name: Gronwall's theorem (maximal order of σ(n)/n)
nodes.description: lim sup_{n→∞} σ(n)/(n log log n) = e^γ, where γ is the Euler–Mascheroni constant.

nodes.name: Minimal order of φ(n)/n
nodes.description: lim inf_{n→∞} φ(n) log log n / n = e^{−γ}; achieved along primorial numbers n_k = ∏_{p≤p_k} p.

nodes.name: Mean value of |ζ(1/2+it)|²
nodes.description: ∫₀ᵀ |ζ(1/2 + it)|² dt ∼ T log T as T → ∞.

nodes.name: Dickman's theorem
nodes.description: For fixed u > 0, Ψ(x, x^{1/u})/x → ρ(u) as x → ∞, where ρ is the Dickman function.

nodes.name: Karamata's Tauberian theorem
nodes.description: If a_n ≥ 0 and ∑a_n n^{−s} ∼ Γ(α+1)(s−α)^{−1}L(1/(s−α)) as s → α⁺ with L slowly varying, then ∑_{n≤x} a_n ∼ x^α L(x).

nodes.name: Delange's Tauberian theorem
nodes.description: If ∑a_n n^{−s} behaves like ζ(s)^z near s = 1 for z ∈ ℂ, then ∑_{n≤x} a_n ∼ Cx(log x)^{z−1}/Γ(z) for an explicit constant C.

nodes.name: Landau–Page theorem
nodes.description: Among all real primitive characters χ mod q with q ≤ Q, at most one L(s, χ) can vanish in the region σ > 1 − c/log Q.

nodes.name: Dual Turán–Kubilius inequality
nodes.description: ∑_{p^k≤x} |g(p^k)|²/p^k ≪ (1/x) ∑_{n≤x} |∑_{p^k‖n} g(p^k)|², dual to the Turán–Kubilius inequality.

nodes.name: Normal order of log d(n)
nodes.description: The normal order of log d(n) is (log 2)(log log n): for almost all n, log d(n) ∼ (log 2) log log n.

nodes.name: Delange's theorem on mean values of multiplicative functions
nodes.description: If f is multiplicative with |f(p)| ≤ 1 and ∑(1 − f(p))/p converges, then (1/x)∑_{n≤x} f(n) → ∏_p(1 − 1/p)(1 + f(p)/p + f(p²)/p² + ⋯).

nodes.name: Equivalence of PNT and ∑μ(n) = o(x)
nodes.description: The prime number theorem is equivalent to ∑_{n≤x} μ(n) = o(x), and also to ∑_{n≤x} μ(n)/n → 0.

nodes.name: Elliott's theorem on multiplicative functions in progressions
nodes.description: Extension of Halász's theorem to averages of multiplicative functions over arithmetic progressions, using character sum techniques.

nodes.name: Hildebrand's extension of Dickman's theorem
nodes.description: Ψ(x, y) = xρ(u)(1 + O(log(u+1)/log y)) uniformly for u ≤ exp((log y)^{3/5−ε}), extending Dickman's result to a wide range.

nodes.name: Hildebrand–Tenenbaum saddle-point estimate for Ψ(x, y)
nodes.description: Ψ(x, y) = (x^{1−α}ζ(α, y))/(α√(2πφ₂(α, y)))(1 + O(1/u)) where α is the saddle point, valid for exp((log log x)^{5/3+ε}) ≤ y ≤ x.

nodes.name: Canfield–Erdős–Pomerance theorem
nodes.description: log Ψ(x, y) ∼ −u log u when u = log x / log y → ∞ with y → ∞, refining the Dickman approximation for large u.

nodes.name: Alladi–Erdős result on average of log P⁺(n)
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} log P⁺(n) = cx + o(x) for an explicit constant c = 1 − ∫₀^∞ ρ(t) dt related to the Dickman function.

nodes.name: Smooth numbers in short intervals
nodes.description: Ψ(x + h, y) − Ψ(x, y) ≫ hρ(u) under suitable conditions on h and y, showing smooth numbers are well-distributed in short intervals.

nodes.name: Asymptotic for rough integers Φ(x, y)
nodes.description: Φ(x, y) = xω(u)∏_{p≤y}(1 − 1/p)(1 + O(1/log y)) for u = log x / log y, where ω is the Buchstab function.

nodes.name: Friable integers in arithmetic progressions
nodes.description: Ψ(x, y; q, a) = Ψ(x, y)/φ(q)(1 + O(…)) under suitable conditions on q and y, showing equidistribution of smooth numbers in progressions.

nodes.name: Distribution of the smallest prime factor
nodes.description: #{n ≤ x : P⁻(n) > y} = x∏_{p≤y}(1 − 1/p)(ω(u) + O(1/log y)); for fixed u the probability that P⁻(n) > n^{1/u} approaches e^{−γ}.

nodes.name: Wintner's theorem on random multiplicative functions
nodes.description: If f(p) = ±1 independently with probability 1/2 each, then ∑_{n≤x} f(n) = O(x^{1/2+ε}) almost surely.

nodes.name: Maier's theorem on short intervals
nodes.description: π(x + (log x)^A) − π(x) is NOT asymptotic to (log x)^{A−1} for any A > 1; short intervals exhibit irregularities beyond PNT predictions.

nodes.name: Daboussi's theorem
nodes.description: If f is multiplicative with |f| ≤ 1, then ∑_{n≤x} f(n)e(nα) = o(x) for every irrational α.

nodes.name: Schnirelman's additive basis theorem
nodes.description: If A has positive Schnirelman density σ(A) > 0 and 0 ∈ A, then A is an additive basis of finite order: every sufficiently large integer is a sum of at most h elements of A.

nodes.name: Tenenbaum's theorem on divisor distribution
nodes.description: For almost all n, the divisors of n are approximately uniformly distributed on a logarithmic scale in [1, n].

nodes.name: Asymptotic for ∑d_z(n) (Selberg–Delange)
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} d_z(n) ∼ Cx(log x)^{z−1}/Γ(z) for z ∈ ℂ, obtained via the Selberg–Delange method applied to ζ(s)^z.

nodes.name: Laplace method for integrals
nodes.function_signature: (∫e^{λφ(t)}g(t)dt, λ→∞) → asymptotic expansion
nodes.description: Asymptotic evaluation of integrals ∫e^{λφ(t)}g(t)dt as λ → ∞ by expanding around the maximum of φ.

nodes.name: Kubilius probabilistic model
nodes.function_signature: (additive function f, primes) → approximate independence model
nodes.description: Models events {p | n} for different primes as approximately independent with probability 1/p, making ω(n) behave like a sum of independent Bernoulli variables.

nodes.name: Turán's second moment method
nodes.function_signature: (additive function f) → normal order via variance bound
nodes.description: Elementary proof of normal order via ∑_{n≤x}(ω(n) − log log x)² = O(x log log x), yielding the Hardy–Ramanujan theorem without complex analysis.

nodes.name: Pretentious distance method (Halász)
nodes.function_signature: (multiplicative f with |f|≤1) → mean value characterization
nodes.description: Characterizes when a multiplicative function has non-vanishing mean value: iff D(f, n^{it}; x) is bounded for some real t.

nodes.name: Effective Tauberian method
nodes.function_signature: (Dirichlet series, zero-free region) → explicit error term in partial sum asymptotic
nodes.description: Quantitative Tauberian theorems providing explicit error terms, typically requiring information about the zero-free region of the associated L-function.

nodes.name: Smooth–rough decomposition for counting primes
nodes.function_signature: (π(x), parameter y) → π(y) + Φ(x,y) − 1 + corrections
nodes.description: Decomposes π(x) = π(y) + Φ(x,y) − 1 plus sieve correction terms, linking prime counting to counts of rough and smooth numbers.

nodes.name: Granville–Soundararajan pretentious number theory
nodes.function_signature: (multiplicative f) → structural classification via pretentious distance
nodes.description: Framework studying multiplicative functions through D(f, χn^{it}; x): f has large partial sums iff it pretends to be χ(n)n^{it} for some character χ and real t.

nodes.name: Rényi–Turán power sum method
nodes.function_signature: (exponential sums, sequence) → discrepancy bound
nodes.description: Bounds the discrepancy of a sequence from its power sums (exponential sums), used in proving equidistribution and large sieve results.

nodes.name: Twisting by Dirichlet characters
nodes.function_signature: (Dirichlet series, character χ) → L(s,χ) separating residue classes
nodes.description: Multiplying a Dirichlet series by a character χ to study its behavior in arithmetic progressions via L(s,χ) = ∑χ(n)n^{−s}.

nodes.name: Logarithmic density of primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.description: The set of primes p ≡ a (mod q) with gcd(a,q) = 1 has logarithmic density 1/φ(q) among all primes, proved as an intermediate step toward Dirichlet's theorem.

nodes.name: Gaussian periods
nodes.description: The sums η_j = ∑_{k} ζ^{g^{ek+j}} where g is a primitive root mod p and e | (p−1), forming the basis for Gauss's theory of cyclotomy and constructibility.

nodes.name: Gauss's theorem on constructible regular polygons
nodes.description: A regular n-gon is constructible by straightedge and compass if and only if n = 2^a p_1 ⋯ p_k where the p_i are distinct Fermat primes.

nodes.name: Fundamental discriminant
nodes.description: An integer D that is the discriminant of a quadratic field ℚ(√d): either D = d with d ≡ 1 (mod 4) squarefree, or D = 4d with d ≡ 2 or 3 (mod 4) squarefree.

nodes.name: Binary quadratic form
nodes.description: A function f(x,y) = ax² + bxy + cy² with a,b,c ∈ ℤ and discriminant D = b² − 4ac, central to the theory of class numbers and representations by forms.

nodes.name: Finite expression for L(1, χ)
nodes.description: For a nonprincipal character χ mod q, L(1,χ) equals a finite sum involving χ(a) and log sin(πa/q) or linear terms, providing computable values of Dirichlet L-functions at s = 1.

nodes.name: Riemann's approximate formula for N(T)
nodes.description: N(T) ≈ (T/2π) log(T/2πe), Riemann's original heuristic approximation for the number of zeros of ζ(s) with imaginary part between 0 and T.

nodes.name: Contour integration for arithmetic functions
nodes.function_signature: (Dirichlet series F(s), contour C) → (Asymptotic formula for ∑_{n≤x} a_n)
nodes.description: Recovers partial sums of arithmetic functions from their Dirichlet series via Perron-type contour integrals, shifting contours past poles and zeros to extract main terms and error estimates.

nodes.name: Truncated explicit formula for ψ(x)
nodes.description: ψ(x) = x − ∑_{|γ|≤T} x^ρ/ρ + O(x log²x / T), a practical form of the explicit formula with controlled truncation error.

nodes.name: Chebyshev ψ-function twisted by χ
nodes.description: ψ(x, χ) = ∑_{n≤x} Λ(n) χ(n), the Chebyshev function weighted by a Dirichlet character, whose analytic properties are governed by the zeros of L(s, χ).

nodes.name: Character sum completion technique
nodes.function_signature: (Incomplete character sum ∑_{a≤N} χ(a)) → (Complete sum over full period + error)
nodes.description: Extends an incomplete character sum to a complete sum over a full period by inserting additive characters, enabling evaluation via Gauss sums.

nodes.name: Further prime number sums
nodes.description: Estimates for sums ∑_{p≤x} f(p) for various arithmetic functions f derived from the prime number theorem and partial summation.

nodes.name: Generalized xi-function ξ(s, χ)
nodes.description: The completed L-function ξ(s, χ) = (q/π)^{(s+a)/2} Γ((s+a)/2) L(s, χ) for primitive χ mod q, an entire function of order 1 satisfying ξ(s, χ) = W(χ) ξ(1−s, χ̄).

nodes.name: Root number W(χ)
nodes.description: The complex constant W(χ) = τ(χ)/(i^a √q) of absolute value 1 appearing in the functional equation of ξ(s, χ), where a = (1−χ(−1))/2.

nodes.name: Counting zeros of entire functions of order 1
nodes.description: An entire function f of order 1 satisfies n(r) = O(r) where n(r) counts zeros with |z| ≤ r, and ∑ 1/|ρ|^{1+ε} converges for every ε > 0.

nodes.name: Hadamard product for ξ(s, χ)
nodes.description: ξ(s, χ) = e^{A(χ)+B(χ)s} ∏_ρ (1 − s/ρ) e^{s/ρ}, the product over nontrivial zeros ρ of L(s, χ), obtained by Hadamard factorization of the entire function ξ(s, χ).

nodes.name: Partial fraction for −L′/L
nodes.description: −L′(s,χ)/L(s,χ) = −B(χ) − ∑_ρ (1/(s−ρ) + 1/ρ) + (terms from trivial zeros), expressing the logarithmic derivative as a sum over nontrivial zeros.

nodes.name: Zero-counting via argument principle
nodes.function_signature: (Meromorphic function f(s), rectangular contour) → (Count of zeros N(T) inside contour)
nodes.description: Counts zeros of ζ(s) or L(s,χ) in a rectangle by integrating (1/2πi) ∮ f′/f ds around the boundary.

nodes.name: log ζ(s) bound near σ = 1
nodes.description: log ζ(σ+it) = O(log t) for σ ≥ 1 − c/log t and |t| ≥ 2, a consequence of the zero-free region providing control on ζ near the 1-line.

nodes.name: Repulsion of zeros by exceptional zero
nodes.description: If L(β₁, χ₁) = 0 with β₁ near 1 for a real character χ₁, then all other zeros ρ of L-functions mod q satisfy enlarged zero-free regions, quantifying the Deuring–Heilbronn phenomenon.

nodes.name: S(T) argument function
nodes.description: S(T) = (1/π) arg ζ(1/2 + iT) defined by continuous variation, satisfying S(T) = O(log T) and appearing in the Riemann–von Mangoldt formula as the oscillatory correction.

nodes.name: N(T, χ) zero-counting function
nodes.description: N(T, χ) counts nontrivial zeros of L(s, χ) with imaginary part in [−T, T], generalizing the Riemann–von Mangoldt N(T) to Dirichlet L-functions.

nodes.name: Asymptotic for N(T, χ)
nodes.description: N(T, χ) = (T/π) log(qT/2πe) + O(log qT) for primitive χ mod q, generalizing the Riemann–von Mangoldt formula to Dirichlet L-functions.

nodes.name: Exponential sum over primes
nodes.description: S(α) = ∑_{p≤N} (log p) e(pα), the generating function for primes used in the circle method, whose size on major and minor arcs controls additive problems involving primes.

nodes.name: Vinogradov's estimate for prime exponential sums
Singular series for three primes
nodes.description: The arithmetic factor 𝔖(N) in the asymptotic for representations of odd N as a sum of three primes, a convergent product over primes encoding local solubility.

nodes.name: Major arc approximation via L-functions
nodes.function_signature: (Exponential sum S(α) on major arc M(q,a)) → (Approximation via L-functions and Gauss sums)
nodes.description: Approximates ∑_{p≤N} (log p) e(pα) on major arcs using Dirichlet characters and L-function zero information, reducing the circle method to analytic properties of L(s, χ).

nodes.name: Large sieve as mean-value estimate
nodes.description: The large sieve inequality reinterpreted as a mean-value bound on character sums averaging over all primitive characters to moduli q ≤ Q, often matching GRH-strength individual bounds.

nodes.name: Vaughan's proof of Bombieri–Vinogradov
nodes.function_signature: (Vaughan's identity + large sieve) → (Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem)
nodes.description: Proves the Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem by decomposing Λ(n) via Vaughan's identity into bilinear forms, then bounding each via the large sieve inequality for characters.

nodes.name: Reduction to primitive characters
nodes.function_signature: (Sum over all χ mod q) → (Sum over primitive χ* mod q* with q*|q)
nodes.description: Replaces sums over all Dirichlet characters mod q by sums over primitive characters of smaller moduli dividing q, exploiting the factorization χ = χ* · χ₀.

nodes.name: Bombieri–Vinogradov as substitute for GRH
nodes.description: The Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem provides, on average over q ≤ x^{1/2−ε}, the same quality of error term in ψ(x;q,a) that GRH would give for each individual q.

nodes.name: Application to the Titchmarsh divisor problem
nodes.description: ∑_{p≤x} d(p−1) ∼ Cx log x for an explicit constant C, proved using the Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem to handle the sum over shifted primes.

nodes.name: De la Vallée-Poussin's proof strategy
nodes.function_signature: (Zero-free region for ζ(s) + Perron/explicit formula) → (PNT with error term)
nodes.description: Establishes the prime number theorem by proving ζ(1+it) ≠ 0 via the 3-4-1 inequality, deriving a zero-free region, then extracting ψ(x) ~ x via contour integration.

nodes.name: Zero-free region for real characters near t = 0
nodes.description: For a real primitive character χ mod q, L(s, χ) has at most one real zero β in (1 − c/log q, 1), requiring treatment separate from the 3-4-1 method which fails near t = 0 for real χ.

nodes.name: Lower bound for L(1, χ) via class number
nodes.description: For real primitive χ mod q, the class number formula gives L(1, χ) ≥ c/√q since h(d) ≥ 1, providing an effective but weak lower bound.

nodes.name: Siegel's lemma on L-function products
nodes.description: If L(β, χ₁) = 0 with β near 1 for real χ₁, then for any other real character χ₂ the product L(s, χ₁)L(s, χ₂) has no zero near s = 1, forcing L(1, χ₂) to be bounded below.

nodes.name: Ineffectivity in Siegel's theorem
nodes.description: The constant c(ε) in Siegel's bound L(1, χ) > c(ε) q^{−ε} cannot be effectively computed because the proof splits into cases depending on the existence of an exceptional zero.

nodes.name: Symmetric pairing of zeros
nodes.description: The functional equation of ξ(s, χ) implies that if ρ is a nontrivial zero of L(s, χ), then 1 − ρ̄ is a zero of L(s, χ̄), and for real χ the zeros come in symmetric pairs.

nodes.name: Density of zeros near σ = 1
nodes.description: The number of zeros ρ of L(s, χ) with Re(ρ) ≥ σ and |Im(ρ)| ≤ T satisfies N(σ, T, χ) = O(T^{A(1−σ)} log T) for σ near 1.

nodes.name: Contribution of major arcs
nodes.description: The integral of S(α)³ e(−Nα) over the major arcs yields the main term (1/2) 𝔖(N) N²/(log N)³ in Vinogradov's three-primes theorem.

nodes.name: Contribution of minor arcs
nodes.description: The integral of S(α)³ e(−Nα) over the minor arcs is O(N²/(log N)^A), shown negligible using Vinogradov's estimate for exponential sums over primes.

nodes.name: Dirichlet polynomial
nodes.description: A finite sum D(s) = ∑_{n≤N} a_n n^{−s}, a fundamental building block in the analytic theory of L-functions, large sieve, and Vaughan's identity.

nodes.name: Character table of (ℤ/qℤ)*
nodes.description: The φ(q) × φ(q) matrix (χ_i(a_j)) of Dirichlet characters mod q evaluated at reduced residue representatives, satisfying row and column orthogonality.

nodes.name: Factorization of characters via CRT
nodes.description: For q = q₁q₂ with gcd(q₁,q₂) = 1, every Dirichlet character χ mod q factors uniquely as χ = χ₁χ₂ via the CRT isomorphism (ℤ/qℤ)* ≅ (ℤ/q₁ℤ)* × (ℤ/q₂ℤ)*.

nodes.name: Dirichlet's L(1, χ) evaluation for quadratic χ
nodes.description: For real primitive χ_D mod |D|, L(1, χ_D) equals an explicit finite sum involving χ_D(a) and log sin(πa/|D|) or linear terms, depending on the sign of D.

nodes.name: Estimate for ∑ χ(p)/p
nodes.description: For nonprincipal χ mod q, ∑_{p≤x} χ(p)/p = O(1) uniformly in x, while for the principal character the sum equals log log x + M + O(1/log x).

nodes.name: Mertens-type estimate in arithmetic progressions
nodes.description: ∑_{p≤x, p≡a mod q} 1/p = (1/φ(q)) log log x + C(q,a) + O(1/log x) for gcd(a,q) = 1, the analogue of Mertens' second theorem for primes in arithmetic progressions.

nodes.name: Cyclotomic polynomial irreducibility over ℚ
nodes.description: The n-th cyclotomic polynomial Φ_n(x) = ∏_{gcd(k,n)=1} (x − e^{2πik/n}) is irreducible over ℚ, equivalently [ℚ(ζ_n):ℚ] = φ(n).

nodes.name: Algebraic integer
nodes.description: An element of an algebraic number field that is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in ℤ.

nodes.name: Norm of an ideal N(𝔞)
nodes.description: For a nonzero ideal 𝔞 of O_K, the finite cardinality N(𝔞) = |O_K/𝔞|, which is multiplicative: N(𝔞𝔟) = N(𝔞)N(𝔟).

nodes.name: Minkowski embedding (canonical embedding)
nodes.description: The ring homomorphism σ: K → ℝ^{r₁} × ℂ^{r₂} sending α to (σ₁(α),...,σ_{r₁}(α),τ₁(α),...,τ_{r₂}(α)), which embeds O_K as a full-rank lattice.

nodes.name: Finiteness of the class number
nodes.description: The ideal class group Cl(K) of any algebraic number field K is finite, proved via the Minkowski bound.

nodes.name: Transitivity of different and discriminant
nodes.description: For a tower K ⊂ L ⊂ M, 𝔇_{M/K} = 𝔇_{M/L}·𝔇_{L/K} and d_{M/K} = N_{L/K}(d_{M/L})·d_{L/K}^{[M:L]}.

nodes.name: Complementary module (codifferent)
nodes.description: The fractional ideal 𝔇_{L/K}^{-1} = {x ∈ L : Tr_{L/K}(x·O_L) ⊂ O_K}, the O_L-dual of O_L with respect to the trace pairing.

nodes.name: Different–discriminant relation
nodes.description: The relative discriminant equals the norm of the different: d_{L/K} = N_{L/K}(𝔇_{L/K}), and a prime ramifies iff it divides d_{L/K}.

nodes.name: Exponent of the different at a prime
nodes.description: For a prime 𝔓|𝔭 with ramification index e, v_𝔓(𝔇_{L/K}) = e−1 if tamely ramified and ≥ e if wildly ramified.

nodes.name: Tame and wild ramification
nodes.description: A prime is tamely ramified if e is coprime to the residue characteristic p (wild inertia group V₁ is trivial), and wildly ramified otherwise.

nodes.name: Discriminant of cyclotomic fields
nodes.description: The discriminant of ℚ(ζ_p) for a prime p is (-1)^{(p-1)/2}·p^{p-2}, and p is the only ramified prime, totally ramified as (1−ζ_p)O = 𝔭^{p-1}.

nodes.name: Chinese Remainder Theorem for Dedekind domains
nodes.description: For pairwise coprime ideals 𝔞₁,...,𝔞ᵣ in a Dedekind domain, O/𝔞₁···𝔞ᵣ ≅ O/𝔞₁ × ··· × O/𝔞ᵣ.

nodes.name: Finiteness of ramification
nodes.description: In any finite extension L/K of number fields, only finitely many primes ramify, namely those dividing the relative discriminant d_{L/K}.

nodes.name: Discrete valuation
nodes.description: A surjective map v: K× → ℤ satisfying v(xy) = v(x) + v(y) and v(x+y) ≥ min(v(x),v(y)), whose valuation ring is a DVR.

nodes.name: Newton polygon
nodes.description: For a polynomial f(x) = Σaᵢxⁱ over a non-archimedean valued field, the lower convex hull of the points (i, v(aᵢ)) in the plane.

nodes.name: Newton polygon theorem
nodes.description: The slopes of the Newton polygon of f(x) over a complete non-archimedean field are the negatives of the valuations of the roots, with multiplicities given by horizontal lengths.

nodes.name: Krasner's lemma
nodes.description: If α is separable over K(β) and |α−β| < |α−α'| for all conjugates α' ≠ α in a complete non-archimedean field, then K(α) ⊆ K(β).

nodes.name: Classification of local fields
nodes.description: A non-archimedean local field of characteristic 0 is a finite extension of ℚ_p; of characteristic p > 0 it is isomorphic to 𝔽_q((t)).

nodes.name: Unramified extension of a local field
nodes.description: A finite extension L/K of local fields with e(L/K) = 1, obtained by adjoining roots of unity of order prime to the residue characteristic.

nodes.name: Totally ramified extension of a local field
nodes.description: A finite extension L/K of local fields with f(L/K) = 1 (same residue field), generated by a root of an Eisenstein polynomial.

nodes.name: Eisenstein polynomial
nodes.description: A monic polynomial f(x) = xⁿ + aₙ₋₁xⁿ⁻¹ + ··· + a₀ with all aᵢ in the maximal ideal 𝔪 and a₀ ∉ 𝔪², which is irreducible and generates a totally ramified extension.

nodes.name: Structure of unramified extensions
nodes.description: For each f ≥ 1 there is a unique unramified extension of degree f of a local field K, obtained by adjoining a (q^f−1)-th root of unity, with cyclic Galois group generated by Frobenius.

nodes.name: Decomposition into unramified and totally ramified parts
nodes.description: Every finite extension L/K of local fields contains a unique maximal unramified subextension T/K with [T:K] = f, and L/T is totally ramified of degree e.

nodes.name: Teichmüller representatives
nodes.description: The unique system of (q−1)-th roots of unity in a local field K providing a canonical multiplicative section of the reduction map O → κ.

nodes.name: Product formula for valuations
nodes.description: For any nonzero α in a number field K, the product of normalized absolute values over all places equals 1: ∏_v |α|_v = 1.

nodes.name: Replete ideal (Arakelov ideal)
nodes.description: A formal product ∏_{𝔭 finite} 𝔭^{v_𝔭} · ∏_{σ infinite} σ^{v_σ} with v_𝔭 ∈ ℤ (almost all zero) and v_σ ∈ ℝ, extending fractional ideals to include archimedean data.

nodes.name: Replete divisor
nodes.description: An element of ⊕_{𝔭 finite} ℤ·𝔭 ⊕ ⊕_{σ infinite} ℝ·σ, the Arakelov-theoretic analogue of a Weil divisor on the arithmetic curve Spec(O_K).

nodes.name: Arakelov class group (replete divisor class group)
nodes.description: The quotient CH¹(O_K) = Div(O_K)/{replete principal divisors}, an extension of the ideal class group by a real torus.

nodes.name: Metrized line bundle on Spec(O_K)
nodes.description: A projective O_K-module of rank 1 equipped with hermitian metrics at each infinite place, the arithmetic-geometric analogue of a line bundle on a curve.

nodes.name: Degree map on replete divisors
nodes.description: The homomorphism deg: Div(O_K) → ℝ defined by deg(D) = Σ_𝔭 v_𝔭·log N(𝔭) + Σ_σ v_σ, inducing a degree map on the Arakelov class group.

nodes.name: Euler–Minkowski characteristic
nodes.description: For a metrized fractional ideal 𝔞, χ(𝔞) = −log(vol(𝔞)) + (n/2)log(π), the arithmetic analogue of the Euler characteristic of a line bundle on a curve.

nodes.name: Riemann–Roch theorem for number fields
nodes.description: For a replete divisor D on Spec(O_K), χ(D) = deg(D) − ½ log|d_K|, analogous to χ(D) = deg(D) − g + 1 for algebraic curves.

nodes.name: Ideal lattice
nodes.description: The image of a fractional ideal 𝔞 under the Minkowski embedding, forming a full lattice in K_ℝ with covolume |d_K|^{1/2}·N(𝔞).

nodes.name: Tate cohomology groups Ĥⁿ(G,A)
nodes.description: For a finite group G and G-module A, a modification of group cohomology defined for all n ∈ ℤ, with Ĥ⁰ = A^G/N_G(A) and Ĥ⁻¹ = ker(N_G)/I_G·A.

nodes.name: Herbrand quotient h(G,A)
nodes.description: For a finite cyclic group G acting on A, the ratio h(G,A) = |Ĥ⁰(G,A)|/|Ĥ⁻¹(G,A)|, which is multiplicative on short exact sequences and equals 1 for finite modules.

nodes.name: Class formation
nodes.description: A pair (G,A) of a profinite group with closed subgroups and a G-module satisfying H¹ = 0 for all layers and H² ≅ (1/n)ℤ/ℤ canonically for degree-n Galois layers.

nodes.name: Formation module
nodes.description: The G-module A in a class formation playing the role of the multiplicative group (local) or idèle class group (global), satisfying the class formation axioms.

nodes.name: Invariant map inv_{L/K}
nodes.description: The canonical isomorphism inv_{L/K}: H²(G_{L/K}, A_L) → (1/[L:K])ℤ/ℤ that is part of the class formation data, generalizing the Hasse invariant for Brauer groups.

nodes.name: Fundamental class u_{L/K}
nodes.description: The unique element of H²(G_{L/K}, A_L) mapping to 1/[L:K] under the invariant map, generating H² as a cyclic group and driving the Nakayama–Tate isomorphism.

nodes.name: Nakayama–Tate duality theorem
nodes.description: Cup product with the fundamental class u_{L/K} induces isomorphisms Ĥⁿ(G,ℤ) → Ĥⁿ⁺²(G,A) for all n; at n = −2 this gives the abstract reciprocity map G^{ab} ≅ A^G/N_G(A).

nodes.name: Abstract reciprocity map
nodes.description: The isomorphism rec_{L/K}: A_K/N_{L/K}(A_L) → G_{L/K}^{ab} from Nakayama–Tate at n = −2, which in concrete cases gives the local or global Artin map.

nodes.name: Abstract existence theorem
nodes.description: In a class formation satisfying an existence axiom, there is a bijection between open subgroups of finite index in A_K and finite abelian extensions of K, via norm groups.

nodes.name: Inflation map in group cohomology
