nodes.description: For a cyclic extension K/F of degree n with generator σ and a ∈ F×, the cyclic algebra (K/F, σ, a) = ⊕_{i=0}^{n-1} Ku^i with u^n = a and ua = σ(a)u; a central simple algebra over F.

nodes.name: Delta-functor (universal)
nodes.description: A sequence of functors {T^n}_{n≥0} with connecting homomorphisms δ^n: T^n(C) → T^{n+1}(A) for each short exact sequence, forming long exact sequences; a universal δ-functor is characterized by T^n being coeffaceable for n ≥ 1.

nodes.name: Discriminant of a number field
nodes.description: For a number field K with [K:ℚ] = n and integral basis {ω_1,...,ω_n}, the discriminant d_K = det(σ_i(ω_j))^2 where σ_i are the n embeddings K → ℂ; an invariant of K detecting ramification.

nodes.name: Embedding of K into ℝ^n (real and complex places)
nodes.description: A number field K of degree n has r_1 real embeddings σ_i: K → ℝ and r_2 pairs of complex conjugate embeddings τ_j, τ̄_j: K → ℂ, with r_1 + 2r_2 = n; these define the archimedean places of K.

nodes.name: Euler product
nodes.description: A product representation ∏_p f(p,s) over primes p for a Dirichlet series, expressing multiplicativity of the coefficients; the Riemann zeta function has ζ(s) = ∏_p (1-p^{-s})^{-1}.

nodes.name: Exponent of a central simple algebra
nodes.description: The order of [A] in the Brauer group Br(F); always divides the index and shares the same prime factors: if ind(A) = p_1^{a_1}...p_k^{a_k}, then exp(A) = p_1^{b_1}...p_k^{b_k} with 1 ≤ b_i ≤ a_i.

nodes.name: Ext^1 and extensions
nodes.description: There is a natural bijection between Ext^1_R(C,A) and equivalence classes of short exact sequences 0 → A → B → C → 0, with the Baer sum making this correspondence a group isomorphism.

nodes.name: Finiteness of form classes
nodes.description: For any discriminant D < 0, the number of proper equivalence classes of primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms of discriminant D is finite.

nodes.name: Form class group
nodes.description: The finite abelian group of proper equivalence classes of primitive binary quadratic forms of discriminant D under Gauss composition; its order h(D) is the class number.

nodes.name: Frobenius theorem (real division algebras)
nodes.description: The only finite-dimensional associative division algebras over ℝ are ℝ, ℂ, and the quaternions ℍ.

nodes.name: Fundamental identity e·f·g = n
nodes.description: For a prime p in ℤ and K/ℚ of degree n, if pO_K = P_1^{e_1}...P_g^{e_g} with f_i = f(P_i|p), then ∑_{i=1}^g e_i f_i = n; in the Galois case all e_i and f_i are equal so efg = n.

nodes.name: Gauss's lemma (quadratic residues)
nodes.description: If p is an odd prime and gcd(a,p)=1, then (a/p) = (-1)^n where n is the number of least positive residues of a, 2a, ..., ((p-1)/2)a modulo p that exceed p/2.

nodes.name: Genus of a binary quadratic form
nodes.description: A genus is a set of proper equivalence classes of binary quadratic forms of discriminant D that represent the same values modulo D (or 4D); genera partition the form class group and form a quotient group.

nodes.name: Hilbert's theorem on Hilbert polynomial
nodes.description: For a finitely generated graded module over k[X_0,...,X_n], the Hilbert function agrees with a polynomial (the Hilbert polynomial) for all sufficiently large arguments.

nodes.name: Hom functor
nodes.description: The bifunctor Hom_R(-,-): R-Mod^op × R-Mod → Ab; contravariant and left exact in the first variable, covariant and left exact in the second; its right derived functors are Ext^n.

nodes.name: Hurwitz formula
nodes.description: For a nonconstant morphism f: C -> C' of smooth projective curves of genera g and g', 2g-2 = deg(f)*(2g'-2) + sum_{P in C} (e_P - 1), where e_P is the ramification index at P.

nodes.name: Induced module
nodes.description: For a subgroup H ≤ G and an H-module M, the induced module Ind_H^G(M) = ℤ[G] ⊗_{ℤ[H]} M; satisfies Shapiro's lemma: H^n(G, Ind_H^G M) ≅ H^n(H, M).

nodes.name: Inner automorphism
nodes.description: An automorphism of a ring or algebra A of the form x ↦ uxu^{-1} for some invertible element u ∈ A; the Skolem-Noether theorem shows all automorphisms of a central simple algebra are inner.

nodes.name: Isomorphism Br(K/F) ≅ H²(Gal(K/F), K×)
nodes.description: For a finite Galois extension K/F, the map sending a factor set to its crossed product algebra induces a group isomorphism from H²(Gal(K/F), K×) to the relative Brauer group Br(K/F).

nodes.name: Jacobian criterion for nonsingularity
nodes.description: A point P on the zero set V(I) in k^n is nonsingular iff the Jacobian matrix (partial f_i/partial x_j) evaluated at P has rank n - dim(V), where the f_i generate I.

nodes.name: Left Noetherian ring
nodes.description: A ring R with identity whose left ideals satisfy the ascending chain condition (ACC): every ascending chain of left ideals stabilizes.

nodes.name: Macaulay's theorem
nodes.description: The Hilbert function of an ideal I equals the Hilbert function of its leading term ideal LT(I), so computing with Gröbner bases reduces Hilbert function computation to the monomial case.

nodes.name: Minkowski's discriminant bound
nodes.description: For any number field K ≠ ℚ, |d_K| > 1; combined with the Dedekind discriminant theorem, this proves every number field other than ℚ has a ramified prime.

nodes.name: Minkowski's lattice point theorem
nodes.description: If Λ is a lattice in ℝ^n and S is a convex symmetric body with vol(S) > 2^n vol(ℝ^n/Λ), then S contains a nonzero lattice point; used to prove finiteness of class number and Dirichlet's unit theorem.

nodes.name: Norm map N_{K/F}
nodes.description: For a finite extension K/F, N_{K/F}(α) = ∏_{σ} σ(α) over all F-embeddings σ of K; for Galois K/F, N_{K/F}: K× → F× is surjective onto its image and its kernel appears in Hilbert's theorem 90.

nodes.name: Nullstellensatz (field-theoretic form)
nodes.description: If K is a field and L is a finitely generated K-algebra that is a field, then L is a finite algebraic extension of K.

nodes.name: Periodicity of cohomology for cyclic groups
nodes.description: If G is a finite cyclic group and M is a G-module, then Ĥ^n(G,M) ≅ Ĥ^{n+2}(G,M) for all n ∈ ℤ in Tate cohomology; in particular H²(G,M) ≅ Ĥ^0(G,M) = M^G/N(M).

nodes.name: Principal genus
nodes.description: The genus containing the principal form x^2 - (D/4)y^2 (D even) or x^2 + xy + (1-D)/4 y^2 (D odd); it equals the subgroup of squares in the form class group.

nodes.name: Proj construction
nodes.description: For a graded ring S = direct sum S_d, Proj(S) is the scheme whose points are homogeneous prime ideals not containing the irrelevant ideal S_+, with structure sheaf built from degree-zero localizations; globalizes projective varieties.

nodes.name: Proper equivalence of binary quadratic forms
nodes.description: Two binary quadratic forms f and g are properly equivalent if g is obtained from f by a linear substitution with matrix in SL_2(ℤ); this preserves the discriminant.

nodes.name: Quadratic number field
nodes.description: A number field of the form ℚ(√d) where d is a squarefree integer; its ring of integers is ℤ[(1+√d)/2] if d ≡ 1 mod 4, and ℤ[√d] otherwise.

nodes.name: Quaternion algebra
nodes.description: A 4-dimensional central simple algebra over a field F generated by i,j with i^2=a, j^2=b, ij=-ji for a,b ∈ F×; denoted (a,b)_F; splits (≅ M_2(F)) iff the norm form ax^2+by^2-abz^2 represents 1.

nodes.name: Ramification of primes
nodes.description: A prime p ∈ ℤ ramifies in O_K if pO_K = ∏ P_i^{e_i} with some e_i > 1; p is unramified if all e_i = 1; p is totally ramified if there is a single prime P with e = [K:ℚ].

nodes.name: Reduced binary quadratic form
nodes.description: A positive definite form ax^2+bxy+cy^2 with D<0 is reduced if |b| ≤ a ≤ c, and b ≥ 0 when |b|=a or a=c; each proper equivalence class contains a unique reduced form.

nodes.name: Relative Brauer group
nodes.description: For a field extension K/F, the relative Brauer group Br(K/F) = ker(Br(F) → Br(K)) consists of classes of CSAs over F split by K; Br(F) = ∪_K Br(K/F) over all finite extensions K/F.

nodes.name: Relative Brauer group for cyclic extensions
nodes.description: If K/F is a cyclic Galois extension of degree n with generator σ, then Br(K/F) ≅ F×/N_{K/F}(K×); every element is represented by a cyclic algebra (K/F, σ, a) for some a ∈ F×.

nodes.name: Restriction and corestriction maps
nodes.description: For a subgroup H ≤ G: restriction res: H^n(G,M) → H^n(H,M) and corestriction cor: H^n(H,M) → H^n(G,M) satisfy cor ∘ res = [G:H]; these are fundamental maps in group cohomology.

nodes.name: Riemann's inequality
nodes.description: For any divisor D on a smooth projective curve C of genus g, l(D) >= deg(D) + 1 - g, with equality for divisors of sufficiently large degree.

nodes.name: Riemann-Roch space
nodes.description: For a divisor D on C, L(D) = {f in k(C)* : div(f) + D >= 0} union {0}, a finite-dimensional k-vector space whose dimension l(D) measures sections of the associated line bundle.

nodes.name: Riemann-Roch theorem for algebraic curves
nodes.description: For a smooth projective curve C of genus g and divisor D, l(D) - l(K_C - D) = deg(D) - g + 1, where K_C is a canonical divisor.

nodes.name: Second cohomology group H²(G,M)
nodes.description: H²(G,M) classifies equivalence classes of factor sets (2-cocycles) f: G×G → M modulo 2-coboundaries; equivalently classifies group extensions 1 → M → E → G → 1 with given G-action on M.

nodes.name: Segre embedding
nodes.description: The map P^m x P^n -> P^{mn+m+n} sending ([x_i],[y_j]) to [x_i*y_j]; realizes the product of projective spaces as a projective variety.

nodes.name: Semisimple decomposition via idempotents
nodes.function_signature: (Semisimple ring R) → (Central primitive idempotent decomposition 1 = e_1 + ... + e_k)
nodes.description: In a semisimple ring R ≅ ∏ M_{n_i}(D_i), the identity 1 = e_1 + ... + e_k decomposes into central primitive idempotents corresponding to the simple factors; each Re_i is a minimal two-sided ideal.

nodes.name: Semisimplicity and tensor products
nodes.description: If A is a central simple algebra over F and B is a semisimple F-algebra, then A ⊗_F B is semisimple; the tensor product of two central simple algebras over F is again central simple.

nodes.name: Splitting field of a central simple algebra
nodes.description: A field extension K/F such that A ⊗_F K ≅ M_n(K); every CSA is split by some finite separable extension, and K splits A iff A ⊗_F K is trivial in Br(K).

nodes.name: Splitting field of a polynomial over a finite field
nodes.function_signature: (Polynomial f(x) ∈ ℤ[x], Prime p) → (Factorization of (p) in O_K)
nodes.description: The technique of factoring a polynomial f(x) ∈ ℤ[x] modulo a prime p to determine the splitting of (p) in O_K = ℤ[α]/f(α) via Kummer's criterion; the degrees of irreducible factors give the inertia degrees.

nodes.name: Splitting of primes
nodes.description: A prime p in ℤ splits in O_K as pO_K = P_1^{e_1}...P_g^{e_g} with ∑ e_i f_i = [K:ℚ] where f_i = [O_K/P_i : ℤ/p]; p splits completely if g = [K:ℚ] (all e_i = f_i = 1).

nodes.name: Tensor product of algebras
nodes.description: For F-algebras A and B, the tensor product A ⊗_F B is an F-algebra with multiplication (a₁⊗b₁)(a₂⊗b₂) = a₁a₂ ⊗ b₁b₂; preserves simplicity and centrality when both factors are central simple.

nodes.name: Tor and flatness criterion
nodes.description: An R-module M is flat if and only if Tor_1^R(M,R/I) = 0 for every finitely generated ideal I; equivalently Tor_1^R(M,N) = 0 for all R-modules N.

nodes.name: Trace map Tr_{K/F}
nodes.description: For a finite extension K/F, Tr_{K/F}(α) = ∑_σ σ(α) summed over all F-embeddings σ: K → F̄; an F-linear map K → F used to define the discriminant and different.

nodes.name: Units of quadratic number fields
nodes.description: The group of units of the ring of integers of ℚ(√d): for d < 0, it is finite ({±1} or {±1, ±i} or the 6th roots of unity); for d > 0, it is {±ε^n : n ∈ ℤ} for a fundamental unit ε.

nodes.name: Universal coefficients theorem (algebraic)
nodes.description: For a chain complex C• of free abelian groups, there are natural short exact sequences 0 → H_n(C)⊗G → H_n(C;G) → Tor_1(H_{n-1}(C),G) → 0 and 0 → Ext^1(H_{n-1}(C),G) → H^n(C;G) → Hom(H_n(C),G) → 0, both split.

nodes.name: Veronese embedding
nodes.description: The map v_d: P^n -> P^N sending [x_0:...:x_n] to all monomials of degree d, where N = binom(n+d,d)-1; an embedding whose image is a projective variety.

nodes.name: Wedderburn's main theorem
nodes.description: If R is a finite-dimensional associative algebra over a field of characteristic 0, then R contains a semisimple subalgebra S such that R = S ⊕ rad(R) as vector spaces, with S ≅ R/rad(R).

nodes.name: Wedderburn's theorem (semisimple rings)
nodes.description: A left semisimple ring R with identity is isomorphic to a finite product M_{n_1}(D_1) × ... × M_{n_k}(D_k) of full matrix rings over division rings D_i; the factors are unique up to order and isomorphism.

nodes.name: Wedderburn-Artin radical
nodes.description: For a left Artinian ring R, rad(R) is the sum of all nilpotent left ideals; it is the unique maximal nilpotent two-sided ideal, and R/rad(R) is semisimple.

nodes.name: Weierstrass equation
nodes.description: A model y^2 = x^3 + ax + b (char != 2,3) or y^2 + a_1 xy + a_3 y = x^3 + a_2 x^2 + a_4 x + a_6 for an elliptic curve, obtained via Riemann-Roch; nonsingular iff discriminant != 0.

nodes.name: Weil differential (repartition)
nodes.description: A k-linear functional on the adele space of k(C) that vanishes on the adeles of bounded denominators at each place, used to define the canonical class and prove Riemann-Roch.

nodes.name: Zariski topology on Spec(R)
nodes.description: The topology on Spec(R) with closed sets V(I) = {p : p supset I} and basis of open sets D(f) = {p : f not in p}; Spec(R) is always quasi-compact.

nodes.name: Zariski topology on affine space
nodes.description: The topology on k^n (or an affine variety V) where closed sets are affine algebraic sets V(I); has very few open sets (not Hausdorff except for finite sets) but is Noetherian.

nodes.name: Zariski topology on projective space
nodes.description: The topology on P^n where closed sets are V(I) for homogeneous ideals I of k[X_0,...,X_n]; the projective analog of the affine Zariski topology.

nodes.name: Zariski's theorem on nonsingular points
nodes.description: A point P on an irreducible variety V is nonsingular iff the local ring O_{V,P} is a regular local ring; equivalently, dim(m_P/m_P^2) = dim(V), and nonsingular points form a dense open set.

nodes.name: adele of a function field
nodes.description: An element of the restricted direct product of completions of the function field k(C) at all places (discrete valuations), used in the proof of Riemann-Roch.

nodes.name: adelic Dirichlet unit theorem
nodes.description: The compactness of J_K^1/K* implies that the unit group O_K* modulo torsion is a free abelian group of rank r_1+r_2-1, where r_1 and r_2 count real and complex places.

nodes.name: adelic finiteness of class number
nodes.description: The compactness of J_K^1/K* implies the class group Cl(K) = J_K / (K* * prod O_v*) is finite, giving the adelic proof of finiteness of the class number.

nodes.name: affine variety
nodes.description: An irreducible affine algebraic set, i.e., a set V(p) for a prime ideal p in k[x_1,...,x_n]; equivalently, one that cannot be written as a union of two proper closed subsets.

nodes.name: algebraic curve
nodes.description: An irreducible algebraic variety of dimension 1; equivalently, defined by a function field of transcendence degree 1 over the base field, studied via its discrete valuations.

nodes.name: birational equivalence of smooth projective curves
nodes.description: Two smooth projective curves are birationally equivalent if and only if they are isomorphic; a rational map from a smooth curve to a projective variety is always a morphism.

nodes.name: canonical embedding
nodes.description: For a smooth curve C of genus g >= 2 that is not hyperelliptic, the complete linear system |K_C| defines an embedding C -> P^{g-1} called the canonical embedding.

nodes.name: classification of irreducible curves
nodes.description: Every irreducible curve is birationally equivalent to a smooth projective curve, unique up to isomorphism; the category of smooth projective curves is equivalent to the category of function fields of transcendence degree 1.

nodes.name: compactness of adele quotient
nodes.description: The quotient A_K / K (adeles modulo the diagonally embedded global field) is compact, encoding both the strong approximation theorem and finiteness results.

nodes.name: compactness of idele class group (norm-one)
nodes.description: The quotient J_K^1 / K* of norm-one ideles modulo K* is compact, simultaneously encoding the finiteness of the class number and the Dirichlet unit theorem.

nodes.name: complete linear system determines morphism
nodes.description: A base-point-free complete linear system |D| on a smooth curve C defines a morphism phi_D: C -> P^{l(D)-1}; the morphism is an embedding iff |D| separates points and tangent vectors.

nodes.name: completion of a valued field
nodes.description: The unique (up to isomorphism) complete valued field K-hat containing K as a dense subfield with the absolute value extending that of K, constructed as the quotient of Cauchy sequences by null sequences.

nodes.name: decomposition field
nodes.description: The fixed field L^{D(P|p)} of the decomposition group, the largest intermediate field where p does not split further below P.

nodes.name: degree of a divisor
nodes.description: For a divisor D = sum n_P * P on a curve, deg(D) = sum n_P; the degree map is a group homomorphism Div(C) -> Z.

nodes.name: degree of a morphism of curves
nodes.description: For a nonconstant morphism f: C -> C' of smooth projective curves, deg(f) = [k(C):f*k(C')], the degree of the induced function field extension.

nodes.name: degree of a principal divisor is zero
nodes.description: For any nonzero rational function f on a smooth projective curve C, deg(div(f)) = 0; equivalently, f has as many zeros as poles counted with multiplicity.

nodes.name: degree of a projective variety
nodes.description: For a projective variety V of dimension d, deg(V) = d! times the leading coefficient of its Hilbert polynomial; equals the number of intersection points with a generic linear subspace of complementary dimension.

nodes.name: different of an extension
nodes.description: The ideal D_{L/K} in O_L that is the inverse of the fractional ideal {x in L : Tr_{L/K}(x*O_L) subset O_K}, measuring ramification of L/K.

nodes.name: dimension of an affine variety
nodes.description: The Krull dimension of the coordinate ring k[V], equivalently the transcendence degree of the function field k(V) over k for an irreducible variety V.

nodes.name: discriminant of an extension
nodes.description: The ideal d_{L/K} = N_{L/K}(D_{L/K}) in O_K, the norm of the different; a prime p ramifies in L/K if and only if p divides d_{L/K}.

nodes.name: divisor class group of a curve
nodes.description: The quotient group Cl(C) = Div(C) / Prin(C) of divisors modulo principal divisors on C; its degree-zero part Cl^0(C) is the Jacobian.

nodes.name: effective divisor
nodes.description: A divisor D = sum n_P * P where all coefficients n_P >= 0; written D >= 0.

nodes.name: elimination ideal
nodes.description: The l-th elimination ideal of I subset k[x_1,...,x_n] is I_l = I intersect k[x_{l+1},...,x_n], obtained by eliminating the first l variables.

nodes.name: elimination theorem
nodes.description: If G is a Gröbner basis for I with respect to a lexicographic order with x_1 > ... > x_n, then G intersect k[x_{l+1},...,x_n] is a Gröbner basis for the l-th elimination ideal I_l.

nodes.name: elliptic curve (genus-one curve with point)
nodes.description: A smooth projective curve of genus 1 together with a specified rational point O, admitting a group law making it an abelian variety of dimension 1.

nodes.name: equivalence of absolute values
nodes.description: Two absolute values |·|_1 and |·|_2 on K are equivalent if they define the same topology, which holds iff |·|_2 = |·|_1^s for some s > 0.

nodes.name: extension theorem
nodes.description: Under suitable conditions on the leading coefficients, a solution of the elimination ideal I_l can be extended to a solution of I by finding values for the eliminated variables; partial converse of the elimination theorem.

nodes.name: function field of an algebraic curve
nodes.description: The field k(C) of rational functions on an irreducible curve C, a finitely generated extension of k of transcendence degree 1; determines the curve up to birational equivalence.

nodes.name: fundamental identity for valuations
nodes.description: For a finite extension L/K of number fields and a prime p of K, the sum of e(P_i|p)*f(P_i|p) over all primes P_i of L above p equals [L:K].

nodes.name: fundamental theorem for infinite Galois extensions
nodes.description: For a Galois extension L/K, there is an inclusion-reversing bijection between intermediate fields K subset F subset L and closed subgroups H of Gal(L/K) in the Krull topology, via F <-> Gal(L/F) and H <-> L^H.

nodes.name: generic point of a scheme
nodes.description: For an irreducible scheme X = Spec(R/p), the point eta = p in Spec(R) whose closure is all of X; the stalk O_{X,eta} is the function field of X.

nodes.name: genus of an algebraic curve
nodes.description: The nonneg integer g such that Riemann's inequality l(D) >= deg(D) + 1 - g holds for all divisors D, and g is the smallest such integer; equals the geometric genus.

nodes.name: geometric dimension (Noetherian topological space)
nodes.description: The supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets Z_0 subset Z_1 subset ... subset Z_d in a Noetherian topological space; agrees with Krull dimension for affine varieties.

nodes.name: homogeneous coordinate ring
nodes.description: The graded ring S(V) = k[X_0,...,X_n]/I(V) for a projective variety V, where I(V) is the homogeneous ideal of V; a graded integral domain.

nodes.name: homogeneous ideal
nodes.description: An ideal I of k[X_0,...,X_n] generated by homogeneous polynomials, equivalently I = direct sum (I intersect k[X_0,...,X_n]_d); needed to define projective algebraic sets.

nodes.name: homogeneous polynomial
nodes.description: A polynomial F in k[X_0,...,X_n] where every monomial has the same total degree d; satisfies F(lambda*x) = lambda^d * F(x).

nodes.name: hyperelliptic curve
nodes.description: A smooth projective curve C of genus g >= 2 admitting a degree-2 morphism to P^1; equivalently, C has a divisor D of degree 2 with l(D) >= 2.

nodes.name: hypersurface
nodes.description: The zero locus V(f) of a single irreducible polynomial f in k[x_1,...,x_n] or a single homogeneous polynomial in projective space; has codimension 1.

nodes.name: ideal of an algebraic set
nodes.description: I(V) = {f in k[x_1,...,x_n] : f(P)=0 for all P in V}, a radical ideal; by the Nullstellensatz, I(V(J)) = sqrt(J).

nodes.name: inertia field
nodes.description: The fixed field L^{I(P|p)} of the inertia group, the largest intermediate field where p is unramified below P.

nodes.name: infinite Galois group
nodes.description: The Galois group Gal(L/K) of an infinite Galois extension L/K, equipped with the Krull topology making it a profinite group isomorphic to lim_F Gal(F/K) over finite Galois subextensions F.

nodes.name: intersection multiplicity (two curves)
nodes.description: For curves F and G in P^2 meeting at P, I(P; F,G) = dim_k O_{P^2,P}/(F,G), the dimension of the local ring quotient; it is symmetric and additive.

nodes.name: intersections in projective space
nodes.description: Two projective varieties in P^n of dimensions r and s with r+s >= n have nonempty intersection; more precisely, every component of the intersection has dimension >= r+s-n.

nodes.name: irreducible decomposition
nodes.description: Every algebraic set V can be written uniquely as a finite union V = V_1 union ... union V_r of irreducible components (maximal irreducible closed subsets), with no V_i contained in V_j for i != j.

nodes.name: linear system of divisors
nodes.description: The projective space |D| = P(L(D)) of effective divisors linearly equivalent to D on a curve C; has dimension l(D)-1 and determines maps to projective space.

nodes.name: local ring at a point of a variety
nodes.description: The ring O_{V,P} of rational functions regular at P, a local ring with maximal ideal m_P = {f in O_{V,P} : f(P)=0}; isomorphic to the localization of k[V] at the maximal ideal of P.

nodes.name: localization of a ring at a prime
nodes.description: The local ring R_p obtained by inverting all elements not in a prime ideal p; its spectrum is the set of primes contained in p, modeling a neighborhood of p in Spec(R).

nodes.name: locally ringed space
nodes.description: A topological space X equipped with a sheaf of rings O_X such that every stalk O_{X,x} is a local ring; the category in which schemes live.

nodes.name: monomial order
nodes.description: A total order on the monomials of k[x_1,...,x_n] that is compatible with multiplication and is a well-ordering; examples include lexicographic, graded lexicographic, and graded reverse lexicographic orders.

nodes.name: morphism of affine schemes
nodes.description: Morphisms Spec(S) -> Spec(R) of affine schemes correspond bijectively to ring homomorphisms R -> S; the functor Spec is a fully faithful contravariant functor from commutative rings to affine schemes.

nodes.name: morphism of affine varieties
nodes.description: A map phi: V -> W between affine varieties given by phi(P) = (f_1(P),...,f_m(P)) for polynomials f_i; equivalently, a map inducing a k-algebra homomorphism phi*: k[W] -> k[V].

nodes.name: morphism of projective varieties
nodes.description: A map phi: V -> W between projective varieties that is locally given by homogeneous polynomials of the same degree; a continuous map in the Zariski topology.

nodes.name: multivariate division algorithm
nodes.function_signature: (Polynomial f, Ordered tuple (g_1,...,g_s), Monomial order) → (Quotients a_i, Remainder r)
nodes.description: Given a polynomial f and an ordered tuple (g_1,...,g_s) with a fixed monomial order, produces f = sum a_i*g_i + r where no term of r is divisible by any LT(g_i); the remainder depends on the ordering of generators unless they form a Gröbner basis.

nodes.name: nonsingular point of a variety
nodes.description: A point P on a variety V where the local ring O_{V,P} is a regular local ring, equivalently dim(m_P/m_P^2) = dim(V).

nodes.name: normalization of a curve
nodes.description: For an irreducible curve C, its normalization C~ is the unique smooth curve with a birational morphism C~ -> C that is an isomorphism away from the singular points of C.

nodes.name: p-adic absolute value
nodes.description: The absolute value |x|_p = p^{-v_p(x)} on Q, where v_p(x) is the p-adic valuation measuring the exact power of p dividing x.

nodes.name: p-adic integers
nodes.description: The ring Z_p of p-adic integers, defined as the inverse limit of Z/p^n Z, forming a complete local ring with maximal ideal (p).

nodes.name: p-adic numbers
nodes.description: The field Q_p obtained as the fraction field of Z_p, or equivalently as the completion of Q with respect to the p-adic absolute value |·|_p.

nodes.name: place of a field
nodes.description: An equivalence class of nontrivial absolute values on a field K; for a number field, places are either finite (nonarchimedean, from primes) or infinite (archimedean, from embeddings).

nodes.name: presheaf on a topological space
nodes.description: A contravariant functor from the category of open sets of X (with inclusions) to a target category (e.g., abelian groups, rings), assigning sections F(U) and restriction maps.

nodes.name: prime spectrum Spec(R)
nodes.description: The set of all prime ideals of a commutative ring R, equipped with the Zariski topology where closed sets are V(I) = {p in Spec(R) : I subset p} for ideals I; the basic space underlying a scheme.

nodes.name: projective algebraic set
nodes.description: The set V(S) in P^n of common zeros of a set S of homogeneous polynomials; closed in the Zariski topology on P^n.

nodes.name: projective closure
nodes.description: The Zariski closure of an affine variety V subset A^n in projective space P^n under the standard embedding A^n -> P^n; obtained by homogenizing the defining polynomials.

nodes.name: projective plane curve
nodes.description: The zero locus V(F) in P^2 of a nonconstant homogeneous polynomial F(X,Y,Z), considered up to scalar multiples; its degree is the degree of F.

nodes.name: projective space P^n
nodes.description: The set of equivalence classes of nonzero points in k^{n+1} under scalar multiplication, i.e., P^n(k) = (k^{n+1} - {0}) / k*; the natural domain for homogeneous polynomials.

nodes.name: projective variety
nodes.description: An irreducible projective algebraic set, i.e., V(p) for a homogeneous prime ideal p not equal to the irrelevant ideal; a complete algebraic variety.

nodes.name: ramification divisor
nodes.description: For a morphism f: C -> C' of curves, the divisor R = sum (e_P-1)*P on C measuring the ramification; appears in the Hurwitz formula as deg(R) = 2g-2 - deg(f)*(2g'-2).

nodes.name: rational curve
nodes.description: A smooth projective curve of genus 0; by Riemann-Roch, it is isomorphic to P^1.

nodes.name: rational function on a variety
nodes.description: An equivalence class of pairs (U, f) where U is a nonempty open set of V and f is a regular function on U, with (U,f) ~ (U',f') if f=f' on U intersect U'; elements of the function field k(V).

nodes.name: rational map of varieties
nodes.description: An equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subsets of a variety V to W; a rational map V --> W may not be defined everywhere.

nodes.name: regular function at a point
nodes.description: A rational function f on V that is defined (representable as g/h with h(P)!=0) at a point P; the set of regular functions at P forms the local ring O_{V,P}.

nodes.name: residue class degree
nodes.description: For an extension L/K with primes P|p, the residue class degree f(P|p) = [O_P/P : O_p/p] is the degree of the residue field extension.

nodes.name: separable closure
nodes.description: The maximal separable subextension K^{sep} of an algebraic closure K-bar of K; K-bar/K^{sep} is purely inseparable.

nodes.name: sheaf on a topological space
nodes.description: A presheaf F on X satisfying: (1) if s|_{U_i}=0 for all U_i in an open cover of U, then s=0 (locality); (2) if s_i in F(U_i) agree on overlaps, they glue to s in F(U) (gluing).

nodes.name: singular point of a variety
nodes.description: A point P on a variety V where dim(m_P/m_P^2) > dim(V), equivalently where the Jacobian matrix does not have maximal rank; the locus of singular points is a proper closed subset.

nodes.name: splitting of primes in extensions
nodes.description: For a prime p of O_K in an extension L/K, the factorization p*O_L = P_1^{e_1} ... P_g^{e_g}; primes can split, remain inert, or ramify depending on the e_i and f_i.

nodes.name: structure sheaf on Spec(R)
nodes.description: The sheaf O on Spec(R) with O(D(f)) = R_f (localization at f) and stalks O_p = R_p (localization at prime p); makes (Spec(R), O) into a locally ringed space.

nodes.name: tangent space (Zariski)
nodes.description: The Zariski tangent space at a point P of a variety V is (m_P/m_P^2)*, the dual of the cotangent space m_P/m_P^2 of the local ring O_{V,P}; its dimension equals dim(V) iff P is nonsingular.

nodes.name: tensor product decomposition of completions
nodes.description: For a finite separable extension L/K and a place v of K, K_v tensor_K L is isomorphic to the product of completions L_w over all places w of L above v.

nodes.name: totally ramified extension
nodes.description: An extension L/K of valued fields where e(P|p) = [L:K] and f(P|p) = 1, so the entire degree is accounted for by ramification.

nodes.name: unramified extension
nodes.description: An extension L/K of valued fields where e(P|p)=1 and the residue field extension is separable, so ramification index is trivial.

nodes.name: zeta function of a variety over a finite field
nodes.description: Z(V,t) = exp(sum_{m>=1} |V(F_{q^m})| * t^m / m), a formal power series encoding point counts of V over all finite extensions of F_q; rational by the Weil conjectures.

nodes.name: Sum of ideals
nodes.description: The sum 𝔞 + 𝔟 of two ideals is the smallest ideal containing both, equal to {a + b : a ∈ 𝔞, b ∈ 𝔟}.

nodes.name: Product of ideals
nodes.description: The product 𝔞𝔟 of two ideals is the ideal generated by all products ab with a ∈ 𝔞, b ∈ 𝔟.

nodes.name: Ideal quotient (colon ideal)
nodes.description: The ideal quotient (𝔞 : 𝔟) is the set of all ring elements x such that x𝔟 ⊆ 𝔞, forming an ideal of A.

nodes.name: Coprime ideals
nodes.description: Two ideals 𝔞, 𝔟 in a commutative ring are coprime (comaximal) if 𝔞 + 𝔟 = (1).

nodes.name: Prime avoidance lemma
nodes.description: If an ideal 𝔞 is contained in a finite union of prime ideals 𝔭₁ ∪ ··· ∪ 𝔭ₙ, then 𝔞 ⊆ 𝔭ᵢ for some i.

nodes.name: Extension and contraction of ideals
nodes.description: For a ring homomorphism f: A → B, the extension 𝔞ᵉ of an ideal 𝔞 ⊆ A is the ideal 𝔞B generated by f(𝔞), and the contraction 𝔟ᶜ of an ideal 𝔟 ⊆ B is f⁻¹(𝔟).

nodes.name: Jacobson radical characterization
nodes.description: An element x belongs to the Jacobson radical J(A) if and only if 1 − xy is a unit in A for every y ∈ A.

nodes.name: Characterization of local rings
nodes.description: A ring is local if and only if its set of non-units forms an ideal, equivalently if it has a unique maximal ideal.

nodes.name: Radical equals intersection of primes containing ideal
nodes.description: The radical √𝔞 of an ideal 𝔞 equals the intersection of all prime ideals containing 𝔞.

nodes.name: Restriction of scalars
nodes.description: Given a ring homomorphism f: A → B and a B-module N, restriction of scalars gives N the structure of an A-module via a·n = f(a)·n.

nodes.name: Algebra over a ring
nodes.description: An A-algebra is a ring B together with a ring homomorphism f: A → B, making B simultaneously an A-module and a ring compatibly.

nodes.name: Ideal-theoretic characterization of flatness
nodes.description: An A-module M is flat if and only if for every ideal 𝔞 of A, the natural map 𝔞 ⊗_A M → M is injective.

nodes.name: Ring of fractions
nodes.description: For a multiplicative subset S of a ring A, the ring of fractions S⁻¹A consists of equivalence classes of pairs (a, s) with a ∈ A, s ∈ S, under the relation (a,s) ~ (b,t) iff u(at − bs) = 0 for some u ∈ S.

nodes.name: Module of fractions
nodes.description: For a multiplicative subset S and an A-module M, the module of fractions S⁻¹M consists of equivalence classes m/s with the natural S⁻¹A-module structure, isomorphic to S⁻¹A ⊗_A M.

nodes.name: Local property of modules
nodes.description: A property P of modules or ring elements is local if it holds globally precisely when it holds after localization at every prime (or every maximal) ideal.

nodes.name: Flatness is a local property
nodes.description: An A-module M is flat if and only if M_𝔭 is a flat A_𝔭-module for every prime ideal 𝔭 of A.

nodes.name: Prime correspondence under localization
nodes.description: The prime ideals of S⁻¹A are in inclusion-preserving bijection with the prime ideals of A that do not meet S, via 𝔭 ↦ S⁻¹𝔭.

nodes.name: Integral closure is a subring
nodes.description: The set of elements in a ring extension B/A that are integral over A forms a subring of B (the integral closure of A in B).

nodes.name: Equivalences for integral elements
nodes.description: An element x ∈ B is integral over A iff A[x] is a finitely generated A-module, iff A[x] is contained in a finitely generated A-submodule of B, iff there exists a faithful A[x]-module finitely generated over A.

nodes.name: Characterization of valuation rings
nodes.description: An integral domain V with fraction field K is a valuation ring if and only if for every x ∈ K×, either x ∈ V or x⁻¹ ∈ V, equivalently if its ideals are totally ordered by inclusion.

nodes.name: Integral closure via valuation rings
nodes.description: The integral closure of an integral domain A in its field of fractions equals the intersection of all valuation rings of K containing A.

nodes.name: Noetherian characterization via exact sequences
nodes.description: In a short exact sequence 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0 of A-modules, M is Noetherian if and only if both M' and M'' are Noetherian.

nodes.name: Hilbert basis theorem for power series rings
nodes.description: If A is a Noetherian ring, then the formal power series ring A[[x]] is also Noetherian.

nodes.name: Irreducible ideal
nodes.description: An ideal 𝔞 is irreducible if 𝔞 = 𝔟 ∩ 𝔠 implies 𝔞 = 𝔟 or 𝔞 = 𝔠; it cannot be written as a non-trivial intersection of two strictly larger ideals.

nodes.name: Irreducible ideals are primary in Noetherian rings
nodes.description: In a Noetherian ring, every irreducible ideal is primary.

nodes.name: Every ideal is a finite intersection of irreducible ideals
nodes.description: In a Noetherian ring, every ideal can be expressed as a finite intersection of irreducible ideals.

nodes.name: Symbolic power of a prime ideal
nodes.description: The n-th symbolic power 𝔭^(n) of a prime ideal 𝔭 is the 𝔭-primary component of 𝔭ⁿ, equivalently 𝔭^(n) = 𝔭ⁿA_𝔭 ∩ A.

nodes.name: Artinian rings have Krull dimension zero
nodes.description: A commutative ring is Artinian if and only if it is Noetherian and has Krull dimension zero (every prime ideal is maximal).

nodes.name: Structure theorem for Artinian rings
nodes.description: Every commutative Artinian ring is uniquely (up to isomorphism) a finite direct product of Artinian local rings.

nodes.name: Artinian ring has finitely many maximal ideals
nodes.description: A commutative Artinian ring has only finitely many maximal ideals.

nodes.name: Characterizations of discrete valuation rings
nodes.description: A Noetherian local domain of dimension 1 is a DVR iff it is integrally closed, iff its maximal ideal is principal, iff it is a regular local ring of dimension 1.

nodes.name: Characterizations of Dedekind domains
nodes.description: A Noetherian domain of dimension ≤ 1 is Dedekind iff it is integrally closed, iff every primary ideal is a prime power, iff every localization at a nonzero prime is a DVR.

nodes.name: Filtered module
nodes.description: A module M over a filtered ring A equipped with a decreasing sequence of submodules M = M₀ ⊇ M₁ ⊇ ··· compatible with the filtration on A.

nodes.name: Completion is exact on finitely generated modules
nodes.description: For a Noetherian ring A with 𝔞-adic topology, the completion functor M ↦ M̂ is exact on the category of finitely generated A-modules.

nodes.name: Flatness of completion
nodes.description: For a Noetherian ring A, the 𝔞-adic completion Â is a flat A-algebra.

nodes.name: Completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian
nodes.description: The 𝔞-adic completion of a Noetherian ring is again Noetherian.

nodes.name: Height of a prime ideal
nodes.description: The height of a prime ideal 𝔭 is the supremum of lengths of chains of prime ideals 𝔭₀ ⊊ 𝔭₁ ⊊ ··· ⊊ 𝔭ₙ = 𝔭 descending from 𝔭.

nodes.name: Coheight of a prime ideal
nodes.description: The coheight of a prime ideal 𝔭 in a ring A is the Krull dimension of A/𝔭, the supremum of lengths of chains of primes ascending from 𝔭.

nodes.name: Regular local ring is an integral domain
nodes.description: Every regular local ring is an integral domain.

nodes.name: Dimension inequality for ring extensions
nodes.description: If A ⊆ B are Noetherian domains and 𝔮 is a prime of B lying over 𝔭 in A, then ht(𝔮) + tr.deg(κ(𝔮)/κ(𝔭)) ≤ ht(𝔭) + tr.deg(B/A).

nodes.name: Primary decomposition technique
nodes.function_signature: (Ideal or submodule in a Noetherian ring) → (Intersection of primary components with known associated primes)
nodes.description: Decomposing an ideal or submodule into primary components to study its associated primes and reduce problems to the primary case.

nodes.name: Integral closure technique
nodes.function_signature: (Ring extension A ⊆ B, algebraic/finiteness conditions) → (Properties of the integral closure of A in B)
nodes.description: Passing to the integral closure to improve ring-theoretic properties while preserving dimension and prime structure.

nodes.name: Noetherian induction
nodes.function_signature: (Property P on ideals of a Noetherian ring) → (P holds for all ideals by induction on the poset of ideals)
nodes.description: Proving a statement for all ideals of a Noetherian ring by assuming it fails and taking a maximal counterexample via the ACC.

nodes.name: Completion technique
nodes.function_signature: (Local ring (A, 𝔪), local property to prove) → (Result via completed ring Â and its improved structure)
nodes.description: Passing to the 𝔞-adic completion of a local ring to exploit completeness, Hensel's lemma, and Cohen structure theorems.

nodes.name: Graded/associated-graded technique
nodes.function_signature: (Filtered ring/module with 𝔞-adic filtration) → (Properties of gr_𝔞(A) transferred back)
nodes.description: Passing from a filtered ring or module to its associated graded object to reduce questions about a local ring to questions about a polynomial ring.

nodes.name: Hilbert function method
nodes.function_signature: (Graded module or local ring with 𝔪-primary ideal) → (Dimension, multiplicity, and growth data from the Hilbert polynomial)
nodes.description: Using the Hilbert function or Hilbert-Samuel polynomial to extract numerical invariants from graded or filtered algebraic structures.

nodes.name: Determinant trick
nodes.function_signature: (Finitely generated module M, endomorphism φ with φ(M) ⊆ IM) → (Monic relation φⁿ + a₁φⁿ⁻¹ + ··· + aₙ = 0 with aᵢ ∈ Iⁱ)
nodes.description: Applying the Cayley-Hamilton theorem to an endomorphism of a finitely generated module to produce integral dependence or annihilation relations.

nodes.name: Residue field
nodes.description: The residue field of a prime ideal 𝔭 in a commutative ring R, defined as the quotient of the localization R_𝔭 by its maximal ideal 𝔭R_𝔭.

nodes.name: Idempotents and connected components of Spec
nodes.description: The connected components of Spec(R) correspond bijectively to primitive idempotents of R; R decomposes as a product of rings iff Spec(R) is disconnected.

nodes.name: Prime filtration of a module
nodes.description: A chain 0 = M₀ ⊂ M₁ ⊂ ··· ⊂ Mₙ = M with each successive quotient Mᵢ/Mᵢ₋₁ ≅ R/𝔭ᵢ for prime ideals 𝔭ᵢ; exists for every finitely generated module over a Noetherian ring.

nodes.name: Finiteness of associated primes
nodes.description: For a finitely generated module M over a Noetherian ring R, the set Ass(M) of associated primes is finite.

nodes.name: Zero divisors equal union of associated primes
nodes.description: For a finitely generated module M over a Noetherian ring, the set of zero divisors on M equals the union of the associated primes of M.

nodes.name: UFD implies integrally closed
nodes.description: Every unique factorization domain is integrally closed in its field of fractions.

nodes.name: Zariski's lemma
nodes.description: If k is a field and K is a finitely generated k-algebra that is also a field, then K is a finite (algebraic) extension of k.

nodes.name: Filtration of a module
nodes.description: A descending chain of submodules M = M₀ ⊇ M₁ ⊇ M₂ ⊇ ··· compatible with the ring filtration; the I-adic filtration Mₙ = IⁿM is the primary example.

nodes.name: Stable filtration (I-stable)
nodes.description: An I-filtration {Mₙ} is I-stable if Mₙ₊₁ = I·Mₙ for all sufficiently large n, equivalently the Rees module ⊕Mₙ is finitely generated over R[It].

nodes.name: Tangent cone
nodes.description: The associated graded ring of a local ring (R, 𝔪) with respect to the maximal ideal, whose Proj is the projectivized tangent cone at the corresponding point of a variety.

nodes.name: Localization is flat
nodes.description: For any multiplicative set S in a commutative ring R, the localization S⁻¹R is a flat R-algebra.

nodes.name: Flat base change for Tor
nodes.description: If R → S is a flat ring homomorphism, then Torᵢᴿ(M, N) ⊗_R S ≅ Torᵢˢ(M ⊗_R S, N ⊗_R S) for all i.

nodes.name: Lazard's theorem
nodes.description: An R-module is flat if and only if it is a filtered colimit of finitely generated free modules.

nodes.name: Flat equals locally free for finitely presented modules
nodes.description: A finitely presented module over a commutative ring is flat if and only if it is locally free (free after localization at every prime ideal).

nodes.name: Weierstrass preparation theorem (formal power series)
nodes.description: In k[[x₁,...,xₙ]], a power series distinguished of order d in xₙ factors uniquely as a unit times a Weierstrass polynomial of degree d in xₙ.

nodes.name: Lifting idempotents
nodes.function_signature: (Complete ring R, idempotent ē ∈ R/I) → (Idempotent e ∈ R with e mod I = ē)
nodes.description: Lifting an idempotent from R/I to the I-adically complete ring R by iterative Newton-type approximation, used for decomposing modules over complete local rings.

nodes.name: Embedding dimension
nodes.description: The minimal number of generators of the maximal ideal 𝔪 of a local ring (R, 𝔪, k), equal to dim_k(𝔪/𝔪²); a regular local ring has edim(R) = dim(R).

nodes.name: Fiber ring of a ring map
nodes.description: The fiber of a ring map φ: R → S over a prime 𝔭 of R, defined as κ(𝔭) ⊗_R S; its Spec is the scheme-theoretic fiber of Spec S → Spec R over 𝔭.

nodes.name: Total ring of fractions
nodes.description: The localization of R at the multiplicative set of all non-zero-divisors; generalizes the fraction field to rings that are not necessarily domains.

nodes.name: I-adic valuation
nodes.description: For a Noetherian ring R and ideal I with ∩Iⁿ = 0, the function assigning to each element the largest power of I containing it, inducing the I-adic topology.

nodes.name: Reduced ring
nodes.description: A commutative ring with no nonzero nilpotent elements, equivalently one whose nilradical is zero.

nodes.name: Homogeneous Nullstellensatz (projective Nullstellensatz)
nodes.description: A homogeneous ideal I in k[x₀,...,xₙ] over an algebraically closed field defines the empty projective variety iff rad(I) contains the irrelevant ideal (x₀,...,xₙ).

nodes.name: Rees algebra technique
nodes.function_signature: (Ring R, ideal I, I-filtration) → (Graded module over R[It] encoding filtration data)
nodes.description: Encoding an I-adic filtration as a graded module over the Rees algebra R[It] to reduce filtration questions to graded algebra; key to proving the Artin-Rees lemma.

nodes.name: Geometric interpretation of primary decomposition
nodes.description: Primary decomposition I = ∩Qᵢ decomposes V(I) into irreducible components (minimal primes) with embedded structure (embedded primes encoding nilpotent or higher-multiplicity behavior).

nodes.name: Module of finite length
nodes.description: A module admitting a composition series of finite length, equivalently both Noetherian and Artinian; the length ℓ(M) is additive on short exact sequences.

nodes.name: Completion is faithfully flat
nodes.description: For a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪), the 𝔪-adic completion R̂ is faithfully flat over R; in particular R → R̂ is injective and detects exactness.

nodes.name: Affine rings are universally catenary
nodes.description: Every finitely generated algebra over a field or over ℤ is universally catenary.

nodes.name: Krull dimension of a module
nodes.description: The Krull dimension of an R-module M, defined as the Krull dimension of the quotient ring R/Ann(M).

nodes.name: Codimension (height) of an ideal
nodes.description: The codimension of an ideal I in a ring R is the infimum of heights of prime ideals containing I.

nodes.name: Equidimensional ring
nodes.description: A Noetherian ring in which all minimal primes have the same coheight, equivalently all irreducible components of Spec(R) have the same dimension.

nodes.name: Dimension via 𝔪-primary ideals
nodes.description: The Krull dimension of a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) equals the minimum number of generators of an 𝔪-primary ideal.

nodes.name: Existence of systems of parameters
nodes.description: Every Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) of dimension d admits a system of parameters: d elements x₁,...,x_d generating an 𝔪-primary ideal.

nodes.name: Dimension drop by one element
nodes.description: If (R, 𝔪) is a Noetherian local ring and x ∈ 𝔪, then dim(R/(x)) ≥ dim(R) − 1, with equality when x avoids all minimal primes of maximal dimension.

nodes.name: Parameter ideal
nodes.description: An ideal in a Noetherian local ring of dimension d generated by a system of parameters; it is 𝔪-primary with exactly d generators.

nodes.name: Regular system of parameters
nodes.description: In a regular local ring (R, 𝔪), a system of parameters x₁,...,x_d that generates the maximal ideal 𝔪, equivalently whose images form a k-basis of 𝔪/𝔪².

nodes.name: Dimension of fibers of a ring map
nodes.description: For a local homomorphism φ: (R, 𝔪) → (S, 𝔫) of Noetherian local rings, dim(S) ≤ dim(R) + dim(S/𝔪S), with equality when φ is flat.

nodes.name: Serre's criterion for normality (R₁ + S₂)
nodes.description: A Noetherian ring is normal (integrally closed in its total ring of fractions) iff it satisfies R₁ (regular in codimension ≤ 1) and S₂ (depth ≥ min(2, ht 𝔭) at every prime 𝔭).

nodes.name: Serre's condition Rₖ
nodes.description: A Noetherian ring satisfies (Rₖ) if the localization R_𝔭 is a regular local ring for every prime 𝔭 of height at most k.

nodes.name: Serre's condition Sₖ
nodes.description: A Noetherian ring satisfies (Sₖ) if depth(R_𝔭) ≥ min(k, ht(𝔭)) for every prime ideal 𝔭; Cohen-Macaulay rings satisfy Sₖ for all k.

nodes.name: Serre's criterion for reducedness (R₀ + S₁)
nodes.description: A Noetherian ring is reduced if and only if it satisfies R₀ (regular at all minimal primes) and S₁ (no embedded associated primes of the zero ideal).

nodes.name: Divisor class group of a normal domain
nodes.description: The group of Weil divisor classes on a Noetherian normal domain R: the free abelian group on height-1 primes modulo principal divisors div(f).

nodes.name: Reflexive module
nodes.description: A finitely generated module M such that the canonical map M → M** = Hom(Hom(M, R), R) is an isomorphism; rank-1 reflexives over a normal domain correspond to divisorial ideals.

nodes.name: UFD iff trivial divisor class group
nodes.description: A Noetherian normal domain is a UFD if and only if its divisor class group Cl(R) is trivial, equivalently every height-1 prime ideal is principal.

nodes.name: Conductor ideal
nodes.description: For a reduced ring R with integral closure R̄, the conductor 𝔠 = {x ∈ R̄ : xR̄ ⊆ R} is the largest ideal of R̄ that is also an ideal of R.

nodes.name: Integral closure of a 1-dimensional Noetherian domain is Dedekind
nodes.description: The integral closure of a one-dimensional Noetherian domain in its fraction field is a Noetherian ring, hence a Dedekind domain.

nodes.name: Multiplicity one implies regularity
nodes.description: A Noetherian local ring has Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity e(R) = 1 if and only if it is a regular local ring.

nodes.name: Associativity formula for multiplicities
nodes.description: For a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) of dimension d and 𝔪-primary ideal q, e(q; M) = Σ_𝔭 e(q; R/𝔭)·ℓ_{R_𝔭}(M_𝔭), summed over minimal primes 𝔭 with dim(R/𝔭) = dim(M).

nodes.name: Reduction of an ideal
nodes.description: An ideal J ⊆ I is a reduction of I if JIⁿ = Iⁿ⁺¹ for some n ≥ 0; minimal reductions have exactly dim(R) generators and share the same multiplicity as I.

nodes.name: Noether normalization (Nagata version)
nodes.description: A version of Noether normalization for finitely generated algebras over any Noetherian ring, where the polynomial subring may require localization; due to Nagata.

nodes.name: Noether normalization for graded rings
nodes.description: For a finitely generated graded k-algebra S, there exist algebraically independent homogeneous elements y₁,...,y_d such that S is a finite module over k[y₁,...,y_d].

nodes.name: Finiteness of integral closure of affine domains
nodes.description: The integral closure of a finitely generated domain over a field (or over ℤ) in a finite extension of its fraction field is a finitely generated module.

nodes.name: Generic freeness lemma (Grothendieck)
nodes.description: If R is a Noetherian domain and M is a finitely generated R-algebra or R-module, then there exists nonzero f ∈ R such that M_f is free over R_f.

nodes.name: Dimension formula for affine domains
nodes.description: For a prime 𝔭 in a finitely generated domain R over a field k: ht(𝔭) + dim(R/𝔭) = dim(R).

nodes.name: Semicontinuity of fiber dimension
nodes.description: For a morphism of finite type between Noetherian schemes, the function y ↦ dim(f⁻¹(y)) is upper semicontinuous on the target.

nodes.name: Going-down for flat extensions
nodes.description: If R → S is a flat ring homomorphism, then the going-down property holds: primes in R that are contained in the contraction of a prime of S lift to primes of S.

nodes.name: Hilbert polynomial of a hypersurface
nodes.description: The Hilbert polynomial of a hypersurface V(f) ⊆ Pⁿ of degree d is P(t) = C(t+n,n) − C(t+n−d,n), so deg(V(f)) = d.

nodes.name: Dimension computation via parameter chains
nodes.function_signature: (Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪)) → (System of parameters and Krull dimension)
nodes.description: Computing Krull dimension by iteratively choosing elements avoiding minimal primes to reduce dimension by one at each step, building a system of parameters.

nodes.name: Extension theorem (elimination theory)
nodes.description: Conditions under which a partial solution in the elimination ideal extends to a full solution of the original polynomial system over an algebraically closed field.

nodes.name: Fiber dimension theorem
nodes.description: For a dominant morphism of irreducible varieties f: X → Y, every irreducible component of a fiber f⁻¹(y) has dimension at least dim(X) − dim(Y), with equality on a dense open set.

nodes.name: Lexicographic monomial order
nodes.description: A monomial order on k[x₁,...,xₙ] where x^α > x^β iff the leftmost nonzero entry of α − β is positive; favored for elimination but computationally expensive.

nodes.name: Graded reverse lexicographic order (grevlex)
nodes.description: A monomial order comparing first by total degree, then breaking ties by the rightmost nonzero entry of α − β being negative; the most efficient order for Gröbner basis computation.

nodes.name: Initial term (leading term)
nodes.description: The largest monomial term of a polynomial f with respect to a fixed monomial order >, written in(f) or LT(f).

nodes.name: Initial ideal
nodes.description: The monomial ideal generated by the initial terms of all nonzero elements of an ideal I; determines the Hilbert function and leading behavior of I.

nodes.name: S-polynomial
nodes.description: For polynomials f, g, the combination S(f,g) = (lcm(LM(f),LM(g))/LT(f))·f − (lcm(LM(f),LM(g))/LT(g))·g designed to cancel leading terms; central to Buchberger's algorithm.

nodes.name: Reduced Gröbner basis
nodes.description: A Gröbner basis where each element is monic and no monomial of any element lies in the initial ideal of the others; unique for a given ideal and monomial order.

nodes.name: Flat degeneration to initial ideal
nodes.description: There exists a flat one-parameter family over A¹ whose general fiber is R/I and special fiber is R/in(I), realizing the initial ideal as a flat degeneration preserving Hilbert function.

nodes.name: Dickson's lemma
nodes.description: Every monomial ideal in k[x₁,...,xₙ] is finitely generated, equivalently every antichain in (ℕⁿ, ≤) is finite.

nodes.name: Gröbner basis and syzygies technique
nodes.function_signature: (Gröbner basis G of ideal I, monomial order) → (Generators of first syzygy module syz(G))
nodes.description: Computing syzygies from a Gröbner basis by lifting S-polynomial reductions to syzygy relations, yielding free resolutions via Schreyer's theorem.

nodes.name: Universal derivation
nodes.description: The canonical R-derivation d: S → Ω_{S/R} such that every R-derivation from S to an S-module M factors uniquely through d, characterizing the module of Kähler differentials.

nodes.name: Conormal module I/I²
nodes.description: For a surjection S ↠ S/I, the S/I-module I/I² measuring first-order deformation of the ideal I; appears in the second exact sequence of Kähler differentials.

nodes.name: Kähler differentials of a polynomial ring
nodes.description: The module Ω_{R[x₁,...,xₙ]/R} is the free R[x₁,...,xₙ]-module of rank n with basis dx₁,...,dxₙ.

nodes.name: Kähler differentials and separability
nodes.description: A finite field extension L/K is separable if and only if Ω_{L/K} = 0; more generally dim_L Ω_{L/K} = tr.deg(L/K) for finitely generated field extensions.

nodes.name: Smoothness via Kähler differentials
nodes.description: A finitely presented k-algebra A (k perfect) is smooth over k iff Ω_{A/k} is projective of rank equal to dim(A).

nodes.name: Generic smoothness
nodes.description: A dominant morphism of varieties over a perfect field is smooth on a dense open subset of the source; equivalently, the generic fiber is geometrically regular.

nodes.name: Jacobian criterion for smoothness
nodes.description: For A = k[x₁,...,xₙ]/(f₁,...,fₘ) with k perfect, A is smooth at a prime 𝔭 iff the Jacobian matrix (∂fᵢ/∂xⱼ) has rank n − dim(A_𝔭) modulo 𝔭.

nodes.name: Koszul complex as tensor product
nodes.description: The Koszul complex K(x₁,...,xₙ; R) is isomorphic to the tensor product K(x₁;R) ⊗_R ··· ⊗_R K(xₙ;R) of one-element Koszul complexes.

nodes.name: Koszul homology
nodes.description: The homology groups Hᵢ(K(x₁,...,xₙ) ⊗ M) of the Koszul complex; H₀ = M/(x₁,...,xₙ)M and higher Hᵢ detect failure of the sequence to be regular.

nodes.name: Depth via Koszul homology
nodes.description: For a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) and ideal I = (x₁,...,xₙ), depth_I(M) = n − max{i : Hᵢ(x₁,...,xₙ; M) ≠ 0}.

nodes.name: Self-duality of the Koszul complex
nodes.description: The Koszul complex K(x₁,...,xₙ; R) is self-dual: Hom_R(Kᵢ, R) ≅ K_{n−i}, inducing isomorphisms Hᵢ(K) ≅ Hⁿ⁻ⁱ(K).

nodes.name: Koszul homology computes Tor
nodes.description: If x₁,...,xₙ is a regular sequence on R, then Hᵢ(x₁,...,xₙ; M) ≅ Torᵢᴿ(R/(x₁,...,xₙ), M) for all i.

nodes.name: Regular sequences are permutable in local rings
nodes.description: In a Noetherian local ring, any permutation of a regular sequence on a finitely generated module is again a regular sequence.

nodes.name: Grade of an ideal
nodes.description: The length of a maximal regular sequence in I on M, equal to min{i : Extⁱ_R(R/I, M) ≠ 0}; agrees with depth_I(M).

nodes.name: Depth inequality (depth ≤ dim)
nodes.description: For a finitely generated module M ≠ 0 over a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪), depth(M) ≤ dim(M); equality defines the Cohen-Macaulay condition.

nodes.name: Polynomial rings over Cohen-Macaulay rings are Cohen-Macaulay
nodes.description: If R is Cohen-Macaulay, then R[x₁,...,xₙ] and R[[x₁,...,xₙ]] are also Cohen-Macaulay; in particular k[x₁,...,xₙ] is Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.name: Flatness and depth formula
nodes.description: If φ: (R, 𝔪) → (S, 𝔫) is a flat local homomorphism and M is a finitely generated S-module, then depth_S(M) = depth_R(M) + depth_{S/𝔪S}(M/𝔪M).

nodes.name: Cohen-Macaulay rings are universally catenary
nodes.description: Every Cohen-Macaulay ring is universally catenary: all maximal chains of primes between any two comparable primes have the same length.

nodes.name: Cohen-Macaulay local rings are equidimensional
nodes.description: A Cohen-Macaulay local ring is equidimensional: all minimal primes have the same coheight, so all irreducible components have the same dimension.

nodes.name: Minimal free resolution
nodes.description: A free resolution of a module M over a local ring (R, 𝔪) where all differentials have entries in 𝔪; unique up to isomorphism with ranks given by Betti numbers.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of minimal free resolutions
nodes.description: Over a Noetherian local ring, the minimal free resolution of a finitely generated module is unique up to isomorphism of chain complexes.

nodes.name: Betti numbers (algebraic)
nodes.description: The ranks βᵢ(M) of the free modules in a minimal free resolution of M over a local ring (R, 𝔪, k); invariants measuring the complexity of M.

nodes.name: Regularity is preserved by localization
nodes.description: If R is a regular local ring and 𝔭 is a prime ideal, then R_𝔭 is also regular; follows from the Auslander-Buchsbaum-Serre characterization.

nodes.name: Stably free modules are free over local rings
nodes.description: Over a local ring, every stably free module (M with M ⊕ Rᵐ ≅ Rⁿ) is free; a consequence of Nakayama's lemma.

nodes.name: Ferrand-Vasconcelos theorem
nodes.description: If I is an ideal in a Noetherian local ring with I/I² free over R/I and pd_R(R/I) < ∞, then I is generated by a regular sequence.

nodes.name: Nagata's lemma
nodes.description: If R is a Noetherian domain, x a nonzero nonunit with (x) prime, and R[1/x] is a UFD, then R is a UFD; used to prove regular local rings are UFDs.

nodes.name: Fitting ideal
nodes.description: For a finitely presented module M with presentation matrix A, the i-th Fitting ideal Fittᵢ(M) is generated by the (n−i)-minors of A; independent of presentation.

nodes.name: Fitting ideals and annihilator
nodes.description: For a finitely presented module with n generators, Fitt₀(M) ⊆ Ann(M)ⁿ ⊆ Fitt₀(M); in particular V(Fitt₀(M)) = V(Ann(M)) = Supp(M).

nodes.name: Buchsbaum-Eisenbud acyclicity criterion
nodes.description: A complex of free modules is acyclic iff at each step the rank condition holds and the ideal of appropriately sized minors of each differential has sufficient depth.

nodes.name: Eagon-Northcott complex
nodes.description: A canonical free complex resolving the ideal of maximal minors of a matrix (or cokernel of a generic map), built from symmetric and exterior powers.

nodes.name: Determinantal ideal
nodes.description: The ideal I_t(A) generated by all t×t minors of a matrix A with entries in a ring R; a fundamental class of ideals in commutative algebra and algebraic geometry.

nodes.name: Expected codimension of determinantal ideals
nodes.description: For a generic m×n matrix, the ideal of t×t minors has codimension (m−t+1)(n−t+1); this is the maximum possible codimension for any determinantal ideal.

nodes.name: Perfect ideal
nodes.description: An ideal I such that pd_R(R/I) = grade(I); equivalently R/I has a finite free resolution of length equal to the grade of I.

nodes.name: Perfect ideals are unmixed
nodes.description: A perfect ideal in a Cohen-Macaulay ring is unmixed: all its associated primes have height equal to the grade of the ideal.

nodes.name: Syzygy module
nodes.description: The k-th syzygy module of M is the image of the k-th differential in a free resolution, measuring higher-order relations among generators.

nodes.name: Existence of canonical module
nodes.description: A Cohen-Macaulay local ring that is a quotient of a Gorenstein local ring possesses a canonical module ω_R, unique up to isomorphism.

nodes.name: Gorenstein iff canonical module is the ring
nodes.description: A Cohen-Macaulay local ring possessing a canonical module is Gorenstein if and only if ω_R ≅ R, equivalently the type r(R) = 1.

nodes.name: Type of a Cohen-Macaulay ring
nodes.description: The type of a Cohen-Macaulay local ring (R, 𝔪, k) of dimension d, equal to dim_k Ext^d_R(k, R); Gorenstein rings are precisely the CM rings of type 1.

nodes.name: Complete intersection ring
nodes.description: A Noetherian local ring whose completion is isomorphic to a regular local ring modulo an ideal generated by a regular sequence; sits between regular and Gorenstein in the hierarchy.

nodes.name: Complete intersections are Gorenstein
nodes.description: Every complete intersection local ring is Gorenstein, giving the hierarchy: regular ⊂ complete intersection ⊂ Gorenstein ⊂ Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.name: Duality for maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules
nodes.description: Over a Gorenstein local ring R, the functor Hom_R(−, R) gives a duality (contravariant self-equivalence) on the category of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules.

nodes.name: Maximal Cohen-Macaulay module
nodes.description: A finitely generated module M over a Cohen-Macaulay local ring (R, 𝔪) with depth(M) = dim(R), the maximum possible value.

nodes.name: Bass numbers
nodes.description: Invariants measuring the multiplicity of the indecomposable injective E(R/𝔭) in the i-th term of a minimal injective resolution of M.

nodes.name: Structure of injective modules over Noetherian rings
nodes.description: Every injective module over a Noetherian ring decomposes uniquely as a direct sum of indecomposable injectives E(R/𝔭) for various primes 𝔭, with multiplicities given by Bass numbers.

nodes.name: Poincaré duality for Gorenstein rings
nodes.description: For a Gorenstein local ring of dimension d, H^i_𝔪(R) = 0 for i ≠ d and H^d_𝔪(R) ≅ E(k), giving Poincaré-type duality via local cohomology.

nodes.name: Local cohomology via Čech complex
nodes.description: For an ideal I = (f₁,...,fᵣ), local cohomology H^i_I(M) is computed as the cohomology of the Čech complex built from localizations M_{f_{j₁}···f_{jₖ}}.

nodes.name: Vanishing of local cohomology
nodes.description: H^i_I(M) = 0 for i < depth_I(M) and for i > dim(M); the first nonvanishing degree equals the depth and the last equals the dimension.

nodes.name: Grothendieck vanishing theorem
nodes.description: For a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) and finitely generated M, H^i_𝔪(M) = 0 for all i > dim(M).

nodes.name: Depth via local cohomology
nodes.description: For a finitely generated module M over a Noetherian ring, depth_I(M) = min{i : H^i_I(M) ≠ 0}, characterizing depth cohomologically.

nodes.name: Local cohomology and sheaf cohomology comparison
nodes.description: For X = Proj(S) and a graded S-module M, there is a long exact sequence relating H^i_𝔪(M), the module M, and sheaf cohomology H^i(X, M̃(n)).

nodes.name: Divided power algebra
nodes.description: The algebra with divided power operations γₙ satisfying γₙ(x)γₘ(x) = C(n+m,n)γ_{n+m}(x); used in constructing Eagon-Northcott and Buchsbaum-Rim complexes.

nodes.name: Schur functor
nodes.description: The functor L_λ associating to a free module F the GL(F)-representation indexed by partition λ, generalizing symmetric and exterior powers.

nodes.name: Buchsbaum-Rim complex
nodes.description: A generalization of the Eagon-Northcott complex providing a free resolution of the cokernel of a map of free modules when the Fitting ideal has expected depth.

nodes.name: Mapping cone
nodes.description: For a chain map f: C → D, the complex cone(f) with cone(f)ₙ = Cₙ₋₁ ⊕ Dₙ fitting into the exact triangle C → D → cone(f) → C[−1].

nodes.name: Spectral sequence of a filtered complex
nodes.description: A filtered chain complex gives rise to a spectral sequence converging to the homology of the total complex, with E₀ page determined by the associated graded.

nodes.name: Spectral sequences of a double complex
nodes.description: A double complex has two spectral sequences from row and column filtrations, both converging to H*(Tot(C)); the E₂ pages are iterated homology in the two directions.

nodes.name: Mittag-Leffler condition
nodes.description: An inverse system {Aₙ} satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition if for each n the images im(Aₘ → Aₙ) stabilize for large m; ensures lim¹ = 0 and exactness of inverse limits.

nodes.name: p-basis of a field
nodes.description: A set {bᵢ} in a field K of characteristic p such that {bᵢ^{eᵢ} : 0 ≤ eᵢ < p} form a basis of K over K^p; measures the degree of imperfection of K.

nodes.name: Auslander depth formula
nodes.description: For finitely generated modules M, N over a regular local ring R with Torᵢ(M,N) = 0 for i > 0: depth(M) + depth(N) = depth(R) + depth(M ⊗ N).

nodes.name: Formally smooth algebra
nodes.description: An R-algebra S such that for every R-algebra A and nilpotent ideal N of A, every R-homomorphism S → A/N lifts to S → A.

nodes.name: Formally unramified algebra
nodes.description: An R-algebra S with Ω_{S/R} = 0, equivalently liftings in the formal smoothness definition are unique when they exist.

nodes.name: Formally étale algebra
nodes.description: An R-algebra S that is both formally smooth and formally unramified, so liftings of homomorphisms past nilpotent ideals exist and are unique.

nodes.name: G-ring (Grothendieck ring)
nodes.description: A Noetherian ring R such that for every prime p, the completion map R_p → R̂_p is a regular homomorphism, i.e., has geometrically regular formal fibres.

nodes.name: Quasi-excellent ring
nodes.description: A Noetherian G-ring R such that for every finitely generated R-algebra S, the singular locus of Spec(S) is closed.

nodes.name: N-1 ring
nodes.description: A Noetherian integral domain whose integral closure in its own fraction field is a finite module over itself.

nodes.name: Buchsbaum ring
nodes.description: A Noetherian local ring (R, m) such that the difference ℓ(R/(x₁,…,x_d)) − e(x₁,…,x_d; R) is independent of the choice of system of parameters.

nodes.name: Geometrically regular formal fibres
nodes.description: The condition on a Noetherian local ring (R, m) that all formal fibres R̂ ⊗_R κ(p) are geometrically regular algebras over κ(p) for every prime p.

nodes.name: Attached primes
nodes.description: For an Artinian module M over a Noetherian ring, Att(M) = {p ∈ Spec(R) : p = Ann(M/N) for some submodule N}, the dual notion to associated primes.

nodes.name: Dualizing complex
nodes.description: A bounded complex D• of injective modules with finitely generated cohomology such that the natural map R → RHom_R(D•, D•) is a quasi-isomorphism; exists for quotients of Gorenstein rings.

nodes.name: Singular locus
nodes.description: Sing(R) = {p ∈ Spec(R) : R_p is not a regular local ring}, the subset of primes where a Noetherian ring fails to be regular.

nodes.name: Formal fibre
nodes.description: For a Noetherian local ring (R, m) and prime p, the formal fibre at p is Spec(R̂ ⊗_R κ(p)), the fibre of the completion morphism Spec(R̂) → Spec(R) over p.

nodes.name: Henselization
nodes.description: The Henselization R^h of a local ring (R, m) is the smallest Henselian local ring through which R → R̂ factors, constructed as a filtered colimit of étale neighborhoods.

nodes.name: Strict Henselization
nodes.description: The strict Henselization R^{sh} of a local ring (R, m) is the Henselization with respect to the separable closure of the residue field, the maximal unramified extension of R.

nodes.name: Local criterion for flatness
nodes.description: For a local homomorphism (R, m) → (S, n) of Noetherian local rings, S is R-flat iff Tor₁^R(R/m, S) = 0, iff the natural map m ⊗_R S → mS is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Equational criterion for flatness
nodes.description: An R-module M is flat iff every linear relation ∑aᵢmᵢ = 0 can be trivialized: there exist nⱼ ∈ M and bᵢⱼ ∈ R with mᵢ = ∑bᵢⱼnⱼ and ∑aᵢbᵢⱼ = 0 for all j.

nodes.name: Generic flatness theorem
nodes.description: If R is a Noetherian domain and M a finitely generated R-module (or R-algebra), there exists nonzero f ∈ R such that M_f is free over R_f.

nodes.name: Grothendieck's non-vanishing theorem
nodes.description: For a Noetherian local ring (R, m) and finitely generated module M, H^d_m(M) ≠ 0 where d = dim(M), so local cohomology does not vanish at the dimension.
aliases: non-vanishing of local cohomology at dimension

nodes.name: Hochster's theorem on big Cohen-Macaulay modules
nodes.description: Every Noetherian local ring containing a field admits a (possibly non-finitely-generated) balanced big Cohen-Macaulay module on which every system of parameters is a regular sequence.

nodes.name: Openness of the regular locus
nodes.description: In an excellent ring (or a ring with geometrically regular formal fibres), the set {p ∈ Spec(R) : R_p is regular} is Zariski-open.

nodes.name: Fibre dimension formula for flat local homomorphisms
nodes.description: For a flat local homomorphism φ: (R, m) → (S, n) of Noetherian local rings, dim(S) = dim(R) + dim(S/mS), relating source, target, and fibre dimensions.

nodes.name: Finitistic dimension theorem
nodes.description: For a commutative Noetherian local ring (R, m), the finitistic projective dimension (supremum of pd(M) over modules M with pd(M) < ∞) equals depth(R).

nodes.name: Cohen structure theorem (mixed characteristic)
nodes.description: A complete Noetherian local ring (R, m) of mixed characteristic p with residue field k is a quotient of V[[x₁, …, xₙ]] where V is a complete DVR with residue field k.
aliases: Cohen's structure theorem for mixed characteristic

nodes.name: Power series ring over a local ring is local
nodes.description: If (R, m) is a local ring, then R[[x₁, …, xₙ]] is a local ring with maximal ideal (m, x₁, …, xₙ).

nodes.name: Power series ring is faithfully flat
nodes.description: The natural inclusion R → R[[x]] is a faithfully flat ring homomorphism.

nodes.name: Grothendieck's theorem on formal functions
nodes.description: Relates the completion of higher direct image sheaves to the cohomology of formal completions along fibres, connecting local and global cohomology in algebraic geometry.

nodes.name: Cohen-Macaulay approximation
nodes.function_signature: (Finitely generated module M over CM local ring R) → (Short exact sequence 0 → Y → X → M → 0 with X maximal CM and Y of finite injective dimension)
nodes.description: Approximating modules over Cohen-Macaulay rings by maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules via short exact sequences, introduced by Auslander-Buchweitz.

nodes.name: Secondary representation
nodes.function_signature: (Artinian module M) → (Decomposition M = M₁ + ⋯ + Mₙ into secondary submodules with attached primes)
nodes.description: Decomposing an Artinian module as a sum of secondary submodules, dual to primary decomposition for Noetherian modules.

nodes.name: Quasi-isomorphism
nodes.description: A chain map f: C• → D• that induces isomorphisms H_n(f): H_n(C) → H_n(D) on all homology groups.

nodes.name: Mapping cylinder (chain complexes)
nodes.description: For a chain map f: C• → D•, the chain complex cyl(f)_n = C_n ⊕ C_{n-1} ⊕ D_n with differential encoding f and the identity, fitting in a short exact sequence with the mapping cone.
aliases: mapping cylinder of a chain map

nodes.name: Split exact sequence
nodes.description: A short exact sequence 0 → A → B → C → 0 that admits a section s: C → B (right split) or retraction r: B → A (left split), equivalently B ≅ A ⊕ C.

nodes.name: Homotopy equivalence of chain complexes
nodes.description: A chain map f: C• → D• such that there exists g: D• → C• with gf and fg both chain homotopic to the respective identities.

nodes.name: Erasable (effaceable/coeffaceable) functor
nodes.description: A functor F is effaceable if for every object A there is a monomorphism u: A → M with F(u) = 0; coeffaceable if dually there is an epimorphism with the same property.

nodes.name: Flat resolution
nodes.description: An exact sequence ··· → F_1 → F_0 → M → 0 where each F_i is a flat module, used to compute Tor.

nodes.name: Weak (global) dimension
nodes.description: The supremum of the flat dimensions of all modules over a ring R, equivalently the supremum of n such that Tor_n^R ≠ 0.

nodes.name: Yoneda Ext
nodes.description: The group Ext^n(A, B) defined as equivalence classes of n-fold extensions of A by B under the Baer sum, isomorphic to the derived functor Ext^n_R(A, B).

nodes.name: Baer sum of extensions
nodes.description: The group operation on Ext^1(A, B) defined by pulling back the direct sum extension along the diagonal and pushing out along the fold map, making Ext^1(A, B) an abelian group.

nodes.name: lim¹ (first derived functor of inverse limit)
nodes.description: The first right derived functor R¹lim of the inverse limit functor on inverse systems of abelian groups, measuring the obstruction to surjectivity of the inverse limit.

nodes.name: Auslander–Buchsbaum–Serre theorem
nodes.description: A Noetherian local ring (R, m) is regular if and only if it has finite global dimension, in which case gl.dim(R) = dim(R) = the minimal number of generators of m.

nodes.name: Grade of a module
nodes.description: For a finitely generated module M over a Noetherian ring R, grade(M) = inf{i : Ext^i_R(M, R) ≠ 0}, the smallest degree in which Ext into R is nonzero.

nodes.name: Derived couple
nodes.description: Given an exact couple (A, E, i, j, k), the derived couple (A', E', i', j', k') where A' = im(i), E' = H(E, d) with d = jk, producing the next page of the associated spectral sequence.

nodes.name: Transgression
nodes.description: In a first-quadrant spectral sequence, the partially defined map d_n: E_n^{0,n-1} → E_n^{n,0} connecting the fiber and base terms, arising as the last possible differential hitting the bottom row.

nodes.name: Cartan–Eilenberg resolution
nodes.description: An injective (or projective) resolution of a chain complex C• that is compatible with homology: a double complex P•• whose columns are resolutions of C_n and whose horizontal homology gives resolutions of H_n(C).

nodes.name: Hyperhomology
nodes.description: The left hyper-derived functors 𝕃_nF(C•) of an additive functor F applied to a chain complex C•, computed via a Cartan–Eilenberg resolution as the homology of the total complex of F(P••).

nodes.name: Hypercohomology
nodes.description: The right hyper-derived functors ℝⁿF(C•) of a left exact functor F applied to a cochain complex, generalizing sheaf cohomology to complexes of sheaves.

nodes.name: Acyclic assembly lemma
nodes.description: If a first-quadrant double complex has exact columns (resp. rows) except in degree zero, then the natural map from the zeroth column (resp. row) to the total complex is a quasi-isomorphism.

nodes.name: G-invariants M^G
nodes.description: For a G-module M, the subgroup M^G = {m ∈ M : gm = m for all g ∈ G} of elements fixed by all group elements, a left exact functor whose right derived functors are group cohomology.

nodes.name: G-coinvariants M_G
nodes.description: For a G-module M, the quotient M_G = M/I_G·M where I_G is the augmentation ideal, a right exact functor whose left derived functors are group homology.

nodes.name: Normalized bar resolution
nodes.description: The quotient of the bar resolution B•(G) by the subcomplex of degenerate simplices, a smaller free ℤG-resolution of ℤ with B̄_n generated by [g₁|…|gₙ] with all gᵢ ≠ 1.

nodes.name: Five-term exact sequence (group cohomology)
nodes.description: For a group extension 1 → N → G → Q → 1, the exact sequence 0 → H¹(Q, Mᴺ) → H¹(G, M) → H¹(N, M)^Q → H²(Q, Mᴺ) → H²(G, M) obtained from the Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence.

nodes.name: Principal crossed homomorphism
nodes.description: A crossed homomorphism f: G → M of the form f(g) = gm − m for some fixed m ∈ M; the group of principal crossed homomorphisms is B¹(G, M), so H¹(G, M) = Z¹/B¹.

nodes.name: Factor set (group extension)
