nodes.description: A function f: G × G → A satisfying the 2-cocycle condition f(g,h) + f(gh,k) = g·f(h,k) + f(g,hk), classifying extensions of G by A up to equivalence via H²(G, A).

nodes.name: Tate cohomology
nodes.description: For a finite group G and G-module M, the cohomology theory Ĥⁿ(G, M) defined for all n ∈ ℤ using a complete resolution, with Ĥ⁰ = M^G/N_G·M and Ĥ⁻¹ = ker(N_G)/I_G·M.

nodes.name: Complete (Tate) resolution
nodes.description: An acyclic complex T• of projective ℤG-modules extending the ordinary projective resolution in both directions, with Hom_G(T•, M) computing Tate cohomology.

nodes.name: Norm map (group cohomology)
nodes.description: For a finite group G and G-module M, the map N_G: M → M defined by N_G(m) = Σ_{g∈G} gm, whose kernel and cokernel appear in Tate cohomology.

nodes.name: Cup product in group cohomology
nodes.description: The associative graded-commutative product ∪: Hⁿ(G, M) ⊗ Hᵐ(G, N) → Hⁿ⁺ᵐ(G, M ⊗ N) induced by the diagonal approximation on the bar resolution.

nodes.name: Cohomological dimension of a group
nodes.description: The supremum cd(G) of all n such that Hⁿ(G, M) ≠ 0 for some G-module M, equivalently the projective dimension of ℤ as a ℤG-module.

nodes.name: Group of type FP
nodes.description: A group G is of type FP_n if ℤ admits a projective ℤG-resolution with all modules finitely generated in degrees ≤ n; type FP if finitely generated in all degrees; type FL if a finite free resolution exists.

nodes.name: Lie algebra homology H_n(𝔤, M)
nodes.description: The left derived functors of the coinvariants functor M ↦ M_𝔤 = M/𝔤·M for a Lie algebra 𝔤 over k with coefficients in a 𝔤-module M, computed via the Chevalley–Eilenberg complex.

nodes.name: Lie algebra cohomology H^n(𝔤, M)
nodes.description: The right derived functors of the invariants functor M ↦ M^𝔤 = {m ∈ M : x·m = 0 ∀x ∈ 𝔤} for a Lie algebra 𝔤 with coefficients in a 𝔤-module M.

nodes.name: Chevalley–Eilenberg complex
nodes.description: The chain complex C_n(𝔤, M) = M ⊗ Λⁿ(𝔤) with differential involving the Lie bracket and the module action, whose homology is the Lie algebra homology H_n(𝔤, M).

nodes.name: Casimir element
nodes.description: For a semisimple Lie algebra 𝔤 with Killing form κ, the element c = Σ xᵢyᵢ ∈ U(𝔤) where {xᵢ} and {yᵢ} are dual bases; c lies in the center of U(𝔤) and acts on irreducible representations by a scalar.

nodes.name: Relative Lie algebra cohomology H^n(𝔤, 𝔨; M)
nodes.description: For a Lie subalgebra 𝔨 ⊂ 𝔤, the cohomology of the subcomplex of 𝔨-basic elements in the Chevalley–Eilenberg complex, used in the theory of (𝔤, K)-modules.

nodes.name: Simplicial object
nodes.description: A contravariant functor X: Δᵒᵖ → C from the simplex category Δ to a category C, specified by objects X_n and face maps dᵢ, degeneracy maps sⱼ satisfying the simplicial identities.

nodes.name: Cosimplicial object
nodes.description: A covariant functor X: Δ → C from the simplex category to a category C, specified by objects X^n with coface and codegeneracy maps satisfying the cosimplicial identities.

nodes.name: Simplicial set
nodes.description: A simplicial object in the category of sets, i.e., a contravariant functor Δᵒᵖ → Set, providing a combinatorial model for topological spaces up to weak homotopy equivalence.

nodes.name: Face map (simplicial)
nodes.description: In a simplicial object X•, the map dᵢ: X_n → X_{n-1} for 0 ≤ i ≤ n, corresponding to the injection [n-1] → [n] that skips i, satisfying dᵢdⱼ = dⱼ₋₁dᵢ for i < j.

nodes.name: Degeneracy map (simplicial)
nodes.description: In a simplicial object X•, the map sⱼ: X_n → X_{n+1} for 0 ≤ j ≤ n, corresponding to the surjection [n+1] → [n] that repeats j, satisfying simplicial identities with face maps.

nodes.name: Moore complex
nodes.description: For a simplicial abelian group A•, the chain complex (A_n, ∂) with ∂ = Σᵢ(-1)ⁱdᵢ, whose homology equals the homotopy groups π_n(A•); the unnormalized version of the Dold–Kan correspondence.
aliases: Moore complex of a simplicial group

nodes.name: Normalized chain complex (simplicial)
nodes.description: For a simplicial abelian group A•, the subcomplex N_n = ∩ᵢ₌₁ⁿ ker(dᵢ) ⊂ A_n with differential d₀, quasi-isomorphic to the Moore complex and corresponding to A• under the Dold–Kan equivalence.

nodes.name: Dold–Kan correspondence
nodes.description: The normalized chain complex functor N: sAb → Ch≥0 is an equivalence of categories between simplicial abelian groups and non-negative chain complexes, with inverse the Eilenberg–MacLane functor.

nodes.name: Alexander–Whitney map
nodes.description: The natural chain map AW: C(X × Y) → C(X) ⊗ C(Y) defined by AW(σ)= Σ (front-p-face of σ) ⊗ (back-q-face of σ), a chain homotopy inverse to the Eilenberg–Zilber shuffle map.

nodes.name: Shuffle map (Eilenberg–Zilber)
nodes.description: The natural chain map ∇: C(X) ⊗ C(Y) → C(X × Y) defined using (p,q)-shuffles, providing a chain homotopy inverse to the Alexander–Whitney map.

nodes.name: Eilenberg–MacLane space K(π, n)
nodes.description: A CW complex K(π, n) with π_n(K(π,n)) ≅ π and π_k(K(π,n)) = 0 for k ≠ n, unique up to homotopy equivalence, representing singular cohomology H^n(−; π) as a functor.

nodes.name: Comonad (cotriple)
nodes.description: A comonoid in the category of endofunctors: a functor G: C → C with natural transformations δ: G → G² (comultiplication) and ε: G → Id (counit) satisfying coassociativity and counit axioms.

nodes.name: Cotriple resolution
nodes.description: For a comonad G on C and object X, the augmented simplicial object ··· ⇉ G²X ⇉ GX → X with face maps using ε and degeneracies using δ, providing canonical resolutions in algebra.

nodes.name: André–Quillen homology
nodes.description: The homology theory D_n(A/k, M) for commutative k-algebras A with coefficients in an A-module M, defined as the left derived functors of derivations and computed via simplicial resolutions.

nodes.name: Cotangent complex
nodes.description: The complex L_{A/k} = Ω_{P•/k} ⊗_{P•} A in the derived category, where P• → A is a simplicial resolution; its homology gives André–Quillen homology D_n(A/k, A) = H_n(L_{A/k}).

nodes.name: Bar construction
nodes.description: For a monad or triple T on C and a T-algebra A, the simplicial object B•(T, A) with B_n = T^{n+1}A, providing a canonical free/projective simplicial resolution of A.

nodes.name: Kan complex
nodes.description: A simplicial set satisfying the Kan extension condition: every horn Λⁿₖ → X has a filler Δⁿ → X, providing the combinatorial analogue of a topological space with well-defined homotopy groups.

nodes.name: Hochschild homology HH_n(A, M)
nodes.description: For an associative k-algebra A and A-bimodule M, the homology HH_n(A, M) = Tor_n^{A^e}(A, M) of the Hochschild complex, where A^e = A ⊗ Aᵒᵖ is the enveloping algebra.

nodes.name: Gerstenhaber bracket
nodes.description: The degree −1 Lie bracket [−,−] on Hochschild cohomology HH*(A,A) making it a Gerstenhaber algebra: a graded commutative ring under cup product with a compatible graded Lie structure.

nodes.name: Formal deformation of an algebra
nodes.description: A k[[t]]-algebra A_t = A[[t]] with product a ∗ b = ab + μ₁(a,b)t + μ₂(a,b)t² + ··· deforming A, where associativity of ∗ is controlled by Hochschild cohomology classes in HH²(A, A).

nodes.name: Cyclic homology HC_n(A)
nodes.description: For a k-algebra A, the homology of the total complex of Connes' cyclic bicomplex (or equivalently of the mixed complex (C•(A), b, B)), fitting in the SBI exact sequence with Hochschild homology.

nodes.name: Mixed complex
nodes.description: A graded module C• with two differentials b: C_n → C_{n-1} of degree −1 and B: C_n → C_{n+1} of degree +1 satisfying b² = B² = bB + Bb = 0, encoding the data for both Hochschild and cyclic homology.

nodes.name: Connes' B operator
nodes.description: The degree +1 map B: C_n(A) → C_{n+1}(A) on the Hochschild complex defined by B = (1 − t)sN where s is the extra degeneracy, t the cyclic operator, and N = 1 + t + ··· + tⁿ.

nodes.name: SBI exact sequence (Connes)
nodes.description: The long exact sequence ··· → HH_n(A) →^I HC_n(A) →^S HC_{n-2}(A) →^B HH_{n-1}(A) → ··· relating Hochschild and cyclic homology via the periodicity operator S and Connes' B.

nodes.name: Cyclic bicomplex
nodes.description: Connes' bicomplex CC•• with columns alternating between the Hochschild complex and its b'-complex, connected by the norm N and extra degeneracy maps, whose total complex computes cyclic homology.

nodes.name: Periodic cyclic homology HP_n(A)
nodes.description: The ℤ/2-graded theory HP_*(A) = lim_S HC_{*+2k}(A) obtained as the inverse limit over the periodicity operator S, satisfying HP_n(A) ≅ HP_{n+2}(A) and related to de Rham cohomology for smooth algebras.

nodes.name: Negative cyclic homology HN_n(A)
nodes.description: The homology HN_*(A) of the product total complex of the cyclic bicomplex, fitting in an exact sequence with HC_* and HP_* and receiving the Dennis trace from algebraic K-theory.

nodes.name: Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem
nodes.description: For a smooth commutative k-algebra A, HH_n(A) ≅ Ω^n_{A/k}, identifying Hochschild homology with differential forms; under this isomorphism, Connes' B operator corresponds to de Rham d.

nodes.name: Loday–Quillen–Tsygan theorem
nodes.description: The Lie algebra homology of gl(A) = lim gl_n(A) satisfies H_*(gl(A); k) ≅ Λ*(HC_{*-1}(A)) as a graded Hopf algebra, relating cyclic homology to the homology of the stable general linear group.

nodes.name: Dennis trace map
nodes.description: The natural map K_n(A) → HH_n(A) from algebraic K-theory to Hochschild homology, factoring through negative cyclic homology: K_n(A) → HN_n(A) → HH_n(A).

nodes.name: Morita invariance of Hochschild and cyclic homology
nodes.description: If A and B are Morita equivalent rings, then HH_*(A) ≅ HH_*(B) and HC_*(A) ≅ HC_*(B); in particular HH_*(M_r(A)) ≅ HH_*(A) for matrix algebras.
aliases: Morita invariance of HH and HC

nodes.name: Homotopy category K(A)
nodes.description: The category K(A) with the same objects as Ch(A) but morphisms modulo chain homotopy equivalence, carrying a natural triangulated structure with shift [1] and distinguished triangles from mapping cones.

nodes.name: Distinguished triangle
nodes.description: In a triangulated category, a triangle X → Y → Z → X[1] isomorphic to a standard triangle arising from a morphism f as X →^f Y → cone(f) → X[1].

nodes.name: Octahedral axiom (TR4)
nodes.description: Axiom TR4 for triangulated categories: given composable morphisms f: X → Y and g: Y → Z with gf: X → Z, the cones of f, g, and gf fit into a distinguished triangle cone(f) → cone(gf) → cone(g) → cone(f)[1].

nodes.name: Verdier quotient
nodes.description: For a triangulated category T and thick subcategory N, the localization T/N obtained by formally inverting all morphisms whose cone lies in N, yielding a triangulated category with a universal property.

nodes.name: Ore conditions (calculus of fractions)
nodes.description: Conditions on a class S of morphisms in a category C ensuring that the localization C[S⁻¹] can be computed by left or right fractions s⁻¹f, without requiring a full zigzag calculus.

nodes.name: Derived category D(A)
nodes.description: The localization D(A) = K(A)[quasi-iso⁻¹] of the homotopy category of chain complexes over an abelian category A at the class of quasi-isomorphisms, the natural domain for derived functors.

nodes.name: Bounded derived category D^b(A)
nodes.description: The full triangulated subcategory D^b(A) ⊂ D(A) of complexes with bounded cohomology, equivalently the localization of K^b(A) at quasi-isomorphisms; similarly D^+(A) and D^-(A) for bounded below/above.

nodes.name: Total left derived functor LF
nodes.description: For a right exact functor F: A → B, the total left derived functor LF: D^-(A) → D^-(B) defined by LF(C•) = F(P•) where P• → C• is a projective resolution in the derived category.

nodes.name: Total right derived functor RF
nodes.description: For a left exact functor F: A → B, the total right derived functor RF: D^+(A) → D^+(B) defined by RF(C•) = F(I•) where C• → I• is an injective resolution in the derived category.

nodes.name: RHom complex
nodes.description: The total right derived functor RHom(A, B) of Hom in the derived category, with H^n(RHom(A,B)) = Ext^n(A,B), providing a derived-category refinement of Ext groups.

nodes.name: Derived tensor product ⊗^L
nodes.description: The total left derived functor A ⊗^L_R B of the tensor product in the derived category, with H_n(A ⊗^L B) = Tor_n(A,B), computed by tensoring with a projective/flat resolution.

nodes.name: Way-out functor
nodes.description: A triangulated functor F: D^+(A) → D^+(B) is way-out right if for every n there exists p such that H^i(F(C•)) = 0 for i > n whenever H^j(C•) = 0 for j > p; way-out left is dual.

nodes.name: Way-out lemma (Hartshorne)
nodes.description: If η: F → G is a natural transformation of way-out right (resp. left) functors that is an isomorphism on D^b, then η is an isomorphism on D^+ (resp. D^-); used to extend derived functor isomorphisms.

nodes.name: t-structure on a triangulated category
nodes.description: A pair (D^≤0, D^≥0) of full subcategories of a triangulated category D satisfying: D^≤0[1] ⊂ D^≤0, D^≥0[-1] ⊂ D^≥0, Hom(D^≤0, D^≥1) = 0, and every object fits in a distinguished triangle.

nodes.name: Heart of a t-structure
nodes.description: The full subcategory C = D^≤0 ∩ D^≥0 of a t-structure (D^≤0, D^≥0), which is always an abelian category; for the standard t-structure on D(A), the heart is equivalent to A.

nodes.name: Truncation functors τ≤n and τ≥n
nodes.description: The functors τ≤n: D → D^≤n and τ≥n: D → D^≥n associated to a t-structure, fitting in distinguished triangles τ≤n(X) → X → τ≥n+1(X) → (τ≤n(X))[1] for every object X.

nodes.name: Grothendieck's AB axioms
nodes.description: A hierarchy of axioms for abelian categories: AB3 (coproducts exist), AB4 (coproducts are exact), AB5 (filtered colimits are exact), and their duals AB3*, AB4*, AB5*; module categories satisfy AB5.

nodes.name: Chevalley–Eilenberg complex computation
nodes.function_signature: (Lie algebra 𝔤, 𝔤-module M) → (H_n(𝔤, M), H^n(𝔤, M))
nodes.description: Computes Lie algebra homology and cohomology by constructing the Chevalley–Eilenberg complex C_n = M ⊗ Λⁿ𝔤 and taking homology/cohomology.

nodes.name: Cartan–Eilenberg resolution construction
nodes.function_signature: (ChainComplex C•) → (DoubleComplex P••, Hyperhomology)
nodes.description: Constructs a double complex of projective/injective objects resolving each term and homology of a chain complex, enabling computation of hyper-derived functors and spectral sequences.

nodes.name: Dold–Kan correspondence
nodes.function_signature: (SimplicialAbelianGroup A•) ↔ (ChainComplex≥0 N(A))
nodes.description: Establishes an equivalence between simplicial abelian groups and non-negative chain complexes via the normalized chain complex functor, translating simplicial homotopy theory into homological algebra.

nodes.name: Spectral sequence of a double complex
nodes.function_signature: (DoubleComplex C••) → (Two SpectralSequences converging to H*(Tot(C••)))
nodes.description: Produces two spectral sequences from the row and column filtrations of a double complex, both converging to the homology of the total complex under suitable boundedness conditions.

nodes.name: SBI exact sequence computation
nodes.function_signature: (k-algebra A) → (relationship HC_*(A) ↔ HH_*(A))
nodes.description: Uses the long exact sequence ··· → HH_n →^I HC_n →^S HC_{n-2} →^B HH_{n-1} → ··· to compute cyclic homology from Hochschild homology iteratively.

nodes.name: Derived category construction (localization)
nodes.function_signature: (AbelianCategory A) → (TriangulatedCategory D(A))
nodes.description: Constructs the derived category D(A) by localizing the homotopy category K(A) at quasi-isomorphisms using calculus of fractions, enabling derived functors as exact functors between triangulated categories.

nodes.name: Cotriple (comonadic) resolution
nodes.function_signature: (Comonad G, Object X) → (SimplicialResolution G•X → X)
nodes.description: Constructs canonical simplicial resolutions using the iterates of a comonad, yielding acyclic resolutions suitable for computing derived functors in non-abelian settings.

nodes.name: Tate cohomology computation
nodes.function_signature: (FiniteGroup G, G-module M) → (Ĥ^n(G,M) for all n ∈ ℤ)
nodes.description: Computes Tate cohomology by splicing a projective resolution with its dual to form a complete resolution, extending group cohomology to negative degrees.

nodes.name: Hyperhomology/hypercohomology computation
nodes.function_signature: (Functor F, ChainComplex C•) → (Hyper-derived functors 𝕃F(C•) or ℝF(C•))
nodes.description: Applies a derived functor to a chain complex via Cartan–Eilenberg resolutions or using the two spectral sequences of the resulting double complex.

nodes.name: Differential
nodes.description: The differential d_n: C_n -> C_{n-1} in a chain complex is the morphism satisfying d_{n-1} composed with d_n = 0.

nodes.name: Cycles
nodes.description: The module of n-cycles of a chain complex C is Z_n(C) = ker(d_n: C_n -> C_{n-1}), the kernel of the n-th differential.

nodes.name: Boundaries
nodes.description: The module of n-boundaries of a chain complex C is B_n(C) = im(d_{n+1}: C_{n+1} -> C_n), the image of the (n+1)-th differential.

nodes.name: Cocycles
nodes.description: The module of n-cocycles of a cochain complex C is Z^n(C) = ker(d^n: C^n -> C^{n+1}).

nodes.name: Coboundaries
nodes.description: The module of n-coboundaries of a cochain complex C is B^n(C) = im(d^{n-1}: C^{n-1} -> C^n).

nodes.name: Bounded chain complex
nodes.description: A chain complex is bounded below if C_n = 0 for n sufficiently negative, bounded above if C_n = 0 for n sufficiently positive, and bounded if both conditions hold.

nodes.name: Chain homotopy
nodes.description: A chain homotopy between chain maps f, g: C -> D is a family of morphisms s_n: C_n -> D_{n+1} such that f_n - g_n = d_{n+1}^D s_n + s_{n-1} d_n^C for all n.

nodes.name: Chain homotopy equivalence implies quasi-isomorphism
nodes.description: Every chain homotopy equivalence is a quasi-isomorphism; chain homotopic maps induce identical maps on homology.

nodes.name: Naturality of the long exact sequence in homology
nodes.description: The long exact sequence in homology is natural: a morphism of short exact sequences of chain complexes induces a morphism of the corresponding long exact sequences.

nodes.name: Mapping cylinder
nodes.description: The mapping cylinder cyl(f) of a chain map f: C -> D is the chain complex with cyl(f)_n = C_{n-1} + C_n + D_n, fitting into a short exact sequence 0 -> D -> cyl(f) -> C[-1] -> 0.

nodes.name: Mapping cone exact triangle
nodes.description: For a chain map f: C -> D, there is a short exact sequence 0 -> D -> cone(f) -> C[-1] -> 0, and the resulting long exact sequence recovers the connecting homomorphism induced by f.

nodes.name: Translation (shift) functor
nodes.description: The shift functor [p] sends a chain complex C to C[p] defined by C[p]_n = C_{n+p} with differential (-1)^p d_{n+p}.

nodes.name: Kernel (abelian category)
nodes.description: The kernel of a morphism f: A -> B in an abelian category is the equalizer of f and the zero map, i.e., a universal morphism i: K -> A such that f i = 0.

nodes.name: Cokernel (abelian category)
nodes.description: The cokernel of a morphism f: A -> B in an abelian category is the coequalizer of f and the zero map, i.e., a universal morphism p: B -> Q such that p f = 0.

nodes.name: Coimage
nodes.description: The coimage of a morphism f: A -> B in an abelian category is coim(f) = coker(ker(f)), and in an abelian category the canonical map coim(f) -> im(f) is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Category Ch(A) of chain complexes
nodes.description: The category Ch(A) of chain complexes over an abelian category A, with chain maps as morphisms, is itself an abelian category.

nodes.name: Homotopy category K(A)
nodes.description: The homotopy category K(A) has chain complexes over A as objects and chain homotopy classes of chain maps as morphisms, forming a triangulated category.

nodes.name: Homology is a functor
nodes.description: For each n, H_n: Ch(A) -> A is an additive functor from the category of chain complexes to the abelian category A.

nodes.name: Hom complex
nodes.description: For chain complexes C and D, the Hom complex Hom(C, D) is the cochain complex with Hom(C, D)^n = prod_i Hom(C_i, D_{i+n}) and differential (df)(c) = d^D(f(c)) - (-1)^n f(d^C(c)).

nodes.name: Existence of projective resolutions
nodes.description: In an abelian category with enough projectives, every object admits a projective resolution, constructed by iteratively taking projective covers of successive kernels.

nodes.name: Existence of injective resolutions
nodes.description: In an abelian category with enough injectives, every object admits an injective resolution, constructed by iteratively embedding successive cokernels into injective objects.

nodes.name: Comparison theorem for injective resolutions
nodes.description: Any morphism f: A -> B lifts to a chain map between injective resolutions, unique up to chain homotopy; thus injective resolutions are unique up to chain homotopy equivalence.

nodes.name: Cohomological delta-functor
nodes.description: A cohomological delta-functor is a sequence of additive functors {T^n}_{n >= 0} with connecting morphisms delta^n: T^n(C) -> T^{n+1}(A) for each short exact sequence 0 -> A -> B -> C -> 0, satisfying exactness and naturality.

nodes.name: Coeffaceable functor
nodes.description: An additive functor T is coeffaceable if for every object A there exists an epimorphism u: M -> A such that T(u) = 0; a homological delta-functor is coeffaceable if T_n is coeffaceable for all n >= 1.

nodes.name: Effaceable delta-functors are universal
nodes.description: An effaceable cohomological delta-functor is universal, and dually a coeffaceable homological delta-functor is universal.

nodes.name: L_0F is naturally isomorphic to F
nodes.description: For a right exact functor F and its left derived functors, there is a natural isomorphism L_0F = F.

nodes.name: R^0G is naturally isomorphic to G
nodes.description: For a left exact functor G and its right derived functors, there is a natural isomorphism R^0G = G.

nodes.name: Left derived functors form a universal delta-functor
nodes.description: The left derived functors {L_nF}_{n >= 0} of a right exact functor F form a universal homological delta-functor.

nodes.name: Right derived functors form a universal delta-functor
nodes.description: The right derived functors {R^nG}_{n >= 0} of a left exact functor G form a universal cohomological delta-functor.

nodes.name: Derived functors vanish on adapted objects
nodes.description: For a right exact functor F, L_nF(P) = 0 for all n >= 1 when P is projective; for a left exact functor G, R^nG(I) = 0 for all n >= 1 when I is injective.

nodes.name: Left adjoints are right exact
nodes.description: A functor that is a left adjoint in an adjunction between abelian categories is right exact.

nodes.name: Right adjoints are left exact
nodes.description: A functor that is a right adjoint in an adjunction between abelian categories is left exact.

nodes.name: Balancing Ext
nodes.description: Ext^n_R(A, B) can be computed using either a projective resolution of A or an injective resolution of B: H^n(Hom_R(P, B)) = H^n(Hom_R(A, I)) = Ext^n_R(A, B).

nodes.name: Independence of resolution for derived functors
nodes.description: The left (resp. right) derived functors L_nF (resp. R^nG) are independent of the choice of projective (resp. injective) resolution up to canonical natural isomorphism.

nodes.name: Tor_0 is the tensor product
nodes.description: For R-modules A and B, Tor_0^R(A, B) is naturally isomorphic to A tensor_R B.

nodes.name: Ext^0 is Hom
nodes.description: For R-modules A and B, Ext^0_R(A, B) is naturally isomorphic to Hom_R(A, B).

nodes.name: Construction of connecting homomorphism via Snake Lemma
nodes.description: Constructs the connecting homomorphism in the long exact sequence of homology by applying the Snake Lemma to the commutative diagram formed by cycles, boundaries, and homology of a short exact sequence of complexes.

nodes.name: Free modules are projective
nodes.description: Every free R-module is projective; in particular, the category of R-modules has enough projectives since every module is a quotient of a free module.

nodes.name: Baer criterion for injectivity
nodes.description: An R-module I is injective if and only if for every ideal J of R, every homomorphism J -> I extends to R.

nodes.name: Balancing via double complexes
nodes.description: Proves balancing of Ext and Tor by forming the double complex from projective resolutions of both arguments and computing the homology of the total complex in two ways.

nodes.name: Flat dimension
nodes.description: The flat dimension fd_R(M) of an R-module M is the infimum of the lengths of flat resolutions of M, equivalently the largest n such that Tor_n^R(M, N) is nonzero for some N.

nodes.name: Ext characterization of projective dimension
nodes.description: For an R-module M, pd_R(M) <= n if and only if Ext^{n+1}_R(M, N) = 0 for all R-modules N, equivalently if and only if the n-th syzygy in any projective resolution is projective.

nodes.name: Ext characterization of injective dimension
nodes.description: For an R-module M, id_R(M) <= n if and only if Ext^{n+1}_R(N, M) = 0 for all R-modules N.

nodes.name: Rings of global dimension zero are semisimple
nodes.description: A ring R has gl.dim(R) = 0 if and only if R is semisimple, which by the Artin-Wedderburn theorem means R is a finite product of matrix rings over division rings.

nodes.name: Hereditary ring
nodes.description: A ring R is (left) hereditary if every (left) ideal of R is projective, equivalently if gl.dim(R) <= 1.

nodes.name: Rings of global dimension at most one
nodes.description: A ring R has gl.dim(R) <= 1 if and only if every submodule of a projective R-module is projective; for commutative domains this is equivalent to R being a Dedekind domain.

nodes.name: Change of rings theorem for dimension (quotient ring)
nodes.description: If x is a central non-zero-divisor in R and M is a nonzero R/xR-module, then pd_R(M) = pd_{R/xR}(M) + 1.

nodes.name: Global dimension of regular local rings
nodes.description: A Noetherian local ring (R, m, k) is regular if and only if gl.dim(R) is finite, in which case gl.dim(R) equals the Krull dimension of R.

nodes.name: Koszul homology (with coefficients)
nodes.description: The Koszul homology H_*(x_1, ..., x_n; M) of an R-module M with respect to elements x_1, ..., x_n is H_*(K(x_1, ..., x_n) tensor_R M).

nodes.name: Koszul acyclicity for regular sequences
nodes.description: If x_1, ..., x_n is a regular sequence on an R-module M, then H_i(x_1, ..., x_n; M) = 0 for all i >= 1 and H_0 = M/(x_1, ..., x_n)M.

nodes.name: Global dimension equals supremum over cyclic modules
nodes.description: For a left Noetherian ring R, gl.dim(R) = sup{pd_R(R/I) : I a left ideal of R}.

nodes.name: Weak dimension is at most global dimension
nodes.description: For any ring R, w.gl.dim(R) <= gl.dim(R), with equality when R is Noetherian.

nodes.name: Auslander's theorem on global dimension
nodes.description: For a commutative Noetherian local ring R with residue field k, gl.dim(R) = pd_R(k).

nodes.name: Koszul complex provides resolution of residue field
nodes.description: If (R, m, k) is a regular local ring with m = (x_1, ..., x_d) where d = dim R, then the Koszul complex K(x_1, ..., x_d) is a free resolution of k of length d.

nodes.name: Koszul H_1 detects regular sequences
nodes.description: For a Noetherian local ring (R, m, k) and x_1, ..., x_n in m, H_1(x_1, ..., x_n; R) = 0 if and only if x_1, ..., x_n is a regular sequence.

nodes.name: Mapping cone and Koszul complex
nodes.description: Constructs K(x_1, ..., x_n) inductively as the mapping cone of multiplication by x_n on K(x_1, ..., x_{n-1}), providing a recursive method for computing Koszul homology.

nodes.name: Horseshoe lemma application in dimension shifting
nodes.description: Uses the horseshoe lemma to construct a projective resolution of the middle term in a short exact sequence from resolutions of the outer terms, enabling systematic dimension shifting for Ext and Tor.

nodes.name: Restriction and induction of scalars
nodes.description: Given a ring map f: R -> S, restriction of scalars views S-modules as R-modules while induction S tensor_R - forms an adjoint pair, used to transfer homological information between R and S.

nodes.name: Spectral sequence
nodes.description: A sequence of bigraded modules {E_r^{p,q}} with differentials d_r satisfying E_{r+1} = H(E_r, d_r), providing successive approximations to a limit term E_infinity.

nodes.name: Associated graded complex
nodes.description: For a filtered chain complex with filtration {F_p C}, the bigraded complex gr_p C = F_p C / F_{p-1} C whose homology forms the E_0 page of the associated spectral sequence.

nodes.name: Bounded filtration
nodes.description: A filtration {F_p C} on a chain complex is bounded if for each n there exist s < t such that F_s C_n = 0 and F_t C_n = C_n, ensuring the associated spectral sequence converges.

nodes.name: Weak convergence of a spectral sequence
nodes.description: A spectral sequence weakly converges to a graded object H_* if E_infinity^{p,q} is isomorphic to F_p H_{p+q} / F_{p-1} H_{p+q} for a filtration F on H_*.

nodes.name: Bounded convergence of a spectral sequence
nodes.description: A spectral sequence converges boundedly to H_* if it weakly converges and the filtration on each H_n is finite, which holds when the filtration on the complex is bounded.

nodes.name: First quadrant spectral sequence
nodes.description: A spectral sequence with E_r^{p,q} = 0 whenever p < 0 or q < 0, which always converges boundedly since for fixed (p,q) only finitely many differentials can be nonzero.

nodes.name: Transgression
nodes.description: In a first quadrant spectral sequence, the differential d_n: E_n^{0,n-1} -> E_n^{n,0} connecting the base and fiber terms, a partially-defined map appearing in the five-term exact sequence.

nodes.name: Five-term exact sequence of a spectral sequence
nodes.description: For a first quadrant spectral sequence converging to H_*, the sequence H_2 -> E_2^{2,0} -> E_2^{0,1} -> H_1 -> E_2^{1,0} -> 0 is exact.

nodes.name: Left hyper-derived functors
nodes.description: For a right exact functor F, the left hyper-derived functors L_n F(C) are H_n(F(P)) where P -> C is a quasi-isomorphism from a complex of projectives, generalizing left derived functors to chain complexes.

nodes.name: Right hyper-derived functors
nodes.description: For a left exact functor F, the right hyper-derived functors R^n F(C) are H^n(F(I)) where C -> I is a quasi-isomorphism to a complex of injectives, generalizing right derived functors to cochain complexes.

nodes.name: Hyperhomology spectral sequences
nodes.description: For a right exact functor F and a chain complex C, there are two spectral sequences with E_2 = (L_p F)(H_q(C)) and E_1 = (L_q F)(C_p) both converging to L_{p+q} F(C).

nodes.name: Existence of Cartan-Eilenberg resolutions
nodes.description: Every bounded-below chain complex over an abelian category with enough projectives admits a Cartan-Eilenberg resolution.

nodes.name: Universal coefficients spectral sequence
nodes.description: For a chain complex C of flat R-modules and an R-module M, there is a spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = Tor_p^R(H_q(C), M) converging to H_{p+q}(C tensor_R M).

nodes.name: Kunneth spectral sequence
nodes.description: For chain complexes C and D over R with C flat, there is a spectral sequence E_2 = Tor_p^R(H_i(C), H_j(D)) converging to H_{p+q}(C tensor_R D).

nodes.name: Mapping lemma for spectral sequences
nodes.description: A morphism of spectral sequences that is an isomorphism at the E_r page for some r is an isomorphism at all subsequent pages and at E_infinity.

nodes.name: Degeneration at E_2
nodes.description: A spectral sequence degenerates at E_2 if all differentials d_r = 0 for r >= 2, so E_2 = E_infinity.

nodes.name: Exact couple construction of spectral sequences
nodes.description: Constructs a spectral sequence from an exact couple by iterating the derived couple operation, producing pages E_r with differentials d_r = j_r k_r.

nodes.name: Spectral sequence comparison technique
nodes.description: Computes the abutment of a spectral sequence by using a second spectral sequence for the same double complex whose E_2 page is simpler, exploiting the fact that both converge to the same target.

nodes.name: Grothendieck spectral sequence construction technique
nodes.description: Applies the Grothendieck spectral sequence to a composite of left exact functors by analyzing the resulting double complex from Cartan-Eilenberg or injective resolutions.

nodes.name: Augmentation map epsilon: ZG -> Z
nodes.description: The ring homomorphism epsilon: ZG -> Z defined by epsilon(sum n_g g) = sum n_g, making Z into a trivial G-module.

nodes.name: Coinvariants M_G
nodes.description: The module of coinvariants M_G = M / I_G M = Z tensor_{ZG} M is the largest quotient of a G-module M on which G acts trivially.

nodes.name: Invariants M^G
nodes.description: The module of G-invariants M^G = {m in M : gm = m for all g in G} = Hom_{ZG}(Z, M) is the largest submodule on which G acts trivially.

nodes.name: H_0(G, M) = M_G
nodes.description: The zeroth group homology H_0(G, M) is naturally isomorphic to the coinvariants M_G.

nodes.name: H^0(G, M) = M^G
nodes.description: The zeroth group cohomology H^0(G, M) is naturally isomorphic to the invariants M^G.

nodes.name: H^1(G, M) classifies crossed homomorphisms
nodes.description: The first cohomology group H^1(G, M) is isomorphic to the group of crossed homomorphisms from G to M modulo the principal crossed homomorphisms.

nodes.name: H_1(G, Z) = G^{ab}
nodes.description: The first homology group H_1(G, Z) with trivial integer coefficients is naturally isomorphic to the abelianization G/[G, G].

nodes.name: Hopf formula for H_2
nodes.description: If G = F/R with F free, then H_2(G, Z) = (R intersect [F,F]) / [F,R].

nodes.name: Inhomogeneous bar resolution
nodes.description: A free ZG-resolution of Z with n-th term the free ZG-module on n-tuples [g_1|...|g_n] of elements of G, with differential using the inhomogeneous bar formulas.

nodes.name: Homogeneous bar resolution
nodes.description: A free ZG-resolution of Z with n-th term the free abelian group on (n+1)-tuples [g_0, ..., g_n] with diagonal G-action.

nodes.name: Coinduced module Coind_H^G N
nodes.description: The coinduced module from a subgroup H to G is Coind_H^G N = Hom_{ZH}(ZG, N), the right adjoint to the restriction functor from G-modules to H-modules.

nodes.name: Ind = Coind for finite index subgroups
nodes.description: If H is a subgroup of finite index in G, then ZG tensor_{ZH} N and Hom_{ZH}(ZG, N) are naturally isomorphic as G-modules.

nodes.name: cor composed with res equals multiplication by [G:H]
nodes.description: For H a subgroup of finite index [G:H] in G, the composite cor res: H^n(G, M) -> H^n(G, M) is multiplication by the index [G:H].

nodes.name: Lyndon-Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence
nodes.description: For a group extension 1 -> N -> G -> Q -> 1, there is a first-quadrant spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = H^p(Q, H^q(N, M)) converging to H^{p+q}(G, M), and a homological analogue.

nodes.name: Five-term exact sequence in group cohomology
nodes.description: For 1 -> N -> G -> Q -> 1, the exact sequence 0 -> H^1(Q, M^N) -> H^1(G, M) -> H^1(N, M)^Q -> H^2(Q, M^N) -> H^2(G, M) arises from the LHS spectral sequence.

nodes.name: Five-term exact sequence in group homology
nodes.description: For 1 -> N -> G -> Q -> 1, the exact sequence H_2(G, Z) -> H_2(Q, Z) -> N/[G,N] -> H_1(G, Z) -> H_1(Q, Z) -> 0.

nodes.name: cd(G) = proj.dim_{ZG}(Z)
nodes.description: The cohomological dimension cd(G) equals the projective dimension of Z as a ZG-module.

nodes.name: Group of type FL
nodes.description: A group G is of type FL if the trivial G-module Z admits a finite free resolution over ZG.

nodes.name: Group of type FP
nodes.description: A group G is of type FP if the trivial G-module Z admits a finite projective resolution over ZG.

nodes.name: Free groups have cd = 1
nodes.description: A group G is free if and only if cd(G) <= 1, equivalently if and only if the augmentation ideal I_G is a free ZG-module.

nodes.name: Complete (Tate) resolution
nodes.description: An acyclic complex of finitely generated free ZG-modules agreeing with a projective resolution of Z in positive degrees and with the dual in negative degrees, spliced via the norm map.

nodes.name: Tate cohomology H-hat^0 = M^G / N_G(M)
nodes.description: For a finite group G, the zeroth Tate cohomology is isomorphic to M^G / im(N_G).

nodes.name: Tate cohomology H-hat^{-1} = ker(N_G) / I_G M
nodes.description: For a finite group G, the Tate cohomology group H-hat^{-1}(G, M) is ker(N_G) / I_G M.

nodes.name: Tate cohomology long exact sequence
nodes.description: For a finite group G and a short exact sequence of G-modules, there is a long exact sequence in Tate cohomology extending over all integers n.

nodes.name: Tate cohomology of induced modules vanishes
nodes.description: For a finite group G, if M is an induced G-module then H-hat^n(G, M) = 0 for all integers n.

nodes.name: Cup product in Tate cohomology
nodes.description: The cup product extends to Tate cohomology as a graded pairing H-hat^p(G, M) tensor H-hat^q(G, N) -> H-hat^{p+q}(G, M tensor N) for all integers p, q.

nodes.name: Periodicity in group cohomology via cup product
nodes.description: A finite group G has periodic cohomology of period d if and only if there exists u in H^d(G, Z) such that cup product with u induces isomorphisms on all Tate cohomology groups.

nodes.name: Maschke's theorem for group cohomology
nodes.description: If G is a finite group of order n and multiplication by n is an isomorphism on M, then H^k(G, M) = 0 for all k >= 1.

nodes.name: Universal coefficient theorem for group cohomology
nodes.description: There is a natural split short exact sequence 0 -> Ext^1_Z(H_{n-1}(G, Z), A) -> H^n(G, A) -> Hom_Z(H_n(G, Z), A) -> 0 for any trivial G-module A.

nodes.name: Cohomology of finite cyclic groups
nodes.description: For Z/nZ with trivial coefficients: H^0 = Z, H^{2k-1} = Z/nZ for k >= 1, H^{2k} = 0 for k >= 1.

nodes.name: Cohomology of free abelian groups
nodes.description: For G = Z^r, the cohomology ring H^*(G, Z) is isomorphic to the exterior algebra Lambda^*(Z^r).

nodes.name: Diagonal approximation on bar resolution
nodes.description: Constructs the cup product in group cohomology by defining a chain map from the bar resolution to its tensor square compatible with the augmentation.

nodes.name: Bar resolution technique for computing group (co)homology
nodes.description: Computes group (co)homology by applying Z tensor_{ZG} - or Hom_{ZG}(-, M) to the bar resolution, producing explicit complexes whose elements are functions on tuples of group elements.

nodes.name: Dimension shifting in group cohomology
nodes.description: Embeds a G-module M into a coinduced module to shift cohomological dimension, reducing H^n statements to H^{n-1} via the connecting homomorphism.

nodes.name: Lie algebra module
nodes.description: A k-module M with a Lie algebra action g x M -> M satisfying [x,y].m = x.(y.m) - y.(x.m), equivalently a left module over U(g).

nodes.name: Augmentation of U(g)
nodes.description: The algebra homomorphism epsilon: U(g) -> k defined by epsilon(x) = 0 for all x in g, making k into a trivial g-module.

nodes.name: H^0(g, M) as invariants
nodes.description: The zeroth Lie algebra cohomology H^0(g, M) = M^g = {m in M : x.m = 0 for all x in g}.

nodes.name: H_0(g, M) as coinvariants
nodes.description: The zeroth Lie algebra homology H_0(g, M) = M_g = M / g.M, the module of g-coinvariants.

nodes.name: H^1(g, M) as derivations modulo inner derivations
nodes.description: The first Lie algebra cohomology H^1(g, M) = Der(g, M)/Inn(g, M).

nodes.name: H^2(g, M) classifies abelian Lie algebra extensions
nodes.description: The second cohomology H^2(g, M) is in natural bijection with equivalence classes of abelian extensions 0 -> M -> e -> g -> 0.

nodes.name: H_1(g, k) as abelianization
nodes.description: The first homology H_1(g, k) with trivial coefficients is isomorphic to g/[g,g].

nodes.name: Abelian Lie algebra extension
nodes.description: A short exact sequence 0 -> M -> e -> g -> 0 of Lie algebras where M is an abelian ideal in e, inheriting a g-module structure.

nodes.name: Chevalley-Eilenberg complex as U(g)-free resolution
nodes.description: The complex V_*(g) = U(g) tensor_k Lambda^*(g) with appropriate differential is a free U(g)-resolution of the trivial module k when g is a free k-module.

nodes.name: Invariant forms and H^*(g, k)
nodes.description: For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra g over characteristic zero, H^*(g, k) is computed by g-invariant forms in Lambda^*(g^*); for semisimple g this is the exterior algebra on primitive generators.

nodes.name: Cohomology of gl_n
nodes.description: Over characteristic zero, H^*(gl_n(k), k) = Lambda(c_1, c_3, ..., c_{2n-1}) on generators of odd degrees.

nodes.name: Cohomology of sl_n
nodes.description: Over characteristic zero, H^*(sl_n(k), k) = Lambda(c_3, c_5, ..., c_{2n-1}) on generators of odd degrees.

nodes.name: Inner derivation of a Lie algebra
nodes.description: For m in M, the derivation d_m: g -> M defined by d_m(x) = x.m, forming the subspace Inn(g, M) of 1-coboundaries in Lie algebra cohomology.

nodes.name: H^n vanishes for semisimple g and nontrivial irreducible M
nodes.description: If g is finite-dimensional semisimple over characteristic zero and M is a nontrivial finite-dimensional irreducible g-module, then H^n(g, M) = 0 for all n >= 0.

nodes.name: H_2(g, k) and central extensions
nodes.description: The second homology H_2(g, k) with trivial coefficients classifies central extensions of the Lie algebra g.

nodes.name: Hopf algebra structure on U(g)
nodes.description: U(g) carries a cocommutative Hopf algebra structure with comultiplication Delta(x) = x tensor 1 + 1 tensor x for x in g, antipode S(x) = -x, and counit epsilon.

nodes.name: Primitive elements of U(g)
nodes.description: The set of primitive elements {x in U(g) : Delta(x) = x tensor 1 + 1 tensor x} is exactly g, recovering the Lie algebra from its universal enveloping algebra.

nodes.name: Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence for Lie algebras
nodes.description: For an ideal h of a Lie algebra g and a g-module M, there is a convergent spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = H^p(g/h, H^q(h, M)) => H^{p+q}(g, M).

nodes.name: Chevalley-Eilenberg coboundary formula
nodes.description: Computes the differential in Lie algebra cohomology by the explicit formula involving the g-action and Lie bracket terms on Hom_k(Lambda^n(g), M).

nodes.name: Casimir operator technique for vanishing theorems
nodes.description: Uses the Casimir element in the center of U(g) to show it acts as zero on trivial modules but invertibly on nontrivial modules, forcing Ext groups to vanish.

nodes.name: Simplex category
nodes.description: The category Delta whose objects are the finite totally ordered sets [n] = {0, 1, ..., n} and whose morphisms are the nondecreasing maps, indexing simplicial objects.

nodes.name: Face maps
nodes.description: The morphisms d_i: X_n -> X_{n-1} for 0 <= i <= n in a simplicial object, induced by the injective order-preserving maps that skip the value i.

nodes.name: Degeneracy maps
nodes.description: The morphisms s_i: X_n -> X_{n+1} for 0 <= i <= n in a simplicial object, induced by the surjective order-preserving maps that repeat the value i.

nodes.name: Simplicial identities
nodes.description: The relations d_i d_j = d_{j-1} d_i for i < j, s_i s_j = s_{j+1} s_i for i <= j, and mixed face-degeneracy relations characterizing the simplex category.

nodes.name: Simplicial abelian group
nodes.description: A simplicial object in the category of abelian groups, i.e., a contravariant functor Delta^op -> Ab.

nodes.name: Standard n-simplex
nodes.description: The simplicial set Delta[n] = Hom_{Delta}(-, [n]) represented by [n], whose k-simplices are order-preserving maps [k] -> [n].

nodes.name: Singular simplicial set
nodes.description: The simplicial set S(X) of a topological space X whose n-simplices are continuous maps from the standard topological n-simplex to X.

nodes.name: Geometric realization
nodes.description: The functor |.|: sSet -> Top defined as the coend |X| = coprod_n (X_n x Delta^n) / ~, left adjoint to the singular simplicial set functor.

nodes.name: Simplicial map
nodes.description: A natural transformation f: X -> Y between simplicial objects, consisting of morphisms f_n: X_n -> Y_n commuting with all face and degeneracy maps.

nodes.name: Simplicial homotopy
nodes.description: A simplicial homotopy between simplicial maps f, g: X -> Y is a simplicial map H: X x Delta[1] -> Y restricting to f and g on the endpoints.

nodes.name: Simplicial homotopy groups
nodes.description: For a Kan complex X with basepoint, the groups pi_n(X) defined as equivalence classes of n-simplices with boundary at the basepoint, generalizing homotopy groups of spaces.

nodes.name: Normalized chain complex
nodes.description: The subcomplex NA of the Moore complex with (NA)_n = intersection of ker(d_i) for i = 1, ..., n, naturally chain homotopy equivalent to the Moore complex.

nodes.name: Degeneracy subcomplex
nodes.description: The subcomplex DA of the Moore complex generated by images of all degeneracy maps, satisfying CA = NA direct sum DA as graded abelian groups.

nodes.name: Dold-Kan inverse functor K
nodes.description: The functor K: Ch_{>=0}(Ab) -> sAb, quasi-inverse to the normalized chain complex functor, reconstructing a simplicial abelian group from a chain complex.

nodes.name: Alexander-Whitney map
nodes.description: The natural chain map AW: C(A x B) -> C(A) tensor C(B) providing one direction of the Eilenberg-Zilber equivalence.

nodes.name: Shuffle map (Eilenberg-MacLane map)
nodes.description: The natural chain map nabla: C(A) tensor C(B) -> C(A x B) defined using (p,q)-shuffles, providing the inverse direction of the Eilenberg-Zilber equivalence.

nodes.name: Shuffle
nodes.description: A (p,q)-shuffle is a permutation of {0, ..., p+q-1} preserving the relative order within the first p and last q elements, used in defining products on chain complexes.

nodes.name: Nerve of a category
nodes.description: The simplicial set N(C) whose n-simplices are composable chains of n morphisms, with face maps by composition and degeneracy maps by identity insertion.

nodes.name: Classifying space of a group (via nerve)
nodes.description: The geometric realization BG = |N(G)| of the nerve of the one-object category of G, with pi_1(BG) = G and contractible universal cover EG.

nodes.name: Cotriple (comonad)
nodes.description: An endofunctor G: C -> C with natural transformations epsilon: G -> id (counit) and delta: G -> G^2 (comultiplication) satisfying coassociativity and counitality.

nodes.name: Cotriple homology
nodes.description: For a cotriple G and coefficient functor E: C -> Ab, the groups H_n^G(A, E) = H_n(E(G_*(A))) obtained by applying E to the cotriple resolution.

nodes.name: Andre-Quillen cohomology
nodes.description: For a commutative k-algebra A and A-module M, the groups D^n(A/k, M) defined as derived functors of derivations Der_k(A, M), classifying algebra extensions.

nodes.name: Bisimplicial object
nodes.description: A functor X: Delta^op x Delta^op -> C, equivalently a simplicial object in simplicial objects, with commuting horizontal and vertical face and degeneracy maps.

nodes.name: Diagonal of a bisimplicial object
nodes.description: The simplicial object diag(X) with diag(X)_n = X_{n,n}, whose geometric realization is naturally homeomorphic to that of the total object.

nodes.name: Normalization theorem
nodes.description: The inclusion of the normalized chain complex into the Moore complex of a simplicial abelian group is a chain homotopy equivalence, with the decomposition CA_n = NA_n direct sum DA_n.

nodes.name: Simplicial homotopy invariance of homology
nodes.description: Simplicially homotopic maps of simplicial abelian groups induce chain homotopic maps on Moore complexes, so simplicial homotopy equivalences induce homology isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Acyclicity of cotriple resolutions
nodes.description: The augmented simplicial object from a cotriple resolution is aspherical when the cotriple arises from an adjunction.

nodes.name: Transitivity exact sequence (Andre-Quillen)
nodes.description: For ring maps k -> A -> B and a B-module M, there is a long exact sequence relating D_n(A/k, M), D_n(B/k, M), and D_n(B/A, M).

nodes.name: Smooth algebra vanishing (Andre-Quillen)
nodes.description: A commutative k-algebra A is smooth if and only if D_n(A/k, M) = 0 for all n >= 1 and all A-modules M.

nodes.name: Extra degeneracy (contracting homotopy)
nodes.description: An extra degeneracy s_{-1} on an augmented simplicial object provides a contracting simplicial homotopy proving the augmented complex is aspherical.

nodes.name: Hochschild complex (bar complex for algebras)
nodes.description: The chain complex with C_n(A, M) = M tensor A^{tensor n} and face maps by multiplication of adjacent factors, computing Hochschild homology.

nodes.name: Formal deformation of an algebra
nodes.description: A k[[t]]-algebra structure on A[[t]] of the form a * b = ab + m_1(a,b)t + m_2(a,b)t^2 + ..., reducing to A modulo t.

nodes.name: HH^2 classifies infinitesimal deformations
nodes.description: HH^2(A, A) classifies equivalence classes of infinitesimal deformations of A, while HH^3(A, A) contains obstructions to extending deformations.

nodes.name: Connes' B operator
nodes.description: The operator B: C_n(A) -> C_{n+1}(A) defined by B = (1 - t)sN satisfying B^2 = 0 and bB + Bb = 0, connecting Hochschild and cyclic homology.

nodes.name: SBI exact sequence
nodes.description: The long exact sequence ... -> HH_n(A) -> HC_n(A) -> HC_{n-2}(A) -> HH_{n-1}(A) -> ... relating Hochschild and cyclic homology via the periodicity operator S and Connes' B.

nodes.name: Connes' bicomplex
nodes.description: The first-quadrant bicomplex with columns C_n^{lambda}(A) = C_n(A)/im(1-t) and horizontal differential induced by B, quasi-isomorphic to the cyclic bicomplex in characteristic zero.

nodes.name: Morita invariance of Hochschild and cyclic homology
nodes.description: Morita equivalent k-algebras have isomorphic Hochschild and cyclic homology in all degrees.

nodes.name: Hochschild-Kostant-Rosenberg theorem
nodes.description: For a smooth commutative k-algebra A, the antisymmetrization map gives HH_n(A) = Omega^n_{A/k}.

nodes.name: Loday-Quillen-Tsygan theorem
nodes.description: There is a natural isomorphism HC_{n-1}(A) = prim H_n(gl(A), k) between cyclic homology and the primitive part of the Lie algebra homology of gl(A).

nodes.name: Excision in Hochschild and cyclic homology
nodes.description: For a surjection A -> B with kernel I, there is a long exact sequence relating HH_*(A), HH_*(B), and HH_*(A, I), with an analogous sequence for cyclic homology when I is H-unital.

nodes.name: Triangulated category axioms (TR1-TR4)
nodes.description: An additive category with shift autoequivalence [1] and distinguished triangles X -> Y -> Z -> X[1] satisfying four axioms: existence, rotation, morphism extension, and the octahedral axiom.

nodes.name: RHom complex
nodes.description: The total right derived functor of Hom, yielding RHom(A, B) in D(Ab) with H^n(RHom(A, B)) = Ext^n(A, B).

nodes.name: Calculus of fractions
nodes.description: Describes morphisms in a localized category C[S^{-1}] as equivalence classes of roofs or coroofs when S satisfies Ore conditions.

nodes.name: Replacing spectral sequences with triangles
nodes.description: Uses distinguished triangles in the derived category to encode information equivalent to spectral sequence E_2 pages, avoiding convergence issues.

nodes.name: Abelian category axioms (AB1-AB5)
nodes.description: Grothendieck's hierarchy: AB1-AB2 define abelian categories; AB3 requires coproducts; AB4 requires exact coproducts; AB5 requires exact filtered colimits; dual axioms AB3*-AB5* concern products.

nodes.name: Grothendieck category
nodes.description: An abelian category satisfying AB5 with a generator, guaranteeing enough injectives by the Grothendieck theorem.

nodes.name: Inverse limit functor lim
nodes.description: For an inverse system {A_i, f_{ij}} indexed by a directed poset, lim A_i is the submodule of prod A_i of compatible elements with f_{ij}(a_j) = a_i for all i <= j.

nodes.name: Mittag-Leffler implies lim^1 vanishes
nodes.description: If a tower of modules satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition, then lim^1 = 0.

nodes.name: lim^1 and short exact sequences of towers
nodes.description: A short exact sequence of towers induces a six-term exact sequence 0 -> lim A_n -> lim B_n -> lim C_n -> lim^1 A_n -> lim^1 B_n -> lim^1 C_n -> 0.

nodes.name: Universal coefficient theorem for homology
nodes.description: For a chain complex C of flat R-modules with flat boundaries, there is a natural split short exact sequence 0 -> H_n(C) tensor M -> H_n(C tensor M) -> Tor_1(H_{n-1}(C), M) -> 0.

nodes.name: Universal coefficient theorem for cohomology
nodes.description: For a chain complex C of free abelian groups, there is a natural split short exact sequence 0 -> Ext^1(H_{n-1}(C), G) -> H^n(Hom(C, G)) -> Hom(H_n(C), G) -> 0.

nodes.name: Symmetry of Tor
nodes.description: For a commutative ring R, there is a natural isomorphism Tor_n^R(A, B) = Tor_n^R(B, A) for all n >= 0.

nodes.name: Tor for abelian groups
nodes.description: For abelian groups, Tor_n^Z(A, B) = 0 for all n >= 2 since Z has global dimension 1.

nodes.name: Ext for abelian groups
nodes.description: For abelian groups, Ext^n_Z(A, B) = 0 for n >= 2, and Ext^1_Z(Z/n, B) = B/nB.

nodes.name: Derivation of LHS via Grothendieck spectral sequence
nodes.description: The Lyndon-Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence arises as a special case of the Grothendieck spectral sequence for the composite of the fixed-point functors (-)^N and (-)^{G/N}.

nodes.name: Metacategory
nodes.description: A metagraph equipped with composition and identity arrows satisfying associativity and unit laws, described without requiring a set-theoretic foundation.

nodes.name: Category
nodes.description: A metacategory whose objects and morphisms each form a collection, with an associative composition law and identity morphisms for every object.

nodes.name: Small category
nodes.description: A category in which both the collection of objects and the collection of morphisms are sets, not proper classes.

nodes.name: Locally small category
nodes.description: A category in which for every pair of objects A, B the hom-collection Hom(A, B) is a set.

nodes.name: Functor
nodes.description: A morphism of categories sending objects to objects and arrows to arrows, preserving composition and identities.

nodes.name: Contravariant functor
nodes.description: A functor from the opposite category C^op to D, equivalently an assignment reversing the direction of morphisms.

nodes.name: Natural isomorphism
nodes.description: A natural transformation whose every component τ_c is an isomorphism in the target category.

nodes.name: Isomorphism of categories
nodes.description: A functor F: C → D for which there exists G: D → C with G∘F = Id_C and F∘G = Id_D as strict equality of functors.

nodes.name: Monomorphism
nodes.description: A morphism m: A → B such that m∘f = m∘g implies f = g for all parallel morphisms into A; the categorical generalization of injectivity.

nodes.name: Epimorphism
nodes.description: A morphism e: A → B such that f∘e = g∘e implies f = g for all parallel morphisms out of B; the categorical generalization of surjectivity.

nodes.name: Section (right inverse)
nodes.description: A morphism s: B → A such that r∘s = id_B for some r: A → B; equivalently, a split monomorphism.

nodes.name: Retraction (left inverse)
nodes.description: A morphism r: A → B such that r∘s = id_B for some s: B → A; equivalently, a split epimorphism.

nodes.name: Universal element
nodes.description: For a functor F: C → Set, an element u ∈ F(r) such that for every object c and x ∈ F(c) there is a unique f: r → c with F(f)(u) = x.

nodes.name: Universal arrow
nodes.description: For a functor U: D → C and object c of C, a pair (r, u: c → U(r)) initial in the comma category (c ↓ U) through which every morphism c → U(d) factors uniquely.

nodes.name: Vertical composition of natural transformations
nodes.description: Given natural transformations α: F ⇒ G and β: G ⇒ H, their vertical composite (β·α)_c = β_c ∘ α_c is a natural transformation F ⇒ H.

nodes.name: Horizontal composition (Godement product)
nodes.description: Given α: F ⇒ G (C → D) and β: H ⇒ K (D → E), the horizontal composite β∗α: HF ⇒ KG defined by (β∗α)_c = β_{G(c)} ∘ H(α_c) = K(α_c) ∘ β_{F(c)}.

nodes.name: Interchange law
nodes.description: Horizontal and vertical composition of natural transformations satisfy (β'·β) ∗ (α'·α) = (β'∗α')·(β∗α), expressing compatibility of the two composition operations in a 2-category.

nodes.name: Whiskering
nodes.description: Pre- or post-composing a natural transformation α: F ⇒ G with a functor H, yielding Hα: HF ⇒ HG or αH: FH ⇒ GH; a special case of horizontal composition.

nodes.name: Yoneda embedding technique
nodes.function_signature: (Category C) → (Full embedding C ↪ [C^op, Set])
nodes.description: Embedding a category fully and faithfully into its presheaf category to reduce categorical statements to set-theoretic verifications.

nodes.name: Opposite category
nodes.description: The category with the same objects as C but with every morphism reversed: Hom_{C^op}(A,B) = Hom_C(B,A), with composition reversed.

nodes.name: Duality principle (categorical)
nodes.function_signature: (Statement about categories) → (Dual statement about opposite categories)
nodes.description: Any valid categorical statement remains valid when all arrows are reversed, yielding an automatic dual theorem about opposite categories.

nodes.name: Product category
nodes.description: The category whose objects are pairs (c,d) and whose morphisms are pairs (f,g) composed componentwise.

nodes.name: Comma category
nodes.description: Given functors F: A → C and G: B → C, the category whose objects are triples (a, b, h: F(a) → G(b)) and morphisms are commuting pairs.

nodes.name: Slice category
nodes.description: The comma category (Id_C ↓ c) whose objects are morphisms f: a → c and morphisms are commuting triangles over c.

nodes.name: Coslice category
nodes.description: The comma category (c ↓ Id_C) whose objects are morphisms f: c → a; the dual of the slice category.

nodes.name: Arrow category
nodes.description: The functor category [2, C] whose objects are morphisms of C and whose morphisms are commutative squares.

nodes.name: Free category on a graph
nodes.description: Given a directed graph, the category whose objects are vertices and morphisms are finite composable paths, with concatenation as composition.

nodes.name: Congruence on a category
nodes.description: An equivalence relation on each hom-set compatible with composition: if f ~ f' and g ~ g' then g∘f ~ g'∘f'.

nodes.name: Quotient category
nodes.description: Given a congruence ~ on a category C, the category C/~ with the same objects and morphisms the equivalence classes [f].

nodes.name: Presheaf (categorical)
nodes.description: A contravariant functor F: C^op → Set; the presheaf category [C^op, Set] serves as the free cocompletion of C.

nodes.name: Limit of a functor
nodes.description: For a diagram F: J → C, a terminal object in the category of cones over F, with a universal natural transformation from the constant functor to F.

nodes.name: Colimit of a functor
nodes.description: For a diagram F: J → C, an initial object in the category of cocones under F, through which every cocone factors uniquely.

nodes.name: Limit computation via products and equalizers
nodes.function_signature: (Diagram F: J → C) → (lim F as Eq(∏ F(j) ⇉ ∏ F(cod α)))
nodes.description: Constructing any limit as an equalizer of a pair of morphisms between products, reducing arbitrary limits to products and equalizers.

nodes.name: Colimit computation via coproducts and coequalizers
nodes.function_signature: (Diagram F: J → C) → (colim F as Coeq(∐ F(dom α) ⇉ ∐ F(j)))
nodes.description: Constructing any colimit as a coequalizer of a pair of morphisms between coproducts, dual to the product-equalizer construction.

nodes.name: Preservation of limits
nodes.description: A functor F preserves limits of type J if whenever (L, π) is a limit cone in the domain, then (F(L), F(π)) is a limit cone in the codomain.

nodes.name: Reflection of limits
nodes.description: A functor F reflects limits of type J if whenever (F(L), F(π)) is a limit cone in the codomain, then (L, π) was already a limit cone in the domain.

nodes.name: Creation of limits
nodes.description: A functor U creates limits of type J if for every diagram whose image has a limit, there is a unique lift to a limit that U preserves and reflects.

nodes.name: Subobject
nodes.description: An equivalence class of monomorphisms into a given object, where two monics are equivalent if they factor through each other by an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Quotient object
nodes.description: An equivalence class of epimorphisms out of a given object, dual to subobject; two epics are equivalent if they factor through each other.

nodes.name: Adjunction
nodes.description: A pair of functors F: C → D and U: D → C with a natural bijection Hom_D(Fc, d) ≅ Hom_C(c, Ud); F is left adjoint to U.

nodes.name: Special adjoint functor theorem (SAFT)
nodes.description: A limit-preserving functor from a complete, locally small, well-powered category with a cogenerating set has a left adjoint; the solution set condition is automatic.

nodes.name: Solution set condition
nodes.description: For a functor U: D → C and object c, the condition that there exists a set of morphisms {c → U(d_i)} through which every c → U(d) factors.

nodes.name: Free-forgetful adjunction
nodes.description: The prototypical adjunction where F constructs free algebraic structures and U forgets the structure; the unit is the inclusion of generators.

nodes.name: Forgetful functor
nodes.description: A functor that discards algebraic structure, sending an object to its underlying set; often faithful and often has a left adjoint.

nodes.name: Free functor
nodes.description: A left adjoint to a forgetful functor, constructing the free algebraic structure on a given set.

nodes.name: Faithful functor
nodes.description: A functor F: C → D such that for all objects A, B the map F: Hom(A,B) → Hom(FA, FB) is injective.

nodes.name: Full functor
nodes.description: A functor F: C → D such that for all objects A, B the map F: Hom(A,B) → Hom(FA, FB) is surjective.

nodes.name: Fully faithful functor
nodes.description: A functor that is both full and faithful, i.e., bijective on all hom-sets; an embedding of one category as a full subcategory.

nodes.name: Essentially surjective functor
nodes.description: A functor F: C → D such that for every object d in D there exists c in C with F(c) ≅ d.

nodes.name: Equivalence iff fully faithful and essentially surjective
nodes.description: A functor is an equivalence of categories if and only if it is full, faithful, and essentially surjective on objects.

nodes.name: Adjunctions give rise to monads
nodes.description: Every adjunction F ⊣ U gives rise to a monad (T = UF, η, μ = UεF) on the base category, where μ: T² ⇒ T is obtained from the counit.

nodes.name: Filtered category
nodes.description: A nonempty small category J where any two objects have a common upper bound and any two parallel morphisms are coequalized by some morphism.

nodes.name: Filtered colimits commute with finite limits in Set
nodes.description: In Set, the canonical map colim_J lim_K F(j,k) → lim_K colim_J F(j,k) is a bijection when J is filtered and K is finite.

nodes.name: Generator (separator)
nodes.description: An object G such that for distinct parallel morphisms f, g: A ⇉ B there exists h: G → A with f∘h ≠ g∘h; equivalently, Hom(G,−) is faithful.

nodes.name: Cogenerator (coseparator)
nodes.description: An object Q such that for distinct f, g: A ⇉ B there exists h: B → Q with h∘f ≠ h∘g; dual of generator.

nodes.name: Well-powered category
nodes.description: A category in which for every object the collection of subobjects forms a set rather than a proper class.

nodes.name: End (category theory)
nodes.description: For a bifunctor S: C^op × C → D, the universal wedge: an object with morphisms e_c: E → S(c,c) satisfying the wedge condition for all f: c → c'.

nodes.name: Coend (category theory)
nodes.description: For a bifunctor S: C^op × C → D, the universal cowedge: the colimit dual to the end, with morphisms S(c,c) → E satisfying the cowedge condition.

nodes.name: Natural transformations as an end
nodes.description: The set Nat(F,G) of natural transformations between functors F, G: C → D equals the end ∫_c Hom(F(c), G(c)).

nodes.name: Limit as an end
nodes.description: For any functor F: J → C, its limit can be expressed as the end ∫_j F(j) with appropriate wedge conditions, unifying limits and ends.

nodes.name: Co-Yoneda lemma (density formula)
nodes.description: Every presheaf F: C^op → Set is a canonical colimit of representables: F ≅ colim_{(c,x) ∈ el(F)} Hom(−,c).

nodes.name: Category of elements
nodes.description: For F: C → Set, the category whose objects are pairs (c, x ∈ F(c)) and morphisms (c,x) → (c',x') are f: c → c' with F(f)(x) = x'.

nodes.name: Representable functors preserve limits
nodes.description: For any object A, the functor Hom(A,−): C → Set preserves all limits; dually, Hom(−,A) sends colimits to limits.

nodes.name: Algebra over a monad (T-algebra)
nodes.description: A pair (A, h: TA → A) satisfying h∘η_A = id_A and h∘μ_A = h∘T(h); an action of the monad T on the object A.

nodes.name: Eilenberg-Moore category
nodes.description: The category of all T-algebras and T-algebra morphisms for a monad T; the terminal resolution of the monad.

nodes.name: Kleisli category
nodes.description: The category with objects of C and morphisms A → B given by C-morphisms A → T(B), with Kleisli composition using the monad multiplication; the initial resolution.

nodes.name: Comparison functor (Eilenberg-Moore)
nodes.description: For an adjunction F ⊣ U inducing monad T, the unique functor K: D → C^T sending d to (U(d), U(ε_d)) comparing D with the category of algebras.

nodes.name: Every monad arises from an adjunction
nodes.description: Every monad (T, η, μ) arises from at least one adjunction: the Kleisli adjunction (initial) and the Eilenberg-Moore adjunction (terminal).

nodes.name: Beck's monadicity theorem (precise form)
nodes.description: A functor U is monadic iff U has a left adjoint, reflects isomorphisms, and its domain has coequalizers of all U-split pairs which U preserves.

nodes.name: Beck's monadicity theorem (crude form)
nodes.description: A functor U with left adjoint is monadic if U reflects isomorphisms and the domain has and U preserves all coequalizers.

nodes.name: Split coequalizer
nodes.description: A coequalizer with a section and a contracting homotopy making it absolute, i.e., preserved by every functor.

nodes.name: Reflexive coequalizer
nodes.description: A coequalizer of a reflexive pair f, g: A ⇉ B where there exists s: B → A with f∘s = g∘s = id_B.

nodes.name: Absolute coequalizer
nodes.description: A coequalizer preserved by every functor; split coequalizers are the paradigmatic example.

nodes.name: Monadic functor
nodes.description: A functor U: D → C such that the comparison functor K: D → C^T is an equivalence, where T is the induced monad.

nodes.name: Creation of limits by monadic functors
nodes.description: If U: D → C is monadic and C has limits of type J, then D has limits of type J and U creates and preserves them.

nodes.name: Free algebra over a monad
nodes.description: For a monad T, the free T-algebra on c is (Tc, μ_c: T²c → Tc); the image of the left adjoint in the Eilenberg-Moore adjunction.

nodes.name: Monad resolution
nodes.function_signature: (T-algebra (A,h)) → (Simplicial resolution ⋯ T³A ⇉ T²A ⇉ TA → A)
nodes.description: The simplicial resolution of a T-algebra by free algebras, used to compute derived functors and homological invariants of monadic structures.

nodes.name: Completeness of Eilenberg-Moore category
nodes.description: If C is complete, then C^T is also complete, with limits created by the forgetful functor U^T: C^T → C.

nodes.name: Beck's conditions verification
nodes.function_signature: (Functor U) → (Is U monadic?)
nodes.description: Proving a functor is monadic by checking existence of left adjoint, reflection of isomorphisms, and preservation/existence of relevant coequalizers.

nodes.name: Monoid object (in a monoidal category)
nodes.type_signature: (M, μ: M⊗M → M, η: I → M)
nodes.description: An object M in a monoidal category with multiplication μ and unit η satisfying associativity and unit axioms as commutative diagrams.

nodes.name: Strict monoidal category
nodes.description: A monoidal category in which the associator and unitors are identity natural transformations, so tensoring is strictly associative and unital.

nodes.name: Pentagon axiom
nodes.description: The coherence condition requiring that two paths of associators from ((A⊗B)⊗C)⊗D to A⊗(B⊗(C⊗D)) coincide, forming a commutative pentagon.

nodes.name: Triangle axiom (unit coherence)
nodes.description: The coherence condition that the diagram involving the associator α_{A,I,B} and the unitors ρ_A⊗id_B and id_A⊗λ_B commutes.

nodes.name: Monoidal functor (lax)
nodes.description: A functor F between monoidal categories with φ₀: I_D → F(I_C) and φ_{A,B}: FA⊗FB → F(A⊗B) satisfying coherence conditions.

nodes.name: Strong monoidal functor
nodes.description: A monoidal functor whose structure morphisms φ₀ and φ_{A,B} are all isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Strict monoidal functor
nodes.description: A monoidal functor whose structure morphisms are identities: F(A⊗B) = FA⊗FB and F(I) = I strictly.

nodes.name: Closed monoidal category
nodes.description: A monoidal category where −⊗B has a right adjoint [B,−] (internal hom) for every B, giving Hom(A⊗B, C) ≅ Hom(A, [B,C]).

nodes.name: Cartesian closed category
nodes.description: A category with finite products that is closed: −×B has a right adjoint B^(−) (exponential) for every B, with Hom(A×B, C) ≅ Hom(A, C^B).

nodes.name: Internal hom (exponential object)
nodes.description: In a closed monoidal category, the object [B,C] representing Hom(−⊗B, C), with evaluation ev: [B,C]⊗B → C.

nodes.name: Eckmann-Hilton argument
nodes.description: If a set carries two monoid structures with interchange, the two multiplications coincide and are commutative; a monoid in monoids is a commutative monoid.

nodes.name: Category of monoids Mon(C)
nodes.description: For a monoidal category C, the category whose objects are monoid objects and morphisms preserve multiplication and unit.

nodes.name: Preadditive category
nodes.description: A category enriched over abelian groups: each hom-set carries an abelian group structure and composition is bilinear.

nodes.name: Biproduct
nodes.description: In a preadditive category, an object simultaneously a product and coproduct of A and B, with projections and injections satisfying π_i∘ι_j = δ_{ij}.

nodes.name: Kernel (categorical)
nodes.description: The equalizer of a morphism f: A → B and the zero morphism, universal among morphisms k with f∘k = 0.

nodes.name: Cokernel (categorical)
nodes.description: The coequalizer of f: A → B and the zero morphism, universal among morphisms q with q∘f = 0.

nodes.name: Image (categorical)
nodes.description: The image of f: A → B is the kernel of the cokernel of f; the smallest subobject of B through which f factors.

nodes.name: Freyd-Mitchell embedding theorem
nodes.description: Every small abelian category admits an exact, fully faithful embedding into the category of modules over some ring.

nodes.name: Regular epimorphism
nodes.description: A morphism that is the coequalizer of some pair of morphisms; in an abelian category, every epimorphism is regular.

nodes.name: Extremal epimorphism
nodes.description: An epimorphism e such that if e = m∘g with m mono, then m is an isomorphism; in abelian categories, coincides with regular and ordinary epimorphisms.

nodes.name: Abelian group object
nodes.description: A group object in a category with finite products: an object G with multiplication, unit, and inverse morphisms satisfying group axioms as commutative diagrams, plus commutativity.

nodes.name: Filtered colimits in algebraic categories
nodes.description: In categories of algebras, filtered colimits exist and are computed on underlying sets; the forgetful functor to Set preserves and creates them.

nodes.name: Interchange of limits and colimits
nodes.description: Under appropriate conditions a canonical morphism colim lim → lim colim exists; precise conditions for it to be an isomorphism involve finality and filteredness.

nodes.name: Final functor (cofinal)
nodes.description: A functor φ: J → K such that for every k in K the comma category (k ↓ φ) is nonempty and connected; colimits over K equal colimits over J.

nodes.name: Final functor theorem
nodes.description: If φ: J → K is final and F: K → C is a diagram, then colim_K F ≅ colim_J F∘φ canonically whenever either exists.

nodes.name: Reflexive coequalizer existence
nodes.description: In many algebraic categories and categories of algebras over a monad, reflexive coequalizers exist even when general coequalizers may not.

nodes.name: Limits in functor categories
nodes.description: If D has limits of type J, then [C,D] has limits of type J computed pointwise: (lim F_i)(c) = lim(F_i(c)).

nodes.name: Creating limits theorem
nodes.description: If U: D → C creates limits of type J and C has such limits, then D has them; combined with monadicity, establishes completeness of algebraic categories.

nodes.name: Left Kan extension
nodes.description: For K: A → B and F: A → C, the functor Lan_K F with universal η: F ⇒ (Lan_K F)∘K, initial among all factorizations of F through K.

nodes.name: Right Kan extension
nodes.description: For K: A → B and F: A → C, the functor Ran_K F with universal ε: (Ran_K F)∘K ⇒ F, terminal among all factorizations of F through K.

nodes.name: Pointwise Kan extension
nodes.description: A Kan extension computable objectwise as a (co)limit: (Lan_K F)(b) = colim_{(K↓b)} F∘π or (Ran_K F)(b) = lim_{(b↓K)} F∘π.

nodes.name: Left Kan extension as colimit formula
nodes.description: When C has sufficient colimits, (Lan_K F)(b) = colim_{(K↓b)} F∘π where π: (K↓b) → A is the projection; the fundamental computational formula.

nodes.name: Right Kan extension as limit formula
nodes.description: When C has sufficient limits, (Ran_K F)(b) = lim_{(b↓K)} F∘π, dual to the left Kan extension colimit formula.

nodes.name: Kan extension along Yoneda embedding
nodes.description: Left Kan extension along y: C → [C^op, Set] gives the free cocompletion: Lan_y F is the unique cocontinuous extension of F to the presheaf category.

nodes.name: Every functor is a Kan extension of itself
nodes.description: For any functor F, F is both Lan_{Id} F and Ran_{Id} F: the Kan extension of F along the identity is F itself.

nodes.name: Adjunctions as Kan extensions
nodes.description: F has right adjoint G iff Ran_F(Id) exists and is preserved by F, giving G = Ran_F(Id); dually, left adjoints are left Kan extensions of identities.

nodes.name: All concepts are Kan extensions (Mac Lane)
nodes.description: Mac Lane's thesis that limits, colimits, adjunctions, ends, coends, and all fundamental constructions of category theory are expressible as Kan extensions.

nodes.name: Dense functor
nodes.description: A functor K: A → C such that every object of C is a canonical colimit of objects in K's image; equivalently, Lan_K(K) ≅ Id_C.

nodes.name: Density theorem (categorical)
nodes.description: A functor K: A → C is dense iff every object c is a canonical colimit c ≅ colim_{(K↓c)} K∘π; equivalently, Lan_K(K) ≅ Id_C.

nodes.name: Kan extension computation
nodes.function_signature: (Functors K, F) → (Lan_K F or Ran_K F via pointwise formula)
nodes.description: Computing Kan extensions via the pointwise formula by identifying the relevant comma category and evaluating the (co)limit.

nodes.name: Symmetric monoidal category
nodes.description: A monoidal category with a symmetry σ_{A,B}: A⊗B → B⊗A satisfying σ_{B,A}∘σ_{A,B} = id and coherence with associator and unitors.

nodes.name: Braided monoidal category
nodes.description: A monoidal category with a braiding σ_{A,B}: A⊗B → B⊗A satisfying two hexagon axioms, but not necessarily σ² = id.

nodes.name: Hexagon axioms
nodes.description: The two coherence conditions for a braiding: hexagonal diagrams involving the braiding σ and associator α must commute.

nodes.name: Coherence for braided monoidal categories
nodes.description: Every diagram of canonical isomorphisms built from associator, unitors, and braiding commutes; the free braided monoidal category is described by braids.

nodes.name: Coherence for symmetric monoidal categories
nodes.description: In a symmetric monoidal category, every diagram of canonical isomorphisms built from associators, unitors, and symmetries commutes.

nodes.name: Braid group from braided monoidal categories
nodes.description: The endomorphisms of the n-fold tensor product in the free braided monoidal category on one generator form the braid group B_n.

nodes.name: Yang-Baxter equation (categorical)
nodes.description: The braiding satisfies (σ⊗id)(id⊗σ)(σ⊗id) = (id⊗σ)(σ⊗id)(id⊗σ), a consequence of the hexagon axioms and naturality.

nodes.name: Enriched category
nodes.description: A category whose hom-sets are replaced by objects of a monoidal category V, with composition and identity V-morphisms satisfying associativity and unit axioms in V.

nodes.name: 2-category
nodes.description: A category enriched over Cat: objects, 1-morphisms, and 2-morphisms with vertical and horizontal composition satisfying the interchange law.

nodes.name: Elementary topos
nodes.description: A cartesian closed category with a subobject classifier Ω: an object with true: 1 → Ω such that every subobject is uniquely classified by a characteristic morphism.

nodes.name: Subobject classifier
nodes.description: An object Ω with true: 1 → Ω such that every monomorphism m: S ↣ A is the pullback of true along a unique characteristic morphism χ_m: A → Ω.

nodes.name: Grothendieck topos
nodes.description: A category of sheaves on a site; equivalently, a left exact reflective subcategory of a presheaf category; a Grothendieck topos is an elementary topos.

nodes.name: Grothendieck topology
nodes.description: An assignment to each object c of covering sieves stable under pullback, transitive, and containing the maximal sieve.

nodes.name: Sieve
nodes.description: A subfunctor of Hom(−,c); equivalently, a collection S of morphisms with codomain c closed under precomposition.

nodes.name: Covering family
