nodes.description: Every closed, densely defined, semibounded quadratic form on a Hilbert space is the form of a unique self-adjoint operator, establishing a bijection between such forms and operators.

nodes.name: Friedrichs extension
nodes.function_signature: (Semibounded symmetric operator A) → (Self-adjoint extension A_F with same lower bound)
nodes.description: Construction of the canonical self-adjoint extension of a semibounded symmetric operator by closing its associated quadratic form and applying the form representation theorem.

nodes.name: Analytic vector
nodes.description: A vector φ in the domain of all powers of an operator A such that Σ ‖Aⁿφ‖ tⁿ/n! converges for some t > 0, used in Nelson's theorem to establish essential self-adjointness.

nodes.name: Kato's inequality
nodes.description: The distributional inequality Δ|u| ≥ Re(sgn(ū)·Δu) for u ∈ L¹_loc with Δu ∈ L¹_loc, a key tool for proving self-adjointness and semigroup domination.

nodes.name: Hypercontractive semigroup
nodes.description: A semigroup e^{−tH} that maps Lᵖ to Lᵍ for q > p after sufficient time, with the optimal bound given by Nelson's best hypercontractive estimate for the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup.

nodes.name: Nelson's best hypercontractive estimate
nodes.description: The Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup e^{−tN} is a contraction from Lᵖ to Lᵍ if and only if e^{−2t} ≤ (p−1)/(q−1), with sharpness attained on Gaussian functions.

nodes.name: Diamagnetic inequality
nodes.description: The pointwise bound |e^{−t(−i∇−A)²}f(x)| ≤ e^{tΔ}|f|(x) showing that magnetic fields raise the ground state energy and reduce the semigroup kernel.

nodes.name: Nelson's commutator theorem
nodes.description: If H is symmetric and N is a self-adjoint operator with D(N) ⊂ D(H) satisfying ±i[H,N] ≤ cN on D(N), then H is essentially self-adjoint on D(N).

nodes.name: Kato class
nodes.description: The class K_d of potentials V for which lim_{r→0} sup_x ∫_{|x−y|<r} |V(y)|·g_d(x−y) dy = 0 where g_d is the Green's function, ensuring −Δ+V is essentially self-adjoint and its semigroup has nice properties.

nodes.name: Cook's method
nodes.function_signature: (Perturbation V, free dynamics H₀) → (Existence of wave operators Ω±)
nodes.description: Proof of existence of wave operators by showing ∫₀^∞ ‖V e^{−iH₀t} φ‖ dt < ∞ for a dense set of φ, reducing existence to an integrability condition on the perturbation.

nodes.name: Enss method
nodes.function_signature: (Short-range potential V, phase space decomposition) → (Asymptotic completeness)
nodes.description: A geometric, time-dependent proof of asymptotic completeness using phase space decomposition into incoming and outgoing states via propagation observables.

nodes.name: Kato smoothness (H-smoothness)
nodes.description: An operator A is H-smooth if ∫_{−∞}^{∞} ‖A e^{−iHt} φ‖² dt ≤ C‖φ‖² for all φ, equivalently sup_{ε>0,λ} ‖A(H−λ−iε)⁻¹A*‖ < ∞, implying absolute continuity of H on Ran(A*).

nodes.name: Kato smoothness implies absolute continuity
nodes.description: If A is H-smooth, then the spectral measure of H restricted to Ran(A*) is absolutely continuous, providing a criterion for absence of singular spectrum.

nodes.name: Lippmann–Schwinger equation
nodes.description: The integral equation ψ± = φ + (H₀ − E ∓ i0)⁻¹ V ψ± for scattering states, connecting the resolvent formalism to the time-independent scattering amplitudes.

nodes.name: Stationary scattering theory
nodes.function_signature: (Resolvent (H−z)⁻¹, boundary values) → (Scattering matrix S(λ))
nodes.description: Construction of the scattering matrix from boundary values of the resolvent at the real axis, relating the time-independent and time-dependent approaches via the Lippmann–Schwinger equation.

nodes.name: Multichannel scattering
nodes.description: Scattering theory for N-body systems with multiple asymptotic cluster decompositions, each channel labeled by a partition of particles into bound clusters with relative free motion.

nodes.name: Asymptotic completeness for N-body systems
nodes.description: The Hilbert space decomposes as H = H_pp ⊕ (⊕_α Ran Ω±_α) where the sum runs over all cluster decompositions α, proved by Sigal–Soffer and Derezinski for short-range potentials.

nodes.name: Dollard modified wave operators
nodes.description: Modified wave operators Ω±_D = s-lim_{t→±∞} e^{iHt} e^{−iH₀t} e^{−iΦ(t)} incorporating a long-range phase correction Φ(t) to handle Coulomb-type potentials where standard wave operators fail to exist.

nodes.name: HVZ theorem (Hunziker–van Winter–Zhislin)
nodes.description: The essential spectrum of an N-body Hamiltonian H equals [Σ, ∞) where Σ = min_α inf σ(H_α) is the minimum over all two-cluster thresholds, identifying the bottom of the continuum.

nodes.name: Zhislin's theorem
nodes.description: A neutral or negatively charged atom (N ≥ Z) has infinitely many bound states below the essential spectrum, proved using the HVZ theorem and variational methods.

nodes.name: Analytic family of type (A)
nodes.description: A family T(κ) of closed operators with common domain D independent of κ such that T(κ)φ is analytic in κ for each φ ∈ D, the Kato framework for non-degenerate perturbation theory.

nodes.name: Analytic family of type (B)
nodes.description: A family of operators defined via analytic quadratic forms t(κ)[φ] with form domain independent of κ, generalizing type (A) to handle perturbations defined only in the form sense.

nodes.name: Asymptotic perturbation theory
nodes.function_signature: (Formal Rayleigh–Schrödinger series) → (Asymptotic expansion of eigenvalues)
nodes.description: Analysis of divergent perturbation series that are nonetheless asymptotic to the true eigenvalues, with error bounds of order (n!)κⁿ requiring summability methods for recovery.

nodes.name: Semiclassical approximation
nodes.function_signature: (Quantum Hamiltonian, ℏ → 0) → (Classical limit, WKB expansion)
nodes.description: Systematic expansion of quantum quantities in powers of ℏ recovering classical mechanics at leading order, including WKB approximation for eigenfunctions and Weyl asymptotics for eigenvalue counting.

nodes.name: Perturbation determinant
nodes.description: The regularized determinant det_p(I + A(z)) for trace-class-type perturbations, whose zeros locate the eigenvalues of H₀ + V and whose logarithmic derivative gives the trace of the resolvent difference.

nodes.name: Resonance (Schrödinger operator)
nodes.description: A pole of the meromorphic continuation of the resolvent (H − z)⁻¹ across the continuous spectrum into the unphysical sheet, with imaginary part determining the metastable state's lifetime.

nodes.name: Absence of singular continuous spectrum
nodes.description: The singular continuous part σ_sc(H) = ∅ for Schrödinger operators under suitable conditions, typically proved via the Mourre estimate or Kato smoothness theory.

nodes.name: Virial theorem
nodes.description: For a Schrödinger operator H = −Δ + V with Hψ = Eψ, the identity 2⟨ψ, Tψ⟩ = ⟨ψ, x·∇V ψ⟩ holds, constraining eigenvalues and ruling out positive eigenvalues for repulsive potentials.

nodes.name: Temple's inequality
nodes.description: A lower bound for the lowest eigenvalue: if ψ is a trial vector and η₁ = inf σ_ess(H), then E₁ ≥ ⟨ψ,Hψ⟩ − (⟨ψ,H²ψ⟩ − ⟨ψ,Hψ⟩²)/(η₁ − ⟨ψ,Hψ⟩), improving on the Rayleigh–Ritz upper bound.

nodes.name: Kato–Birman invariance principle
nodes.description: If ψ(λ) is a monotone function and the wave operators Ω±(H, H₀) exist and are complete, then Ω±(ψ(H), ψ(H₀)) also exist and are complete, allowing passage between different operator representations.

nodes.name: IMS localization formula
nodes.function_signature: (Partition of unity {Jₐ}) → (H = Σₐ Jₐ H Jₐ − Σₐ |∇Jₐ|²)
nodes.description: The identity H = Σₐ Jₐ H Jₐ − Σₐ |∇Jₐ|² for a smooth partition of unity, decomposing the Hamiltonian into localized pieces for N-body analysis and proof of the HVZ theorem.

nodes.name: Rollnik class
nodes.description: The class of potentials V on ℝ³ satisfying ∫∫ |V(x)||V(y)|/|x−y|² dx dy < ∞, ensuring that the Birman–Schwinger kernel is Hilbert–Schmidt and enabling spectral analysis of −Δ+V.

nodes.name: Simon's theorem on absence of positive eigenvalues
nodes.description: For Schrödinger operators −Δ + V with V satisfying suitable decay conditions, there are no positive eigenvalues embedded in the continuous spectrum, extending the classical Kato result.

nodes.name: Decoupling inequalities
nodes.function_signature: (N-body Hamiltonian, cluster decomposition) → (Lower bounds on inter-cluster interaction)
nodes.description: Inequalities bounding the interaction energy between particle clusters from below, used in proving stability of matter and analyzing N-body quantum systems.

nodes.name: Hahn-Banach First Geometric Form
nodes.description: If A and B are disjoint nonempty convex subsets of a normed space with A open, then there exists a closed hyperplane separating A and B.

nodes.name: Hahn-Banach Second Geometric Form
nodes.description: If A and B are disjoint nonempty convex subsets of a normed space with A closed and B compact, then there exists a closed hyperplane strictly separating A and B.

nodes.name: Conjugate Convex Function (Legendre-Fenchel Transform)
nodes.description: For a function f: E -> (-inf, +inf], the conjugate f*(x*) = sup_{x in E} (<x*, x> - f(x)) is a convex lower semicontinuous function on E*.

nodes.name: Fenchel-Moreau Theorem
nodes.description: A proper lower semicontinuous convex function on a locally convex space equals its biconjugate, f** = f.

nodes.name: Young-Fenchel Inequality
nodes.description: For any function f and its conjugate f*, the inequality f(x) + f*(x*) >= <x*, x> holds for all x in E and x* in E*.

nodes.name: Subdifferential
nodes.description: The subdifferential of a convex function f at x is the set of all x* in E* satisfying f(y) >= f(x) + <x*, y - x> for all y, generalizing the derivative to nonsmooth convex functions.

nodes.name: Complemented Subspace
nodes.description: A closed subspace M of a Banach space X is complemented if there exists a closed subspace N such that X = M + N and M ∩ N = {0}, equivalently if there exists a bounded linear projection onto M.

nodes.name: Weak* Topology σ(E*, E)
nodes.description: The coarsest topology on the dual E* making all evaluation maps x* -> <x*, x> continuous for each x in E, always coarser than the weak topology on E*.

nodes.name: Finite-Rank Operator
nodes.description: A bounded linear operator whose range is finite-dimensional; finite-rank operators are compact and their norm closure equals the space of compact operators when the target has a Schauder basis.

nodes.name: Courant-Fischer Min-Max Principle
nodes.description: The k-th eigenvalue of a compact self-adjoint operator equals the min over k-dimensional subspaces of the max of the Rayleigh quotient, providing a variational characterization of all eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Maximal Monotone Operator
nodes.description: A multivalued operator A: D(A) subset H -> 2^H is maximal monotone if <Au - Av, u - v> >= 0 for all u, v in D(A) and the graph of A is not properly contained in any other monotone operator's graph.

nodes.name: Yosida Approximation
nodes.description: For a maximal monotone operator A, the Yosida approximation A_lambda = (1/lambda)(I - J_lambda) is a bounded Lipschitz monotone operator converging to the minimal section element of A as lambda -> 0.

nodes.name: Resolvent of a Monotone Operator
nodes.description: For a maximal monotone operator A and lambda > 0, the resolvent J_lambda = (I + lambda A)^{-1} is a contraction defined on all of H, mapping each point to the unique solution of the inclusion.

nodes.name: m-Dissipative Operator
nodes.description: An operator A on a Banach space is m-dissipative if it is dissipative and R(I - lambda A) = X for some (equivalently all) lambda > 0, ensuring generation of a contraction semigroup by Lumer-Phillips.

nodes.name: Strongly Continuous (C₀) Semigroup
nodes.description: A family {S(t)}_{t >= 0} of bounded linear operators on a Banach space satisfying S(0) = I, S(t+s) = S(t)S(s), and strong continuity lim_{t -> 0+} S(t)u = u for all u.

nodes.name: Infinitesimal Generator of a Semigroup
nodes.description: The unbounded operator A defined by Au = lim_{t -> 0+} (S(t)u - u)/t on the domain of all u where this limit exists, characterizing the semigroup through the abstract Cauchy problem du/dt = Au.

nodes.name: Exponential Formula for Semigroups
nodes.description: For a C₀ contraction semigroup with generator A, the semigroup is recovered by S(t)u = lim_{n -> inf} (I - (t/n)A)^{-n} u for all u and t >= 0.

nodes.name: Crandall-Liggett Theorem
nodes.description: For an m-accretive operator A on a Banach space, the limit S(t)u = lim_{n -> inf} (I + (t/n)A)^{-n} u defines a nonlinear contraction semigroup on the closure of D(A).

nodes.name: Characterization of W^{1,p} in One Dimension
nodes.description: A function u belongs to W^{1,p}(I) for an interval I if and only if u has a representative that is absolutely continuous and whose classical derivative belongs to L^p(I).

nodes.name: Compact Embedding W^{1,p} into C in One Dimension
nodes.description: The injection W^{1,p}(I) into C(I-bar) is compact for any bounded interval I and 1 <= p <= inf, a one-dimensional precursor to Rellich-Kondrachov.

nodes.name: Eigenvalues of -d²/dx² on (0,L)
nodes.description: The eigenvalues of -u'' = lambda u on (0,L) with Dirichlet boundary conditions are lambda_n = (n pi / L)^2 for n >= 1, with eigenfunctions sin(n pi x / L).

nodes.name: Sobolev Extension Operator
nodes.description: For a bounded domain Omega with Lipschitz boundary, there exists a bounded linear operator P: W^{1,p}(Omega) -> W^{1,p}(R^N) such that Pu|_Omega = u for 1 <= p <= inf.

nodes.name: Morrey's Inequality
nodes.description: If p > N, then W^{1,p}(R^N) embeds continuously into C^{0,alpha}(R^N) with alpha = 1 - N/p, so Sobolev functions with high integrability are Holder continuous.

nodes.name: Poincaré-Wirtinger Inequality
nodes.description: For u in W^{1,p}(Omega) on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain, ||u - u_avg||_{Lp} <= C ||grad u||_{Lp}, where u_avg is the mean value of u over Omega.

nodes.name: Green's Formula in Sobolev Spaces
nodes.description: For u in H^2(Omega) and v in H^1(Omega), the identity integral(-Delta u)v dx = integral grad u . grad v dx - integral_{dOmega} (du/dn)v dsigma holds, extending integration by parts to Sobolev functions.

nodes.name: Negative Sobolev Space H^{-1}(Ω)
nodes.description: The dual space of H^1_0(Omega), consisting of distributions that can be written as f_0 + sum d f_i / d x_i with each f_i in L^2(Omega).

nodes.name: Sobolev Space W₀^{1,p}(Ω)
nodes.description: The closure of C_c^inf(Omega) in W^{1,p}(Omega), consisting of W^{1,p} functions with zero trace on the boundary, generalizing H^1_0 = W_0^{1,2}.

nodes.name: Trace Space W^{1-1/p,p}(∂Ω)
nodes.description: The fractional Sobolev space on the boundary that is the image of the trace operator gamma_0: W^{1,p}(Omega) -> W^{1-1/p,p}(partial Omega), characterizing boundary values of Sobolev functions.

nodes.name: Eigenvalues of -Δ on H¹₀(Ω)
nodes.description: For a bounded open set Omega, -Delta with Dirichlet conditions has eigenvalues 0 < lambda_1 < lambda_2 <= ... -> inf with an orthonormal basis of L^2(Omega) consisting of eigenfunctions in H^1_0.

nodes.name: Variational Characterization of First Eigenvalue
nodes.description: The first eigenvalue lambda_1 of -Delta on H^1_0(Omega) equals inf{integral |grad u|^2 / integral |u|^2 : u in H^1_0, u != 0}, achieved by a positive eigenfunction.

nodes.name: Domain Monotonicity of Dirichlet Eigenvalues
nodes.description: If Omega_1 subset Omega_2 are bounded open sets, then lambda_k(Omega_1) >= lambda_k(Omega_2) for each k, so enlarging the domain decreases eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Faber-Krahn Inequality
nodes.description: Among all bounded domains of fixed volume, the ball minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue: lambda_1(Omega) >= lambda_1(Omega*) where Omega* is the ball with |Omega*| = |Omega|.

nodes.name: Space of Functions of Bounded Variation BV(Ω)
nodes.description: The space of L^1 functions whose distributional gradient is a finite Radon measure, strictly containing W^{1,1} and fundamental for free boundary and image processing problems.

nodes.name: Polarization Identity
nodes.description: In a real inner product space, <x,y> = (1/4)(||x+y||^2 - ||x-y||^2), recovering the inner product from the norm; in the complex case, an analogous formula with four terms is used.

nodes.name: Orthogonal Decomposition Theorem (Hilbert Space)
nodes.description: If M is a closed subspace of a Hilbert space H, then H = M + M^perp as an orthogonal direct sum, so every element decomposes uniquely into its projection onto M and a component in M^perp.

nodes.name: Duality of Lp Spaces
nodes.description: For 1 <= p < inf with conjugate exponent q, the dual (L^p)* is isometrically isomorphic to L^q via the pairing integral fg; for p = 1, (L^1)* = L^inf.

nodes.name: Reflexivity of Lp for 1 < p < ∞
nodes.description: For 1 < p < inf, the space L^p is reflexive, meaning the canonical embedding J: L^p -> (L^p)** is surjective.

nodes.name: Density of C_c^∞ in Lp
nodes.description: For 1 <= p < inf, the space C_c^inf(R^N) is dense in L^p(R^N), enabling approximation of any Lp function by smooth compactly supported functions.

nodes.name: Continuity of Translation in Lp
nodes.description: For 1 <= p < inf and f in L^p(R^N), the map h -> tau_h f is continuous from R^N to L^p, that is ||tau_h f - f||_p -> 0 as h -> 0.

nodes.name: Interpolation Inequality for Lp Norms
nodes.description: If f in L^p ∩ L^q with 1 <= p <= r <= q <= inf, then f in L^r and ||f||_r <= ||f||_p^a ||f||_q^{1-a} where 1/r = a/p + (1-a)/q.

nodes.name: Obstacle Problem (Variational Inequality Formulation)
nodes.description: Find u in K = {v in H^1_0 : v >= psi a.e.} minimizing integral |grad v|^2 - 2 integral fv, equivalently satisfying a(u, v-u) >= (f, v-u) for all v in K, a prototypical free boundary problem.

nodes.name: Gagliardo-Nirenberg Interpolation Inequality (General)
nodes.description: ||D^j u||_{Lr} <= C ||D^m u||_{Lp}^a ||u||_{Lq}^{1-a} for suitable exponents satisfying 1/r = j/N + a(1/p - m/N) + (1-a)/q, interpolating between different orders of Sobolev norms.

nodes.name: Nečas Inequality
nodes.description: A distribution f on a bounded Lipschitz domain belongs to L^p if and only if f and all its first-order distributional derivatives lie in W^{-1,p}, with equivalent norms.

nodes.name: Minkowski Gauge Technique
nodes.function_signature: (Open convex set containing origin in normed space) → (Sublinear functional inducing the set as sublevel set, bridging geometric and analytic Hahn-Banach)
nodes.description: Constructs a sublinear functional p_C(x) = inf{alpha > 0 : x/alpha in C} from a convex set C, used to prove geometric forms of the Hahn-Banach theorem from the analytic form.

nodes.name: Difference Quotient Technique for Regularity
nodes.function_signature: (Weak solution u in H^1 of elliptic PDE) → (Higher regularity u in H^2_loc via uniform bounds on discrete derivatives)
nodes.description: Approximates partial derivatives by difference quotients D_h u = (u(x+he)-u(x))/h, derives uniform H^1 bounds, then passes to the limit to gain one order of Sobolev regularity.

nodes.name: Symmetric Decreasing Rearrangement Technique
nodes.function_signature: (Nonneg measurable function) → (Radially symmetric decreasing equimeasurable function preserving Lp norms while decreasing gradient norms)
nodes.description: Replaces a function by its equimeasurable radially symmetric decreasing rearrangement, used together with Polya-Szego inequality to prove symmetry of extremals and sharp functional inequalities.

nodes.name: Weak Convergence Methods in Sobolev Spaces
nodes.function_signature: (Minimizing sequence for energy functional in reflexive Sobolev space) → (Existence of minimizer via weak compactness + compact embedding + lower semicontinuity)
nodes.description: Combines weak sequential compactness in reflexive spaces, compact Sobolev embeddings, and weak lower semicontinuity of convex integrals to prove existence of minimizers in variational problems.

nodes.name: Hardy–Littlewood maximal theorem
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ L^p(ℝⁿ) → Weak (1,1) and strong (p,p) bounds
nodes.description: The Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator M is of weak type (1,1) with bound |{Mf > λ}| ≤ C_n‖f‖₁/λ, and bounded on L^p for 1 < p ≤ ∞.

nodes.name: Dyadic cubes in ℝⁿ
nodes.description: The collection 𝒟 = {2^{−k}([0,1)ⁿ + m) : k ∈ ℤ, m ∈ ℤⁿ} of half-open cubes forming a nested filtration of ℝⁿ with each cube split into 2ⁿ children.

nodes.name: Weak-type (p,p) estimate
nodes.description: A sublinear operator T is of weak type (p,p) if |{|Tf| > λ}| ≤ (C‖f‖_p / λ)^p for all f ∈ L^p and λ > 0.

nodes.name: Maximal function characterization of L^p
nodes.description: A function f belongs to L^p(ℝⁿ) for 1 < p ≤ ∞ if and only if its Hardy–Littlewood maximal function Mf belongs to L^p, with equivalent norms.

nodes.name: Hilbert transform
nodes.description: The singular integral operator Hf(x) = (1/π) p.v. ∫ f(y)/(x − y) dy, equivalently the Fourier multiplier with symbol −i sgn(ξ).

nodes.name: Truncated singular integral
nodes.type_signature: (CZ kernel K, ε > 0, f ∈ L^p) → Function
nodes.description: The ε-truncated singular integral T_ε f(x) = ∫_{|x−y|>ε} K(x−y)f(y) dy, a well-defined absolutely convergent integral for f ∈ L^p.

nodes.name: Pointwise convergence of truncated singular integrals
nodes.description: For f ∈ L^p(ℝⁿ) with 1 ≤ p < ∞ and T a Calderón–Zygmund operator, the truncated integrals T_ε f(x) converge to Tf(x) as ε → 0 for almost every x.

nodes.name: Maximal singular integral operator
nodes.description: The operator T*f(x) = sup_{ε>0} |T_ε f(x)| controlling the pointwise convergence of truncated Calderón–Zygmund singular integrals.

nodes.name: Cotlar's inequality
nodes.description: For a Calderón–Zygmund operator T, the maximal singular integral satisfies T*f(x) ≤ C(M(Tf)(x) + Mf(x)) pointwise, reducing L^p bounds for T* to those for T.

nodes.name: Calderón–Zygmund rotation method
nodes.function_signature: (Odd CZ kernel on ℝⁿ) → (Reduction to Hilbert transform on ℝ)
nodes.description: Reduces L^p bounds for singular integrals with odd homogeneous kernels on ℝⁿ to one-dimensional Hilbert transform bounds by averaging over rotations on S^{n−1}.

nodes.name: Hörmander kernel condition
nodes.description: The integral condition sup_{y≠0} ∫_{|x|>2|y|} |K(x−y) − K(x)| dx ≤ C, sufficient together with L² boundedness to imply L^p boundedness of the associated operator.

nodes.name: Fourier multiplier representation of singular integrals
nodes.type_signature: T CZ operator on ℝⁿ → Bounded multiplier
nodes.description: Every translation-invariant Calderón–Zygmund singular integral operator T with kernel K has Fourier multiplier representation (Tf)^∧ = m f̂ where m(ξ) = K̂(ξ) is bounded and homogeneous of degree 0.

nodes.name: L^p boundedness of Riesz transforms
nodes.description: Each Riesz transform R_j is bounded on L^p(ℝⁿ) for 1 < p < ∞ and of weak type (1,1), with ‖R_j f‖_p ≤ C_p‖f‖_p.

nodes.name: Riesz transforms and the Laplacian
nodes.description: The Riesz transforms satisfy R_j = ∂_j(−Δ)^{−1/2} and Σ_j R_j² = −I, providing a singular-integral factorization of the Laplacian: ∂_i∂_j(−Δ)^{−1} = −R_iR_j.

nodes.name: Conjugate Poisson integral
nodes.description: The vector-valued function Q_y ∗ f(x) where Q_y is the conjugate Poisson kernel, forming the system of conjugate harmonic functions in the upper half-space.

nodes.name: Spherical harmonic decomposition of L²(S^{n−1})
nodes.description: L²(S^{n−1}) = ⊕_{k=0}^∞ H_k where H_k is the finite-dimensional space of spherical harmonics of degree k, mutually orthogonal eigenspaces of the Laplace–Beltrami operator.

nodes.name: Hecke's identity for spherical harmonics
nodes.description: The Fourier transform of a function of the form P_k(x)f(|x|), where P_k is a solid harmonic of degree k, factors as i^{−k}P_k(ξ)g(|ξ|) for an explicit radial function g involving Bessel functions.

nodes.name: Boundary behavior of Poisson integrals in ℝ^{n+1}_+
nodes.description: The Poisson integral u(x,y) = P_y ∗ f(x) in the upper half-space ℝ^{n+1}_+ converges nontangentially to f(x) at almost every x ∈ ℝⁿ for f ∈ L^p.

nodes.name: Multiplier formula via spherical harmonics
nodes.type_signature: m homogeneous of degree 0 on ℝⁿ → Spherical harmonic expansion
nodes.description: A homogeneous-of-degree-0 Fourier multiplier of a Calderón–Zygmund operator can be expanded in spherical harmonics, and L^p boundedness is determined by the decay of the coefficients.

nodes.name: Littlewood–Paley g-function
nodes.description: The square function g(f)(x) = (∫₀^∞ |∇u(x,t)|² t dt)^{1/2} where u = P_t ∗ f is the Poisson integral, measuring oscillation of f via its harmonic extension.

nodes.name: Littlewood–Paley g*_λ function
nodes.description: The nontangential variant g*_λ(f)(x) = (∫∫_{ℝ^{n+1}_+} (t/(t+|x−y|))^{nλ} |∇u(y,t)|² t^{1−n} dy dt)^{1/2}, controlling the area integral with parameter λ.

nodes.name: Lusin area integral (S-function)
nodes.description: The area integral S(f)(x) = (∫∫_{Γ(x)} |∇u(y,t)|² t^{1−n} dy dt)^{1/2} over the cone Γ(x) = {(y,t) : |x−y| < t}, measuring nontangential variation of the Poisson extension.

nodes.name: S-function L^p norm equivalence
nodes.description: For 1 < p < ∞, the Lusin area integral satisfies ‖S(f)‖_p ≈ ‖f‖_p, providing an equivalent characterization of L^p norms via the area function.

nodes.name: Marcinkiewicz multiplier theorem
nodes.type_signature: m : ℝⁿ → ℂ satisfying Marcinkiewicz condition → L^p bound
nodes.description: A bounded function m on ℝⁿ satisfying coordinate-wise bounded variation conditions in each variable separately defines an L^p-bounded Fourier multiplier for 1 < p < ∞.

nodes.name: Partial sums operator for Fourier integrals
nodes.description: The operator S_R f = (χ_{B(0,R)} f̂)^∨ projecting f onto frequencies in the ball of radius R, whose L^p boundedness in dimension n ≥ 2 fails for p ≠ 2.

nodes.name: L^p boundedness of Fourier partial sums in one dimension
nodes.description: In one dimension the partial sums operator S_R is bounded on L^p(ℝ) for 1 < p < ∞, reducible to compositions of the Hilbert transform.

nodes.name: Bessel potential space L^p_α
nodes.description: The space L^p_α(ℝⁿ) = {f ∈ 𝒮′ : (1+|ξ|²)^{α/2} f̂ ∈ L^p} = J_{−α}(L^p), where J_α = (I − Δ)^{−α/2} is the Bessel potential operator.

nodes.name: Equivalence of Sobolev and Bessel potential spaces
nodes.description: For integer k ≥ 0 and 1 < p < ∞, W^{k,p}(ℝⁿ) = L^p_k(ℝⁿ) with equivalent norms, identifying classical Sobolev spaces with Bessel potential spaces.

nodes.name: Lipschitz space Λ_α
nodes.description: The space Λ_α(ℝⁿ) defined for 0 < α < 1 by the Hölder condition |f(x+h) − f(x)| ≤ C|h|^α, and for general α > 0 by iterated differences of order k > α.

nodes.name: Zygmund class Λ_*
nodes.description: The space Λ_*(ℝⁿ) of continuous functions satisfying |f(x+h) + f(x−h) − 2f(x)| ≤ C|h|, strictly larger than Lip₁ and the correct substitute for Lipschitz order 1 in the Littlewood–Paley scale.

nodes.name: Characterization of Λ_α via Poisson integral
nodes.description: A tempered distribution f belongs to Λ_α if and only if its Poisson integral u(x,t) satisfies |∂_t^k u(x,t)| ≤ Ct^{α−k} for all integers k > α.

nodes.name: Characterization of L^p_α via Littlewood–Paley theory
nodes.description: A tempered distribution f belongs to L^p_α(ℝⁿ) if and only if (Σ_j 2^{2jα}|Δ_j f|²)^{1/2} is in L^p, where Δ_j is the j-th Littlewood–Paley projection.

nodes.name: Homogeneous Sobolev space Ẇ^{s,p}
nodes.description: The homogeneous Sobolev space Ẇ^{s,p}(ℝⁿ) defined by the seminorm ‖(−Δ)^{s/2}f‖_{L^p}, lacking lower-order terms present in the inhomogeneous space W^{s,p}.

nodes.name: Riesz potential characterization of Sobolev spaces
nodes.description: For 1 < p < n/k, the homogeneous Sobolev space Ẇ^{k,p}(ℝⁿ) consists precisely of functions representable as I_k(g) for g ∈ L^p, where I_k is the Riesz potential of order k.

nodes.name: Difference characterization of Bessel potential spaces
nodes.description: For α > 0 and 1 < p < ∞, f ∈ L^p_α(ℝⁿ) iff f ∈ L^p and ∫(|Δ_h^M f(x)|^p / |h|^{n+αp}) dh ∈ L¹ for M > α, characterizing Bessel potential spaces via integrated differences.

nodes.name: Extension theorem for Sobolev spaces on Lipschitz domains
nodes.type_signature: (Ω Lipschitz, k ∈ ℕ, 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞) → Bounded extension
nodes.description: There exists a bounded linear extension operator E : W^{k,p}(Ω) → W^{k,p}(ℝⁿ) with Ef|_Ω = f, valid simultaneously for all k and p when Ω has Lipschitz boundary.

nodes.name: Stein's total extension operator
nodes.type_signature: (Half-space or Lipschitz domain) → Bounded extension operator
nodes.description: A single linear operator extending functions from a half-space to all of ℝⁿ that is bounded on every W^{k,p} simultaneously, constructed via regularized reflection.

nodes.name: Restriction theorem for Riesz potentials
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ L^p_α(ℝⁿ), α > 0 → Trace on submanifold
nodes.description: Riesz potentials I_α f of L^p functions restrict to lower-dimensional submanifolds with bounds determined by the codimension and the relation of α, p, and n.

nodes.name: Reflection method for Sobolev extension
nodes.function_signature: (f on half-space ℝⁿ_+) → (Extension to ℝⁿ via reflected averages)
nodes.description: Extends a Sobolev function from the half-space to all of ℝⁿ by defining the extension for x_n < 0 as a linear combination of f evaluated at reflected points, preserving differentiability.

nodes.name: Nontangential maximal function
nodes.type_signature: u : ℝ^{n+1}_+ → ℂ → Measurable function on ℝⁿ
nodes.description: The function N(u)(x) = sup_{(y,t)∈Γ(x)} |u(y,t)| where Γ(x) = {(y,t) : |x−y| < t} is the cone at x, controlling the size of a function in the upper half-space.

nodes.name: Nontangential convergence
nodes.type_signature: u : ℝ^{n+1}_+ → ℂ, x₀ ∈ ℝⁿ → Limit
nodes.description: A function u(y,t) in the upper half-space converges nontangentially to L at x₀ if u(y,t) → L as (y,t) → (x₀,0) within every cone Γ_α(x₀) = {(y,t) : |y−x₀| < αt}.

nodes.name: Fatou's theorem for the upper half-space
nodes.type_signature: u harmonic in ℝ^{n+1}_+ with sup_t ‖u(·,t)‖_p < ∞ → a.e. nontangential limits
nodes.description: A harmonic function u in ℝ^{n+1}_+ with bounded L^p means for some 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ has nontangential boundary limits at almost every point of ℝⁿ.

nodes.name: Area integral characterization of harmonic functions
nodes.type_signature: u harmonic in ℝ^{n+1}_+ → S(u) ∈ L^p iff N(u) ∈ L^p
nodes.description: For a harmonic function u in the upper half-space, the L^p norm of the area integral S(u) is comparable to the L^p norm of the nontangential maximal function N(u) for 0 < p < ∞.

nodes.name: H^p–L^p equivalence for p > 1
nodes.description: For 1 < p < ∞ the real Hardy space H^p(ℝⁿ) coincides with L^p(ℝⁿ) with equivalent norms; the two spaces differ only when p ≤ 1.

nodes.name: Singular integrals map L^∞ to BMO
nodes.type_signature: T CZ operator, f ∈ L^∞(ℝⁿ) → Tf ∈ BMO
nodes.description: A Calderón–Zygmund singular integral operator T maps L^∞(ℝⁿ) boundedly into BMO(ℝⁿ) with ‖Tf‖_{BMO} ≤ C‖f‖_∞, the endpoint substitute for the failing L^∞ → L^∞ bound.

nodes.name: Area integral characterization of H^p
nodes.description: A tempered distribution f belongs to H^p(ℝⁿ) iff the area integral S(u) of its Poisson extension u = P ∗ f belongs to L^p, with ‖S(u)‖_p ≈ ‖f‖_{H^p}.

nodes.name: Nontangential maximal function characterization of H^p
nodes.description: A tempered distribution f belongs to H^p(ℝⁿ) iff the nontangential maximal function N(P∗f) belongs to L^p, and ‖f‖_{H^p} ≈ ‖N(P∗f)‖_p.

nodes.name: Conjugate function characterization of H^p
nodes.description: For n/(n+1) < p ≤ 1, f ∈ H^p(ℝⁿ) iff f and all its Riesz transforms R_jf belong to L^p, with ‖f‖_{H^p} ≈ ‖f‖_p + Σ_j‖R_jf‖_p.

nodes.name: Fefferman–Stein sharp function
nodes.description: The sharp maximal function f^#(x) = sup_Q (1/|Q|)∫_Q |f(y) − f_Q| dy, measuring local oscillation of f and controlling the BMO seminorm.

nodes.name: Fefferman–Stein inequality for the sharp function
nodes.description: For 1 < p < ∞, ‖f‖_p ≤ C_p‖f^#‖_p, so that L^p norms are controlled by the sharp maximal function, bridging pointwise oscillation and global integrability.

nodes.name: L^p differentiability
nodes.description: A function f is L^p-differentiable at x if there exists a linear map L such that (r^{−n}∫_{B(x,r)} |f(y) − f(x) − L(y−x)|^p dy)^{1/p} = o(r) as r → 0.

nodes.name: Calderón's theorem on L^p differentiability
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ), 1 < p ≤ ∞ → a.e. L^p differentiability
nodes.description: Every function in the Sobolev space W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ) for 1 < p ≤ ∞ is L^p-differentiable at almost every point.

nodes.name: Calderón–Zygmund theorem on a.e. differentiability
nodes.description: If f ∈ W^{k,p}(ℝⁿ) with kp > n, then f is classically differentiable of order k−1 a.e.; for kp ≤ n, f is L^p-differentiable of order k at almost every point.

nodes.name: Maximal operator for Sobolev functions
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ), 1 < p ≤ n → Sobolev-type bound
nodes.description: The Hardy–Littlewood maximal function Mf of f ∈ W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ), 1 < p ≤ n, belongs to W^{1,p} with ‖∇Mf‖_p ≤ C‖∇f‖_p.

nodes.name: Lebesgue point theorem for Sobolev functions
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ), 1 ≤ p ≤ n → a.e. Lebesgue points
nodes.description: Every f ∈ W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ) has Lebesgue points at all x outside a set of p-capacity zero, a finer statement than the measure-zero exceptional set of classical Lebesgue differentiation.

nodes.name: p-capacity
nodes.description: Cap_p(E) = inf{‖u‖_{W^{1,p}}^p : u ≥ 1 on E, u ∈ W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ)}, measuring the size of E from the viewpoint of Sobolev functions; the correct notion of exceptional sets for Sobolev-space theory.

nodes.name: Real interpolation method (K-functional)
nodes.function_signature: (Compatible couple (A₀,A₁), θ ∈ (0,1), q ∈ [1,∞]) → Interpolation space (A₀,A₁)_{θ,q}
nodes.description: Constructs the interpolation space (A₀,A₁)_{θ,q} using the Peetre K-functional K(t,a) = inf_{a=a₀+a₁}(‖a₀‖_{A₀} + t‖a₁‖_{A₁}) with norm (∫(t^{−θ}K(t,a))^q dt/t)^{1/q}.

nodes.name: Complex interpolation method
nodes.function_signature: (Compatible couple (A₀,A₁), θ ∈ (0,1)) → Interpolation space [A₀,A₁]_θ
nodes.description: Constructs [A₀,A₁]_θ as the values f(θ) where f is bounded analytic on the strip {0 < Re z < 1} with continuous boundary values in A₀ and A₁.

nodes.name: Good-λ inequality technique
nodes.function_signature: (Operators S, T) → (L^p comparison of S and T)
nodes.description: Proves ‖Sf‖_p ≤ C‖Tf‖_p by showing |{Sf > 2λ, Tf ≤ γλ}| ≤ c(γ)|{Sf > λ}| for small γ, then integrating over λ to transfer L^p bounds.

nodes.name: L² boundedness of CZ operators via Fourier transform
nodes.function_signature: (CZ operator T with kernel K) → (L² bound via Plancherel)
nodes.description: Establishes L² boundedness of a CZ operator by showing its Fourier multiplier m = K̂ is bounded, using homogeneity and smoothness of K; combined with CZ theorem gives all L^p bounds.

nodes.name: Duality argument for weak-type estimates
nodes.function_signature: (Sublinear operator T, dual pairing) → (Weak-type bound)
nodes.description: Proves weak-type (1,1) bounds by dualizing and using the adjoint T* together with the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition to handle the singular part.

nodes.name: Subordination formula for Poisson semigroup
nodes.function_signature: (Heat semigroup e^{tΔ}) → (Poisson semigroup e^{−t√{−Δ}})
nodes.description: Recovers the Poisson semigroup from the heat semigroup via e^{−t√{−Δ}}f = (t/(2√π))∫₀^∞ s^{−3/2}e^{−t²/(4s)}e^{sΔ}f ds, transferring heat kernel estimates to Poisson kernel estimates.

nodes.name: Multiplier problem for the ball
nodes.type_signature: n ≥ 2, p ≠ 2 → Failure of L^p boundedness
nodes.description: The characteristic function χ_{B(0,1)} is not an L^p Fourier multiplier for p ≠ 2 when n ≥ 2 (Fefferman's theorem), in contrast to the one-dimensional case.

nodes.name: Bochner–Riesz conjecture
nodes.description: The conjecture that Bochner–Riesz means S^δ_R are bounded on L^p(ℝⁿ) iff δ > max(n|1/p − 1/2| − 1/2, 0); proved for n = 2, open in higher dimensions.

nodes.name: Calderón–Zygmund lemma (dyadic version)
nodes.description: For f ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) and λ > 0, there exist disjoint dyadic cubes {Q_j} with averages exceeding λ and summing to at most ‖f‖₁/λ, yielding the canonical good/bad decomposition.

nodes.name: Fractional Laplacian (−Δ)^s
nodes.description: The operator (−Δ)^s defined via ((−Δ)^s f)^∧(ξ) = |ξ|^{2s}f̂(ξ), equivalently c_{n,s} p.v. ∫(f(x) − f(y))/|x−y|^{n+2s} dy, interpolating between identity and Laplacian.

nodes.name: Singular integral operator restricted to a domain
nodes.type_signature: (T CZ operator, Ω domain in ℝⁿ) → Operator on L^p(Ω)
nodes.description: The operator T_Ω f(x) = ∫_Ω K(x,y)f(y) dy for f supported in Ω, whose L^p boundedness follows from that of T on ℝⁿ by extension and restriction.

nodes.name: L^p elliptic regularity via singular integrals
nodes.type_signature: (Lu = f, L elliptic of order 2k, f ∈ L^p) → u ∈ W^{2k,p}
nodes.description: For a uniformly elliptic operator L of order 2k with 1 < p < ∞, Lu = f with f ∈ L^p implies u ∈ W^{2k,p}_{loc}, proved via representation through Calderón–Zygmund singular integrals.

nodes.name: Newtonian potential
nodes.description: The convolution Nf(x) = c_n ∫ f(y)/|x−y|^{n−2} dy solving −Δ(Nf) = f, whose second derivatives are Calderón–Zygmund singular integrals yielding W^{2,p} regularity.

nodes.name: Calderón commutator theorem
nodes.type_signature: (A Lipschitz, H Hilbert transform) → L² bound
nodes.description: The first Calderón commutator C₁f(x) = p.v. ∫(A(x)−A(y))/(x−y)² f(y) dy is bounded on L² when A is Lipschitz, with ‖C₁‖ ≤ C‖A′‖_∞.

nodes.name: Homogeneous distribution
nodes.description: A tempered distribution u satisfying u(tx) = t^λ u(x) in the distributional sense for all t > 0; Calderón–Zygmund kernels are homogeneous distributions of degree −n with cancellation.

nodes.name: Laplace–Beltrami operator on S^{n−1}
nodes.description: The intrinsic Laplacian Δ_{S^{n−1}} on the unit sphere, with eigenvalues −k(k+n−2) for k = 0,1,2,… and eigenspaces the spaces of spherical harmonics of degree k.

nodes.name: Stein's maximal principle
nodes.description: If {T_t} converges to the identity a.e. on a dense subclass of L^p and the maximal operator T*f = sup_t|T_tf| is of weak type, then T_tf → f a.e. for all f ∈ L^p.

nodes.name: Semigroup characterization of Bessel potentials
nodes.description: The Bessel potential J_α f = (I−Δ)^{−α/2}f equals (1/Γ(α/2))∫₀^∞ e^{−t}e^{tΔ}f t^{α/2−1} dt, expressing Bessel potentials via the heat semigroup.

nodes.name: Heat kernel on ℝⁿ
nodes.description: The Gaussian kernel W_t(x) = (4πt)^{−n/2}exp(−|x|²/(4t)), the fundamental solution of the heat equation ∂_tu = Δu, whose convolution W_t∗f defines the heat semigroup.

nodes.name: Dual characterization of H¹
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) → H¹ membership via dual action
nodes.description: H¹(ℝⁿ) is the subspace of L¹ consisting of distributions f with sup{|⟨f,φ⟩| : φ ∈ BMO, ‖φ‖_{BMO} ≤ 1} finite, equivalently the predual of BMO.

nodes.name: Interpolation between H¹ and L^∞
nodes.description: The complex interpolation space [H¹, L^∞]_θ = L^p for 1/p = 1−θ, extending the classical L^p interpolation scale through the Hardy space endpoint.

nodes.name: Calderón's formula for Sobolev norms
nodes.description: The L^p_α norm of f equals ‖(∫₀^∞ |t^{−α}ψ_t∗f|² dt/t)^{1/2}‖_p for suitable ψ, connecting the Calderón reproducing formula to Sobolev-space norms.

nodes.name: Circle group 𝕋
nodes.description: The quotient group ℝ/ℤ (equivalently the unit circle {z ∈ ℂ : |z| = 1} under multiplication), the fundamental domain for Fourier series.

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients on 𝕋
nodes.description: The map f ↦ f̂(n) = ∫_𝕋 f(t)e^{−2πint} dt assigning to each integrable function on 𝕋 its sequence of Fourier coefficients.

nodes.name: Trigonometric polynomial
nodes.description: A finite linear combination p(t) = ∑_{|n|≤N} c_n e^{2πint} of exponentials, forming a dense subspace of C(𝕋) and all L^p(𝕋).

nodes.name: Convolution on 𝕋
nodes.description: The operation (f ∗ g)(x) = ∫_𝕋 f(x − t)g(t) dt turning L¹(𝕋) into a commutative Banach algebra with (f̂∗g)(n) = f̂(n)ĝ(n).

nodes.name: Approximate identity on 𝕋
nodes.description: A family {K_n} in L¹(𝕋) satisfying ∫K_n = 1, sup_n ‖K_n‖₁ < ∞, and ∫_{|t|>δ} |K_n(t)| dt → 0 for each δ > 0, so that K_n ∗ f → f in L^p and uniformly for continuous f.

nodes.name: Dirichlet kernel on 𝕋
nodes.description: D_N(t) = ∑_{n=−N}^{N} e^{2πint} = sin(π(2N+1)t)/sin(πt), the convolution kernel for the N-th partial sum of the Fourier series; ‖D_N‖₁ ~ (4/π²) log N.

nodes.name: Fejér kernel on 𝕋
nodes.description: F_N(t) = (1/N)∑_{k=0}^{N−1} D_k(t) = (1/N)(sin(Nπt)/sin(πt))², a non-negative approximate identity giving the Cesàro means of the Fourier series.

nodes.name: Fejér's theorem (uniform Cesàro convergence)
nodes.description: The Cesàro means σ_N(f) = F_N ∗ f converge uniformly to f for every continuous function f on 𝕋, and converge in L^p norm for every f ∈ L^p(𝕋) with 1 ≤ p < ∞.

nodes.name: Poisson kernel on 𝕋
nodes.description: P_r(t) = ∑_{n∈ℤ} r^{|n|} e^{2πint} = (1 − r²)/(1 − 2r cos 2πt + r²), the non-negative approximate identity for Abel summability of Fourier series.

nodes.name: Abel summability of Fourier series
nodes.description: For f ∈ L¹(𝕋), the Abel means P_r ∗ f(x) = ∑ f̂(n)r^{|n|}e^{2πinx} converge to f(x) at every Lebesgue point of f as r → 1⁻, and uniformly for continuous f.

nodes.name: Uniqueness theorem for Fourier series
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ L¹(𝕋) → Injectivity of Fourier map
nodes.description: If f̂(n) = 0 for all n ∈ ℤ then f = 0 a.e.; equivalently, the Fourier coefficient map L¹(𝕋) → c₀(ℤ) is injective.

nodes.name: Riemann–Lebesgue lemma on 𝕋
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ L¹(𝕋) → Decay of Fourier coefficients
nodes.description: For f ∈ L¹(𝕋), the Fourier coefficients satisfy f̂(n) → 0 as |n| → ∞, i.e., the Fourier transform maps L¹(𝕋) into c₀(ℤ).

nodes.name: Parseval's theorem on 𝕋
nodes.description: The Fourier coefficient map f ↦ (f̂(n))_{n∈ℤ} is a unitary isomorphism from L²(𝕋) onto ℓ²(ℤ), with ‖f‖₂² = ∑|f̂(n)|².

nodes.name: Bessel's inequality on 𝕋
nodes.description: For f ∈ L²(𝕋) and any orthonormal system, the sum of squared Fourier coefficients is bounded by ‖f‖₂², with equality (Parseval) for complete systems.

nodes.name: Weierstrass trigonometric approximation theorem
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ C(𝕋) → Density of trigonometric polynomials
nodes.description: The trigonometric polynomials are uniformly dense in C(𝕋); proved as a corollary of Fejér's theorem by showing σ_N(f) → f uniformly.

nodes.name: Formal multiplication of Fourier series
nodes.description: The Fourier series of f · g has coefficients (f̂ · ĝ)^∧(n) obtained via discrete convolution of Fourier coefficient sequences: ∑_k f̂(k)ĝ(n − k).

nodes.name: Partial sum operator on 𝕋
nodes.description: The N-th partial sum S_N(f)(x) = ∑_{|n|≤N} f̂(n)e^{2πinx} = (D_N ∗ f)(x), a bounded operator on L^p for 1 < p < ∞ but unbounded on L¹ and C(𝕋).

nodes.name: Dini's test for pointwise convergence
nodes.type_signature: (f ∈ L¹(𝕋), x₀ ∈ 𝕋, integrability condition) → Pointwise convergence
nodes.description: If ∫₀^δ |f(x₀ + t) + f(x₀ − t) − 2s|/t dt < ∞ for some s and δ > 0, then S_N(f)(x₀) → s as N → ∞.

nodes.name: Jordan's test for Fourier convergence
nodes.type_signature: (f of bounded variation near x₀) → Pointwise convergence
nodes.description: If f is of bounded variation in a neighborhood of x₀, then S_N(f)(x₀) → ½(f(x₀⁺) + f(x₀⁻)) as N → ∞.

nodes.name: Dirichlet–Jordan theorem
nodes.type_signature: f of bounded variation on 𝕋 → Pointwise convergence everywhere
nodes.description: If f is of bounded variation on 𝕋, the Fourier series of f converges at every point to ½(f(x⁺) + f(x⁻)), and converges uniformly on every closed interval of continuity.

nodes.name: du Bois-Reymond theorem (divergent Fourier series)
nodes.type_signature: ∃ f ∈ C(𝕋) with divergent Fourier series at a point
nodes.description: There exists a continuous function on 𝕋 whose Fourier series diverges at a given point, proved via the unboundedness of the Dirichlet kernel norms ‖D_N‖₁ → ∞ and the Banach–Steinhaus theorem.

nodes.name: Localization principle for Fourier series
nodes.type_signature: (f, g ∈ L¹(𝕋) agree near x₀) → Same convergence behavior
nodes.description: If f = g on an open interval containing x₀, then S_N(f)(x₀) − S_N(g)(x₀) → 0, so convergence of Fourier series at a point depends only on the local behavior of the function.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov's divergence example
nodes.type_signature: ∃ f ∈ L¹(𝕋) with a.e.-divergent Fourier series
nodes.description: There exists an integrable function f ∈ L¹(𝕋) whose Fourier series diverges at every point, showing Carleson's theorem cannot extend to L¹.

nodes.name: Banach–Steinhaus theorem applied to Fourier divergence
nodes.description: Since ‖S_N‖ = ‖D_N‖₁ → ∞, the Banach–Steinhaus theorem implies that the set of continuous functions whose Fourier series diverges at a fixed point is a dense G_δ in C(𝕋).

nodes.name: Lebesgue constants for Fourier partial sums
nodes.description: The operator norms L_N = ‖S_N‖ = ‖D_N‖₁ = (4/π²) log N + O(1), measuring the worst-case amplification of the N-th partial sum operator on C(𝕋).

nodes.name: Best approximation by trigonometric polynomials
nodes.description: The partial sum S_N(f) satisfies ‖f − S_N(f)‖_∞ ≤ (1 + L_N)E_N(f) where E_N(f) is the best uniform approximation by degree-N trigonometric polynomials.

nodes.name: Conjugate Fourier series
nodes.description: The formal series f̃(x) ~ ∑_{n≠0} (−i sgn n) f̂(n) e^{2πinx}, obtained by replacing cos by sin in the Fourier expansion; the boundary value of the conjugate harmonic function.

nodes.name: Conjugate function on 𝕋
nodes.description: The function f̃(x) = limₑ→₀ ∫_{ε<|t|<½} f(x − t) cot(πt)/2 dt, the periodic analogue of the Hilbert transform, existing a.e. for f ∈ L¹(𝕋).

nodes.name: Hilbert transform on 𝕋
nodes.description: The bounded linear operator H : f ↦ f̃ on L^p(𝕋) for 1 < p < ∞, acting on Fourier coefficients by f̃̂(n) = −i sgn(n) f̂(n) and serving as the periodic Hilbert transform.

nodes.name: M. Riesz theorem (L^p boundedness of conjugate function)
nodes.description: The conjugate function operator f ↦ f̃ is bounded on L^p(𝕋) for 1 < p < ∞, with norm growing as C_p ~ 1/(p−1) as p → 1⁺ and as p for p → ∞.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov's weak-type (1,1) inequality for conjugate function
nodes.description: The conjugate function operator satisfies |{x : |f̃(x)| > λ}| ≤ C‖f‖₁/λ for all λ > 0 and f ∈ L¹(𝕋), the best possible substitute for L¹ boundedness which fails.

nodes.name: Zygmund's L log L theorem for conjugate function
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ L log L(𝕋) → f̃ ∈ L¹(𝕋)
nodes.description: If f ∈ L log L(𝕋) (i.e., ∫|f| log⁺|f| < ∞), then the conjugate function f̃ belongs to L¹(𝕋), identifying the precise Orlicz class below which L¹ boundedness of the conjugate holds.

nodes.name: Hardy space H^p on the disk (Katznelson)
nodes.description: The space H^p(𝔻) of analytic functions F on the open unit disk with sup_{0<r<1} (∫_𝕋 |F(re^{2πit})|^p dt)^{1/p} < ∞; boundary values lie in L^p(𝕋) with non-negative Fourier coefficients.

nodes.name: Conjugate Poisson kernel on 𝕋
nodes.description: Q_r(t) = 2r sin(2πt)/(1 − 2r cos(2πt) + r²), the imaginary part of the Cauchy kernel (1 + re^{2πit})/(1 − re^{2πit}), whose convolution with f gives the conjugate harmonic function.

nodes.name: Inner-outer factorization in H^p
nodes.type_signature: F ∈ H^p(𝔻), F ≠ 0 → F = B · S · O
nodes.description: Every non-zero H^p function factors as F = BSO where B is a Blaschke product, S is a singular inner function, and O is an outer function, each determined up to a unimodular constant.

nodes.name: Helson–Lowdenslager prediction theorem
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ L²(𝕋), f ≥ 0 a.e. → log f ∈ L¹ iff prediction is non-degenerate
nodes.description: The subspace ∨{e^{2πint} : n ≥ 1} applied to L²(w dt) equals L²(w dt) if and only if ∫ log w = −∞ (Szegő's condition); otherwise the complement is one-dimensional.

nodes.name: Riesz–Thorin interpolation theorem (Katznelson)
nodes.type_signature: (T bounded on L^{p₀} and L^{p₁}) → T bounded on L^{p_θ}
nodes.description: If a linear operator T is bounded from L^{p₀} to L^{q₀} and from L^{p₁} to L^{q₁}, then T is bounded from L^{p_θ} to L^{q_θ} with 1/p_θ = (1−θ)/p₀ + θ/p₁, and log‖T‖ is convex in θ.

nodes.name: Marcinkiewicz interpolation theorem (Katznelson)
nodes.description: If a sublinear operator T is of weak type (p₀,p₀) and weak type (p₁,p₁) with p₀ < p₁, then T is bounded on L^p for all p₀ < p < p₁.

nodes.name: Hausdorff–Young inequality (Katznelson)
nodes.description: For 1 ≤ p ≤ 2 and p' = p/(p−1), the Fourier coefficients satisfy ‖f̂‖_{ℓ^{p'}} ≤ ‖f‖_{L^p}, proved by interpolating between L¹ → ℓ^∞ (trivial) and L² → ℓ² (Parseval).

nodes.name: Young's convolution inequality on 𝕋 (Katznelson)
nodes.description: If f ∈ L^p(𝕋), g ∈ L^q(𝕋) with 1/p + 1/q ≥ 1, then ‖f ∗ g‖_r ≤ ‖f‖_p ‖g‖_q where 1/r = 1/p + 1/q − 1.

nodes.name: Three-lines lemma (Hadamard)
nodes.function_signature: (F analytic on strip, bounded on boundary lines) → (Bound on interior)
nodes.description: If F is analytic and bounded on the strip 0 ≤ Re z ≤ 1 with |F(it)| ≤ M₀ and |F(1+it)| ≤ M₁, then |F(θ+it)| ≤ M₀^{1−θ} M₁^θ; the key analytic tool in the proof of Riesz–Thorin interpolation.

nodes.name: Lacunary series (Hadamard gaps)
nodes.type_signature: (n_k) with n_{k+1}/n_k ≥ q > 1 → Fourier series with special properties
nodes.description: A trigonometric series ∑ c_k e^{2πin_k t} whose frequencies {n_k} satisfy the Hadamard gap condition n_{k+1}/n_k ≥ q > 1, exhibiting pseudo-random behavior.

nodes.name: Lacunary convergence theorem
nodes.type_signature: Lacunary Fourier series of f ∈ L¹(𝕋) → a.e. convergence
nodes.description: If {n_k} is a lacunary sequence and f ∈ L¹(𝕋), then the partial sums ∑_{k≤K} f̂(n_k)e^{2πin_k x} converge a.e., in contrast to the general L¹ case where divergence can occur everywhere.

nodes.name: Sidon set
nodes.description: A subset Λ ⊂ ℤ such that every bounded function on Λ extends to the Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a measure on 𝕋; equivalently, every continuous function with spectrum in Λ has absolutely convergent Fourier series.

nodes.name: Characterization of Sidon sets
nodes.description: A set Λ ⊂ ℤ is Sidon if and only if for every f ∈ C(𝕋) with supp f̂ ⊂ Λ, the Fourier series converges absolutely, if and only if ‖f‖_A ≤ C‖f‖_∞ for such f.

nodes.name: Riesz product
nodes.description: The weak-∗ limit μ = ∏_{k=1}^∞ (1 + a_k cos 2πn_k t) defines a positive measure on 𝕋 with Fourier coefficients supported on sums of ±n_k, used to construct singular measures and prove Sidon set results.

nodes.name: Quasi-analytic class C{M_n}
nodes.description: The class C{M_n} of C^∞ functions f on 𝕋 with ‖f^{(n)}‖_∞ ≤ A^n M_n for all n; the class is quasi-analytic if the only f ∈ C{M_n} vanishing to infinite order at a point is f ≡ 0.

nodes.name: Denjoy–Carleman theorem
nodes.description: The class C{M_n} is quasi-analytic if and only if ∑_{n=1}^∞ M_{n−1}/M_n = ∞ (equivalently ∑ (inf_{n} M_n^{1/n}/n) = ∞), characterizing when growth conditions on derivatives force unique determination.

nodes.name: Rudin–Shapiro polynomials
nodes.type_signature: n ∈ ℕ → Trigonometric polynomial of degree 2ⁿ − 1
nodes.description: Trigonometric polynomials P_n of degree 2ⁿ − 1 with coefficients ±1 satisfying ‖P_n‖_∞ ≤ C√(2ⁿ), showing that flat polynomials with ±1 coefficients achieve optimal sup-norm growth.

nodes.name: L^p equivalence for lacunary series
nodes.type_signature: f with lacunary Fourier support, 1 ≤ p < ∞ → L^p norms equivalent
nodes.description: If f ∈ L¹(𝕋) has Fourier support on a lacunary set, then f ∈ L^p for all 1 ≤ p < ∞ and the L^p norms are mutually equivalent: c_p ‖f‖₂ ≤ ‖f‖_p ≤ C_p ‖f‖₂.

nodes.name: Fourier transform on L¹(ℝ)
nodes.description: The map f ↦ f̂(ξ) = ∫_ℝ f(x)e^{−2πixξ} dx, a bounded linear map from L¹(ℝ) to C₀(ℝ) (by Riemann–Lebesgue) that is injective but not surjective.

nodes.name: Fourier inversion formula on ℝ
nodes.description: If both f and f̂ belong to L¹(ℝ), then f(x) = ∫_ℝ f̂(ξ)e^{2πixξ} dξ a.e., and f agrees a.e. with a continuous function.

nodes.name: Plancherel theorem on ℝ
nodes.description: The Fourier transform extends uniquely from L¹ ∩ L² to a unitary operator on L²(ℝ) with ‖f̂‖₂ = ‖f‖₂, the L² isometry for the real line.

nodes.name: Schwartz space 𝒮(ℝ) (Katznelson)
nodes.type_signature: Fréchet space of rapidly decreasing functions
nodes.description: The space 𝒮(ℝ) of C^∞ functions on ℝ with x^α ∂^β f → 0 as |x| → ∞ for all α, β; the Fourier transform is an automorphism of 𝒮(ℝ).

nodes.name: Tempered distributions 𝒮′(ℝ) (Katznelson)
nodes.description: The topological dual 𝒮′(ℝ) of the Schwartz space, on which the Fourier transform extends by duality to a continuous automorphism; includes L^p functions, measures, and polynomials.

nodes.name: Poisson summation formula (Katznelson)
nodes.description: For suitable f on ℝ (e.g., f ∈ 𝒮(ℝ)), the identity ∑_{n∈ℤ} f(n) = ∑_{n∈ℤ} f̂(n) holds, relating the periodization of f to the sampling of f̂.

nodes.name: Heisenberg uncertainty principle (Fourier analysis formulation)
nodes.description: A non-zero L² function and its Fourier transform cannot both be concentrated near the origin: ‖xf‖₂ · ‖ξf̂‖₂ ≥ ‖f‖₂²/(4π), with equality only for Gaussians.

nodes.name: Wiener's Tauberian theorem (Katznelson)
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ L¹(ℝ) with f̂ nowhere zero → span{translates of f} dense in L¹
nodes.description: If f ∈ L¹(ℝ) and f̂(ξ) ≠ 0 for all ξ ∈ ℝ, then the closed ideal generated by f in L¹(ℝ) is all of L¹(ℝ); equivalently, the translates of f span a dense subspace.

nodes.name: Fourier–Stieltjes transform on ℝ
nodes.description: The map μ ↦ μ̂(ξ) = ∫_ℝ e^{−2πixξ} dμ(x) extending the Fourier transform to finite Borel measures, with μ̂ bounded, uniformly continuous, and ‖μ̂‖_∞ ≤ ‖μ‖.

nodes.name: Wiener algebra A(ℝ)
nodes.description: The space A(ℝ) = {f̂ : f ∈ L¹(ℝ)} with norm ‖g‖_A = ‖f‖₁ where g = f̂, a regular commutative Banach algebra of continuous functions vanishing at infinity.

nodes.name: Bernstein's inequality for trigonometric polynomials
nodes.type_signature: p trigonometric polynomial of degree N → ‖p′‖_∞ ≤ 2πN‖p‖_∞
nodes.description: For a trigonometric polynomial p of degree at most N, the derivative satisfies ‖p′‖_∞ ≤ 2πN‖p‖_∞, with equality for p(t) = e^{2πiNt}; extends to L^p norms.

nodes.name: Locally compact abelian group (Katznelson)
nodes.description: A topological group G that is locally compact, Hausdorff, and abelian; the natural domain for abstract Fourier analysis, encompassing ℝ, ℤ, 𝕋, ℝⁿ, ℤ_p, finite abelian groups, and their products.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of Haar measure (Katznelson)
nodes.type_signature: G LCA → Unique (up to scalar) translation-invariant Radon measure
nodes.description: Every LCA group G admits a nonzero, translation-invariant, regular Borel measure (Haar measure), unique up to a positive multiplicative constant.

nodes.name: Dual group (Pontryagin dual)
nodes.description: The group Ĝ = Hom(G, 𝕋) of continuous characters χ : G → 𝕋 under pointwise multiplication and the compact-open topology; Ĝ is itself an LCA group.

nodes.name: Pontryagin duality theorem (Katznelson)
nodes.description: The natural evaluation map G → Ĝ̂ sending x to the character χ ↦ χ(x) is a topological group isomorphism, so every LCA group is canonically isomorphic to its double dual.

nodes.name: Fourier transform on LCA groups
nodes.description: The map f ↦ f̂(χ) = ∫_G f(x) χ(−x) dx from L¹(G) to C₀(Ĝ), generalizing both Fourier series (G = 𝕋) and the Fourier transform (G = ℝ).

nodes.name: Plancherel theorem for LCA groups
nodes.description: The Fourier transform extends to a unitary isomorphism from L²(G) onto L²(Ĝ) (with appropriately normalized Haar measures), generalizing Parseval/Plancherel for 𝕋 and ℝ.

nodes.name: Fourier inversion formula on LCA groups
nodes.description: For f ∈ L¹(G) with f̂ ∈ L¹(Ĝ), one has f(x) = ∫_Ĝ f̂(χ) χ(x) dχ for appropriately dual-normalized Haar measures, recovering f from its Fourier transform.

nodes.name: Bochner's theorem on LCA groups (Katznelson)
nodes.type_signature: φ : G → ℂ positive definite ⟺ φ = μ̂ for μ ≥ 0
nodes.description: A continuous function φ on an LCA group G is positive definite if and only if it is the Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a unique non-negative finite Borel measure on Ĝ.

nodes.name: Structure theorem for LCA groups
nodes.type_signature: G LCA → G ≅ ℝⁿ × H with H containing compact open subgroup
nodes.description: Every LCA group G is topologically isomorphic to ℝⁿ × H where n ≥ 0 and H contains a compact open subgroup; in particular, every compactly generated LCA group is ℝⁿ × ℤᵐ × K with K compact.

nodes.name: Standard dual group identifications
nodes.description: The canonical dual group identifications: ℝ̂ ≅ ℝ, 𝕋̂ ≅ ℤ, ℤ̂ ≅ 𝕋, (ℤ/nℤ)̂ ≅ ℤ/nℤ, and (G₁ × G₂)̂ ≅ Ĝ₁ × Ĝ₂.

nodes.name: Annihilator of a subgroup
nodes.description: For a closed subgroup H of LCA group G, the annihilator H⊥ = {χ ∈ Ĝ : χ|_H = 1} is a closed subgroup of Ĝ, with (G/H)̂ ≅ H⊥ and Ĥ ≅ Ĝ/H⊥.

nodes.name: Positive definite function on LCA group
nodes.type_signature: φ : G → ℂ continuous → Kernel property
nodes.description: A continuous function φ on G such that ∑_{i,j} c_i c̄_j φ(x_i − x_j) ≥ 0 for all finite sets {x_i} and scalars {c_i}; the class of functions representable as Fourier transforms of positive measures.

nodes.name: Commutative Banach algebra (Katznelson)
nodes.description: A commutative algebra A over ℂ that is a Banach space with ‖ab‖ ≤ ‖a‖‖b‖, equipped with the Gelfand theory framework for spectral analysis of convolution operators.

nodes.name: Maximal ideal space (spectrum) of a Banach algebra
nodes.type_signature: A commutative Banach algebra → Compact Hausdorff space
nodes.description: The space Δ(A) (or M_A) of all non-zero multiplicative linear functionals on A, equipped with the weak-∗ topology, a compact Hausdorff space (compact if A is unital).

nodes.name: Gelfand transform (Katznelson)
nodes.description: The map â(φ) = φ(a) sending each element a ∈ A to the continuous function â on the maximal ideal space, a contractive algebra homomorphism A → C₀(Δ(A)).

nodes.name: Gelfand representation theorem (Katznelson)
nodes.type_signature: A commutative unital Banach algebra → C(Δ(A)) representation
nodes.description: The Gelfand transform is a continuous algebra homomorphism from A into C(Δ(A)) with ‖â‖_∞ ≤ ‖a‖ and r(a) = ‖â‖_∞ = lim ‖aⁿ‖^{1/n} (spectral radius formula).

nodes.name: Wiener's lemma (absolutely convergent Fourier series)
nodes.description: If f has an absolutely convergent Fourier series and never vanishes on 𝕋, then 1/f also has an absolutely convergent Fourier series; proved elegantly via the Gelfand theory of the Banach algebra A(𝕋).

nodes.name: Wiener algebra A(𝕋)
nodes.description: The Banach algebra A(𝕋) = {f ∈ C(𝕋) : ‖f‖_A = ∑|f̂(n)| < ∞} of functions with absolutely convergent Fourier series, with pointwise multiplication and norm ‖f‖_A = ‖f̂‖_{ℓ¹}.

nodes.name: Gelfand–Mazur theorem (Katznelson)
nodes.type_signature: A Banach division algebra → A ≅ ℂ
nodes.description: Every commutative Banach algebra in which every non-zero element is invertible is isometrically isomorphic to ℂ.

nodes.name: Spectral synthesis
nodes.type_signature: Closed ideal I in A(G) → Determined by its hull
nodes.description: The question of whether every closed ideal I in a group algebra (or regular Banach algebra) is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it, i.e., whether I is uniquely determined by its hull h(I).

nodes.name: Spectral analysis holds in L¹(G)
nodes.type_signature: I proper closed ideal in L¹(G) → h(I) ≠ ∅
nodes.description: Every proper closed ideal in L¹(G) for an LCA group G has non-empty hull (i.e., is contained in a maximal ideal), proved via the regularity of L¹(G) as a Banach algebra.

nodes.name: Malliavin's theorem (failure of spectral synthesis)
nodes.type_signature: G non-compact LCA → Spectral synthesis fails
nodes.description: For every non-compact locally compact abelian group G, spectral synthesis fails in L¹(G): there exist closed ideals not determined by their hulls, answering a question of Beurling and others.

nodes.name: Regular Banach algebra
nodes.type_signature: A commutative Banach algebra → Separation property
nodes.description: A commutative Banach algebra A is regular if for every closed set E ⊂ Δ(A) and φ₀ ∉ E, there exists a ∈ A with â(φ₀) = 1 and â|_E = 0; L¹(G) is regular for every LCA group G.

nodes.name: Hull-kernel topology
nodes.type_signature: A commutative Banach algebra → Topology on Δ(A)
nodes.description: The topology on Δ(A) defined by closure operation E ↦ h(k(E)) where k(E) = ∩{ker φ : φ ∈ E} and h(I) = {φ : I ⊂ ker φ}; coincides with Gelfand topology iff A is regular.

nodes.name: Ideal theory of L¹(G)
nodes.type_signature: G LCA → Closed ideals in L¹(G)
nodes.description: The correspondence between closed ideals of the group algebra L¹(G), closed subsets of the dual group Ĝ, and translation-invariant closed subspaces of L¹(G), governed by Wiener's theorem and spectral synthesis.

nodes.name: Gelfand theory technique
nodes.function_signature: (Commutative Banach algebra A) → (Spectral data on Δ(A))
nodes.description: Reducing algebraic and analytic questions about a commutative Banach algebra to function-theoretic questions on its maximal ideal space via the Gelfand transform; exemplified by the proof of Wiener's lemma.

nodes.name: Approximate identity method in harmonic analysis
nodes.function_signature: (Approximate identity {K_n}, f ∈ L^p) → (K_n ∗ f → f in appropriate topology)
nodes.description: Using families of kernels with mass 1, bounded L¹ norm, and vanishing tails to approximate functions via convolution; the common mechanism behind Fejér, Poisson, and general summability methods.

nodes.name: Summability method for Fourier series
nodes.function_signature: (Divergent or slowly converging Fourier partial sums) → (Convergent averaged sums)
nodes.description: Replacing partial sums S_N(f) by weighted averages (Cesàro/Abel/de la Vallée-Poussin) to obtain convergence; each method corresponds to convolution with a specific approximate identity kernel.

nodes.name: de la Vallée-Poussin kernel
nodes.description: V_N = 2F_{2N} − F_N, a trigonometric polynomial with V̂_N(n) = 1 for |n| ≤ N, providing a smooth approximate identity that also reproduces trigonometric polynomials of degree ≤ N exactly.

nodes.name: Gelfand space of L¹(G) is Ĝ
nodes.description: The maximal ideal space of the group algebra L¹(G) is canonically homeomorphic to the dual group Ĝ, with the Gelfand transform reducing to the Fourier transform.

nodes.name: Vibrating string equation
nodes.description: The PDE ∂²u/∂t² = c²∂²u/∂x² with boundary conditions u(0,t) = u(L,t) = 0 modeling the transverse displacement of a vibrating string fixed at both ends.

nodes.name: D’Alembert’s solution to the wave equation
nodes.type_signature: (Initial data f, g on ℝ) → u(x,t)
nodes.description: The general solution u(x,t) = ½[f(x+ct) + f(x−ct)] + (1/(2c))∫_{x−ct}^{x+ct} g(s) ds of the one-dimensional wave equation with initial displacement f and velocity g.

nodes.name: Standing wave solution
nodes.description: A separable solution u_n(x,t) = sin(nπx/L)(A_n cos(nπct/L) + B_n sin(nπct/L)) of the vibrating string equation, representing a mode with n half-wavelengths.

nodes.name: Superposition principle for linear PDEs
nodes.function_signature: (Linear PDE, family of solutions {u_n}) → (Formal series ∑ c_n u_n as solution)
nodes.description: For a linear homogeneous PDE, any convergent linear combination of solutions is again a solution, enabling construction of general solutions from elementary modes.

nodes.name: Fourier’s program for solving PDEs
nodes.function_signature: (Linear PDE with boundary conditions) → (Formal Fourier series solution)
nodes.description: The strategy of expanding a solution as a Fourier series, substituting into the PDE to determine coefficients, then verifying convergence and boundary behavior.

nodes.name: Formal solution to Dirichlet problem on the disk
nodes.description: The formal series u(r,θ) = ∑_{n∈ℤ} f̂(n) r^{|n|} e^{inθ} for the Laplace equation on the disk with boundary data f, whose rigorous justification involves the Poisson kernel.

nodes.name: Riemann integrable function on the circle
nodes.description: A function f on the circle 𝕋 that is Riemann integrable, the natural domain for classical Fourier series before Lebesgue theory.

nodes.name: Convolution identity for Fourier coefficients
nodes.description: The nth Fourier coefficient of the convolution f ∗ g equals the product f̂(n)ĝ(n), converting convolution on the circle to pointwise multiplication of Fourier coefficients.

nodes.name: Approximation theorem for good kernels
nodes.type_signature: (Good kernel {K_n}, f ∈ C(𝕋)) → K_n ∗ f → f uniformly
nodes.description: If {K_n} is a family of good kernels and f is continuous on 𝕋, then K_n ∗ f converges to f uniformly; for integrable f, convergence holds at points of continuity.

nodes.name: Cesàro mean (Nth)
nodes.description: The Nth Cesàro mean of a sequence of partial sums, σ_N = (s_0 + s_1 + ... + s_{N−1})/N, the basic building block of Cesàro summability.

nodes.name: Dirichlet kernel is not a good kernel
nodes.description: The L¹ norms of the Dirichlet kernels satisfy ‖D_N‖₁ ∼ (4/π²) log N → ∞, so {D_N} does not form a family of good kernels.

nodes.name: Fejér kernel is a good kernel
nodes.description: The Fejér kernel F_N is non-negative with ∫F_N = 1 and ∫_{|t|>δ} F_N(t) dt → 0 for every δ > 0, making it a family of good kernels.

nodes.name: Poisson kernel is a good kernel
nodes.description: The Poisson kernel P_r is a non-negative approximate identity as r → 1⁻, satisfying all three conditions of a good kernel family.

nodes.name: L² inner product on the circle
nodes.description: The Hermitian inner product ⟨f,g⟩ = ∫₀¹ f(t)g̅(t) dt on L²(𝕋) making it a separable Hilbert space with orthonormal basis {e^{2πint}}_{n∈ℤ}.

nodes.name: Orthonormality of exponentials on 𝕋
nodes.description: The complex exponentials {e^{2πint}}_{n∈ℤ} form an orthonormal system in L²(𝕋).

nodes.name: Mean-square convergence of Fourier series
nodes.description: For f ∈ L²(𝕋), the partial sums S_N(f) converge to f in the L² norm, equivalent to Parseval’s identity.

nodes.name: Completeness of the trigonometric system
nodes.description: The exponentials {e^{2πint}}_{n∈ℤ} form a complete orthonormal system in L²(𝕋): if all Fourier coefficients vanish, then f = 0 a.e.

nodes.name: Pointwise convergence of Fourier series under Hölder condition
nodes.type_signature: (f Hölder of order α > 0 near x₀) → S_N(f)(x₀) → f(x₀)
nodes.description: If f satisfies |f(x₀+t) − f(x₀)| ≤ C|t|^α for some α > 0 near x₀, then the Fourier series converges pointwise to f(x₀).

nodes.name: Fourier analytic proof of the isoperimetric inequality
nodes.function_signature: (Simple closed curve in ℝ²) → (A ≤ L²/(4π) via Fourier coefficients)
nodes.description: Proving the isoperimetric inequality by expanding the curve’s coordinates as Fourier series, applying Parseval’s identity and the arc-length constraint.

nodes.name: Weyl’s criterion for equidistribution
nodes.type_signature: (Sequence {x_n} in [0,1)) → Equidistribution iff exponential sums vanish
nodes.description: A sequence {x_n} is equidistributed mod 1 if and only if (1/N)∑_{n=1}^{N} e^{2πikx_n} → 0 for every nonzero integer k.

nodes.name: Continuous nowhere-differentiable function
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ C(𝕋), f’(x) does not exist for any x
nodes.description: A continuous function on 𝕋 differentiable at no point, constructed via a lacunary Fourier series f(x) = ∑ b^{−nα} e^{2πib^n x}.

nodes.name: Construction via lacunary Fourier series
nodes.function_signature: (Lacunary frequencies {n_k}, coefficients {a_k}) → (Function with pathological properties)
nodes.description: Using Fourier series with rapidly growing frequencies to construct continuous nowhere-differentiable functions or other pathological examples.

nodes.name: Heat equation on the circle
nodes.description: The parabolic PDE ∂u/∂t = ∂²u/∂x² for u(x,t) periodic in x with initial condition u(x,0) = f(x), modeling heat diffusion on a circular ring.

nodes.name: Solution of heat equation on circle via Fourier series
nodes.description: The solution to the heat equation on 𝕋 with initial data f is u(x,t) = ∑ f̂(n) e^{−4π²n²t} e^{2πinx}, converging for all t > 0.

nodes.name: Heat kernel on the circle
nodes.description: The periodized Gaussian H_t(x) = ∑_{n∈ℤ} e^{−4π²n²t} e^{2πinx}, the fundamental solution of the heat equation on 𝕋.

nodes.name: Heat kernel on circle is a good kernel
nodes.description: As t → 0⁺, the heat kernel H_t on 𝕋 forms a family of good kernels: H_t ≥ 0, ∫H_t = 1, and ∫_{|x|>δ} H_t → 0.

nodes.name: Smoothing property of the heat equation
nodes.description: For any integrable initial data f, the solution u(x,t) = H_t ∗ f of the heat equation is C^∞ for all t > 0.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of solution to heat equation on circle
nodes.type_signature: (Continuous solution u on 𝕋 × [0,∞)) → u = H_t ∗ f
nodes.description: A continuous solution of the heat equation on 𝕋 that is C² for t > 0 and satisfies u(x,0) = f(x) is uniquely determined.

nodes.name: Steady-state solution of the heat equation
nodes.description: A time-invariant solution of the heat equation satisfying Laplace’s equation; on the circle, steady states are constants; on the disk, they are harmonic functions.

nodes.name: Basic properties of the Fourier transform on ℝ
nodes.description: The Fourier transform satisfies linearity, translation-modulation duality, dilation, and conjugation symmetry on L¹(ℝ).

nodes.name: Fourier transform of the Gaussian
nodes.description: The Gaussian e^{−πx²} is an eigenfunction of the Fourier transform with eigenvalue 1.

nodes.name: Fourier transform maps 𝒮(ℝ) to 𝒮(ℝ)
nodes.description: The Fourier transform is a continuous linear bijection from the Schwartz space onto itself, with inverse given by the inverse Fourier transform.

nodes.name: Multiplication formula for the Fourier transform
nodes.description: For f, g ∈ L¹(ℝ), ∫f̂(x)g(x) dx = ∫f(x)ĝ(x) dx, a self-adjointness relation used in extending the Fourier transform to L².

nodes.name: Convolution theorem on ℝ
nodes.description: The Fourier transform converts convolution to pointwise multiplication: (f ∗ g)^(ξ) = f̂(ξ)ĝ(ξ).

nodes.name: Equality case in the Heisenberg uncertainty principle
nodes.description: Equality in the Heisenberg uncertainty principle holds if and only if f(x) = Ce^{−αx²} for constants C ∈ ℂ and α > 0.

nodes.name: Solution of the heat equation on ℝ via Fourier transform
nodes.description: The solution of ∂u/∂t = ∂²u/∂x² on ℝ with u(x,0) = f(x) is u(x,t) = W_t ∗ f where W_t is the heat kernel.

nodes.name: Heat kernel on ℝ is a good kernel
nodes.description: The Gaussian heat kernel W_t(x) = (4πt)^{−1/2}e^{−x²/(4t)} forms a family of good kernels as t → 0⁺.

nodes.name: Fourier transform and differentiation correspondence
nodes.description: Differentiation corresponds to multiplication by 2πiξ in frequency domain, and multiplication by −2πix corresponds to differentiation of the transform.

nodes.name: Functions of moderate decrease
nodes.description: A continuous function f on ℝ satisfying |f(x)| ≤ A/(1+|x|)^{1+ε} for some A, ε > 0, sufficient for the Poisson summation formula.

nodes.name: Schwartz space 𝒮(ℝ^d)
nodes.description: The space 𝒮(ℝ^d) of C^∞ functions with sup |x^α ∂^β f(x)| < ∞ for all multi-indices α, β, on which the Fourier transform is an automorphism.

nodes.name: Solution of wave equation via Fourier transform
nodes.function_signature: (Wave equation u_tt = c²Δu, initial data f, g) → (u(x,t) via inverse FT)
nodes.description: Taking the spatial Fourier transform of the wave equation reduces it to an ODE in t for each frequency, yielding the solution via inverse transform.

nodes.name: Spherical means
nodes.type_signature: (f : ℝ^d → ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^d, r > 0) → M_f(x,r)
nodes.description: The average M_f(x,r) of f over the sphere of radius r centered at x, satisfying the Darboux equation and fundamental to wave equation solutions in higher dimensions.

nodes.name: Kirchhoff’s formula for the wave equation in ℝ³
nodes.type_signature: (Initial data f, g on ℝ³) → u(x,t)
nodes.description: The solution of u_tt = Δu in ℝ³ is u(x,t) = ∂/∂t[tM_f(x,t)] + tM_g(x,t), depending only on data on the sphere |y−x| = t.

nodes.name: Huygens’ principle
nodes.description: In odd spatial dimensions d ≥ 3, wave propagation is sharp: the solution at (x,t) depends only on initial data on the sphere |y−x| = ct.

nodes.name: Failure of Huygens’ principle in even dimensions
nodes.description: In even spatial dimensions, the wave equation solution at (x,t) depends on initial data in the entire ball |y−x| ≤ ct, causing residual signals.

nodes.name: Hadamard’s method of descent
nodes.function_signature: (Solution in ℝ^{d+1}) → (Solution in ℝ^d)
nodes.description: Deriving the wave equation solution in ℝ^d from the known solution in ℝ^{d+1} by treating initial data as independent of the extra variable.

nodes.name: Wave equation solution in ℝ² (Poisson’s formula)
nodes.type_signature: (Initial data f, g on ℝ²) → u(x,t)
nodes.description: The solution of u_tt = Δu in ℝ², obtained from Kirchhoff’s formula via the method of descent, involving integration over the disk |y−x| ≤ t.

nodes.name: Radon transform
nodes.description: The integral transform Rf(ω,s) = ∫_{x·ω=s} f(x) dx integrating f over hyperplanes, fundamental to CT imaging and related to the Fourier transform via the Fourier slice theorem.

nodes.name: Fourier slice theorem (projection-slice theorem)
nodes.description: The 1D Fourier transform of the Radon transform Rf(ω,·) equals the restriction of the d-dimensional Fourier transform f̂ to the line through the origin in direction ω.

nodes.name: Radon inversion formula
nodes.description: The function f can be recovered from its Radon transform via filtered backprojection, using the Fourier slice theorem and inverse Fourier transform.

nodes.name: Fourier transform of radial functions via Bessel functions
nodes.description: If f is radial on ℝ^d, then f̂ is also radial and expressible via Bessel functions: f̂(ξ) = 2π|ξ|^{−(d/2−1)} ∫ f₀(r) J_{d/2−1}(2π|ξ|r) r^{d/2} dr.

nodes.name: Fourier transform of the indicator of a ball
nodes.description: The Fourier transform of the characteristic function of the ball B(0,R) in ℝ^d, expressed via the Bessel function J_{d/2}.

nodes.name: Discrete Fourier transform (DFT)
nodes.description: The DFT of f on ℤ/Nℤ is f̂(k) = ∑_{n=0}^{N−1} f(n) e^{−2πink/N}, a linear isomorphism of ℂ^N.

nodes.name: Inverse discrete Fourier transform
nodes.description: The DFT is inverted by f(n) = (1/N)∑ f̂(k) e^{2πink/N}, proved using orthogonality of characters of ℤ/Nℤ.

nodes.name: Parseval’s identity for the DFT
nodes.description: The DFT preserves ℓ² norms up to scaling: ∑|f(n)|² = (1/N)∑|f̂(k)|², the finite analogue of Parseval’s theorem.

nodes.name: Convolution on ℤ/Nℤ
nodes.description: The circular convolution (f ∗ g)(n) = ∑ f(m)g(n−m mod N) on ℤ/Nℤ, satisfying (f∗g)^ = f̂ĝ under the DFT.

nodes.name: Convolution theorem for the DFT
nodes.description: The DFT converts circular convolution on ℤ/Nℤ to pointwise multiplication.

nodes.name: Fast Fourier transform (FFT)
nodes.function_signature: (f : ℤ/Nℤ → ℂ, N = 2^m) → (f̂ in O(N log N) operations)
nodes.description: The Cooley-Tukey algorithm computing the DFT in O(N log N) operations by recursively splitting into even- and odd-indexed sub-problems.

nodes.name: FFT complexity
nodes.type_signature: N = 2^m → DFT in O(N log N)
nodes.description: The FFT computes the DFT of N = 2^m points using O(N log N) multiplications and additions, compared to O(N²) naively.

nodes.name: Polynomial multiplication via FFT
nodes.function_signature: (Polynomials of degree ≤ n) → (Product in O(n log n))
nodes.description: Multiplying two polynomials by evaluating at roots of unity via FFT, pointwise multiplying, and interpolating via inverse FFT.

nodes.name: Fast integer multiplication via FFT
nodes.function_signature: (n-digit integers) → (Product in O(n log n log log n))
nodes.description: The Schönhage-Strassen algorithm multiplying large integers by representing them as polynomials and using FFT-based polynomial multiplication.

nodes.name: Non-vanishing of L(1,χ) for complex Dirichlet characters
nodes.description: For a complex (non-real) Dirichlet character χ, L(1,χ) ≠ 0, proved by showing ∏_χ L(s,χ) has nonnegative coefficients and a pole at s = 1.

nodes.name: Non-vanishing of L(1,χ) for real Dirichlet characters
nodes.description: For a real non-principal Dirichlet character, L(1,χ) ≠ 0, proved by a more delicate argument involving the theta function or Dirichlet’s class number formula.

nodes.name: Analytic continuation of L(s,χ) to Re(s) > 0
nodes.type_signature: χ non-principal → L(s,χ) analytic for Re(s) > 0
nodes.description: For non-principal χ, L(s,χ) extends analytically to Re(s) > 0 via Abel summation, since ∑_{n≤x} χ(n) is bounded.

nodes.name: Natural density of primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.description: Primes p ≡ a (mod d) have natural density 1/φ(d) among all primes, a quantitative refinement of Dirichlet’s theorem.

nodes.name: Gibbs phenomenon
nodes.description: At a jump discontinuity, the Fourier partial sums S_N(f) overshoot by approximately 9% of the jump size, and this overshoot persists as N → ∞.

nodes.name: Absolute convergence of Fourier series under smoothness
nodes.description: If f is twice continuously differentiable on 𝕋, then f̂(n) = O(1/n²), hence the Fourier series converges absolutely and uniformly.

nodes.name: Decay of Fourier coefficients and smoothness
nodes.description: If f ∈ C^k(𝕋), then f̂(n) = o(|n|^{−k}); conversely, rapid decay implies smoothness, establishing a precise smoothness-decay duality.

nodes.name: Wirtinger’s inequality
nodes.description: For a mean-zero C¹ function on 𝕋, ‖f‖₂ ≤ (1/(2π))‖f’‖₂, with equality iff f is a first-order trigonometric polynomial.

nodes.name: Gronwall inequality (integral form)
nodes.description: If u(t) ≤ α + ∫₀ᵗ β(s)u(s) ds with β ≥ 0, then u(t) ≤ α exp(∫₀ᵗ β(s) ds); the integral version of Gronwall’s inequality used for stability and continuous dependence estimates.

nodes.name: Continuous dependence on initial conditions
nodes.description: Solutions of y' = f(t, y) depend continuously on the initial data (t₀, y₀) in the topology of uniform convergence on compact subintervals of the maximal existence interval.

nodes.name: Continuous dependence on parameters
nodes.description: If f(t, y, λ) is continuous in all variables and Lipschitz in y, then the solution y(t; λ) of y' = f(t, y, λ) is continuous in the parameter λ uniformly on compact time intervals.

nodes.name: Differentiability with respect to initial conditions
nodes.description: If f(t, y) is Cᵏ, then the solution y(t; t₀, y₀) is Cᵏ in the initial data (t₀, y₀), and the derivative ∂y/∂y₀ satisfies the variational equation.

nodes.name: Variational equation
