nodes.description: The linearization Z' = (∂f/∂y)(t, y(t))Z of an ODE y' = f(t, y) along a solution y(t), governing the first-order sensitivity of solutions to perturbations in initial data.

nodes.name: Characteristic multipliers (Floquet multipliers)
nodes.description: The eigenvalues ρ₁, …, ρₙ of the monodromy matrix M = Φ(T) of a T-periodic linear system; their moduli determine stability: |ρᵢ| < 1 for all i implies asymptotic stability.

nodes.name: Floquet normal form
nodes.description: The representation Φ(t) = P(t)e^{tB} of the fundamental matrix of a T-periodic system, where P(t) is T-periodic and B is a constant matrix (the Floquet exponent matrix).

nodes.name: Stability zones for periodic equations
nodes.description: Regions in parameter space where all solutions of a periodic ODE (e.g., Hill’s or Mathieu’s equation) remain bounded, separated by instability zones where solutions grow exponentially.

nodes.name: Self-adjointness of Sturm–Liouville operators
nodes.description: The operator L[y] = −(py’)’ + qy with separated boundary conditions on [a,b] is self-adjoint in L²([a,b], w), ensuring real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenfunctions.

nodes.name: Sturm separation theorem
nodes.description: Between any two consecutive zeros of one non-trivial solution of a second-order linear ODE, there lies exactly one zero of every linearly independent solution.

nodes.name: Sturm oscillation theorem
nodes.description: The n-th eigenfunction of a regular Sturm–Liouville problem has exactly n−1 zeros in the open interval (a, b), and the eigenvalues form an increasing sequence tending to infinity.

nodes.name: Green’s function for ODE boundary value problem
nodes.description: The kernel G(t, s) that inverts a linear differential operator with boundary conditions, so that the unique solution of L[y] = f is y(t) = ∫ G(t, s)f(s) ds.

nodes.name: Eigenfunction expansion theorem (Sturm–Liouville)
nodes.description: Every function in L²([a,b], w) can be expanded as a convergent series in the eigenfunctions of a regular Sturm–Liouville problem, with convergence in L² and pointwise convergence under regularity.

nodes.name: Min-max principle for eigenvalues (Sturm–Liouville)
nodes.description: The n-th eigenvalue λₙ of a self-adjoint Sturm–Liouville operator equals the min over n-dimensional subspaces V of the max Rayleigh quotient over V, providing variational characterization of eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Asymptotic stability
nodes.description: An equilibrium y* is asymptotically stable if it is Lyapunov stable and additionally all solutions starting sufficiently close converge to y* as t → ∞.

nodes.name: Lyapunov instability theorem
nodes.description: If there exists a function V with V̇ > 0 in a punctured neighborhood of an equilibrium and V takes positive values arbitrarily close to the equilibrium, then the equilibrium is unstable.

nodes.name: Lyapunov equation for linear systems
nodes.description: The linear matrix equation AᵀP + PA = −Q; a Hurwitz matrix A admits a unique positive-definite solution P for every positive-definite Q, providing a Lyapunov function V(x) = xᵀPx.

nodes.name: Exponential stability
nodes.description: An equilibrium is exponentially stable if nearby solutions satisfy ‖y(t) − y*‖ ≤ Ce^{−αt}‖y(0) − y*‖ for constants C, α > 0; stronger than asymptotic stability.

nodes.name: Uniform stability
nodes.description: The equilibrium of a non-autonomous system y' = f(t, y) is uniformly stable if the δ in Lyapunov stability can be chosen independent of the initial time t₀.

nodes.name: Phase plane
nodes.description: The (y₁, y₂)-plane for a two-dimensional autonomous system, in which solution trajectories (phase curves) provide a qualitative picture of the global dynamics.

nodes.name: ω-limit set
nodes.description: The set ω(γ) of all accumulation points of a forward trajectory γ(t) as t → +∞; a non-empty compact connected invariant set when the trajectory is bounded.

nodes.name: α-limit set
nodes.description: The set α(γ) of all accumulation points of a trajectory γ(t) as t → −∞; the time-reversed analogue of the ω-limit set.

nodes.name: Limit cycle
nodes.description: An isolated periodic orbit in the phase plane, i.e., a closed trajectory with no other periodic orbit in a neighborhood; the simplest non-equilibrium attractor or repeller in ℝ².

nodes.name: Bendixson criterion (negative criterion)
nodes.description: If div(f) = ∂f₁/∂y₁ + ∂f₂/∂y₂ does not change sign in a simply connected region, then the planar system y' = f(y) has no periodic orbit in that region.

nodes.name: Orbital stability
nodes.description: A periodic orbit γ is orbitally stable if every trajectory starting near γ remains close to the orbit (not to a specific point on it) for all future time.

nodes.name: Index of a closed curve (Poincaré index)
nodes.description: The winding number of the vector field f(y) around a simple closed curve not passing through any equilibrium; equals the sum of indices of equilibria enclosed.

nodes.name: Index theorem for equilibria
nodes.description: The index of an isolated equilibrium of a planar vector field is +1 for a node, focus, or center, and −1 for a simple saddle; the index of any closed curve equals the sum of indices of enclosed equilibria.

nodes.name: Poincaré expansion theorem
nodes.description: If f(t, y, ε) is analytic in ε, the solution y(t, ε) of the initial value problem is analytic in ε for |ε| sufficiently small, justifying regular perturbation series.

nodes.name: Singular perturbation
nodes.description: A perturbation problem εy'' + a(t)y' + b(t)y = 0 where setting ε = 0 reduces the order of the equation, causing non-uniform convergence and boundary layers.

nodes.name: Boundary layer
nodes.description: A narrow region (of width O(ε) or O(ε^α)) near the boundary where the solution of a singularly perturbed ODE transitions rapidly between the outer solution and a boundary condition.

nodes.name: Classification of equilibria in ℝ²
nodes.description: For a linear system ẏ = Ay in ℝ², the eigenvalues of A classify the equilibrium as a stable/unstable node, saddle, stable/unstable focus, center, or degenerate node/star.

nodes.name: Separatrices
nodes.description: Distinguished trajectories (typically stable/unstable manifolds of saddle points) that divide the phase plane into regions of qualitatively different behavior.

nodes.name: Topological equivalence of phase portraits
nodes.description: Two autonomous systems are topologically equivalent if there is a homeomorphism mapping orbits of one to orbits of the other preserving orientation; the natural notion of qualitative sameness.

nodes.name: Weyl limit-point/limit-circle classification
nodes.description: At a singular endpoint of a Sturm–Liouville problem, either all solutions are L² (limit-circle case) or exactly one solution is L² (limit-point case); determines whether a boundary condition is needed.

nodes.name: Weyl m-function
nodes.description: The Herglotz–Nevanlinna function m(z) selecting the unique L² solution at a singular endpoint of a Sturm–Liouville problem; its boundary values on ℝ encode the spectral measure.

nodes.name: Titchmarsh–Weyl theory
nodes.description: The spectral theory of singular Sturm–Liouville operators via the Weyl m-function, establishing the eigenfunction expansion and spectral measure for operators on a half-line or the full line.

nodes.name: Singular Sturm–Liouville problem
nodes.description: A Sturm–Liouville problem −(py’)’ + qy = λwy on an interval where at least one endpoint is singular (infinite, or p, w vanish/q is unbounded), requiring Weyl theory for spectral analysis.

nodes.name: Eigenfunction expansion on half-line
nodes.description: For a singular Sturm–Liouville problem on [0, ∞), every L²-function admits a generalized Fourier transform f̂(λ) = ∫ f(t)φ(t,λ) dt with Parseval equality via the spectral measure dρ(λ).

nodes.name: Regular singular point of an ODE
nodes.description: A point z₀ where the coefficient functions of a linear ODE have poles, but (z−z₀)p(z) and (z−z₀)²q(z) are analytic; solutions have at most algebraic-logarithmic growth near z₀.

nodes.name: Irregular singular point of an ODE
nodes.description: A singular point that is not regular; solutions generically have essential singularities with exponential growth/decay, and formal series solutions are typically divergent (asymptotic).

nodes.name: Logarithmic solutions at regular singular points
nodes.description: When indicial exponents differ by an integer at a regular singular point, a second linearly independent solution may require a log(z−z₀) term: y₂ = cy₁ log(z−z₀) + z^{r₂} Σ bₙ zⁿ.

nodes.name: Fuchs’s theorem
nodes.description: A linear ODE has all its singular points regular (is Fuchsian) if and only if the sum of all indicial exponents at all singular points (including ∞) satisfies the Fuchs relation.

nodes.name: Asymptotic solutions at irregular singular points
nodes.description: Near an irregular singular point of rank r, there exist formal solutions of the form e^{Q(z)} z^ρ Σ aₙ z⁻ⁿ where Q is a polynomial of degree r; these are asymptotic to true solutions in Stokes sectors.

nodes.name: Ordinary point of an ODE in ℂ
nodes.description: A point z₀ where all coefficient functions of a linear ODE are analytic; solutions are analytic in a disk centered at z₀ with radius equal to the distance to the nearest singularity.

nodes.name: Monodromy representation
nodes.description: The group homomorphism ρ: π₁(ℂ \ {singularities}, z₀) → GL(n, ℂ) sending each loop to the linear transformation on the solution space obtained by analytic continuation around the loop.

nodes.name: Riemann–Hilbert problem (for linear ODE)
nodes.description: Given points a₁, …, aₘ in ℂP¹ and a representation ρ: π₁(ℂP¹ \ {aᵢ}) → GL(n, ℂ), find a Fuchsian system with those singularities and that monodromy; solvable with possible apparent singularities by Plemelj, with negative results (Bolibruch) for strict Fuchsian systems.

nodes.name: Perron’s theorem on asymptotic integration
nodes.description: For the system y' = (A + R(t))y where A is a constant matrix with distinct eigenvalues and R(t) → 0 as t → ∞, there exist solutions asymptotic to e^{λᵢt}vᵢ where λᵢ, vᵢ are eigenvalue-eigenvector pairs of A.

nodes.name: Levinson’s theorem (asymptotic integration)
nodes.description: Refines Perron’s theorem: if A has distinct real parts and ∫₀^∞ ‖R(t)‖ dt < ∞, then y' = (A + R(t))y has a fundamental system of solutions yₖ(t) ~ e^{λₖt}vₖ as t → ∞, with precise error estimates.

nodes.name: Global existence for linear ODE systems
nodes.description: If A(t) and b(t) are continuous on [a, b], then the solution of y' = A(t)y + b(t), y(t₀) = y₀ exists on the entire interval [a, b]; linear systems cannot blow up in finite time.

nodes.name: Euler polygonal approximation method
nodes.function_signature: (ODE y' = f(t,y), step size h) → (Piecewise-linear approximate solution)
nodes.description: Constructs piecewise-linear approximations yₙ₊₁ = yₙ + hf(tₙ, yₙ) used in Peano’s existence proof and as the simplest numerical ODE integrator.

nodes.name: Green’s function construction for BVP
nodes.function_signature: (Linear ODE L[y] = f, boundary conditions) → (Green’s function G(t,s))
nodes.description: Constructs G(t, s) by patching two solutions satisfying opposite boundary conditions at t = s with a jump in the derivative determined by the Wronskian.

nodes.name: Prüfer transformation
nodes.function_signature: (Second-order linear ODE y'' + q(t)y = 0) → (Polar variables (r(t), θ(t)) with θ' = cos²θ + q sin²θ)
nodes.description: Transforms a second-order ODE into a system for amplitude and angle, reducing oscillation and comparison questions to the monotonicity analysis of the angle variable θ(t).

nodes.name: Regular perturbation method
nodes.function_signature: (ODE y' = f(t, y, ε), small parameter ε) → (Power series solution y = y₀ + εy₁ + ε²y₂ + ⋯)
nodes.description: Expands the solution in powers of a small parameter ε and solves order-by-order; valid when the solution depends analytically on ε.

nodes.name: Matched asymptotic expansions
nodes.function_signature: (Singularly perturbed ODE) → (Composite asymptotic solution uniformly valid on full interval)
nodes.description: Constructs separate inner (boundary-layer) and outer expansions and determines free constants by matching in an overlap region where both are valid.

nodes.name: Averaging method
nodes.function_signature: (Slowly varying system ẋ = εf(t, x)) → (Averaged autonomous system ẋ = εf̄(x))
nodes.description: Replaces a rapidly oscillating non-autonomous system by its time-averaged autonomous approximation, with error O(ε) on time intervals of length O(1/ε).

nodes.name: Analytic continuation of ODE solutions
nodes.function_signature: (Local analytic ODE solution near z₀, path γ in ℂ avoiding singularities) → (Continued solution along γ)
nodes.description: Extends a local analytic solution of a linear ODE along a path in the complex plane; the result depends on the homotopy class of the path, generating the monodromy representation.

nodes.name: Reduction of order
nodes.function_signature: (n-th order linear ODE, one known solution y₁) → ((n−1)-th order ODE for the remaining solutions)
nodes.description: Given one solution y₁ of a homogeneous linear ODE, substitutes y = y₁v and reduces to a lower-order equation in v’, lowering the problem by one degree.

nodes.name: Differential inequality technique
nodes.function_signature: (Differential inequality u' ≤ f(t, u) and comparison ODE v' = f(t, v)) → (Bound u(t) ≤ v(t))
nodes.description: Bounds solutions of an ODE above or below by comparing with solutions of a simpler inequality via the comparison principle, yielding a priori estimates.

nodes.name: Higher-order linear ODE reduction to first-order system
nodes.function_signature: (n-th order ODE y⁽ⁿ⁾ + aₙ₋₁y⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾ + ⋯ + a₀y = f) → (First-order system Y' = AY + F in ℝⁿ)
nodes.description: Converts a scalar n-th order linear ODE to an equivalent first-order system by introducing y₁ = y, y₂ = y', …, yₙ = y⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾, reducing all higher-order theory to the first-order framework.

nodes.name: Phase space of a dynamical system
nodes.description: The space M of all possible states of a system, in which the evolution of the system is described as motion of a point along a phase curve.

nodes.name: Phase curve (integral curve of an ODE)
nodes.type_signature: (Phase flow g^t, Initial point x₀) → Curve γ ⊂ M
nodes.description: The image {g^t(x₀) : t ∈ I} of a solution trajectory in phase space; the orbit of a point under the phase flow.

nodes.name: Phase portrait
nodes.type_signature: (Autonomous ODE on M) → Partition of M into phase curves
nodes.description: The partition of the phase space into the union of all phase curves, providing a complete qualitative picture of the dynamics.

nodes.name: Phase flow
nodes.type_signature: (Autonomous ODE ẋ = v(x)) → One-parameter group {g^t : M → M}
nodes.description: The one-parameter group of diffeomorphisms g^t: M → M defined by g^t(x₀) = φ(t; x₀), where φ is the solution of ẋ = v(x) with φ(0) = x₀.

nodes.name: Phase velocity vector field
nodes.type_signature: (Phase flow {g^t}) → Vector field v : M → TM
nodes.description: The vector field v(x) = (d/dt)g^t(x)|_{t=0} whose integral curves are the phase curves of the flow, equivalently the right-hand side of ẋ = v(x).

nodes.name: Non-autonomous ODE
nodes.type_signature: (f : ℝ × M → TM) : ODE ẋ = f(t, x)
nodes.description: An ordinary differential equation ẋ = f(t, x) in which the right-hand side depends explicitly on time, reducible to an autonomous system on the extended phase space ℝ × M.

nodes.name: Direction field (line element field)
nodes.type_signature: (First-order ODE y' = f(x, y)) → Field of line elements in ℝ²
nodes.description: The field assigning to each point (x, y) the line through (x, y) with slope f(x, y), whose integral curves are the solutions of y' = f(x, y).

nodes.name: Solution by quadrature (Barrow's formula)
nodes.function_signature: (Scalar autonomous ODE ẋ = v(x)) → (Implicit solution via ∫dx/v(x) = t + C)
nodes.description: Solving a one-dimensional autonomous ODE ẋ = v(x) by direct integration: t − t₀ = ∫_{x₀}^{x} ds/v(s), the fundamental antiderivative method.

nodes.name: Separation of variables for ODEs
nodes.function_signature: (ODE of form dy/dx = f(x)g(y)) → (∫dy/g(y) = ∫f(x)dx + C)
nodes.description: Solving a first-order ODE dy/dx = f(x)g(y) by separating the variables and integrating each side independently.

nodes.name: Rectification theorem (flow box theorem)
nodes.type_signature: (v(x₀) ≠ 0, v smooth) ⟹ Local diffeomorphism straightening v to ∂/∂x₁
nodes.description: Near any non-singular point of a smooth vector field, there exists a local coordinate system in which the field equals the constant field ∂/∂x₁ and the flow is a translation.

nodes.name: Extension theorem for ODE solutions
nodes.type_signature: (Local Lipschitz ODE on open U) ⟹ Solution extends until it leaves every compact K ⊂ U
nodes.description: A solution of ẋ = f(t, x) on a maximal interval (α, β) with β < ∞ must eventually leave every compact subset of the domain; equivalently, bounded solutions on open domains extend to the boundary of the interval.

nodes.name: Differentiable dependence on initial conditions
nodes.type_signature: (f ∈ Cᵏ) ⟹ (Flow map x₀ ↦ φ(t; x₀) is Cᵏ)
nodes.description: If the right-hand side f of ẋ = f(t, x) is Cᵏ in (t, x), then the solution φ(t; t₀, x₀) is Cᵏ in the initial condition x₀, with the derivative satisfying the variational equation.

nodes.name: Superposition principle for linear ODE systems
nodes.type_signature: (Linear ODE ẋ = A(t)x, Solutions x₁,...,xₖ) ⟹ ∑cᵢxᵢ is a solution
nodes.description: Any linear combination of solutions of a homogeneous linear system ẋ = A(t)x is again a solution; the solution set forms a vector space of dimension n.

nodes.name: Wronskian
nodes.type_signature: (Solutions x₁,...,xₙ of linear ODE) → W(t) = det[x₁(t)|...|xₙ(t)]
nodes.description: The determinant of the matrix whose columns are n solutions of an n-dimensional linear system; nonzero at one point if and only if the solutions are linearly independent (form a fundamental system).

nodes.name: Quasi-polynomial
nodes.description: A function of the form p(t)e^{λt} where p is a polynomial, arising as a solution component of a constant-coefficient linear ODE when λ is an eigenvalue of multiplicity exceeding the polynomial degree plus one.

nodes.name: Complexification of a real linear operator
nodes.function_signature: (Real vector space V, Operator A : V → V) → (V_ℂ = V ⊗ ℂ, A_ℂ = A ⊗ id_ℂ)
nodes.description: Extending a real linear operator A to the complexified space V ⊗ ℂ to exploit the algebraic closure of ℂ, enabling diagonalization and spectral decomposition even when real eigenvalues do not exist.

nodes.name: Decomplexification (realification)
nodes.function_signature: (Complex eigenvalue λ = α + iβ, Complex eigenvector z) → (Real 2D invariant subspace, Rotation-dilation block)
nodes.description: Converting complex eigendata of a real operator back to real form: a conjugate pair λ, λ̄ with eigenvectors z, z̄ yields a real invariant 2-plane on which the operator acts as e^{αt}(cos βt · I + sin βt · J).

nodes.name: Stable node
nodes.type_signature: (2D linear system ẋ = Ax, eigenvalues λ₁ ≤ λ₂ < 0 real) : Equilibrium type
nodes.description: An equilibrium of a planar linear system where both eigenvalues are real and negative, so all trajectories approach the origin tangent to the eigenvector of the eigenvalue of larger absolute value.

nodes.name: Unstable node
nodes.type_signature: (2D linear system ẋ = Ax, eigenvalues 0 < λ₁ ≤ λ₂ real) : Equilibrium type
nodes.description: An equilibrium of a planar linear system where both eigenvalues are real and positive, so all trajectories recede from the origin; the time-reversal of a stable node.

nodes.name: Saddle point (planar linear system)
nodes.type_signature: (2D linear system ẋ = Ax, eigenvalues λ₁ < 0 < λ₂) : Equilibrium type
nodes.description: An equilibrium of a planar linear system with one positive and one negative real eigenvalue; the stable and unstable eigenspaces are invariant lines, and all other orbits are hyperbolas asymptotic to them.

nodes.name: Stable focus (spiral sink)
nodes.type_signature: (2D linear system ẋ = Ax, eigenvalues α ± iβ with α < 0) : Equilibrium type
nodes.description: An equilibrium of a planar linear system with complex conjugate eigenvalues having negative real part, so trajectories spiral inward toward the origin.

nodes.name: Unstable focus (spiral source)
nodes.type_signature: (2D linear system ẋ = Ax, eigenvalues α ± iβ with α > 0) : Equilibrium type
nodes.description: An equilibrium of a planar linear system with complex conjugate eigenvalues having positive real part, so trajectories spiral outward from the origin.

nodes.name: Center (elliptic equilibrium)
nodes.type_signature: (2D linear system ẋ = Ax, eigenvalues ±iβ, β ≠ 0) : Equilibrium type
nodes.description: An equilibrium of a planar linear system with purely imaginary eigenvalues, surrounded by a family of closed elliptical orbits; Lyapunov stable but not asymptotically stable.

nodes.name: Topological classification of planar linear systems
nodes.type_signature: (Two 2D linear systems ẋ = Ax, ẏ = By) ⟹ Topologically equivalent iff same type (node/saddle/focus/center)
nodes.description: Two non-degenerate planar linear systems are topologically equivalent (related by a homeomorphism sending orbits to orbits preserving orientation) if and only if they have the same qualitative type determined by the signs of eigenvalue real parts.

nodes.name: Stability of equilibrium of a linear system
nodes.type_signature: (Linear system ẋ = Ax) ⟹ (Stable iff Re(λᵢ) ≤ 0 with simple elementary divisors for Re(λᵢ)=0; asymptotically stable iff Re(λᵢ) < 0 for all i)
nodes.description: The equilibrium x = 0 of ẋ = Ax is Lyapunov stable if and only if all eigenvalues have non-positive real part and those on the imaginary axis have equal algebraic and geometric multiplicity, and asymptotically stable if and only if all eigenvalues have strictly negative real part.

nodes.name: Proof of differentiable dependence via Gronwall
nodes.function_signature: (Variational equation, Gronwall inequality) → (Cᵏ dependence of solutions on initial data)
nodes.description: Establishing that the difference quotient of the flow in the initial condition converges to the solution of the variational equation, using Gronwall's inequality to control the error.

nodes.name: Tangent vector
nodes.type_signature: (Smooth manifold M, Point p ∈ M) → v ∈ TₚM
nodes.description: An equivalence class of curves through p in a smooth manifold, or equivalently a derivation on the algebra of germs of smooth functions at p, representing an infinitesimal displacement at p.

nodes.name: Tangent space
nodes.type_signature: (Smooth manifold M, Point p ∈ M) → TₚM : n-dimensional real vector space
nodes.description: The vector space TₚM of all tangent vectors at a point p of an n-dimensional smooth manifold M, isomorphic to ℝⁿ via any chart.

nodes.name: One-parameter group of diffeomorphisms
nodes.type_signature: (Smooth manifold M) → Group homomorphism g : (ℝ, +) → Diff(M)
nodes.description: A smooth action g : ℝ × M → M such that each g^t is a diffeomorphism, g⁰ = id, and g^{s+t} = g^s ∘ g^t, equivalently a global flow on M.

nodes.name: Completeness of a vector field
nodes.description: A vector field is complete if every maximal integral curve is defined for all t ∈ ℝ, equivalently if it generates a global one-parameter group of diffeomorphisms.

nodes.name: Compactness implies completeness of vector fields
nodes.type_signature: (M compact, v smooth on M) ⟹ v is complete
nodes.description: Every smooth vector field on a compact manifold is complete: since solutions cannot escape a compact set, the extension theorem guarantees they exist for all time.

nodes.name: Lie bracket of vector fields
nodes.type_signature: (Vector fields X, Y on M) → [X, Y] : Vector field on M
nodes.description: The Lie bracket [X, Y] = XY − YX as derivations on C^∞(M), measuring the failure of the flows of X and Y to commute to second order.

nodes.name: Lie algebra of vector fields
nodes.description: The space 𝔛(M) of all smooth vector fields on M equipped with the Lie bracket, forming an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra over ℝ satisfying skew-symmetry and the Jacobi identity.

nodes.name: Commutativity of flows iff vanishing Lie bracket
nodes.type_signature: (Complete vector fields X, Y) ⟹ (Flows commute ⟺ [X, Y] = 0)
nodes.description: Two complete vector fields on a manifold have commuting flows (g^s_X ∘ g^t_Y = g^t_Y ∘ g^s_X for all s, t) if and only if their Lie bracket vanishes identically.

nodes.name: Lie derivative of a vector field
nodes.type_signature: (Vector fields X, Y on M) → L_X Y = [X, Y] : Vector field
nodes.description: The derivative of Y along the flow of X, defined as L_X Y = lim_{t→0} ((g^{-t}_*)Y − Y)/t, which equals the Lie bracket [X, Y].

nodes.name: Pushforward of a vector field by a diffeomorphism
nodes.type_signature: (Diffeomorphism φ : M → N, Vector field X on M) → φ_*X : Vector field on N
nodes.description: The image of a vector field X under a diffeomorphism φ, defined by (φ_*X)_{φ(p)} = dφ_p(X_p), giving the natural action of Diff(M) on 𝔛(M).

nodes.name: Linearization at an equilibrium
nodes.function_signature: (Nonlinear ODE ẋ = f(x), Equilibrium f(x₀) = 0) → (Linear system δx' = Df(x₀)·δx)
nodes.description: Replacing a nonlinear system by its first-order Taylor approximation at an equilibrium point to study local qualitative behavior, justified by the Hartman-Grobman theorem when the equilibrium is hyperbolic.

nodes.name: Lyapunov's indirect method (stability by linearization)
nodes.type_signature: (ẋ = f(x), f(0) = 0, A = Df(0)) ⟹ (Re(λᵢ(A)) < 0 ⟹ asymptotically stable; ∃ Re(λᵢ) > 0 ⟹ unstable)
nodes.description: If all eigenvalues of the Jacobian Df(0) have strictly negative real part, the equilibrium of the nonlinear system is asymptotically stable; if any eigenvalue has positive real part, it is unstable.

nodes.name: Periodic orbit
nodes.type_signature: (Autonomous ODE on M, Period T > 0) → γ = {φ(t; x₀) : 0 ≤ t < T} : Closed curve in M
nodes.description: A phase curve γ for which there exists a minimal T > 0 such that φ(t + T; x₀) = φ(t; x₀) for all t, forming a closed loop in phase space distinct from an equilibrium point.

nodes.name: Poincaré index of a singular point
nodes.type_signature: (Planar vector field v, Isolated singular point p) → ind_p(v) ∈ ℤ
nodes.description: The winding number of the vector field v around a simple closed curve enclosing an isolated singular point p, counting the number of full turns of v(x) as x traverses the curve counterclockwise.

nodes.name: Sturm-Liouville equation
nodes.description: A second-order linear ODE eigenvalue problem of the form −(p(x)y')' + q(x)y = λw(x)y with p > 0, w > 0, and prescribed boundary conditions, whose spectral theory yields orthogonal eigenfunction expansions.

nodes.name: Boundary value problem for second-order ODEs
nodes.type_signature: (ODE L[y] = f on [a,b], Conditions B_a[y] = α, B_b[y] = β) : BVP
nodes.description: The problem of finding a solution of a second-order ODE on an interval [a, b] subject to conditions imposed at both endpoints, in contrast to an initial value problem where all conditions are at one point.

nodes.name: Homoclinic orbit
nodes.type_signature: (Autonomous ODE, Equilibrium p) → γ : Orbit with α(γ) = ω(γ) = {p}
nodes.description: A non-equilibrium trajectory that is biasymptotic to the same equilibrium point, approaching it as t → +∞ and as t → −∞, lying in the intersection of the stable and unstable manifolds of p.

nodes.name: Heteroclinic orbit (saddle connection)
nodes.type_signature: (Autonomous ODE, Equilibria p ≠ q) → γ : Orbit with α(γ) = {p}, ω(γ) = {q}
nodes.description: A trajectory connecting two distinct equilibrium points, lying in the intersection of the unstable manifold of p and the stable manifold of q.

nodes.name: First integral (constant of motion)
nodes.type_signature: (ODE ẋ = v(x), Smooth function F : M → ℝ) : dF/dt ≡ 0 along solutions
nodes.description: A smooth function F that is constant along every solution trajectory, satisfying ∇F · v = 0, whose level sets are invariant under the flow and reduce the dimension of the system by one.

nodes.name: Invariance of ODE systems under coordinate changes
nodes.type_signature: (ODE ẋ = v(x), Diffeomorphism y = φ(x)) ⟹ ẏ = Dφ(φ⁻¹(y)) · v(φ⁻¹(y))
nodes.description: Under a smooth change of coordinates y = φ(x), the vector field v transforms by the pushforward φ_*v, showing that the qualitative theory of ODEs is intrinsic to the manifold structure and independent of coordinate choice.

nodes.name: Transport equation
nodes.description: The linear first-order PDE u_t + b · Du = 0 with velocity field b, whose solutions are constant along characteristic lines x(t) = x_0 + bt.

nodes.name: Classification of second-order linear PDEs
nodes.description: A second-order PDE Σ a_{ij} u_{x_ix_j} + ⋯ = 0 is elliptic if A is definite, parabolic if det A = 0 with rank n−1, and hyperbolic if A has signature (n−1,1).

nodes.name: Fundamental solution of the Laplace equation
nodes.description: The function Φ(x) = −(1/(n(n−2)α(n)))|x|^{2−n} for n ≥ 3 (Φ(x) = (1/(2π)) log|x| for n = 2) satisfying −ΔΦ = δ_0 in the distributional sense.

nodes.name: Poisson's formula for the ball
nodes.type_signature: (Continuous boundary data g on ∂B(0,r)) → (Harmonic function u on B(0,r))
nodes.description: The unique harmonic function in B(0,r) with boundary data g is u(x) = (r²−|x|²)/(nα(n)r) ∫_{∂B} g(y)/|x−y|^n dS(y), the convolution of g with the Poisson kernel.

nodes.name: Smoothness of harmonic functions
nodes.description: Every harmonic function u on an open set Ω is infinitely differentiable (in fact real-analytic) in Ω, as follows from the Poisson integral representation.

nodes.name: Derivative estimates for harmonic functions
nodes.description: If u is harmonic in B(x_0,r), then |D^α u(x_0)| ≤ C(n,|α|) r^{−n−|α|} ||u||_{L^1(B(x_0,r))} for each multi-index α.

nodes.name: Analyticity of harmonic functions
nodes.description: Every harmonic function u on an open set Ω is real-analytic: at each x_0 ∈ Ω, u equals its Taylor series in a neighborhood, as a consequence of the derivative estimates.

nodes.name: Infinite speed of propagation for the heat equation
nodes.description: If u solves u_t − Δu = 0 with compactly supported initial data u(·,0) = g ≥ 0, g ≢ 0, then u(x,t) > 0 for all x ∈ ℝ^n and t > 0.

nodes.name: Mean value property for the heat equation
nodes.type_signature: (u solving u_t − Δu = 0) → (Mean value over heat ball)
nodes.description: A solution of the heat equation satisfies u(x,t) = (1/(4r^n)) ∫∫_{E(x,t;r)} u(y,s) |x−y|²/(t−s)² dy ds over the heat ball E(x,t;r).

nodes.name: Strong maximum principle for the heat equation
nodes.type_signature: (u solving u_t − Δu ≤ 0 on Ω_T) → (Maximum on parabolic boundary)
nodes.description: If u attains its maximum at an interior point of the parabolic cylinder Ω_T, then u is constant on the connected component reachable by paths going backward in time.

nodes.name: Euler-Poisson-Darboux equation
nodes.description: The PDE U_{tt} + ((n−1)/t) U_t = U_{rr} satisfied by the spherical mean of a wave equation solution, reducing wave propagation to a singular 1D problem.

nodes.name: Finite speed of propagation for the wave equation
nodes.description: The solution of the wave equation at point (x,t) depends only on initial data in the backward cone {y : |x−y| ≤ ct}, so disturbances travel at most at speed c.

nodes.name: Domain of dependence for the wave equation
nodes.description: The domain of dependence of a point (x_0, t_0) for the wave equation u_tt = c²Δu is the closed ball B(x_0, ct_0) in the initial hyperplane t = 0.

nodes.name: Green's identities
nodes.description: First: ∫_Ω (Δu)v dx = −∫_Ω Du·Dv dx + ∫_{∂Ω} (∂u/∂ν)v dS. Second: ∫_Ω (uΔv − vΔu) dx = ∫_{∂Ω} (u ∂v/∂ν − v ∂u/∂ν) dS.

nodes.name: Characteristic equations for first-order PDEs
nodes.description: The ODE system ẋ = D_p F, ṗ = −D_x F − D_z F · p, ż = p · D_p F that defines the characteristic strips along which a first-order PDE reduces to ODEs.

nodes.name: Hamilton-Jacobi equation (PDE)
nodes.description: The PDE u_t + H(Du, x) = 0 for t > 0 with initial data u(x,0) = g(x), where H is the Hamiltonian; a fundamental equation linking optimal control, calculus of variations, and conservation laws.

nodes.name: Hopf-Lax formula
nodes.type_signature: (H convex, g Lipschitz) → (Viscosity solution of HJ)
nodes.description: The function u(x,t) = min_y [tL((x−y)/t) + g(y)] where L = H* is the Legendre transform of H, gives the unique viscosity solution of u_t + H(Du) = 0.

nodes.name: Scalar conservation law
nodes.description: The PDE u_t + F(u)_x = 0 for a scalar unknown u and flux function F, modeling transport with nonlinear wave speeds F'(u).

nodes.name: Weak solution of a conservation law
nodes.description: A bounded measurable function u satisfying ∫∫ [u φ_t + F(u) φ_x] dx dt + ∫ g φ(x,0) dx = 0 for all test functions φ ∈ C^1_c, allowing discontinuous (shock) solutions.

nodes.name: Lax entropy condition
nodes.type_signature: (Shock with left state u_l, right state u_r, speed s) → Bool
nodes.description: A shock is admissible if the characteristics impinge on it: F'(u_l) > s > F'(u_r), selecting the physically relevant weak solution among multiple possibilities.

nodes.name: Entropy/entropy-flux pair
nodes.description: A pair (η, q) with η convex and q' = η' F' such that entropy solutions of u_t + F(u)_x = 0 satisfy η(u)_t + q(u)_x ≤ 0 in the distributional sense.

nodes.name: Lax-Oleinik formula
nodes.type_signature: (Convex F, L^∞ initial data g) → (Entropy solution)
nodes.description: An explicit minimization formula giving the entropy solution of the scalar conservation law u_t + F(u)_x = 0 with convex flux, analogous to the Hopf-Lax formula for Hamilton-Jacobi equations.

nodes.name: Rarefaction wave
nodes.description: A continuous self-similar weak solution u(x,t) = v(x/t) of a conservation law connecting two constant states, existing when the characteristic speed is monotone across the wave fan.

nodes.name: Formation of singularities for first-order PDEs
nodes.type_signature: (Smooth initial data with compressive characteristics) → (Gradient blowup in finite time)
nodes.description: For the conservation law u_t + F(u)_x = 0 with F'' > 0, if g'(x_0) < 0 at some point, then Du blows up at time T* = −1/min(F''(g) g'), forming a shock.

nodes.name: Hopf-Cole transformation
nodes.function_signature: (Burgers equation u_t + u u_x = ε u_xx) → (Heat equation via w = e^{−u/(2ε)})
nodes.description: The substitution u = −2ε (w_x/w) transforms the viscous Burgers equation into the linear heat equation w_t = ε w_xx, yielding an explicit solution formula.

nodes.name: Similarity solutions (self-similar reduction)
nodes.function_signature: (PDE with scaling symmetry) → (ODE for profile function)
nodes.description: Seeking solutions of the form u(x,t) = t^α f(x/t^β) reduces a PDE to an ODE for the profile f, exploiting the scaling invariance of the equation.

nodes.name: Sobolev conjugate exponent
nodes.description: The critical exponent p* = np/(n−p) such that W^{1,p}(ℝ^n) embeds into L^{p*}(ℝ^n), the largest Lebesgue exponent achievable by the Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev inequality.

nodes.name: Trace zero characterization of W^{1,p}_0
nodes.description: For Ω with C^1 boundary and 1 ≤ p < ∞, a function u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) belongs to W^{1,p}_0(Ω) if and only if its trace Tu vanishes on ∂Ω.

nodes.name: Difference quotient characterization of Sobolev spaces
nodes.type_signature: (u ∈ L^p(Ω)) → (u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) iff ||D_h u||_{Lp} ≤ C uniformly)
nodes.description: A function u ∈ L^p(Ω) belongs to W^{1,p}(Ω) (1 < p ≤ ∞) if and only if its difference quotients D_h^i u are uniformly bounded in L^p.

nodes.name: General Sobolev inequalities (higher order)
nodes.description: For u ∈ W^{k,p}(ℝ^n): if kp < n then W^{k,p} ↪ L^{np/(n−kp)}; if kp > n then W^{k,p} ↪ C^{j,α}; with appropriate j, α depending on n, k, p.

nodes.name: Negative Sobolev space W^{−k,p'}(Ω)
nodes.description: The dual space (W^{k,p}_0(Ω))*, consisting of distributions f representable as f = Σ_{|α|≤k} D^α f_α with f_α ∈ L^{p'}, the natural space for right-hand sides of elliptic PDEs.

nodes.name: Interpolation inequalities for Sobolev spaces
nodes.type_signature: (u ∈ W^{k,p}(Ω), 0 ≤ j < k) → (||D^j u||_{L^q} controlled by ||D^k u|| and ||u||)
nodes.description: Intermediate derivatives are controlled by interpolation: ||D^j u||_q ≤ ε||D^k u||_p + C(ε)||u||_r for suitable exponents, relating intermediate to highest and lowest order terms.

nodes.name: Campanato space L^{p,λ}(Ω)
nodes.description: The space of L^p functions u with sup_{x,r} r^{−λ} ∫_{B(x,r)∩Ω} |u − u_{x,r}|^p dy < ∞; for λ ∈ (n, n+p], Campanato's theorem identifies L^{p,λ} with C^{0,(λ−n)/p}.

nodes.name: Campanato's characterization of Hölder spaces
nodes.description: The Campanato space L^{p,λ}(Ω) is isomorphic to C^{0,α}(Ω) with α = (λ−n)/p when n < λ ≤ n+p, providing an integral characterization of Hölder continuity.

nodes.name: Uniform ellipticity condition
nodes.description: A second-order operator Lu = −Σ(a^{ij} u_{x_i})_{x_j} + lower order is uniformly elliptic if θ|ξ|² ≤ Σ a^{ij}(x)ξ_iξ_j ≤ Θ|ξ|² for all x ∈ Ω, ξ ∈ ℝ^n.

nodes.name: Bilinear form B[u,v] for elliptic operator
nodes.description: The bilinear form B[u,v] = ∫_Ω [a^{ij} u_{x_i} v_{x_j} + b^i u_{x_i} v + cuv] dx associated to a divergence-form elliptic operator, encoding the weak formulation Lu = f.

nodes.name: Interior H^2 regularity for elliptic equations
nodes.type_signature: (u ∈ H^1(Ω) weak solution of Lu = f ∈ L^2) → (u ∈ H^2_loc(Ω))
nodes.description: If u ∈ H^1(Ω) weakly solves Lu = f with f ∈ L^2 and smooth coefficients, then u ∈ H^2_loc(Ω) with ||u||_{H^2(V)} ≤ C(||f||_{L^2} + ||u||_{L^2}) for V ⋐ Ω.

nodes.name: Boundary H^2 regularity for elliptic equations
nodes.description: If Ω has C^2 boundary and u ∈ H^1_0(Ω) weakly solves Lu = f ∈ L^2, then u ∈ H^2(Ω) with ||u||_{H^2} ≤ C(||f||_{L^2} + ||u||_{L^2}).

nodes.name: Elliptic regularity bootstrapping
nodes.function_signature: (u ∈ H^1 solving Lu = f ∈ H^m, smooth coefficients) → (u ∈ H^{m+2})
nodes.description: Iteratively applying regularity estimates: if f ∈ H^m and coefficients are C^∞, then u ∈ H^{m+2}_loc, and inducting gives u ∈ C^∞ when f ∈ C^∞.

nodes.name: Weak maximum principle for elliptic equations in divergence form
nodes.type_signature: (Lu ≤ 0 in Ω, c ≥ 0) → (sup_Ω u ≤ sup_{∂Ω} u^+)
nodes.description: If u ∈ H^1(Ω) satisfies B[u,v] ≤ 0 for all v ≥ 0 in H^1_0(Ω), then sup_Ω u ≤ sup_{∂Ω} u^+, where boundary values are in the trace sense.

nodes.name: Strong maximum principle for elliptic equations in divergence form
nodes.type_signature: (Lu ≤ 0 in connected Ω, c = 0) → (u ≡ const or u < sup u in Ω)
nodes.description: If u ∈ H^1(Ω) ∩ C(Ω̄) is a subsolution of Lu = 0 in a connected domain with c = 0, and u attains its maximum at an interior point, then u is constant.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue theory for symmetric elliptic operators
nodes.type_signature: (L symmetric uniformly elliptic, Ω bounded) → (Discrete spectrum 0 < λ_1 ≤ λ_2 ≤ ⋯ → ∞)
nodes.description: The eigenvalue problem Lu = λu in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω has a countable sequence of eigenvalues 0 < λ_1 ≤ λ_2 ≤ ⋯ → ∞ with eigenfunctions forming an orthonormal basis of L^2.

nodes.name: Principal eigenvalue of an elliptic operator
nodes.description: The smallest eigenvalue λ_1 of −L on H^1_0(Ω), characterized by λ_1 = min{B[u,u]/||u||²_{L^2} : u ∈ H^1_0, u ≠ 0}, with a corresponding eigenfunction of one sign.

nodes.name: Energy estimates for elliptic PDEs
nodes.description: From coercivity B[u,u] ≥ α||u||²_{H^1_0} and the Poincaré inequality, the weak solution satisfies ||u||_{H^1_0} ≤ C||f||_{H^{-1}}, the fundamental a priori estimate.

nodes.name: Parabolic cylinder
nodes.description: The space-time domain Ω_T = Ω × (0,T] with parabolic boundary ∂_p Ω_T = (∂Ω × [0,T]) ∪ (Ω × {0}), the natural domain for parabolic initial-boundary value problems.

nodes.name: Weak solution of a parabolic PDE
nodes.description: A function u satisfying ⟨u',v⟩ + B[u,v;t] = ⟨f,v⟩ for a.e. t and all v ∈ H^1_0(Ω), with u(0) = g, the distributional formulation of u_t + Lu = f.

nodes.name: Existence of weak solutions for parabolic equations
nodes.type_signature: (f ∈ L^2(0,T; H^{-1}), g ∈ L^2(Ω)) → (Unique weak solution u)
nodes.description: For u_t + Lu = f with L uniformly elliptic, there exists a unique weak solution u ∈ L^2(0,T; H^1_0) with u' ∈ L^2(0,T; H^{-1}), proved by Galerkin approximation and energy estimates.

nodes.name: Energy estimates for parabolic equations
nodes.type_signature: (u weak solution of u_t + Lu = f) → (a priori bound on ||u||)
nodes.description: Testing u_t + Lu = f against u and using coercivity and Gronwall gives sup_{t} ||u||²_{L^2} + ∫ ||Du||²_{L^2} ≤ C(||g||²_{L^2} + ||f||²_{L^2(H^{-1})}).

nodes.name: Parabolic regularity
nodes.type_signature: (u weak solution, smooth data) → (u smooth for t > 0)
nodes.description: If f and coefficients are smooth and ∂Ω is smooth, the weak solution of u_t + Lu = f satisfies u ∈ C^∞(Ω × (0,T]); proved by difference quotients, energy estimates, and bootstrapping.

nodes.name: Weak maximum principle for parabolic equations
nodes.type_signature: (u_t + Lu ≤ 0 in Ω_T) → (sup_{Ω_T} u ≤ sup_{∂_p Ω_T} u^+)
nodes.description: A subsolution of u_t + Lu = 0 in the parabolic cylinder Ω_T attains its maximum on the parabolic boundary ∂_p Ω_T.

nodes.name: Strong maximum principle for parabolic equations
nodes.type_signature: (u_t + Lu ≤ 0, max at interior (x_0,t_0)) → (u ≡ const for t ≤ t_0)
nodes.description: If a subsolution of u_t + Lu = 0 attains its maximum at an interior space-time point (x_0,t_0), then u is constant on Ω × (0,t_0].

nodes.name: Lions-Magenes lemma
nodes.description: If V ↪ H ↪ V* is an evolution triple and u ∈ L^2(0,T; V) with u' ∈ L^2(0,T; V*), then u ∈ C([0,T]; H) with the energy equality d/dt ||u||²_H = 2⟨u',u⟩.

nodes.name: Weak solution of a second-order hyperbolic PDE
nodes.description: A function u satisfying ⟨u'',v⟩ + B[u,v;t] = ⟨f,v⟩ for a.e. t and all v ∈ H^1_0(Ω), with u(0) = g ∈ H^1_0 and u'(0) = h ∈ L^2.

nodes.name: Existence of weak solutions for hyperbolic equations
nodes.type_signature: (f ∈ L^2(Ω_T), g ∈ H^1_0, h ∈ L^2) → (Unique weak solution u)
nodes.description: For u_tt + Lu = f with L symmetric uniformly elliptic, there exists a unique weak solution, proved by Galerkin approximation and hyperbolic energy estimates.

nodes.name: Energy estimates for hyperbolic equations
nodes.type_signature: (u solving u_tt + Lu = f) → (Bound on kinetic + potential energy)
nodes.description: Testing u_tt + Lu = f against u_t and applying Gronwall gives ||u'||²_{L^2} + B[u,u] ≤ C(||h||² + B[g,g] + ||f||²), controlling the solution.

nodes.name: Finite speed of propagation for general hyperbolic equations
nodes.type_signature: (u_tt + Lu = f, L uniformly elliptic) → (Finite domain of influence)
nodes.description: For general second-order hyperbolic equations, the domain of influence of initial data on a set S is contained in a cone, proved by energy estimates in truncated cones.

nodes.name: Quasiconvexity (Morrey)
nodes.description: L is quasiconvex if ∫_D L(A + Dφ) dx ≥ |D| L(A) for all bounded D, matrix A, and φ ∈ W^{1,∞}_0(D; ℝ^m); the natural convexity condition for weak lower semicontinuity in vector-valued problems.

nodes.name: Polyconvexity (Ball)
nodes.description: L(A) = g(A, adj₂A, …, det A) for some convex g of all minors; implies quasiconvexity and is verifiable, applicable in nonlinear elasticity.

nodes.name: Weak lower semicontinuity of integral functionals
nodes.type_signature: (L convex in Du, u_k ⇀ u in W^{1,p}) → (∫L(Du) ≤ liminf ∫L(Du_k))
nodes.description: If L(x,z,p) is convex in p and satisfies growth conditions, then I[u] = ∫ L(x,u,Du) dx is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous on W^{1,p}.

nodes.name: Null Lagrangian
nodes.description: A Lagrangian L for which ∫ L(Du) dx depends only on boundary values of u; equivalently, L is both quasiconvex and quasiconcave, consisting of linear combinations of minors of Du.

nodes.name: Regularity of minimizers in the calculus of variations
nodes.type_signature: (Minimizer u of ∫L(Du) dx, L uniformly convex and smooth) → (u ∈ C^∞)
nodes.description: If L is smooth and uniformly convex (D²_{pp} L ≥ θI), any minimizer u ∈ H^1(Ω) of I[u] = ∫ L(Du) dx is smooth in the interior.

nodes.name: Minimax methods for critical points
nodes.function_signature: (C^1 functional I on Banach space, saddle geometry) → (Critical point at minimax level c)
nodes.description: Finding critical points by characterizing critical values as c = inf_{A∈Γ} max_{u∈A} I(u) over a suitable class Γ, combining deformation lemmas with topological linking conditions.

nodes.name: Deformation lemma
nodes.type_signature: (C^1 functional I, no critical values in [a,b]) → (Sublevel set deformation retract)
nodes.description: If I ∈ C^1(X,ℝ) has no critical values in [c−ε, c+ε], the sublevel set {I ≤ c+ε} can be continuously deformed into {I ≤ c−ε} via the negative gradient flow.

nodes.name: Convexity conditions on the Lagrangian
nodes.description: The hierarchy convex ⟹ polyconvex ⟹ quasiconvex ⟹ rank-one convex for integrands L(x,z,p) in the calculus of variations; convexity in p ensures weak lower semicontinuity.

nodes.name: Direct method of the calculus of variations
nodes.function_signature: (Coercive, weakly l.s.c. functional I on reflexive W^{1,p}) → (Existence of minimizer)
nodes.description: Taking a minimizing sequence, extracting a weakly convergent subsequence by coercivity and reflexivity, then showing the limit is a minimizer by weak lower semicontinuity.

nodes.name: Method of sub- and supersolutions
nodes.function_signature: (Subsolution u_− ≤ supersolution u_+ of −Δu = f(u)) → (Existence of u with u_− ≤ u ≤ u_+)
nodes.description: If u_− ≤ u_+ satisfy −Δu_− ≤ f(u_−) and −Δu_+ ≥ f(u_+), then there exists a solution u with u_− ≤ u ≤ u_+, via monotone iteration or fixed-point arguments.

nodes.name: Moser iteration technique
nodes.function_signature: (Weak subsolution u of Lu ≤ 0 in divergence form) → (L^∞ bound on u)
nodes.description: Testing the equation against u^{p−1} for increasing p and using Sobolev embedding to bootstrap integrability iteratively: ||u||_{L^∞} ≤ C||u||_{L^2}.

nodes.name: Stampacchia truncation method
nodes.function_signature: (Weak solution u of elliptic PDE) → (L^∞ estimate via level sets)
nodes.description: Testing against (u−k)_+ to bound the measure of superlevel sets {u > k}, iterating De Giorgi-style to obtain L^∞ bounds from L^2 data.

nodes.name: Leray-Schauder fixed point theorem
nodes.type_signature: (T compact, a priori bound on σT fixed points) → (T has fixed point)
nodes.description: If T : X → X is compact and {u : u = σTu for σ ∈ [0,1]} is bounded, then T has a fixed point; a nonlinear generalization of Schauder's theorem via topological degree.

nodes.name: Comparison principle for viscosity solutions
nodes.type_signature: (u subsolution, v supersolution) → (u ≤ v on ∂Ω implies u ≤ v on Ω)
nodes.description: If u is a viscosity subsolution and v a supersolution of F(D²u,Du,u,x) = 0 with u ≤ v on ∂Ω, then u ≤ v in Ω; proved by doubling of variables.

nodes.name: Doubling of variables technique
nodes.function_signature: (Viscosity sub- and supersolutions u, v) → (Comparison u ≤ v)
nodes.description: Introducing Φ(x,y) = u(x) − v(y) − |x−y|²/(2ε) and analyzing its maximum as ε → 0 to transfer viscosity conditions to the same test point.

nodes.name: Dynamic programming principle (Bellman)
nodes.type_signature: (Optimal control problem) → (Value function satisfies HJ equation)
nodes.description: The value function V(x,t) = inf_α ∫_t^T L(y,α) ds + g(y(T)) satisfies the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation V_t + H(DV,x) = 0, connecting optimal control to PDE theory.

nodes.name: Stability of viscosity solutions
nodes.type_signature: (u_ε viscosity solutions, u_ε → u locally uniformly) → (u viscosity solution of limit equation)
nodes.description: If u_ε → u locally uniformly and H_ε → H, then u is a viscosity solution of the limiting equation; the viscosity framework is designed for this stability property.

nodes.name: Hopf-Lax formula gives the viscosity solution
nodes.type_signature: (Hopf-Lax formula) → (Unique viscosity solution of u_t + H(Du) = 0)
nodes.description: The Hopf-Lax formula gives the unique viscosity solution of u_t + H(Du) = 0, u(·,0) = g, establishing the connection between the explicit formula and the viscosity framework.

nodes.name: Vanishing viscosity method
nodes.function_signature: (First-order PDE F(Du,u) = 0) → (Solve εΔu + F = 0, let ε → 0)
nodes.description: Approximating a first-order PDE by adding εΔu, solving the parabolic problem, and passing ε → 0 to obtain a viscosity/entropy solution of the original equation.

nodes.name: System of conservation laws
nodes.description: The system U_t + F(U)_x = 0 for U : ℝ × [0,∞) → ℝ^m with flux F : ℝ^m → ℝ^m, generalizing scalar conservation laws to vector-valued unknowns.

nodes.name: Strict hyperbolicity
nodes.description: A system of conservation laws is strictly hyperbolic if the Jacobian DF(U) has m distinct real eigenvalues λ_1(U) < ⋯ < λ_m(U) for all U.

nodes.name: Genuine nonlinearity
nodes.description: The k-th characteristic field (λ_k, r_k) is genuinely nonlinear if Dλ_k · r_k ≠ 0 for all U, so wave speed varies monotonically across rarefactions.

nodes.name: Linear degeneracy
nodes.description: The k-th characteristic field (λ_k, r_k) is linearly degenerate if Dλ_k · r_k = 0 for all U; waves propagate as contact discontinuities rather than shocks or rarefactions.

nodes.name: Contact discontinuity
nodes.description: A discontinuity across which the characteristic speed equals the propagation speed (λ_k = s), occurring in linearly degenerate fields of a conservation law system.

nodes.name: Lax's theorem on the Riemann problem
nodes.type_signature: (Strictly hyperbolic system, U_L close to U_R) → (Solution as m elementary waves)
nodes.description: For a strictly hyperbolic system with each field genuinely nonlinear or linearly degenerate, the Riemann problem with U_L close to U_R has a unique solution of m waves.

nodes.name: Glimm's random choice method
nodes.function_signature: (System of conservation laws, small BV data) → (Global entropy solution)
nodes.description: Solving local Riemann problems on a staggered grid and randomly sampling the solution, converging to a global weak solution when the total variation of initial data is small.

nodes.name: Glimm interaction functional
nodes.description: The functional Q(t) = Σ |σ_α||σ_β| over approaching wave pairs, whose decrease at interactions compensates total variation increase, ensuring convergence of Glimm's scheme.

nodes.name: Existence of global entropy solutions (Glimm's theorem)
nodes.type_signature: (Strictly hyperbolic system, small TV data) → (Global BV entropy solution)
nodes.description: For strictly hyperbolic conservation systems with small total variation initial data, Glimm's scheme converges to a global entropy solution in BV.

nodes.name: Rankine-Hugoniot condition for systems
nodes.type_signature: (Shock speed s, states U_L, U_R) → s[U] = [F(U)]
nodes.description: For U_t + F(U)_x = 0, a discontinuity at speed s satisfies s(U_R − U_L) = F(U_R) − F(U_L), the conservation condition across the shock.

nodes.name: Lax entropy condition for systems
nodes.description: A k-shock is admissible if λ_k(U_L) > s > λ_k(U_R) and λ_{k−1}(U_L) < s < λ_{k+1}(U_R), ensuring exactly one family of characteristics enters from each side.

nodes.name: Simple waves (rarefaction waves) for systems
nodes.description: A continuous self-similar solution U(ξ) with U' parallel to r_k(U) and ξ = λ_k(U(ξ)); exists for genuinely nonlinear fields in strictly hyperbolic systems.

nodes.name: Young measures
nodes.type_signature: (Bounded sequence u_j in L^∞) → (Parametrized probability measures ν_x)
nodes.description: A family of probability measures {ν_x} such that for continuous f, f(u_j) ⇀ ∫ f(λ) dν_x(λ) weakly-*, encoding oscillation behavior of weakly convergent sequences.

nodes.name: Tartar's compensated compactness framework
nodes.function_signature: (Approximate solutions with PDE constraints + entropy) → (Strong convergence)
nodes.description: Combining the div-curl lemma with entropy conditions to show Young measures are Dirac masses, proving strong convergence of vanishing viscosity approximations.

nodes.name: Local existence for semilinear wave equations
nodes.type_signature: (u_tt − Δu = f(u), data ∈ H^s × H^{s−1}) → (Local solution in C([0,T]; H^s))
nodes.description: For u_tt − Δu = f(u) with smooth f and Sobolev data with s > n/2, there exists a unique local solution, proved by fixed-point iteration in Sobolev spaces.

nodes.name: Global existence for small data (semilinear wave)
nodes.type_signature: (u_tt − Δu = |u|^p, small data, p > p_c(n)) → (Global solution)
nodes.description: For u_tt − Δu = |u|^p with p above the Strauss exponent p_c(n) and sufficiently small initial data, the solution exists globally in time.

nodes.name: Blow-up in finite time for semilinear wave equations
nodes.description: For u_tt − Δu = |u|^{p−1}u with suitable data and subcritical exponent, the solution blows up in finite time; proved by energy/virial arguments or Levine's concavity method.

nodes.name: Levine's concavity method for blow-up
nodes.function_signature: (Energy functional, concavity of ||u||²) → (Finite-time blow-up)
nodes.description: Setting F(t) = ||u(t)||² and showing F'' ≥ c(F')^{1+δ} or that 1/F is concave, proving F → ∞ in finite time.

nodes.name: Strauss conjecture (critical exponent for semilinear wave)
nodes.type_signature: (u_tt − Δu = |u|^p in ℝ^n) → Critical exponent p_c(n)
nodes.description: The critical power p_c(n) is the positive root of (n−1)p² − (n+1)p − 2 = 0; for p > p_c small-data global existence holds, for 1 < p ≤ p_c blow-up occurs.

nodes.name: Bochner space L^p(0,T; X)
nodes.description: The space of strongly measurable functions u : (0,T) → X with ∫_0^T ||u(t)||_X^p dt < ∞, the natural setting for time-dependent PDE solutions valued in Sobolev spaces.

nodes.name: Evolution triple (Gelfand triple)
nodes.description: A triple V ⊂ H ⊂ V* with V reflexive Banach densely embedded in Hilbert H; the standard framework for weak solutions of parabolic PDEs (e.g., H^1_0 ⊂ L^2 ⊂ H^{-1}).

nodes.name: Hölder space C^{k,γ}(Ω̄)
nodes.description: The Banach space of functions with continuous derivatives up to order k whose k-th derivatives are γ-Hölder continuous, with norm ||u||_{C^{k,γ}} = Σ_{|α|≤k} ||D^α u||_∞ + Σ_{|α|=k} [D^α u]_γ.

nodes.name: Duhamel's principle
nodes.function_signature: (Homogeneous solution operator S(t), source f) → (u(t) = S(t)g + ∫_0^t S(t−s)f(s) ds)
nodes.description: Representing the solution of an inhomogeneous linear evolution equation as the homogeneous solution plus a source convolution, the continuous analogue of variation of parameters.

nodes.name: Solution of Poisson's equation via Newtonian potential
nodes.description: The convolution u(x) = ∫ Φ(x−y) f(y) dy with the fundamental solution Φ of Laplace's equation solves −Δu = f in ℝ^n.

nodes.name: Energy methods for the wave equation
nodes.function_signature: (u solving u_tt − Δu = f) → (Conservation of E(t) = ½∫ |u_t|² + |Du|² dx)
nodes.description: Multiplying u_tt − Δu = f by u_t and integrating yields dE/dt = ∫ f u_t dx; E is conserved when f = 0, giving uniqueness and continuous dependence.

nodes.name: Open subset Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ
nodes.description: An open subset of ℝⁿ serving as the domain for test functions and distributions.

nodes.name: Multi-index notation
nodes.description: An n-tuple α = (α₁,…,αₙ) of non-negative integers with |α| = α₁+⋯+αₙ, Dᵅ = ∂^|α|/(∂x₁^α₁⋯∂xₙ^αₙ), and α! = α₁!⋯αₙ!, the notational framework for PDE theory.

nodes.name: Smooth functions C^∞(Ω)
nodes.description: The space of infinitely differentiable functions on Ω with the topology of uniform convergence of all derivatives on compact subsets.

nodes.name: Test function space C^∞_c(Ω) = 𝒟(Ω)
nodes.description: The space of smooth functions with compact support in Ω, topologized as the strict inductive limit of Fréchet spaces C^∞_K(Ω) over compact exhaustions K ⋐ Ω.

nodes.name: Strict inductive limit topology on 𝒟(Ω)
nodes.description: φⱼ → φ in 𝒟(Ω) iff there exists K ⋐ Ω with supp φⱼ ⊂ K for all j and Dᵅφⱼ → Dᵅφ uniformly for every α; this makes 𝒟(Ω) a non-metrizable locally convex space.

nodes.name: Smooth partition of unity
nodes.description: A locally finite family of non-negative smooth functions {ψᵢ} subordinate to an open cover, with ∑ψᵢ ≡ 1 on Ω; exists because ℝⁿ is paracompact and admits smooth cutoffs.

nodes.name: Smooth cutoff function
nodes.type_signature: (K ⊂ U open) → χ ∈ C^∞_c(U) with χ ≡ 1 near K
nodes.description: A smooth function identically 1 on a neighborhood of a compact set K and compactly supported in U, constructed by mollifying characteristic functions.

nodes.name: Standard mollifier (Friedrich's mollifier)
nodes.description: The function ρ_ε(x) = ε⁻ⁿρ(x/ε) where ρ(x) = c·exp(−1/(1−|x|²)) for |x| < 1, ρ = 0 for |x| ≥ 1, with ∫ρ = 1; convolution with ρ_ε provides smooth approximation.

nodes.name: Mollification (Friedrich's smoothing)
nodes.function_signature: (f locally integrable on Ω, ε > 0) → f ∗ ρ_ε ∈ C^∞(Ω_ε)
nodes.description: Convolving a locally integrable function with a smooth compactly supported approximate identity ρ_ε to produce a smooth approximation converging to f in L^p_{loc} and pointwise a.e.

nodes.name: Distribution u ∈ 𝒟'(Ω)
nodes.description: A continuous linear functional on the test function space 𝒟(Ω); equivalently, a linear form u such that for every K ⋐ Ω there exist C, N with |⟨u,φ⟩| ≤ C ∑_{|α|≤N} sup|Dᵅφ| for supp φ ⊂ K.

nodes.name: Regular distribution (L¹_loc ↪ 𝒟')
nodes.description: The embedding f ↦ u_f defined by ⟨u_f, φ⟩ = ∫f φ dx, which is injective and identifies L¹_loc(Ω) with a subspace of 𝒟'(Ω); regular distributions have order 0.

nodes.name: Distributions of compact support ℰ'(Ω)
nodes.description: The space ℰ'(Ω) = {u ∈ 𝒟'(Ω) : supp u compact}, canonically identified with the topological dual of C^∞(Ω); every u ∈ ℰ' has finite order.

nodes.name: Sheaf property of distributions
nodes.type_signature: 𝒟' is a flabby sheaf on ℝⁿ
nodes.description: If u_i ∈ 𝒟'(Ω_i) agree on overlaps Ω_i ∩ Ω_j, then there exists a unique u ∈ 𝒟'(⋃Ω_i) restricting to each u_i; proved using partitions of unity.

nodes.name: Fundamental solution of a differential operator
nodes.type_signature: P(D) constant-coefficient operator → E ∈ 𝒟'(ℝⁿ) with P(D)E = δ
nodes.description: A distribution E satisfying P(D)E = δ, so that P(D)(E ∗ f) = f for f ∈ ℰ'(ℝⁿ), providing a right inverse for P(D) via convolution.

nodes.name: Leibniz rule for distributions
nodes.description: Dᵅ(au) = ∑_{β≤α} (α choose β)(Dᵝa)(D^{α−β}u) for smooth a and distributional u, extending the classical product rule.

nodes.name: Derivative of the Heaviside function
nodes.description: The distributional derivative of the Heaviside step function H(x) = 1_{x>0} is the Dirac delta: ⟨H', φ⟩ = −⟨H, φ'⟩ = −∫₀^∞ φ' dx = φ(0).

nodes.name: Division of distributions by smooth functions
nodes.type_signature: (a ∈ C^∞(Ω), u ∈ 𝒟'(Ω)) → solutions of av = u
nodes.description: The equation a·v = u for v ∈ 𝒟'(Ω) given smooth a; solvable when a has only zeros of finite order, yielding solutions modulo distributions supported on {a = 0}.

nodes.name: Principal value distribution p.v.(1/x)
nodes.description: The distribution ⟨p.v.(1/x), φ⟩ = lim_{ε→0} ∫_{|x|>ε} φ(x)/x dx, an order-1 distribution that extends 1/x across the origin; satisfies x · p.v.(1/x) = 1.

nodes.name: Structure theorem for distributions
nodes.type_signature: u ∈ 𝒟'(Ω) → locally u = ∑ Dᵅ f_α with f_α continuous
nodes.description: Every distribution is locally a finite sum of derivatives of continuous functions: for each K ⋐ Ω, u|_K = ∑_{|α|≤N} Dᵅf_α with f_α ∈ C⁰(K), where N is the local order.

nodes.name: Structure theorem for ℰ'(ℝⁿ)
nodes.type_signature: u ∈ ℰ'(ℝⁿ) → u = ∑ Dᵅ f_α globally
nodes.description: Every distribution of compact support is a finite sum of derivatives of compactly supported continuous functions: u = ∑_{|α|≤N} Dᵅf_α with f_α ∈ C_c⁰(ℝⁿ).

nodes.name: Distributions supported at a point
nodes.type_signature: supp u = {a} → u = ∑ c_α Dᵅδ_a (finite sum)
nodes.description: A distribution supported at a single point a is a finite linear combination of the Dirac delta and its derivatives at a: u = ∑_{|α|≤N} c_α Dᵅδ_a.

nodes.name: Convolution algebra ℰ'(ℝⁿ)
nodes.description: ℰ'(ℝⁿ) equipped with convolution is an associative algebra with unit δ; satisfies supp(u∗v) ⊂ supp u + supp v and sing supp(u∗v) ⊂ sing supp u + sing supp v.

nodes.name: Convolution support theorem
nodes.type_signature: supp(u ∗ v) ⊂ supp u + supp v
nodes.description: The support of a convolution is contained in the Minkowski sum of the supports; more refined: ch(supp(u∗v)) ⊂ ch(supp u) + ch(supp v) where ch denotes convex hull.

nodes.name: Singular support of a convolution
nodes.type_signature: sing supp(u ∗ v) ⊂ sing supp u + sing supp v
nodes.description: The singular support of u ∗ v is contained in the Minkowski sum of the singular supports, provided the convolution is defined.

nodes.name: Regularization of distributions by convolution
nodes.type_signature: (u ∈ 𝒟'(ℝⁿ), φ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝⁿ)) → u ∗ φ ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ)
nodes.description: Convolution of any distribution with a test function yields a smooth function: u ∗ φ ∈ C^∞ with (u ∗ φ)(x) = ⟨u, φ(x − ·)⟩, and D^α(u ∗ φ) = (D^α u) ∗ φ = u ∗ (D^α φ).

nodes.name: Density of C^∞_c in 𝒟'
nodes.type_signature: u ∈ 𝒟'(Ω) → u = lim u ∗ ρ_ε in 𝒟'
nodes.description: Every distribution is the limit of smooth functions: u ∗ ρ_ε → u in 𝒟'(Ω) as ε → 0, where ρ_ε is a mollifier; more precisely, C^∞_c(Ω) is sequentially dense in 𝒟'(Ω).

nodes.name: Regularization by convolution with mollifier
nodes.description: Approximating distributions by smooth functions via convolution with a mollifier; fundamental tool for transferring pointwise arguments to distributional settings.

nodes.name: Tensor product of distributions
nodes.type_signature: (u ∈ 𝒟'(Ω₁), v ∈ 𝒟'(Ω₂)) → u ⊗ v ∈ 𝒟'(Ω₁ × Ω₂)
nodes.description: The unique distribution u ⊗ v on the product satisfying ⟨u ⊗ v, φ ⊗ ψ⟩ = ⟨u,φ⟩⟨v,ψ⟩, with supp(u ⊗ v) = supp u × supp v.

nodes.name: Schwartz kernel theorem
nodes.type_signature: Continuous linear T: 𝒟(Ω₂) → 𝒟'(Ω₁) ↔ K ∈ 𝒟'(Ω₁ × Ω₂)
nodes.description: Every continuous linear map T: C^∞_c(Ω₂) → 𝒟'(Ω₁) has a unique distributional kernel K ∈ 𝒟'(Ω₁ × Ω₂) with ⟨Tφ, ψ⟩ = ⟨K, ψ ⊗ φ⟩; establishes the canonical isomorphism between operators and distributions on the product.

nodes.name: Schwartz kernel method
nodes.function_signature: Linear operator → Distribution on product space
nodes.description: Representing a continuous linear operator between distribution spaces as a distributional kernel on the product, reducing operator questions to distribution-theoretic questions.

nodes.name: Pullback of a distribution by a diffeomorphism
nodes.type_signature: (κ: Ω₁ → Ω₂ diffeo, u ∈ 𝒟'(Ω₂)) → κ*u ∈ 𝒟'(Ω₁)
nodes.description: For a diffeomorphism κ, the pullback κ*u is defined by ⟨κ*u, φ⟩ = ⟨u, (φ ∘ κ⁻¹)|det Dκ⁻¹|⟩, extending the change-of-variables formula to distributions.

nodes.name: Pullback of a distribution by a submersion
nodes.type_signature: (f: ℝᵐ → ℝⁿ submersion, u ∈ 𝒟'(ℝⁿ)) → f*u ∈ 𝒟'(ℝᵐ)
nodes.description: For a smooth submersion f (surjective differential), pullback f*u is defined by fibered integration; extends u ∘ f from smooth functions to distributions.

nodes.name: Distribution on a submanifold (restriction/trace)
nodes.description: The restriction of a distribution to a smooth submanifold, well-defined when the wavefront set of u has no conormal directions to M.

nodes.name: Push-forward of a distribution
nodes.type_signature: (f: Ω₁ → Ω₂ proper smooth, u ∈ 𝒟'(Ω₁)) → f_*u ∈ 𝒟'(Ω₂)
nodes.description: For proper f, the push-forward f_*u defined by ⟨f_*u, φ⟩ = ⟨u, f*φ⟩; dual operation to pullback.

nodes.name: Change of variables for distributions
nodes.function_signature: (Diffeomorphism κ, u ∈ 𝒟') → κ*u ∈ 𝒟'
nodes.description: Pulling back distributions through diffeomorphisms or submersions to transfer distributional problems between coordinate systems.

nodes.name: Schwartz space 𝒮(ℝⁿ)
nodes.description: The space of rapidly decreasing smooth functions: φ ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ) with sup_x |x^α Dᵝφ(x)| < ∞ for all α, β, topologized by these seminorms; dense in L^p for 1 ≤ p < ∞.

nodes.name: Tempered distributions 𝒮'(ℝⁿ)
nodes.description: The dual of the Schwartz space: continuous linear functionals on 𝒮(ℝⁿ); includes all distributions of polynomial growth, all L^p functions, all polynomials, and all distributions of compact support.

nodes.name: Fourier transform on 𝒮(ℝⁿ)
nodes.description: The map φ̂(ξ) = ∫ e^{−ix·ξ} φ(x) dx is a topological automorphism of 𝒮(ℝⁿ), with inverse φ(x) = (2π)⁻ⁿ ∫ e^{ix·ξ} φ̂(ξ) dξ.

nodes.name: Fourier transform on 𝒮'(ℝⁿ)
nodes.description: Extended by duality: ⟨û, φ⟩ = ⟨u, φ̂⟩ for u ∈ 𝒮', φ ∈ 𝒮; an automorphism of 𝒮' interchanging differentiation with polynomial multiplication and support with smoothness.

nodes.name: Fourier exchange rules (derivative ↔ multiplication)
nodes.description: The Fourier transform satisfies (D^α u)^ = (iξ)^α û and (x^α u)^ = (iD_ξ)^α û, exchanging differentiation with polynomial multiplication and converting PDEs into algebraic equations.

nodes.name: Plancherel theorem (L² isometry)
nodes.description: The Fourier transform extends from 𝒮(ℝⁿ) to a unitary isomorphism of L²(ℝⁿ): ‖φ̂‖₂ = (2π)^{n/2} ‖φ‖₂, and ∫φ̂ψ̄ dξ = (2π)ⁿ ∫φψ̄ dx (Parseval).

nodes.name: Fourier transform of ℰ'(ℝⁿ) (entire analytic functions)
nodes.type_signature: u ∈ ℰ'(ℝⁿ) → û ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ) ∩ O(ℂⁿ) of exponential type
nodes.description: The Fourier transform of u ∈ ℰ' is the entire analytic function û(ζ) = ⟨u, e^{−i⟨·,ζ⟩}⟩ satisfying |û(ζ)| ≤ C(1+|ζ|)^N e^{A|Im ζ|} where supp u ⊂ B̄(0,A).

nodes.name: Paley–Wiener–Schwartz theorem
nodes.type_signature: ℰ'(ℝⁿ) ↔ {entire functions of exponential type with polynomial growth on ℝⁿ}
nodes.description: A distribution u has compact support (u ∈ ℰ') iff its Fourier transform û extends to an entire function of exponential type: û ∈ O(ℂⁿ) with |û(ζ)| ≤ C(1+|ζ|)^N exp(H_K(Im ζ)) where H_K is the supporting function of the convex hull of supp u.

nodes.name: Paley–Wiener theorem for C^∞_c
nodes.type_signature: C^∞_c(ℝⁿ) ↔ {entire functions of exponential type rapidly decreasing on ℝⁿ}
nodes.description: φ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝⁿ) with supp φ ⊂ B̄(0,A) iff φ̂ extends to an entire function with |φ̂(ζ)| ≤ C_N(1+|ζ|)^{−N} exp(A|Im ζ|) for all N.

nodes.name: Sobolev space H^s(ℝⁿ) via Fourier transform
nodes.description: H^s(ℝⁿ) = {u ∈ 𝒮'(ℝⁿ) : (1+|ξ|²)^{s/2} û ∈ L²(ℝⁿ)}, with norm ‖u‖_s = ‖(1+|ξ|²)^{s/2} û‖₂; for s ∈ ℕ₀, equivalent to requiring D^α u ∈ L² for |α| ≤ s.

nodes.name: Sobolev embedding via Fourier transform
nodes.description: If s > n/2 + k then H^s(ℝⁿ) embeds continuously into C^k(ℝⁿ) with bounded derivatives: proved by showing (1+|ξ|²)^{−s/2} ∈ L² when s > n/2, hence û ∈ L¹ by Cauchy–Schwarz.

nodes.name: Fourier inversion formula
nodes.type_signature: φ ∈ 𝒮(ℝⁿ) → φ(x) = (2π)⁻ⁿ ∫ e^{ix·ξ} φ̂(ξ) dξ
nodes.description: The inverse Fourier transform recovers φ from φ̂: φ(x) = (2π)⁻ⁿ ∫ e^{ix·ξ} φ̂(ξ) dξ, valid pointwise for φ ∈ 𝒮 and in 𝒮' for tempered distributions.

nodes.name: Convolution theorem (Fourier)
nodes.description: The Fourier transform converts convolution to pointwise multiplication: (u ∗ v)^ = û · v̂ when u ∈ 𝒮' and v ∈ ℰ', or when both are in L¹ or L².

nodes.name: Fourier transform method for constant-coefficient PDE
nodes.function_signature: P(D)u = f → P(ξ)û = f̂ → û = f̂/P(ξ)
nodes.description: Applying the Fourier transform to reduce a constant-coefficient PDE to an algebraic equation, then solving by division; requires analyzing the zero set of the symbol P(ξ).

nodes.name: Wavefront set WF(u)
nodes.description: WF(u) = {(x,ξ) ∈ Ω × (ℝⁿ\0) : ξ ∉ Σ_x(u)} where Σ_x(u) is the set of directions in which the localized Fourier transform φu decays rapidly; a refinement of singular support encoding directional singularity information.

nodes.name: Projection of WF(u) is sing supp u
nodes.description: The projection of the wavefront set onto the base space equals the singular support: x ∈ sing supp u iff there exists ξ with (x,ξ) ∈ WF(u).

nodes.name: Wavefront set under differentiation
nodes.description: Differentiation does not create new singularities: WF(Dᵅu) ⊂ WF(u) for all multi-indices α, and more generally WF(Pu) ⊂ WF(u) for any differential operator P with smooth coefficients.

nodes.name: Wavefront set of a product of distributions
nodes.description: When the product uv is well-defined, WF(uv) ⊂ WF(u) ∪ WF(v) ∪ {(x,ξ+η) : (x,ξ) ∈ WF(u), (x,η) ∈ WF(v)}, providing microlocal control of the product's singularities.

nodes.name: Hörmander's condition for multiplication of distributions
nodes.description: The product uv of two distributions is well-defined as a distribution if there is no (x,ξ) ∈ WF(u) with (x,−ξ) ∈ WF(v); i.e., the fiber-wise sum WF(u)_x + WF(v)_x never contains 0.

nodes.name: Wavefront set under pullback
nodes.description: For a smooth map f: Ω₁ → Ω₂, if f*u is well-defined then WF(f*u) ⊂ {(x, ᵗf'(x)η) : (f(x),η) ∈ WF(u)}, the canonical pullback of the wavefront set via the transpose of the Jacobian.

nodes.name: Elliptic regularity (microlocal version)
nodes.type_signature: P(x,D)u = f, P elliptic at (x₀,ξ₀) → (x₀,ξ₀) ∉ WF(u) \ WF(f)
nodes.description: If the principal symbol p_m(x₀,ξ₀) ≠ 0 (ellipticity at a covector), then (x₀,ξ₀) ∈ WF(u) implies (x₀,ξ₀) ∈ WF(f); thus WF(u) \ WF(f) ⊂ Char(P), the characteristic set.

nodes.name: Characteristic set of a differential operator
nodes.description: The zero set of the principal symbol p_m(x,ξ) in the cotangent bundle (minus zero section); WF(u) \ WF(Pu) ⊂ Char(P) by microlocal elliptic regularity.

nodes.name: Conic set in T*Ω \ 0
nodes.type_signature: Γ ⊂ T*Ω \ 0, (x,ξ) ∈ Γ ⇒ (x,tξ) ∈ Γ for t > 0
nodes.description: A subset Γ of the cotangent bundle (with zero section removed) that is invariant under positive fiber dilations; wavefront sets are always closed conic sets.

nodes.name: Microlocal smoothness (absence from WF)
nodes.description: A distribution u is microlocally smooth at (x₀,ξ₀) if there exists φ ∈ C^∞_c with φ(x₀) ≠ 0 and a conic neighborhood Γ of ξ₀ such that |φ̂u(ξ)| ≤ C_N(1+|ξ|)^{−N} for ξ ∈ Γ and all N.

nodes.name: Wavefront set of a convolution
nodes.description: The wavefront set of u ∗ v (when defined) satisfies WF(u∗v) ⊂ {(x+y,ξ) : (x,ξ) ∈ WF(u) and (y,ξ) ∈ WF(v)}, refining the singular support addition rule with directional information.

nodes.name: Microlocal analysis (wavefront set calculus)
nodes.function_signature: (u ∈ 𝒟', operations) → WF bounds on results
nodes.description: Tracking the wavefront set through operations (differentiation, multiplication, pullback, push-forward, convolution) to determine well-definedness and regularity of distributional constructions.

nodes.name: Oscillatory integral
nodes.description: An integral I(x) = ∫ e^{iΦ(x,θ)} a(x,θ) dθ with phase Φ and amplitude a in a symbol class, defined by regularization; the wavefront set is contained in {(x, Φ'_x) : Φ'_θ = 0}.

nodes.name: Stationary phase method
nodes.function_signature: ∫ e^{iλΦ(x)} a(x) dx → asymptotic expansion as λ → ∞
nodes.description: Asymptotic expansion of oscillatory integrals: contributions concentrate at critical points of the phase Φ, with leading term involving (det Φ'')^{−1/2}; fundamental for relating wavefront sets to geometry.

nodes.name: Distribution of finite order
nodes.type_signature: u ∈ 𝒟'(Ω) of global order ≤ N
nodes.description: A distribution u such that |⟨u,φ⟩| ≤ C ∑_{|α|≤N} sup|Dᵅφ| for all φ ∈ 𝒟(Ω) with supp φ ⊂ K and a single N valid for all K; extends to Cᴺ_c(Ω) by continuity.

nodes.name: Positive distributions are measures
nodes.type_signature: u ∈ 𝒟'(Ω), ⟨u,φ⟩ ≥ 0 for φ ≥ 0 → u is a positive Radon measure
nodes.description: If ⟨u,φ⟩ ≥ 0 for all non-negative test functions φ, then u is a positive Radon measure on Ω; this is order 0 and follows from the Riesz representation theorem.

nodes.name: Fourier–Laplace transform
nodes.type_signature: u ∈ ℰ'(ℝⁿ) → û(ζ) entire analytic on ℂⁿ
nodes.description: The extension of the Fourier transform of u ∈ ℰ' to complex arguments: û(ζ) = ⟨u, e^{−i⟨·,ζ⟩}⟩ for ζ ∈ ℂⁿ, an entire function of exponential type characterized by the Paley–Wiener–Schwartz theorem.

nodes.name: Propagation of singularities (distribution-theoretic version)
nodes.type_signature: P(x,D)u = f → WF(u) \ WF(f) invariant along bicharacteristics
nodes.description: For a principal-type operator P with real principal symbol, WF(u) \ WF(f) is a union of maximally extended bicharacteristic strips of P inside Char(P); singularities propagate along the Hamiltonian flow of p_m.

nodes.name: FBI transform
nodes.description: The Fourier–Bros–Iagolnitzer transform Tu(x,ξ,λ) = ∫ e^{iλ⟨y−x,ξ⟩ − λ|y−x|²/2} u(y) dy, a Gaussian-windowed Fourier transform that characterizes microlocal regularity: (x₀,ξ₀) ∉ WF(u) iff Tu decays exponentially in λ near (x₀,ξ₀).

nodes.name: Analytic wave front set WF_A(u)
nodes.description: The analytic wave front set WF_A(u) ⊂ T*Ω \ 0 refines WF(u) by measuring failure of analytic (rather than C^∞) regularity at each codirection, defined via exponential decay of the FBI transform.

nodes.name: FBI characterization of analytic regularity
nodes.description: A distribution u is real-analytic near x₀ if and only if WF_A(u) ∩ ({x₀} × (ℝⁿ\0)) = ∅, characterized by exponential decay of the FBI transform Tu(x,ξ,λ) as λ → ∞.

nodes.name: Schwartz kernel method
nodes.function_signature: (Continuous linear map 𝒟(Ω₂) → 𝒟'(Ω₁)) → (Kernel K ∈ 𝒟'(Ω₁ × Ω₂))
nodes.description: Representing continuous linear maps between distribution spaces via their Schwartz kernel to reduce operator-theoretic questions to distributional properties of the kernel.

nodes.name: P-convexity for supports
nodes.type_signature: Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ open, P(D) const-coeff → Bool
nodes.description: An open set Ω is P-convex for supports if for every compact K ⊂ Ω, the P-support hull of K relative to Ω is compact; equivalent to surjectivity of P(D): 𝒟'(Ω) → 𝒟'(Ω).

nodes.name: P-convexity for singular supports
nodes.type_signature: Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ open, P(D) const-coeff → Bool
nodes.description: An open set Ω is P-convex for singular supports if for every compact K ⊂ Ω, the set of points whose singular support hull meets K is relatively compact; required for smooth solvability P(D)u = f with f ∈ C^∞(Ω).

nodes.name: Exponential-polynomial solution approximation (Malgrange)
nodes.type_signature: P(D) const-coeff, Ω convex → density result
nodes.description: For a convex open set Ω, exponential-polynomial solutions x^α e^{⟨ζ,x⟩} with P(ζ) = 0 are dense in the space of all C^∞ solutions of P(D)u = 0 on Ω in the C^∞ topology.

nodes.name: Geometric characterization of P-convexity
nodes.type_signature: P(D) const-coeff, Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ → geometric criterion
nodes.description: P-convexity for supports is characterized by the condition that for each compact K ⊂ Ω, the convex hull of K with respect to the propagation cone of P remains compact in Ω.

nodes.name: Existence theorem for PDE on P-convex domains
nodes.description: If Ω is P-convex for supports, then P(D): 𝒟'(Ω) → 𝒟'(Ω) is surjective; if also P-convex for singular supports, then P(D): C^∞(Ω) → C^∞(Ω) is surjective.

nodes.name: Convexity implies P-convexity
nodes.type_signature: Ω convex → Ω is P-convex for all P
nodes.description: Every convex open set Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ is P-convex for supports and for singular supports for every constant-coefficient operator P(D).

nodes.name: Regularity index of a hypoelliptic operator
nodes.description: The supremum δ such that |ξ|^δ = O(|P(ξ)|) as |ξ| → ∞; measures Sobolev regularity gain: if P(D)u ∈ H^s then u ∈ H^{s+mδ}. For elliptic operators δ = 1; for the heat operator δ = 1/2.

nodes.name: Analytically hypoelliptic operator
nodes.description: A linear PDE operator P is analytically hypoelliptic if whenever Pu is real-analytic on an open set U, the solution u is also real-analytic on U; stronger than C^∞ hypoellipticity.

nodes.name: Characterization of analytically hypoelliptic operators
nodes.type_signature: P(D) const-coeff → necessary and sufficient condition
nodes.description: A constant-coefficient operator P(D) is analytically hypoelliptic if and only if the variety V(P) = {ζ ∈ ℂⁿ : P(ζ) = 0} satisfies |Im ζ| → ∞ when |ζ| → ∞ on V(P), with Im ζ growing at least linearly in |Re ζ|.

nodes.name: Well-posedness of Cauchy problem (Gårding–Petrowsky)
nodes.type_signature: P(D) const-coeff, hyperbolicity → well-posedness in C^∞
nodes.description: The Cauchy problem for P(D) with data on t = 0 is well-posed in C^∞ if and only if P is hyperbolic with respect to the t-direction.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic polynomial
nodes.type_signature: P: ℝⁿ⁺¹ → ℝ homogeneous, N ∈ ℝⁿ⁺¹ → Bool
nodes.description: A homogeneous polynomial P(ξ) of degree m is hyperbolic with respect to N if P(N) ≠ 0 and for every ξ the equation P(ξ + τN) = 0 has only real roots τ; the hyperbolicity cone is convex (Gårding).

nodes.name: Petrowsky lacuna
nodes.type_signature: P(D) hyperbolic → region where fundamental solution vanishes
nodes.description: A connected component of the complement of the wave front surface of a hyperbolic fundamental solution where it vanishes identically; the sharp Huygens principle in odd dimensions ≥ 3 is the classical example.

nodes.name: Herglotz–Petrovsky–Leray formula
nodes.type_signature: P(D) hyperbolic, fundamental solution → integral representation
nodes.description: An explicit integral representation of the fundamental solution of a hyperbolic operator as a period integral over a cycle in projective space determined by the characteristic surface; vanishing of these integrals characterizes Petrowsky lacunae.

nodes.name: Atiyah–Bott–Gårding lacuna criterion
nodes.type_signature: P(D) hyperbolic → topological criterion for lacunae
nodes.description: A Petrowsky lacuna is characterized by the vanishing of the Petrovsky cycle in the homology of the complement of the complexified characteristic surface; gives necessary and sufficient topological conditions.

nodes.name: Operator of constant strength
nodes.description: A variable-coefficient operator P(x,D) has constant strength if for every pair x₀, x₁, the frozen operators P(x₀,D) and P(x₁,D) are equally strong: their symbol ratios are bounded for large ξ.

nodes.name: Existence theorem for operators of constant strength
nodes.type_signature: P(x,D) constant strength, Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ → local solvability
nodes.description: If P(x,D) has constant strength, the equation P(x,D)u = f is locally solvable, proved by reducing to the constant-coefficient case via parametrix construction and perturbation.

nodes.name: Hypoellipticity for operators of constant strength
nodes.type_signature: P(x,D) constant strength, frozen P(x₀,D) hypoelliptic → P hypoelliptic
nodes.description: If P(x,D) has constant strength and each frozen operator P(x₀,D) is hypoelliptic, then P(x,D) itself is hypoelliptic with the same regularity index.
