nodes.name: Abstract Cauchy–Kovalevsky theorem (Nirenberg–Nishida)
nodes.type_signature: Banach scale {E_s}, nonlinear operator → local existence
nodes.description: In a scale of Banach spaces {E_s}, if F: E_s → E_{s'} satisfies a Lipschitz condition with norm ≤ C/(s−s'), then du/dt = F(u), u(0) = u₀ has a unique solution on a small time interval; unifies existence results for nonlinear analytic PDE.

nodes.name: Holmgren–John global uniqueness
nodes.type_signature: P(x,D) analytic coefficients, non-characteristic surface → global uniqueness
nodes.description: Extension of Holmgren's theorem: uniqueness of solutions vanishing on one side of a non-characteristic surface propagates along bicharacteristics, sweeping the surface to obtain global uniqueness.

nodes.name: Ehrenpreis fundamental principle
nodes.type_signature: P(D) const-coeff system → representation of solutions
nodes.description: Every solution of a constant-coefficient PDE system P(D)u = 0 on a convex open set can be represented as an integral of exponential-polynomial solutions over the characteristic variety V(P) with Noetherian operators encoding multiplicity.

nodes.name: Mean-periodic function
nodes.description: A continuous function f is mean-periodic if there exists a nonzero μ ∈ ℰ'(ℝ) with μ ∗ f = 0; generalizes periodic functions and solutions of constant-coefficient ODE.

nodes.name: Spectral synthesis for mean-periodic functions
nodes.description: Every mean-periodic function on ℝ can be approximated by finite sums of x^k e^{λx} where λ ranges over zeros of μ̂(ζ); the Delsarte–Schwartz theorem on spectral synthesis.

nodes.name: Noetherian operator (PDE)
nodes.description: In the Ehrenpreis–Palamodov theory, differential operators with polynomial coefficients that, applied to e^{i⟨x,ζ⟩} and integrated over V(P), generate all solutions of P(D)u = 0; they encode the multiplicity structure of V(P).

nodes.name: Division theorem for distributions (Ehrenpreis–Malgrange)
nodes.type_signature: P polynomial, u ∈ 𝒮'(ℝⁿ) → v ∈ 𝒮'(ℝⁿ) with Pv = u
nodes.description: For any nonzero polynomial P and tempered distribution u, there exists v ∈ 𝒮'(ℝⁿ) with Pv = u; multiplication by P is surjective on 𝒮'(ℝⁿ). Key ingredient in the Malgrange–Ehrenpreis existence theorem.

nodes.name: Slowly decreasing condition
nodes.description: The Fourier–Laplace transform μ̂(ζ) of μ ∈ ℰ'(ℝⁿ) is slowly decreasing if for every ζ there exists ζ' nearby with |μ̂(ζ')| polynomially bounded below; necessary and sufficient for surjectivity of f ↦ μ ∗ f on C^∞(ℝⁿ).

nodes.name: Surjectivity of convolution operators on C^∞
nodes.type_signature: μ ∈ ℰ'(ℝⁿ) → μ∗: C^∞ → C^∞ surjective iff slowly decreasing
nodes.description: The convolution operator f ↦ μ ∗ f is surjective on C^∞(ℝⁿ) if and only if μ̂ is slowly decreasing; generalizes Malgrange–Ehrenpreis from polynomial operators to arbitrary convolution operators.

nodes.name: Supports theorem for convolution (Titchmarsh generalization)
nodes.type_signature: u, v ∈ ℰ'(ℝⁿ) → convex hull of support
nodes.description: For u, v ∈ ℰ'(ℝⁿ), ch(supp(u ∗ v)) = ch(supp u) + ch(supp v) where ch is convex hull and + is Minkowski sum; generalizes Titchmarsh's convolution theorem.

nodes.name: Subelliptic estimate
nodes.type_signature: P diff operator, ε > 0 → a priori estimate
nodes.description: An a priori estimate ‖u‖_{H^{s+ε}} ≤ C(‖Pu‖_{H^s} + ‖u‖_{H^{s₀}}) with 0 < ε < 1, weaker than elliptic estimates; satisfied by Hörmander sum-of-squares operators with ε depending on bracket-generation step.

nodes.name: Kohn's subelliptic multiplier method
nodes.function_signature: (∂̄-Neumann problem) → (Subelliptic estimate via ideal of multipliers)
nodes.description: Establishing subelliptic estimates by iteratively constructing an ideal of multipliers using Lie brackets and algebraic operations until the ideal contains a nonvanishing function.

nodes.name: Rothschild–Stein lifting theorem
nodes.type_signature: Hörmander vector fields → free nilpotent approximation
nodes.description: Vector fields satisfying Hörmander's bracket condition of step r can be locally lifted to left-invariant vector fields on a free nilpotent Lie group of step r, yielding sharp subelliptic estimates via group convolution.

nodes.name: Classical symbol class S^m_cl
nodes.description: The subclass of S^m_{1,0} admitting an asymptotic expansion a ~ ∑_{j≥0} a_{m-j} with a_{m-j} homogeneous of degree m−j in ξ for |ξ| ≥ 1; the leading term a_m is the principal symbol.

nodes.name: Pseudodifferential operator Op(a)
nodes.description: The operator Op(a)u(x) = (2π)^{−n} ∫ e^{i⟨x,ξ⟩} a(x,ξ) û(ξ) dξ defined by Kohn–Nirenberg quantization; differential operators of order m correspond to polynomial symbols of degree m.

nodes.name: Asymptotic expansion of symbols
nodes.type_signature: sequence a_j ∈ S^{m_j} with m_j → −∞ → a ∈ S^{m_0}
nodes.description: Given a_j ∈ S^{m_j}_{ρ,δ} with m_j ↘ −∞, there exists a ∈ S^{m_0} such that a − ∑_{j<N} a_j ∈ S^{m_N} for all N, unique modulo S^{−∞}; fundamental for parametrix construction and composition.

nodes.name: Composition formula for pseudodifferential operators
nodes.description: For a ∈ S^{m₁}_{ρ,δ} and b ∈ S^{m₂}_{ρ,δ} with ρ > δ, the composition Op(a) ∘ Op(b) = Op(c) with c ~ ∑_α (1/α!) ∂^α_ξ a · D^α_x b; the principal symbol of the composition is the product of principal symbols.

nodes.name: Adjoint formula for pseudodifferential operators
nodes.description: The L² adjoint of Op(a) with a ∈ S^m_{ρ,δ} (ρ > δ) is Op(a*) where a* ~ ∑_α (1/α!) ∂^α_ξ D^α_x ā; the principal symbol of the adjoint is the complex conjugate of the original.

nodes.name: Kernel characterization of pseudodifferential operators
nodes.type_signature: A: C_c^∞ → 𝒟' → A ∈ Ψ^m iff kernel conditions
nodes.description: A continuous linear operator belongs to Ψ^m_{ρ,δ} if and only if its Schwartz kernel is C^∞ off the diagonal and satisfies specific singular estimates near the diagonal.

nodes.name: Elliptic symbol
nodes.description: A symbol a ∈ S^m is elliptic if |a(x,ξ)| ≥ c|ξ|^m for large |ξ|; ellipticity guarantees existence of a parametrix and full elliptic regularity.

nodes.name: Elliptic parametrix construction
nodes.type_signature: a ∈ S^m elliptic → b ∈ S^{−m} with Op(a)Op(b) = I mod Ψ^{−∞}
nodes.description: For an elliptic symbol a, one constructs b₀ = 1/a for large ξ, then iteratively corrects via the composition formula to get Op(a)Op(b) = I + R with R smoothing.

nodes.name: Elliptic regularity for pseudodifferential operators
nodes.type_signature: P ∈ Ψ^m elliptic, Pu = f → u regularity
nodes.description: If P ∈ Ψ^m is elliptic and Pu = f ∈ H^s_{loc}, then u ∈ H^{s+m}_{loc}; microlocally, WF(u) = WF(Pu), giving microlocal elliptic regularity.

nodes.name: Calderón–Vaillancourt theorem
nodes.type_signature: a ∈ S^0_{ρ,ρ}, 0 ≤ ρ < 1 → Op(a): L² → L² bounded
nodes.description: If a ∈ S⁰_{ρ,ρ} with 0 ≤ ρ < 1, then Op(a) is bounded on L²(ℝⁿ), with norm controlled by finitely many symbol seminorms; fails for ρ = 1.

nodes.name: Beals characterization of pseudodifferential operators
nodes.type_signature: A: L² → L² → A ∈ Ψ^0 iff iterated commutator bounds
nodes.description: A bounded operator A on L² belongs to Ψ⁰ if and only if iterated commutators ad(x_j)^α ad(D_j)^β A are bounded on L² for all multi-indices; gives a quantization-free characterization.

nodes.name: Weyl quantization
nodes.description: The symmetric quantization Op^w(a)u(x) = (2π)^{−n} ∫∫ e^{i⟨x−y,ξ⟩} a((x+y)/2, ξ) u(y) dy dξ; real symbols give formally self-adjoint operators, and composition uses the Moyal product.

nodes.name: Moyal product
nodes.type_signature: a, b ∈ S^m → a #_w b ∈ S^{m₁+m₂}
nodes.description: The composition law for Weyl symbols: (a #_w b) ~ ab + (i/2){a,b} + ... where {a,b} is the Poisson bracket; makes the symbol space a noncommutative associative algebra.

nodes.name: Sharp Gårding inequality
nodes.description: For a(x,ξ) ≥ 0 with a ∈ S^m_{1,0}, Re⟨Op(a)u, u⟩ ≥ −C‖u‖²_{H^{(m−1)/2}}, improving the classical Gårding inequality by losing only (m−1)/2 derivatives; proved via Friedrichs symmetrization.

nodes.name: Fefferman–Phong inequality
nodes.type_signature: a ∈ S², a ≥ 0 → Op^w(a) + C ≥ 0 on L²
nodes.description: If a ∈ S²_{1,0} satisfies a ≥ 0, then Op^w(a) ≥ −C on L², gaining a full derivative over the sharp Gårding inequality; proved via decomposition into wave packets.

nodes.name: Symbol smoothing (Friedrichs symmetrization)
nodes.function_signature: (Non-negative symbol a ∈ S^m) → (Smoothed symbol b with Op(b) ≥ 0 and a − b ∈ S^{m−1})
nodes.description: Regularizing a symbol by Gaussian convolution in phase space at scale |ξ|^{−1/2} to produce a non-negative symbol differing from the original by a lower-order term.

nodes.name: Pseudodifferential operators on manifolds Ψ^m(M)
nodes.type_signature: M smooth manifold → Ψ^m(M) operator algebra
nodes.description: The algebra Ψ^m(M) of operators on a manifold M that are pseudodifferential with symbol in S^m_{1,0} in every local chart modulo smoothing; the principal symbol σ_m(A) is a well-defined function on T*M \ 0.

nodes.name: Principal symbol on a manifold
nodes.description: The equivalence class of the full symbol modulo S^{m−1}, transforming as a function on T*M \ 0 homogeneous of degree m; invariantly defined and multiplicative under composition.

nodes.name: Fredholm property of elliptic operators on compact manifolds
nodes.type_signature: P ∈ Ψ^m(M), M compact, P elliptic → P Fredholm
nodes.description: An elliptic P ∈ Ψ^m(M) on a compact manifold without boundary is Fredholm: H^s(M) → H^{s−m}(M) with finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel in C^∞(M); index computed by Atiyah–Singer.

nodes.name: Seeley's complex powers
nodes.type_signature: P ∈ Ψ^m(M) elliptic positive → P^z ∈ Ψ^{mz}(M)
nodes.description: For an elliptic positive self-adjoint P on a compact manifold, the complex powers P^z form a holomorphic family of pseudodifferential operators of order mRe(z); Tr(P^{−z}) yields the spectral zeta function.

nodes.name: Weyl's law with sharp remainder (Hörmander)
nodes.type_signature: P elliptic on compact M → N(λ) = cλ^{n/m} + O(λ^{(n-1)/m})
nodes.description: The eigenvalue counting function N(λ) = #{λ_j ≤ λ} for a positive elliptic self-adjoint operator of order m on compact n-manifold satisfies N(λ) = (2π)^{−n} vol({p_m ≤ λ}) + O(λ^{(n−1)/m}); Hörmander's 1968 proof via propagation of singularities.

nodes.name: Calderón projector
nodes.type_signature: P elliptic on M, ∂M → Ψ^0(∂M) projection
nodes.description: A pseudodifferential projector on ∂M projecting the space of all boundary Cauchy data onto the subspace of Cauchy data of solutions of Pu = 0; its principal symbol encodes the boundary behavior.

nodes.name: Shapiro–Lopatinskii condition
nodes.description: The compatibility condition ensuring an elliptic BVP is Fredholm: at each boundary point, the frozen ODE on the half-line must have a unique decaying solution for each boundary datum.

nodes.name: Boutet de Monvel calculus
nodes.type_signature: M manifold with boundary → algebra of boundary operators
nodes.description: A calculus of 2×2 matrix operators [P₊+G, K; T, S] on manifolds with boundary combining interior pseudodifferential, singular Green, Poisson, and trace operators; closed under composition with Fredholm theory.

nodes.name: Poisson operator (Boutet de Monvel)
nodes.description: An operator in the Boutet de Monvel calculus mapping boundary data on ∂M to solutions in the interior, the off-diagonal entry converting boundary conditions to interior functions.

nodes.name: Singular Green operator
nodes.description: An operator in the Boutet de Monvel calculus capturing boundary effects invisible to the interior pseudodifferential calculus; singular only at the boundary diagonal.

nodes.name: Fredholm property for elliptic BVPs
nodes.type_signature: (P, B) elliptic BVP satisfying Shapiro–Lopatinskii → Fredholm
nodes.description: An elliptic BVP satisfying the Shapiro–Lopatinskii condition on a compact manifold with boundary is Fredholm between Sobolev spaces; index computed by the Atiyah–Bott or Boutet de Monvel index theorem.

nodes.name: Hodge decomposition for elliptic complexes
nodes.type_signature: elliptic complex on compact M → orthogonal decomposition
nodes.description: For an elliptic complex on a compact Riemannian manifold, each section space decomposes as ker Δ_k ⊕ im d_{k-1} ⊕ im d_k*, with harmonic space ker Δ_k isomorphic to cohomology; generalizes the classical Hodge theorem.

nodes.name: Symplectic classification of submanifolds
nodes.description: Submanifolds of a symplectic manifold classified by ω|_Σ: Lagrangian (ω|_Σ = 0, dim = n), symplectic (non-degenerate), isotropic (ω|_Σ = 0, dim < n), coisotropic (Σ^ω ⊂ Σ).

nodes.name: Bicharacteristic strip
nodes.type_signature: integral curve of H_{p_m} on Char(P) ⊂ T*M \ 0
nodes.description: An integral curve of the Hamilton vector field H_{p_m} lying on the characteristic set {p_m = 0}; its projection is a bicharacteristic curve (ray). Singularities of PDE solutions propagate along bicharacteristic strips.

nodes.name: Operator of principal type
nodes.description: A pseudodifferential operator P is of principal type if dp_m ≠ 0 on Char(P); equivalently, H_{p_m} is nonvanishing on the characteristic set, ensuring bicharacteristics are well-defined curves.

nodes.name: Condition (Ψ) (Nirenberg–Treves)
nodes.description: Im(p_m) does not change sign from − to + along oriented bicharacteristics of Re(p_m); necessary and sufficient for local solvability (necessity: Hörmander; sufficiency: Dencker 2006).

nodes.name: Subelliptic operators (loss of δ derivatives)
nodes.type_signature: P ∈ Ψ^m, 0 < δ ≤ 1 → subelliptic with loss δ
nodes.description: P is subelliptic with loss δ if ‖u‖_{H^{s+m−δ}} ≤ C(‖Pu‖_{H^s} + ‖u‖_{H^{s₀}}); the loss δ = k/(k+1) corresponds to bracket depth k in the Hörmander condition.

nodes.name: Microlocal hypoellipticity
nodes.description: P is microlocally hypoelliptic at (x₀,ξ₀) if (x₀,ξ₀) ∉ WF(u) whenever (x₀,ξ₀) ∉ WF(Pu); the microlocal refinement of hypoellipticity.

nodes.name: Strictly hyperbolic operator (PDE)
nodes.description: P is strictly hyperbolic if its principal symbol p_m(t,x,τ,ξ) = 0 has m distinct real roots τ = τ_j(t,x,ξ) for ξ ≠ 0; implies well-posedness of the Cauchy problem with finite speed of propagation.

nodes.name: Well-posedness of strictly hyperbolic Cauchy problem
nodes.type_signature: P strictly hyperbolic → unique H^s solution with energy estimates
nodes.description: The Cauchy problem for a strictly hyperbolic operator of order m has a unique solution u ∈ C([0,T]; H^s) with energy estimates controlling ‖u‖ by data and source terms.

nodes.name: Parametrix for strictly hyperbolic Cauchy problem
nodes.type_signature: P strictly hyperbolic → FIO solution operator
nodes.description: The solution operator for the strictly hyperbolic Cauchy problem is a Fourier integral operator whose canonical relation is the graph of the bicharacteristic flow; constructed via the Lax parametrix method.

nodes.name: Propagation of singularities for hyperbolic equations
nodes.type_signature: P hyperbolic, Pu = f → WF(u) ⊂ WF(f) ∪ bicharacteristics through WF(data)
nodes.description: For a strictly hyperbolic P, WF(u) \ WF(f) is a union of bicharacteristic strips, giving the sharp description of singular support propagation along rays.

nodes.name: Lax parametrix construction
nodes.function_signature: (Strictly hyperbolic P) → (FIO approximate solution via eikonal + transport equations)
nodes.description: Constructing the parametrix by solving the eikonal equation for the phase and transport equations for the amplitude, producing an FIO approximation to the solution operator.

nodes.name: Hadamard's construction of fundamental solutions
nodes.function_signature: (Second-order hyperbolic P) → (Fundamental solution via Riesz distributions on light cone)
nodes.description: Writing E = ∑ U_j Γ^{j−(n−2)/2} + (log Γ) ∑ V_j Γ^j where Γ is the squared Lorentzian distance; coefficients determined recursively by transport equations along null geodesics.

nodes.name: Glancing rays
nodes.description: Bicharacteristics tangent to the boundary at a point, neither entering nor leaving transversally; propagation near glancing rays requires the Melrose–Sjöstrand theory.

nodes.name: Diffractive rays
nodes.type_signature: glancing bicharacteristic leaving boundary → ray type
nodes.description: Bicharacteristics tangent to the boundary that then leave into the interior; singularities can split between gliding along the boundary and diffracting into the interior.

nodes.name: Melrose–Sjöstrand propagation theorem
nodes.type_signature: P hyperbolic, Ω with boundary → WF(u) along generalized rays
nodes.description: Singularities of solutions to the wave equation in a domain with boundary propagate along generalized bicharacteristic rays: reflecting at transversal points, gliding at glancing points.

nodes.name: Gliding rays
nodes.type_signature: bicharacteristic confined to boundary → ray type
nodes.description: Bicharacteristic rays trapped on the boundary ∂Ω carrying singularities in the shadow region; on convex obstacles, these are the geodesics on the boundary (creeping rays).

nodes.name: Non-degenerate phase function
nodes.description: A phase function φ(x,θ) homogeneous of degree 1 in θ with dφ ≠ 0 and d(∂φ/∂θ_j) linearly independent on C_φ = {∂φ/∂θ = 0}; the critical set C_φ parameterizes a Lagrangian submanifold Λ_φ ⊂ T*X.

nodes.name: Canonical relation
nodes.type_signature: Λ ⊂ T*X × T*Y Lagrangian for ω_X − ω_Y
nodes.description: A Lagrangian submanifold of T*X × T*Y with the twisted symplectic form, serving as the geometric invariant of a Fourier integral operator; composition of FIOs corresponds to composition of canonical relations.

nodes.name: Lagrangian distribution I^μ(X, Λ)
nodes.type_signature: X manifold, Λ Lagrangian, μ ∈ ℝ → distribution space
nodes.description: The space of distributions on X with WF contained in Λ and singularity of order μ, locally expressible as oscillatory integrals ∫ e^{iφ(x,θ)} a(x,θ) dθ with appropriate symbol order.

nodes.name: Principal symbol of a Lagrangian distribution
nodes.description: The invariantly defined leading term in the half-density bundle tensored with the Maslov bundle; determines u modulo I^{μ−1} and is multiplicative under FIO composition.

nodes.name: Maslov index
nodes.type_signature: γ loop in Lagrangian Grassmannian → ℤ
nodes.description: An integer-valued topological invariant measuring the rotation of a Lagrangian plane relative to a reference; gives the phase shift e^{−iπ/2} at each caustic crossing in the WKB approximation.

nodes.name: Maslov bundle
nodes.type_signature: Λ Lagrangian → flat line bundle M_Λ
nodes.description: A flat complex line bundle on Λ with holonomy e^{−iπμ(γ)/2} around loops; sections of Ω^{1/2}(Λ) ⊗ M_Λ are the natural home for principal symbols of Lagrangian distributions.

nodes.name: Clean intersection composition of FIOs
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ I^μ, B ∈ I^ν, clean with excess e → A∘B ∈ I^{μ+ν+e/2}
nodes.description: When canonical relations compose cleanly with excess e, the FIO composition belongs to I^{μ+ν+e/2} associated to the composed canonical relation; the excess shifts the order.

nodes.name: Transversal composition of FIOs
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ I^μ, B ∈ I^ν, transversal → A∘B ∈ I^{μ+ν}
nodes.description: When canonical relations compose transversally (excess e = 0), the composition is an FIO of order μ + ν with principal symbol equal to the product of principal symbols.

nodes.name: L² continuity of FIOs
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ I^0, canonical relation a local graph → A: L² → L² bounded
nodes.description: A Fourier integral operator of order 0 whose canonical relation is a local canonical graph is bounded on L²; the order 0 is sharp.

nodes.name: Hörmander–Sato lemma on WF of FIOs
nodes.type_signature: A FIO, canonical relation C → WF(Au) ⊂ C ∘ WF(u)
nodes.description: For an FIO with canonical relation C, the wavefront set satisfies WF(Au) ⊂ C ∘ WF(u), giving a precise microlocal mapping property showing singularities propagate along the canonical relation.

nodes.name: Global calculus of oscillatory integrals
nodes.function_signature: (Local oscillatory integrals + equivalence of phase functions) → (Invariant FIO theory on manifolds)
nodes.description: Patching local oscillatory integral representations to define FIOs globally via partition of unity; the class I^μ(X,Λ) is independent of the choice of non-degenerate phase function.

nodes.name: Refined symbol calculus for type (1,0)
nodes.function_signature: (S^m_{1,0} symbols) → (Improved composition estimates with precise remainders)
nodes.description: Sharper estimates for composition and commutators of type (1,0) operators, with precise remainder dependence on seminorms; needed for Fefferman–Phong, sharp Gårding, and L² boundedness.

nodes.name: Carleman estimate (general form)
nodes.type_signature: P diff operator, φ weight → weighted a priori estimate
nodes.description: An estimate ∑ τ^{m−1−|α|} ‖e^{τφ} D^α u‖_{L²} ≤ C ‖e^{τφ} Pu‖_{L²} for τ ≥ τ₀ and u ∈ C_c^∞, where φ satisfies a pseudo-convexity condition; the main tool for unique continuation.

nodes.name: Strong pseudo-convexity condition
nodes.type_signature: P diff operator, φ weight → Bool
nodes.description: The condition {p_m, p̄_m}/(2i) > 0 on the complexified characteristic set with the weight φ; ensures Carleman estimates hold and is the natural condition for unique continuation.

nodes.name: Holmgren's uniqueness (microlocal version)
nodes.description: If P has analytic coefficients and Pu = 0, the analytic wavefront set WF_A(u) propagates along bicharacteristic strips; u vanishing on one side of a non-characteristic surface implies WF_A(u) cannot contain conormals to S.

nodes.name: Calderón uniqueness theorem
nodes.type_signature: P second-order, non-characteristic surface → unique continuation
nodes.description: If P is a second-order operator with Lipschitz coefficients and u satisfies Pu = 0, vanishing on one side of a non-characteristic surface S, then u = 0 near S; proved via Carleman estimates.

nodes.name: Strong unique continuation property
nodes.type_signature: P elliptic, u vanishes to infinite order → u ≡ 0
nodes.description: If P is second-order elliptic and |Pu| ≤ C(|u| + |∇u|), and u vanishes to infinite order at x₀, then u ≡ 0 in a connected neighborhood; proved by Carleman estimates with logarithmic weights.

nodes.name: Unique continuation across non-characteristic surfaces
nodes.type_signature: P(x,D) smooth coefficients, S non-characteristic → uniqueness
nodes.description: For P of any order with smooth coefficients, if S is strongly pseudo-convex and non-characteristic and u satisfies Pu = 0 with u = 0 on one side, then u = 0 near S.

nodes.name: Tauberian theorem for spectral function
nodes.function_signature: (Wave trace singularity structure) → (Eigenvalue counting asymptotics)
nodes.description: Converting wave trace distributional information into pointwise asymptotics of N(λ) via Tauberian arguments; the remainder O(λ^{(n−1)/m}) follows from propagation of singularities and finite speed of propagation.

nodes.name: Spectral function asymptotic
nodes.type_signature: P elliptic on compact M → e(x,x,λ) ~ cλ^{n/m} + O(λ^{(n−1)/m})
nodes.description: The on-diagonal spectral function e(x,x,λ) = ∑_{λ_j ≤ λ} |φ_j(x)|² satisfies e(x,x,λ) = (2π)^{−n} ∫_{p_m(x,ξ)≤λ} dξ + O(λ^{(n−1)/m}); integrating gives Weyl's law.

nodes.name: Wave trace formula
nodes.type_signature: M compact Riemannian → Tr(cos(t√Δ)) singularity structure
nodes.description: The distributional trace Tr(cos(t√Δ)) has singular support in {0} ∪ {±L : L length of closed geodesic}; singularities at t = ±L encode geometric data about closed geodesics via Poincaré maps.

nodes.name: Sharpness of remainder in Weyl's law
nodes.type_signature: S^n round sphere → remainder exactly O(λ^{(n-1)/m})
nodes.description: The O(λ^{(n−1)/m}) remainder in Weyl's law is optimal: on the round sphere, eigenvalue clustering produces oscillations of this order; improved remainders hold when the set of periodic bicharacteristics has measure zero.

nodes.name: Local Weyl law
nodes.type_signature: P elliptic, A ∈ Ψ^0 → ∑ ⟨Aφ_j, φ_j⟩ asymptotic
nodes.description: For P elliptic on compact M and A ∈ Ψ^0, ∑_{λ_j ≤ λ} ⟨Aφ_j, φ_j⟩ = (2π)^{−n} ∫_{p_m ≤ λ} σ_0(A) dω + O(λ^{(n−1)/m}); implies quantum ergodicity when geodesic flow is ergodic.

nodes.name: Asymptotic completeness for long-range potentials
nodes.type_signature: H = −Δ + V, V long-range → modified wave operators complete
nodes.description: For potentials with |∂^α V| ≤ C⟨x⟩^{−ρ−|α|} (ρ > 0), Dollard modified wave operators exist and are complete: Ran(Ω±_D) = H_{ac}(H); combines Mourre estimates, propagation estimates, and phase space analysis.

nodes.name: Limiting absorption principle (long-range)
nodes.type_signature: H = −Δ + V long-range → resolvent boundary values in weighted L²
nodes.description: Resolvent boundary values (H − λ ± i0)^{−1} exist as bounded operators ⟨x⟩^{−s}L² → ⟨x⟩^s L² (s > 1/2) for λ in the a.c. spectrum; proved via Mourre theory.

nodes.name: Scattering matrix for long-range potentials
nodes.type_signature: H = −Δ + V long-range → S(λ) on L²(S^{n−1})
nodes.description: The scattering matrix S(λ) defined via Dollard modified wave operators is a pseudodifferential operator on S^{n−1} whose symbol encodes the long-range scattering data.

nodes.name: Phase space characterization of long-range scattering
nodes.function_signature: (Propagation observables + asymptotic velocity) → (Completeness of modified wave operators)
nodes.description: Characterizing scattering states via the asymptotic velocity operator P± = s-lim x(t)/t and propagation estimates; completeness follows from showing P± exists and determines scattering channels.

nodes.name: Sommerfeld radiation condition (generalized)
nodes.type_signature: (Δ + k²)u = f → outgoing behavior at infinity
nodes.description: The condition ∂u/∂r − iku = o(r^{−(n−1)/2}) selecting the unique outgoing solution of the Helmholtz equation; generalized for variable-coefficient operators via the limiting absorption principle.

nodes.name: Differentiable manifold
nodes.description: A topological manifold equipped with a maximal atlas of charts whose transition maps are smooth (C^infty) diffeomorphisms.

nodes.name: Submanifold
nodes.description: A subset S of a manifold M that is itself a manifold and whose inclusion map is an injective immersion.

nodes.name: Orientation of a manifold
nodes.description: A consistent choice of orientation for all tangent spaces of a smooth manifold, equivalently a nowhere-vanishing top-degree differential form.

nodes.name: Vector field
nodes.description: A smooth section of the tangent bundle TM, assigning to each point p of a manifold M a tangent vector in T_pM.

nodes.name: Riemannian manifold
nodes.description: A smooth manifold equipped with a Riemannian metric, i.e., a smoothly varying positive-definite inner product on each tangent space.

nodes.name: Length of a curve
nodes.description: The integral L(gamma) = integral_a^b |gamma'(t)|_g dt of the speed of a piecewise smooth curve in a Riemannian manifold.

nodes.name: Riemannian distance
nodes.description: The metric d(p, q) = inf { L(gamma) : gamma joins p to q } on a connected Riemannian manifold, making it a metric space compatible with its topology.

nodes.name: Isometry (Riemannian)
nodes.description: A diffeomorphism f : (M, g) -> (N, h) between Riemannian manifolds satisfying f*h = g, preserving the metric tensor.

nodes.name: Local isometry
nodes.description: A smooth map f : M -> N such that the differential df_p is a linear isometry between the tangent spaces at every point.

nodes.name: Pullback metric (induced metric)
nodes.description: The Riemannian metric f*g on M induced by an immersion f : M -> (N, g), defined by (f*g)_p(u, v) = g_{f(p)}(df_p u, df_p v).

nodes.name: Product metric
nodes.description: The Riemannian metric on M x N defined as the direct sum g_M + g_N on the product tangent spaces.

nodes.name: Affine connection
nodes.description: An operator nabla : X(M) x X(M) -> X(M) satisfying C^infty(M)-linearity in the first argument and the Leibniz rule in the second, specifying differentiation of vector fields on a manifold.

nodes.name: Covariant derivative along a curve
nodes.description: The operator D/dt on vector fields along a curve gamma, induced by a connection, satisfying the Leibniz rule and agreeing with nabla on extendible fields.

nodes.name: Geodesic equation in local coordinates
nodes.description: The system of ODEs d^2 x^k/dt^2 + Gamma^k_{ij} (dx^i/dt)(dx^j/dt) = 0 characterizing geodesics in a coordinate chart.

nodes.name: Normal coordinates
nodes.description: Coordinates on a normal neighborhood of p obtained via exp_p, in which Christoffel symbols vanish and the metric is Euclidean to first order at p.

nodes.name: Normal neighborhood
nodes.description: An open set U containing p such that exp_p maps a star-shaped open subset of T_pM diffeomorphically onto U.

nodes.name: Geodesic ball and geodesic sphere
nodes.description: The geodesic ball B(p, r) = { q in M : d(p,q) < r } and geodesic sphere S(p, r) = { q in M : d(p,q) = r } centered at p.

nodes.name: Gauss lemma (Riemannian geometry)
nodes.description: Radial geodesics from p are orthogonal to geodesic spheres centered at p; equivalently (d exp_p)_v preserves inner products with radial directions.

nodes.name: Minimizing property of geodesics
nodes.description: Within a normal neighborhood, the radial geodesic from p to q is the unique length-minimizing curve, and any locally minimizing curve is a geodesic.

nodes.name: Convex neighborhood
nodes.description: An open set in a Riemannian manifold such that any two points are joined by a unique minimizing geodesic lying entirely within the set.

nodes.name: Whitehead's theorem on convex neighborhoods
nodes.description: Every point of a Riemannian manifold has a fundamental system of convex neighborhoods.

nodes.name: Symmetries of the curvature tensor
nodes.description: The algebraic identities of the Riemann tensor: skew-symmetry in the first and second pairs, pair symmetry, and the first Bianchi identity.

nodes.name: First Bianchi identity
nodes.description: For the Riemann curvature tensor of a torsion-free connection: R(X,Y)Z + R(Y,Z)X + R(Z,X)Y = 0.

nodes.name: Sectional curvature
nodes.description: For a 2-plane sigma in T_pM spanned by X, Y, the number K(sigma) = <R(X,Y)Y, X> / (|X|^2|Y|^2 - <X,Y>^2), generalizing Gaussian curvature to higher dimensions.

nodes.name: Ricci curvature
nodes.description: The symmetric (0,2)-tensor Ric(X,Y) = trace(Z -> R(Z,X)Y), obtained by contracting the Riemann tensor, measuring average sectional curvature in a direction.

nodes.name: Scalar curvature
nodes.description: The smooth function S = trace_g(Ric) obtained by tracing the Ricci tensor with the metric, giving the total average of sectional curvatures at a point.

nodes.name: Curvature tensor determined by sectional curvature
nodes.description: The Riemann curvature tensor at a point is completely determined by the sectional curvatures of all 2-planes at that point.

nodes.name: Ricci determines curvature in dimension 3
nodes.description: In dimension 3, the Riemann curvature tensor is completely determined by the Ricci tensor because the Weyl tensor vanishes identically.

nodes.name: Jacobi fields as geodesic variations
nodes.description: A Jacobi field along a geodesic gamma arises as the variational vector field J(t) = (d/ds)|_{s=0} gamma_s(t) of a one-parameter family of geodesics.

nodes.name: Conjugate point
nodes.description: A point gamma(t_0) along a geodesic gamma is conjugate to gamma(0) if there exists a nonzero Jacobi field vanishing at both t = 0 and t = t_0.

nodes.name: Multiplicity of a conjugate point
nodes.description: The dimension of the space of Jacobi fields along a geodesic that vanish at both endpoints, equivalently the dimension of the kernel of (d exp_p)_{t_0 v}.

nodes.name: Conjugate points as singularities of exp
nodes.description: The point gamma(t_0) is conjugate to gamma(0) = p along gamma if and only if t_0 gamma'(0) is a critical point of the exponential map exp_p.

nodes.name: Geodesics cease to minimize past conjugate points
nodes.description: A geodesic segment containing an interior conjugate point is not length-minimizing; the first conjugate point bounds the minimizing interval.

nodes.name: Isometric immersion
nodes.description: An immersion f : (M, g) -> (N, h) between Riemannian manifolds satisfying f*h = g, preserving the metric.

nodes.name: Second fundamental form
nodes.description: The symmetric bilinear form II(X, Y) = (nabla_X Y)^perp on an isometrically immersed submanifold, measuring extrinsic curvature via the normal component of the ambient covariant derivative.

nodes.name: Normal connection
nodes.description: The connection nabla^perp on the normal bundle of a submanifold, defined as the normal component of the ambient connection restricted to normal vector fields.

nodes.name: Shape operator (Weingarten map)
nodes.description: The self-adjoint linear map A_eta : T_pM -> T_pM defined by <A_eta X, Y> = <II(X,Y), eta>, encoding directional extrinsic curvature.

nodes.name: Gauss equation
nodes.description: Relates intrinsic and extrinsic curvature of a submanifold: <R^M(X,Y)Z, W> = <R^N(X,Y)Z, W> + <II(X,W), II(Y,Z)> - <II(X,Z), II(Y,W)>.

nodes.name: Codazzi equation (Codazzi-Mainardi)
nodes.description: The normal component of the ambient curvature restricted to a submanifold equals the difference of covariant derivatives of the second fundamental form: (R^N(X,Y)Z)^perp = (nabla_X II)(Y,Z) - (nabla_Y II)(X,Z).

nodes.name: Ricci equation (normal curvature equation)
nodes.description: Relates normal bundle curvature to ambient curvature and shape operators: <R^perp(X,Y)eta, xi> = <R^N(X,Y)eta, xi> + <[A_eta, A_xi]X, Y>.

nodes.name: Totally geodesic submanifold
nodes.description: A submanifold whose second fundamental form vanishes identically, equivalently every geodesic of the submanifold is a geodesic of the ambient manifold.

nodes.name: Minimal submanifold
nodes.description: A submanifold whose mean curvature vector vanishes identically, equivalently a critical point of the volume functional for compactly supported variations.

nodes.name: Geodesic completeness
nodes.description: A Riemannian manifold is geodesically complete if every geodesic extends to all of R, equivalently exp_p is defined on all of T_pM for every p.

nodes.name: Cut point
nodes.description: The point gamma(t_0) along a geodesic from p beyond which gamma ceases to minimize distance from p, either due to a shorter path or a conjugate point.

nodes.name: Model spaces S^n, R^n, H^n
nodes.description: The simply connected complete Riemannian manifolds of constant sectional curvature: the n-sphere (K > 0), Euclidean space (K = 0), and hyperbolic space (K < 0).

nodes.name: Hyperbolic space H^n
nodes.description: The unique simply connected complete Riemannian n-manifold of constant sectional curvature -1, realizable via the hyperboloid, Poincare disk, or upper half-space model.

nodes.name: Cartan's theorem on space forms
nodes.description: Two simply connected complete Riemannian manifolds of the same dimension and same constant sectional curvature are isometric.

nodes.name: Classification of space forms
nodes.description: Every complete Riemannian manifold of constant sectional curvature k is isometric to M_k^n / Gamma where M_k^n is the simply connected model space and Gamma is a discrete group of isometries acting freely.

nodes.name: Energy functional
nodes.description: The functional E(gamma) = (1/2) integral_a^b |gamma'(t)|^2 dt on piecewise smooth curves, whose critical points are geodesics parametrized proportionally to arc length.

nodes.name: First variation of energy
nodes.description: For a variation gamma_s of a curve, dE/ds|_{s=0} = -integral <V, nabla_{gamma'} gamma'> dt + boundary terms, showing critical points of energy are geodesics.

nodes.name: First variation of arc length
nodes.description: The derivative dL/ds|_{s=0} for a variation of a curve, showing critical points of arc length among fixed-endpoint curves are geodesics.

nodes.name: Second variation of energy
nodes.description: For a proper variation of a geodesic, d^2E/ds^2|_{s=0} = integral_0^l (|V'|^2 - <R(gamma', V)gamma', V>) dt, relating stability of geodesics to curvature.

nodes.name: Index form
nodes.description: The symmetric bilinear form I(V, W) = integral_0^l (<V', W'> - <R(gamma', V)gamma', W>) dt on vector fields along a geodesic, encoding the second variation of energy.

nodes.name: Synge's lemma
nodes.description: On a manifold with positive sectional curvature, a closed geodesic admits a length-decreasing variation via parallel transport whenever orientation is preserved around the loop.

nodes.name: Berger's lemma
nodes.description: On a complete Riemannian manifold, if a minimizing geodesic from p to q realizes d(p, q) then its tangent at q makes a controlled angle with other minimizing directions from p.

nodes.name: Klingenberg's injectivity radius estimate
nodes.description: On a compact simply connected Riemannian manifold with sectional curvature 0 < K <= K_max, the injectivity radius satisfies inj(M) >= pi / sqrt(K_max).

nodes.name: Injectivity radius
nodes.description: The largest radius r such that exp_p is a diffeomorphism on B(0, r) in T_pM; globally inj(M) = inf_p inj(p) equals the distance from p to its cut locus.

nodes.name: Toponogov comparison (hinge version)
nodes.description: If K >= k and a geodesic hinge in M has sides a, b with angle alpha, then the opposite side length is at most the corresponding length in the model space of curvature k.

nodes.name: Index of a geodesic
nodes.description: The maximum dimension of a subspace on which the index form I is negative definite, counting independent directions that decrease energy along the geodesic.

nodes.name: Nullity of a geodesic
nodes.description: The dimension of the null space of the index form I, equal to the multiplicity of the terminal point as a conjugate point.

nodes.name: Morse index theorem
nodes.description: The index of a geodesic equals the total number of interior conjugate points counted with multiplicity.

nodes.name: Byers' theorem
nodes.description: Every solvable subgroup of the fundamental group of a compact Riemannian manifold with strictly negative sectional curvature is infinite cyclic.

nodes.name: Closed geodesic in free homotopy class
nodes.description: On a compact Riemannian manifold, every nontrivial free homotopy class of closed curves contains a closed geodesic of minimal length.

nodes.name: Geodesic variation
nodes.description: A smooth map f : (-epsilon, epsilon) x [a,b] -> M such that each curve t -> f(s,t) is a geodesic, used to derive the Jacobi equation.

nodes.name: Energy vs length minimizers
nodes.description: By Cauchy-Schwarz, E(gamma) >= L(gamma)^2/(b-a) with equality iff gamma has constant speed, so among constant-speed curves, energy and length minimizers coincide.

nodes.name: Laplacian comparison theorem
nodes.description: Under Ric >= (n-1)k the Laplacian of the distance function satisfies Delta r <= Delta_k r where Delta_k r is the Laplacian in the model space of curvature k.

nodes.name: Geodesic convexity
nodes.description: A subset C of a Riemannian manifold is geodesically convex if any two points in C are joined by a unique minimizing geodesic lying entirely in C.

nodes.name: Normal coordinate computation
nodes.function_signature: (Riemannian manifold, point p, geometric quantity) -> (Simplified expression at p)
nodes.description: Evaluating geometric expressions in normal coordinates where Christoffel symbols vanish and the metric is Euclidean to first order, simplifying tensor computations at the center.

nodes.name: Sturm-Liouville comparison for Jacobi fields
nodes.function_signature: (ODE comparison of Jacobi field norms under curvature bounds) -> (Norm estimates for Jacobi fields)
nodes.description: Applying Sturm comparison theorems to the scalar ODE satisfied by Jacobi field norms to obtain bounds via curvature bounds, the key analytic tool behind Rauch comparison.

nodes.name: Covering space argument for negative curvature
nodes.function_signature: (Complete manifold with K < 0, subgroup of pi_1) -> (Algebraic constraints on pi_1)
nodes.description: Lifting geodesics to the universal cover (diffeomorphic to R^n by Cartan-Hadamard) to transfer geometric rigidity to algebraic constraints on the fundamental group.

nodes.name: Comparison of Jacobi fields
nodes.function_signature: (Jacobi fields on M with curvature bounds, Jacobi fields on model space) -> (Pointwise norm inequalities)
nodes.description: Comparing Jacobi field magnitudes on a manifold with curvature bounds to those on a constant-curvature model space to deduce distance, volume, and topology estimates.

nodes.name: Smoothly compatible charts
nodes.description: Two charts (U,φ) and (V,ψ) such that the transition map ψ ∘ φ⁻¹: φ(U ∩ V) → ψ(U ∩ V) is a C^∞ diffeomorphism.

nodes.name: Smooth atlas
nodes.description: An atlas in which every pair of charts is smoothly compatible.

nodes.name: Maximal smooth atlas (smooth structure)
nodes.description: A smooth atlas not properly contained in any larger smooth atlas; the unique maximal atlas containing a given smooth atlas.

nodes.name: Interior and boundary of a manifold with boundary
nodes.description: Int M consists of points with neighborhoods homeomorphic to open subsets of R^n; ∂M consists of points mapped to ∂H^n under some chart.

nodes.name: Product manifold
nodes.description: The Cartesian product M × N of smooth manifolds carries a unique smooth structure making the product charts smooth.

nodes.name: Smooth manifold chart lemma
nodes.description: If a set M has a countable collection of injections into R^n whose transition maps are smooth and images are open, then M has a unique smooth manifold structure making these charts smooth.

nodes.name: Invariance of the boundary
nodes.description: For a topological manifold with boundary, ∂M and Int M are disjoint with M = Int M ∪ ∂M; no point is simultaneously interior and boundary.

nodes.name: Smooth function ring C^∞(M)
nodes.description: The commutative R-algebra of all smooth real-valued functions on M with pointwise operations.

nodes.name: Smooth extension lemma
nodes.description: A smooth function on a closed subset A of a smooth manifold (in the sense of local smooth extensions) extends to a smooth function on all of M.

nodes.name: Exhaustion function
nodes.description: A smooth function f: M → R whose sublevel sets {f ≤ c} are compact for every c; every smooth manifold admits one.

nodes.name: Derivation at a point (tangent vector)
nodes.description: A tangent vector at p ∈ M defined as a linear map v: C^∞(M) → R satisfying the Leibniz rule v(fg) = f(p)v(g) + g(p)v(f).

nodes.name: Coordinate basis for tangent space
nodes.description: Given a chart (U,φ) with coordinates (x^1,...,x^n), the partial derivative operators ∂/∂x^i|_p form a basis for T_pM.

nodes.name: Differential of a smooth map
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap F: M → N, Point p) → LinearMap(T_pM, T_{F(p)}N)
nodes.description: The differential dF_p: T_pM → T_{F(p)}N defined by (dF_p(v))(f) = v(f ∘ F) for v ∈ T_pM and f ∈ C^∞(N).

nodes.name: Chain rule for differentials
nodes.description: For smooth maps F: M → N and G: N → P, the differential satisfies d(G ∘ F)_p = dG_{F(p)} ∘ dF_p.

nodes.name: Natural coordinates on TM
nodes.description: A chart (U,φ) for M induces coordinates (x^1,...,x^n, v^1,...,v^n) on π⁻¹(U) ⊆ TM via v = v^i ∂/∂x^i|_p.

nodes.name: Velocity of a curve
nodes.description: For a smooth curve γ: (a,b) → M, the velocity vector γ'(t) ∈ T_{γ(t)}M is defined as dγ_t(d/dt).

nodes.name: Smooth map of constant rank
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap F: M → N, r ∈ N) → Prop
nodes.description: A smooth map F: M → N has constant rank r if rank(dF_p) = r for all p ∈ M.

nodes.name: Inverse function theorem for manifolds
nodes.description: A smooth map F: M → N is a local diffeomorphism if and only if dF_p is a linear isomorphism for every p ∈ M.

nodes.name: Global rank theorem
nodes.description: A smooth map of constant rank that is surjective is a smooth submersion; one that is injective is a smooth immersion.

nodes.name: Local immersion theorem
nodes.description: If dF_p is injective at p, then F is a smooth immersion on some neighborhood of p, and in suitable coordinates has the canonical inclusion form.

nodes.name: Local submersion theorem
nodes.description: If dF_p is surjective at p, then F is a smooth submersion on some neighborhood of p, and in suitable coordinates has the canonical projection form.

nodes.name: Local section of a submersion
nodes.description: Every smooth submersion admits smooth local sections through every point in its image.

nodes.name: Smooth covering map
nodes.description: A smooth surjective map π: E → M such that every point of M has a neighborhood U evenly covered by π (π⁻¹(U) is a disjoint union of open sets each mapped diffeomorphically onto U).

nodes.name: Embedded submanifold (regular submanifold)
nodes.description: A subset S ⊆ M that is a smooth manifold in the subspace topology with the inclusion S ↪ M a smooth embedding.

nodes.name: Slice chart (adapted chart)
nodes.description: A chart (U,φ) for M such that S ∩ U is mapped by φ to the intersection of φ(U) with a coordinate subspace R^k × {0} ⊆ R^n.

nodes.name: Local slice criterion for embedded submanifolds
nodes.description: A subset S ⊆ M is an embedded k-submanifold if and only if around each point of S there exists a slice chart.

nodes.name: Immersed submanifold
nodes.description: A subset S ⊆ M with a smooth manifold topology (possibly finer than subspace topology) such that the inclusion is a smooth immersion.

nodes.name: Level set
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap F: M → N, c ∈ N) → Subset(M)
nodes.description: For F: M → N smooth and c ∈ N, the level set F⁻¹(c) = {p ∈ M : F(p) = c}.

nodes.name: Regular value
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap F: M → N, c ∈ N) → Prop
nodes.description: A point c ∈ N is a regular value of F: M → N if dF_p is surjective for every p ∈ F⁻¹(c).

nodes.name: Tangent space to a level set
nodes.description: If S = F⁻¹(c) for a regular value c, then T_pS = ker(dF_p) for every p ∈ S.

nodes.name: Set of measure zero in a manifold
nodes.description: A subset A ⊆ M has measure zero if φ(A ∩ U) has measure zero in R^n for every smooth chart (U,φ).

nodes.name: Critical point (manifold context)
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap F: M → N, Point p) → Prop
nodes.description: A point p ∈ M where dF_p: T_pM → T_{F(p)}N is not surjective; the image F(p) is a critical value.

nodes.name: Parametric transversality theorem
nodes.description: If F: M × S → N is transverse to a submanifold Z ⊆ N, then for almost every s ∈ S the restricted map F(·,s) is transverse to Z.

nodes.name: Lie group isomorphism
nodes.description: A Lie group homomorphism that is also a diffeomorphism; equivalently a bijective Lie group homomorphism (the inverse is automatically smooth).

nodes.name: Embedded Lie subgroup
nodes.description: A Lie subgroup that is an embedded submanifold, equivalently a closed subgroup of a Lie group.

nodes.name: Left and right translation
nodes.description: For g ∈ G, the diffeomorphism L_g: G → G defined by L_g(h) = gh (resp. R_g(h) = hg).

nodes.name: Smooth group action
nodes.type_signature: (LieGroup G, SmoothManifold M) → SmoothMap(G × M, M)
nodes.description: A smooth map θ: G × M → M satisfying θ(e,p) = p and θ(g,θ(h,p)) = θ(gh,p) for all g,h ∈ G, p ∈ M.

nodes.name: Orbit and stabilizer (isotropy group)
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothGroupAction G × M → M, Point p) → (Orbit O_p, Stabilizer G_p)
nodes.description: The orbit O_p = {g · p : g ∈ G}; the stabilizer G_p = {g ∈ G : g · p = p}, a closed Lie subgroup of G.

nodes.name: Free action
nodes.description: A group action such that g · p = p implies g = e, equivalently all stabilizers are trivial.

nodes.name: Proper action
nodes.description: A continuous group action such that the map (g,p) ↦ (g·p, p) is proper (preimages of compact sets are compact).

nodes.name: Quotient manifold theorem (for group actions)
nodes.description: If a Lie group acts smoothly, freely, and properly on a smooth manifold M, then M/G has a unique smooth manifold structure making the quotient map a smooth submersion.

nodes.name: Equivariant map
nodes.description: A map F: M → N between G-spaces satisfying F(g · p) = g · F(p) for all g ∈ G and p ∈ M.

nodes.name: Covering group theorem
nodes.description: If G is a connected Lie group, its universal covering space admits a unique Lie group structure making the covering map a Lie group homomorphism.

nodes.name: F-related vector fields
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap F: M → N, VectorField X on M, VectorField Y on N) → Prop
nodes.description: Vector fields X on M and Y on N are F-related if dF_p(X_p) = Y_{F(p)} for all p ∈ M.

nodes.name: Naturality of the Lie bracket
nodes.description: If X₁, X₂ are F-related to Y₁, Y₂ respectively, then [X₁,X₂] is F-related to [Y₁,Y₂].

nodes.name: Lie algebra homomorphism induced by Lie group homomorphism
nodes.description: A Lie group homomorphism F: G → H induces a Lie algebra homomorphism dF_e: g → h that preserves brackets.

nodes.name: Integral curve
nodes.type_signature: (VectorField X, Interval J, Point p) → SmoothCurve
nodes.description: A smooth curve γ: J → M such that γ'(t) = X_{γ(t)} for all t ∈ J.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of integral curves
nodes.description: For every smooth vector field X on M and every p ∈ M, there exists a unique maximal integral curve of X starting at p.

nodes.name: Flow domain
nodes.type_signature: VectorField X → OpenSubset D ⊆ R × M
nodes.description: The maximal flow domain D ⊆ R × M of a vector field X, an open subset containing {0} × M on which the flow is defined.

nodes.name: Complete vector field
nodes.description: A vector field whose flow is defined for all t ∈ R, i.e., the flow domain is all of R × M.

nodes.name: Flowout theorem
nodes.description: If S is an embedded submanifold and X a vector field nowhere tangent to S, the flow starting from S maps a neighborhood of {0} × S in R × S diffeomorphically onto a neighborhood of S in M.

nodes.name: Lie derivative equals Lie bracket
nodes.description: For smooth vector fields X and Y, the Lie derivative L_X Y equals the Lie bracket [X,Y].

nodes.name: Commuting vector fields and flows
nodes.description: Two smooth vector fields X,Y commute ([X,Y] = 0) if and only if their flows commute wherever both sides are defined.

nodes.name: Canonical form for nonvanishing vector fields
nodes.description: If X_p ≠ 0, there exist smooth coordinates near p in which X = ∂/∂x^1.

nodes.name: Local trivialization
nodes.type_signature: (VectorBundle E → M, OpenSet U ⊆ M) → Diffeomorphism
nodes.description: A fiber-preserving diffeomorphism Φ: π⁻¹(U) → U × R^k restricting to a linear isomorphism on each fiber.

nodes.name: Transition function of a vector bundle
nodes.type_signature: (LocalTrivialization α, LocalTrivialization β) → SmoothMap(U_α ∩ U_β, GL(k,R))
nodes.description: The map τ_{αβ}: U_α ∩ U_β → GL(k,R) describing the change of fiber coordinates between overlapping trivializations, satisfying the cocycle condition.

nodes.name: Section of a vector bundle
nodes.description: A smooth map σ: M → E such that π ∘ σ = id_M; a local section is defined on an open subset.

nodes.name: Local frame for a vector bundle
nodes.type_signature: (VectorBundle E → M, OpenSet U) → k-tuple of Sections
nodes.description: An ordered k-tuple (σ_1,...,σ_k) of local sections over U such that (σ_1(p),...,σ_k(p)) is a basis for E_p at every p ∈ U.

nodes.name: Vector bundle construction theorem
nodes.description: Given an open cover and smooth transition functions satisfying the cocycle condition, there is a smooth vector bundle realizing these transitions, unique up to isomorphism.

nodes.name: Bundle map (bundle homomorphism)
nodes.type_signature: (VectorBundle E → M, VectorBundle E' → M') → Pair(F,f)
nodes.description: A pair of smooth maps (F,f) with F: E → E' and f: M → M' such that π' ∘ F = f ∘ π and F is linear on each fiber.

nodes.name: Subbundle
nodes.description: A smooth vector bundle D ⊆ E whose total space is an embedded submanifold of E and whose inclusion is a bundle map with injective fiber maps.

nodes.name: Covector (cotangent vector)
nodes.description: An element of the dual space T_p*M = (T_pM)*; a linear functional ω: T_pM → R.

nodes.name: Coordinate covector fields (dx^i)
nodes.description: Given local coordinates (x^i), the covector fields dx^i defined by dx^i(∂/∂x^j) = δ^i_j, forming the dual basis to coordinate vector fields.

nodes.name: Covector field (1-form)
nodes.description: A smooth section ω: M → T*M of the cotangent bundle; a smooth assignment p ↦ ω_p ∈ T_p*M.

nodes.name: Line integral of a covector field
nodes.description: For a covector field ω and a piecewise smooth curve γ: [a,b] → M, the integral ∫_γ ω = ∫_a^b ω_{γ(t)}(γ'(t)) dt.

nodes.name: Conservative covector field characterization
nodes.description: A smooth covector field on a smooth manifold is exact if and only if its line integral around every piecewise smooth closed curve is zero.

nodes.name: Poincare lemma for covector fields
nodes.description: On a simply connected smooth manifold, every closed covector field is exact.

nodes.name: Multilinear map (k-tensor)
nodes.description: A multilinear map F: V^k → R; the space of covariant k-tensors on V is T^k(V*) = (V*)^{⊗k}.

nodes.name: Mixed tensor
nodes.type_signature: (VectorSpace V, k contravariant, l covariant) → T^{(k,l)}(V)
nodes.description: An element of V^{⊗k} ⊗ (V*)^{⊗l}, a multilinear map (V*)^k × V^l → R with k contravariant and l covariant indices.

nodes.name: Symmetric tensor
nodes.description: A covariant k-tensor α invariant under all permutations of its arguments: α(v_{σ(1)},...,v_{σ(k)}) = α(v_1,...,v_k) for every σ ∈ S_k.

nodes.name: Alternating tensor
nodes.description: A covariant k-tensor α such that α(v_{σ(1)},...,v_{σ(k)}) = (sgn σ) α(v_1,...,v_k) for every permutation σ; the space is Λ^k(V*).

nodes.name: Symmetrization and alternation operators
nodes.description: Sym(α) = (1/k!) Σ_σ α ∘ σ averages over all permutations; Alt(α) = (1/k!) Σ_σ (sgn σ) α ∘ σ antisymmetrizes.

nodes.name: Pullback of tensor fields
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap F: M → N, CovariantTensorField A on N) → CovariantTensorField on M
nodes.description: The pullback F*A defined by (F*A)_p(v_1,...,v_k) = A_{F(p)}(dF_p v_1,...,dF_p v_k).

nodes.name: Tensor characterization lemma
nodes.description: A map F: X(M)^k × Ω¹(M)^l → C^∞(M) is induced by a tensor field if and only if it is C^∞(M)-multilinear.

nodes.name: Existence of Riemannian metrics
nodes.description: Every smooth manifold admits a Riemannian metric, constructed via partitions of unity.

nodes.name: Musical isomorphisms (flat and sharp)
nodes.description: The Riemannian metric induces ♭: TM → T*M by v ↦ g(v,·) with inverse ♯: T*M → TM.

nodes.name: Pseudo-Riemannian metric
nodes.description: A smooth symmetric covariant 2-tensor field that is nondegenerate but not necessarily positive definite at each point; the signature (r,s) counts positive and negative directions.

nodes.name: Pseudo-Riemannian manifold
nodes.description: A smooth manifold equipped with a pseudo-Riemannian metric; Lorentzian manifolds are the special case of signature (n−1,1).

nodes.name: Interior multiplication (contraction)
nodes.description: The interior product ι_X: Ω^k(M) → Ω^{k−1}(M) defined by (ι_X ω)(Y_1,...,Y_{k−1}) = ω(X,Y_1,...,Y_{k−1}), an antiderivation of degree −1.

nodes.name: Invariant formula for the exterior derivative
nodes.description: For a k-form ω and vector fields X_0,...,X_k: dω(X_0,...,X_k) = Σ_i (−1)^i X_i(ω(...X̂_i...)) + Σ_{i<j} (−1)^{i+j} ω([X_i,X_j],...X̂_i...X̂_j...).

nodes.name: Orientation of a vector space
nodes.description: An equivalence class of ordered bases, where two bases are equivalent if the change-of-basis matrix has positive determinant.

nodes.name: Oriented double cover
nodes.description: Every connected nonorientable smooth manifold has a connected orientable double cover M̃ with a 2-sheeted smooth covering map π: M̃ → M.

nodes.name: Riemannian volume form
nodes.description: The unique n-form dV_g such that dV_g(E_1,...,E_n) = 1 for every oriented orthonormal frame; in coordinates dV_g = √(det g_{ij}) dx^1 ∧ ··· ∧ dx^n.

nodes.name: Integration of differential forms on oriented manifolds
nodes.description: The integral ∫_M ω of a compactly supported n-form on an oriented n-manifold, defined via oriented atlas and partition of unity, independent of choices.

nodes.name: Induced boundary orientation
nodes.description: The boundary ∂M inherits an orientation by the convention that an outward-pointing vector followed by an oriented basis for T_p(∂M) gives an oriented basis for T_pM.

nodes.name: Manifold with corners
nodes.description: A second-countable Hausdorff space locally modeled on the corner spaces R^n_k = {x ∈ R^n : x^{n−k+1} ≥ 0,...,x^n ≥ 0}, with smooth transition maps.

nodes.name: Stokes's theorem for manifolds with corners
nodes.description: Stokes's theorem extends to oriented manifolds with corners: ∫_M dω = ∫_{∂M} ω, where boundary faces are smooth manifolds with corners of one lower dimension.

nodes.name: Induced map on de Rham cohomology
nodes.description: A smooth map F induces a pullback F*: H^k_{dR}(N) → H^k_{dR}(M), functorial: (G∘F)* = F*∘G* and id* = id.

nodes.name: Homotopy invariance of de Rham cohomology
nodes.description: If F,G: M → N are smoothly homotopic, then F* = G* on H^k_{dR}; homotopy equivalent manifolds have isomorphic de Rham cohomology.

nodes.name: Homotopy operator (cochain homotopy)
nodes.description: Construction of a linear map h satisfying h ∘ d + d ∘ h = i₁* − i₀*, proving homotopy invariance of de Rham cohomology.

nodes.name: Poincare lemma
nodes.description: Every closed differential form on a contractible manifold is exact: H^k_{dR}(R^n) = 0 for k ≥ 1.

nodes.name: Cohomology of spheres
nodes.description: H^k_{dR}(S^n) ≅ R if k = 0 or k = n, and H^k_{dR}(S^n) = 0 otherwise.

nodes.name: Smooth singular homology
nodes.description: The smooth singular homology groups H_k^∞(M; R) defined using smooth singular simplices; naturally isomorphic to ordinary singular homology H_k(M; R).

nodes.name: De Rham homomorphism
nodes.description: The map I: H^k_{dR}(M) → H^k(M; R) defined by [ω] ↦ [σ ↦ ∫_σ ω], integrating closed k-forms over smooth singular k-cycles.

nodes.name: Distribution (tangent subbundle)
nodes.description: A smooth subbundle D ⊆ TM of rank k, assigning a k-dimensional subspace D_p ⊆ T_pM to each point p smoothly.

nodes.name: Integral manifold of a distribution
nodes.description: A connected immersed submanifold N ⊆ M such that T_pN = D_p for every p ∈ N.

nodes.name: Integrable distribution
nodes.description: A distribution that admits an integral manifold through every point of M.

nodes.name: Differential form criterion for involutivity
nodes.description: A rank-k distribution D = ker{ω^1,...,ω^{n-k}} is involutive if and only if each dω^i ∧ ω^1 ∧ ··· ∧ ω^{n-k} = 0.

nodes.name: Lie subalgebra-Lie subgroup correspondence
nodes.description: Every Lie subalgebra h ⊆ g = Lie(G) is the Lie algebra of a unique connected Lie subgroup H of G, obtained as a maximal integral manifold of the left-invariant distribution generated by h.

nodes.name: Exponential map of a Lie group
nodes.description: The map exp: g → G defined by exp(X) = γ_X(1) where γ_X is the one-parameter subgroup tangent to X at e; a smooth map with d(exp)_0 = id_g.

nodes.name: Continuous homomorphisms between Lie groups are smooth
nodes.description: Every continuous group homomorphism between Lie groups is automatically smooth.

nodes.name: Infinitesimal generator of a group action
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothAction G × M → M, X ∈ g) → VectorField on M
nodes.description: The vector field X̂ on M defined by X̂_p = d/dt|_{t=0} θ(exp(tX), p), generating the flow t ↦ θ(exp(tX), ·).

nodes.name: Adjoint representation of the Lie algebra
nodes.description: The representation ad: g → gl(g) defined by ad(X)(Y) = [X,Y]; the differential of Ad at the identity.

nodes.name: Homogeneous space
nodes.description: A smooth manifold G/H where G is a Lie group and H a closed subgroup, with natural transitive G-action and smooth structure from the quotient manifold theorem.

nodes.name: Covering manifold
nodes.description: A smooth covering map π: M̃ → M where M̃ inherits a unique smooth structure from M making π a local diffeomorphism.

nodes.name: Symplectic form on a vector space
nodes.description: A nondegenerate skew-symmetric bilinear form ω: V × V → R; the dimension of V must be even.

nodes.name: Symplectomorphism
nodes.description: A diffeomorphism F: (M₁,ω₁) → (M₂,ω₂) satisfying F*ω₂ = ω₁.

nodes.name: Contact structure
nodes.description: A smooth hyperplane distribution ξ = ker α on a (2n+1)-dimensional manifold, where α ∧ (dα)^n ≠ 0 everywhere (maximal non-integrability).

nodes.name: Contact manifold
nodes.description: An odd-dimensional smooth manifold equipped with a contact structure.

nodes.name: Cotangent bundle as symplectic manifold
nodes.description: T*M carries a canonical symplectic structure ω = −dλ where λ is the tautological 1-form defined by λ_{(p,ξ)}(v) = ξ(dπ(v)).

nodes.name: Chart computation technique
nodes.function_signature: (GlobalSmoothProperty) → (LocalCoordinateVerification)
nodes.description: Verifying global smooth-manifold properties by working in local coordinate charts and checking expressions transform correctly under transition maps.

nodes.name: Rank theorem technique
nodes.function_signature: (SmoothMap of constant rank) → (Normal form in suitable coordinates)
nodes.description: Using the constant rank theorem to put smooth maps into canonical form in suitable coordinates, simplifying local analysis of submersions and immersions.

nodes.name: Flow box / straightening technique
nodes.function_signature: (NonvanishingVectorField) → (Coordinates with X = ∂/∂x^1)
nodes.description: Using the flow of a nonvanishing vector field to construct coordinates in which the field takes the standard form ∂/∂x^1.

nodes.name: Mayer-Vietoris induction
nodes.function_signature: (OpenCover M = U ∪ V) → (H^k_{dR}(M) via long exact sequence)
nodes.description: Computing de Rham cohomology by decomposing M = U ∪ V and using the Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence recursively.

nodes.name: Exhaustion by compact sets technique
nodes.function_signature: (NoncompactManifold, LocalProperty) → (GlobalProperty)
nodes.description: Constructing global objects on noncompact manifolds by working on an increasing sequence of compact subsets covering M.

nodes.name: Smooth maps into Euclidean space (gluing lemma)
nodes.function_signature: (LocalSmoothData, PartitionOfUnity) → (GlobalSmoothMap)
nodes.description: Using partitions of unity to construct global smooth maps and functions by patching together locally defined smooth data.

nodes.name: Space form
nodes.description: A complete simply connected Riemannian manifold of constant sectional curvature k: Euclidean space (k=0), sphere (k>0), or hyperbolic space (k<0).

nodes.name: Principal curvatures
nodes.type_signature: (Regular surface S ⊂ ℝ³, point p ∈ S) → (κ₁, κ₂) ∈ ℝ²
nodes.description: The eigenvalues κ₁, κ₂ of the shape operator (Weingarten map) at a point of a surface in ℝ³, giving the extremal normal curvatures.

nodes.name: Mean curvature of a surface
nodes.type_signature: (Regular surface S ⊂ ℝ³, point p ∈ S) → H ∈ ℝ
nodes.description: The arithmetic mean H = (κ₁ + κ₂)/2 of the principal curvatures at a point, equivalently half the trace of the shape operator.

nodes.name: Riemannian submanifold
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (N, h), embedded submanifold M ↪ N) → (M, ι*h)
nodes.description: An embedded or immersed submanifold of a Riemannian manifold equipped with the pullback (induced) metric from the ambient space.

nodes.name: Riemannian distance induces the manifold topology
nodes.description: The metric topology on a connected Riemannian manifold induced by the Riemannian distance function d_g coincides with the original manifold topology.

nodes.name: Riemannian density
nodes.description: The canonical density |dV_g| associated to a Riemannian metric, allowing integration on possibly non-orientable manifolds without choosing an orientation.

nodes.name: Euclidean space (Riemannian)
nodes.description: The manifold ℝⁿ equipped with the standard flat Riemannian metric g_E = δᵢⱼ dxⁱ dxʲ, the model space of zero curvature.

nodes.name: Round metric on Sⁿ
nodes.description: The standard Riemannian metric on the n-sphere induced by the embedding Sⁿ ⊂ ℝⁿ⁺¹, having constant sectional curvature +1.

nodes.name: Poincaré ball model
nodes.description: The open unit ball Bⁿ ⊂ ℝⁿ with the conformally flat metric g_P = 4(1 - |x|²)⁻² g_E, a model of hyperbolic space Hⁿ.

nodes.name: Poincaré half-space model
nodes.description: The upper half-space {x ∈ ℝⁿ : xₙ > 0} with metric g_H = xₙ⁻² (dx₁² + ⋯ + dxₙ²), a model of hyperbolic space Hⁿ.

nodes.name: Homogeneous Riemannian manifold
nodes.description: A Riemannian manifold whose isometry group acts transitively, so the geometry is the same at every point.

nodes.name: Isotropic Riemannian manifold
nodes.description: A Riemannian manifold such that for every point p and every unit tangent vector at p, there exists an isometry fixing p and mapping the vector to any other unit tangent vector at p.

nodes.name: Frame-homogeneous Riemannian manifold
nodes.description: A Riemannian manifold whose isometry group acts transitively on the orthonormal frame bundle, the strongest homogeneity condition.

nodes.name: Classification of frame-homogeneous spaces
nodes.description: A connected frame-homogeneous Riemannian manifold is isometric to a Euclidean space, a sphere, a real projective space, or a hyperbolic space.

nodes.name: Riemannian covering
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (M, g), covering map π: M̃ → M) → (M̃, π*g)
nodes.description: A covering space of a Riemannian manifold equipped with the unique pullback metric making the covering map a local isometry.

nodes.name: Connection in a local frame
nodes.description: The connection 1-forms ωⁱⱼ defined by ∇_X Eⱼ = ωⁱⱼ(X) Eᵢ, representing the connection relative to a chosen local frame of the vector bundle.

nodes.name: Parallel transport characterizes connection
nodes.description: A connection on a vector bundle is uniquely determined by its parallel transport maps along curves; conversely any smooth system of parallel transport maps defines a connection.

nodes.name: Metric connection
nodes.description: A connection ∇ on a Riemannian manifold satisfying ∇g = 0, equivalently parallel transport preserves inner products.

nodes.name: Symmetric (torsion-free) connection
nodes.description: A connection with vanishing torsion tensor: ∇_X Y - ∇_Y X = [X, Y] for all vector fields X, Y.

nodes.name: Christoffel symbols of the Levi-Civita connection
nodes.description: The explicit formula Γᵏᵢⱼ = ½gᵏˡ(∂ᵢgⱼˡ + ∂ⱼgᵢˡ - ∂ˡgᵢⱼ) for the Christoffel symbols of the Levi-Civita connection in local coordinates.

nodes.name: Geodesics have constant speed
nodes.description: A geodesic γ satisfying ∇_{γ'} γ' = 0 has constant speed |γ'(t)|_g, since d/dt <γ', γ'> = 2<∇_{γ'} γ', γ'> = 0.

nodes.name: Exponential map is a local diffeomorphism
nodes.description: For each p ∈ M, the exponential map exp_p is a diffeomorphism from a neighborhood of 0 in T_pM onto a neighborhood of p in M, since d(exp_p)_0 = id.

nodes.name: Fermi coordinates
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (M, g), geodesic γ) → coordinate system near γ
nodes.description: Coordinates adapted to a geodesic γ constructed via the exponential map of the normal bundle, in which Christoffel symbols vanish along γ and the metric is Euclidean to first order along γ.

nodes.name: Riemannian geodesics as locally length-minimizing curves
nodes.description: A curve in a Riemannian manifold is locally length-minimizing if and only if it is a geodesic (up to reparametrization), and sufficiently short geodesic segments are globally minimizing.

nodes.name: Variation of a curve
nodes.type_signature: (Curve γ : [a,b] → M) → (F : (-ε,ε) × [a,b] → M with F(0,·) = γ)
nodes.description: A smooth one-parameter family of curves F(s, t) with F(0, t) = γ(t), used to derive the first and second variation formulas for length and energy.

nodes.name: Uniformly normal neighborhood
nodes.description: An open set U such that U ⊂ B(p, r) for some normal ball B(p, r) for every p ∈ U, ensuring uniform control of the exponential map.

nodes.name: Distance function from a point
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (M, g), point p ∈ M) → r_p : M → ℝ
nodes.description: The function r_p(q) = d(p, q) giving the Riemannian distance from a fixed point p; smooth on M \ ({p} ∪ Cut(p)) with |grad r_p| = 1.

nodes.name: Cut locus has measure zero
nodes.description: The cut locus Cut(p) of any point p in a complete Riemannian manifold has measure zero with respect to the Riemannian volume measure.

nodes.name: Riemann curvature endomorphism
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (M, g), connection ∇) → R : 𝔛(M)³ → 𝔛(M)
nodes.description: The (1,3)-tensor R(X,Y)Z = ∇_X∇_Y Z - ∇_Y∇_X Z - ∇_{[X,Y]} Z measuring the failure of second covariant derivatives to commute.

nodes.name: Second Bianchi identity
nodes.description: The differential Bianchi identity: (∇_X R)(Y,Z) + (∇_Y R)(Z,X) + (∇_Z R)(X,Y) = 0 for the Riemann curvature tensor of the Levi-Civita connection.

nodes.name: Schouten tensor
nodes.description: The tensor A = (1/(n-2))(Ric - S/(2(n-1)) g) appearing in the decomposition of the Riemann tensor into Weyl, Ricci, and scalar parts.

nodes.name: Decomposition of the Riemann curvature tensor
nodes.description: The Riemann curvature tensor decomposes orthogonally as Rm = W + A ∧ g where W is the Weyl tensor and A is the Schouten tensor, separating conformal, Ricci, and scalar curvature components.

nodes.name: Curvature of constant-curvature spaces
nodes.description: A Riemannian manifold has constant sectional curvature k if and only if Rm = k/2 (g ∧ g), i.e., R(X,Y)Z = k(<Y,Z>X - <X,Z>Y).

nodes.name: Contracted second Bianchi identity
nodes.description: Contracting the second Bianchi identity yields div(Ric) = ½ dS, equivalently div(Ric - ½Sg) = 0, showing the Einstein tensor is divergence-free.

nodes.name: Curvature of product manifolds
nodes.description: For a Riemannian product (M₁ × M₂, g₁ ⊕ g₂), the curvature tensor splits: mixed sectional curvatures vanish and R_{M₁×M₂} = R_{M₁} + R_{M₂} in the appropriate sense.

nodes.name: Gauss formula
nodes.description: For an isometric immersion M ↪ N, the ambient covariant derivative decomposes as ∇̃_X Y = ∇_X Y + II(X, Y) into tangential and normal components.

nodes.name: Weingarten equation
nodes.description: For a normal vector field η along a submanifold, ∇̃_X η decomposes as -A_η X + ∇⊥_X η, relating the shape operator A_η to the normal connection.

nodes.name: Curvature of hypersurfaces
nodes.description: For a hypersurface with unit normal N and shape operator A, the Gauss equation gives K_M(X,Y) = K_N(X,Y) + <AX,X><AY,Y> - <AX,Y>², relating intrinsic curvature to the eigenvalues of A.

nodes.name: Fundamental theorem of hypersurface theory
nodes.description: A simply connected domain in ℝⁿ with a Riemannian metric and symmetric (0,2)-tensor satisfying the Gauss and Codazzi-Mainardi equations can be isometrically immersed in ℝⁿ⁺¹, uniquely up to rigid motion.

nodes.name: Local Gauss-Bonnet theorem
nodes.description: For a geodesic polygon P on an oriented Riemannian surface, ∫∫_P K dA + ∫_{∂P} κ_g ds + Σ θᵢ = 2π, relating total Gaussian curvature, geodesic curvature of the boundary, and exterior angles.

nodes.name: Gauss-Bonnet theorem with boundary
nodes.description: For a compact oriented Riemannian 2-manifold M with boundary, ∫_M K dA + ∫_{∂M} κ_g ds = 2π χ(M), extending Gauss-Bonnet to manifolds with boundary.

nodes.name: Euler characteristic
nodes.description: The alternating sum χ(X) = Σ (-1)^k rank H_k(X) of Betti numbers, a topological invariant equal to V - E + F for polyhedra.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of Jacobi fields
nodes.description: Given initial conditions J(0) and J'(0) along a geodesic, there exists a unique Jacobi field satisfying the Jacobi equation; the space of Jacobi fields along a geodesic has dimension 2n.

nodes.name: Jacobi fields on constant-curvature spaces
nodes.description: On a space of constant sectional curvature K, normal Jacobi fields with J(0) = 0 have the form J(t) = sn_K(t) E(t) where sn_K is sin(√K t)/√K, t, or sinh(√|K| t)/√|K| accordingly.

nodes.name: No conjugate points before cut point
nodes.description: Along a geodesic from p, the first conjugate point (if it exists) occurs at or after the cut point; there are no conjugate points along a minimizing geodesic segment except possibly at the endpoint.

nodes.name: Second variation of arc length
nodes.description: For a normal variation of a unit-speed geodesic γ with variation field V, d²L/ds²|_{s=0} = ∫₀ˡ (|V'⊥|² - <R(γ',V)γ',V>) dt, relating curvature to length stability.

nodes.name: Index form characterization of conjugate points
nodes.description: A geodesic segment has no interior conjugate points if and only if the index form I is positive definite on the space of proper normal vector fields along it.

nodes.name: Hessian comparison theorem
nodes.description: Under a sectional curvature bound K ≤ k (or K ≥ k), the Hessian of the distance function r from a point satisfies Hess(r) ≥ (≤) the corresponding Hessian in the model space of curvature k.

nodes.name: Relative volume comparison
nodes.description: Under Ric ≥ (n-1)k, the ratio Vol(B(p,r))/Vol_k(r) is non-increasing in r, where Vol_k(r) is the volume of a ball of radius r in the space form of curvature k.

nodes.name: Milnor's theorem on fundamental groups
nodes.description: The fundamental group of a compact Riemannian manifold with Ric ≥ 0 has polynomial growth; if Ric > 0 then π₁ is finite.

nodes.name: Weinstein's theorem (Riemannian)
nodes.description: An orientation-preserving isometry of a compact even-dimensional Riemannian manifold with positive sectional curvature has a fixed point.

nodes.name: Berger's quarter-pinched sphere theorem
nodes.description: A compact simply connected Riemannian n-manifold with ¼ < K ≤ 1 is homeomorphic to Sⁿ; the sharp version (Brendle-Schoen) gives diffeomorphism for ¼-pinching.

nodes.name: Killing vector field
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (M, g)) → X ∈ 𝔛(M) with L_X g = 0
nodes.description: A vector field X whose flow consists of isometries, equivalently satisfying the Killing equation ∇_i X_j + ∇_j X_i = 0.

nodes.name: Killing fields form a Lie algebra
nodes.description: The space of Killing vector fields on a Riemannian manifold is a finite-dimensional Lie algebra under the Lie bracket, isomorphic to the Lie algebra of the isometry group.

nodes.name: Maximum dimension of the isometry group
nodes.description: The isometry group of an n-dimensional Riemannian manifold has dimension at most n(n+1)/2, with equality if and only if the manifold has constant sectional curvature.

nodes.name: Cartan-Ambrose-Hicks theorem
nodes.description: A connection-preserving map between simply connected complete Riemannian manifolds that preserves the curvature tensor along all broken geodesics from a base point is a global isometry.

nodes.name: Local-to-global isometry extension
nodes.description: A local isometry from a complete connected Riemannian manifold into a simply connected Riemannian manifold is a covering map; if both are simply connected, it is a global isometry.

nodes.name: Flat Riemannian manifold
nodes.description: A Riemannian manifold with vanishing Riemann curvature tensor, locally isometric to Euclidean space.

nodes.name: Geodesic curvature
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian surface (S, g), curve γ ⊂ S) → κ_g : ℝ
nodes.description: The tangential component of the acceleration of a unit-speed curve on a surface, measuring deviation from being a geodesic; κ_g = <∇_{γ'}γ', n> where n is the unit normal within the surface.

nodes.name: Normal Jacobi field
nodes.description: The component of a Jacobi field perpendicular to the geodesic, satisfying the Jacobi equation independently; governs infinitesimal distance changes between nearby geodesics.

nodes.name: Tangential Jacobi field
nodes.description: The component of a Jacobi field tangent to the geodesic, always of the form (a + bt)γ'(t) and geometrically trivial, corresponding to reparametrization.

nodes.name: Parallel transport preserves inner products
nodes.description: For a metric connection (in particular the Levi-Civita connection), parallel transport along any curve is a linear isometry between the tangent spaces at the endpoints.

nodes.name: Variational methods for geodesics
nodes.function_signature: (Riemannian manifold, curve space, length/energy functional) → (Existence and properties of geodesics)
nodes.description: Using first and second variation formulas of length and energy functionals to characterize geodesics as critical points and study their stability and minimizing properties.

nodes.name: Symmetry and group action methods
nodes.function_signature: (Lie group G acting by isometries on (M, g)) → (Simplified geometric analysis via quotients, orbits, and invariant objects)
nodes.description: Exploiting transitive or cohomogeneity-one isometric group actions to reduce geometric problems to algebraic ones on homogeneous or cohomogeneity-one spaces.

nodes.name: Index form methods
nodes.function_signature: (Index form on vector fields along geodesic, conjugate point structure) → (Minimality, stability, and topology conclusions)
nodes.description: Using the index form and Morse index theorem to determine whether geodesics minimize, count conjugate points, and extract topological information from curvature bounds.

nodes.name: Geodesic deviation analysis
nodes.function_signature: (Jacobi equation along geodesic, curvature data) → (Behavior of nearby geodesics)
nodes.description: Analyzing the Jacobi equation to determine how nearby geodesics converge or diverge, detecting conjugate points and estimating distances.

nodes.name: Busemann function
nodes.type_signature: (Complete Riemannian manifold (M, g), ray γ : [0,∞) → M) → b_γ : M → ℝ
nodes.description: The function b_γ(q) = lim_{t→∞} (t - d(q, γ(t))), a convex exhaustion function on non-negatively curved manifolds, used in the splitting theorem and soul theorem.

nodes.name: Busemann function technique
nodes.function_signature: (Complete manifold with Ric ≥ 0, geodesic ray/line) → (Splitting, soul, and rigidity conclusions)
nodes.description: Constructing and analyzing Busemann functions to detect lines, produce splittings, and find totally convex compact submanifolds (souls) in nonnegative curvature.

nodes.name: Maximum principle (Riemannian)
nodes.function_signature: (Subharmonic/superharmonic function on Riemannian manifold, Laplacian comparison) → (Rigidity or vanishing conclusions)
