nodes.description: Applying the strong maximum principle or Laplacian comparison to subharmonic or superharmonic functions on complete Riemannian manifolds to deduce rigidity.

nodes.name: Product Riemannian manifold
nodes.description: The Cartesian product of Riemannian manifolds with the direct sum metric g₁ ⊕ g₂, having curvature decomposing as the direct sum of the factors' curvatures.

nodes.name: Warped product metric
nodes.type_signature: ((B, g_B), (F, g_F), f : B → ℝ₊) → (B ×_f F, g_B + f² g_F)
nodes.description: The metric g_B + f² g_F on the product B × F where f is a positive smooth function on B, generalizing surfaces of revolution and model spaces.

nodes.name: Curvature of warped products
nodes.description: For a warped product B ×_f F, the sectional curvatures are expressible in terms of curvatures of B and F and derivatives of f: e.g., K(X, V) = -(Hess f(X,X))/(f|X|²) for X tangent to B and V tangent to F.

nodes.name: Riemannian submersion
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (M, g), (B, h), surjective submersion π : M → B) → Prop
nodes.description: A smooth surjective submersion π : (M, g) → (B, h) whose differential restricted to horizontal spaces is a linear isometry, relating the geometry of total space, base, and fibers.

nodes.name: O'Neill's formula
nodes.description: For a Riemannian submersion π : M → B, the sectional curvature of B satisfies K_B(X,Y) = K_M(X̃,Ỹ) + ¾|[X̃,Ỹ]^V|² where X̃, Ỹ are horizontal lifts, showing the base has curvature ≥ that of the total space.

nodes.name: Ambrose-Singer holonomy theorem
nodes.description: The Lie algebra of the holonomy group of a connection equals the subspace of End(T_pM) generated by all parallel translates of curvature endomorphisms R(X,Y) along paths from p.

nodes.name: Volume of geodesic balls
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (M, g), point p, radius r) → Vol(B(p,r))
nodes.description: Vol(B(p,r)) = ω_n r^n (1 - S(p)/(6(n+2)) r² + O(r⁴)) where ω_n is the Euclidean ball volume and S(p) is scalar curvature, quantifying how curvature affects volume.

nodes.name: Laplacian (Riemannian)
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (M, g), f ∈ C^∞(M)) → Δf ∈ C^∞(M)
nodes.description: The Laplace-Beltrami operator Δf = div(grad f) = g^{ij}(∂²f/∂xⁱ∂xʲ - Γᵏᵢⱼ ∂f/∂xᵏ) on a Riemannian manifold, generalizing the Euclidean Laplacian.

nodes.name: Hessian (Riemannian)
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (M, g), f ∈ C^∞(M)) → Hess f ∈ Γ(S²T*M)
nodes.description: The covariant Hessian Hess f(X, Y) = <∇_X (grad f), Y> = (∇²f)(X,Y), the symmetric (0,2)-tensor of second covariant derivatives of f.

nodes.name: Gradient (Riemannian)
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (M, g), f ∈ C^∞(M)) → grad f ∈ 𝔛(M)
nodes.description: The vector field grad f = (df)♯ defined by g(grad f, X) = df(X) = X(f) for all X, the metric dual of the differential.

nodes.name: Divergence (Riemannian)
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (M, g), X ∈ 𝔛(M)) → div X ∈ C^∞(M)
nodes.description: The divergence div X = trace(Y ↦ ∇_Y X) = (1/√det g) ∂ᵢ(√det g Xⁱ), measuring the infinitesimal volume change of the flow of X.

nodes.name: Conformally flat manifold
nodes.description: A Riemannian manifold locally conformal to flat space: every point has a neighborhood where g = e^{2u} g_E for some smooth function u.

nodes.name: Weyl tensor vanishing and conformal flatness
nodes.description: In dimension n ≥ 4, a Riemannian manifold is conformally flat if and only if its Weyl tensor vanishes identically.

nodes.name: Cotton tensor
nodes.description: The tensor C_{ijk} = ∇_i R_{jk} - ∇_j R_{ik} - (1/(2(n-1)))(∇_i S g_{jk} - ∇_j S g_{ik}), the obstruction to conformal flatness in dimension 3.

nodes.name: Conformal flatness in dimension 3
nodes.description: In dimension 3, the Weyl tensor vanishes identically and a Riemannian manifold is conformally flat if and only if the Cotton tensor vanishes.

nodes.name: Normal bundle
nodes.type_signature: (Riemannian manifold (N, h), submanifold M ↪ N) → NM : vector bundle over M
nodes.description: The vector bundle NM over a Riemannian submanifold whose fiber at p is the orthogonal complement of T_pM in T_pN.

nodes.name: Comparison triangle
nodes.type_signature: (Geodesic triangle Δ in M, curvature bound k) → Δ̄ in M_k²
nodes.description: A geodesic triangle Δ̄ in the model space M_k² of constant curvature k with the same side lengths as a given triangle Δ in M, used in Toponogov and Alexandrov comparison.

nodes.name: Alexandrov angle comparison
nodes.description: On a Riemannian manifold with sectional curvature ≥ k, angles in a geodesic triangle are ≥ the corresponding angles in the comparison triangle in the space form of curvature k.

nodes.name: Ricci identity (commutation of covariant derivatives)
nodes.description: For a tensor field T, (∇²_{X,Y} - ∇²_{Y,X}) T = R(X,Y) · T, expressing the commutator of second covariant derivatives in terms of the curvature tensor acting on T.

nodes.name: Parallel transport along geodesics
nodes.function_signature: (Metric connection, geodesic γ, vector/frame at γ(0)) → (Isometrically transported vector/frame along γ)
nodes.description: Constructing parallel frames along geodesics to reduce geometric computations to ODE analysis, used in Synge's lemma, holonomy arguments, and comparison theorems.

nodes.name: Curvature estimation via comparison
nodes.function_signature: (Curvature bounds on manifold, model space quantities) → (Quantitative geometric estimates)
nodes.description: Using Rauch, Toponogov, Bishop-Gromov, and Laplacian comparison to convert curvature bounds into quantitative estimates for distances, volumes, eigenvalues, and angles.

nodes.name: Principal fibre bundle
nodes.description: A fibre bundle P(M, G) with fibre G and a free right G-action such that M = P/G and the projection π: P → M is the orbit map.

nodes.name: Frame bundle L(M)
nodes.description: The principal GL(n,ℝ)-bundle over M whose fibre at p consists of all ordered bases (linear frames) of T_pM.

nodes.name: Orthonormal frame bundle O(M)
nodes.description: The principal O(n)-subbundle of L(M) consisting of orthonormal frames with respect to a Riemannian metric.

nodes.name: Connection on a principal bundle
nodes.description: A smooth G-invariant distribution of horizontal subspaces H_u ⊂ T_uP complementary to the vertical subspace at each point of a principal bundle.

nodes.name: Horizontal lift of a curve
nodes.description: The unique curve in a principal bundle P projecting to a given base curve γ, with tangent vectors lying in the horizontal distribution of the connection.

nodes.name: Restricted holonomy group
nodes.description: The identity component Φ⁰(u) of the holonomy group, consisting of parallel transport around null-homotopic loops based at u.

nodes.name: Exterior covariant derivative
nodes.description: The operator D on tensorial forms on a principal bundle defined by Dφ(X₁,…,X_{k+1}) = dφ(hX₁,…,hX_{k+1}), projecting arguments to horizontal components.

nodes.name: Cartan structure equation
nodes.description: Ω = dω + ½[ω,ω], relating the curvature form Ω to the connection form ω on a principal bundle.

nodes.name: Bianchi identity on principal bundle
nodes.description: DΩ = 0, the vanishing of the exterior covariant derivative of the curvature form on a principal bundle.

nodes.name: Reduction theorem for connections
nodes.description: A connection on P(M,G) reduces to a connection on a subbundle Q(M,H) if and only if the holonomy group is contained in H.

nodes.name: Existence of connections on principal bundles
nodes.description: Every principal bundle over a paracompact base manifold admits a connection.

nodes.name: Induced connection on associated bundle
nodes.description: A connection on a principal bundle P induces a covariant derivative on every associated vector bundle P ×_G V.

nodes.name: Gauge transformation
nodes.description: A G-equivariant diffeomorphism f: P → P of a principal bundle covering the identity on the base manifold M.

nodes.name: Linear connection
nodes.description: A connection on the frame bundle L(M), equivalently a covariant derivative operator ∇ on TM satisfying C^∞-linearity in the first argument and the Leibniz rule.

nodes.name: Torsion tensor
nodes.description: The (1,2)-tensor T(X,Y) = ∇_X Y − ∇_Y X − [X,Y] of a linear connection, measuring the antisymmetric failure of covariant derivatives to commute with Lie brackets.

nodes.name: Canonical form (solder form) on L(M)
nodes.description: The ℝⁿ-valued 1-form θ on L(M) defined by θ_u(X) = u⁻¹(π_*X), providing the canonical identification of horizontal vectors with ℝⁿ.

nodes.name: Torsion form on L(M)
nodes.description: The ℝⁿ-valued 2-form Θ = Dθ on L(M), the exterior covariant derivative of the canonical form, encoding the torsion of the connection.

nodes.name: Structure equations of a linear connection
nodes.description: Θ = dθ + ω∧θ and Ω = dω + ω∧ω on L(M), expressing torsion and curvature in terms of the connection form and canonical form.

nodes.name: Development of curves
nodes.function_signature: (Curve on manifold with affine connection) → (Curve in affine tangent space)
nodes.description: Rolling a manifold with affine connection onto its tangent affine space along a curve, producing a curve in ℝⁿ that encodes parallel transport and torsion.

nodes.name: Parallel section
nodes.description: A section s of a vector bundle satisfying ∇s = 0, constant along horizontal lifts of all curves.

nodes.name: Fundamental theorem of Riemannian geometry
nodes.description: Every Riemannian manifold admits a unique torsion-free metric-compatible linear connection, the Levi-Civita connection.

nodes.name: Koszul formula
nodes.description: 2g(∇_X Y, Z) = Xg(Y,Z) + Yg(Z,X) − Zg(X,Y) − g(X,[Y,Z]) + g(Z,[X,Y]) + g(Y,[Z,X]), determining the Levi-Civita connection explicitly from the metric.

nodes.name: Interior product
nodes.description: The operator ι_X: Ω^k(M) → Ω^{k−1}(M) defined by contraction of a differential form with a vector field X.

nodes.name: Cartan's magic formula
nodes.description: L_X = ι_X ∘ d + d ∘ ι_X, expressing the Lie derivative of differential forms as the sum of interior product composed with exterior derivative and vice versa.

nodes.name: Affine transformation
nodes.description: A diffeomorphism of a manifold with linear connection that preserves the connection, mapping geodesics to geodesics with affine parameter.

nodes.name: Infinitesimal affine transformation
nodes.description: A vector field X with L_X∇ = 0, generating a local one-parameter group of affine transformations.

nodes.name: Killing equation
nodes.description: ∇_iX_j + ∇_jX_i = 0, the system of first-order PDEs characterizing Killing vector fields as infinitesimal isometries.

nodes.name: Maximum dimension of isometry group
nodes.description: dim Isom(Mⁿ, g) ≤ n(n+1)/2, with equality if and only if (M,g) has constant sectional curvature.

nodes.name: De Rham decomposition theorem
nodes.description: A complete simply-connected Riemannian manifold with reducible holonomy decomposes as a Riemannian product of irreducible factors, uniquely up to order.

nodes.name: Holonomy of flat connections
nodes.description: A connection is flat iff its restricted holonomy group is trivial; the full holonomy is then a quotient of the fundamental group π₁(M).

nodes.name: Symmetric space
nodes.description: A connected Riemannian manifold admitting at each point an involutive isometry (geodesic symmetry) with that point as isolated fixed point.

nodes.name: Locally symmetric space
nodes.description: A Riemannian manifold with parallel curvature tensor ∇R = 0, equivalently admitting local geodesic symmetries at every point.

nodes.name: Locally symmetric iff parallel curvature
nodes.description: A Riemannian manifold is locally symmetric if and only if the curvature tensor satisfies ∇R = 0.

nodes.name: Cartan's local-to-global symmetric space theorem
nodes.description: Every complete simply-connected locally symmetric Riemannian manifold is a globally symmetric space G/H.

nodes.name: Totally umbilic submanifold
nodes.description: A submanifold whose second fundamental form is proportional to the metric: h(X,Y) = g(X,Y)H for all tangent vectors X,Y.

nodes.name: Gauss map
nodes.description: For a hypersurface in Euclidean space, the map sending each point to its unit outward normal vector in the unit sphere Sⁿ⁻¹.

nodes.name: Flat normal connection
nodes.description: A normal connection with vanishing curvature R^⊥ = 0, equivalent to all shape operators commuting.

nodes.name: Reduction of codimension theorem
nodes.description: If the first normal space of a submanifold has constant dimension and the normal connection is flat on its orthogonal complement, then the submanifold lies in a totally geodesic submanifold of lower codimension.

nodes.name: Hermitian metric
nodes.description: A Riemannian metric g on a manifold with almost complex structure J satisfying g(JX, JY) = g(X,Y) for all tangent vectors.

nodes.name: Kähler form (fundamental 2-form)
nodes.description: The 2-form Ω(X,Y) = g(JX,Y) associated to a Hermitian metric, whose closure dΩ = 0 characterizes Kähler manifolds.

nodes.name: Kähler potential
nodes.description: A local smooth real-valued function Φ on a Kähler manifold such that the Kähler metric is g_{iȷ̄} = ∂²Φ/∂zⁱ∂z̄ʲ.

nodes.name: Holomorphic sectional curvature
nodes.description: The sectional curvature K(X, JX) restricted to J-invariant 2-planes (complex lines) in the tangent space of a Kähler manifold.

nodes.name: Constant holomorphic sectional curvature characterization
nodes.description: A Kähler manifold has constant holomorphic sectional curvature c iff its curvature tensor equals (c/4) times the standard expression involving g, J, and the symmetries of the Kähler structure.

nodes.name: Complex space form
nodes.description: A simply connected complete Kähler manifold of constant holomorphic sectional curvature: ℂPⁿ (c>0), ℂⁿ (c=0), or ℂHⁿ (c<0).

nodes.name: Complex projective space ℂPⁿ
nodes.description: The quotient (ℂⁿ⁺¹ \ {0})/ℂ* with the Fubini–Study metric, the unique (up to scale) complete Kähler manifold of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature.

nodes.name: Fubini–Study metric
nodes.description: The canonical Kähler metric on ℂPⁿ induced from the round metric on S²ⁿ⁺¹ via the Hopf fibration, having constant holomorphic sectional curvature.

nodes.name: Type decomposition of differential forms
nodes.description: On a complex manifold, the decomposition Ωᵏ = ⊕_{p+q=k} Ω^{p,q} into (p,q)-type forms with p holomorphic and q antiholomorphic indices.

nodes.name: Holomorphic vector bundle
nodes.description: A complex vector bundle over a complex manifold whose transition functions are holomorphic maps.

nodes.name: Ricci form of a Kähler manifold
nodes.description: The closed (1,1)-form ρ = −i∂∂̄ log det(g_{jk̄}), representing 2π times the first Chern class c₁(M).

nodes.name: Bochner curvature tensor
nodes.description: The Kähler analogue of the Weyl conformal curvature tensor, the conformally invariant component of the curvature respecting the complex structure.

nodes.name: Kähler submanifold
nodes.description: A complex submanifold of a Kähler manifold that inherits a Kähler structure and is necessarily minimal.

nodes.name: Reductive homogeneous space
nodes.description: A homogeneous space G/H with an Ad(H)-invariant decomposition 𝔤 = 𝔥 ⊕ 𝔪, identifying 𝔪 with the tangent space at the origin.

nodes.name: Naturally reductive homogeneous space
nodes.description: A reductive homogeneous space satisfying ⟨[X,Y]_𝔪, Z⟩ + ⟨Y, [X,Z]_𝔪⟩ = 0 for all X,Y,Z ∈ 𝔪, ensuring geodesics are orbits of one-parameter subgroups.

nodes.name: Invariant connection on G/H
nodes.description: A G-invariant connection on a homogeneous space, determined by a linear map Λ: 𝔪 → 𝔤𝔩(𝔪) compatible with the Ad(H)-action.

nodes.name: Canonical connection on reductive homogeneous space
nodes.description: The unique G-invariant connection with T(X,Y) = −[X,Y]_𝔪 and ∇R = ∇T = 0, where parallel transport corresponds to the reductive decomposition.

nodes.name: Curvature of naturally reductive spaces
nodes.description: R(X,Y)Z = −[[X,Y]_𝔥, Z] for X,Y,Z ∈ 𝔪, reducing curvature computation to Lie bracket operations in a naturally reductive homogeneous space.

nodes.name: Isotropy representation
nodes.description: The representation of the isotropy group H on T_o(G/H) ≅ 𝔪 via h ↦ (dL_h)_o, determining invariant geometric structures on the homogeneous space.

nodes.name: Invariant metric on G/H
nodes.description: A G-invariant Riemannian metric on G/H, corresponding to an Ad(H)-invariant inner product on 𝔪.

nodes.name: G-invariant almost complex structure on G/H
nodes.description: An Ad(H)-invariant endomorphism J: 𝔪 → 𝔪 with J² = −Id satisfying an integrability condition for complex structure on the homogeneous space.

nodes.name: Geodesic symmetry
nodes.description: The involutive diffeomorphism s_p defined by s_p(exp_p v) = exp_p(−v), which is an isometry in a symmetric space.

nodes.name: Riemannian symmetric pair
nodes.description: A pair (G, H) with an involutive automorphism σ of G such that (G^σ)₀ ⊆ H ⊆ G^σ, inducing a symmetric space structure on G/H.

nodes.name: Rank of a symmetric space
nodes.description: The dimension of a maximal flat totally geodesic submanifold, equivalently the dimension of a maximal abelian subspace of 𝔭 in the Cartan decomposition.

nodes.name: Symmetric space of compact type
nodes.description: A symmetric space G/H with G compact semisimple, having non-negative sectional curvature and negative definite Killing form on 𝔭.

nodes.name: Symmetric space of noncompact type
nodes.description: A symmetric space G/H with G noncompact semisimple of finite center, having non-positive sectional curvature, diffeomorphic to ℝⁿ.

nodes.name: Duality of symmetric spaces
nodes.description: A one-to-one correspondence between simply connected symmetric spaces of compact type and noncompact type, obtained by 𝔭 ↦ i𝔭 in the complexification, reversing curvature sign.

nodes.name: Curvature of symmetric spaces
nodes.description: The curvature tensor of a symmetric space G/H is R(X,Y)Z = −[[X,Y],Z] for X,Y,Z ∈ 𝔭 ≅ T_oM, determined entirely by the Lie bracket.

nodes.name: De Rham decomposition for symmetric spaces
nodes.description: A simply connected symmetric space decomposes uniquely as M₀ × M₁ × ··· × M_k where M₀ is Euclidean and each Mᵢ is irreducible symmetric.

nodes.name: Maximal flat submanifold
nodes.description: A maximal totally geodesic flat submanifold through a point in a symmetric space, isometric to ℝʳ or a flat torus Tʳ where r is the rank.

nodes.name: Compact symmetric space has non-negative curvature
nodes.description: K(X,Y) = |[X,Y]|²/(|X|²|Y|² − ⟨X,Y⟩²) ≥ 0 for a symmetric space of compact type.

nodes.name: Symmetric space is complete
nodes.description: Every Riemannian symmetric space is geodesically complete.

nodes.name: Isotropy-irreducible symmetric space
nodes.description: A symmetric space G/H where the isotropy representation of H on 𝔭 is irreducible, forcing the invariant metric to be unique up to scaling.

nodes.name: Weil homomorphism
nodes.function_signature: (Ad-invariant polynomial, Connection with curvature Ω) → (Closed differential form in H^{2k}(M))
nodes.description: The ring homomorphism from Ad-invariant polynomials I^k(G) to de Rham cohomology H^{2k}(M;ℝ), mapping P to the closed form P(Ω,…,Ω).

nodes.name: Chern–Weil construction
nodes.function_signature: (Principal bundle with connection, Invariant polynomial) → (Characteristic cohomology class)
nodes.description: Constructing characteristic classes from curvature: invariant polynomials applied to the curvature form produce closed forms whose cohomology classes are connection-independent.

nodes.name: Total Chern class
nodes.description: c(E) = 1 + c₁(E) + c₂(E) + ··· ∈ H*(M;ℤ), the generating series of Chern classes satisfying c(E⊕F) = c(E)∪c(F).

nodes.name: Whitney product formula for Chern classes
nodes.description: c(E ⊕ F) = c(E) ∪ c(F), the multiplicativity of the total Chern class under direct sum of complex vector bundles.

nodes.name: First Chern class
nodes.description: c₁(E) ∈ H²(M;ℤ), classifying complex line bundles up to isomorphism; for a Kähler manifold c₁(M) = [ρ/2π] with ρ the Ricci form.

nodes.name: Total Pontryagin class
nodes.description: p(E) = 1 + p₁(E) + p₂(E) + ··· ∈ H*(M;ℤ), the generating series of Pontryagin classes of a real vector bundle.

nodes.name: Euler class
nodes.description: The characteristic class e(E) ∈ Hⁿ(M;ℤ) of an oriented real rank-n vector bundle, satisfying e(E)² = p_{n/2}(E) when n is even.

nodes.name: Chern number
nodes.description: An integer topological invariant obtained by evaluating a monomial c₁^{a₁}c₂^{a₂}··· on the fundamental class [M] of a compact complex manifold.

nodes.name: Pontryagin number
nodes.description: An integer topological invariant obtained by evaluating a monomial in Pontryagin classes on the fundamental class [M] of a compact oriented manifold.

nodes.name: Transgression
nodes.function_signature: (Pair of connections, Invariant polynomial) → (Transgression (2k−1)-form)
nodes.description: Constructing a (2k−1)-form TP whose exterior derivative equals the difference P(Ω₁) − P(Ω₀) of Chern–Weil forms for two connections, yielding secondary characteristic classes.

nodes.name: Splitting principle technique
nodes.function_signature: (Vector bundle E) → (Pullback bundle f*E splitting as direct sum of line bundles)
nodes.description: Reducing characteristic class computations for general vector bundles to line bundles by pulling back to a space where the bundle splits as a direct sum of line bundles.

nodes.name: Chern class of a line bundle
nodes.description: For a complex line bundle L, c₁(L) = [(i/2π)Ω] classifies L up to isomorphism via its curvature 2-form.

nodes.name: Characteristic classes of flat bundles vanish
nodes.description: A flat connection on a principal bundle gives vanishing real characteristic classes in positive degrees via Chern–Weil theory.

nodes.name: Morse function
nodes.description: A smooth real-valued function f: M → ℝ on a smooth manifold all of whose critical points are non-degenerate (the Hessian at each critical point is non-singular).

nodes.name: Critical point of a smooth function
nodes.description: A point p ∈ M at which df_p = 0, i.e., all partial derivatives of f vanish in any local coordinate system.

nodes.name: Index of a critical point
nodes.description: The number of negative eigenvalues of the Hessian matrix of f at a non-degenerate critical point p, denoted λ or ind(p); equals the dimension of the maximal subspace on which the Hessian is negative definite.

nodes.name: Hessian of a smooth function at a critical point
nodes.description: The symmetric bilinear form H_p(f)(v,w) = v(w̃(f)) on T_pM at a critical point p, represented in local coordinates by the matrix (∂²f/∂xᵢ∂xⱼ)(p); well-defined independent of coordinates at critical points.

nodes.name: Sublevel set
nodes.description: For f: M → ℝ and a ∈ ℝ, the sublevel set Mᵃ = f⁻¹(−∞, a] = {x ∈ M : f(x) ≤ a}.

nodes.name: Handle attachment theorem
nodes.description: If p is a non-degenerate critical point of f with index λ and f(p) = c, then for sufficiently small ε > 0, M^{c+ε} has the homotopy type of M^{c−ε} with a λ-cell (handle of index λ) attached: M^{c+ε} ≃ M^{c−ε} ∪_φ e^λ.

nodes.name: Handle of index λ
nodes.description: A thickened cell D^λ × D^{n−λ} attached to the boundary of a manifold along S^{λ−1} × D^{n−λ}, modeling the topological change at a critical point of index λ.

nodes.name: CW complex structure from a Morse function
nodes.description: If M is a compact manifold admitting a Morse function f with critical points p₁,…,pₖ of indices λ₁,…,λₖ, then M has the homotopy type of a CW complex with one cell of dimension λᵢ for each critical point pᵢ.

nodes.name: Morse number Cₖ
nodes.description: The number of critical points of index k of a Morse function f on a manifold M, denoted Cₖ(f) or simply Cₖ.

nodes.name: Weak Morse inequalities
nodes.description: For a Morse function f on a compact manifold M: Cₖ ≥ βₖ for each k, where βₖ = rank Hₖ(M; F) is the k-th Betti number with coefficients in a field F.

nodes.name: Strong Morse inequalities
nodes.description: For a Morse function on a compact manifold: ∑_{k=0}^{t} (−1)^{t−k} Cₖ ≥ ∑_{k=0}^{t} (−1)^{t−k} βₖ for all t, with equality when t = dim M (recovering the Euler characteristic formula).

nodes.name: Poincaré polynomial (Morse context)
nodes.description: P_t(M) = ∑ βₖ tᵏ, the generating polynomial for the Betti numbers of M; the Morse inequalities state M_t(f) = ∑ Cₖ tᵏ satisfies M_t(f) = P_t(M) + (1+t)Q(t) for some polynomial Q with non-negative integer coefficients.

nodes.name: Lacunary principle
nodes.description: If a Morse function has critical points only in even dimensions (Cₖ = 0 for k odd), then the Morse inequalities are equalities: βₖ = Cₖ for all k, so M has no torsion in homology.

nodes.name: Euler characteristic via Morse theory
nodes.description: χ(M) = ∑ₖ (−1)ᵏ Cₖ for any Morse function on a compact manifold M, equating the Euler characteristic with the alternating sum of critical point counts.

nodes.name: Gradient flow of a Morse function
nodes.description: The flow φ_t of the negative gradient vector field −grad f on a Riemannian manifold (M,g), satisfying dφ_t(x)/dt = −grad f(φ_t(x)), used to deform sublevel sets.

nodes.name: Gradient-like vector field
nodes.description: A vector field ξ on M such that ξ(f) > 0 away from critical points of f, and near each critical point p the Morse lemma coordinates give ξ = −2∑_{i≤λ} xᵢ ∂/∂xᵢ + 2∑_{i>λ} xᵢ ∂/∂xᵢ; always exists for a Morse function on a compact manifold.

nodes.name: Stable manifold of a critical point
nodes.description: W^s(p) = {x ∈ M : lim_{t→∞} φ_t(x) = p}, the set of points flowing into the critical point p under the negative gradient flow; has dimension n − λ where λ = ind(p).

nodes.name: Unstable manifold of a critical point
nodes.description: W^u(p) = {x ∈ M : lim_{t→−∞} φ_t(x) = p}, the set of points flowing out of the critical point p under the negative gradient flow; has dimension λ = ind(p).

nodes.name: Cobordism via Morse theory
nodes.description: A Morse function on a cobordism W with ∂W = M₀ ⊔ M₁ decomposes W into a sequence of elementary cobordisms, each corresponding to a single handle attachment at a critical point.

nodes.name: Path space Ω(M; p, q)
nodes.description: The space of piecewise smooth paths ω: [0,1] → M with ω(0) = p and ω(1) = q, topologized with the compact-open topology; the domain for Morse theory of geodesics.

nodes.name: Energy sublevel set Ωᶜ
nodes.description: Ωᶜ = {ω ∈ Ω(M;p,q) : E(ω) ≤ c}, the sublevel set of the energy functional; has the homotopy type of a finite-dimensional manifold with corners when M is complete.

nodes.name: Finite-dimensional approximation of path space
nodes.description: The space Ω(t₀,…,tₖ) of piecewise geodesic paths with breakpoints at fixed parameter values t₀ < t₁ < ⋯ < tₖ; a finite-dimensional manifold that approximates Ω(M;p,q) and on which E restricts to a smooth function with the same critical points (geodesics).

nodes.name: Morse index of a geodesic
nodes.description: The index of a geodesic γ as a critical point of the energy functional E: the maximal dimension of a subspace on which I is negative definite; equals the number of conjugate points along γ counted with multiplicity.

nodes.name: Focal point
nodes.description: Given a submanifold N ⊂ M and a geodesic γ perpendicular to N at γ(0), a point γ(t₀) is a focal point of N along γ if there exists a non-zero Jacobi field J along γ with J(0) ∈ T_{γ(0)}N, (DJ/dt)(0) + S_{γ̇(0)}J(0) = 0, and J(t₀) = 0, where S is the shape operator.

nodes.name: Index theorem with focal points
nodes.description: For the energy functional on paths from a submanifold N to a point q, the index of a geodesic γ perpendicular to N equals the number of focal points of N along γ in the open interval (0,1), counted with multiplicity.

nodes.name: Homotopy groups of classical Lie groups
nodes.description: The stable homotopy groups πₖ(O), πₖ(U), πₖ(Sp) for the infinite orthogonal, unitary, and symplectic groups, computed via Bott periodicity: πₖ(U) cycles with period 2, πₖ(O) and πₖ(Sp) cycle with period 8 (offset by 4).

nodes.name: Loop space of a symmetric space
nodes.description: The space Ω(G/K; p, q) of paths in a symmetric space G/K between two points; Milnor shows the energy functional on this space is a perfect Morse function with critical points forming totally geodesic submanifolds.

nodes.name: Bott–Samelson theorem
nodes.description: On a compact symmetric space, every geodesic is periodic, the set of geodesics from p to q of a given energy forms a smooth manifold, and the energy functional on the path space is a perfect Morse function (Morse inequalities are equalities with integer coefficients).

nodes.name: Bott's iteration formula
nodes.description: The index of an iterated geodesic γᵏ (traversing γ exactly k times) is computed from the index and nullity of γ by a formula involving the eigenvalues of the holonomy around γ.

nodes.name: Perfect Morse function
nodes.description: A Morse function for which the Morse inequalities are equalities over ℤ: Cₖ = βₖ for all k; equivalently M_t(f) = P_t(M), the Morse polynomial equals the Poincaré polynomial.

nodes.name: Geodesic as critical point of energy
nodes.description: A path ω ∈ Ω(M;p,q) is a critical point of the energy functional E iff ω is a geodesic from p to q; follows from the first variation formula.

nodes.name: Existence of Morse functions
nodes.description: Every smooth manifold admits a Morse function; moreover Morse functions form an open and dense subset of C^∞(M,ℝ) in the C² topology (genericity of Morse functions).

nodes.name: Compact Lie group as symmetric space
nodes.description: A compact Lie group G with a bi-invariant metric is a symmetric space of type (G×G)/Δ(G), where Δ(G) is the diagonal; geodesics are one-parameter subgroups.

nodes.name: Bi-invariant metric on a Lie group
nodes.description: A Riemannian metric on a Lie group G that is invariant under both left and right multiplication; exists on every compact Lie group, and geodesics through e are one-parameter subgroups.

nodes.name: Geodesics in a symmetric space
nodes.description: In a symmetric space G/K, the geodesic through eK with initial velocity X ∈ 𝔭 is t ↦ exp(tX) · eK; all geodesics arise this way, and they are orbits of one-parameter subgroups.

nodes.name: Periodicity of geodesics in compact symmetric spaces
nodes.description: In a compact symmetric space of rank r, every geodesic is periodic (closed); the minimal period depends on the direction and the root system of the symmetric space.

nodes.name: Morse theory on the loop space of a symmetric space
nodes.description: Applying Morse theory to the energy functional E on Ω(G/K; p, q): the critical manifolds are totally geodesic submanifolds, the indices are computed from the root system, and the Morse inequalities become equalities (perfect Morse function).

nodes.name: Non-degenerate critical submanifold
nodes.description: A connected submanifold C of critical points of f such that the null space of the Hessian at each point p ∈ C equals T_pC; generalizes non-degenerate critical point to positive-dimensional critical loci (Bott's extension).

nodes.name: Morse–Bott theory
nodes.description: Extension of Morse theory where critical points form non-degenerate critical submanifolds C_i: M has the homotopy type of a space built by attaching disk bundles over C_i, and the Morse inequalities hold with Poincaré polynomials P_t(C_i) replacing 1 for each critical submanifold.

nodes.name: Minimax principle (Morse theory)
nodes.description: If Hₖ(Mᵇ, Mᵃ) ≠ 0 for a < b, then f has a critical value in [a,b]; more generally c = inf_{[α] ∈ H_k \{0}} sup_{x ∈ supp α} f(x) is a critical value, yielding existence of critical points from homological non-triviality.

nodes.name: Normal bundle of a critical submanifold (negative bundle)
nodes.description: The subbundle ν⁻ of the normal bundle of a critical submanifold C on which the Hessian of f is negative definite; its fibre dimension is the index λ, and the disk bundle D(ν⁻) is the generalized handle attached in Morse–Bott theory.

nodes.name: Condition (C) (Palais–Smale condition)
nodes.description: A function f on a complete Riemannian manifold (possibly infinite-dimensional) satisfies Condition (C) if every sequence {xₙ} with f(xₙ) bounded and |grad f(xₙ)| → 0 has a convergent subsequence; ensures the deformation lemma extends to infinite dimensions.

nodes.name: Energy functional satisfies Condition (C)
nodes.description: On a complete Riemannian manifold M, the energy functional E on the path space Ω(M;p,q) (with the H¹ Sobolev metric) satisfies the Palais–Smale condition (C), enabling Morse theory in this infinite-dimensional setting.

nodes.name: Homotopy type of path space sublevel sets
nodes.description: For a complete M, the sublevel set Ω^c = {ω : E(ω) ≤ c} has the homotopy type of a CW complex with one cell of dimension λ for each geodesic from p to q with energy ≤ c and Morse index λ (and nullity 0).

nodes.name: Existence of geodesics via Morse theory
nodes.description: If M is complete and Ω(M;p,q) is not contractible, the energy functional must have critical points at arbitrarily high energy levels; hence there exist infinitely many geodesics from p to q.

nodes.name: Theorem of Serre on closed geodesics
nodes.description: On any compact simply connected Riemannian manifold, there exist infinitely many geometrically distinct geodesics connecting any two points; proved using the non-trivial topology of the loop space.

nodes.name: Curvature bounds and conjugate points
nodes.description: If K ≥ δ > 0, then every geodesic has a conjugate point within distance π/√δ from the starting point (Bonnet's theorem); if K ≤ 0 there are no conjugate points (Hadamard's theorem).

nodes.name: Homology of the loop space via Morse theory
nodes.description: The Morse theory of the energy functional on Ω(M;p,p) computes the homology of the loop space ΩM; for symmetric spaces, the energy is a perfect Morse function yielding explicit additive homology computations.

nodes.name: Gradient flow deformation
nodes.function_signature: (Morse function f, Riemannian metric g) → (Deformation retraction of M^b onto M^a)
nodes.description: Using the flow of −grad f to deform the manifold, retracting M^b onto M^a when [a,b] contains no critical values; the fundamental technique underlying sublevel set topology in Morse theory.

nodes.name: Handle attachment technique
nodes.function_signature: (Critical point of index λ) → (Homotopy equivalence M^{c+ε} ≃ M^{c−ε} ∪ e^λ)
nodes.description: Attaching a λ-cell to the sublevel set when passing a critical value c of a Morse function, using the gradient flow to identify the attaching map from the stable manifold of the critical point.

nodes.name: Second variation analysis
nodes.function_signature: (Geodesic γ, variation field W) → (Sign of d²E/ds²)
nodes.description: Computing the second variation of energy to determine the index of a geodesic: constructing variation fields that make d²E/ds² < 0 detects negative eigenvalues of the index form and thus conjugate points.

nodes.name: Jacobi field method for index computation
nodes.function_signature: (Geodesic γ, curvature tensor R) → (Index = count of conjugate points with multiplicity)
nodes.description: Computing the Morse index of a geodesic by solving the Jacobi equation along γ and counting zeros of Jacobi fields: each zero contributes its multiplicity to the index, by the Morse index theorem.

nodes.name: Finite-dimensional approximation of path spaces
nodes.function_signature: (Path space Ω(M;p,q), partition 0=t₀<⋯<tₖ=1) → (Finite-dimensional manifold Ω(t₀,…,tₖ) ≃ Ωᶜ)
nodes.description: Replacing the infinite-dimensional path space by the finite-dimensional manifold of broken geodesics with fixed breakpoints; the energy restricts to a genuine Morse function, and the inclusion is a homotopy equivalence on sublevel sets for sufficiently fine partitions.

nodes.name: Symmetric space Morse theory
nodes.function_signature: (Compact symmetric space G/K, path space Ω) → (Homotopy groups of G/K via energy critical manifolds)
nodes.description: Exploiting the group action on a symmetric space to show the energy functional is equivariantly perfect Morse–Bott: critical manifolds are explicitly computable symmetric spaces of lower rank, and the resulting cell decomposition yields homotopy-theoretic information (used for Bott periodicity).

nodes.name: Morse theory technique (deforming sublevel sets)
nodes.function_signature: (Morse function f on M) → (CW decomposition of M)
nodes.description: The master technique of Morse theory: sweeping through critical values of f, using gradient flow to deform sublevel sets across regular intervals, and attaching handles at critical points, to build a CW complex homotopy equivalent to M.

nodes.name: Normal bundle along a geodesic
nodes.description: The vector bundle ν(γ) over [0,1] whose fibre at t is {v ∈ T_{γ(t)}M : g(v, γ̇(t)) = 0}; vector fields along γ in this bundle are the relevant variations for the second variation formula.

nodes.name: Broken geodesic (piecewise geodesic path)
nodes.description: A path in Ω(M;p,q) that is geodesic on each subinterval [tᵢ, t_{i+1}] but may have corners (discontinuities of the tangent vector) at the breakpoints; forms the finite-dimensional approximation space.

nodes.name: Topology of Sⁿ via Morse theory
nodes.description: The height function on Sⁿ ⊂ ℝⁿ⁺¹ is a Morse function with two critical points (index 0 and index n); by Reeb's theorem Sⁿ is homeomorphic to Sⁿ, and by CW structure Sⁿ ≃ e⁰ ∪ eⁿ.

nodes.name: Topology of projective spaces via Morse theory
nodes.description: A natural Morse function on ℂPⁿ (or ℝPⁿ) obtained from a generic linear function on the ambient space has n+1 critical points of indices 0, 2, 4, …, 2n (resp. 0,1,…,n); by the lacunary principle the homology is free.

nodes.name: Topology of Grassmannians via Morse theory
nodes.description: The function f(V) = ∑ᵢ λᵢ dim(V ∩ Eᵢ) on the Grassmannian G(k,n) is a Morse function whose critical points are the coordinate k-planes; the Schubert cell decomposition coincides with the Morse CW structure.

nodes.name: Stable unitary group U
nodes.description: U = lim_{n→∞} U(n), the colimit of unitary groups under the standard inclusions U(n) ↪ U(n+1); the classifying space BU classifies complex vector bundles.

nodes.name: Stable orthogonal group O
nodes.description: O = lim_{n→∞} O(n), the colimit of orthogonal groups; πₖ(O) is periodic with period 8 by Bott periodicity.

nodes.name: Stable symplectic group Sp
nodes.description: Sp = lim_{n→∞} Sp(n), the colimit of compact symplectic groups; πₖ(Sp) is periodic with period 8, shifted by 4 relative to πₖ(O).

nodes.name: Bott periodicity chain of symmetric spaces
nodes.description: The sequence of symmetric spaces O → O/U → U/Sp → Sp → Sp/U → U/O → O (period 8), where each space is the loop space of the next; encodes the 8-fold periodicity of πₖ(O).

nodes.name: Index form is positive definite before first conjugate point
nodes.description: If a geodesic γ: [0,1] → M has no conjugate points in (0,1], then the index form I(W,W) > 0 for all non-zero W vanishing at endpoints; equivalently the Morse index is 0 and γ is a local minimum of energy.

nodes.name: Isotropy representation of a symmetric space
nodes.description: The representation Ad|_K: K → GL(𝔭) of the isotropy group K on the tangent space 𝔭 ≅ T_{eK}(G/K) of a symmetric space G/K; its orbits classify geodesic directions, and its decomposition determines the rank and root structure.

nodes.name: Quasi-projective variety
nodes.description: A locally closed subset of projective space, i.e. an open subset of a projective variety; the most general class of classical varieties.

nodes.name: Ringed space
nodes.description: A topological space X equipped with a sheaf of rings O_X; the general framework before requiring stalks to be local rings.

nodes.name: Separated morphism
nodes.description: A morphism f: X → Y of schemes such that the diagonal morphism X → X ×_Y X is a closed immersion; the scheme-theoretic analogue of the Hausdorff property.

nodes.name: Proper morphism
nodes.description: A morphism that is separated, of finite type, and universally closed; the algebraic geometry analogue of a proper continuous map between compact spaces.

nodes.name: Projective morphism
nodes.description: A morphism f: X → Y that factors as a closed immersion X → P^n_Y followed by the projection P^n_Y → Y for some n.

nodes.name: Quasi-coherent sheaf
nodes.description: An O_X-module that is locally a cokernel of free modules, equivalently one that restricts to the sheaf associated to a module on each affine open.

nodes.name: Coherent sheaf
nodes.description: A quasi-coherent O_X-module that is locally of finite presentation: locally the cokernel of a map between finite-rank free sheaves.

nodes.name: Invertible sheaf
nodes.description: A locally free O_X-module of rank one; equivalently a line bundle, the sheaf-theoretic incarnation of a Cartier divisor class.

nodes.name: Ideal sheaf
nodes.description: A sheaf of ideals I in O_X defining a closed subscheme Z = V(I), with O_Z = O_X/I as the structure sheaf of the subscheme.

nodes.name: Very ample divisor
nodes.description: A divisor D on X such that the associated invertible sheaf O(D) defines a closed immersion of X into some projective space.

nodes.name: Flat morphism
nodes.description: A morphism f: X → Y such that for every x in X, the local ring O_{X,x} is a flat O_{Y,f(x)}-module; the algebraic notion of a continuously varying family.

nodes.name: Regular scheme
nodes.description: A locally Noetherian scheme all of whose local rings are regular local rings; the scheme-theoretic generalization of nonsingularity.

nodes.name: Normal scheme
nodes.description: A scheme whose local rings are integrally closed domains; equivalently a scheme satisfying Serre conditions R_1 and S_2.

nodes.name: Arithmetic genus
nodes.description: For a projective variety X of dimension n, p_a(X) = (-1)^n(P(0) − 1) where P is the Hilbert polynomial; equals h^1(O_X) for curves.

nodes.name: Geometric genus
nodes.description: For a smooth projective variety X, p_g(X) = h^0(ω_X) = dim H^0(X, ω_X), the number of linearly independent holomorphic n-forms.

nodes.name: Ruled surface
nodes.description: A smooth projective surface that is birational to C × P^1 for some curve C; equivalently a P^1-bundle over a curve.

nodes.name: Rational surface
nodes.description: A smooth projective surface birational to P^2; equivalently a surface with p_g = q = 0 and P_2 = 0.

nodes.name: Minimal model (surface)
nodes.description: A smooth projective surface containing no exceptional curves of the first kind (−1 curves); every surface has a minimal model obtained by contracting such curves.

nodes.name: Exceptional curve of the first kind
nodes.description: A smooth rational curve E on a surface with self-intersection E² = −1; can be blown down by Castelnuovo's criterion.

nodes.name: Closed immersion
nodes.description: A morphism f: X → Y inducing a homeomorphism of X onto a closed subset of Y, with O_Y → f_*O_X surjective; corresponds to an ideal sheaf in O_Y.

nodes.name: Open immersion
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes that is an isomorphism of X onto an open subscheme of Y.

nodes.name: Finite morphism
nodes.description: A morphism f: X → Y such that f^{−1}(U) = Spec(B) for each affine open Spec(A) = U in Y, where B is a finite A-algebra.

nodes.name: Unramified morphism
nodes.description: A morphism of finite type such that the sheaf of relative differentials Ω_{X/Y} vanishes; together with flatness gives an étale morphism.

nodes.name: Formal scheme
nodes.description: A topological ringed space locally isomorphic to Spf(A) for an I-adically complete ring A; captures formal neighborhoods and completions in algebraic geometry.

nodes.name: Elliptic curve
nodes.description: A smooth projective curve of genus 1 with a specified rational point O; carries a natural group law and is its own Jacobian.

nodes.name: Canonical sheaf
nodes.description: For a smooth variety X of dimension n, the invertible sheaf ω_X = det(Ω^1_X) = ∧^n(Ω^1_{X/k}), the sheaf of regular n-forms.

nodes.name: Dualizing sheaf
nodes.description: For a projective scheme X over k, the sheaf ω_X° representing the functor F → H^n(X, F)' via Serre duality; agrees with the canonical sheaf when X is smooth.

nodes.name: Conormal sheaf
nodes.description: For a closed immersion Y → X defined by ideal sheaf I, the sheaf I/I² on Y; its dual is the normal sheaf N_{Y/X}.

nodes.name: Euler sequence
nodes.description: The fundamental exact sequence 0 → Ω^1_{P^n} → O(−1)^{n+1} → O → 0 on projective space, relating the cotangent sheaf to twisting sheaves.

nodes.name: Twisting sheaf O(n)
nodes.description: The invertible sheaf O_{P^r}(n) on projective space, where O(1) is the tautological quotient line bundle; tensoring with O(n) is Serre's twist.

nodes.name: Sheaf of relative differentials
nodes.description: For a morphism f: X → Y, the quasi-coherent sheaf Ω^1_{X/Y} on X generated by symbols df subject to the Leibniz rule and f*-linearity.

nodes.name: Strict transform
nodes.description: For a subvariety Y of X and the blowup π: Bl_Z(X) → X, the closure of π^{−1}(Y \ Z) in the blowup; the proper transform of Y.

nodes.name: Higher direct image sheaf
nodes.description: For a morphism f: X → Y and a sheaf F on X, the sheaves R^i f_*(F) on Y obtained as the right derived functors of the direct image functor f_*.

nodes.name: Irregularity
nodes.description: For a smooth projective surface X, q(X) = h^1(O_X) = dim H^0(Ω^1_X); equals the dimension of the Albanese variety.

nodes.name: Albanese variety
nodes.description: The universal abelian variety Alb(X) receiving a morphism from X; dual to the Picard variety Pic°(X), with dimension equal to the irregularity q(X).

nodes.name: Cubic surface
nodes.description: A smooth surface of degree 3 in P^3; isomorphic to P^2 blown up at 6 points in general position and contains exactly 27 lines.

nodes.name: Serre vanishing theorem
nodes.description: For a coherent sheaf F on a projective scheme X over a Noetherian ring, H^i(X, F(n)) = 0 for all i > 0 and n sufficiently large.

nodes.name: Adjunction formula
nodes.description: For a smooth divisor Y on a smooth variety X, ω_Y ≅ (ω_X ⊗ O(Y))|_Y, relating the canonical sheaves via the normal bundle.

nodes.name: Noether's formula
nodes.description: For a smooth projective surface X, χ(O_X) = (1/12)(K_X² + e(X)) where e(X) is the topological Euler characteristic.

nodes.name: Semicontinuity theorem (sheaf cohomology)
nodes.description: For a proper morphism f: X → Y and a coherent sheaf F on X flat over Y, the function y → dim_k(y) H^i(X_y, F_y) is upper semicontinuous on Y.

nodes.name: Flat base change theorem
nodes.description: For a flat base change u: Y' → Y and a proper morphism f: X → Y with coherent sheaf F, there is a natural isomorphism u* R^i f_*(F) ≅ R^i f'_*(v* F).

nodes.name: Projection formula (sheaves)
nodes.description: For a morphism f: X → Y, a quasi-coherent sheaf F on X and a locally free sheaf E on Y, R^i f_*(F ⊗ f*E) ≅ R^i f_*(F) ⊗ E.

nodes.name: Enriques classification of surfaces
nodes.description: Every minimal smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 falls into exactly one class: rational, ruled, abelian, K3, Enriques, elliptic, or general type.

nodes.name: Castelnuovo–de Franchis theorem
nodes.description: If ω_1, ω_2 are linearly independent 1-forms on a smooth projective surface X with ω_1 ∧ ω_2 = 0, there exists a fibration f: X → C to a curve of genus ≥ 2.

nodes.name: Degree-genus formula
nodes.description: A smooth plane curve of degree d in P^2 has genus g = (d−1)(d−2)/2.

nodes.name: Valuative criterion of properness
nodes.description: A morphism f: X → Y of finite type is proper iff for every valuation ring R with fraction field K, every K-valued point of X over Y extends uniquely to an R-valued point.

nodes.name: Valuative criterion of separatedness
nodes.description: A morphism f: X → Y of finite type is separated iff for every valuation ring R with fraction field K, every K-valued point of X over Y extends to at most one R-valued point.

nodes.name: Serre's criterion for affineness
nodes.description: A Noetherian scheme X is affine if and only if H^i(X, F) = 0 for all quasi-coherent sheaves F and all i > 0.

nodes.name: Cohomology of projective space
nodes.description: H^0(P^n, O(d)) = k[x_0,...,x_n]_d for d ≥ 0, H^n(P^n, O(d)) is dual to H^0(P^n, O(−d−n−1)), and all other cohomology groups vanish.

nodes.name: Cartier's theorem on smoothness
nodes.description: Every group scheme of finite type over a field of characteristic zero is smooth; equivalently every reduced group scheme over a perfect field is smooth.

nodes.name: Stein factorization
nodes.description: Every proper morphism f: X → Y factors as X → Z → Y where X → Z has connected fibers and Z → Y is finite, with Z = Spec(f_* O_X).

nodes.name: Spec construction
nodes.function_signature: (CommutativeRing A) → (AffineScheme Spec(A))
nodes.description: Constructs the affine scheme Spec(A) from a ring A: points are prime ideals, topology is Zariski, structure sheaf assigns localizations A_f to basic opens D(f).

nodes.name: Sheaf Hom construction
nodes.function_signature: (Sheaf F, Sheaf G) → Sheaf(Hom(F,G))
nodes.description: Constructs the sheaf Hom(F, G) assigning to each open U the module Hom_{O_X|U}(F|_U, G|_U); the internal hom in the category of O_X-modules.

nodes.name: Tensor product of sheaves
nodes.function_signature: (Sheaf F, Sheaf G) → Sheaf(F ⊗ G)
nodes.description: Forms the tensor product F ⊗_{O_X} G by sheafifying the presheaf U → F(U) ⊗_{O_X(U)} G(U); preserves quasi-coherence and coherence.

nodes.name: Veronese embedding technique
nodes.function_signature: (P^n, d:ℤ) → Embedding(P^n → P^N)
nodes.description: Re-embeds P^n via all degree-d monomials to convert degree-d hypersurfaces into hyperplane sections, reducing problems to the linear case.

nodes.name: Segre embedding technique
nodes.function_signature: (P^m × P^n) → Embedding(P^m × P^n → P^{mn+m+n})
nodes.description: Embeds a product of projective spaces into a single projective space via the bilinear map [x_i] × [y_j] → [x_i y_j], realizing products as projective varieties.

nodes.name: Linear system embedding
nodes.function_signature: (X, LinearSystem |D|) → Morphism(X → P^n)
nodes.description: Uses a base-point-free linear system |D| to define a morphism to projective space by sending x to [s_0(x):...:s_n(x)] for a basis of sections.

nodes.name: Adjunction technique (algebraic geometry)
nodes.function_signature: (Divisor Y in X) → CanonicalClass(Y)
nodes.description: Computes the canonical class of a subvariety Y from that of the ambient variety X via K_Y = (K_X + Y)|_Y, yielding genus formulas and classification tools.

nodes.name: Flattening stratification
nodes.function_signature: (Morphism f, Sheaf F) → Stratification(Y)
nodes.description: Decomposes the base Y of a morphism into locally closed strata over which a coherent sheaf has constant Hilbert polynomial, reducing to the flat case.

nodes.name: Semicontinuity method
nodes.function_signature: (Family f, Sheaf F) → Bounds(h^i)
nodes.description: Uses upper semicontinuity of h^i(X_y, F_y) and constancy of the Euler characteristic to deduce cohomological information across fibers of a flat family.

nodes.name: Formal completion
nodes.function_signature: (Scheme X, Subscheme Y) → FormalScheme(X̂_Y)
nodes.description: Replaces a scheme X with the formal scheme along a closed subscheme Y, capturing infinitesimal neighborhoods; connects local and global properties via the theorem on formal functions.

nodes.name: Castelnuovo contraction
nodes.function_signature: (Surface S, (−1)-curve E) → Surface(S')
nodes.description: Contracts an exceptional curve E on a surface S to a smooth point, producing a smooth surface S' with K_{S'}² = K_S² + 1; used iteratively to reach the minimal model.

nodes.name: Minimal model program step
nodes.function_signature: (Surface S) → Surface(S_min)
nodes.description: Iteratively contracts (−1)-curves on a surface until none remain, reaching a minimal model that is either ruled (if κ = −∞) or has nef canonical class.

nodes.name: Taking stalks
nodes.function_signature: (Sheaf F, Point x) → Module(F_x)
nodes.description: Extracts the stalk F_x = colim_{U ∋ x} F(U) at a point x, reducing sheaf-theoretic statements to module-theoretic ones by exploiting that sheaf properties can be checked stalkwise.

nodes.name: Čech cohomology computation
nodes.function_signature: (Sheaf F, Cover U) → H^i(X, F)
nodes.description: Computes sheaf cohomology via an open affine cover using the Čech complex with terms ∏ F(U_{i_0} ∩ ... ∩ U_{i_p}); agrees with derived functor cohomology for separated schemes.

nodes.name: Canonical embedding technique
nodes.function_signature: (NonhyperellipticCurve C) → Embedding(C → P^{g−1})
nodes.description: Embeds a non-hyperelliptic curve of genus g into P^{g−1} via the complete canonical linear system |K_C|, producing a curve of degree 2g−2 whose geometry encodes intrinsic properties.

nodes.name: Holomorphic map
nodes.description: A map between complex manifolds that is locally given by holomorphic functions in local coordinates.

nodes.name: Dolbeault complex
nodes.description: The complex of smooth (p,q)-forms with the ∂̄-operator as differential, whose cohomology yields Dolbeault cohomology.

nodes.name: Theta divisor
nodes.description: The canonical effective divisor on the Jacobian variety defined as the image of the (g−1)-fold symmetric product of C under the Abel–Jacobi map.

nodes.name: Schubert cycle
nodes.description: A cohomology class on the Grassmannian defined by a Schubert variety, indexed by a partition λ, forming an additive basis for the cohomology ring.

nodes.name: Grothendieck residue
nodes.description: A multivariate generalization of the classical residue, assigning to a meromorphic n-form on an n-dimensional complex manifold a complex number at an isolated pole.

nodes.name: Hodge filtration
nodes.description: The decreasing filtration on the complexified cohomology of a compact Kähler manifold defined by the Hodge decomposition, varying holomorphically in families.

nodes.name: Variation of Hodge structure
nodes.description: A family of Hodge structures on a local system over a base S, with Hodge filtration varying holomorphically and satisfying Griffiths transversality.

nodes.name: Dolbeault cohomology
nodes.description: The cohomology of the Dolbeault complex, computing sheaf cohomology H^q(X, Ω^p_X) on compact complex manifolds via the ∂̄-operator.

nodes.name: Abel–Jacobi map
nodes.description: The map sending a degree-zero divisor on a curve C to a point in the Jacobian via integration of holomorphic 1-forms, inducing an isomorphism Pic^0(C) ≅ J(C).

nodes.name: Lefschetz pencil
nodes.description: A one-parameter family of hyperplane sections of a projective variety with only isolated ordinary double point singularities in the total space.

nodes.name: Pluricanonical system
nodes.description: The complete linear system of the m-th tensor power of the canonical bundle, whose behavior for large m determines the Kodaira dimension and the Iitaka fibration.

nodes.name: Period mapping
nodes.description: The holomorphic map from a parameter space of algebraic varieties to the period domain, sending each variety to its Hodge structure modulo monodromy.

nodes.name: Dolbeault theorem
nodes.description: The isomorphism H^{p,q}_{∂̄}(X) ≅ H^q(X, Ω^p_X) identifying Dolbeault cohomology with sheaf cohomology of holomorphic p-forms.

nodes.name: Hard Lefschetz theorem
nodes.description: On a compact Kähler manifold of dimension n, the iterated cup product with the Kähler class gives isomorphisms L^k: H^{n−k}(X) → H^{n+k}(X) for all k ≥ 0.

nodes.name: Lefschetz (1,1) theorem
nodes.description: A class in H^2(X, ℤ) on a compact Kähler manifold is the first Chern class of a holomorphic line bundle if and only if its image in H^2(X, ℂ) lies in H^{1,1}(X).

nodes.name: Riemann–Roch for surfaces
nodes.description: For a divisor D on a smooth projective surface X: χ(𝒪_X(D)) = (1/2)D·(D − K_X) + χ(𝒪_X), combining intersection theory with Euler characteristic.

nodes.name: Abel's theorem
nodes.description: A divisor of degree zero on a compact Riemann surface is principal if and only if its image under the Abel–Jacobi map is zero in the Jacobian.

nodes.name: Jacobi inversion theorem
nodes.description: The Abel–Jacobi map from the g-fold symmetric product of a genus-g curve to the Jacobian is surjective, so every point of J(C) is represented by an effective divisor of degree g.

nodes.name: Torelli theorem
nodes.description: A compact Riemann surface is determined up to isomorphism by its polarized Hodge structure, i.e., by its period matrix with the intersection pairing.

nodes.name: Bertini's theorem
nodes.description: A general member of a basepoint-free linear system on a smooth projective variety is smooth; more generally, the singular locus has the expected codimension.

nodes.name: GAGA principle
nodes.description: Serre's theorem that on a projective algebraic variety over ℂ, the categories of algebraic and analytic coherent sheaves are equivalent, and their cohomologies coincide.

nodes.name: Riemann bilinear relations
nodes.description: The conditions on the period matrix Ω of a compact Riemann surface: ΩJΩ^T = 0 and iΩJΩ̄^T > 0, characterizing which complex tori are Jacobians.

nodes.name: Wirtinger's theorem
nodes.description: The volume of a k-dimensional complex submanifold of a Kähler manifold equals (1/k!) times the integral of the k-th power of the Kähler form, and complex submanifolds are volume-minimizing.

nodes.name: Newlander–Nirenberg theorem
nodes.description: An almost complex structure J on a smooth manifold is integrable (comes from a complex structure) if and only if its Nijenhuis tensor vanishes.

nodes.name: Castelnuovo's rationality criterion
nodes.description: A smooth projective surface over ℂ is rational if and only if its irregularity q = 0 and its second plurigenus P_2 = 0.

nodes.name: Enriques–Kodaira classification
nodes.description: The classification of compact complex surfaces into ten classes by Kodaira dimension (−∞, 0, 1, 2), refining Enriques's classification of algebraic surfaces.

nodes.name: Exponential sheaf sequence
nodes.description: The short exact sequence 0 → ℤ → 𝒪_X → 𝒪_X^* → 0, whose long exact cohomology sequence relates Pic(X) to H^1(X, 𝒪_X) and H^2(X, ℤ).

nodes.name: Grothendieck residue theorem
nodes.description: The global residue theorem for meromorphic n-forms on a compact complex n-manifold: the sum of all Grothendieck residues at the poles equals zero.

nodes.name: Kodaira–Spencer deformation theory
nodes.description: The theory describing infinitesimal deformations of compact complex manifolds via the Kodaira–Spencer map ρ: T_0 S → H^1(X, T_X), with obstructions in H^2(X, T_X).

nodes.name: Dolbeault cohomology computation
nodes.function_signature: (Complex manifold X, bidegree (p,q)) → H^{p,q}(X)
nodes.description: Computing Dolbeault cohomology groups via ∂̄-closed forms modulo ∂̄-exact forms, using symmetry, vanishing theorems, or explicit representatives.

nodes.name: Hodge-theoretic methods
nodes.function_signature: (Compact Kähler manifold X) → constraints on topology and algebraic cycles
nodes.description: Using Hodge decomposition, Lefschetz operators, and Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations to constrain cohomology, prove vanishing, or detect algebraic classes.

nodes.name: Residue calculus on manifolds
nodes.function_signature: (Meromorphic form ω on X, polar divisor D) → residue classes and integrals
nodes.description: Computing integrals and cohomology classes via Grothendieck residues and the residue exact sequence on complex manifolds.

nodes.name: Schubert calculus
nodes.function_signature: (Enumerative problem on G(k,n)) → intersection number
nodes.description: Computing intersection numbers on Grassmannians by multiplying Schubert classes using the Pieri and Giambelli formulas.

nodes.name: Blow-up technique
nodes.function_signature: (Variety X, center Z) → (X̃, exceptional divisor E, birational map π)
nodes.description: Resolving singularities or separating infinitely near points by replacing a subvariety with its projectivized normal cone.

nodes.name: Adjunction formula technique
nodes.function_signature: (Smooth divisor Y ⊂ X) → K_Y and invariants of Y
nodes.description: Computing the canonical class and genus of a subvariety by restricting the canonical and normal bundles from the ambient space.

nodes.name: Lefschetz pencil method
nodes.function_signature: (Projective variety X) → topological/cohomological decomposition
nodes.description: Studying the topology of a projective variety by fibering it into hyperplane sections and analyzing vanishing cycles and monodromy.

nodes.name: Period mapping and Torelli-type arguments
nodes.function_signature: (Family of varieties) → injectivity/properties of period map
nodes.description: Using the period map to moduli of Hodge structures to prove uniqueness results or study moduli of algebraic varieties.

nodes.name: Deformation theory methods
nodes.function_signature: (Compact complex manifold X_0) → deformation space and obstructions
nodes.description: Studying infinitesimal and local deformations of complex structures via Kodaira–Spencer classes and obstruction theory in H^2(X, T_X).

nodes.name: Smooth variety
nodes.description: A variety all of whose points are nonsingular, i.e., the local ring at every point is a regular local ring.

nodes.name: Complete variety
nodes.description: A variety X such that for every variety Y the projection X×Y → Y is a closed map; the algebraic analogue of compactness.

nodes.name: Unirational variety
nodes.description: A variety X admitting a dominant rational map from projective space Pⁿ ⇢ X; equivalently, k(X) embeds into a purely transcendental extension.

nodes.name: Rational variety
nodes.description: A variety birational to projective space Pⁿ; equivalently, its function field is a purely transcendental extension k(t₁,…,tₙ).

nodes.name: Algebraic cycle
nodes.description: A formal Z-linear combination of irreducible closed subvarieties of X; cycles of codimension p form Zᵖ(X), modulo rational equivalence yielding the Chow group CHᵖ(X).

nodes.name: Pure Hodge structure
nodes.description: A finite-dimensional Z-module H_Z with a decomposition H_C = ⊕_{p+q=n} H^{p,q} of its complexification satisfying H^{p,q} = conjugate(H^{q,p}).

nodes.name: Plurigenera
nodes.description: The birational invariants P_m = h⁰(X, mK_X) for m ≥ 1, measuring sections of pluricanonical bundles, fundamental in the classification of algebraic surfaces.

nodes.name: Formal neighborhood
nodes.description: The formal scheme Spf(Ô_{X,p}) capturing the infinitesimal structure of a variety X at a point p up to all orders via the m-adic completion of the local ring.

nodes.name: Multiplicity of a singularity
nodes.description: The leading coefficient mult_p(X) of the Hilbert-Samuel polynomial of O_{X,p}, equal to the degree of the tangent cone; equals 1 if and only if p is smooth.

nodes.name: Intersection number (global)
nodes.description: For divisors D₁,…,Dₙ on a complete n-dimensional variety, the integer (D₁·…·Dₙ) defined by multilinearity and the moving lemma, counting intersections with multiplicity.

nodes.name: Degree of a finite morphism
nodes.description: For a dominant morphism f: X → Y of varieties of equal dimension, deg(f) = [k(X):k(Y)], the degree of the induced function field extension.

nodes.name: Genus formula for plane curves
nodes.description: A smooth projective plane curve of degree d has arithmetic genus g = (d−1)(d−2)/2, computed via the adjunction formula K_C = (K_{P²} + C)|_C.

nodes.name: Chevalley's theorem on constructible sets
nodes.description: The image of a morphism of finite type between Noetherian schemes is a constructible set (a finite Boolean combination of locally closed sets).

nodes.name: Moving lemma
nodes.description: On a smooth quasi-projective variety, any two cycles of complementary dimension can be moved by rational equivalence to intersect properly.

nodes.name: Noether's theorem on rational curves on surfaces
nodes.description: On a smooth projective surface with ample canonical class, rational curves form a bounded family and do not cover the surface.

nodes.name: Adjunction formula
nodes.function_signature: (Smooth divisor Y ⊂ smooth variety X, K_X) → (K_Y = (K_X + Y)|_Y)
nodes.description: Relating the canonical class of a smooth hypersurface to that of the ambient space via K_Y = (K_X + Y)|_Y.

nodes.name: Linear system technique
nodes.function_signature: (Complete linear system |D|, basis of L(D)) → (Morphism φ_{|D|}: X → Pⁿ)
nodes.description: Using a basis of the Riemann-Roch space L(D) to define a morphism to projective space for embeddings, contractions, and fibrations.

nodes.name: Projection from a point
nodes.function_signature: (Variety X ⊂ Pⁿ, point p ∉ X) → (Finite morphism X → P^{n−1})
nodes.description: The rational map sending x to the line ⟨p,x⟩ ∩ P^{n−1}; restricts to a finite morphism on varieties not containing p, reducing dimension.

nodes.name: Normalization of a variety
nodes.function_signature: (Irreducible variety X) → (Normal variety X̃, finite birational ν: X̃ → X)
nodes.description: Taking the integral closure of the structure sheaf in the function field to produce a normal variety resolving non-normal singularities.

nodes.name: Base change technique
nodes.function_signature: (Morphism f: X → S, base morphism g: T → S) → (Fiber product X×_S T → T)
nodes.description: Forming the fiber product to study fibers, specialize, or extend scalars; with flatness yields cohomology base change isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Descent technique
nodes.function_signature: (Object over cover T → S, cocycle data on T×_S T) → (Object over S)
nodes.description: Recovering geometric objects over a base from data over a cover with gluing data satisfying the cocycle condition; includes faithfully flat and Galois descent.

nodes.name: Specialization argument
nodes.function_signature: (Flat family X → S, property of special fiber) → (Property of general fiber)
nodes.description: Deducing properties of a general fiber from a special fiber using semicontinuity and openness of geometric conditions in flat families.

nodes.name: Generic point argument
nodes.function_signature: (Statement about generic fiber X_η) → (Statement on dense open U ⊂ S)
nodes.description: Reducing geometric statements to the generic fiber, then spreading out to an open subset of the base using finite presentation arguments.

nodes.name: Smooth homotopy
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap f, SmoothMap g : M → N) → SmoothMap F : M × [0,1] → N
nodes.description: A smooth map F: M × [0,1] → N with F(·,0) = f and F(·,1) = g; the differentiable-topology analogue of continuous homotopy.

nodes.name: Degree modulo 2
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap f: M → N, RegularValue y) → ℤ/2
nodes.description: For a smooth map f between compact manifolds of equal dimension, deg₂(f) = #f⁻¹(y) mod 2 for any regular value y; independent of the choice of regular value.

nodes.name: Sign of a regular preimage point
nodes.description: The sign +1 or −1 assigned to x ∈ f⁻¹(y) according to whether df_x: T_xM → T_yN preserves or reverses orientation.

nodes.name: Homotopy invariance of Brouwer degree
nodes.description: If f, g: M → N are smoothly homotopic maps between compact oriented manifolds without boundary, then deg(f) = deg(g).

nodes.name: Boundary theorem for degree
nodes.description: If f: ∂W → N extends to a smooth map F: W → N from a compact oriented manifold with boundary, then deg(f) = 0.

nodes.name: Degree of a composition
nodes.description: For smooth maps f: M → N and g: N → P between compact oriented manifolds of equal dimension, deg(g ∘ f) = deg(g) · deg(f).

nodes.name: Nonzero degree implies surjectivity
nodes.description: A smooth map f: M → N between compact connected oriented manifolds of equal dimension is surjective if deg(f) ≠ 0.

nodes.name: Classification of compact 1-manifolds
nodes.description: Every compact connected smooth 1-manifold is diffeomorphic to [0,1] or to S¹.

nodes.name: Smooth approximation theorem
nodes.description: Every continuous map between smooth manifolds is homotopic to a smooth map; if already smooth on a closed subset, the homotopy can be taken relative to that subset.

nodes.name: Index of an isolated zero of a vector field
nodes.type_signature: (VectorField v on M, IsolatedZero p) → ℤ
nodes.description: The degree of the map x ↦ v(x)/|v(x)| from a small sphere around the isolated zero p to Sⁿ⁻¹, measuring the local winding of the vector field.

nodes.name: Linking number
nodes.type_signature: (DisjointClosedCurves K, L in S³ or ℝ³) → ℤ
nodes.description: The integer lk(K,L) counting signed crossings of K over L in a diagram, equivalently the degree of the map (x,y) ↦ (x−y)/|x−y| from K × L to S².

nodes.name: Hopf fibration
nodes.description: The fiber bundle η: S³ → S² defined by η(z₁,z₂) = z₁/z₂ (in complex coordinates), with fiber S¹; the generator of π₃(S²) ≅ ℤ.

nodes.name: Smooth retraction
nodes.description: A smooth map r: W → A where A ⊆ W is a submanifold and r|_A = id_A; a smooth left inverse of the inclusion.

nodes.name: Framed submanifold
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothManifold M, Submanifold N, Trivialization of ν(N,M))
nodes.description: A submanifold N ⊆ M together with a trivialization of its normal bundle ν(N,M), i.e., a smooth choice of basis for each normal fiber.

nodes.name: Framed cobordism
nodes.description: An equivalence relation: N₀ and N₁ in M are framed cobordant if there exists a framed submanifold W ⊆ M × [0,1] whose boundary components are N₀ × {0} and N₁ × {1} with matching framings.

nodes.name: Pontryagin manifold
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap f: Sⁿ⁺ᵏ → Sⁿ, RegularValue y) → FramedSubmanifold
nodes.description: The framed submanifold f⁻¹(y) ⊆ Sⁿ⁺ᵏ for a regular value y ∈ Sⁿ, with framing induced by df; represents the homotopy class of f via the Pontryagin-Thom correspondence.

nodes.name: Smooth isotopy
nodes.type_signature: (Embedding f₀, Embedding f₁ : N → M) → SmoothMap F : N × [0,1] → M
nodes.description: A smooth homotopy F: N × [0,1] → M such that F(·,t) is an embedding for every t ∈ [0,1]; a continuous path through the space of embeddings.

nodes.name: Density of regular values
nodes.description: For a smooth map f: M → N, the set of regular values is dense in N; an immediate corollary of Sard's theorem since the set of critical values has measure zero.

nodes.name: Well-definedness of mod 2 degree
nodes.description: For a smooth map f: M → N between compact manifolds of equal dimension (M without boundary), the parity #f⁻¹(y) mod 2 is the same for every regular value y.

nodes.name: Boundary theorem (mod 2)
nodes.description: If M = ∂W for a compact manifold W and f: M → N extends smoothly to F: W → N, then deg₂(f) = 0.

nodes.name: Index of a non-degenerate zero
nodes.description: If p is a non-degenerate zero of a vector field v (i.e., the Jacobian dv_p is nonsingular), then the index of v at p equals sign(det dv_p) = ±1.

nodes.name: Nonvanishing vector fields on odd-dimensional spheres
nodes.description: For every odd n, the sphere Sⁿ admits a nowhere-vanishing smooth tangent vector field, since χ(Sⁿ) = 0 when n is odd.

nodes.name: Linking number is a homotopy invariant
nodes.description: The linking number lk(K,L) is invariant under smooth isotopies of K and L that keep K and L disjoint throughout.

nodes.name: Existence of maps of any given degree
nodes.description: For every integer d and every n ≥ 1, there exists a smooth map f: Sⁿ → Sⁿ of degree d.

nodes.name: Brown's refinement of Sard's theorem
nodes.description: The set of critical values of a Cᵏ map f: ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ has measure zero provided k ≥ max(n−m+1, 1), extending Sard's result to finite differentiability.

nodes.name: Induction on dimension (Sard proof)
nodes.function_signature: (SmoothMap f: U ⊆ ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ, CriticalSet C) → (C has measure zero in ℝᵐ)
nodes.description: Prove Sard's theorem by inducting on the source dimension, stratifying the critical set by vanishing order of derivatives and applying Fubini's theorem on each stratum.

nodes.name: Proof of Brouwer fixed point theorem via Sard
nodes.function_signature: (Continuous f: Dⁿ → Dⁿ) → (FixedPoint x with f(x) = x)
nodes.description: Derive Brouwer's fixed point theorem from the no-retraction theorem, which itself follows from Sard's theorem applied to a hypothetical retraction Dⁿ → Sⁿ⁻¹.

nodes.name: One-manifold classification argument
nodes.function_signature: (Compact 1-manifold M) → (M ≅ disjoint union of circles and intervals)
nodes.description: Classify compact 1-manifolds by following flow lines or using local charts to show each component is diffeomorphic to S¹ or [0,1]; used to establish boundary and degree theorems.

nodes.name: Diagonal map and self-intersection number
nodes.function_signature: (Compact oriented manifold M) → (Self-intersection I(Δ,Δ) = χ(M))
nodes.description: Compute the Euler characteristic χ(M) as the self-intersection number of the diagonal Δ ⊆ M × M, connecting the Lefschetz number of the identity to the Poincaré-Hopf theorem.

nodes.name: Degree-based surjectivity argument
nodes.function_signature: (SmoothMap f: M → N with deg(f) ≠ 0) → (f is surjective)
nodes.description: Show a map is surjective by computing its degree as nonzero; every point in N has a nonempty preimage since the signed count of preimages is constant over regular values.

nodes.name: Local parametrization
nodes.type_signature: (Manifold X, Point x) -> Diffeomorphism(Open subset R^k, Neighborhood of x in X)
nodes.description: A diffeomorphism phi from an open subset of R^k onto an open neighborhood of a point in a k-dimensional manifold, providing local coordinates.

nodes.name: Derivative of a smooth map between manifolds
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap f: X -> Y, Point x in X) -> LinearMap(T_xX, T_{f(x)}Y)
nodes.description: The linear map df_x: T_xX -> T_{f(x)}Y induced by a smooth map f between manifolds, defined via local parametrizations as df_x = d(psi^{-1} circ f circ phi)_0.

nodes.name: Tangent space of a preimage
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap f: X -> Y, RegularValue y) -> T_x(f^{-1}(y)) = ker(df_x)
nodes.description: At a regular value y, the tangent space to the preimage f^{-1}(y) at a point x equals the kernel of the derivative df_x: T_xX -> T_yY.

nodes.name: Transversal preimage theorem
nodes.description: If f: X -> Y is smooth and transverse to a submanifold Z subset Y, then f^{-1}(Z) is a submanifold of X with codim f^{-1}(Z) = codim Z.

nodes.name: Transverse intersection dimension formula
nodes.description: If submanifolds X and Z intersect transversally in Y, then X cap Z is a submanifold of dimension dim X + dim Z - dim Y.

nodes.name: Stability of immersions
nodes.description: If f: X -> Y is an immersion and X is compact, then every map sufficiently close to f in the C^1 topology is also an immersion.

nodes.name: Stability of submersions
nodes.description: If f: X -> Y is a submersion and X is compact, then every map sufficiently close to f in the C^1 topology is also a submersion.

nodes.name: Stability of embeddings
nodes.description: If f: X -> Y is an embedding and X is compact, then every map sufficiently close to f in the C^1 topology is also an embedding.

nodes.name: Stability of diffeomorphisms
nodes.description: If f: X -> Y is a diffeomorphism between compact manifolds, then every map sufficiently close to f in the C^1 topology is also a diffeomorphism.

nodes.name: Stability of transversality
nodes.description: If f: X -> Y is transverse to a submanifold Z subset Y and X is compact, then every map sufficiently close to f in the C^1 topology is also transverse to Z.

nodes.name: Nondegenerate critical points are isolated
nodes.description: A nondegenerate critical point of a smooth function (one with nonsingular Hessian) is an isolated critical point.

nodes.name: Compact manifolds have finitely many Morse critical points
nodes.description: A Morse function on a compact manifold has only finitely many critical points, since nondegenerate critical points are isolated.

nodes.name: Boundary of a manifold is a manifold
nodes.description: If X is a k-dimensional manifold with boundary, then the boundary dX is a smooth (k-1)-dimensional manifold without boundary.

nodes.name: Epsilon-neighborhood theorem
nodes.description: Every compact manifold X embedded in R^N possesses an epsilon-neighborhood X^epsilon that is a tubular neighborhood diffeomorphic to the normal bundle of X.

nodes.name: Transversality homotopy theorem
nodes.description: For any smooth map f: X -> Y and submanifold Z subset Y, there exists a smooth map g homotopic to f such that g is transverse to Z.

nodes.name: Extension theorem for transversality
nodes.description: If f: X -> Y is already transverse to Z on a closed subset C subset X, then f can be deformed rel C to a map transverse to Z on all of X.

nodes.name: Intersection number mod 2
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap f: X -> Y, Submanifold Z subset Y) -> Z/2
nodes.description: The mod 2 count I_2(f, Z) = #f^{-1}(Z) mod 2 for f transverse to Z, where X is compact without boundary and dim X = codim Z; a homotopy invariant.

nodes.name: Homotopy invariance of intersection number mod 2
nodes.description: If f_0 and f_1 are homotopic smooth maps from a compact boundaryless manifold X to Y, then I_2(f_0, Z) = I_2(f_1, Z) for any closed submanifold Z.

nodes.name: Mod 2 intersection number of submanifolds
nodes.type_signature: (Submanifold X subset Y, Submanifold Z subset Y) -> Z/2
nodes.description: For complementary-dimensional compact boundaryless submanifolds X, Z of Y, the mod 2 intersection number I_2(X, Z) defined via the inclusion map.

nodes.name: Homotopy invariance of degree mod 2
nodes.description: If f, g: X -> Y are homotopic smooth maps between compact connected boundaryless manifolds of equal dimension, then deg_2(f) = deg_2(g).

nodes.name: No retraction theorem
nodes.description: There is no smooth retraction from the closed unit ball B^n to its boundary sphere S^{n-1}, proved via degree theory.

nodes.name: Brouwer fixed-point theorem (mod 2 proof)
nodes.description: Every smooth map f: B^n -> B^n has a fixed point, proved via the no-retraction theorem using mod 2 degree theory.

nodes.name: Oriented intersection number
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap f: X -> Y, Submanifold Z subset Y) -> Z
nodes.description: The integer I(f, Z) = sum_{x in f^{-1}(Z)} sign(x) for f transverse to Z, where X, Y, Z are oriented and X is compact without boundary.

nodes.name: Homotopy invariance of oriented intersection number
nodes.description: If f_0 and f_1 are smoothly homotopic maps from a compact oriented boundaryless manifold to an oriented manifold Y, then I(f_0, Z) = I(f_1, Z).

nodes.name: Oriented intersection number of submanifolds
nodes.type_signature: (OrientedSubmanifold X subset Y, OrientedSubmanifold Z subset Y) -> Z
