nodes.description: For complementary-dimensional compact oriented boundaryless submanifolds X, Z of an oriented manifold Y, the integer I(X, Z) defined via the inclusion.

nodes.name: Oriented boundary theorem
nodes.description: If f: X -> Y extends to a smooth map F: W -> Y where dW = X with induced orientation, then I(f, Z) = 0 for every closed oriented submanifold Z of complementary dimension.

nodes.name: Brouwer degree
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothMap f: M -> N, CompactOrientedManifolds dim M = dim N) -> Z
nodes.description: The integer deg(f) = sum_{x in f^{-1}(y)} sign(df_x) for any regular value y, well-defined and independent of the choice of regular value.

nodes.name: Hopf degree theorem
nodes.description: Two smooth maps f, g: S^n -> S^n are smoothly homotopic if and only if deg(f) = deg(g), establishing [S^n, S^n] = Z.

nodes.name: Local Lefschetz number
nodes.description: The local contribution of an isolated fixed point x to the Lefschetz number, equal to sign(det(I - df_x)) when x is a nondegenerate fixed point.

nodes.name: Euler characteristic as self-intersection of diagonal
nodes.description: For a compact oriented manifold X, the Euler characteristic equals chi(X) = I(Delta, Delta), the self-intersection number of the diagonal Delta subset X x X.

nodes.name: Euler characteristic equals Lefschetz number of identity
nodes.description: For a compact oriented manifold X, chi(X) = L(id_X), since the graph of the identity is the diagonal in X x X.

nodes.name: Self-intersection number
nodes.description: The oriented intersection number I(X, X) computed by perturbing X to a transverse copy via a section of the normal bundle, then counting signed intersections.

nodes.name: Euler characteristic of spheres
nodes.description: The Euler characteristic of the n-sphere is chi(S^n) = 1 + (-1)^n, which equals 2 for even n and 0 for odd n.

nodes.name: Brouwer fixed-point theorem (oriented proof)
nodes.description: Every smooth map f: B^n -> B^n has a fixed point, proved using the Lefschetz fixed-point theorem: L(f) = 1 since B^n is contractible.

nodes.name: Intersection number symmetry
nodes.description: For compact oriented boundaryless submanifolds X, Z of complementary dimension in Y, I(X, Z) = (-1)^{dim X * dim Z} I(Z, X).

nodes.name: Pullback commutes with wedge product
nodes.description: For a smooth map f: X -> Y and differential forms omega, eta on Y, the pullback satisfies f*(omega wedge eta) = f*omega wedge f*eta.

nodes.name: Change of variables for differential forms
nodes.description: If phi: X -> Y is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of compact oriented manifolds, then integral_Y omega = integral_X phi*omega for every n-form omega on Y.

nodes.name: Degree formula via integration
nodes.description: For a smooth map f: M -> N between compact oriented manifolds of equal dimension, deg(f) * integral_N omega = integral_M f*omega for every n-form omega on N.

nodes.name: Dimension counting for transversality
nodes.function_signature: (Manifolds X, Z subset Y with dim X + dim Z < dim Y) -> (Generic maps f: X -> Y miss Z)
nodes.description: When dim X < codim Z in Y, a generic smooth map f: X -> Y has empty preimage f^{-1}(Z), since transversality forces f^{-1}(Z) to have negative dimension.

nodes.name: Parametric transversality method (Thom's method)
nodes.function_signature: (Family F: S x X -> Y transverse to Z) -> (F_s transverse to Z for almost all s in S)
nodes.description: Achieve transversality for a specific map by embedding it in a parametric family and applying Sard's theorem to the parameter space.

nodes.name: Cobordism argument
nodes.function_signature: (Compact manifold W with dW = X_0 disjoint X_1, Map F: W -> Y) -> (Invariant on X_0 equals invariant on X_1)
nodes.description: Prove a topological invariant is unchanged by exhibiting a cobordism W between two manifolds and extending the map over W, using the boundary theorem.

nodes.name: Isotopy and deformation argument
nodes.function_signature: (SmoothMap f: X -> Y, Desired property P) -> (SmoothMap g homotopic to f satisfying P)
nodes.description: Deform a smooth map through a one-parameter family to achieve a desired geometric property such as transversality or general position.

nodes.name: Diagonal intersection method
nodes.function_signature: (SmoothMap f: X -> X) -> (Fixed-point count via I(Delta, graph(f)) in X x X)
nodes.description: Detect and count fixed points of a self-map f by computing the intersection number of the diagonal Delta with the graph of f inside X x X.

nodes.name: Degree computation by counting preimages
nodes.function_signature: (SmoothMap f: M -> N, RegularValue y) -> deg(f) = sum sign(df_x) over x in f^{-1}(y)
nodes.description: Compute the Brouwer degree of a smooth map between compact oriented manifolds by choosing a regular value and summing the orientation signs at all preimage points.

nodes.name: Integration pairing for topological invariants
nodes.function_signature: (de Rham class [omega] in H^k(M), Cycle [C]) -> integral_C omega in R
nodes.description: Pair a de Rham cohomology class with a homology cycle by integration, yielding topological invariants such as the degree, Euler characteristic, or linking number.

nodes.name: Compactly supported de Rham cohomology
nodes.description: The cohomology H^k_c(M) of the complex Ω^*_c(M) of differential forms with compact support, covariant for proper maps and contravariant (with reversed arrows) for open inclusions.

nodes.name: Cohomology with compact vertical support
nodes.description: The cohomology H^*_cv(E) of forms on a vector bundle E that have compact support along the fibers, used to define the Thom class and prove the Thom isomorphism via integration along the fiber.

nodes.name: Bump form
nodes.description: A smooth compactly supported n-form on ℝⁿ with total integral 1, serving as the generator of H^n_c(ℝⁿ) ≅ ℝ and the basic building block for Thom forms and Poincaré duals of submanifolds.

nodes.name: Relative de Rham cohomology
nodes.type_signature: (SmoothManifold M, ClosedSubmanifold A) → GradedVectorSpace H*(M, A)
nodes.description: The cohomology H*(Ω*(M, A)) of the complex of forms ω on M with i*ω = 0 on A, fitting into a long exact sequence with H*(M) and H*(A).

nodes.name: Acyclic cover (Leray cover)
nodes.description: An open cover U = {U_α} such that every finite intersection U_{α₀} ∩ ··· ∩ U_{αₚ} has vanishing higher cohomology with respect to the sheaf in question; for such covers Čech cohomology equals sheaf cohomology.

nodes.name: Tautological bundle over the Grassmannian
nodes.description: The rank-k vector bundle γ^k → G_k(V) whose fiber over a k-plane W ∈ G_k(V) is W itself; the universal bundle for rank-k vector bundles, pulling back to any rank-k bundle via the classifying map.

nodes.name: Integration along the fiber
nodes.type_signature: (OrientedFiberBundle π: E → M, fiber F^k) → (LinearMap π_*: Ω^{n+k}(E) → Ω^n(M))
nodes.description: The pushforward map π_*: Ω^{n+k}(E) → Ω^n(M) defined by fiberwise integration of (n+k)-forms over the k-dimensional fiber, commuting with d and inducing a map on cohomology.

nodes.name: Global angular form
nodes.description: A (k−1)-form ψ on the total space of an oriented sphere bundle S^{k-1} → E → M whose restriction to each fiber is the volume form of S^{k-1}, with dψ = −π*e(E) where e(E) is the Euler class.

nodes.name: Diagonal class
nodes.description: The cohomology class δ_M ∈ H^n(M × M) that is Poincaré dual to the diagonal Δ ⊂ M × M; under the Künneth decomposition δ_M = Σ_a η_a × η_a^∨ where {η_a} and {η_a^∨} are Poincaré dual bases.

nodes.name: Collapsing of a spectral sequence
nodes.description: A spectral sequence collapses at the E_r page if d_k = 0 for all k ≥ r, so E_r ≅ E_{r+1} ≅ ··· ≅ E_∞; this occurs when E_r^{p,q} = 0 unless p or q lies in a single row or column.

nodes.name: Cohomology of SO(n)
nodes.description: The de Rham cohomology ring of SO(n), computed inductively using the Wang sequence for the fibration SO(n−1) → SO(n) → S^{n−1}; for odd n, H*(SO(2k+1)) is an exterior algebra on generators in degrees 3, 7, …, 4k−1.

nodes.name: Flag bundle
nodes.type_signature: (VectorBundle E → M, rank n) → FiberBundle(Fl(E) → M, fiber = Fl(ℂⁿ))
nodes.description: The associated fiber bundle Fl(E) → M whose fiber over x is the complete flag manifold of E_x; the pullback of E to Fl(E) splits as a direct sum of line bundles, implementing the splitting principle.

nodes.name: Poincaré lemma for compactly supported cohomology
nodes.description: H^k_c(ℝⁿ) ≅ ℝ if k = n and H^k_c(ℝⁿ) = 0 otherwise, the compactly supported analogue of the Poincaré lemma with cohomology concentrated in the top degree.

nodes.name: Mayer-Vietoris sequence for compact supports
nodes.description: For M = U ∪ V open, the long exact sequence ··· → H^k_c(U∩V) → H^k_c(U) ⊕ H^k_c(V) → H^k_c(M) → H^{k+1}_c(U∩V) → ···, with arrows reversed relative to the ordinary Mayer-Vietoris.

nodes.name: Finite-dimensionality of de Rham cohomology
nodes.description: For a manifold admitting a finite good cover, each H^k_{dR}(M) is a finite-dimensional vector space, proved by Mayer-Vietoris induction on the number of open sets in the cover.

nodes.name: Generalized Mayer-Vietoris principle
nodes.description: For a good cover U of M, the natural maps Ω*(M) → Č*(U, Ω*) ← Č*(U, ℝ) are quasi-isomorphisms of the de Rham complex into and out of the Čech-de Rham double complex, yielding a proof of the de Rham theorem.

nodes.name: Partition of unity argument for presheaves of forms
nodes.description: The presheaf Ω^q of differential q-forms on a manifold has vanishing higher Čech cohomology Ȟ^p(U, Ω^q) = 0 for p ≥ 1 with respect to any open cover, because smooth partitions of unity provide the required cochain homotopy.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence of a pair for compact supports
nodes.description: For U ⊂ M open, the long exact sequence ··· → H^k_c(U) → H^k_c(M) → H^k_c(M \ U) → H^{k+1}_c(U ∩ V) → ··· induced by extension by zero of compactly supported forms.

nodes.name: Infinite Grassmannian as classifying space
nodes.description: G_k(ℝ^∞) ≅ BO(k) and G_k(ℂ^∞) ≅ BU(k); every rank-k real (resp. complex) vector bundle over a paracompact base is the pullback of the tautological bundle via a map unique up to homotopy.

nodes.name: Cohomology of BU(k)
nodes.description: H*(BU(k); ℝ) ≅ ℝ[c₁, c₂, …, cₖ], a polynomial ring generated by the universal Chern classes cᵢ in degree 2i, computed via the Leray-Hirsch theorem and induction on the fibration U(k)/U(k−1) ≅ S^{2k−1}.

nodes.name: Cohomology of BO(k)
nodes.description: H*(BO(k); ℝ) ≅ ℝ[p₁, p₂, …, p_{⌊k/2⌋}] (times an additional Euler class generator e in degree k when k is even), a polynomial ring in the universal Pontryagin classes pᵢ in degree 4i.

nodes.name: Naturality of characteristic classes
nodes.description: For a smooth map f: N → M and vector bundle E → M, the characteristic classes satisfy c_k(f*E) = f*(c_k(E)), and similarly for Pontryagin, Euler, and Stiefel-Whitney classes; characteristic classes are natural transformations from the bundle functor to cohomology.

nodes.name: Homotopy axiom for Čech cohomology
nodes.description: If f: X → Y is a homotopy equivalence between spaces admitting good covers, then f*: Ȟ*(Y; ℝ) → Ȟ*(X; ℝ) is an isomorphism; proved via the generalized Mayer-Vietoris principle and homotopy invariance of de Rham cohomology.

nodes.name: Zigzag argument in a double complex
nodes.function_signature: (Čech-de Rham double complex, local cocycles) → (Global closed form or global Čech cocycle)
nodes.description: Constructing a global cocycle from compatible local data by alternately applying horizontal and vertical coboundary operators in a double complex, descending the staircase from one edge to the other.

nodes.name: Cochain homotopy construction
nodes.function_signature: (Homotopy H: M × [0,1] → N, differential forms on N) → (Cochain homotopy K with dK + Kd = g* − f*)
nodes.description: Explicitly constructing a degree −1 operator K via integration along the fiber of the projection M × [0,1] → M, proving that homotopic maps induce identical maps on de Rham cohomology.

nodes.name: Compact exhaustion and direct limit for H*_c
nodes.function_signature: (Non-compact manifold M, exhaustion K₁ ⊂ K₂ ⊂ ···) → H*_c(M) = lim_{→} H*_c(U_i)
nodes.description: Computing compactly supported cohomology of a non-compact manifold as the direct limit over an exhaustion by precompact open subsets, using extension by zero to form the directed system.

nodes.name: Symplectic subspace
nodes.description: A linear subspace W of a symplectic vector space (V,ω) such that ω|_W is nondegenerate; equivalently W ∩ W^ω = {0}.

nodes.name: Isotropic subspace
nodes.description: A linear subspace W of (V,ω) with ω|_W = 0, equivalently W ⊂ W^ω; necessarily dim W ≤ n.

nodes.name: Coisotropic subspace
nodes.description: A linear subspace W of (V,ω) satisfying W^ω ⊂ W; necessarily dim W ≥ n.

nodes.name: Lagrangian subspace
nodes.description: A linear subspace L of (V,ω) with L = L^ω, equivalently isotropic of maximal dimension n; simultaneously isotropic and coisotropic.

nodes.name: Symplectic complement
nodes.description: The symplectic complement W^ω = {v ∈ V : ω(v,w) = 0 for all w ∈ W}; satisfies dim W + dim W^ω = dim V and (W^ω)^ω = W.

nodes.name: Lagrangian Grassmannian Λ(n)
nodes.description: The manifold of all Lagrangian subspaces of (ℝ²ⁿ, ω₀), diffeomorphic to U(n)/O(n); has dimension n(n+1)/2 and fundamental group π₁(Λ(n)) ≅ ℤ.

nodes.name: Compatible complex structure on symplectic vector space
nodes.description: A linear map J with J² = -Id such that g(u,v) = ω(u,Jv) defines a positive definite inner product; equivalently ω(Ju,Jv) = ω(u,v) and ω(v,Jv) > 0.

nodes.name: Positive compatible triple (ω, J, g)
nodes.type_signature: (ω: SymplecticForm, J: ComplexStructure, g: InnerProduct) → Prop
nodes.description: A triple (ω, J, g) on a vector space V where any two determine the third via g(u,v) = ω(u,Jv); the space of such triples is contractible.

nodes.name: Space of compatible complex structures J(V,ω)
nodes.description: The space of all ω-compatible complex structures on V, diffeomorphic to Sp(2n)/U(n); contractible, hence all compatible choices are homotopy equivalent.

nodes.name: Polar decomposition in Sp(2n)
nodes.description: Every A ∈ Sp(2n) decomposes uniquely as A = PO with P symmetric positive definite symplectic and O ∈ Sp(2n) ∩ O(2n) = U(n); proves Sp(2n) deformation retracts onto U(n).

nodes.name: Maslov index for paths of Lagrangian subspaces
nodes.description: An integer index for a path of Lagrangian subspaces relative to a fixed Lagrangian L, defined by counting signed crossings of the Maslov cycle Σ_L; extends the loop index via the boundary map.

nodes.name: Maslov cycle
nodes.type_signature: Lagrangian L ∈ Λ(n) → Codimension-1 cycle Σ_L ⊂ Λ(n)
nodes.description: The algebraic variety Σ_L = {L' ∈ Λ(n) : L' ∩ L ≠ {0}} of codimension 1 in the Lagrangian Grassmannian; its complement has two connected components and generates H^1(Λ(n);ℤ).

nodes.name: Conley-Zehnder index
nodes.type_signature: Path Ψ: [0,1] → Sp(2n) with Ψ(0) = Id, det(Ψ(1) - Id) ≠ 0 → ℤ
nodes.description: An integer-valued index for nondegenerate paths in Sp(2n) starting at the identity; assigns a winding number measuring the rotation of eigenvalues; fundamental in grading Floer homology.

nodes.name: Moser isotopy lemma (relative version)
nodes.type_signature: (M compact, ω₀ = ω₁ near submanifold N, [ω_t] constant) → Isotopy φ_t
nodes.description: If two symplectic forms on a compact manifold agree on a neighborhood of a submanifold and are connected by a path with constant cohomology class, there exists an isotopy pulling one back to the other, fixing the submanifold.

nodes.name: Weinstein isotropic neighborhood theorem
nodes.description: A neighborhood of a compact isotropic submanifold N in (M,ω) is symplectomorphic to a standard neighborhood determined by the symplectic normal bundle; generalizes the Weinstein Lagrangian neighborhood theorem.

nodes.name: Isotropic submanifold
nodes.description: A submanifold N of (M,ω) with ω|_N = 0, equivalently TₚN is isotropic in (TₚM, ωₚ) for all p; dim N ≤ n.

nodes.name: Coisotropic submanifold
nodes.description: A submanifold C of (M,ω) with (TₚC)^ω ⊂ TₚC for all p; the null distribution (TC)^ω is integrable, giving the characteristic foliation.

nodes.name: Symplectic fiber bundle
nodes.type_signature: (Bundle π: P → B, Fiber (F,σ), StructureGroup Symp(F,σ)) → FiberBundle
nodes.description: A locally trivial fiber bundle whose fiber is a symplectic manifold (F,σ) and whose structure group is the symplectomorphism group Symp(F,σ).

nodes.name: Symplectic connection on a fibration
nodes.type_signature: SymplecticFibration π: (P,Ω) → B → Distribution Hor ⊂ TP
nodes.description: A horizontal distribution on a symplectic fibration whose parallel transport maps are symplectomorphisms of fibers; equivalently an Ehresmann connection preserving the fiberwise symplectic form.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian isotopy
nodes.description: A smooth family of symplectomorphisms {φ_t}_{t∈[0,1]} with φ₀ = id generated by a time-dependent Hamiltonian H_t via dφ_t/dt = X_{H_t} ∘ φ_t; two Hamiltonian isotopies compose to another.

nodes.name: Poisson bracket
nodes.description: The bracket {F,G} = ω(X_F, X_G) = X_F(G) making C^∞(M) a Lie algebra; satisfies Leibniz rule, antisymmetry, Jacobi identity; {F,G} = 0 iff F is constant along X_G flow.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of moment maps
nodes.type_signature: (Symplectic G-action on (M,ω)) → Conditions for moment map μ: M → g*
nodes.description: A symplectic G-action admits a moment map iff the lifted map g → C^∞(M) is a Lie algebra homomorphism; obstructions lie in H¹(g, H¹(M;ℝ)) and uniqueness fails by (g*)^G.

nodes.name: Symplectic reduction at a general level
nodes.type_signature: (Hamiltonian G-action, μ: M → g*, ξ ∈ g*) → SymplecticManifold μ⁻¹(ξ)/G_ξ
nodes.description: For coadjoint orbit value ξ, if G_ξ acts freely on μ⁻¹(ξ), the quotient μ⁻¹(ξ)/G_ξ inherits a natural symplectic structure; generalizes Marsden-Weinstein reduction at 0.

nodes.name: Coadjoint orbit
nodes.type_signature: LieGroup G, ξ ∈ g* → Submanifold O_ξ ⊂ g*
nodes.description: The orbit O_ξ = {Ad*_g(ξ) : g ∈ G} ⊂ g* under the coadjoint action; carries the Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau symplectic form ω_ξ(ad*_X ξ, ad*_Y ξ) = ξ([X,Y]).

nodes.name: Coadjoint orbits as symplectic manifolds
nodes.description: Every coadjoint orbit of a Lie group carries a natural symplectic structure via the Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau form; the inclusion O_ξ ↪ g* is a moment map for the coadjoint action.

nodes.name: Flux homomorphism
nodes.description: The homomorphism Flux({φ_t}) = ∫₀¹ [ι_{X_t}ω] dt from the universal cover of Symp₀(M,ω) to H¹(M;ℝ); its kernel is the Hamiltonian group Ham(M,ω).

nodes.name: Flux conjecture (Ono)
nodes.description: The flux group Γ_ω = Image(Flux: π₁(Symp₀) → H¹(M;ℝ)) is discrete; equivalently Ham(M,ω) is C¹-closed in Symp₀(M,ω). Proved by Ono (2006).

nodes.name: Calabi homomorphism
nodes.description: A surjective homomorphism Cal: Ham_c(M,ω) → ℝ defined by Cal(φ_H) = ∫₀¹ ∫_M H_t ωⁿ dt for compactly supported Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms; its kernel is a simple group.

nodes.name: Hofer metric on Ham(M,ω)
nodes.description: The bi-invariant Finsler metric d(φ,ψ) = inf_H ∫₀¹ (max H_t - min H_t) dt on Ham(M,ω); nondegeneracy proved by Hofer using holomorphic curves or capacities.

nodes.name: Hofer's nondegeneracy theorem
nodes.description: The Hofer metric on Ham(M,ω) is nondegenerate: d(id, φ) > 0 for φ ≠ id; equivalently the Hofer norm ||φ|| = inf_H ∫₀¹ osc(H_t) dt is a genuine norm.

nodes.name: Hofer-Zehnder capacity
nodes.description: The symplectic capacity c_{HZ}(M,ω) = sup{max H : H admissible, flow of H has no nonconstant periodic orbit of period ≤ 1}; satisfies monotonicity, conformality, and normalization axioms.

nodes.name: Displacement energy
nodes.description: e(A) = inf{||φ||_Hofer : φ ∈ Ham(M,ω), φ(A) ∩ A = ∅}; satisfies e(A) ≥ c(A) for any capacity c, providing a lower bound on energy needed to displace A.

nodes.name: Tame almost complex structure
nodes.description: An almost complex structure J on (M,ω) such that ω(v, Jv) > 0 for all nonzero v; weaker than compatibility but sufficient for Gromov's theory of J-holomorphic curves.

nodes.name: Compatible almost complex structure on symplectic manifold
nodes.description: An almost complex structure J satisfying ω(v,Jv) > 0 and ω(Jv,Jw) = ω(v,w); the triple (ω,J,g) with g = ω(·,J·) is a compatible Hermitian structure.

nodes.name: Contractibility of J(M,ω)
nodes.description: The space J(M,ω) of ω-compatible (or ω-tame) almost complex structures on a symplectic manifold is nonempty and contractible; proved using the pointwise contractibility of Sp(2n)/U(n).

nodes.name: Symplectic capacity (axiomatic)
nodes.description: A functor c satisfying monotonicity under symplectic embeddings, conformality c(M,λw) = |λ|c(M,ω), and normalization c(B²ⁿ(1)) = π = c(Z²ⁿ(1)).

nodes.name: Gromov width
nodes.description: w_G(M,ω) = sup{πr² : B²ⁿ(r) symplectically embeds into (M,ω)}; the smallest symplectic capacity, measuring the radius of the largest embeddable ball.

nodes.name: Ekeland-Hofer capacities
nodes.type_signature: SymplecticManifold (M,ω) → Sequence c₁ ≤ c₂ ≤ c₃ ≤ ⋯ in ℝ≥0 ∪ {∞}
nodes.description: An infinite sequence of symplectic capacities c_k defined via variational methods on the loop space; c₁ equals the Gromov width on ellipsoids and c_k(B²ⁿ(1)) = π for all k.

nodes.name: J-holomorphic curve
nodes.description: A smooth map u: (Σ,j) → (M,J) satisfying the Cauchy-Riemann equation du ∘ j = J ∘ du, equivalently ∂̄_J(u) = 0; the fundamental object of Gromov's symplectic topology.

nodes.name: Energy of a J-holomorphic curve
nodes.description: E(u) = ½∫_Σ |du|² vol_Σ = ∫_Σ u*ω for ω-tame J; the energy identity E(u) = [ω]·[u] shows energy equals the symplectic area of the homology class.

nodes.name: Energy identity for J-holomorphic curves
nodes.description: For an ω-compatible J, the energy E(u) = ½∫|du|² equals the symplectic area ∫u*ω; implies J-holomorphic curves are absolute minima of energy in their homology class.

nodes.name: Moduli space of J-holomorphic curves
nodes.type_signature: (A ∈ H₂(M), genus g, AlmostComplexStructure J) → TopologicalSpace M_{g,k}(M,A,J)
nodes.description: The space of equivalence classes of J-holomorphic maps u: Σ → M representing class A with k marked points, modulo reparametrization; for generic J, a smooth manifold of the expected dimension.

nodes.name: Fredholm theory for the ∂̄_J operator
nodes.description: The linearization of the Cauchy-Riemann operator at a J-holomorphic curve u is a real Cauchy-Riemann operator, hence Fredholm; its index gives the virtual dimension via the Riemann-Roch formula.

nodes.name: Virtual dimension of moduli space of J-holomorphic curves
nodes.description: virdim M_{g,k}(M,A,J) = n(2-2g) + 2c₁(A) + 2k - 6; determined by the Fredholm index of D_u via Riemann-Roch; equals actual dimension when transversality holds.

nodes.name: Simple (somewhere injective) J-holomorphic curve
nodes.description: A J-holomorphic curve u: Σ → M not factoring as u = v ∘ φ for a branched cover φ of degree > 1; equivalently ∃z with u⁻¹(u(z)) = {z} and du(z) ≠ 0. Transversality can be achieved for simple curves.

nodes.name: Transversality for simple J-holomorphic curves
nodes.description: For a generic (Baire second category) ω-tame J, every simple J-holomorphic curve is regular (D_u surjective) and the moduli space is a smooth manifold of the expected dimension.

nodes.name: Bubbling phenomenon for J-holomorphic curves
nodes.description: When a sequence of J-holomorphic curves has bounded energy but gradient blow-up, rescaling produces a nonconstant J-holomorphic sphere; the energy splits: E(u_∞) + ΣE(bubbles) = lim E(u_n).

nodes.name: Stable map
nodes.description: A J-holomorphic map from a nodal marked Riemann surface with finite automorphism group on each unstable component; the objects compactifying the moduli space M̄_{g,k}(M,A,J).

nodes.name: Evaluation map in Gromov-Witten theory
nodes.description: The map ev = (ev₁,...,ev_k) sending a stable map to the images of its marked points; used to define GW invariants as ∫_{[M̄]^{vir}} ev₁*α₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ ev_k*α_k.

nodes.name: Removal of singularities for J-holomorphic curves
nodes.description: A J-holomorphic map u: D\{0} → (M,J) with finite energy extends smoothly across the puncture to ū: D → M; the symplectic analogue of Riemann's removable singularity theorem.

nodes.name: Monotonicity lemma for J-holomorphic curves
nodes.description: If u: Σ → (M,J,g) is J-holomorphic passing through p, the area of u(Σ) ∩ B(p,r) is at least πr² for small r; provides uniform local area bounds preventing energy concentration without bubbling.

nodes.name: Symplectic packing problem
nodes.description: The problem of determining the maximal volume fraction fillable by k disjoint symplectically embedded balls; Gromov showed the answer is not always 1, revealing symplectic rigidity beyond volume.

nodes.name: Symplectic form on surfaces
nodes.description: On a closed oriented surface, any area form is symplectic; Moser's theorem implies the symplectic structure is determined up to symplectomorphism by total area and genus.

nodes.name: Eliashberg rigidity theorem
nodes.description: The group Symp(M,ω) is C⁰-closed in Diff(M); a C⁰-limit of symplectomorphisms that is smooth is itself a symplectomorphism. Shows symplectic topology is not purely smooth.

nodes.name: McDuff's theorem on rational and ruled symplectic 4-manifolds
nodes.description: A closed symplectic 4-manifold containing a symplectically embedded sphere of nonnegative self-intersection is rational or ruled; proved using J-holomorphic curve techniques.

nodes.name: Taubes' theorem (SW = Gr)
nodes.description: On a closed symplectic 4-manifold, Seiberg-Witten invariants equal the Gromov invariants counting embedded J-holomorphic curves; establishes SW(M, s_can) = 1 bridging gauge theory and symplectic topology.

nodes.name: Existence of J-holomorphic curves via Taubes
nodes.description: On any closed symplectic 4-manifold with b₂⁺ > 1, the canonical class K has nonvanishing SW invariant; by SW = Gr there exist J-holomorphic curves representing PD(K) for generic J.

nodes.name: Symplectic isotopy problem
nodes.description: The question of whether symplectomorphic submanifolds in the same homology class are symplectically isotopic; related to the topology of Symp(M,ω) and braid monodromy factorizations.

nodes.name: Positivity of intersections of J-holomorphic curves
nodes.description: Two distinct J-holomorphic curves in an almost complex 4-manifold intersect with positive local intersection number at each point; algebraic and geometric intersection numbers agree for distinct curves.

nodes.name: Adjunction formula for J-holomorphic curves
nodes.description: For a simple closed J-holomorphic curve u: Σ → M⁴ representing A: 2g(Σ) - 2 = A·A - c₁(A) + 2δ(u) where δ(u) ≥ 0 counts singularities; embedded iff δ(u) = 0.

nodes.name: Recurrence theorem for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms
nodes.description: On a closed symplectic manifold, every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism is recurrent: for every open set U, there exists n > 0 with φⁿ(U) ∩ U ≠ ∅; follows from Liouville volume preservation.

nodes.name: Liouville measure on a symplectic manifold
nodes.description: The canonical volume measure μ_L = ωⁿ/n! on a 2n-dimensional symplectic manifold; invariant under all symplectomorphisms and Hamiltonian flows (Liouville's theorem).

nodes.name: Contact-type hypersurface in a symplectic manifold
nodes.description: A hypersurface Σ ⊂ (M,ω) admitting a Liouville vector field Y (L_Yω = ω) defined near Σ and transverse to Σ; then α = ι_Yω|_Σ is a contact form on Σ.

nodes.name: Liouville vector field
nodes.description: A vector field Y satisfying L_Yω = ω, equivalently d(ι_Yω) = ω; its flow dilates the symplectic form by e^t. Exists globally on exact symplectic manifolds where ω = dλ.

nodes.name: Symplectization of a contact manifold
nodes.type_signature: ContactManifold (Σ, ξ = ker α) → SymplecticManifold (ℝ × Σ, d(e^t α))
nodes.description: The symplectic manifold (ℝ × Σ, d(e^t α)) associated to a contact manifold (Σ, α); equivalently the symplectic cone (ℝ₊ × Σ, d(rα)).

nodes.name: Symplectic vector bundle
nodes.description: A vector bundle E → M with a smoothly varying nondegenerate skew-symmetric bilinear form on each fiber; the structure group reduces from GL(2n) to Sp(2n).

nodes.name: Characteristic foliation on a coisotropic submanifold
nodes.type_signature: CoisotropicSubmanifold C ⊂ (M,ω) → Foliation F on C
nodes.description: The integrable distribution (TC)^ω on C whose leaves are isotropic; the leaf space C/(TC)^ω inherits a symplectic structure when smooth (symplectic reduction).

nodes.name: Exact Lagrangian submanifold
nodes.description: A Lagrangian L in (M, dλ) with λ|_L exact (λ|_L = df for f: L → ℝ); in T*Q the zero section is the canonical example.

nodes.name: Exact symplectic manifold
nodes.description: A symplectic manifold (M,ω) with ω = dλ for a global 1-form λ; necessarily noncompact since ∫_M ωⁿ ≠ 0. Examples: T*Q, Stein manifolds.

nodes.name: Spectral invariants in Hamiltonian Floer theory
nodes.type_signature: (Hamiltonian H, Quantum cohomology class a) → ℝ
nodes.description: Real numbers c(a, H) defined as minimax values of the action functional over Floer cycles representing a ∈ QH*(M); satisfy Hofer-Lipschitz continuity, spectrality, and triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian Floer homology
nodes.description: Homology of a chain complex generated by 1-periodic orbits of X_H with differential counting Floer cylinders; isomorphic to quantum homology QH*(M) by the PSS isomorphism.

nodes.name: Energy-capacity inequality
nodes.description: For any compact A ⊂ (M,ω), the displacement energy e(A) ≥ c(A) for any symplectic capacity c; in particular e(B²ⁿ(r)) ≥ πr². Links Hofer geometry to symplectic capacities.

nodes.name: Moser's method
nodes.function_signature: (Family of cohomologous symplectic forms ω_t) → (Isotopy φ_t with φ_t*ω_t = ω₀)
nodes.description: Constructs a diffeomorphism isotopy by solving for the vector field X_t via ι_{X_t}ω_t = -σ_t; the key technique behind Darboux, Moser stability, and Weinstein neighborhood theorems.

nodes.name: Thurston's construction for symplectic fiber bundles
nodes.function_signature: (Symplectic fibration π: P → B with closed coupling form) → (Symplectic form on total space P)
nodes.description: Constructs a symplectic form on the total space of a symplectic fibration by adding a large multiple of the pullback of the base form to a closed extension of the fiber form.

nodes.name: Symplectic cutting
nodes.function_signature: (Hamiltonian S¹-action on (M,ω), level c ∈ ℝ) → (Symplectic manifold M_cut)
nodes.description: Lerman's construction: forms M × ℂ with diagonal S¹-action and reduces at level c to obtain a symplectic manifold that cuts M along μ⁻¹(c).

nodes.name: Generating function for Lagrangians
nodes.function_signature: (Lagrangian submanifold L ⊂ T*M) → (Function S: M × ℝᴺ → ℝ with L = critical set)
nodes.description: Represents a Lagrangian as the critical set of a generating function S(x,ξ); reduces symplectic intersection questions to Morse-theoretic ones via the Chaperon-Sikorav-Viterbo framework.

nodes.name: Neck-stretching technique
nodes.function_signature: (Contact hypersurface Σ ⊂ (M,ω), Sequence J_n with neck → ∞) → (Holomorphic buildings in SFT)
nodes.description: Deforms the almost complex structure near a contact-type hypersurface by stretching the neck to infinity; in the limit, J-holomorphic curves decompose into holomorphic buildings.

nodes.name: Gromov compactification of moduli spaces
nodes.function_signature: (Moduli space M(A,J)) → (Compact space M̄(A,J) with boundary strata of stable maps)
nodes.description: Compactifies the moduli space of J-holomorphic curves by adding nodal stable maps as boundary strata; the key tool for defining Gromov-Witten invariants.

nodes.name: Symplectic sum construction
nodes.function_signature: ((M₁,ω₁,Σ₁), (M₂,ω₂,Σ₂), Σ₁ ≅ Σ₂) → SymplecticManifold M₁ #_Σ M₂
nodes.description: Gompf's construction: removes tubular neighborhoods of codimension-2 symplectic submanifolds with opposite normal Euler classes and glues boundaries to produce a new symplectic manifold.

nodes.name: Symplectic blowup
nodes.function_signature: (SymplecticManifold (M,ω), Point p, Size ε) → (SymplecticManifold (M̃, ω̃))
nodes.description: Replaces a symplectic ball B²ⁿ(ε) at p by its projectivization, producing (M̃, ω̃) with exceptional divisor E ≅ ℂPⁿ⁻¹ of area ε; depends on the embedding and ε.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian perturbation technique
nodes.function_signature: (Lagrangian L, Hamiltonian H) → Perturbed Lagrangian φ_H(L)
nodes.description: Displaces a Lagrangian by a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism to achieve transversality; intersection points L ∩ φ_H(L) correspond to time-1 Hamiltonian chords, connecting to Floer theory.

nodes.name: Uncountable set
nodes.description: A set that is not countable; it cannot be put into bijection with any subset of the natural numbers.

nodes.name: Subbasis for a topology
nodes.description: A collection S of subsets of X whose union equals X; the topology generated by S has as basis all finite intersections of members of S.

nodes.name: Box topology
nodes.description: The topology on a product of spaces whose basis consists of all products of open sets, with no restriction to finitely many non-trivial factors.

nodes.name: Metric topology
nodes.description: The topology on a metric space (X, d) generated by the collection of all open balls B(x, epsilon).

nodes.name: Metrizable space
nodes.description: A topological space whose topology is induced by some metric.

nodes.name: Hausdorff spaces have unique limits
nodes.description: In a Hausdorff space, every convergent sequence (or net) has a unique limit.

nodes.name: Separation of a topological space
nodes.description: A pair (U, V) of disjoint nonempty open sets whose union is X, witnessing that X is disconnected.

nodes.name: Connected subspace
nodes.description: A subspace A of a topological space X that is connected in the subspace topology; equivalently, A cannot be written as a union of two nonempty sets each open in A.

nodes.name: Path connectedness implies connectedness
nodes.description: Every path-connected space is connected; the converse does not hold in general.

nodes.name: Path component
nodes.description: A maximal path-connected subset of a topological space; the path components partition the space.

nodes.name: Locally path-connected space
nodes.description: A topological space in which every point has a neighborhood base of path-connected open sets.

nodes.name: Compact space
nodes.description: A topological space in which every open cover has a finite subcover.

nodes.name: Compact subspace
nodes.description: A subspace Y of a topological space X that is compact in the subspace topology.

nodes.name: Tube lemma
nodes.description: If x_0 times Y is contained in an open set N of the product X times Y with Y compact, then there is an open W containing x_0 such that W times Y is contained in N.

nodes.name: Limit point compactness
nodes.description: A topological space in which every infinite subset has a limit point; implied by compactness, equivalent to it in metrizable spaces.

nodes.name: Every metrizable space is normal
nodes.description: If X is metrizable, then X is normal: any two disjoint closed sets can be separated by disjoint open sets.

nodes.name: Every regular second-countable space is normal
nodes.description: A regular Hausdorff space with a countable basis is normal.

nodes.name: Every paracompact Hausdorff space is normal
nodes.description: A paracompact Hausdorff space is normal; more generally, any two disjoint closed sets can be separated by a continuous function.

nodes.name: Smirnov metrization theorem
nodes.description: A topological space is metrizable if and only if it is paracompact Hausdorff and locally metrizable.

nodes.name: Baire space
nodes.description: A topological space in which every countable intersection of dense open sets is dense; equivalently, the complement of any meager set is dense.

nodes.name: Baire category theorem (locally compact Hausdorff version)
nodes.description: Every locally compact Hausdorff space is a Baire space: countable intersections of dense open sets are dense.

nodes.name: Homotopy of paths
nodes.description: A continuous deformation of one path to another through paths sharing the same endpoints; formally, a continuous map F: [0,1] x [0,1] to X with F(s,0) = f(s), F(s,1) = g(s), and fixed endpoints.

nodes.name: Homotopy equivalence
nodes.description: A continuous map f: X to Y such that there exists g: Y to X with g composed with f homotopic to id_X and f composed with g homotopic to id_Y; X and Y are then said to have the same homotopy type.

nodes.name: Path homotopy class
nodes.description: The equivalence class [f] of a path f under the relation of path homotopy (homotopy relative to endpoints).

nodes.name: Simply connected space
nodes.description: A path-connected topological space whose fundamental group is trivial; equivalently, every loop is null-homotopic.

nodes.name: Fundamental group of the circle
nodes.description: The fundamental group pi_1(S^1) is isomorphic to Z, generated by the homotopy class of the loop that winds once around the circle.

nodes.name: Path lifting property
nodes.description: Given a covering map p: E to B, every path in B starting at b and every lift e_0 of b, there exists a unique path in E starting at e_0 that lifts the given path.

nodes.name: Homotopy lifting property
nodes.description: Given a covering map p: E to B, every homotopy F: [0,1]^2 to B and a lift of F(-, 0) can be uniquely lifted to a homotopy in E.

nodes.name: Lifting criterion (general lifting lemma)
nodes.description: A continuous map f: (Y, y_0) to (B, b_0) with Y path-connected and locally path-connected lifts to a map to the covering space E iff f_*(pi_1(Y)) is contained in p_*(pi_1(E)).

nodes.name: Deformation retract
nodes.description: A subspace A of X such that there exists a continuous map H: X x [0,1] to X with H(x,0) = x, H(x,1) in A for all x, and H(a,t) = a for all a in A and t; A is then a deformation retract of X.

nodes.name: Deformation retract preserves fundamental group
nodes.description: If A is a deformation retract of X, then the inclusion-induced homomorphism pi_1(A) to pi_1(X) is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Induced homomorphism on fundamental groups
nodes.description: A continuous map f: (X, x_0) to (Y, y_0) induces a group homomorphism f_*: pi_1(X, x_0) to pi_1(Y, y_0) defined by f_*([alpha]) = [f composed with alpha]; this assignment is functorial.

nodes.name: Fundamental group of a product space
nodes.description: For path-connected spaces X and Y, pi_1(X x Y, (x_0, y_0)) is isomorphic to pi_1(X, x_0) x pi_1(Y, y_0).

nodes.name: Jordan separation theorem
nodes.description: A topological embedding of S^(n-1) into S^n separates S^n into exactly two components.

nodes.name: Nonseparation theorem for arcs
nodes.description: A topological embedding of [0,1] into S^2 does not separate S^2; the complement of any arc in S^2 is connected.

nodes.name: Fundamental group of a wedge sum
nodes.description: If X and Y are path-connected with well-behaved base points, then pi_1(X v Y) is isomorphic to the free product pi_1(X) * pi_1(Y), by the Seifert-van Kampen theorem.

nodes.name: Computing pi_1 of surfaces via van Kampen
nodes.function_signature: (Fundamental polygon presentation) -> (pi_1 of surface as generators and relations)
nodes.description: Applies the Seifert-van Kampen theorem to the CW-structure of a surface given by a fundamental polygon to compute its fundamental group.

nodes.name: Fundamental group of the torus
nodes.description: The fundamental group pi_1(T^2) is isomorphic to Z x Z, the free abelian group on two generators.

nodes.name: Fundamental group of the real projective plane
nodes.description: The fundamental group pi_1(RP^2) is isomorphic to Z/2Z.

nodes.name: Surface (2-manifold)
nodes.description: A second-countable Hausdorff topological space in which every point has a neighborhood homeomorphic to an open subset of R^2.

nodes.name: Fundamental polygon
nodes.description: A convex polygon with edge identifications that yields a compact surface as its quotient space; encodes the surface via a word in edge labels.

nodes.name: Orientable surface
nodes.description: A compact surface that can be presented by a fundamental polygon whose boundary word has each edge label appearing once with each sign; equivalently, a surface with no embedded Mobius band.

nodes.name: Equivalence of covering spaces
nodes.description: Two covering spaces p_1: E_1 to B and p_2: E_2 to B are equivalent if there exists a homeomorphism h: E_1 to E_2 with p_2 composed with h = p_1.

nodes.name: Lifting correspondence (monodromy action)
nodes.description: For a covering map p: E to B and a path class [gamma] in pi_1(B, b_0), the lifting of gamma defines a bijection from the fiber p^{-1}(b_0) to itself, giving a group action of pi_1(B, b_0) on the fiber.

nodes.name: Classification of covering spaces
nodes.description: For a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected space B, there is a bijection between equivalence classes of connected coverings of B and conjugacy classes of subgroups of pi_1(B).

nodes.name: Semilocally simply connected space
nodes.description: A space X such that every point x has a neighborhood U with the inclusion-induced map pi_1(U, x) to pi_1(X, x) trivial; the necessary condition for the existence of a universal covering.

nodes.name: Existence of universal covering space
nodes.description: A connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected space admits a simply connected covering space (universal cover), unique up to covering equivalence.

nodes.name: Normal (regular) covering space
nodes.description: A covering space p: E to B for which the group of deck transformations acts transitively on each fiber; equivalently, p_*(pi_1(E)) is a normal subgroup of pi_1(B).

nodes.name: Index formula for coverings
nodes.description: For a connected covering space p: E to B, the number of sheets equals the index [pi_1(B, b_0) : p_*(pi_1(E, e_0))].

nodes.name: Urysohn function construction (dyadic rational technique)
nodes.function_signature: (Pair of disjoint closed sets in a normal space) -> (Continuous [0,1]-valued function separating them)
nodes.description: Constructs a continuous function via inductive assignment of open sets indexed by dyadic rationals, using normality at each step to interpolate between existing levels.

nodes.name: Lebesgue number argument
nodes.function_signature: (Open cover of a compact metric space) -> (Uniform positive lower bound delta for cover membership)
nodes.description: Uses sequential compactness of a compact metric space to obtain a Lebesgue number delta > 0 such that every set of diameter less than delta lies in some member of the cover.

nodes.name: Tube lemma argument
nodes.function_signature: (Open cover of a compact slice in a product) -> (Tube neighborhood containing the slice)
nodes.description: Extracts a tube neighborhood around a compact slice {x_0} x Y inside a product open set by first covering the slice with finitely many product-basis sets.

nodes.name: Sequence lemma
nodes.description: In a first-countable space, a point x lies in the closure of A iff there is a sequence of points in A converging to x; a map is continuous iff it preserves convergent sequences.

nodes.name: Metric space is second-countable iff separable
nodes.description: A metric space is second-countable if and only if it is separable; equivalently, it is Lindelof if and only if it is separable.

nodes.name: Long line
nodes.description: The order topology on S_Omega x [0,1) in the dictionary order, minus the minimal element; a path-connected, locally homeomorphic to R space that is not second-countable and not metrizable.

nodes.name: Topologist's sine curve
nodes.description: The closure in R^2 of the graph of sin(1/x) for x > 0; a connected space that is not path-connected, providing a standard counterexample.

nodes.name: T0-space (Kolmogorov)
nodes.description: A topological space in which for any two distinct points, at least one has a neighborhood not containing the other.

nodes.name: Pseudometric space
nodes.description: A set with a function d satisfying d(x,x)=0, symmetry, and triangle inequality, but not necessarily d(x,y)=0 implies x=y.

nodes.name: Quotient map (identification map)
nodes.description: A surjection p: X → Y such that U is open in Y if and only if p⁻¹(U) is open in X.

nodes.name: Locally compact space
nodes.description: A topological space in which every point has a neighborhood base consisting of compact sets.

nodes.name: Equicontinuous family
nodes.description: A family F of functions from X to a uniform space Y such that for each x and each entourage V, a single neighborhood U of x satisfies (f(y),f(x)) ∈ V for all f ∈ F and y ∈ U.

nodes.name: Totally bounded (precompact) uniform space
nodes.description: A uniform space in which for every entourage V there is a finite cover by V-small sets.

nodes.name: Cauchy net in a uniform space
nodes.description: A net (x_α) in a uniform space such that for every entourage V there exists α₀ with (x_α, x_β) ∈ V for all α, β ≥ α₀.

nodes.name: Base for a uniformity
nodes.description: A collection B of entourages such that every entourage contains a member of B, determining the uniformity as a filter base.

nodes.name: Even continuity
nodes.description: A family F of maps from X to Y is evenly continuous if for each (x,y) and each neighborhood W of y, there exist neighborhoods U of x and V of y such that f(x) ∈ V implies f(U) ⊂ W for all f ∈ F.

nodes.name: Convergence class
nodes.description: A class of pairs (net, point) satisfying Kelley's axioms (constant nets converge, subnets of convergent nets converge, Urysohn property, iterated limits) that uniquely determines a topology.

nodes.name: Realcompact space (Hewitt-Nachbin space)
nodes.description: A completely regular Hausdorff space homeomorphic to a closed subspace of a product of copies of ℝ; equivalently, every real maximal ideal of C(X) is fixed.

nodes.name: Morse-Kelley set theory
nodes.description: An axiomatic set theory with proper classes as first-class objects, stronger than NBG due to impredicative class comprehension.

nodes.name: Classification axiom scheme (MK comprehension)
nodes.description: For every formula φ (possibly quantifying over classes), {x : x is a set and φ(x)} is a class; the impredicative comprehension scheme of Morse-Kelley set theory.

nodes.name: Axiom of choice
nodes.description: For every family of nonempty sets, there exists a function choosing one element from each set.

nodes.name: Topology generated by a subbase
nodes.description: The coarsest topology containing a given subbase S, whose open sets are unions of finite intersections of members of S.

nodes.name: Eventually in
nodes.description: A net (x_α) is eventually in a set A if there exists α₀ such that x_α ∈ A for all α ≥ α₀.

nodes.name: Frequently in
nodes.description: A net (x_α) is frequently in a set A if for every α₀ there exists α ≥ α₀ with x_α ∈ A.

nodes.name: Cluster point of a net
nodes.description: A point x such that the net is frequently in every neighborhood of x.

nodes.name: Universal net (ultranet)
nodes.description: A net that is eventually in A or eventually in the complement of A for every subset A of the space.

nodes.name: Eventuality filter (filter generated by a net)
nodes.description: The filter of all sets that a given net is eventually in; establishes the correspondence between nets and filters.

nodes.name: Evaluation map (diagonal map)
nodes.description: The map e: X → ∏Y_f sending x to (f(x))_f, used to embed a Tychonoff space into a product of intervals.

nodes.name: Partition of unity
nodes.description: A locally finite family of continuous functions φ_i: X → [0,1] subordinate to an open cover with Σφ_i ≡ 1 at every point.

nodes.name: Hewitt realcompactification
nodes.description: The realcompactification υX of a Tychonoff space X, the smallest realcompact space containing X densely, to which every continuous real-valued function extends.

nodes.name: Gauge (family of pseudometrics)
nodes.description: A family of pseudometrics generating a uniformity; every uniformity arises from a gauge and the topology is the coarsest making all pseudometrics continuous.

nodes.name: Metrizable uniformity
nodes.description: A uniformity induced by a single metric; a uniformity is metrizable if and only if it has a countable base.

nodes.name: Existence of universal subnets
nodes.description: Every net has a universal (ultra) subnet; proved using Zorn's lemma or the ultrafilter lemma.

nodes.name: Kelley's convergence class theorem
nodes.description: A convergence class satisfying Kelley's four axioms uniquely determines a topology on the underlying set.

nodes.name: Existence of ultrafilters (ultrafilter lemma)
nodes.description: Every proper filter can be extended to an ultrafilter; equivalent to the Boolean prime ideal theorem.

nodes.name: Equivalence of nets and filters
nodes.description: Nets and filters are equivalent descriptions of convergence: every net determines an eventuality filter and every filter arises from a net, preserving convergence.

nodes.name: Universal property of product topology
nodes.description: A map into a product space is continuous if and only if each component is continuous; the product topology is initial for projections.

nodes.name: Universal property of quotient topology
nodes.description: A function out of a quotient space is continuous if and only if its composition with the quotient map is continuous.

nodes.name: Product of continuous functions is continuous
nodes.description: If f_i: X → Y_i is continuous for each i, then the product map x ↦ (f_i(x)) into ∏Y_i is continuous.

nodes.name: Closed continuous surjection is a quotient map
nodes.description: A continuous surjection that is a closed map is automatically a quotient map.

nodes.name: Open continuous surjection is a quotient map
nodes.description: A continuous surjection that is an open map is automatically a quotient map.

nodes.name: Completely regular spaces separate points from closed sets
nodes.description: A space is completely regular iff for each point x and closed set F not containing x, there is a continuous f: X → [0,1] with f(x)=0 and f|_F=1.

nodes.name: Tychonoff embedding theorem
nodes.description: Every Tychonoff space embeds homeomorphically into a product of unit intervals [0,1]^κ via the evaluation map.

nodes.name: Normal spaces are completely regular
nodes.description: Every normal T1 space is completely regular, as Urysohn's lemma provides the separating functions.

nodes.name: Filter characterization of compactness
nodes.description: A space is compact if and only if every ultrafilter converges, equivalently if every filter has a cluster point.

nodes.name: Tychonoff theorem equivalent to axiom of choice
nodes.description: Tychonoff's theorem for arbitrary products of compact spaces is equivalent to the axiom of choice in ZF (Kelley, 1950).

nodes.name: Alexandroff compactification Hausdorff iff locally compact Hausdorff
nodes.description: The one-point compactification of X is Hausdorff if and only if X is locally compact and Hausdorff.

nodes.name: Universal property of Stone-Čech compactification
nodes.description: Every continuous map from a Tychonoff space X to a compact Hausdorff space K extends uniquely through βX.

nodes.name: Compact implies paracompact
nodes.description: Every compact space is paracompact, since every open cover has a finite (hence locally finite) refinement.

nodes.name: Unique uniformity on compact Hausdorff space
nodes.description: A compact Hausdorff space admits exactly one uniformity compatible with its topology, consisting of all neighborhoods of the diagonal.

nodes.name: Baire category theorem (complete metric space)
nodes.description: Every complete metric space is a Baire space: countable intersections of dense open sets are dense.

nodes.name: Hausdorff uniform space is completely regular
nodes.description: Every Hausdorff uniform space is completely regular (Tychonoff).

nodes.name: Uniform continuity implies continuity
nodes.description: Every uniformly continuous map between uniform spaces is continuous with respect to the induced uniform topologies.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of completion
nodes.description: Every uniform space has a Hausdorff completion, unique up to uniform isomorphism, constructed via equivalence classes of Cauchy filters.

nodes.name: Extension of uniformly continuous functions
nodes.description: A uniformly continuous function from a dense subspace to a complete Hausdorff uniform space extends uniquely to the whole space.

nodes.name: Compact-open topology refines pointwise convergence
nodes.description: The compact-open topology on C(X,Y) is finer than the topology of pointwise convergence.

nodes.name: Evaluation map continuity
nodes.description: The evaluation map ev: C(X,Y) × X → Y is jointly continuous when C(X,Y) has the compact-open topology and X is locally compact Hausdorff.

nodes.name: Compact-open equals uniform convergence for compact domain
nodes.description: When X is compact, the compact-open topology on C(X,Y) coincides with the topology of uniform convergence.

nodes.name: Equicontinuity and topology agreement
nodes.description: On an equicontinuous family, the topologies of pointwise convergence, compact convergence, and compact-open all coincide.

nodes.name: Even continuity and equicontinuity relationship
nodes.description: Equicontinuity implies even continuity; the converse holds under compactness hypotheses on the codomain.

nodes.name: Ascoli theorem via even continuity (Kelley)
nodes.description: A subset of C(X,Y) is compact in the compact-open topology iff it is closed, evenly continuous, and pointwise precompact; Kelley's generalization beyond metric spaces.

nodes.name: Net argument for compactness
nodes.function_signature: (Net in space, Zorn's lemma) → (Convergent subnet, compactness result)
nodes.description: Proves compactness properties by extracting convergent or universal subnets from arbitrary nets using Zorn's lemma.

nodes.name: Filter argument for compactness
nodes.function_signature: (Ultrafilter, FIP characterization) → (Compactness result)
nodes.description: Proves compactness by showing every ultrafilter converges, using the finite intersection property and ultrafilter extension.

nodes.name: Diagonal argument for metrization
nodes.function_signature: (Countable base/family) → (Compatible metric)
nodes.description: Constructs a compatible metric from a countable base by summing weighted pseudometrics via a diagonal enumeration.

nodes.name: Zorn's lemma in topology
nodes.function_signature: (Partially ordered family of sets/filters) → (Maximal object)
nodes.description: Applies Zorn's lemma to produce maximal filters (ultrafilters), maximal chains, or universal nets in topological arguments.

nodes.name: Cofinal subnet extraction
nodes.function_signature: (Net, desired property) → (Subnet with property)
nodes.description: Extracts a subnet with a desired property by constructing a cofinal map from a refined directed set.

nodes.name: Cauchy filter completion construction
nodes.function_signature: (Uniform space) → (Complete uniform space)
nodes.description: Constructs the completion of a uniform space as equivalence classes of minimal Cauchy filters with extended uniformity.

nodes.name: Cofinite topology trick (Kelley's AC proof)
nodes.function_signature: (Family of nonempty sets) → (Choice function)
nodes.description: Derives the axiom of choice from Tychonoff's theorem by endowing each set with the cofinite topology and extracting a choice function from the product.

nodes.name: Evaluation map embedding
nodes.function_signature: (Tychonoff space, separating family) → (Embedding in product of intervals)
nodes.description: Embeds a Tychonoff space into [0,1]^κ via the evaluation map x ↦ (f(x))_f for a separating family of continuous functions.

nodes.name: CW complex
nodes.description: A topological space X built inductively by attaching n-cells via maps φ_α: S^{n-1} → X^{n-1}, equipped with the weak topology where A ⊆ X is closed iff A ∩ closure(e_α) is closed for each cell e_α.

nodes.name: n-skeleton
nodes.description: The subspace X^n of a CW complex X consisting of all cells of dimension at most n, constructed inductively from X^{n-1} by attaching n-cells.

nodes.name: Cell attachment
nodes.function_signature: (Space A, attaching map φ: S^{n-1} → A) → (Space A ∪_φ D^n)
nodes.description: Constructs a new space by gluing an n-disk to A along its boundary via the attaching map φ, forming the adjunction space A ∪_φ D^n.

nodes.name: Contractible space
nodes.description: A topological space X that is homotopy equivalent to a point, equivalently the identity map id_X is homotopic to a constant map.

nodes.name: Homotopy extension property
nodes.description: A pair (X, A) has the HEP if every homotopy of A and every map of X extending the initial map of A can be extended to a homotopy of X; equivalently the inclusion A ↪ X is a cofibration.

nodes.name: Change of basepoint isomorphism
nodes.description: For a path γ from x₀ to x₁ in X, the map [f] ↦ [γ̄·f·γ] is a group isomorphism between the fundamental groups at the two basepoints.

nodes.name: Universal covering space
nodes.description: A covering space p: X̃ → X where X̃ is simply connected; it is unique up to isomorphism for connected, locally path-connected, semi-locally simply connected X and covers every other connected covering of X.

nodes.name: Fundamental group of a graph
nodes.description: The fundamental group of a connected graph is a free group, with rank equal to 1 minus the Euler characteristic of the graph (i.e., the number of edges not in a maximal spanning tree).

nodes.name: Fundamental group of closed surfaces
nodes.description: The fundamental group of the closed orientable surface of genus g has presentation ⟨a₁,b₁,…,a_g,b_g | [a₁,b₁]⋯[a_g,b_g]⟩, and similarly for non-orientable surfaces with appropriate relations.

nodes.name: Singular n-simplex
nodes.description: A continuous map from the standard n-simplex Δⁿ to a topological space X, serving as the generating element for singular chain groups.

nodes.name: Singular chain group Cₙ(X)
nodes.description: The free abelian group generated by all singular n-simplices in X, forming the degree-n component of the singular chain complex.

nodes.name: Boundary operator ∂ₙ
nodes.description: The homomorphism defined by ∂ₙ(σ) = Σᵢ(-1)ⁱ σ|[v₀,…,v̂ᵢ,…,vₙ], satisfying ∂ₙ₋₁∘∂ₙ = 0 and making C_*(X) a chain complex.

nodes.name: Singular homology group Hₙ(X)
nodes.description: The n-th homology group of X, defined as the quotient of n-cycles by n-boundaries in the singular chain complex, measuring n-dimensional holes in X.

nodes.name: Reduced homology
nodes.description: A modified version of singular homology using the augmented chain complex ε: C₀(X) → ℤ, satisfying H̃ₙ(X) = Hₙ(X) for n ≥ 1 and H̃₀(X) ⊕ ℤ ≅ H₀(X), with H̃ₙ(pt) = 0 for all n.

nodes.name: Homotopy invariance of homology
nodes.type_signature: f ≃ g ⟹ f_* = g_*: Hₙ(X) → Hₙ(Y)
nodes.description: If f, g: X → Y are homotopic maps then they induce identical homomorphisms on all singular homology groups, so homotopy equivalent spaces have isomorphic homology.

nodes.name: Chain homotopy
nodes.function_signature: (Chain maps f_#, g_#: C_*(X) → C_*(Y)) → (Proof that f_* = g_*: H_*(X) → H_*(Y))
nodes.description: Constructs a sequence of homomorphisms Pₙ: Cₙ(X) → Cₙ₊₁(Y) satisfying ∂P + P∂ = g_# - f_#, proving f_# and g_# induce the same maps on homology.

nodes.name: Relative homology group Hₙ(X, A)
nodes.description: The homology of the quotient chain complex C_*(X)/C_*(A), measuring n-dimensional holes in X modulo those in A, fitting into the long exact sequence of the pair (X, A).

nodes.name: Barycentric subdivision
nodes.function_signature: (Singular chain in Cₙ(X)) → (Chain of smaller simplices in Cₙ(X))
nodes.description: Iteratively subdivides singular simplices into smaller ones whose diameters approach zero, used to prove excision by making chains small relative to a cover.

nodes.name: Good pair (X, A)
nodes.description: A pair (X, A) where A is a nonempty closed subspace that is a deformation retract of some open neighborhood in X, ensuring that the quotient map X → X/A induces an isomorphism Hₙ(X, A) ≅ H̃ₙ(X/A).

nodes.name: Homology of spheres
nodes.description: The singular homology groups of the n-sphere are ℤ in dimensions 0 and n and zero elsewhere, computed via the Mayer-Vietoris sequence or cellular homology.

nodes.name: Local homology group
nodes.description: The relative homology group at a point x ∈ X, detecting the local topological structure; for an n-manifold it equals ℤ in dimension n and zero otherwise.

nodes.name: Homology with coefficients
nodes.description: Homology computed from the chain complex C_*(X) tensored with an abelian group G, allowing detection of torsion phenomena invisible to integer homology.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence of a triple
nodes.type_signature: ⋯ → Hₙ(B, A) → Hₙ(X, A) → Hₙ(X, B) → Hₙ₋₁(B, A) → ⋯
nodes.description: For A ⊆ B ⊆ X, the relative homology groups fit into a long exact sequence relating the three pairs (B,A), (X,A), and (X,B).

nodes.name: Homology of ℝPⁿ
nodes.description: H₀(ℝPⁿ) ≅ ℤ, Hₖ(ℝPⁿ) ≅ ℤ/2 for odd k with 0 < k < n, Hₙ(ℝPⁿ) ≅ ℤ if n is odd (0 if n even), and all other groups vanish.

nodes.name: Homology of ℂPⁿ
nodes.description: H₂ₖ(ℂPⁿ) ≅ ℤ for 0 ≤ k ≤ n and all odd-dimensional homology groups vanish, following from the CW structure with one cell in each even dimension.

nodes.name: Transfer homomorphism (covering spaces)
nodes.function_signature: (n-sheeted covering p: X̃ → X) → (τ: Hₙ(X) → Hₙ(X̃) with p_*∘τ = multiplication by n)
nodes.description: Lifts chains from the base to the total space of a finite-sheeted covering by summing over all lifts, yielding a chain map whose composition with p_* is multiplication by the number of sheets.

nodes.name: Coboundary operator δⁿ
nodes.description: The dual of the boundary operator, defined by (δφ)(σ) = φ(∂σ) for cochains φ, satisfying δⁿ⁺¹∘δⁿ = 0 and making C*(X; G) a cochain complex.

nodes.name: Cross product (cohomology)
nodes.type_signature: ×: Hᵖ(X; R) ⊗ Hᵍ(Y; R) → Hᵖ⁺ᵍ(X × Y; R)
nodes.description: The external product defined by a × b = p₁*(a) ∪ p₂*(b) where p₁, p₂ are projections, relating the cohomology of a product to those of its factors via the Künneth theorem.

nodes.name: Cap product
nodes.type_signature: ∩: Hₙ(X; R) × Hᵖ(X; R) → Hₙ₋ₚ(X; R)
nodes.description: A bilinear pairing defined by σ ∩ φ = φ(σ|[v₀,…,vₚ])·σ|[vₚ,…,vₙ], making homology a module over the cohomology ring and used to state Poincaré duality as [M] ∩ −: Hᵖ(M) → Hₙ₋ₚ(M).

nodes.name: Fundamental class of a manifold
nodes.description: For a closed connected oriented n-manifold M, the unique generator [M] of Hₙ(M; ℤ) ≅ ℤ that restricts to the local orientation at every point.

nodes.name: Cohomology with compact support
nodes.description: The direct limit of cohomology groups Hⁿ(X, X∖K; R) over compact subsets K ⊆ X, used to formulate Poincaré duality for non-compact manifolds.

nodes.name: Bockstein homomorphism
nodes.function_signature: (Short exact sequence 0 → G′ → G → G″ → 0) → (β: Hⁿ(X; G″) → Hⁿ⁺¹(X; G′))
nodes.description: The connecting homomorphism in the long exact cohomology sequence induced by a short exact sequence of coefficient groups, detecting elements not liftable to G-cohomology.

nodes.name: Orientation double cover
nodes.description: The unique connected double covering of a connected manifold M whose total space is orientable; M is orientable iff this cover is disconnected (trivial).

nodes.name: Higher homotopy group πₙ(X)
nodes.description: The set of basepoint-preserving homotopy classes of maps (Sⁿ, s₀) → (X, x₀), forming an abelian group for n ≥ 2 under the composition inherited from the group structure on Sⁿ as a co-H-space.

nodes.name: πₙ is abelian for n ≥ 2
nodes.description: For n ≥ 2 the homotopy group πₙ(X, x₀) is abelian, following from the Eckmann-Hilton argument since elements can be composed in two independent directions.

nodes.name: Relative homotopy group πₙ(X, A)
nodes.description: The set of homotopy classes of maps (Dⁿ, S^{n-1}, s₀) → (X, A, x₀), forming a group for n ≥ 2 (abelian for n ≥ 3), fitting into the long exact sequence of the pair.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence of a pair (homotopy)
nodes.description: For a pair (X, A) with basepoint in A, the inclusion and boundary maps form an exact sequence of homotopy groups extending down to π₀.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence of a fibration
nodes.description: For a fibration F → E → B, the homotopy groups fit into a long exact sequence relating the fiber, total space, and base, induced by the boundary map ∂: πₙ(B) → πₙ₋₁(F).

nodes.name: CW approximation theorem
nodes.description: Every topological space X admits a CW complex Z and a weak homotopy equivalence Z → X, and the construction is functorial up to homotopy.

nodes.name: Relative Hurewicz theorem
nodes.description: If (X, A) is (n-1)-connected with n ≥ 2, A simply connected and nonempty, then Hᵢ(X, A) = 0 for i < n and the Hurewicz map πₙ(X, A) → Hₙ(X, A) is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: n-connected space
nodes.description: A topological space X such that πᵢ(X) = 0 for all i ≤ n, meaning every map Sⁱ → X for i ≤ n extends to a map Dⁱ⁺¹ → X.

nodes.name: n-connected pair
nodes.description: A pair (X, A) such that πᵢ(X, A) = 0 for all i ≤ n, equivalently every map (Dⁱ, S^{i-1}) → (X, A) for i ≤ n is homotopic rel S^{i-1} to a map into A.

nodes.name: Postnikov tower
nodes.description: A sequence of fibrations Xₙ → Xₙ₋₁ with fibers K(πₙ(X), n) such that X → Xₙ induces isomorphisms on πᵢ for i ≤ n and πᵢ(Xₙ) = 0 for i > n, decomposing the homotopy type of X.

nodes.name: k-invariants
nodes.description: The cohomology class that classifies the fibration Xₙ → Xₙ₋₁ in a Postnikov tower, determining how the n-th homotopy group is attached to the lower stages.

nodes.name: Obstruction theory
nodes.function_signature: (Map f: A → Y, extension problem over CW pair (X, A)) → (Obstruction classes in Hⁿ⁺¹(X, A; πₙ(Y)))
nodes.description: Determines whether a map defined on a subcomplex extends over the next skeleton by computing an obstruction cocycle; the map extends over all of X iff all obstruction classes vanish.

nodes.name: Loop space ΩX
nodes.description: The space of basepoint-preserving loops in X with the compact-open topology, satisfying πₙ(ΩX) ≅ πₙ₊₁(X) and serving as the fiber of the path-loop fibration PX → X.

nodes.name: Path-loop fibration
nodes.description: The fibration where PX is the contractible space of paths starting at the basepoint, the projection sends a path to its endpoint, and the fiber over x₀ is the loop space ΩX.

nodes.name: π₃(S²) ≅ ℤ
nodes.description: The third homotopy group of the 2-sphere is infinite cyclic, generated by the Hopf fibration η: S³ → S², proved using the long exact sequence of the Hopf bundle.

nodes.name: Fiber sequence (Puppe sequence)
nodes.type_signature: ⋯ → Ω²B → Ω F → ΩE → ΩB → F → E → B
nodes.description: The iterated extension of a fibration F → E → B to the left by taking loop spaces, yielding an infinite sequence where each three consecutive terms form a fiber sequence.

nodes.name: Cofiber sequence (Puppe sequence)
nodes.description: The iterated extension of a cofibration A → X to the right by taking cones and suspensions, yielding an exact sequence on homotopy classes [−, Y] for any Y.

nodes.name: π₁ action on πₙ
nodes.type_signature: π₁(X, x₀) × πₙ(X, x₀) → πₙ(X, x₀)
nodes.description: The action of the fundamental group on higher homotopy groups defined by transporting spheroids along loops, making πₙ(X) a module over ℤ[π₁(X)]; X is n-simple if this action is trivial.

nodes.name: Compression lemma
nodes.description: If (X, A) is a CW pair and (Y, B) is a pair with πₙ(Y, B) = 0 for all n such that X∖A has cells of dimension n, then any map (X, A) → (Y, B) is homotopic rel A to a map into B.

nodes.name: Δ-complex
nodes.description: A space built from a collection of simplices identified along faces by face maps (without requiring distinct vertices), intermediate between simplicial complexes and CW complexes, with a well-defined simplicial homology.

nodes.name: Acyclic models
nodes.function_signature: (Natural transformations between functors on a category with models) → (Chain homotopy equivalence)
nodes.description: Proves that two chain complex-valued functors are naturally chain homotopy equivalent by checking they agree on a set of acyclic model objects, used to prove commutativity of cross products and Eilenberg-Zilber.

nodes.name: Naturality of long exact sequences
nodes.description: A map of pairs f: (X, A) → (Y, B) induces a commutative ladder between the long exact homology sequences of the two pairs, so connecting homomorphisms are natural transformations.

nodes.name: Suspension ΣX
nodes.description: The quotient of X × [0,1] obtained by collapsing X×{0} to one point and X×{1} to another point; satisfies H̃ₙ(ΣX) ≅ H̃ₙ₋₁(X) and Σ: πₙ(X) → πₙ₊₁(ΣX).

nodes.name: Suspension isomorphism (cohomology)
nodes.description: The natural isomorphism between the reduced cohomology of X and the shifted reduced cohomology of its suspension, characterizing cohomology operations via stability.

nodes.name: Homology of a wedge sum
nodes.description: The reduced homology of a wedge of spaces is the direct sum of the reduced homologies of the summands, provided the wedge has the topology of a CW complex.

nodes.name: Effect of cell attachment on homology
nodes.description: If Y = X ∪_φ eⁿ is obtained by attaching an n-cell, then Hₖ(Y, X) ≅ ℤ for k = n and 0 otherwise, and the long exact sequence determines how H_*(Y) differs from H_*(X).

nodes.name: Cellular homology equals singular homology
nodes.description: For a CW complex X, the homology of the cellular chain complex (with Cₙ = Hₙ(Xⁿ, Xⁿ⁻¹) free abelian on n-cells) is naturally isomorphic to singular homology.

nodes.name: Degree as sum of local degrees
nodes.description: For f: Sⁿ → Sⁿ and a regular value y, the degree of f equals the sum of local degrees at preimage points, where each local degree is ±1 for a local homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Degree of the antipodal map
nodes.description: The antipodal map a: Sⁿ → Sⁿ has degree (-1)^{n+1}, since it is the composition of (n+1) reflections each of degree -1.

nodes.name: Mapping degree formula
nodes.description: For a map f: M → N between closed connected oriented n-manifolds, the induced map on top homology is multiplication by the integer deg(f), which equals the signed count of preimages of any regular value.

nodes.name: Cohomology ring of ℝPⁿ
nodes.description: The mod-2 cohomology ring of ℝPⁿ is a truncated polynomial ring on one generator α in degree 1, proved using the cup product structure.

nodes.name: Cohomology ring of ℂPⁿ
nodes.description: The integral cohomology ring of ℂPⁿ is a truncated polynomial ring on one generator α in degree 2, distinguishing ℂPⁿ from a product of spheres.

nodes.name: Graded commutativity of cup product
nodes.description: For α ∈ Hᵖ(X; R) and β ∈ Hᵍ(X; R), the cup product satisfies α ∪ β = (-1)^{pq} β ∪ α, making H*(X; R) a graded-commutative ring.

nodes.name: Cohomological Mayer-Vietoris sequence
nodes.description: For X = A ∪ B with A, B open, the long exact sequence in cohomology relating H*(X), H*(A) ⊕ H*(B), and H*(A∩B), dual to the homological Mayer-Vietoris sequence.

nodes.name: Cup product distinguishes spaces
nodes.description: Spaces with isomorphic cohomology groups but different ring structures (e.g., ℂP² vs S² ∨ S⁴) are not homotopy equivalent, demonstrating that the cup product carries strictly more information than additive cohomology.

nodes.name: Fiber bundle is a Serre fibration
nodes.description: Every fiber bundle F → E → B with paracompact base is a Serre fibration (has the homotopy lifting property for CW complexes), so its long exact homotopy sequence applies.

nodes.name: Intersection form
nodes.type_signature: Q_M: H_n(M²ⁿ; ℤ) × H_n(M²ⁿ; ℤ) → ℤ
nodes.description: The bilinear form on middle homology of a closed oriented 2n-manifold defined by algebraic intersection number, equivalently by the cup product pairing via Poincaré duality.

nodes.name: Homology manifold
nodes.description: A topological space X whose local homology groups H_*(X, X∖{x}; ℤ) at every point x are isomorphic to those of ℝⁿ, allowing Poincaré duality to hold without a manifold structure.

nodes.name: Smith theory
nodes.function_signature: (ℤ/p-action on space X) → (Constraints on homology of fixed-point set X^{ℤ/p})
nodes.description: Uses transfer and localization in mod-p homology to bound the total Betti numbers of the fixed-point set of a ℤ/p-action by those of the ambient space.

nodes.name: Homotopy type
nodes.description: The equivalence class of a topological space under homotopy equivalence; two spaces have the same homotopy type iff there exist continuous maps f: X → Y and g: Y → X with g∘f ≃ id_X and f∘g ≃ id_Y.

nodes.name: Retraction (topological)
nodes.type_signature: r: X → A, r ∘ ι = id_A
nodes.description: A continuous map r: X → A where A ⊆ X such that r restricts to the identity on A; A is then called a retract of X.

nodes.name: Fundamental groupoid
nodes.description: The category whose objects are points of X and whose morphisms are path-homotopy classes of paths, with composition given by concatenation; it generalizes the fundamental group to a basepoint-free invariant.

nodes.name: H-space
nodes.type_signature: (X, μ, e) where μ: X × X → X
nodes.description: A topological space X with a continuous multiplication μ: X × X → X and a two-sided identity e up to homotopy (μ(e,x) ≃ x ≃ μ(x,e)); examples include loop spaces, topological groups, and S¹, S³, S⁷.

nodes.name: Co-H-space (H-cogroup)
nodes.type_signature: (X, ν) where ν: X → X ∨ X
nodes.description: A pointed space X with a comultiplication ν: X → X ∨ X that is coassociative and counital up to homotopy; the suspension ΣA is the prototypical co-H-space, and [X, Y] carries a natural group structure when X is a co-H-space.

nodes.name: Hurewicz fibration
nodes.description: A continuous map p: E → B satisfying the homotopy lifting property with respect to all topological spaces, strictly stronger than a Serre fibration which only requires HLP for CW complexes.

nodes.name: Mapping path space (path-space fibration)
nodes.description: For a map f: X → Y, the space of pairs (x, γ) where γ is a path in Y starting at f(x); the endpoint projection Ef → Y is a Hurewicz fibration factoring f, used to replace arbitrary maps by fibrations.

nodes.name: Abstract simplicial complex
nodes.description: A collection Σ of finite subsets (simplices) of a vertex set V, closed under taking subsets; its geometric realization |K| is a topological space obtained by assigning a geometric simplex to each abstract simplex.

nodes.name: Star and link of a simplex
nodes.description: For a simplex σ in a simplicial complex K, the star St(σ) is the union of interiors of all simplices containing σ, and the link Lk(σ) is the subcomplex of simplices in the closure of St(σ) that are disjoint from σ.

nodes.name: Cellular map
nodes.type_signature: f: X → Y with f(Xⁿ) ⊆ Yⁿ
nodes.description: A continuous map between CW complexes that sends the n-skeleton of the domain into the n-skeleton of the codomain for every n; the cellular approximation theorem states every continuous map between CW complexes is homotopic to a cellular map.

nodes.name: Relative CW complex
nodes.description: A pair (X, A) where X is obtained from A by successively attaching cells of increasing dimension; generalizes CW complexes (where A = ∅) and provides the natural setting for relative homology and obstruction theory.

nodes.name: Relative singular homology
nodes.description: The homology of the quotient chain complex C_*(X)/C_*(A), fitting into the long exact sequence ⋯ → Hₙ(A) → Hₙ(X) → Hₙ(X,A) → Hₙ₋₁(A) → ⋯ and satisfying excision.

nodes.name: Short five lemma
nodes.description: If 0 → A → B → C → 0 and 0 → A' → B' → C' → 0 are short exact sequences with vertical maps α, β, γ forming a commutative diagram, then if α and γ are isomorphisms, so is β.

nodes.name: Slant product
nodes.description: A bilinear pairing that takes a cohomology class on a product and a homology class on one factor and produces a cohomology class on the other factor; used in the construction of Poincare duality and the Thom isomorphism.

nodes.name: Kronecker pairing
nodes.description: The evaluation pairing between cohomology and homology defined by ⟨[φ],[c]⟩ = φ(c), inducing the homomorphism Hⁿ(X; R) → Hom(Hₙ(X; R), R) that appears in the universal coefficient theorem.

nodes.name: n-connected map
nodes.description: A continuous map f: X → Y such that all homotopy fibers are (n-1)-connected, equivalently f_*: πₖ(X) → πₖ(Y) is an isomorphism for k < n and a surjection for k = n.

nodes.name: Suspension-loop space adjunction (Σ ⊣ Ω)
nodes.description: The natural bijection between pointed homotopy classes of maps from the suspension ΣX to Y and pointed maps from X to the loop space ΩY, making Σ and Ω an adjoint pair in the pointed homotopy category.

nodes.name: Representability of cohomology
nodes.description: For CW complexes X, the n-th cohomology group with coefficients in G is naturally isomorphic to the set of homotopy classes of maps from X to the Eilenberg-MacLane space K(G,n); this is the prototypical application of Brown representability.

nodes.name: Obstruction cocycle
nodes.description: The (n+1)-cochain that measures the failure of extending a map f defined on the n-skeleton to the (n+1)-skeleton; it is a cocycle whose cohomology class is the obstruction to extension.

nodes.name: Difference cochain
nodes.description: For two maps f, g: Xⁿ → Y that agree on Xⁿ⁻¹, the n-cochain measuring their difference on each n-cell; satisfies δd(f,g) = cⁿ⁺¹(g) - cⁿ⁺¹(f), providing the key tool for modifying maps to kill obstructions.

nodes.name: Moore-Postnikov decomposition
nodes.description: A factorization of a map f: X → Y into a tower of fibrations where each stage X[n] → X[n-1] is a principal fibration with fiber K(πₙ(f), n), refining the Postnikov tower to maps between spaces.

nodes.name: Cohomology operation
nodes.description: A natural transformation between cohomology functors; by the representability theorem, classified by [K(G,n), K(G',m)] and including Steenrod squares, Steenrod powers, and Bockstein homomorphisms as primary examples.

nodes.name: Steenrod squares
nodes.description: The unique stable cohomology operations Sqⁱ in mod-2 cohomology satisfying Sq⁰ = id, Sqⁿ(x) = x² for |x| = n, Sqⁱ(x) = 0 for i > |x|, the Cartan formula, and the Adem relations; they generate the mod-2 Steenrod algebra.

nodes.name: Steenrod reduced powers
