nodes.description: The stable cohomology operations Pⁱ in mod-p cohomology for odd primes p, satisfying P⁰ = id, the Cartan formula, and Adem relations; together with the Bockstein β they generate the mod-p Steenrod algebra.

nodes.name: Steenrod algebra
nodes.description: The graded associative algebra over 𝔽_p generated by the Steenrod squares (p=2) or the Bockstein and reduced powers (p odd), subject to the Adem relations; it is a Hopf algebra and H*(X; 𝔽_p) is naturally a module over 𝒜_p.

nodes.name: Thom space
nodes.description: For a vector bundle ξ over B, the quotient of the disk bundle by the sphere bundle, equivalently the one-point compactification of the total space; carries the Thom class and realizes the Thom isomorphism.

nodes.name: Cone CX
nodes.description: The quotient of X × [0,1] by collapsing X × {1} to a point; CX is always contractible, and the mapping cone Cf = CX ∪_f Y of a map f: X → Y is the basic building block of the Puppe sequence.

nodes.name: Join of spaces
nodes.description: The quotient of X × Y × [0,1] identifying (x,y₁,0) ~ (x,y₂,0) and (x₁,y,1) ~ (x₂,y,1); satisfies Sⁿ * Sᵐ ≅ Sⁿ⁺ᵐ⁺¹ and X * S⁰ ≅ ΣX, used in constructing the Milnor join model of classifying spaces.

nodes.name: Homotopy pullback
nodes.description: The homotopy-invariant version of the categorical pullback, defined as the space of triples (x, γ, y) where γ is a path in B from f(x) to g(y); it is invariant under replacing f or g by homotopic maps.

nodes.name: Homotopy fiber
nodes.description: The homotopy fiber of f: X → B over b₀, defined as the pullback of f along the path-space fibration; it fits into the fiber sequence hofiber(f) → X → B and its homotopy groups yield the long exact sequence of f.

nodes.name: Induced fibration (pullback bundle)
nodes.description: For a fibration p: E → B and a map f: X → B, the pullback f*E → X is again a fibration with the same fiber; this construction is fundamental in classifying bundle theory and the definition of characteristic classes.

nodes.name: Hopf algebra structure on H-space homology
nodes.description: For a connected H-space X with field coefficients, the homology H_*(X; k) is a graded connected Hopf algebra with product from the Pontryagin product and coproduct from the diagonal; classified by the Milnor-Moore and Borel structure theorems.

nodes.name: Tensor product of chain complexes
nodes.description: The chain complex with degree-n component ⊕_{p+q=n} Cₚ ⊗ Dq and differential ∂(c ⊗ d) = ∂c ⊗ d + (-1)^|c| c ⊗ ∂d; the Eilenberg-Zilber theorem identifies C_*(X × Y) with C_*(X) ⊗ C_*(Y) up to chain homotopy equivalence.

nodes.name: Smash product
nodes.description: The quotient of the product X × Y by the wedge X ∨ Y for pointed spaces; satisfies Sⁿ ∧ Sᵐ ≅ Sⁿ⁺ᵐ and ΣX ≅ S¹ ∧ X, and serves as the symmetric monoidal product in the stable homotopy category.

nodes.name: Wedge sum
nodes.description: The coproduct in the category of pointed spaces, formed by identifying the basepoints of X and Y; satisfies π₁(X ∨ Y) ≅ π₁(X) * π₁(Y) for well-pointed spaces and H̃ₙ(X ∨ Y) ≅ H̃ₙ(X) ⊕ H̃ₙ(Y).

nodes.name: Homotopy pushout
nodes.description: The homotopy-invariant version of the categorical pushout for a span X ← A → Y, constructed as X ⊔ (A × [0,1]) ⊔ Y with appropriate identifications; the double mapping cylinder of f: A → X and g: A → Y.

nodes.name: Spectral sequence computation
nodes.function_signature: (Filtered complex or fibration) → (Target homology/cohomology groups)
nodes.description: Computes homology or cohomology of a total space, filtered complex, or composition of functors by identifying the E₂ page, propagating differentials, and reading off the abutment from E_∞ via extension problems.

nodes.name: NDR pair (neighborhood deformation retract pair)
nodes.description: A pair (X, A) together with maps u: X → [0,1] and h: X × I → X such that A = u⁻¹(0), h₀ = id, h_t|_A = id_A, and h₁(u⁻¹([0,1))) ⊂ A; equivalently, A ↪ X is a cofibration.

nodes.name: NDR pair characterization of cofibrations
nodes.description: An inclusion A ↪ X of compactly generated spaces is a cofibration if and only if (X, A) is an NDR pair.

nodes.name: Loop space of Eilenberg-MacLane space delooping
nodes.description: The loop space of an Eilenberg-MacLane space K(G, n+1) is homotopy equivalent to K(G, n) for n ≥ 1 and any abelian group G.

nodes.name: Spectrum (stable homotopy theory)
nodes.description: A sequence of pointed spaces {Eₙ} with structure maps σₙ: ΣEₙ → Eₙ₊₁ representing generalized cohomology theories in the stable homotopy category.

nodes.name: Omega spectrum (Ω-spectrum)
nodes.description: A spectrum in which the adjoint structure maps Eₙ → ΩEₙ₊₁ are weak homotopy equivalences; every generalized cohomology theory is represented by an Ω-spectrum.

nodes.name: Stiefel-Whitney numbers
nodes.description: For a closed n-manifold M, the mod-2 integers ⟨w_{i₁}(TM) ⌣ ··· ⌣ w_{iₖ}(TM), [M]⟩ with i₁ + ··· + iₖ = n; two manifolds are unoriented-cobordant iff all their Stiefel-Whitney numbers agree.

nodes.name: Wu formula
nodes.description: The Stiefel-Whitney classes of a closed manifold M are determined by the Wu classes vᵢ via Sq(v) = w, where vᵢ is characterized by ⟨vᵢ ⌣ x, [M]⟩ = ⟨Sqⁱ(x), [M]⟩.

nodes.name: Localization of spaces at a set of primes
nodes.description: For a set of primes T, the T-localization X_T of a nilpotent space X with πₙ(X_T) ≅ πₙ(X) ⊗ ℤ_T, initial among maps inducing T-local isomorphisms on homotopy groups.

nodes.name: Rationalization of a space
nodes.description: The localization of a nilpotent space X at the empty set of primes, yielding X_ℚ with πₙ(X_ℚ) ≅ πₙ(X) ⊗ ℚ; captures the rational homotopy type.

nodes.name: p-localization of a space
nodes.description: The localization of a nilpotent space X at the prime p, yielding X_(p) with πₙ(X_(p)) ≅ πₙ(X) ⊗ ℤ_(p); retains only p-primary torsion and rational information.

nodes.name: p-completion of a space
nodes.description: The Bousfield-Kan p-completion of a nilpotent space X, with πₙ(X_p^∧) ≅ πₙ(X) ⊗ ℤ_p^∧ for finitely generated πₙ(X); captures p-adic homotopy information.

nodes.name: Sullivan arithmetic square (fracture theorem)
nodes.description: A nilpotent space X of finite type is the homotopy pullback of its rationalization X_ℚ and profinite completion ∏_p X_p^∧ over their common rationalization, fracturing a global homotopy type into local pieces.

nodes.name: Formal space (rational homotopy theory)
nodes.description: A simply connected space X whose rational homotopy type is a formal consequence of its rational cohomology ring; compact Kähler manifolds are formal by Deligne-Griffiths-Morgan-Sullivan.

nodes.name: Hopf algebra structure on loop space homology
nodes.description: The homology H*(ΩX; k) carries a graded Hopf algebra structure with product from the Pontryagin product, coproduct from the diagonal, and antipode from loop inversion.

nodes.name: Cellular chain complex
nodes.description: For a CW complex X, the chain complex with Cₙ(X) = Hₙ(Xⁿ, Xⁿ⁻¹) ≅ ℤ^{number of n-cells} and boundary maps given by degrees of attaching maps; its homology equals singular homology.

nodes.name: Graph as 1-dimensional CW complex
nodes.description: A graph is a 1-dimensional CW complex with 0-cells as vertices and 1-cells as edges; every connected graph deformation-retracts onto a maximal spanning tree with free fundamental group.

nodes.name: Based versus free homotopy comparison
nodes.function_signature: (Pointed homotopy classes [X, Y]_*) → (Free homotopy classes [X, Y] via π₁(Y)-action quotient)
nodes.description: Relates pointed homotopy classes [X, Y]_* to free homotopy classes [X, Y] via the action of π₁(Y); the free classes are the orbit set of this action.

nodes.name: HELP lemma (homotopy extension and lifting property)
nodes.function_signature: (n-connected map e: Y → Z, CW pair (X, A) with dim ≤ n) → (Simultaneous extension and lift)
nodes.description: Combines HEP for cofibrations and HLP for fibrations to solve simultaneous extension-lifting problems for n-connected maps and low-dimensional CW pairs.

nodes.name: Zabrodsky mixing
nodes.function_signature: (p-local homotopy types {X_(p)}) → (Global space X with prescribed p-local types)
nodes.description: Constructs new homotopy types by assembling different p-localizations via the fracture theorem; produces exotic H-spaces and spaces with prescribed local behavior.

nodes.name: Computing H*(K(ℤ,n)) via Serre spectral sequence
nodes.function_signature: (Path-loop fibration K(ℤ,n) → PK(ℤ,n+1) → K(ℤ,n+1)) → (H*(K(ℤ,n); ℤ))
nodes.description: Uses the Serre spectral sequence of the path-loop fibration with contractible total space to inductively determine the cohomology of Eilenberg-MacLane spaces.

nodes.name: Boolean lattice B_n
nodes.description: The poset of all subsets of an n-element set ordered by inclusion, isomorphic to the product of n copies of the 2-element chain.

nodes.name: Partition lattice Pi_n
nodes.description: The lattice of all set partitions of {1,...,n} ordered by refinement, with Möbius function μ(0̂,1̂) = (-1)^{n-1}(n-1)!.

nodes.name: Young's lattice
nodes.description: The poset of all integer partitions ordered by inclusion of Young diagrams, forming a distributive lattice and a differential poset of rank 1.

nodes.name: Zeta function of a poset
nodes.description: The element ζ in the incidence algebra of a locally finite poset P defined by ζ(x,y) = 1 for all x ≤ y, whose inverse is the Möbius function μ.

nodes.name: Philip Hall's theorem (Möbius function)
nodes.description: For a finite poset P, μ(x,y) = ∑_{k≥0} (-1)^k c_k where c_k is the number of chains x = z_0 < z_1 < ··· < z_k = y of length k from x to y.

nodes.name: Crosscut theorem (Rota)
nodes.description: For a finite lattice L with crosscut C (an antichain meeting every maximal chain), μ(0̂,1̂) = ∑_{k≥0} (-1)^k N_k where N_k counts k-element subsets of C with join equal to 1̂.

nodes.name: Euler characteristic and Möbius function
nodes.description: For a finite poset P, μ_P(x,y) = χ̃(Δ(x,y)) where χ̃ is the reduced Euler characteristic of the order complex of the open interval (x,y).

nodes.name: Order complex Δ(P)
nodes.description: The simplicial complex whose k-simplices are the chains of length k in the poset P.

nodes.name: Order polynomial Ω(P, m)
nodes.description: The number of order-preserving maps σ: P → {1,...,m} from a finite poset P, which is a polynomial in m of degree |P|.

nodes.name: Strict order polynomial Ω̄(P, m)
nodes.description: The number of strictly order-preserving maps σ: P → {1,...,m}, which is a polynomial in m of degree |P|.

nodes.name: Reciprocity theorem for order polynomials (Stanley)
nodes.description: Ω̄(P, m) = (-1)^{|P|} Ω(P, -m), relating the strict and weak order polynomials of a poset P via evaluation at negative integers.

nodes.name: Exponential generating function
nodes.description: The formal power series EGF(a_n; x) = ∑_{n≥0} a_n x^n/n!, encoding sequences with labeled combinatorial interpretations.

nodes.name: Rational generating function
nodes.description: A generating function f(x) = P(x)/Q(x) with P, Q polynomials, equivalent to the sequence satisfying a linear recurrence with constant coefficients.

nodes.name: D-finite (holonomic) generating function
nodes.description: A formal power series satisfying a linear ODE with polynomial coefficients, equivalently whose coefficient sequence satisfies a polynomial recurrence (P-recursive).

nodes.name: Transfer matrix method
nodes.function_signature: (Directed graph G, weights) → (Rational generating function for weighted path counts)
nodes.description: Encodes walks in a directed graph via a matrix whose (i,j)-entry is the weight of edge i→j, yielding GF as entries of (I - xT)^{-1}.

nodes.name: Sieve methods (inclusion-exclusion)
nodes.function_signature: (Finite set S, properties P_1,...,P_n) → (Count of elements with none/some of the properties)
nodes.description: Counts elements avoiding specified properties by alternating over-/under-counting via subsets of conditions.

nodes.name: Principle of inclusion-exclusion
nodes.description: |A_1 ∪ ··· ∪ A_n| = ∑_i |A_i| - ∑_{i<j} |A_i ∩ A_j| + ··· + (-1)^{n-1}|A_1 ∩ ··· ∩ A_n|, expressing the union's cardinality as an alternating sum over intersections.

nodes.name: Composition of an integer
nodes.description: An ordered tuple (a_1,...,a_k) of positive integers with a_1 + ··· + a_k = n; the number of compositions of n is 2^{n-1}.

nodes.name: Descent of a permutation
nodes.description: A position i such that σ(i) > σ(i+1) in a permutation σ ∈ S_n; the descent set Des(σ) ⊆ {1,...,n-1} encodes the permutation's shape.

nodes.name: Descent number and major index
nodes.description: For σ ∈ S_n, des(σ) = |Des(σ)| and maj(σ) = ∑_{i ∈ Des(σ)} i; both are equidistributed with inv(σ) via the Carlitz q-Eulerian polynomial.

nodes.name: Inversion of a permutation
nodes.description: A pair (i,j) with i < j and σ(i) > σ(j); the inversion number inv(σ) equals the minimum number of adjacent transpositions to sort σ.

nodes.name: Eulerian polynomial A_n(t)
nodes.description: A_n(t) = ∑_{σ ∈ S_n} t^{des(σ)+1} = ∑_{k=1}^n A(n,k) t^k, satisfying ∑_{m≥0} m^n t^m = A_n(t)/(1-t)^{n+1}.

nodes.name: q-analog of n!
nodes.description: [n]_q! = [1]_q [2]_q ··· [n]_q = (1-q)(1-q^2)···(1-q^n)/(1-q)^n, the generating function for inversions: ∑_{σ ∈ S_n} q^{inv(σ)} = [n]_q!.

nodes.name: Exponential formula (combinatorics)
nodes.description: If C(x) = ∑ c_n x^n/n! is the EGF for connected structures, then exp(C(x)) is the EGF for structures decomposable into connected components.

nodes.name: Compositional formula (exponential)
nodes.description: If F(x) = ∑ f_n x^n/n! counts structures on [n] with components counted by G(x), then F(x) = exp(G(x)) or more generally F(x) = H(G(x)) for assembly operations H.

nodes.name: P-partition generating function
nodes.description: The formal power series F_P(x) = ∑_{σ: P-partition} x_1^{σ(1)} x_2^{σ(2)} ···, a quasisymmetric function encoding P-partitions of a labeled poset P.

nodes.name: Fundamental theorem of P-partitions (Stanley)
nodes.description: The generating function for P-partitions of a naturally labeled poset P decomposes as a sum over linear extensions: F_P(q) = ∑_{w ∈ L(P)} q^{maj(w)} / (1-q)(1-q^2)···(1-q^n).

nodes.name: Linear extension of a poset
nodes.description: A total order on the elements of P that is compatible with the partial order; the number e(P) of linear extensions is #P-hard to compute in general.

nodes.name: Rank function and graded poset
nodes.description: A poset with a rank function ρ: P → ℕ satisfying ρ(y) = ρ(x) + 1 whenever y covers x; equivalently, all maximal chains between two elements have the same length.

nodes.name: Rank generating function
nodes.description: For a graded poset P with rank function ρ, the polynomial F(P,q) = ∑_{x ∈ P} q^{ρ(x)} encoding the Whitney numbers of the second kind.

nodes.name: Characteristic polynomial of a lattice
nodes.description: For a finite graded lattice L, χ_L(t) = ∑_{x ∈ L} μ(0̂,x) t^{ρ(1̂)-ρ(x)}, generalizing the chromatic polynomial of a graph to geometric lattices.

nodes.name: Chromatic polynomial χ_G(k)
nodes.description: The polynomial giving the number of proper k-colorings of a graph G; satisfies the deletion-contraction recurrence χ_G = χ_{G-e} - χ_{G/e}.

nodes.name: Stirling numbers of the second kind S(n,k)
nodes.description: The number of partitions of an n-element set into exactly k nonempty blocks, satisfying S(n,k) = kS(n-1,k) + S(n-1,k-1) with x^n = ∑_k S(n,k) x(x-1)···(x-k+1).

nodes.name: Stirling numbers of the first kind c(n,k)
nodes.description: The unsigned number |s(n,k)| counting permutations of n elements with exactly k cycles, satisfying x(x+1)···(x+n-1) = ∑_k c(n,k) x^k.

nodes.name: Binomial poset
nodes.description: A locally finite graded poset with a unique minimal element in which every interval [x,y] of rank k has the same number B(k) of maximal chains.

nodes.name: Eulerian poset
nodes.description: A graded poset in which every nontrivial interval [x,y] satisfies μ(x,y) = (-1)^{ρ(y)-ρ(x)}, equivalently the h-vector of every interval is symmetric.

nodes.name: Differential poset
nodes.description: A graded poset satisfying DU - UD = rI for the up and down operators on its linear span, where r is a positive integer; Young's lattice is the unique r=1 example.

nodes.name: Monomial symmetric function m_λ
nodes.description: The sum of all distinct monomials x_1^{a_1} x_2^{a_2}··· obtainable by permuting the parts of the partition λ = (a_1,a_2,...); the {m_λ} form a Z-basis of Λ.

nodes.name: Homogeneous symmetric function h_k
nodes.description: h_k = ∑_{i_1 ≤ ··· ≤ i_k} x_{i_1}···x_{i_k} = m_{(1^k)} + ··· + m_{(k)}, algebraically independent generators of the ring of symmetric functions over Z.

nodes.name: Hall inner product
nodes.description: The bilinear form ⟨·,·⟩ on the ring of symmetric functions defined by ⟨s_λ, s_μ⟩ = δ_{λμ}, equivalently ⟨h_λ, m_μ⟩ = δ_{λμ}.

nodes.name: Knuth equivalence
nodes.description: The equivalence relation on words generated by xzy ~ zxy (for x ≤ y < z) and yxz ~ yzx (for x < y ≤ z); two permutations are Knuth-equivalent iff they have the same insertion tableau under RSK.

nodes.name: Jeu de taquin (Schützenberger)
nodes.function_signature: (Skew tableau of shape λ/μ) → (Standard or semistandard tableau of straight shape)
nodes.description: Slides entries into inner corners by a sequence of local moves, rectifying a skew tableau to a straight-shape tableau; defines Schützenberger's theory of slides and tableau equivalence.

nodes.name: Promotion and evacuation (Schützenberger)
nodes.function_signature: (Standard Young tableau of shape λ) → (Standard Young tableau of shape λ)
nodes.description: Promotion rotates the entries via jeu de taquin; evacuation applies promotion n times giving an involution whose fixed points count self-complementary tableaux.

nodes.name: Littlewood-Richardson tableau
nodes.description: A semistandard skew tableau of shape λ/μ whose reverse reading word is a lattice word (Yamanouchi word); the number of such tableaux of content ν is c^λ_{μν}.

nodes.name: Border strip (rim hook)
nodes.description: A connected skew shape containing no 2×2 square; its height ht(β) = (number of rows) - 1 determines the sign (-1)^{ht(β)} in the Murnaghan-Nakayama rule.

nodes.name: Dual Cauchy identity
nodes.description: ∏_{i,j}(1 + x_i y_j) = ∑_λ s_λ(x) s_{λ'}(y), where λ' is the conjugate partition, the companion identity to the Cauchy identity.

nodes.name: Omega involution ω
nodes.function_signature: (Symmetric function f) → (Symmetric function ω(f))
nodes.description: The ring involution on Λ defined by ω(e_k) = h_k, equivalently ω(s_λ) = s_{λ'}, interchanging elementary and homogeneous symmetric functions.

nodes.name: Skew Schur function s_{λ/μ}
nodes.description: Defined by ⟨s_{λ/μ}, s_ν⟩ = c^λ_{μν} (the LR coefficient), equivalently the generating function for semistandard tableaux of skew shape λ/μ.

nodes.name: Hall-Littlewood polynomial P_λ(x;t)
nodes.description: A one-parameter family of symmetric functions interpolating between Schur functions (t=0) and monomial symmetric functions (t=1), with connections to p-adic groups.

nodes.name: Macdonald polynomial P_λ(x;q,t)
nodes.description: A two-parameter family of symmetric functions that are joint eigenfunctions of Macdonald's q-difference operators, specializing to Hall-Littlewood (q=0), Jack (t=q^α, q→1), and Schur (q=t).

nodes.name: MacMahon's plane partition generating function
nodes.description: The generating function for all plane partitions is ∏_{k≥1} 1/(1-q^k)^k, proved by MacMahon using the theory of partitions.

nodes.name: Lattice path
nodes.description: A sequence of steps in ℤ^d from a fixed step-set, typically unit steps East and North in ℤ^2; lattice paths model binomial coefficients, Catalan numbers, and ballot problems.

nodes.name: Reflection principle (André)
nodes.function_signature: (Set of lattice paths crossing a barrier) → (Bijection with unrestricted paths from a reflected starting point)
nodes.description: Counts paths staying above a line by reflecting the initial segment at the first crossing, establishing a bijection with paths from a reflected origin.

nodes.name: Chromatic symmetric function X_G (Stanley)
nodes.description: X_G(x) = ∑_{κ proper} x_{κ(1)} x_{κ(2)}···x_{κ(n)}, a symmetric function generalizing the chromatic polynomial; conjectured to distinguish non-isomorphic trees.

nodes.name: Stanley symmetric function F_w
nodes.description: A symmetric function indexed by a permutation w ∈ S_n, defined as a sum over reduced decompositions of w; its Schur expansion gives the number of reduced words for the longest permutation.

nodes.name: Fundamental quasisymmetric function F_{n,S}
nodes.description: For S ⊆ {1,...,n-1}, F_{n,S} = ∑_{i_1 ≤ ··· ≤ i_n, i_j < i_{j+1} if j ∈ S} x_{i_1}···x_{i_n}; the {F_{n,S}} form a basis of the degree-n quasisymmetric functions.

nodes.name: Quasisymmetric function
nodes.description: A formal power series f(x_1,x_2,...) of bounded degree invariant under the operation x_{i_1}^{a_1}···x_{i_k}^{a_k} ↦ x_{j_1}^{a_1}···x_{j_k}^{a_k} whenever i_1<···<i_k and j_1<···<j_k; forms a Hopf algebra QSym containing Sym.

nodes.name: Gessel's formula for P-partitions
nodes.description: The P-partition generating function of a labeled poset P equals ∑_{w ∈ L(P)} F_{n,Des(w)}, expressing it as a sum of fundamental quasisymmetric functions over linear extensions.

nodes.name: Schur positivity
nodes.description: A symmetric function f is Schur-positive if all coefficients in its expansion f = ∑_λ c_λ s_λ satisfy c_λ ≥ 0, typically implying a representation-theoretic interpretation.

nodes.name: Hook content formula
nodes.description: The number of semistandard Young tableaux of shape λ with entries in {1,...,n} is s_λ(1^n) = ∏_{u ∈ λ} (n + c(u))/h(u) where c(u) is the content and h(u) the hook length.

nodes.name: Involution principle (Garsia-Milne)
nodes.function_signature: (Sign-reversing involution on a signed set) → (Bijective proof that |positive elements| - |negative elements| = |fixed points|)
nodes.description: Constructs bijective proofs of combinatorial identities by composing two sign-reversing involutions, with the non-cancelled terms providing the desired bijection.

nodes.name: Schensted's theorem
nodes.description: Under the RSK correspondence, the length of the longest increasing subsequence of a permutation σ equals the length of the first row of its insertion tableau P(σ).

nodes.name: Greene's theorem
nodes.description: For a permutation σ with RSK insertion tableau P(σ) of shape λ, the maximum length of a union of k increasing subsequences equals λ_1 + ··· + λ_k for all k.

nodes.name: Hillman-Grassl correspondence
nodes.function_signature: (Reverse plane partition of shape λ) → (Array of nonneg integers indexed by hooks of λ)
nodes.description: A weight-preserving bijection between reverse plane partitions and hook-indexed arrays, providing a combinatorial proof of the generating function for reverse plane partitions.

nodes.name: Stanley's hook content formula for column-strict plane partitions
nodes.description: The generating function for column-strict plane partitions of shape λ with entries ≤ n is ∏_{u ∈ λ} (1-q^{n+c(u)})/(1-q^{h(u)}).

nodes.name: Theory of combinatorial species (Joyal)
nodes.function_signature: (Species F: FinSet^{bij} → FinSet) → (Generating functions: EGF, type GF, cycle index)
nodes.description: Joyal's framework treating combinatorial structures as functors from finite sets with bijections, enabling systematic passage to generating functions and composition operations.

nodes.name: Gaussian elimination and q-counting
nodes.function_signature: (Subspace counting problem over F_q) → (q-analog formula)
nodes.description: Uses row reduction over finite fields to count subspaces, yielding q-binomial coefficients and q-analogs of combinatorial identities via the lattice of subspaces.

nodes.name: f-vector and h-vector of a simplicial complex
nodes.description: For a (d-1)-dimensional simplicial complex Δ, f_i = number of i-dimensional faces; the h-vector (h_0,...,h_d) is defined by ∑ h_i t^{d-i} = ∑ f_{i-1}(t-1)^{d-i} and satisfies the Dehn-Sommerville relations for Eulerian complexes.

nodes.name: Shellability
nodes.description: A pure simplicial complex is shellable if its maximal faces can be ordered F_1,...,F_t so that F_k ∩ (F_1 ∪ ··· ∪ F_{k-1}) is pure of codimension 1 for all k; implies the complex has the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres.

nodes.name: EL-shellability and CL-shellability
nodes.function_signature: (Edge labeling of Hasse diagram) → (Shelling order + Möbius function computation)
nodes.description: An edge labeling of a bounded poset's Hasse diagram is an EL-labeling if every interval has a unique increasing maximal chain which is lexicographically first; implies shellability of the order complex and computes μ by counting descending chains.

nodes.name: Polyhedral geometry of partitions
nodes.function_signature: (Partition/composition constraints) → (Ehrhart theory and lattice point enumeration)
nodes.description: Realizes partition-counting problems as lattice point enumeration in rational polytopes, connecting to Ehrhart polynomials, Barvinok's algorithm, and inside-out polytopes.

nodes.name: Multigraph
nodes.description: A graph allowing multiple edges between the same pair of vertices.

nodes.name: Subgraph
nodes.description: A graph H is a subgraph of G if V(H) ⊆ V(G) and E(H) ⊆ E(G).

nodes.name: Induced subgraph
nodes.description: The subgraph G[S] induced by S ⊆ V(G) contains all edges of G between vertices in S.

nodes.name: Spanning subgraph
nodes.description: A subgraph H of G with V(H) = V(G).

nodes.name: Path (graph theory)
nodes.description: A non-empty graph P with vertices x₀, …, xₖ and edges xᵢxᵢ₊₁, all vertices distinct.

nodes.name: Cycle (graph theory)
nodes.description: A closed path of length ≥ 3 with all vertices distinct except first and last.

nodes.name: Connected graph
nodes.description: A graph in which every two vertices are linked by a path.

nodes.name: Tree (graph theory)
nodes.description: A connected graph containing no cycle; equivalently, a connected graph on n vertices with exactly n−1 edges.

nodes.name: Forest
nodes.description: An acyclic graph; equivalently, a disjoint union of trees.

nodes.name: Spanning tree
nodes.description: A spanning subgraph that is a tree.

nodes.name: Vertex degree
nodes.description: The degree d(v) of a vertex v is the number of edges incident with v.

nodes.name: Minimum degree δ(G)
nodes.description: The minimum vertex degree δ(G) = min{d(v) : v ∈ V(G)}.

nodes.name: Euler tour
nodes.description: A closed walk in a graph that traverses every edge exactly once.

nodes.name: Euler's theorem on Euler tours
nodes.description: A connected graph has an Euler tour if and only if every vertex has even degree.

nodes.name: Bipartite characterization
nodes.description: A graph is bipartite if and only if it contains no odd cycle.

nodes.name: Handshaking lemma
nodes.description: The sum of all vertex degrees equals twice the number of edges: Σ d(v) = 2|E|.

nodes.name: Complement graph
nodes.description: The complement Ḡ has edge set consisting of all pairs not in E(G).

nodes.name: Complete graph K_n
nodes.description: The graph on n vertices where every pair of distinct vertices is joined by an edge.

nodes.name: Complete bipartite graph K_{r,s}
nodes.description: The bipartite graph with parts of sizes r and s where every cross-pair is adjacent.

nodes.name: Edge contraction
nodes.description: The operation of contracting edge e = xy, identifying x and y and removing loops.

nodes.name: Graph minor
nodes.description: H is a minor of G if H can be obtained from a subgraph of G by contracting edges.

nodes.name: Topological minor (subdivision)
nodes.description: H is a topological minor of G if G contains a subdivision of H (edges replaced by internally disjoint paths).

nodes.name: Vertex cover
nodes.description: A set of vertices S such that every edge has at least one endpoint in S.

nodes.name: Independent set
nodes.description: A set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices in a graph.

nodes.name: Edge cover
nodes.description: A set of edges F such that every vertex is incident to at least one edge in F.

nodes.name: Gallai's identities
nodes.description: For a graph without isolated vertices: α(G) + β(G) = |V(G)| and α'(G) + β'(G) = |V(G)|.

nodes.name: Hall's marriage theorem
nodes.description: A bipartite graph G = (A ∪ B, E) has a matching saturating A iff |N(S)| ≥ |S| for every S ⊆ A.

nodes.name: König's theorem (matching-cover duality)
nodes.description: In a bipartite graph, the maximum matching size equals the minimum vertex cover size.

nodes.name: Tutte's 1-factor theorem
nodes.description: G has a perfect matching iff for every S ⊆ V(G), the number of odd components of G − S is at most |S|.

nodes.name: Deficiency version of Hall's theorem
nodes.description: The maximum matching in bipartite G = (A ∪ B, E) has size |A| − max_{S ⊆ A}(|S| − |N(S)|).

nodes.name: Berge's theorem (maximum matching)
nodes.description: A matching M is maximum if and only if G contains no M-augmenting path.

nodes.name: k-connected graph
nodes.description: G is k-connected if |V(G)| > k and G − S is connected for every S with |S| < k.

nodes.name: Vertex connectivity κ(G)
nodes.description: The maximum k such that G is k-connected.

nodes.name: Edge connectivity λ(G)
nodes.description: The minimum number of edges whose removal disconnects G.

nodes.name: Whitney's inequality
nodes.description: For every graph G: κ(G) ≤ λ(G) ≤ δ(G).

nodes.name: Menger's theorem
nodes.description: The maximum number of internally vertex-disjoint s–t paths equals the minimum s–t separating set size.

nodes.name: Menger's theorem (edge version)
nodes.description: The maximum number of edge-disjoint s–t paths equals the minimum edge cut size separating s from t.

nodes.name: Menger's theorem (global version)
nodes.description: G is k-connected iff every pair of vertices can be joined by k internally vertex-disjoint paths.

nodes.name: Block (2-connected component)
nodes.description: A maximal 2-connected subgraph, or a bridge with its endpoints.

nodes.name: Block-cut tree
nodes.description: The tree whose vertices are blocks and cut-vertices, with edges joining each cut vertex to its blocks.

nodes.name: Ear decomposition
nodes.description: A sequence of paths (ears) decomposing a 2-connected graph, each ear sharing only its endpoints with earlier structure.

nodes.name: Ear decomposition theorem (Whitney)
nodes.description: A graph is 2-connected if and only if it has an ear decomposition starting from a cycle.

nodes.name: Tutte's wheel theorem
nodes.description: Every 3-connected graph can be obtained from a wheel by edge additions and vertex splits.

nodes.name: Ear decomposition technique
nodes.description: Constructing 2-connected graphs by adding ears to prove structural results.

nodes.name: Face of a plane graph
nodes.description: A connected region of ℝ² \ G in a plane embedding, including the unbounded outer face.

nodes.name: Euler's formula for planar graphs
nodes.description: For a connected plane graph: |V| − |E| + |F| = 2.

nodes.name: Planar graph edge bound
nodes.description: Every planar graph on n ≥ 3 vertices has at most 3n − 6 edges; if triangle-free, at most 2n − 4.

nodes.name: Non-planarity of K₅ and K₃,₃
nodes.description: Neither K₅ nor K₃,₃ is planar, as verified by the edge bound from Euler's formula.

nodes.name: Kuratowski's theorem
nodes.description: A graph is planar iff it contains no subdivision of K₅ or K₃,₃.

nodes.name: Wagner's theorem
nodes.description: A graph is planar iff it has no K₅ or K₃,₃ minor.

nodes.name: Dual graph (planar)
nodes.description: The graph G* whose vertices are faces of G, with edges for shared boundaries.

nodes.name: Mac Lane's planarity criterion
nodes.description: A graph is planar iff its cycle space has a basis where every edge belongs to at most two basis cycles.

nodes.name: Six-color theorem for planar graphs
nodes.description: Every planar graph is 6-colorable, corollary of the edge bound δ(G) ≤ 5.

nodes.name: Kempe chain argument
nodes.description: Recoloring along a maximal bichromatic path to free a color at a vertex.

nodes.name: Outerplanar graph
nodes.description: A planar graph admitting an embedding with all vertices on the outer face.

nodes.name: Genus of a graph
nodes.description: The minimum genus of a surface in which the graph can be embedded without crossings.

nodes.name: Proper vertex coloring
nodes.description: An assignment of colors to vertices such that no two adjacent vertices share the same color.

nodes.name: Chromatic number χ(G)
nodes.description: The minimum number of colors needed for a proper vertex coloring of G.

nodes.name: Clique number ω(G)
nodes.description: The maximum size of a complete subgraph in G.

nodes.name: Brooks' theorem
nodes.description: Every connected graph with Δ(G) ≥ 3 satisfies χ(G) ≤ Δ(G), unless G is complete or an odd cycle.

nodes.name: Greedy coloring bound
nodes.description: The greedy algorithm with any vertex ordering produces a proper coloring using at most Δ(G) + 1 colors.

nodes.name: Chromatic polynomial P(G, k)
nodes.description: The polynomial P(G, k) counting proper k-colorings of G.

nodes.name: Proper edge coloring
nodes.description: An assignment of colors to edges so that no two edges sharing an endpoint share a color.

nodes.name: Chromatic index χ'(G)
nodes.description: The minimum number of colors needed for a proper edge coloring.

nodes.name: Vizing's theorem
nodes.description: For every simple graph: Δ(G) ≤ χ'(G) ≤ Δ(G) + 1.

nodes.name: List coloring
nodes.description: A proper coloring where each vertex must receive a color from its prescribed list.

nodes.name: Choosability (list chromatic number)
nodes.description: The minimum k such that G is L-colorable for every list assignment with |L(v)| ≥ k.

nodes.name: Perfect graph theorem (Lovász)
nodes.description: A graph is perfect iff its complement is perfect.

nodes.name: Strong perfect graph theorem (Chudnovsky–Robertson–Seymour–Thomas)
nodes.description: A graph is perfect iff neither it nor its complement contains an induced odd cycle of length ≥ 5.

nodes.name: Mycielski construction
nodes.description: A construction producing triangle-free graphs with arbitrarily large chromatic number.

nodes.name: Deletion-contraction
nodes.description: Computing graph invariants recursively via P(G,k) = P(G−e,k) − P(G/e,k).

nodes.name: Degeneracy (k-degenerate graph)
nodes.description: A graph is k-degenerate if every subgraph has a vertex of degree at most k.

nodes.name: Nowhere-zero flow
nodes.description: An assignment of non-zero group elements to edges satisfying Kirchhoff's law at every vertex.

nodes.name: Nowhere-zero k-flow
nodes.description: A ℤ-flow with all values in {±1, …, ±(k−1)} satisfying flow conservation.

nodes.name: Flow-coloring duality (planar graphs)
nodes.description: A planar graph has a proper k-coloring iff its dual has a nowhere-zero k-flow.

nodes.name: Tutte's flow conjectures
nodes.description: Every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 5-flow (5-flow conjecture); without Petersen minor a 4-flow.

nodes.name: Six-flow theorem (Seymour)
nodes.description: Every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 6-flow.

nodes.name: Eight-flow theorem (Jaeger)
nodes.description: Every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 8-flow.

nodes.name: Four-color theorem via flows
nodes.description: The four-color theorem is equivalent to every bridgeless planar graph having a nowhere-zero 4-flow.

nodes.name: Group-valued flow
nodes.description: A flow with edge values in a finite abelian group Γ satisfying flow conservation.

nodes.name: Tutte's theorem on group-valued flows
nodes.description: Existence of a nowhere-zero Γ-flow depends only on |Γ|, not on the group structure.

nodes.name: Turán's theorem
nodes.description: The max edges in a K_{r+1}-free n-vertex graph is (1 − 1/r)n²/2, achieved uniquely by T(n,r).

nodes.name: Turán graph T(n,r)
nodes.description: The complete r-partite graph on n vertices with parts as equal as possible.

nodes.name: Extremal number ex(n, H)
nodes.description: The max edges in an n-vertex graph containing no subgraph isomorphic to H.

nodes.name: Szemerédi regularity lemma
nodes.description: For every ε > 0 there exists M such that V(G) can be partitioned into ≤ M classes with all but εk² pairs ε-regular.

nodes.name: ε-regular pair
nodes.description: A pair (A, B) is ε-regular if for all large subsets the edge density deviates by less than ε from d(A,B).

nodes.name: Graph removal lemma
nodes.description: For H and ε > 0 there exists δ > 0 so that an n-vertex graph with < δn^{v(H)} copies of H can be made H-free by removing ≤ εn² edges.

nodes.name: Ramsey's theorem (finite, graph version)
nodes.description: For all r, s there exists n such that every 2-coloring of E(K_n) has a red K_r or blue K_s.

nodes.name: Ramsey number R(r, s)
nodes.description: The minimum n for which every 2-coloring of E(K_n) contains monochromatic K_r or K_s.

nodes.name: Erdős probabilistic lower bound for Ramsey numbers
nodes.description: R(k, k) ≥ 2^{k/2} by the probabilistic method.

nodes.name: Zarankiewicz problem
nodes.description: Determining the max 1s in a 0-1 matrix of given size with no all-1 submatrix of specified dimensions.

nodes.name: Regularity method
nodes.description: Three-step method: apply regularity lemma, clean up, find structure in reduced graph.

nodes.name: Double counting (combinatorics)
nodes.description: Counting the same quantity two ways to establish an identity or inequality.

nodes.name: Probabilistic method (graph theory)
nodes.description: Proving existence by showing a random construction has positive probability of satisfying the desired property.

nodes.name: König's infinity lemma
nodes.description: Every infinite finitely-branching rooted tree contains an infinite path.

nodes.name: Ray (one-way infinite path)
nodes.description: A one-way infinite path x₀x₁x₂… in a graph.

nodes.name: End of a graph
nodes.description: An equivalence class of rays, where two rays are equivalent if no finite vertex set separates them.

nodes.name: Locally finite graph
nodes.description: A graph in which every vertex has finite degree.

nodes.name: Halin's theorem (grid minor from thick ends)
nodes.description: A graph has a thick end iff it contains a subdivision of the hexagonal half-grid.

nodes.name: Star-comb lemma
nodes.description: For infinite U in connected G, G contains either a comb with teeth in U or a subdivided star with leaves in U.

nodes.name: De Bruijn–Erdős compactness theorem for coloring
nodes.description: An infinite graph is k-colorable iff every finite subgraph is k-colorable.

nodes.name: Infinite Ramsey theorem
nodes.description: For every finite coloring of r-element subsets of an infinite set, there exists an infinite monochromatic subset.

nodes.name: Canonical Ramsey theorem (Erdős–Rado)
nodes.description: For every coloring of pairs of ℕ, there exists an infinite set on which the coloring is canonical.

nodes.name: Graph Ramsey number R(G, H)
nodes.description: The minimum n such that every 2-coloring of E(K_n) contains red G or blue H.

nodes.name: Ramsey multiplicity
nodes.description: The minimum number of monochromatic copies of H in any 2-coloring of E(K_n).

nodes.name: Hamilton cycle
nodes.description: A cycle visiting every vertex exactly once.

nodes.name: Hamilton path
nodes.description: A path visiting every vertex exactly once.

nodes.name: Dirac's theorem (Hamilton cycles)
nodes.description: Every graph on n ≥ 3 vertices with δ(G) ≥ n/2 contains a Hamilton cycle.

nodes.name: Chvátal's theorem (degree sequence condition)
nodes.description: G on n vertices with degree sequence d₁ ≤ … ≤ dₙ is Hamiltonian if for all i < n/2: dᵢ ≤ i implies d_{n−i} ≥ n − i.

nodes.name: Chvátal–Erdős theorem
nodes.description: If κ(G) ≥ α(G) for G with |V| ≥ 3, then G is Hamiltonian.

nodes.name: Tutte's theorem (4-connected planar graphs are Hamiltonian)
nodes.description: Every 4-connected planar graph has a Hamilton cycle.

nodes.name: Toughness of a graph
nodes.description: t(G) = min |S|/c(G−S) over all cutsets S, where c counts components.

nodes.name: Chvátal's toughness conjecture
nodes.description: There exists t₀ such that every t₀-tough graph is Hamiltonian.

nodes.name: Bondy–Chvátal closure theorem
nodes.description: G is Hamiltonian iff its closure cl(G) is Hamiltonian, where cl(G) adds edges between non-adjacent vertices with degree sum ≥ n.

nodes.name: Erdős–Rényi random graph model G(n, p)
nodes.description: The random graph on n vertices where each edge is included independently with probability p.

nodes.name: Threshold function
nodes.description: A function p*(n) such that P[G(n,p) has Q] → 0 if p/p* → 0, and → 1 if p/p* → ∞.

nodes.name: Connectivity threshold for G(n, p)
nodes.description: The threshold for G(n, p) to be connected a.a.s. is p = (log n)/n.

nodes.name: Giant component threshold (Erdős–Rényi)
nodes.description: In G(n, c/n): if c < 1 all components are O(log n); if c > 1 there is a unique giant component of Θ(n) vertices.

nodes.name: Evolution of random graphs
nodes.description: As p increases in G(n,p), the graph undergoes phase transitions: trees → unicyclic → giant component → connected → Hamiltonian.

nodes.name: Zero-one law for random graphs
nodes.description: For constant p ∈ (0,1), every first-order graph property has probability tending to 0 or 1 in G(n, p).

nodes.name: Chromatic number of random graphs
nodes.description: χ(G(n, 1/2)) = Θ(n/log n) almost surely.

nodes.name: Hamilton cycle threshold
nodes.description: The threshold for G(n, p) to contain a Hamilton cycle a.a.s. is p = (log n + log log n)/n.

nodes.name: First moment method (Markov bound)
nodes.description: Proving P[X ≥ 1] ≤ E[X] for non-negative X, to show a property a.a.s. does not hold.

nodes.name: Second moment method (Chebyshev)
nodes.description: Proving P[X > 0] ≥ (E[X])²/E[X²] to show a property a.a.s. does hold.

nodes.name: Tree-width
nodes.description: The minimum width of a tree-decomposition of G, where width is max bag size minus one.

nodes.name: Tree-decomposition
nodes.description: A pair (T, {Bₜ}) covering all vertices and edges, with bags of any vertex inducing a connected subtree of T.

nodes.name: Bramble (screen)
nodes.description: A family of pairwise touching connected subgraphs; its order is the minimum hitting set size.

nodes.name: Tree-width duality theorem (Seymour–Thomas)
nodes.description: The tree-width of G equals the maximum bramble order minus one.

nodes.name: Robertson–Seymour theorem (graph minor theorem)
nodes.description: The minor relation on finite graphs is a well-quasi-ordering.

nodes.name: Finite forbidden minor characterization
nodes.description: Every minor-closed class has a finite set of excluded minors (corollary of Robertson–Seymour).

nodes.name: Well-quasi-ordering (WQO)
nodes.description: A quasi-order with no infinite antichains and no infinite strictly descending sequences.

nodes.name: Graph structure theorem (Robertson–Seymour)
nodes.description: Graphs with no H-minor can be built by clique-sums from graphs almost-embeddable in surfaces excluding H.

nodes.name: Grid minor theorem (Robertson–Seymour)
nodes.description: For every k there exists f(k) such that every graph of tree-width ≥ f(k) contains a k × k grid minor.

nodes.name: Excluded minor characterization of planar graphs
nodes.description: Planar graphs are exactly those with no K₅ minor and no K₃,₃ minor.

nodes.name: Path-width
nodes.description: The minimum width of a path-decomposition (tree-decomposition where the tree is a path).

nodes.name: Clique-sum
nodes.description: Gluing two graphs along a common clique and possibly deleting some clique edges.

nodes.name: Haven
nodes.description: A strategy for a robber to escape fewer than k cops; equivalent to tree-width ≥ k.

nodes.name: Cops and robbers characterization of tree-width
nodes.description: tw(G) + 1 equals the minimum number of cops needed to catch a robber on G.

nodes.name: Well-quasi-ordering technique
nodes.description: Using WQO theory (Higman's lemma, Kruskal's theorem) to prove finiteness of obstruction sets.

nodes.name: Graph minor testing algorithm
nodes.description: Robertson–Seymour's O(n³) algorithm for testing whether a fixed H is a minor of input G.

nodes.name: Petersen graph
nodes.description: The 3-regular graph on 10 vertices; a fundamental counterexample in graph theory.

nodes.name: Line graph
nodes.description: L(G) has edges of G as vertices, adjacent when the edges share an endpoint.

nodes.name: Tutte polynomial T(G; x, y)
nodes.description: A bivariate polynomial encoding extensive combinatorial information, generalizing chromatic and flow polynomials.

nodes.name: Girth of a graph
nodes.description: The length of the shortest cycle; ∞ if acyclic.

nodes.name: Erdős theorem on girth and chromatic number
nodes.description: For all g, k there exists a graph with girth > g and chromatic number > k.

nodes.name: Kirchhoff's matrix tree theorem
nodes.description: The number of spanning trees equals any cofactor of the Laplacian matrix.

nodes.name: Kruskal's tree theorem
nodes.description: Finite rooted trees are WQO by the homeomorphic embedding relation.

nodes.name: Higman's lemma
nodes.description: If (Q, ≤) is a WQO, then finite sequences over Q are WQO under subsequence embedding.

nodes.name: Gallai–Milgram theorem
nodes.description: The minimum directed path cover size of a digraph equals the maximum independent set in the underlying graph.

nodes.name: Alon–Tarsi theorem
nodes.description: G is L-colorable from lists of size k if the numbers of even and odd Eulerian subgraphs differ.

nodes.name: Hadwiger's conjecture
nodes.description: Every graph with χ(G) ≥ k has a K_k minor.

nodes.name: Augmenting path method
nodes.description: Finding alternating paths between exposed vertices to increase matching size by one.

nodes.name: Discharging method
nodes.description: Assigning charges via Euler's formula and redistributing by local rules to derive contradictions.

nodes.name: Extremal counting (Zykov symmetrization)
nodes.description: Showing the extremal graph is complete multipartite via successive vertex identification.

nodes.name: Network flow
nodes.description: An assignment of flow values to directed edges satisfying conservation at internal vertices.

nodes.name: Max-flow min-cut theorem (Ford–Fulkerson)
nodes.description: In a network, the max flow value equals the min s–t cut capacity.

nodes.name: Mader's theorem (average degree forces topological minors)
nodes.description: For every H there exists c(H) such that average degree ≥ c(H) forces a topological minor of H.

nodes.name: Cycle space
nodes.description: The GF(2)-vector space generated by edge sets of cycles; dimension |E| − |V| + c(G).

nodes.name: Cut space
nodes.description: The GF(2)-vector space generated by minimal edge cuts; orthogonal complement of cycle space.

nodes.name: Tree-decomposition dynamic programming
nodes.description: Solving NP-hard problems in polynomial time on bounded tree-width graphs via DP along tree-decomposition.

nodes.name: Graph products (Cartesian, tensor, strong)
nodes.description: Three standard products defining adjacency in V(G) × V(H) differently.

nodes.name: Heawood's map coloring theorem
nodes.description: The chromatic number of graphs on a surface of genus g ≥ 1 is at most ⌊(7 + √(1+48g))/2⌋.

nodes.name: Degree of a vertex
nodes.description: The degree d(v) of a vertex v in a graph G is the number of edges incident to v.

nodes.name: Walk (graph theory)
nodes.description: A walk in a graph is a sequence of vertices v₀, v₁, …, vₖ where each consecutive pair is joined by an edge.

nodes.name: Trail (graph theory)
nodes.description: A trail is a walk in which all edges are distinct.

nodes.name: Prüfer sequence
nodes.description: A unique sequence of n−2 integers from {1,…,n} encoding a labeled tree on n vertices, establishing a bijection used to prove Cayley's formula.

nodes.name: König's edge-coloring theorem
nodes.description: For every bipartite graph G, the chromatic index equals the maximum degree: χ'(G) = Δ(G).

nodes.name: Clique
nodes.description: A clique in a graph G is a set of pairwise adjacent vertices, equivalently a subset inducing a complete subgraph.

nodes.name: Electrical network on a graph
nodes.description: A graph with positive real conductances (or resistances) assigned to each edge, modeling an electrical resistor network.

nodes.name: Kirchhoff's current law (graph)
nodes.description: At every non-terminal vertex of an electrical network, the sum of currents flowing in equals the sum flowing out.

nodes.name: Kirchhoff's voltage law (graph)
nodes.description: Around every cycle in an electrical network, the sum of the voltage drops (current times resistance) is zero.

nodes.name: Effective resistance
nodes.description: The effective resistance R_eff(a,b) between vertices a and b is the voltage difference needed to drive a unit current from a to b.

nodes.name: Rayleigh's monotonicity law
nodes.description: Increasing any edge resistance in a network does not decrease the effective resistance between any two nodes.

nodes.name: Series-parallel reduction
nodes.function_signature: (ElectricalNetwork) → (SimplifiedNetwork)
nodes.description: Simplifying a resistor network by replacing series resistors with their sum and parallel resistors with their harmonic mean.

nodes.name: Random walk on a graph
nodes.description: A stochastic process on the vertices of a graph where at each step the walker moves to a uniformly random neighbour of the current vertex.

nodes.name: Hitting time
nodes.description: The expected number of steps for a random walk starting at vertex u to first reach vertex v.

nodes.name: Commute time
nodes.description: The expected number of steps for a random walk to travel from u to v and back, equal to 2|E| · R_eff(u,v) by the commute-time identity.

nodes.name: Random walk–electrical network correspondence
nodes.description: Voltages in an electrical network on a graph equal hitting probabilities of the corresponding random walk, and commute times equal 2|E| times effective resistances.

nodes.name: Nash-Williams recurrence criterion
nodes.description: A connected locally finite graph has a recurrent random walk if and only if there exist disjoint finite cutsets with divergent sum of reciprocal capacities.

nodes.name: Ford–Fulkerson algorithm
nodes.function_signature: (Network, s, t) → MaxFlow
nodes.description: Iteratively finding augmenting s–t paths in the residual graph and pushing flow along them until no augmenting path remains.

nodes.name: f-factor
nodes.description: For a function f: V(G) → ℤ≥₀, an f-factor is a spanning subgraph H with d_H(v) = f(v) for every vertex v.

nodes.name: Tutte's f-factor theorem
nodes.description: A graph G has an f-factor if and only if for every disjoint pair S, T ⊆ V, the Tutte deficiency condition q(S,T) ≤ Σ_{v∈S} f(v) holds.

nodes.name: Erdős–Szekeres bound on Ramsey numbers
nodes.description: R(s,t) ≤ C(s+t−2, s−1), establishing that the Ramsey number R(s,t) is at most the central binomial coefficient.

nodes.name: Thomassen's theorem (5-list-coloring of planar graphs)
nodes.description: Every planar graph is 5-choosable, that is, it admits a proper coloring from any assignment of lists of size 5 to vertices.

nodes.name: Voigt's example (non-4-choosable planar graph)
nodes.description: A planar graph constructed by Voigt (1993) that is not 4-choosable, showing that the list chromatic number of planar graphs can exceed 4.

nodes.name: Chordal graph
nodes.description: A graph in which every cycle of length four or more has a chord; equivalently, a graph with a perfect elimination ordering.

nodes.name: Shannon's multigraph edge-coloring bound
nodes.description: For any multigraph G, the chromatic index satisfies χ'(G) ≤ ⌊3Δ(G)/2⌋.

nodes.name: Vizing's adjacency lemma
nodes.description: If G is a simple graph with χ'(G) = Δ(G) + 1, then every vertex of maximum degree is adjacent to at least two other vertices of maximum degree.

nodes.name: Class 1 and Class 2 graphs
nodes.description: A simple graph is Class 1 if χ'(G) = Δ(G) and Class 2 if χ'(G) = Δ(G) + 1, the only possibilities by Vizing's theorem.

nodes.name: Vizing fan argument
nodes.function_signature: (SimpleGraph, Edge) → ProperEdgeColoring
nodes.description: Constructing a fan of edges at a vertex and recoloring along Kempe-type paths to extend a partial edge coloring, proving Vizing's theorem.

nodes.name: Ramsey's theorem (multicolor version)
nodes.description: For any positive integers r, k₁, …, kᵣ, there exists N such that every r-coloring of the edges of K_N contains a monochromatic K_{kᵢ} in color i for some i.

nodes.name: Diagonal Ramsey number bounds
nodes.description: The diagonal Ramsey number satisfies √2^k ≤ R(k,k) ≤ 4^k, with the lower bound from Erdős's probabilistic argument and the upper from the Erdős–Szekeres recurrence.

nodes.name: Off-diagonal Ramsey bounds
nodes.description: For fixed s ≥ 3, the Ramsey number R(s,t) satisfies c₁ t^{(s+1)/2-1}/(log t)^{...} ≤ R(s,t) ≤ c₂ t^{s-1}/log^{s-2} t as t → ∞.

nodes.name: Schur number S(r)
nodes.description: The largest integer n such that {1,…,n} can be r-colored with no monochromatic solution to x + y = z.

nodes.name: Combinatorial line
nodes.description: A set of k points in [k]^n obtained by fixing some coordinates and letting the remaining coordinates run through all of {1,…,k} in unison.

nodes.name: Erdős–Rado stepping-up lemma
nodes.description: A recursive tool converting Ramsey-type bounds for r-uniform hypergraphs to bounds for (r+1)-uniform hypergraphs, yielding tower-type lower bounds for hypergraph Ramsey numbers.

nodes.name: Compactness principle for Ramsey theory
nodes.description: The finite Ramsey theorem follows from the infinite version by a compactness (König's infinity lemma) argument: if no finite bound existed, an infinite counterexample could be constructed.

nodes.name: Uniform random graph model G(n, M)
nodes.description: The random graph chosen uniformly at random from all graphs on n labeled vertices with exactly M edges.

nodes.name: Subgraph appearance threshold
nodes.description: The threshold for the appearance of a fixed subgraph H in G(n,p) is p*(n) = n^{−1/ρ(H)} where ρ(H) = max_{J⊆H} |E(J)|/|V(J)| is the maximum density.

nodes.name: Double jump in random graph evolution
nodes.description: The phase transition near p = 1/n in G(n,p) where the largest component jumps from O(log n) to Θ(n^{2/3}) at p = 1/n and then to Θ(n) for p > 1/n.

nodes.name: Clique number of random graphs
nodes.description: Almost surely, ω(G(n,1/2)) = (2 + o(1)) log₂ n, concentrating on at most two consecutive values.

nodes.name: Janson's inequality
nodes.description: For a family of events determined by independent random variables, the probability that none occur is at most exp(−μ + Δ/2), where μ is the sum of probabilities and Δ accounts for pairwise dependencies.

nodes.name: Automorphism group of a graph
nodes.description: The group Aut(G) of all adjacency-preserving permutations of V(G), capturing the symmetries of the graph.

nodes.name: Vertex-transitive graph
nodes.description: A graph G such that for every pair of vertices u, v there exists an automorphism mapping u to v.

nodes.name: Frucht's theorem
nodes.description: Every finite group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of some finite simple graph.

nodes.name: Adjacency matrix of a graph
nodes.description: The n×n matrix A with A_{ij} = 1 if vertices i and j are adjacent and 0 otherwise.

nodes.name: Spectrum of a graph
nodes.description: The multiset of eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix A(G), providing algebraic invariants of the graph.

nodes.name: Spectral radius of a graph
nodes.description: The largest eigenvalue λ₁ of the adjacency matrix of G, satisfying d_avg ≤ λ₁ ≤ Δ(G) with equality iff G is regular.

nodes.name: Algebraic connectivity (Fiedler value)
nodes.description: The second-smallest eigenvalue λ₂ of the Laplacian matrix L(G), positive if and only if G is connected.

nodes.name: Expander graph
nodes.description: A sparse graph with strong connectivity properties: every subset S with |S| ≤ |V|/2 has neighbourhood |N(S)| ≥ c|S| for a constant c > 0.

nodes.name: Spectral gap of a graph
nodes.description: The difference d − λ₂ between the degree d and the second-largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix; a large spectral gap implies good expansion.

nodes.name: Expander mixing lemma
nodes.description: For a d-regular graph with second eigenvalue λ, and any vertex sets S, T: |e(S,T) − d|S||T|/n| ≤ λ√(|S||T|).

nodes.name: Discrete Cheeger inequality
nodes.description: For a d-regular graph, (d − λ₂)/2 ≤ h(G) ≤ √(2d(d − λ₂)), relating the Cheeger constant h(G) to the spectral gap.

nodes.name: Cheeger constant of a graph
nodes.description: h(G) = min_{S: 0<|S|≤|V|/2} |∂S|/|S|, the minimum edge-boundary-to-volume ratio over all small vertex subsets.

nodes.name: Ramanujan graph
nodes.description: A connected d-regular graph whose nontrivial adjacency eigenvalues all satisfy |λ| ≤ 2√(d−1), achieving the Alon–Boppana bound.

nodes.name: Alon–Boppana bound
nodes.description: For any d-regular graph on n vertices, the second-largest eigenvalue satisfies λ₂ ≥ 2√(d−1) − o(1) as n → ∞.

nodes.name: Lubotzky–Phillips–Sarnak (LPS) construction
nodes.description: An explicit construction of (p+1)-regular Ramanujan graphs using quaternion algebras and the Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture for GL₂.

nodes.name: Strongly regular graph srg(n, k, λ, μ)
nodes.description: A regular graph on n vertices of degree k where every adjacent pair has λ common neighbours and every non-adjacent pair has μ common neighbours.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue interlacing
nodes.description: If H is an induced subgraph of G on m vertices, the eigenvalues of A(H) interlace those of A(G): λᵢ(G) ≥ λᵢ(H) ≥ λ_{n−m+i}(G).

nodes.name: Cover time of a graph
nodes.description: The expected time for a random walk to visit every vertex of the graph, starting from the worst-case vertex.

nodes.name: Blanket time
nodes.description: The expected time until a random walk has visited every vertex at least a fraction of the stationary-measure times, within a constant factor of the cover time by a theorem of Kahn–Kim–Lovász.

nodes.name: Mixing time of a Markov chain
nodes.description: The minimum time t_mix(ε) until the total variation distance between the distribution at time t and the stationary distribution is at most ε for all initial states.

nodes.name: Total variation distance (Markov chains)
nodes.description: d_TV(μ, ν) = (1/2)Σ_x |μ(x) − ν(x)| = max_A |μ(A) − ν(A)|, measuring the distance between a chain's distribution and stationarity.

nodes.name: Cutoff phenomenon
nodes.description: A family of Markov chains exhibits cutoff if the total variation distance drops abruptly from near 1 to near 0 over a window of o(t_mix) steps around the mixing time.

nodes.name: Rapid mixing
nodes.description: A Markov chain mixes rapidly if its mixing time is polynomial in the natural size parameter, often established via spectral gap, coupling, or canonical paths.

nodes.name: Whitney rank polynomial (rank-nullity generating function)
nodes.description: R(G; x,y) = Σ_{A⊆E} x^{r(E)−r(A)} y^{|A|−r(A)}, encoding the rank and nullity of each edge subset; related to the Tutte polynomial by T(G;x,y) = R(G;x−1,y−1).

nodes.name: Flow polynomial
nodes.description: The polynomial F(G; k) counting the number of nowhere-zero k-flows on G, obtained from the Tutte polynomial as F(G;k) = (−1)^{|E|−|V|+c} T(G; 0, 1−k).

nodes.name: Reliability polynomial
nodes.description: The probability R(G; p) that a graph remains connected when each edge fails independently with probability 1−p, expressible via the Tutte polynomial.

nodes.name: Cographic matroid
nodes.description: The matroid M*(G) on the edges of G whose circuits are the minimal edge cuts (bonds) of G, dual to the graphic matroid M(G).

nodes.name: Matroid minor
nodes.description: A matroid obtained from M by a sequence of deletions M\e and contractions M/e of elements, generalizing graph minors to matroids.

nodes.name: Potts model
nodes.description: A statistical mechanical model on a graph G with q spin states per vertex and interaction energy β, whose partition function Z_Potts(G; q, β) is an evaluation of the Tutte polynomial.

nodes.name: Computational complexity of the Tutte polynomial
nodes.description: Evaluating the Tutte polynomial T(G; x, y) is #P-hard for all (x,y) except along the hyperbola (x−1)(y−1) = 1 and at finitely many special points, by a result of Jaeger–Vertigan–Welsh.

nodes.name: Partition function of a graph (statistical mechanics)
nodes.description: Z(G) = Σ_{A⊆E} w(A), a weighted sum over spanning subgraphs whose specializations yield the chromatic, flow, and reliability polynomials via the Tutte polynomial.

nodes.name: Dichromatic polynomial (Whitney)
nodes.description: Whitney's two-variable polynomial Q(G; q, v) = Σ_{A⊆E} q^{k(A)} v^{|A|}, the precursor of the Tutte polynomial encoding the number of components and edges of each spanning subgraph.

nodes.name: Uniform random coloring
nodes.function_signature: (Combinatorial structure, Palette of c colors) -> (Expected bad-event count, Existence of good coloring)
nodes.description: Color each element independently and uniformly at random from a palette, then compute expected bad events to prove existence of a good coloring.

nodes.name: Property B existence for uniform hypergraphs
nodes.description: Every n-uniform hypergraph with fewer than 2^{n-1} edges is 2-colorable (has Property B).

nodes.name: Max-cut probabilistic lower bound
nodes.description: Every graph on m edges has a bipartite subgraph (cut) with at least m/2 edges.

nodes.name: Sum-free subset probabilistic bound
nodes.description: Every set of n nonzero integers contains a sum-free subset of size greater than n/3.

nodes.name: Property B of a hypergraph
nodes.description: A hypergraph has Property B if its vertex set can be 2-colored so that no edge is monochromatic.

nodes.name: Linearity of expectation technique
nodes.function_signature: (Random variable as sum of indicators) -> (E[X] = sum E[X_i], Existence bound via first moment)
nodes.description: Decompose a random variable as a sum of indicator random variables, compute E[X] = sum E[X_i] without requiring independence, then apply the first moment method.

nodes.name: Tournament dominating set bound
nodes.description: Every tournament on n players has a dominating set of size at most ceil(log_2 n) + 1.

nodes.name: Balancing vectors bound
nodes.description: Given n vectors v_1,...,v_n in R^n with ||v_i||_2 <= 1, there exist signs epsilon_i in {+1,-1} with ||sum epsilon_i v_i||_infinity <= sqrt(2 ln(2n)).

nodes.name: Unbalancing lights
nodes.description: For any n x n matrix A with entries in {+1,-1}, there exist epsilon in {+/-1}^n with ||A epsilon||_infinity >= sqrt(n * 2/pi).

nodes.name: Independence number greedy-expectation bound
nodes.description: For any graph G, alpha(G) >= sum_{v in V} 1/(d(v)+1) where d(v) is the degree of vertex v.

nodes.name: Crossing number inequality
nodes.description: For any graph with m >= 4n edges, the crossing number satisfies cr(G) >= m^3/(64n^2).

nodes.name: Ramsey lower bound via alteration
nodes.description: R(k,k) >= (1+o(1))(k/(e*sqrt(2))) * 2^{k/2}, improving the basic probabilistic bound by alteration.

nodes.name: Shearer's bound for triangle-free graphs
nodes.description: Every triangle-free d-regular graph on n vertices satisfies alpha(G) >= Omega(sqrt(n log n / d)).

nodes.name: Independent transversal via alteration
nodes.description: If each partition class has size >= 2*Delta(G), then an independent transversal exists.

nodes.name: Paley-Zygmund inequality
nodes.description: For a nonnegative random variable X, Pr[X > 0] >= (E[X])^2 / E[X^2].

nodes.name: Paley graph properties
nodes.description: The Paley graph P(q) on F_q has no clique or independent set of size exceeding (1+o(1)) log_2 q.

nodes.name: Variance
nodes.description: Var[X] = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2, measuring the expected squared deviation of X from its mean.

nodes.name: Lovasz Local Lemma technique
nodes.function_signature: (Bad events {A_i}, Dependency graph G) -> (Pr[cap A_i^c] > 0, Existence of object avoiding all bad events)
nodes.description: Define bad events, construct a dependency graph, verify the LLL condition ep(d+1) <= 1 (symmetric) or x_i weights (general), then conclude all bad events can be simultaneously avoided.

nodes.name: Lovasz Local Lemma (symmetric form)
nodes.description: If each event A_i has Pr[A_i] <= p and is dependent on at most d others, and ep(d+1) <= 1, then Pr[intersection of all A_i^c] > 0.

nodes.name: Lopsided Lovasz Local Lemma
nodes.description: The LLL holds under the weaker condition of a lopsidependency graph, where Pr[A_i | intersection of A_j^c for j in S] <= Pr[A_i] for non-neighbors S.

nodes.name: Moser-Tardos algorithmic LLL
nodes.description: The Moser-Tardos resampling algorithm finds a satisfying assignment in expected O(sum x_i/(1-x_i)) steps under the LLL conditions.

nodes.name: k-SAT LLL bound
nodes.description: A k-CNF formula in which each clause shares variables with at most 2^k/e - 1 other clauses is satisfiable.

nodes.name: Latin transversal via LLL
nodes.description: An n x n array where each symbol appears at most n/(4e) times has a Latin transversal.

nodes.name: Lopsidependency graph
nodes.description: A graph on events where Pr[A_i | intersection of A_j^c for j in S] <= Pr[A_i] for every set S of non-neighbors of i.

nodes.name: FKG inequality
nodes.description: On a finite distributive lattice with a log-supermodular measure mu, for increasing functions f and g: E[fg] >= E[f]E[g].

nodes.name: Four functions theorem (Ahlswede-Daykin)
nodes.description: If alpha, beta, gamma, delta are nonneg functions on a finite lattice with alpha(a)beta(b) <= gamma(a v b)delta(a ^ b) for all a,b, then (sum alpha)(sum beta) <= (sum gamma)(sum delta).

nodes.name: Reimer inequality (BK inequality)
nodes.description: For events A, B on {0,1}^n, Pr[A box B] <= Pr[A]*Pr[B], where A box B denotes disjoint occurrence. Proved by Reimer, resolving the van den Berg-Kesten conjecture.

nodes.name: Increasing event
nodes.description: An event A in {0,1}^n such that omega in A and omega <= omega' coordinatewise implies omega' in A.

nodes.name: Disjoint occurrence (box product)
nodes.description: A box B is the event that disjoint witness sets of coordinates certify A and B simultaneously.

nodes.name: Azuma-Hoeffding technique
nodes.function_signature: (Function f, Sequential exposure of variables) -> (Doob martingale, Bounded differences, Exponential tail bound)
nodes.description: Construct a Doob martingale by sequential exposure, verify bounded-difference conditions, then apply Azuma-Hoeffding to obtain exponential concentration.

nodes.name: Vertex exposure martingale
nodes.function_signature: (Graph parameter f, G(n,p)) -> (Doob martingale via vertex-by-vertex exposure, Concentration bound)
nodes.description: Expose vertices of G(n,p) one by one; the resulting Doob martingale gives concentration for Lipschitz graph parameters.

nodes.name: Edge exposure martingale
nodes.function_signature: (Graph parameter f, G(n,p)) -> (Doob martingale via edge-by-edge exposure, Tighter concentration bound)
nodes.description: Expose potential edges of G(n,p) one by one; yields tighter concentration than vertex exposure when the parameter is edge-Lipschitz.

nodes.name: Chromatic number concentration
nodes.description: The chromatic number chi(G(n,1/2)) is concentrated in an interval of width O(sqrt(n)).

nodes.name: Kim-Vu polynomial concentration
nodes.description: Tight concentration bounds for multilinear polynomials of independent {0,1} random variables.

nodes.name: Doob martingale (combinatorial)
nodes.description: M_i = E[f | F_i] defines a martingale by sequential exposure of random variables; the fundamental tool for applying martingale concentration in combinatorics.

nodes.name: Lipschitz function on product space
nodes.description: A function f on a product space is c-Lipschitz if changing any single coordinate changes f by at most c.

nodes.name: Stein-Chen Poisson approximation
nodes.function_signature: (Sum of weakly dependent indicators) -> (Poisson approximation, Explicit TV distance bound)
nodes.description: Approximate the distribution of a sum of weakly dependent indicator random variables by a Poisson distribution, with explicit total-variation bounds.

nodes.name: Triangle threshold in G(n,p)
nodes.description: The threshold for triangles in G(n,p) is p = n^{-1}; when p = c/n the number of triangles converges in distribution to Poisson(c^3/6).

nodes.name: Bonferroni inequalities
nodes.description: Truncated inclusion-exclusion sums yield alternating upper and lower bounds for Pr[union of A_i].

nodes.name: Expander mixing technique
nodes.function_signature: ((n,d,lambda)-graph, Vertex subsets S,T) -> (Edge count approximation, Pseudo-random bound)
nodes.description: Use the spectral gap of a regular graph to show that edge distribution between vertex subsets approximates that of a random graph.

nodes.name: Paley graph pseudo-randomness
nodes.description: The Paley graph is an (n, (n-1)/2, O(sqrt(n)))-graph, exhibiting strong pseudo-random properties.

nodes.name: (n,d,lambda)-graph
nodes.description: A d-regular graph on n vertices whose second-largest eigenvalue (in absolute value) of the adjacency matrix is at most lambda.

nodes.name: Erdos-Renyi G(n,m) model
nodes.description: A uniform random graph on n labelled vertices with exactly m edges.

nodes.name: Katona's cyclic permutation proof of EKR
nodes.description: Katona's elegant proof of the Erdos-Ko-Rado theorem using counting over cyclic permutations and arcs.

nodes.name: Lovasz theta sandwich theorem
nodes.description: For any graph G, alpha(G) <= theta(G) <= chi_bar(G), sandwiching the Lovasz theta function between the independence number and the fractional chromatic number.

nodes.name: Shannon capacity of C_5
nodes.description: The Shannon capacity of the 5-cycle is Theta(C_5) = sqrt(5), determined by Lovasz via the theta function.

nodes.name: Ramsey bound via Lovasz theta function
nodes.description: R(3,k) >= Omega(k^2/log^2 k), obtained using the Lovasz theta function.

nodes.name: Shannon capacity of a graph
nodes.description: Theta(G) = lim_{n->inf} (alpha(G^{box n}))^{1/n}, the zero-error capacity of a noisy channel with confusability graph G.

nodes.name: Lovasz theta function
nodes.description: An SDP-computable graph parameter theta(G) satisfying alpha(G) <= theta(G) <= chi_bar(G).

nodes.name: Partial coloring method
nodes.function_signature: (Set system, Pigeonhole/entropy argument) -> (Partial coloring with low discrepancy, Iteration to full coloring)
nodes.description: Find a partial coloring of low discrepancy by pigeonhole or entropy arguments, then iterate to color all elements.

nodes.name: Beck-Fiala technique
nodes.function_signature: (Set system with bounded degree t) -> (Coloring with discrepancy <= 2t-2)
nodes.description: Fix colors of elements appearing in few active sets by a dimension/linear algebra argument, iterating until all elements are colored.

nodes.name: Partial coloring lemma
nodes.description: There exists a coloring with at least n/2 nonzero entries and discrepancy O(sqrt(n)) for any n sets on n elements.

nodes.name: Discrepancy of arithmetic progressions
nodes.description: The discrepancy of the set system of arithmetic progressions in [n] is Theta(n^{1/4}).

nodes.name: Combinatorial discrepancy
nodes.description: disc(S) = min_{chi: X -> {-1,+1}} max_{S in S} |sum_{x in S} chi(x)|, the minimum worst-case imbalance over all 2-colorings.

nodes.name: Method of conditional expectations
nodes.function_signature: (Probabilistic existence argument with E[X]) -> (Deterministic sequential construction achieving E[X] bound)
nodes.description: Sequentially set each random variable to the value that keeps the conditional expectation favorable, derandomizing a probabilistic proof.

nodes.name: Pairwise independence derandomization
nodes.function_signature: (Probabilistic argument using only 1st/2nd moments) -> (Deterministic construction with O(log n) random bits)
nodes.description: Replace full independence with pairwise independence, preserving first and second moment arguments while reducing randomness.

nodes.name: k-wise independence derandomization
nodes.function_signature: (Probabilistic argument using k-th moments) -> (Deterministic construction with O(k log n) bits)
nodes.description: Use k-wise independent random variables constructible from O(k log n) random bits to derandomize arguments depending on k-th moments.

nodes.name: Derandomized Ramsey lower bound
nodes.description: Constructive proof that R(k,k) >= 2^{k/2} via the method of conditional expectations.

nodes.name: Deterministic max-cut algorithm
nodes.description: A polynomial-time greedy algorithm produces a cut with at least m/2 edges, derandomizing the probabilistic max-cut bound.

nodes.name: k-wise independent random variables
nodes.description: A collection of random variables where every subset of size at most k is mutually independent.

nodes.name: Pairwise independent random variables
nodes.description: Random variables satisfying E[X_i X_j] = E[X_i]E[X_j] for all i != j, i.e., 2-wise independence.

nodes.name: Graph property testing
nodes.function_signature: (Graph property, Error parameter epsilon) -> (Constant-query randomized test)
nodes.description: Test a graph property by querying a random constant-size induced subgraph and checking the property on it.

nodes.name: Testability of hereditary graph properties
nodes.description: Every hereditary graph property is testable with a constant number of queries (depending only on epsilon).

nodes.name: Triangle removal lemma
nodes.description: A graph with at most delta*n^3 triangles can be made triangle-free by removing at most epsilon*n^2 edges.

nodes.name: Ruzsa-Szemeredi (6,3)-theorem
nodes.description: A graph on n vertices in which every edge belongs to exactly one triangle has o(n^2) edges.

nodes.name: Chernoff bound technique
nodes.function_signature: (Sum of independent RVs, Tail parameter t) -> (Exponential tail bound via MGF optimization)
nodes.description: Bound tail probabilities by optimizing the exponential moment E[exp(lambda X)] over lambda (exponential tilting / Cramér method).

nodes.name: Janson inequality technique
nodes.function_signature: (Dependent indicators {I_A}, Pairwise dependency measure Delta) -> (Lower tail bound Pr[X=0])
nodes.description: Control pairwise correlations among dependent indicators to obtain lower tail bounds, bounding Pr[X=0] <= exp(-mu + Delta/2).

nodes.name: Janson extended inequality
nodes.description: Pr[X=0] <= exp(-mu^2/(2 Delta)) when the dependency measure Delta >= mu, giving a stronger bound in the high-dependency regime.

nodes.name: Subgraph count concentration
nodes.description: The number of copies of a fixed subgraph H in G(n,p) is concentrated around its expectation.

nodes.name: Weierstrass product inequality
nodes.description: For x_i in [0,1]: prod_{i}(1 - x_i) >= 1 - sum_{i} x_i, a basic inequality used in probabilistic lower bounds.

nodes.name: Entropy method in combinatorics
nodes.function_signature: (Combinatorial counting problem) -> (Counting bound via subadditivity, chain rule, max-entropy principle)
nodes.description: Use subadditivity of Shannon entropy, the chain rule, and the maximum entropy principle to derive combinatorial counting and discrepancy bounds.

nodes.name: Shearer's entropy lemma
nodes.description: If each coordinate is covered at least t times by sets A_1,...,A_m, then t*H(X) <= sum_{i} H(X_{A_i}).

nodes.name: Bregman's theorem (permanent bound)
nodes.description: For a 0-1 matrix A with row sums r_1,...,r_n, the permanent satisfies perm(A) <= prod_{i} (r_i!)^{1/r_i}.

nodes.name: Kahn-Zhao theorem on independent sets
nodes.description: The number of independent sets in a d-regular bipartite graph on 2n vertices is at most (2^{d+1} - 1)^{n/d}, with equality for a disjoint union of K_{d,d}.

nodes.name: Shearer's independent set bound via entropy
nodes.description: Entropy-based bound on the number of independent sets in a graph, strengthening the naive 2^n bound using local structure.

nodes.name: Hypergraph container method
nodes.function_signature: (r-uniform hypergraph H) -> (Small collection of containers, Each independent set in some container)
nodes.description: Construct a small collection of 'containers' (almost-independent vertex sets) such that every independent set of the hypergraph is contained in some container.

nodes.name: Saxton-Thomason container theorem
nodes.description: For uniform hypergraphs satisfying codegree conditions, there exists a small family of containers for independent sets with controlled supersaturation.

nodes.name: Balogh-Morris-Samotij container theorem
nodes.description: An independent container theorem for hypergraphs using a supersaturation approach, yielding strong bounds on the number of independent sets.

nodes.name: Sum-free subsets count via containers
nodes.description: The number of sum-free subsets of [n] is 2^{n/2 + o(n)}, proved using the container method.

nodes.name: Triangle-free graph count via containers
nodes.description: The number of triangle-free graphs on n labelled vertices is 2^{n^2/4 + o(n^2)}, proved using the container method.

nodes.name: Sparse regularity method
nodes.function_signature: (Sparse graph with density p, Epsilon parameter) -> (Sparse epsilon-regular partition, Counting/embedding results)
nodes.description: Adapt Szemeredi's regularity lemma to sparse graphs with edge density p, obtaining meaningful partitions and counting lemmas relative to p.

nodes.name: Kohayakawa-Rodl sparse regularity lemma
nodes.description: Every graph satisfying an upper-uniformity condition admits an epsilon-regular partition relative to its density, extending Szemeredi regularity to sparse graphs.

nodes.name: Sparse counting lemma
nodes.description: A counting lemma for sparse epsilon-regular graphs: the number of copies of a fixed graph in a sparse regular setup matches the expected count up to a small error.

nodes.name: Rodl-Rucinski sparse Ramsey theorem
nodes.description: For any graph H and integer r, there exists a threshold p_0(n) such that for p >> p_0, every r-coloring of edges of G(n,p) a.a.s. contains a monochromatic copy of H.

nodes.name: Shamir-Spencer chromatic concentration
nodes.description: For constant p in (0,1), the chromatic number chi(G(n,p)) is concentrated on an interval of length about sqrt(n).

nodes.name: Off-diagonal Ramsey bound via LLL
nodes.description: R(3,k) >= Omega(k^2/log k) obtained via the Lovasz Local Lemma and Property B arguments.

nodes.name: Chromatic number lower bound via theta
nodes.description: chi(G) >= n/theta(G), giving a lower bound on the chromatic number using the Lovasz theta function of the complement.

nodes.name: 2-density of a graph
