nodes.description: m_2(H) = max_{J subseteq H, v(J) >= 3} (e(J)-1)/(v(J)-2), the maximum 2-density over subgraphs, governing thresholds for balanced subgraph appearance.

nodes.name: Upper uniformity condition
nodes.description: A no-dense-spots condition requiring that no subgraph is significantly denser than the ambient density p, needed for sparse regularity to be meaningful.

nodes.name: k-uniform set system (k-graph)
nodes.description: A family F ⊆ ([n] choose k) where every member has exactly k elements; the combinatorial analogue of a k-uniform hypergraph.

nodes.name: Chain in a poset
nodes.description: A totally ordered subset of a partially ordered set; in 2^[n], a sequence ∅ ⊂ A₁ ⊂ A₂ ⊂ ··· ⊂ [n].

nodes.name: Shattering
nodes.description: A set system F shatters S ⊆ X if the trace F|_S = {A ∩ S : A ∈ F} equals 2^S, realizing all 2^|S| subsets.

nodes.name: Trace of a set system
nodes.description: For F ⊆ 2^X and S ⊆ X, the trace F|_S = {A ∩ S : A ∈ F}, the projection of F onto the coordinate set S.

nodes.name: Covering number (τ)
nodes.description: The minimum size of a set T ⊆ X such that T ∩ A ≠ ∅ for all A ∈ F; the transversal number of the hypergraph.

nodes.name: Packing number (matching number)
nodes.description: The maximum number of pairwise disjoint sets in a family F; the matching number ν(F) of the hypergraph.

nodes.name: Epsilon-net
nodes.description: For a set system (X, F) and probability measure μ on X, a subset N ⊆ X is an ε-net if N ∩ A ≠ ∅ for every A ∈ F with μ(A) ≥ ε.

nodes.name: Boolean function
nodes.description: A function f: {0,1}^n → {0,1}; the fundamental object of study in combinatorial complexity and analysis of Boolean functions.

nodes.name: Sensitivity of a Boolean function
nodes.description: The sensitivity s(f) = max_x |{i : f(x) ≠ f(x ⊕ eᵢ)}|, the maximum number of sensitive coordinates over all inputs.

nodes.name: Block sensitivity
nodes.description: bs(f) = max_x max over disjoint blocks B₁,...,Bₖ with f(x) ≠ f(x ⊕ Bⱼ) for all j; always satisfies bs(f) ≥ s(f).

nodes.name: Certificate complexity
nodes.description: C(f,x) = min{|S| : S ⊆ [n], for all y with y|_S = x|_S we have f(y) = f(x)}, the minimum bits certifying the output on input x.

nodes.name: Decision tree complexity
nodes.description: D(f) = minimum depth of a decision tree computing f; the worst-case number of variable queries needed to evaluate f.

nodes.name: Influence of a variable
nodes.description: Inf_i(f) = Pr[f(x) ≠ f(x ⊕ eᵢ)] where x is uniform on {0,1}^n; the probability that the i-th variable is pivotal.

nodes.name: Total influence
nodes.description: I(f) = ∑ᵢ Inf_i(f), the sum of all variable influences; equals the average sensitivity and the edge-boundary measure on the Boolean cube.

nodes.name: Error-correcting code
nodes.description: A subset C ⊆ F_q^n with minimum Hamming distance d(C) = min{d(x,y) : x ≠ y ∈ C}; an [n,k,d]-code if |C| = q^k.

nodes.name: Partition regularity
nodes.description: A system of equations Ax = 0 is partition regular if for every finite coloring of ℕ there exists a monochromatic solution; characterized by Rado's theorem.

nodes.name: Noise sensitivity
nodes.description: A Boolean function f is noise sensitive if Corr(f(x), f(x_ε)) → 0 as n → ∞ where x_ε flips each bit of x independently with probability ε.

nodes.name: Monotone Boolean function
nodes.description: A Boolean function f with f(x) ≤ f(y) whenever x ≤ y componentwise; computable by a circuit with only AND and OR gates.

nodes.name: Turán density π(F)
nodes.description: For a forbidden k-uniform hypergraph F, π(F) = lim_{n→∞} ex_k(n,F)/(n choose k), the asymptotic extremal density.

nodes.name: Extremal number for set systems
nodes.description: The maximum |G| over k-uniform families G on [n] containing no copy of the forbidden configuration F; the hypergraph Turán number ex_k(n,F).

nodes.name: Hypergraph Ramsey number
nodes.description: R_k(s,t) = min N such that every 2-coloring of ([N] choose k) contains a monochromatic s-set or t-set; grows as a tower of height k−1.

nodes.name: Van der Waerden number W(k,r)
nodes.description: The minimum N such that every r-coloring of [N] contains a monochromatic k-term arithmetic progression.

nodes.name: Hales-Jewett number HJ(k,r)
nodes.description: The minimum n such that every r-coloring of [k]^n contains a monochromatic combinatorial line.

nodes.name: Dual set system
nodes.description: For F ⊆ 2^[n], the dual F* has ground set F and sets {A ∈ F : i ∈ A} for each i ∈ [n]; transposes the incidence matrix.

nodes.name: Growth function (shatter function)
nodes.description: π_F(m) = max_{|S|=m} |F|_S|, the maximum trace size on m-element sets; bounded by Φ_d(m) = ∑_{i≤d} (m choose i) when VC-dim(F) = d.

nodes.name: Nisan-Wigderson design
nodes.description: A combinatorial design yielding pseudorandom generators: a family of sets with bounded pairwise intersections used for hardness-based derandomization.

nodes.name: Symmetric chain decomposition of 2^[n]
nodes.description: A partition of the Boolean lattice 2^[n] into (n choose ⌊n/2⌋) symmetric chains, each a maximal chain symmetric about level n/2.

nodes.name: Normalized matching property
nodes.description: A graded poset satisfies the normalized matching property if for consecutive levels, the ratio of up-degree to level size is non-increasing; implies the LYM inequality.

nodes.name: Turán problem for forbidden traces
nodes.description: The problem of bounding the maximum size of F ⊆ 2^[n] whose trace on every m-set avoids a forbidden configuration; connects VC dimension to forbidden subconfigurations.

nodes.name: Hilton-Milner theorem
nodes.description: If n ≥ 2k and F ⊆ ([n] choose k) is intersecting but not a principal family, then |F| ≤ (n-1 choose k-1) − (n-k-1 choose k-1) + 1.

nodes.name: Frankl's theorem on t-intersecting families
nodes.description: For n sufficiently large relative to k and t, if F ⊆ ([n] choose k) is t-intersecting, then |F| ≤ (n-t choose k-t).

nodes.name: Lovász continuous Kruskal-Katona theorem
nodes.description: If |F| = (x choose k) for real x ≥ k, then |∂F| ≥ (x choose k−1); a continuous extension of the Kruskal-Katona shadow bound.

nodes.name: Ramsey's theorem (hypergraph version)
nodes.description: For all k, r, s there exists N such that every r-coloring of ([N] choose k) contains a monochromatic s-element set; numbers grow as towers of height k.

nodes.name: Rado's theorem (partition regularity)
nodes.description: A system Ax = 0 is partition regular over ℕ if and only if the columns of A satisfy the columns condition, a nested divisibility condition on column sums.

nodes.name: Pajor's lemma
nodes.description: For a down-closed family F ⊆ 2^[n], the number of subsets shattered by F equals |F|; relates the trace structure to family size.

nodes.name: Haussler packing lemma
nodes.description: For a set system of VC dimension d, the maximum number of ε-separated sets (packing number) is O((1/ε)^d).

nodes.name: Epsilon-net theorem (Haussler-Welzl)
nodes.description: For a set system of VC dimension d and any probability measure, there exists an ε-net of size O((d/ε) log(1/ε)).

nodes.name: Fractional Helly theorem
nodes.description: If among all (d+1)-tuples of n convex sets in ℝ^d at least α-fraction intersect, then some point lies in at least β(α,d)·n of the sets.

nodes.name: Colorful Helly theorem (Bárány)
nodes.description: Given d+1 families of convex sets in ℝ^d each with nonempty common intersection, if every colorful (d+1)-tuple intersects, then one family has a common point.

nodes.name: (p,q)-theorem (Alon-Kleitman)
nodes.description: For p ≥ q ≥ d+1, there exists c(p,q,d) such that if among every p convex sets in ℝ^d some q intersect, then c points pierce all sets.

nodes.name: Ray-Chaudhuri-Wilson theorem
nodes.description: If F ⊆ 2^[n] and |A ∩ B| takes at most s distinct values for A ≠ B ∈ F, then |F| ≤ (n choose s).

nodes.name: Oddtown theorem
nodes.description: If F ⊆ 2^[n] with |A| odd for all A ∈ F and |A ∩ B| even for all distinct A, B ∈ F, then |F| ≤ n.

nodes.name: Two-distance sets theorem
nodes.description: The maximum number of points in ℝ^d with only two distinct pairwise distances is at most (d+2 choose 2).

nodes.name: Combinatorial Nullstellensatz (Alon)
nodes.description: If f ∈ F[x₁,...,xₙ] has degree ∑tᵢ and the coefficient of ∏xᵢ^{tᵢ} is nonzero, then for sets Sᵢ with |Sᵢ| > tᵢ there exists a ∈ ∏Sᵢ with f(a) ≠ 0.

nodes.name: Johnson bound
nodes.description: An upper bound on code size refining the Hamming bound by bounding the list-decodability radius as a function of code parameters.

nodes.name: KKL theorem (Kahn-Kalai-Linial)
nodes.description: For any Boolean function f with Pr[f=1] = p ∈ (0,1), there exists a variable i with Inf_i(f) ≥ Ω(p(1−p) log n / n).

nodes.name: Friedgut's theorem on sharp thresholds
nodes.description: A monotone Boolean function with bounded total influence and transitive symmetry exhibits a sharp threshold: transition from Pr[f=1] ≈ 0 to ≈ 1 in an interval of width O(1/log n).

nodes.name: Bollobás two-families theorem (generalized)
nodes.description: If (Aᵢ,Bᵢ) are set pairs with |Aᵢ|=aᵢ, |Bᵢ|=bᵢ, and Aᵢ ∩ Bⱼ = ∅ iff i=j, then ∑ 1/(aᵢ+bᵢ choose aᵢ) ≤ 1.

nodes.name: Katona's intersection theorem
nodes.description: For an intersecting family F ⊆ 2^[n] (not necessarily uniform), |F| ≤ 2^{n−1}; the non-uniform generalization of Erdős-Ko-Rado.

nodes.name: Bondy's theorem on traces
nodes.description: If |F| > Φ_{d−1}(n) = ∑_{i<d} (n choose i) then F shatters some d-element set; a converse to the Sauer-Shelah lemma.

nodes.name: Alon-Babai-Suzuki theorem
nodes.description: If F ⊆ ([n] choose k) with k ≡ 0 mod p and |Aᵢ ∩ Aⱼ| mod p ∈ L for i ≠ j where 0 ∉ L and |L| = s, then |F| ≤ (n choose s).

nodes.name: Elias-Bassalygo bound
nodes.description: An upper bound on code rate: R ≤ 1 − H_q(J_q(δ)) where J_q is the Johnson radius, improving the Hamming bound for certain distance ranges.

nodes.name: Threshold phenomenon for monotone properties
nodes.description: Every monotone increasing graph property has a threshold p_c such that Pr_{G(n,p)}[property holds] transitions sharply from 0 to 1 as p crosses p_c.

nodes.name: Improved sunflower lemma (Alweiss-Lovett-Wu-Zhang)
nodes.description: A family of more than (C·log s)^s sets of size s contains a sunflower with 3 petals, exponentially improving the Erdős-Ko (p−1)^s·s! bound.

nodes.name: Compression / shifting
nodes.function_signature: (Set family F, ordering on ground set) → (Left-compressed family F' with |F'|=|F| and extremal properties preserved)
nodes.description: Replacing A by (A\{j})∪{i} for i<j when the result is absent; pushes families toward extremal configurations while preserving size and intersection properties.

nodes.name: Sunflower extraction (greedy peeling)
nodes.function_signature: (Family F of bounded-size sets) → (Sunflower with prescribed petal count)
nodes.description: Iteratively selecting and removing sets to extract a sunflower; the greedy argument underlying the sunflower lemma proof.

nodes.name: Dimension argument (linear algebra bound)
nodes.function_signature: (Family of combinatorial objects) → (Upper bound via vector space dimension)
nodes.description: Associating vectors to combinatorial objects and bounding family size by the dimension of the ambient vector space; if vectors are independent in F^n, the family has ≤ n elements.

nodes.name: Cascading representation
nodes.function_signature: (Integer m, parameter k) → (Unique binomial representation m = (a_k choose k) + (a_{k−1} choose k−1) + ···)
nodes.description: Decomposing integers via binomial coefficients in the cascading (falling factorial) representation; used to state and prove the Kruskal-Katona theorem.

nodes.name: Weight function method
nodes.function_signature: (Antichain or family F) → (Bound on |F| via weight sum ≤ 1)
nodes.description: Assigning weights to sets (e.g., 1/(n choose |A|) in LYM) and showing the total weight is at most 1 to derive bounds on family size.

nodes.name: Product / tensor argument
nodes.function_signature: (Combinatorial structure, dimension parameter n) → (Pattern forced in high-dimensional product)
nodes.description: Taking Cartesian products or tensor powers of structures to force patterns; used in Hales-Jewett and density arguments where product structure guarantees substructures.

nodes.name: Stepping-up technique
nodes.function_signature: (k-uniform Ramsey lower bound) → ((k+1)-uniform Ramsey lower bound via tower growth)
nodes.description: A recursive construction lifting Ramsey lower bounds from k-uniform to (k+1)-uniform hypergraphs by encoding colorings via orderings; produces tower-type growth.

nodes.name: Derandomization via conditional expectations
nodes.function_signature: (Probabilistic existence proof) → (Deterministic construction)
nodes.description: Converting a probabilistic existence proof into a deterministic construction by iteratively fixing random choices to maintain or improve the expected value.

nodes.name: Fourier analysis on the Boolean cube
nodes.function_signature: (Boolean function f: {0,1}^n → ℝ) → (Fourier expansion f = ∑_S f̂(S)χ_S with spectral analysis)
nodes.description: Expanding functions on {0,1}^n in the Walsh-Fourier basis to analyze influence, noise sensitivity, and threshold phenomena via spectral properties.

nodes.name: Chain partition technique
nodes.function_signature: (Poset P) → (Partition into chains witnessing Dilworth's theorem)
nodes.description: Constructing chain decompositions of posets via matching, flow, or greedy algorithms; the constructive dual of antichain bounds.

nodes.name: Multilinear polynomial representation
nodes.function_signature: (Set system F ⊆ 2^[n]) → (Multilinear polynomials encoding membership)
nodes.description: Representing sets as multilinear polynomials over a field and using polynomial degree/independence to bound family size; key to the linear algebra method.

nodes.name: Algebraic rank argument
nodes.function_signature: (Family of sets with intersection constraints) → (Rank bound on incidence matrix)
nodes.description: Constructing a matrix whose rows correspond to sets, showing full rank to bound family size; proves Oddtown, Fisher's inequality, and Frankl-Wilson.

nodes.name: Turán-type extremal method
nodes.function_signature: (Forbidden substructure F, host structure on n elements) → (Maximum size of F-free family)
nodes.description: Determining the maximum size of a structure avoiding a forbidden substructure by analyzing the extremal configuration; generalizes from graphs to hypergraphs and set systems.

nodes.name: Amalgamation technique
nodes.function_signature: (Collection of certified local structures) → (Global structure with combined properties)
nodes.description: Combining Ramsey-type and density-type arguments by gluing smaller certified pieces while maintaining global properties.

nodes.name: Inclusion-exclusion as counting technique
nodes.function_signature: (Overlapping sets A₁,...,Aₙ) → (|A₁ ∪ ··· ∪ Aₙ| via alternating signed intersection sums)
nodes.description: Computing union sizes via alternating sums of intersection sizes; used in sieve methods, derangement counting, and chromatic polynomial computations.

nodes.name: Difference set A−B
nodes.description: A−B = {a−b : a ∈ A, b ∈ B}; the set of all pairwise differences between elements of A and B in an abelian group.

nodes.name: Iterated sumset kA
nodes.description: kA = A + A + ⋯ + A (k copies), the k-fold sumset; distinct from the dilation k·A = {ka : a ∈ A}.

nodes.name: Doubling constant σ(A)
nodes.description: σ(A) = |A+A|/|A|, measuring how far A is from being a subgroup or coset; σ(A) = 1 iff A is a coset of a finite subgroup.

nodes.name: Ruzsa distance d(A,B)
nodes.description: d(A,B) = log(|A−B|/√(|A||B|)), a pseudo-metric on finite subsets of an abelian group satisfying the triangle inequality up to additive constants.

nodes.name: Additive energy E(A,B)
nodes.description: E(A,B) = |{(a₁,a₂,b₁,b₂) ∈ A²×B² : a₁+b₁ = a₂+b₂}|; measures the additive structure shared by A and B, with E(A,A) ∈ [|A|², |A|³].

nodes.name: Freiman homomorphism of order s
nodes.description: A map φ: A → B such that a₁+⋯+aₛ = a'₁+⋯+a'ₛ implies φ(a₁)+⋯+φ(aₛ) = φ(a'₁)+⋯+φ(a'ₛ); preserves additive structure up to s-fold sums.

nodes.name: Freiman isomorphism of order s
nodes.description: A bijective Freiman s-homomorphism whose inverse is also a Freiman s-homomorphism; the correct notion of structural equivalence in additive combinatorics.

nodes.name: Generalized arithmetic progression (GAP)
nodes.description: P = {a₀ + x₁v₁ + ⋯ + xₐvₐ : 0 ≤ xᵢ < Nᵢ} for base point a₀, generators v₁,…,vₐ, and lengths N₁,…,Nₐ; a d-dimensional GAP has rank/dimension d.

nodes.name: Proper generalized arithmetic progression
nodes.description: A GAP P = {a₀ + ∑xᵢvᵢ : 0 ≤ xᵢ < Nᵢ} is proper if |P| = ∏Nᵢ, i.e., all sums are distinct and the representation map is injective.

nodes.name: Bohr set B(S,ε)
nodes.description: B(S,ε) = {x ∈ G : |χ(x)−1| ≤ ε for all χ ∈ S} for a finite set S of characters; a structured neighborhood of 0 that generalizes subgroups.

nodes.name: Dissociated set
nodes.description: A set Λ ⊂ G such that any equation ∑_{λ∈Λ} ε_λ λ = 0 with ε_λ ∈ {−1,0,1} forces all ε_λ = 0; the combinatorial analog of linear independence for sumset problems.

nodes.name: K-approximate group
nodes.description: A finite symmetric set A containing the identity in a group G such that A·A can be covered by at most K translates of A; generalizes the notion of a finite subgroup.

nodes.name: Combinatorial dimension of a Bohr set
nodes.description: The cardinality |S| of the frequency set S in a Bohr set B(S,ε); controls the size and structure of the Bohr set via |B(S,ε)| ≈ εᵈ|G| for d = |S|.

nodes.name: Progression-free set (3-AP-free set)
nodes.description: A subset A of an abelian group containing no non-trivial 3-term arithmetic progression; the maximum size r₃(N) of such a set in {1,…,N} is the subject of Roth's theorem.

nodes.name: Sumset growth function
nodes.description: The function K ↦ f(K) bounding |kA−lA| in terms of |A| when |A+A| ≤ K|A|; the key quantitative object in Plünnecke–Ruzsa theory.

nodes.name: Plünnecke graph
nodes.description: A commutative layered bipartite graph (V₀,…,Vₕ) with a matching from Vᵢ to Vᵢ₊₁ modeling the map A → A+B; the combinatorial device underlying Plünnecke's inequality.

nodes.name: Magnification ratio
nodes.description: For a Plünnecke graph, Dₕ = min_{∅≠X⊆V₀} |im_h(X)|/|X|, the minimal expansion ratio from V₀ to Vₕ; the quantity controlled in Plünnecke's inequality.

nodes.name: Normalized additive energy
nodes.description: e(A) = E(A,A)/|A|³, the additive energy per unit cube; e(A) = 1 iff A is a coset, and e(A) ≥ 1/|A| always holds.

nodes.name: ε-regular pair (Szemerédi)
nodes.description: A pair (U,W) in a graph is ε-regular if for all X ⊂ U, Y ⊂ W with |X| ≥ ε|U|, |Y| ≥ ε|W|, |d(X,Y)−d(U,W)| ≤ ε; the quasirandom condition in the regularity lemma.

nodes.name: Popular difference
nodes.description: An element d ∈ G is a popular difference for A if |{a ∈ A : a+d ∈ A}| ≥ δ|A| for some threshold δ; appears in density increment and Balog–Szemerédi arguments.

nodes.name: Additive quadruple
nodes.description: A tuple (a₁,a₂,b₁,b₂) ∈ A²×B² with a₁+b₁ = a₂+b₂; the additive energy E(A,B) counts the number of such quadruples.

nodes.name: Coset progression
nodes.description: A set of the form P + H where P is a GAP and H is a finite subgroup; the natural generalization of GAP needed for Freiman's theorem in arbitrary abelian groups.

nodes.name: Convolution (representation) function r_{A+B}
nodes.description: r_{A+B}(x) = |{(a,b) ∈ A×B : a+b = x}|, counting representations of x as a sum from A and B; satisfies ∑_x r_{A+B}(x) = |A||B|.

nodes.name: Spectrum (large Fourier coefficients) of a set
nodes.description: Spec_δ(A) = {γ ∈ Ĝ : |Â(γ)| ≥ δ|A|}, the set of characters on which the Fourier transform of 1_A is large; controlled by Chang's theorem.

nodes.name: Pseudorandom measure (Green–Tao)
nodes.description: A non-negative function ν: ℤ_N → ℝ≥0 with 𝔼ν = 1+o(1) satisfying a linear forms condition and a correlation condition; the majorant for W-tricked primes in the Green–Tao argument.

nodes.name: W-trick (Green–Tao)
nodes.description: Restricting to primes p ≡ b (mod W) for W = ∏_{p≤w} p to remove small-prime biases; converts the primes into a set with better pseudorandomness properties.

nodes.name: Linear forms condition
nodes.description: The condition 𝔼_{x∈ℤ_N^d} ∏ᵢ ν(ψᵢ(x)) = 1+o(1) for a pseudorandom measure ν and a finite system of affine-linear forms ψᵢ with finite complexity; key hypothesis in the Green–Tao transference principle.

nodes.name: Correlation condition (Green–Tao)
nodes.description: The condition 𝔼_x ∏_{j=1}^m ν(x+h_j) ≤ ∑_{1≤i<j≤m} τ(h_i−h_j) for a weight τ with controlled moments; ensures the pseudorandom measure is not too concentrated.

nodes.name: Gowers uniformity norm U^k
nodes.description: ‖f‖_{U^k}^{2^k} = 𝔼_{x,h₁,…,hₖ} ∏_{ω∈{0,1}^k} C^{|ω|} f(x+ω·h), where C is conjugation; measures k-step uniformity and controls counts of (k+1)-term APs.

nodes.name: Gowers anti-uniform function
nodes.description: A dual function F with ‖F‖∞ ≤ 1 maximizing |⟨f,F⟩| subject to ‖F‖_{U^k} being small; used in the density/energy increment strategy for Szemerédi's theorem.

nodes.name: Plünnecke's inequality
nodes.description: If |A+B| ≤ K|A| then |hB−lB| ≤ K^{h+l}|A| for all h,l ≥ 0; proved via magnification ratios in Plünnecke graphs, controlling iterated sumset growth from a single doubling bound.

nodes.name: Ruzsa triangle inequality
nodes.description: |A−C| ≤ |A−B||B−C|/|B| for finite non-empty subsets A,B,C of an abelian group; the key tool making Ruzsa distance into a quasi-metric.

nodes.name: Ruzsa covering lemma
nodes.description: If |A+B| ≤ K|A| then B ⊆ A−A+T for some set T with |T| ≤ K; used to embed sets of small doubling into translates of a structured set.

nodes.name: Ruzsa sum-triangle inequality
nodes.description: |A+C| ≤ |A+B||B+C|/|B| for finite non-empty subsets of an abelian group; the sum-version complementing the difference-version of Ruzsa's triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Ruzsa distance–energy duality
nodes.description: E(A,B) ≥ |A|²|B|²/|A−B| by Cauchy–Schwarz, so small Ruzsa distance implies large additive energy; the bridge between metric and energy viewpoints.

nodes.name: Freiman–Ruzsa theorem in 𝔽₂ⁿ
nodes.description: If A ⊆ 𝔽₂ⁿ satisfies |A+A| ≤ K|A|, then A is contained in a subspace of size at most 2^{O(K)}|A|; the model-case inverse sumset theorem with polynomial bounds.

nodes.name: Balog–Szemerédi–Gowers theorem
nodes.description: If E(A,A) ≥ |A|³/K then there exists A' ⊂ A with |A'| ≥ c|A|/K and |A'+A'| ≤ CK⁴|A'|; converts large additive energy into a dense subset with small doubling, with polynomial bounds due to Gowers.

nodes.name: Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture (Dias da Silva–Hamidoune)
nodes.description: |{a+b : a,b ∈ A, a ≠ b}| ≥ min(p, 2|A|−3) for A ⊆ ℤ/pℤ; the restricted-sumset analog of Cauchy–Davenport, proved via the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz.

nodes.name: Elekes sum-product estimate
nodes.description: max(|A+A|, |A·A|) ≥ c|A|^{5/4} for finite A ⊂ ℝ; proved via the Szemerédi–Trotter theorem, confirming a weak form of the Erdős–Szemerédi conjecture.

nodes.name: Erdős–Szemerédi sum-product conjecture
nodes.description: For finite A ⊂ ℝ, max(|A+A|, |A·A|) ≥ c_ε|A|^{2−ε} for every ε > 0; asserts that a set cannot be simultaneously additively and multiplicatively structured.

nodes.name: Bergelson–Leibman theorem (polynomial Szemerédi)
nodes.description: For any polynomials p₁,…,pₖ ∈ ℤ[x] with pᵢ(0) = 0 and δ > 0, any sufficiently dense subset of {1,…,N} contains a configuration {a, a+p₁(d), …, a+pₖ(d)}; extends Szemerédi to polynomial progressions.

nodes.name: Inverse Littlewood–Offord theorem (Tao–Vu)
nodes.description: If P(v₁ε₁+⋯+vₙεₙ = x) ≥ n^{−C} for random signs εᵢ and non-degenerate vᵢ, then most vᵢ lie in a proper GAP of small rank and size O(n^{1/2+o(1)}); the structural characterization complementing the Erdős–Littlewood–Offord problem.

nodes.name: Littlewood–Offord problem
nodes.description: Given non-zero v₁,…,vₙ ∈ ℝ, maximize P(|v₁ε₁+⋯+vₙεₙ| ≤ 1) over random signs εᵢ ∈ {±1}; the classical answer is C(n,⌊n/2⌋)/2ⁿ ∼ c/√n by the Erdős bound, with the inverse problem asking for structural conditions achieving near-maximal probability.

nodes.name: Chang's theorem (large Fourier spectrum)
nodes.description: If A ⊆ ℤ/Nℤ with |A| = αN, then Spec_δ(A) is contained in a subspace of dimension O(δ⁻² log(1/α)); sharp control on the structure of the large spectrum using dissociated sets.

nodes.name: Bogolyubov's lemma
nodes.description: If A ⊆ ℤ/Nℤ has density α, then 2A−2A contains a Bohr set B(S,1/4) with |S| ≤ O(1/α²); iterated sumsets of dense sets contain highly structured subsets.

nodes.name: Sanders' quasi-polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa theorem
nodes.description: If A ⊆ 𝔽₂ⁿ with |A+A| ≤ K|A|, then A is contained in a subspace of size at most 2^{O(K(log K)^C)}|A|; the quasi-polynomial improvement toward the polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture.

nodes.name: Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture
nodes.description: If A ⊆ 𝔽₂ⁿ with |A+A| ≤ K|A|, then A can be covered by poly(K) translates of a subspace of size ≤ |A|; equivalently, the covering number in Freiman's theorem should be polynomial in K.

nodes.name: Gowers inverse theorem for U³
nodes.description: If ‖f‖_{U³} ≥ δ with |f| ≤ 1, then |⟨f, e(qφ)⟩| ≥ c(δ) for some quadratic phase φ; the inverse theorem identifying U³-structured functions with quadratic phases, key to Gowers' proof of Szemerédi for k=4.

nodes.name: Gowers inverse conjecture for U^k (Green–Tao–Ziegler)
nodes.description: If ‖f‖_{U^{k+1}} ≥ δ then f correlates with a nilsequence of step ≤ k and complexity O_{δ,k}(1); proved by Green–Tao–Ziegler, completing the inverse program characterizing Gowers norms.

nodes.name: Generalized von Neumann theorem
nodes.description: The count of k-APs 𝔼_{x,d} ∏ᵢ fᵢ(x+id) is controlled by min_i ‖fᵢ‖_{U^{k−1}}; the structure theorem reducing AP-counting to Gowers norm estimates.

nodes.name: Solymosi's sum-product estimate
nodes.description: max(|A+A|, |A·A|) ≥ c|A|^{4/3}/log^{1/3}|A| for finite A ⊂ ℝ; an improvement over the Elekes 5/4 exponent using the multiplicative energy approach.

nodes.name: Sum-product estimate in finite fields (Bourgain–Katz–Tao)
nodes.description: For A ⊆ 𝔽_p with p^δ ≤ |A| ≤ p^{1−δ}: max(|A+A|, |A·A|) ≥ |A|^{1+ε} for some ε = ε(δ) > 0; the finite field sum-product phenomenon.

nodes.name: Ruzsa modeling lemma
nodes.description: If A ⊆ ℤ/Nℤ has density α, then A is Freiman 2-isomorphic to a subset of ℤ/Mℤ of density ≥ α^{O(1)} for some M ≤ N; used to transfer Freiman-type results between ambient groups.

nodes.name: Ruzsa's proof of Freiman's theorem (via covering lemma)
nodes.description: Streamlined proof: if |A+A| ≤ K|A|, use the Ruzsa covering lemma to embed A in few translates of A−A, then the Plünnecke–Ruzsa inequality and a geometry-of-numbers argument to find a containing GAP.

nodes.name: Gowers quantitative bound for Szemerédi's theorem
nodes.description: r_k(N) ≤ N/(log log N)^{c_k} for the maximum size of a k-AP-free subset of {1,…,N}; the first effective bound for arbitrary k, via the Gowers uniformity norms and inverse theorems.

nodes.name: Regularity counting lemma (embedding lemma)
nodes.description: In an ε-regular partition with appropriately dense pairs, the count of copies of any fixed graph H is (1+o(1)) times the expected count for a random graph with the same densities.

nodes.name: Koopman–von Neumann structure theorem (in additive combinatorics)
nodes.description: Any bounded function f on ℤ_N decomposes as f = f_s + f_u + f_e where f_s is structured (low U^k norm correlation), f_u is uniform (small U^k norm), and f_e is small in L²; the structure–randomness dichotomy underlying energy increment arguments.

nodes.name: Arithmetic regularity lemma (Green)
nodes.description: For any f: ℤ_N → [0,1] and ε > 0, there exists a Bohr set B such that f is ε-uniform on cosets of B in the Gowers U² norm; the Fourier-analytic analog of graph regularity for additive problems.

nodes.name: Goldston–Yıldırım pseudorandom majorant for primes
nodes.description: The function ν(n) = (φ(W)/W)(log R)⁻¹(∑_{d|n, d≤R} μ(d)log(R/d))² satisfying the linear forms and correlation conditions; provides the pseudorandom measure dominating the W-tricked primes in the Green–Tao argument.

nodes.name: Hypergraph regularity lemma (Gowers, Nagle–Rödl–Schacht–Skokan)
nodes.description: Every k-uniform hypergraph admits a regular partition with respect to a (k−1)-complex of controlled complexity; the higher-order generalization enabling the regularity proof of Szemerédi's theorem for arbitrary k.

nodes.name: Hypergraph removal lemma
nodes.description: If a k-uniform hypergraph on n vertices contains o(nᵏ⁺¹) copies of a fixed k-uniform hypergraph H, then all copies can be removed by deleting o(nᵏ) edges; generalizes the triangle removal lemma to hypergraphs.

nodes.name: Multidimensional Szemerédi theorem (Furstenberg–Katznelson)
nodes.description: For any finite S ⊂ ℤᵈ and δ > 0, any sufficiently large subset of {1,…,N}ᵈ of density ≥ δ contains a homothetic copy a+tS for some t > 0; the multi-dimensional density generalization of Szemerédi.

nodes.name: Long arithmetic progressions in sumsets
nodes.description: If A, B ⊆ {1,…,N} with |A| = αN, |B| = βN, then A+B contains an AP of length at least exp(c(αβ log N)^{1/2}); combining probabilistic, Fourier, and combinatorial methods.

nodes.name: Bourgain's bound for 3-AP-free sets
nodes.description: r₃(N) ≤ N(log log N)^{1/2}/(log N)^{1/2}; improved Roth's original log log N bound using iterated density increment with Bohr set techniques.

nodes.name: Meshulam's theorem (Roth in 𝔽₃ⁿ)
nodes.description: The maximum size of a 3-AP-free subset of 𝔽₃ⁿ is O(3ⁿ/n); the clean model-case Roth theorem in the finite field setting.

nodes.name: Bateman–Katz bound for cap sets
nodes.description: A 3-AP-free subset of 𝔽₃ⁿ has size O(3ⁿ/n^{1+ε}) for some ε > 0; improved the Meshulam O(3ⁿ/n) bound in the cap set problem.

nodes.name: Rankin's construction (k-AP-free sets)
nodes.description: A k-AP-free subset of {1,…,N} of size N·exp(−c_k(log N)^{1/(⌈log₂ k⌉)}); the higher-k generalization of Behrend's sphere-based construction.

nodes.name: Green–Tao linear equations in primes
nodes.description: Systems of linear equations of finite complexity have the expected number of prime solutions (up to local factors), asymptotically; generalizes the Green–Tao theorem on APs to general linear configurations.

nodes.name: Plünnecke graph method
nodes.description: Model iterated sumset growth via a commutative layered graph with matchings; derive magnification ratio bounds by Menger's theorem and the submodularity of image sets. Used in the original Plünnecke–Ruzsa inequality.

nodes.name: Ruzsa calculus
nodes.description: The systematic use of Ruzsa's triangle inequality, covering lemma, and distance to chain sumset estimates: derive |kA−lA| bounds from |A+A|/|A|, embed sets into GAPs, and transfer between groups. The core toolkit of sumset geometry.

nodes.name: Fourier analysis on finite abelian groups
nodes.description: Expand indicator functions 1_A as ∑_γ Â(γ)γ over the dual group; use Parseval, convolution identities, and large-value estimates to count additive configurations. Central to Roth's theorem and the Bohr set method.

nodes.name: Density increment argument
nodes.description: If A has no k-AP, find a long subprogression (or Bohr set) where A has higher density; iterate O(1/δ) times until the density exceeds 1, yielding a contradiction. The inductive engine of Roth's and Szemerédi's Fourier proofs.

nodes.name: Energy increment argument
nodes.description: Iteratively refine a partition/decomposition so that the 'energy' (L² norm of the structured part) increases by a definite amount at each step; must terminate in O(1/ε²) steps. Used in regularity proofs and Gowers' approach to Szemerédi.

nodes.name: Regularity method for arithmetic combinatorics
nodes.description: Apply the Szemerédi regularity lemma to an auxiliary graph encoding the arithmetic structure (e.g., the graph on A with edges {(a,b): a+b ∈ A}), then use the counting/embedding lemma to find the desired configuration.

nodes.name: Graph removal technique
nodes.description: Encode an arithmetic problem (e.g., 3-APs) as a subgraph counting problem in a tripartite graph; apply the removal lemma to deduce density results. The bridge from Szemerédi regularity to Roth's theorem and the corners theorem.

nodes.name: Probabilistic method in additive combinatorics
nodes.description: Use random sampling, random dilations, or random restrictions to show existence of sets/configurations with desired additive properties; includes random subsets of sumsets, probabilistic covering arguments, and the alteration method.

nodes.name: Polynomial method (Combinatorial Nullstellensatz applications)
nodes.description: Encode additive problems as polynomial nonvanishing: choose a polynomial whose nonzero coefficient certifies the configuration, then apply Alon's Nullstellensatz or Chevalley–Warning to guarantee solutions. Yields Cauchy–Davenport, Erdős–Heilbronn, and EGZ.

nodes.name: Sum-product technique
nodes.description: Exploit the tension between additive and multiplicative structure: if A has small sumset then A·A must be large, via incidence geometry (Szemerédi–Trotter) or energy estimates. Leads to expander results in finite fields.

nodes.name: Incidence geometry method
nodes.description: Bound the number of incidences between points and curves (lines, circles) using cell decomposition or crossing number inequalities; apply to sumset and sum-product problems by encoding sums/products as point-line incidences.

nodes.name: Tensor product trick (Ruzsa)
nodes.description: Embed A ⊂ ℤ into A^d ⊂ ℤᵈ and exploit the multiplicativity of sumset growth under Cartesian products to amplify Freiman-type bounds; converts approximate bounds into exact structural results via a limiting argument.

nodes.name: Ergodic theory approach (Furstenberg)
nodes.description: Via the Furstenberg correspondence, translate combinatorial density problems to ergodic recurrence; prove the recurrence using weak mixing/compact decomposition and the van der Corput trick in Hilbert space.

nodes.name: Hypergraph regularity method
nodes.description: Extend graph regularity to k-uniform hypergraphs via a hierarchy of regular approximations (simplicial complexes); combined with a hypergraph counting lemma, yields Szemerédi's theorem for arbitrary k and the Hales–Jewett theorem.

nodes.name: Cell decomposition (for incidence bounds)
nodes.description: Partition ℝ² into O(r²) cells using r vertical lines and r polynomial curves so each cell has few points; aggregate local incidence bounds using the Szemerédi–Trotter framework.

nodes.name: Dyadic pigeonholing
nodes.description: Partition a range into O(log N) dyadic intervals [2ᵏ, 2ᵏ⁺¹) and select the interval contributing the most to a sum; loses only a logarithmic factor while reducing to a level-set estimate. Ubiquitous in sumset and energy arguments.

nodes.name: Compression/symmetrization
nodes.description: Replace a set A by its successive compressions (projections onto coordinate hyperplanes followed by downsets) to reduce to the extremal case without increasing the sumset; used to prove sumset lower bounds and the Cauchy–Davenport theorem.

nodes.name: Additive energy amplification
nodes.description: Boost additive energy by passing to a popular-difference subset or applying iterated sumset operations; combined with Balog–Szemerédi–Gowers, converts partial structure into full small-doubling structure.

nodes.name: Bohr set method
nodes.description: Use Bohr sets as substitutes for subgroups in ℤ/Nℤ: perform density increments on Bohr sets, control their size via dimension, and exploit their near-invariance under addition. Central to improved Roth bounds and the Green–Tao argument.

nodes.name: Weyl differencing
nodes.description: Reduce the degree of a phase function by squaring an exponential sum and changing variables: |∑ e(f(n))|² = ∑_h ∑_n e(f(n+h)−f(n)); iterating reduces polynomial phases to linear ones. Fundamental in both analytic number theory and Gowers norm analysis.

nodes.name: Van der Corput trick/inequality
nodes.description: |𝔼_n f(n)|² ≤ (1/H) ∑_{|h|<H} (1−|h|/H) 𝔼_n f(n+h)f̄(n); converts a single average into a double average over differences, reducing equidistribution to correlation decay. Used in ergodic theory, exponential sum, and Gowers norm arguments.

nodes.name: Dependent random choice
nodes.description: Choose a random subset by selecting common neighbors of a random tuple in a graph; the resulting set is small but has the property that any small sub-tuple has many common neighbors. Yields efficient proofs of Ramsey-type and Balog–Szemerédi–Gowers-type results.

nodes.name: Stepanov method
nodes.description: Construct an auxiliary polynomial vanishing to high order at the points of interest, then bound its degree against its vanishing order to get a point count; an elementary alternative to Weil's algebraic-geometry approach for character sum and curve-point bounds over finite fields.

nodes.name: Character sum method
nodes.description: Express indicator functions of structured sets (squares, kth powers) via multiplicative characters and bound the resulting character sums using Weil-type estimates; used for Sárközy's theorem, sum-product in finite fields, and distribution of primes in APs.

nodes.name: Geometry of numbers in Freiman's theorem
nodes.description: Apply Minkowski's lattice point theorem or John's ellipsoid theorem to find a proper GAP containing A: given A−A ⊆ a coset progression from covering, find a GAP of controlled dimension and size via lattice basis reduction.

nodes.name: Structure–randomness dichotomy
nodes.description: Decompose a function/set into a structured (low-complexity) component and a pseudorandom (uniform) component; the structured part determines the count of the desired configuration while the uniform part is negligible. The overarching philosophy of modern additive combinatorics.

nodes.name: ε-net/covering argument for Bohr sets
nodes.description: Construct a maximal separated subset (ε-net) inside a Bohr set to control its metric entropy; used to estimate |B(S,ε)| and to find large structured subsets via pigeonhole on Bohr set coverings.

nodes.name: Nilsequence
nodes.description: A sequence n ↦ F(g(n)Γ) where G/Γ is a nilmanifold, g: ℤ → G is a polynomial sequence, and F is Lipschitz; the higher-order structured objects arising in the inverse theory for Gowers norms U^k with k ≥ 3.

nodes.name: Nilmanifold G/Γ
nodes.description: A compact homogeneous space G/Γ where G is a connected nilpotent Lie group and Γ ≤ G is a cocompact discrete subgroup; the phase space for nilsequences in the Gowers inverse theory.

nodes.name: Stabilizer (period) of a sumset
nodes.description: H(A+B) = {g ∈ G : g+A+B = A+B}, the largest subgroup preserving A+B; the critical object in Kneser's theorem controlling how much |A+B| can fall below |A|+|B|.

nodes.name: Davenport constant D(G)
nodes.description: The smallest d such that any sequence of d elements in G contains a non-empty subsequence summing to 0; D(ℤ/nℤ) = n and the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv theorem states D(ℤ/nℤ) in the restricted sense is 2n−1.

nodes.name: Sum-free set
nodes.description: A set A ⊆ G such that (A+A) ∩ A = ∅; the maximum size of a sum-free subset of {1,…,n} is ⌈n/2⌉, and the study of sum-free sets connects to Schur's theorem and Ramsey theory.

nodes.name: Covering number (Ruzsa)
nodes.description: cov(B, A−A) = the minimum number of translates of A−A needed to cover B; the Ruzsa covering lemma bounds this by |A+B|/|A|.

nodes.name: Szemerédi's theorem via graph regularity
nodes.description: Proof of Szemerédi's theorem using the regularity lemma: encode k-APs as cliques in an auxiliary (k−1)-partite graph, apply regularity + counting lemma; the original approach for k ≥ 4.

nodes.name: Roth's theorem via Fourier analysis
nodes.description: Proof: the 3-AP count T₃(A) = ∑_r |Â(r)|²Â(−2r)·N⁻¹; if T₃(A) is small, a large Fourier coefficient gives a density increment on a subprogression. Iterate to contradiction.

nodes.name: Roth's theorem via triangle removal
nodes.description: For A ⊆ ℤ/Nℤ, construct a tripartite graph where triangles encode 3-APs in A; the triangle removal lemma gives |{3-APs}| = o(N²) implies |A| = o(N). A clean graph-theoretic route to Roth.

nodes.name: Structure of the Green–Tao proof
nodes.description: Step 1: W-trick to derandomize primes. Step 2: Construct Goldston–Yıldırım majorant ν. Step 3: Verify linear forms + correlation conditions. Step 4: Apply relative Szemerédi (transference). Step 5: Conclude APs in primes.

nodes.name: Additive combinatorics in 𝔽_p (finite field model)
nodes.description: The study of sumsets, additive energy, and structure theorems in ℤ/pℤ or 𝔽_pⁿ, where the absence of torsion issues and availability of exact Fourier analysis make many arguments cleaner; the 'model case' for the integers.

nodes.name: Inverse sumset problem
nodes.description: Given that |A+A| ≤ K|A|, characterize the structure of A; the central question of additive combinatorics, answered (in various precisions) by Freiman's theorem, Balog–Szemerédi–Gowers, and the polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture.

nodes.name: Cap set problem
nodes.description: Determine the maximum size of a 3-AP-free subset of 𝔽₃ⁿ; the Ellenberg–Gijswijt (2016) bound of O(2.756ⁿ) via the polynomial method was a breakthrough (outside this book's scope but the problem is central to Ch 10).

nodes.name: Gowers norms control AP counts
nodes.description: |Λ_k(f) − Λ_k(1)| ≤ min_i ‖fᵢ − 1‖_{U^{k-1}} where Λ_k(f) = 𝔼_{x,d} ∏ f(x+id); the U^{k-1} norm is the correct notion of uniformity for k-APs, as small U^{k-1} norm implies the correct AP count.

nodes.name: Balog–Szemerédi–Gowers graph argument
nodes.description: Build a bipartite graph on A×A with edges where the sumset representation is popular; use graph-theoretic path-counting (or dependent random choice) to find a dense subset A' with small sumset. The combinatorial core of the BSG theorem.

nodes.name: AP count formula via Fourier analysis
nodes.description: The number of k-APs in A ⊆ ℤ/Nℤ equals N ∑_r |Â(r)|^k · (Fourier coefficient of the k-AP kernel); for k=3, this is N⁻¹ ∑_r Â(r)²Â(−2r), making the problem amenable to spectral analysis.

nodes.name: Sumset lower bound problem
nodes.description: The direct sumset problem: given |A|, |B| and the ambient group, determine the minimum possible |A+B|; answered by Cauchy–Davenport for ℤ/pℤ and Kneser for general abelian groups.

nodes.name: Vosper's theorem
nodes.description: If A, B ⊆ ℤ/pℤ with |A|, |B| ≥ 2 and |A+B| = |A|+|B|−1 < p, then A and B are arithmetic progressions with the same common difference; the inverse theorem for equality in Cauchy–Davenport.

nodes.name: Freiman's 3k−4 theorem
nodes.description: If A ⊂ ℤ with |A+A| ≤ 3|A|−4, then A is contained in an arithmetic progression of length |A+A|−|A|+1 ≤ 2|A|−3; the tight inverse theorem for very small doubling.

nodes.name: Erdős–Littlewood–Offord inequality
nodes.description: For non-zero v₁,…,vₙ and random signs εᵢ ∈ {±1}: P(|∑ εᵢvᵢ − x| ≤ 1) ≤ C(n,⌊n/2⌋)/2ⁿ ∼ c/√n for any x; the optimal anti-concentration bound, proved by Erdős via Sperner's theorem.

nodes.name: Halász-type inequality (additive combinatorics)
nodes.description: P(∑ εᵢvᵢ ∈ a+S) ≤ C·sup_t |𝔼 e^{itS}| · ∏ cos(tvᵢ) bounds; anti-concentration via characteristic function methods, underlying the Littlewood–Offord inverse theory.

nodes.name: Small ball probability (Lévy concentration function)
nodes.description: Q(X, ε) = sup_x P(|X−x| ≤ ε), the concentration function of a random variable; the Littlewood–Offord problem amounts to bounding Q(∑εᵢvᵢ, 1) and the inverse problem characterizes when Q is large.

nodes.name: Probability space
nodes.description: A triple (Ω, F, P) where Ω is a sample space, F is a σ-algebra of events, and P is a probability measure with P(Ω) = 1.

nodes.name: Probability measure
nodes.description: A countably additive set function P: F → [0,1] on a σ-algebra F with P(Ω) = 1.

nodes.name: Random variable
nodes.description: A measurable function X: (Ω, F) → (ℝ, B(ℝ)), i.e., {ω : X(ω) ≤ x} ∈ F for every x ∈ ℝ.

nodes.name: Distribution (law) of a random variable
nodes.description: The probability measure μ_X(B) = P(X ∈ B) on (ℝ, B(ℝ)) induced by a random variable X, also written L(X) or P ∘ X⁻¹.

nodes.name: Independence of events
nodes.description: Events A₁, …, Aₙ are independent if P(Aᵢ₁ ∩ ··· ∩ Aᵢₖ) = P(Aᵢ₁)···P(Aᵢₖ) for every subcollection of distinct indices.

nodes.name: Independence of random variables
nodes.description: Random variables X₁, …, Xₙ are independent if the σ-algebras σ(X₁), …, σ(Xₙ) are independent, equivalently P(X₁ ∈ B₁, …, Xₙ ∈ Bₙ) = ∏ P(Xᵢ ∈ Bᵢ).

nodes.name: Almost sure convergence
nodes.description: Xₙ → X almost surely if P({ω : Xₙ(ω) → X(ω)}) = 1.

nodes.name: Convergence in probability
nodes.description: Xₙ → X in probability if P(|Xₙ − X| > ε) → 0 for every ε > 0.

nodes.name: Convergence in distribution
nodes.description: Xₙ →_d X if Fₙ(x) → F(x) at every continuity point x of F, where Fₙ, F are the respective distribution functions.

nodes.name: Characteristic function
nodes.description: The function φ_X(t) = E[e^{itX}] for t ∈ ℝ, the Fourier transform of the distribution of X, which uniquely determines the distribution.

nodes.name: Stable distribution
nodes.description: A distribution with index α ∈ (0,2] such that the sum of n i.i.d. copies, suitably normalized, has the same distribution; the Gaussian (α=2) and Cauchy (α=1) are special cases.

nodes.name: Domain of attraction
nodes.description: A distribution F belongs to the domain of attraction of a stable law G with index α if there exist aₙ > 0, bₙ such that (Sₙ − bₙ)/aₙ →_d G.

nodes.name: Tightness of a family of probability measures
nodes.description: A family {μ_α} of probability measures on a metric space is tight if for every ε > 0 there exists a compact K with μ_α(K) > 1 − ε for all α.

nodes.name: Poisson limit theorem
nodes.description: If Xₙ ~ Binomial(n, pₙ) with npₙ → λ, then Xₙ →_d Poisson(λ); the Poisson distribution arises as the limit of rare Bernoulli events.

nodes.name: Local central limit theorem
nodes.description: For i.i.d. integer-valued random variables with span 1, the probability P(Sₙ = k) is asymptotically (σ√(2πn))⁻¹ exp(−(k − nμ)²/(2nσ²)) uniformly in k.

nodes.name: Strong Markov property for random walks
nodes.description: For a random walk Sₙ and a stopping time τ < ∞ a.s., the post-τ increments (S_{τ+k} − S_τ)_{k≥1} are independent of F_τ and have the same distribution as the original walk.

nodes.name: Arc sine law
nodes.description: For a symmetric random walk, the fraction of time spent positive up to step 2n converges in distribution to the arc sine distribution with density 1/(π√(x(1−x))) on (0,1).
aliases: arc sine law for random walks

nodes.name: Gambler's ruin
nodes.description: For a simple random walk with absorbing barriers at 0 and N, the ruin probability starting from k is (q/p)^k − (q/p)^N)/(1 − (q/p)^N) when p ≠ q, and 1 − k/N when p = q = 1/2.

nodes.name: Ladder variables
nodes.description: For a random walk Sₙ, the ascending ladder time T⁺ = inf{n ≥ 1 : Sₙ > 0} and ladder height H⁺ = S_{T⁺}; iterating these defines the ascending ladder process.

nodes.name: Convergence of random series
nodes.description: The series Σ Xₙ of independent random variables converges a.s. if and only if it converges in probability, which holds iff the three series of Kolmogorov's three-series theorem converge.

nodes.name: Kronecker's lemma
nodes.description: If bₙ ↑ ∞ and Σ aₙ/bₙ converges, then (1/bₙ) Σₖ₌₁ⁿ aₖ → 0; the key tool converting convergence of a series to convergence of Cesàro-type averages in SLLN proofs.

nodes.name: Tower property of conditional expectation
nodes.description: If H ⊂ G are sub-σ-algebras, then E[E[X | G] | H] = E[X | H] a.s.; the law of iterated expectations.

nodes.name: Uniform integrability and L¹ convergence
nodes.description: A uniformly integrable martingale (Xₙ, Fₙ) converges a.s. and in L¹ to X∞ = E[X∞ | Fₙ]; conversely, an L¹-bounded martingale converges in L¹ iff it is uniformly integrable.

nodes.name: Doob's decomposition theorem (discrete)
nodes.description: Every adapted integrable process Xₙ admits a unique decomposition Xₙ = Mₙ + Aₙ where M is a martingale and A is a predictable process with A₀ = 0.

nodes.name: Backward martingale convergence theorem
nodes.description: If (Xₙ)_{n≤0} is a backward martingale with respect to (Fₙ)_{n≤0}, then Xₙ → E[X₀ | F₋∞] a.s. and in L¹ as n → −∞.

nodes.name: Lévy's 0-1 law
nodes.description: If Fₙ ↑ F∞ and A ∈ F∞, then P(A | Fₙ) → 1_A a.s.; conditional probabilities of a tail event converge to its indicator.

nodes.name: Branching process (Galton-Watson)
nodes.description: A Markov chain Zₙ where Z₀ = 1 and each individual in generation n independently produces a random number of offspring with a fixed distribution, giving Zₙ₊₁ = Σᵢ₌₁^{Zₙ} ξᵢ.

nodes.name: Extinction criterion for branching processes
nodes.description: The extinction probability q = P(Zₙ → 0) equals 1 if the mean offspring μ ≤ 1, and equals the unique fixed point in [0,1) of the offspring generating function if μ > 1.

nodes.name: Martingale central limit theorem
nodes.description: For a martingale difference array (Xₙᵢ) with conditional variances Σᵢ E[Xₙᵢ² | Fₙ,ᵢ₋₁] →_P 1 and a Lindeberg-type condition, the partial sums converge in distribution to N(0,1).

nodes.name: Exponential martingale
nodes.description: For i.i.d. Xᵢ with E[e^{θXᵢ}] = M(θ) < ∞, the process exp(θSₙ − n log M(θ)) is a martingale; a key tool for large deviation and stopping time computations.

nodes.name: Markov chain
nodes.description: A sequence of random variables (Xₙ) in a countable state space S with the Markov property: P(Xₙ₊₁ = j | X₀, …, Xₙ) = P(Xₙ₊₁ = j | Xₙ) = p(Xₙ, j).

nodes.name: Transition matrix
nodes.description: A matrix P = (p(i,j))_{i,j ∈ S} with nonneg entries and row sums equal to 1, encoding one-step transition probabilities of a Markov chain.

nodes.name: Chapman-Kolmogorov equations
nodes.description: The n-step transition probabilities satisfy p^{(m+n)}(i,j) = Σ_k p^{(m)}(i,k) p^{(n)}(k,j), equivalently P^{m+n} = P^m P^n.

nodes.name: Markov property
nodes.description: Conditional on Xₙ = i, the future process (Xₙ₊ₖ)_{k≥0} is independent of the past (X₀, …, Xₙ₋₁) and has the law of a chain started at i.

nodes.name: Strong Markov property for Markov chains
nodes.description: For a Markov chain and stopping time τ with P(τ < ∞) > 0, conditional on τ < ∞ and X_τ = i, the post-τ process is independent of F_τ and has the law of a chain started at i.

nodes.name: Communication classes
nodes.description: States i, j communicate (i ↔ j) if i → j and j → i, where i → j means p^{(n)}(i,j) > 0 for some n; communication is an equivalence relation partitioning the state space into classes.

nodes.name: Irreducibility of a Markov chain
nodes.description: A Markov chain is irreducible if every state communicates with every other state, i.e., the state space consists of a single communication class.

nodes.name: Recurrence for Markov chains
nodes.description: A state i is recurrent if P_i(Xₙ = i for some n ≥ 1) = 1, equivalently Σₙ p^{(n)}(i,i) = ∞.

nodes.name: Transience for Markov chains
nodes.description: A state i is transient if P_i(Xₙ = i for some n ≥ 1) < 1, equivalently Σₙ p^{(n)}(i,i) < ∞.

nodes.name: Recurrence is a class property
nodes.description: If i ↔ j and i is recurrent, then j is recurrent; thus recurrence and transience are properties of communication classes, not individual states.

nodes.name: Positive recurrence
nodes.description: A recurrent state i is positive recurrent if the expected return time E_i[T_i] < ∞, where T_i = inf{n ≥ 1 : Xₙ = i}.

nodes.name: Null recurrence
nodes.description: A recurrent state i is null recurrent if the expected return time E_i[T_i] = ∞; the state is visited infinitely often but the average return time is infinite.

nodes.name: Period of a state
nodes.description: The period of state i is d(i) = gcd{n ≥ 1 : p^{(n)}(i,i) > 0}; a state with period 1 is called aperiodic.
aliases: periodicity of a Markov chain state

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of stationary distribution
nodes.description: An irreducible positive recurrent Markov chain has a unique stationary distribution π with π(i) = 1/E_i[T_i]; an irreducible chain has a stationary distribution iff it is positive recurrent.

nodes.name: Convergence theorem for Markov chains
nodes.description: For an irreducible, aperiodic, positive recurrent Markov chain with stationary distribution π, p^{(n)}(i,j) → π(j) as n → ∞ for all i, j.
aliases: basic limit theorem for Markov chains

nodes.name: Detailed balance
nodes.description: A distribution π and transition matrix P satisfy detailed balance if π(i)p(i,j) = π(j)p(j,i) for all i, j; this implies π is stationary for P.

nodes.name: Ratio limit theorem
nodes.description: For an irreducible recurrent Markov chain, Σₖ₌₀ⁿ p^{(k)}(i,j) / Σₖ₌₀ⁿ p^{(k)}(i,i) → π(j)/π(i) (or E_i[T_i]/E_j[T_j]) as n → ∞.

nodes.name: Mean return time
nodes.description: The expected first return time E_i[T_i] where T_i = inf{n ≥ 1 : Xₙ = i}; equals 1/π(i) for positive recurrent state i with stationary distribution π.

nodes.name: Absorbing state
nodes.description: A state i is absorbing if p(i,i) = 1; once the chain enters state i it remains there forever.

nodes.name: Ergodicity
nodes.description: A measure-preserving transformation T on (Ω, F, μ) is ergodic if every T-invariant set A (T⁻¹A = A) satisfies μ(A) = 0 or μ(A) = 1.

nodes.name: Maximal ergodic lemma
nodes.description: For f ∈ L¹ and T measure-preserving, ∫_{A} f dμ ≥ 0 where A = {ω : sup_{n≥1} (1/n)Σₖ₌₀ⁿ⁻¹ f(Tᵏω) > 0}; the key lemma in proving the pointwise ergodic theorem.

nodes.name: Strong mixing
nodes.description: A measure-preserving transformation T is strongly mixing if μ(A ∩ T⁻ⁿB) → μ(A)μ(B) for all measurable A, B as n → ∞.

nodes.name: Stationary process
nodes.description: A stochastic process (Xₙ) whose joint distributions are shift-invariant: (X_{n₁+k}, …, X_{nₘ+k}) has the same distribution as (X_{n₁}, …, X_{nₘ}) for all k.

nodes.name: Shannon-McMillan-Breiman theorem
nodes.description: For an ergodic stationary process, −(1/n) log μ(partition cell containing (X₁,…,Xₙ)) → h a.s., where h is the entropy rate; typical sequences have probability ≈ e^{−nh}.

nodes.name: Kac's lemma
nodes.description: For an ergodic measure-preserving transformation T on a probability space and A with μ(A) > 0, the expected return time to A is E_A[τ_A] = 1/μ(A).

nodes.name: Kolmogorov-Čentsov continuity theorem
nodes.description: If E[|X_t − X_s|^α] ≤ C|t − s|^{1+β} for some α, β > 0, then X has a continuous modification with locally Hölder continuous paths of any exponent γ < β/α.

nodes.name: Markov property of Brownian motion
nodes.description: For Brownian motion B_t and fixed time s, the process (B_{s+t} − B_s)_{t≥0} is a standard Brownian motion independent of F_s.

nodes.name: Strong Markov property of Brownian motion
nodes.description: For Brownian motion B_t and an a.s. finite stopping time τ, the process (B_{τ+t} − B_τ)_{t≥0} is a standard Brownian motion independent of F_τ.

nodes.name: Blumenthal's 0-1 law
nodes.description: Every event in the germ σ-algebra F_{0+} = ∩_{t>0} F_t of a Brownian motion has probability 0 or 1; the immediate future of BM is deterministic given the starting point.

nodes.name: Reflection principle for Brownian motion
nodes.description: For Brownian motion and the hitting time τ_a = inf{t : B_t = a}, the reflected process B̃_t = B_t for t ≤ τ_a and B̃_t = 2a − B_t for t > τ_a is also a Brownian motion.

nodes.name: Distribution of the maximum of Brownian motion
nodes.description: P(max_{0≤s≤t} B_s ≥ a) = 2P(B_t ≥ a) = 2(1 − Φ(a/√t)) for a ≥ 0, derived from the reflection principle.

nodes.name: Arc sine law for Brownian motion
nodes.description: The last zero of BM before time 1, the time at which BM attains its maximum on [0,1], and the Lebesgue measure of {t ∈ [0,1] : B_t > 0} all follow the arc sine distribution on [0,1].

nodes.name: Nowhere differentiability of Brownian motion
nodes.description: Almost surely, the paths of Brownian motion are nowhere differentiable: for a.e. ω, there is no t at which lim_{h→0} (B_{t+h}(ω) − B_t(ω))/h exists.

nodes.name: Quadratic variation of Brownian motion
nodes.description: The quadratic variation of Brownian motion on [0,t] equals t: Σᵢ (B_{tᵢ} − B_{tᵢ₋₁})² → t in L² (and in probability) as the mesh of the partition goes to 0.

nodes.name: Brownian motion and harmonic functions
nodes.description: For a bounded domain D ⊂ ℝⁿ with regular boundary and continuous f on ∂D, the function u(x) = E_x[f(B_{τ_D})] solves the Dirichlet problem Δu = 0 in D with u = f on ∂D.

nodes.name: Recurrence and transience of Brownian motion
nodes.description: Brownian motion in ℝᵈ is recurrent (visits every open set infinitely often) for d ≤ 2 and transient (|B_t| → ∞ a.s.) for d ≥ 3.

nodes.name: Time inversion of Brownian motion
nodes.description: If B_t is a standard Brownian motion, then the process X_t = tB_{1/t} for t > 0 and X_0 = 0 is also a standard Brownian motion.

nodes.name: Scaling property of Brownian motion
nodes.description: For any c > 0, the process (c⁻¹/² B_{ct})_{t≥0} is a standard Brownian motion; BM is self-similar with exponent 1/2.

nodes.name: Brownian motion as a martingale
nodes.description: Standard Brownian motion B_t is a continuous martingale w.r.t. its natural filtration; moreover B_t² − t is also a martingale.

nodes.name: Construction of Brownian motion
nodes.description: Brownian motion can be constructed via Lévy's interpolation (dyadic), the Wiener series (random Fourier series on [0,1]), or the Kolmogorov extension theorem combined with the Kolmogorov-Čentsov continuity theorem.

nodes.name: Hitting times of Brownian motion
nodes.description: The hitting time τ_a = inf{t ≥ 0 : B_t = a} is a.s. finite for all a ∈ ℝ (d=1), has the distribution of a²/N² where N ~ N(0,1) (related to inverse Gaussian), and E[τ_a] = ∞.

nodes.name: Subsequence argument
nodes.function_signature: (Convergence in probability) → (a.s. convergence along subsequence → full a.s. convergence)
nodes.description: Extracts an a.s. convergent subsequence from a sequence converging in probability, then extends the conclusion to the full sequence by monotonicity or interpolation.

nodes.name: Borel-Cantelli technique
nodes.function_signature: (Tail probability estimates Σ P(Aₙ)) → (a.s. occurrence/non-occurrence of {Aₙ i.o.})
nodes.description: Proves almost sure convergence or divergence by bounding the sum of probabilities of bad events and applying the first or second Borel-Cantelli lemma.

nodes.name: Moment method (probabilistic)
nodes.function_signature: (Moments E[Xₙᵏ]) → (Convergence in distribution)
nodes.description: Establishes convergence in distribution by computing all moments of Xₙ, showing convergence to moments of the target, and verifying the target is moment-determined.

nodes.name: Skorokhod representation technique
nodes.function_signature: (Convergence in distribution) → (a.s. convergence on a coupled space)
nodes.description: Replaces convergence in distribution with almost sure convergence by constructing equivalent random variables on a common probability space via Skorokhod's representation theorem.

nodes.name: Maximal inequality technique
nodes.function_signature: (Tail bound on max_{k≤n} |Sₖ|) → (a.s. convergence or rate bounds)
nodes.description: Controls the fluctuations of partial sums or martingales using Kolmogorov's, Doob's, or Lévy's maximal inequality to deduce almost sure convergence or moment bounds.

nodes.name: Stopping time technique
nodes.function_signature: (Process Xₙ, stopping time τ) → (Properties of X_τ via optional stopping/sampling)
nodes.description: Analyzes a process at a random time by applying optional stopping theorems, the strong Markov property, or Wald's equations to extract information about hitting probabilities, expected values, or distributional properties.

nodes.name: Diagonalization technique (probability)
nodes.function_signature: (Countable family of subsequential limits) → (Single subsequence with all properties)
nodes.description: Extracts a single subsequence satisfying countably many convergence requirements simultaneously by iterating subsequence extraction and taking the diagonal.

nodes.name: Sample space
nodes.description: The set Ω of all possible outcomes of a random experiment, forming the first component of a probability space (Ω, F, P).

nodes.name: Classical probability (Laplace)
nodes.description: For a finite sample space with equally likely outcomes, P(A) = |A|/|Ω|; the combinatorial definition of probability due to Laplace.

nodes.name: Multinomial coefficient
nodes.description: The number n!/(k₁!k₂!⋯kᵣ!) of ways to partition n objects into r groups of sizes k₁,…,kᵣ with k₁+⋯+kᵣ=n.

nodes.name: Multinomial distribution
nodes.description: The joint distribution of counts (X₁,…,Xᵣ) in n independent trials with r outcomes of probabilities p₁,…,pᵣ, with P(X₁=k₁,…,Xᵣ=kᵣ) = n!/(k₁!⋯kᵣ!) p₁^{k₁}⋯pᵣ^{kᵣ}.

nodes.name: Hypergeometric distribution
nodes.description: The distribution of the number of successes in n draws without replacement from a population of N containing K successes: P(X=k) = C(K,k)C(N−K,n−k)/C(N,n).

nodes.name: Birthday problem
nodes.description: The probability that among n persons at least two share a birthday; for n=23 this exceeds 1/2, illustrating the surprising frequency of coincidences in moderate-sized samples.

nodes.name: Bose–Einstein statistics
nodes.description: The occupancy model in which n indistinguishable particles are distributed among r cells with all arrangements equally likely; the number of such arrangements is C(n+r−1, n).

nodes.name: Fermi–Dirac statistics
nodes.description: The occupancy model in which n indistinguishable particles are placed in r cells with at most one per cell, all C(r,n) arrangements equally likely.

nodes.name: First passage time
nodes.description: For a random walk (Sₙ), the first time T_a = inf{n ≥ 1 : Sₙ = a} that the walk reaches level a; a fundamental quantity in fluctuation theory.

nodes.name: Matching problem (problème des rencontres)
nodes.description: The problem of counting fixed points (matches) in a random permutation of n objects; the probability of at least one match converges to 1 − e⁻¹ as n → ∞.

nodes.name: Law of total probability
nodes.description: If {B₁,…,Bₙ} is a partition of Ω with P(Bᵢ) > 0, then P(A) = Σᵢ P(A|Bᵢ)P(Bᵢ); the marginal probability as a mixture over conditioning events.

nodes.name: Pólya urn model
nodes.description: An urn initially containing a red and b blue balls; at each step a ball is drawn and returned together with c additional balls of the same color, producing exchangeable but dependent draws.

nodes.name: Bernoulli trial
nodes.description: A sequence of independent experiments each having exactly two outcomes (success with probability p, failure with probability 1−p); the fundamental building block of discrete probability.

nodes.name: Negative binomial distribution
nodes.description: The distribution of the number of failures before the r-th success in independent Bernoulli trials with success probability p: P(X=k) = C(k+r−1,k) pʳ(1−p)ᵏ.

nodes.name: Covariance
nodes.description: Cov(X,Y) = E[(X−EX)(Y−EY)] = E[XY] − E[X]E[Y], measuring the linear dependence between two random variables.

nodes.name: Standard deviation
nodes.description: σ(X) = √Var(X), the square root of the variance, measuring dispersion in the same units as X.

nodes.name: Probability generating function
nodes.description: G_X(s) = E[sˣ] = Σₖ P(X=k)sᵏ for |s| ≤ 1; encodes the distribution of a non-negative integer-valued random variable and converts convolution to multiplication.

nodes.name: Convolution theorem for PGFs
nodes.description: If X₁,…,Xₙ are independent ℕ-valued random variables, then G_{X₁+⋯+Xₙ}(s) = G_{X₁}(s)⋯G_{Xₙ}(s); independence turns convolution into multiplication of generating functions.

nodes.name: Continuity theorem for probability generating functions
nodes.description: If Gₙ(s) → G(s) for all s ∈ [0,1) and G is a PGF, then the corresponding distributions converge; the PGF analogue of Lévy's continuity theorem.

nodes.name: Random sum (compound distribution)
nodes.description: S_N = X₁ + X₂ + ⋯ + X_N where N is a random variable independent of the i.i.d. summands Xᵢ; its PGF satisfies G_{S_N}(s) = G_N(G_X(s)).

nodes.name: Compound Poisson distribution
nodes.description: The distribution of S_N = Σᵢ₌₁ᴺ Xᵢ where N ~ Poisson(λ) is independent of i.i.d. summands Xᵢ with distribution F; characterized by φ(t) = exp(λ(φ_X(t)−1)).

nodes.name: Criticality classification of branching processes
nodes.description: A Galton–Watson process with offspring mean μ is subcritical if μ < 1, critical if μ = 1, or supercritical if μ > 1; the extinction probability equals 1 iff μ ≤ 1.

nodes.name: Recurrent event (Feller)
nodes.description: An event E occurring at epochs n₁ < n₂ < ⋯ such that the inter-occurrence times are i.i.d.; Feller's axiomatization of renewal phenomena via generating functions.

nodes.name: Persistent (certain) recurrent event
nodes.description: A recurrent event is persistent (certain) if the probability of its eventual occurrence equals 1, i.e., Σₙ fₙ = 1 where fₙ is the first-occurrence probability at time n.

nodes.name: Transient (uncertain) recurrent event
nodes.description: A recurrent event is transient (uncertain) if the probability of its eventual occurrence is strictly less than 1, i.e., Σₙ fₙ < 1.

nodes.name: Periodic and aperiodic recurrent event
nodes.description: The period of a recurrent event is d = gcd{n : fₙ > 0}; the event is periodic if d > 1 and aperiodic if d = 1, where fₙ is the first-occurrence probability at time n.

nodes.name: Renewal equation
nodes.description: The integral equation Z(t) = z(t) + ∫₀ᵗ Z(t−s) dF(s) where F is the inter-renewal distribution; solved by Z = z * U where U is the renewal measure.

nodes.name: Elementary renewal theorem
nodes.description: For a renewal process with inter-arrival mean μ, the expected number of renewals satisfies E[N(t)]/t → 1/μ as t → ∞.

nodes.name: Excess life (residual waiting time)
nodes.description: γ(t) = S_{N(t)+1} − t, the time from t until the next renewal; its asymptotic distribution is (1/μ)∫₀ˣ (1−F(u)) du when the inter-renewal distribution F has mean μ.

nodes.name: Delayed (modified) renewal process
nodes.description: A renewal process in which the first inter-arrival time has a different distribution from the subsequent i.i.d. inter-arrivals; used to construct stationary renewal processes.

nodes.name: Duration of the gambler's ruin
nodes.description: The expected duration of the gambler's ruin game starting with capital a against an opponent with capital b; for p ≠ 1/2, E[D] = (a/(q−p)) − ((a+b)/(q−p)) · (1−(q/p)ᵃ)/(1−(q/p)^{a+b}).

nodes.name: Duality principle for random walks
nodes.function_signature: (Path properties of Sₙ) → (Path properties of Sₙ − Sₙ₋ₖ)
nodes.description: The path (S₁,…,Sₙ) has the same joint distribution as (Sₙ−Sₙ₋₁, Sₙ−Sₙ₋₂,…,Sₙ−S₀), enabling transfer of results about maxima to results about last-visit times.

nodes.name: Aperiodic Markov chain
nodes.description: A Markov chain (or state) is aperiodic if every state has period 1; equivalently, gcd{n ≥ 1 : p^{(n)}(i,i) > 0} = 1 for all states i.

nodes.name: Convergence theorem for periodic Markov chains
nodes.description: For an irreducible positive recurrent chain with period d, the Cesàro average (1/n)Σₖ p^{(k)}(i,j) → π(j) and p^{(nd)}(i,i) → d·π(i) as n → ∞.

nodes.name: Absorption probability
nodes.description: The probability hᵢⱼ = Pᵢ(Xₙ = j for some n) of a Markov chain starting in transient state i being eventually absorbed into absorbing state j, satisfying hᵢⱼ = Σₖ pᵢₖ hₖⱼ.

nodes.name: Mean absorption time
nodes.description: The expected number of steps gᵢ = Eᵢ[T] until an absorbing Markov chain is absorbed, satisfying gᵢ = 1 + Σⱼ pᵢⱼ gⱼ summed over transient states j.

nodes.name: Canonical form for absorbing Markov chains
nodes.function_signature: (Transition matrix P) → (Q, R, N=(I−Q)⁻¹)
nodes.description: Rearranges the transition matrix of an absorbing chain into P = [[Q, R],[0, I]] with Q for transient states and R for absorption; the fundamental matrix N = (I−Q)⁻¹ gives expected visits.

nodes.name: Doubly stochastic matrix
nodes.description: A non-negative matrix whose rows and columns each sum to 1; the stationary distribution of the corresponding Markov chain is the uniform distribution.

nodes.name: Exponential distribution
nodes.description: The continuous distribution with density f(x) = λe^{−λx} for x ≥ 0 and CDF F(x) = 1−e^{−λx}; the unique continuous memoryless distribution with mean 1/λ.

nodes.name: Memoryless property
nodes.description: P(X > s+t | X > s) = P(X > t) for all s,t ≥ 0; characterizes the exponential distribution among continuous distributions and the geometric among discrete distributions.

nodes.name: Superposition of Poisson processes
nodes.description: The superposition (merger) of independent Poisson processes with rates λ₁,…,λₖ is a Poisson process with rate λ₁+⋯+λₖ.

nodes.name: Thinning of a Poisson process
nodes.description: If each arrival of a Poisson process with rate λ is independently retained with probability p, the retained arrivals form a Poisson process with rate λp.

nodes.name: Pure birth process
nodes.description: A continuous-time Markov chain on ℕ with transitions only from n to n+1 at rate λₙ; the simplest continuous-time chain, generalizing the Poisson process (λₙ = λ).

nodes.name: Yule process (pure birth with linear rate)
nodes.description: A pure birth process with birth rate λₙ = nλ, modeling population growth where each individual independently gives birth at rate λ; the population size grows as e^{λt}.

nodes.name: Birth-death process
nodes.description: A continuous-time Markov chain on ℕ with transitions n→n+1 at rate λₙ (birth) and n→n−1 at rate μₙ (death); the canonical model for population dynamics and queueing.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov forward equations
nodes.description: P'(t) = P(t)Q, or p'ᵢⱼ(t) = Σₖ pᵢₖ(t)qₖⱼ, governing the evolution of transition probabilities forward in time; also called the Fokker–Planck equations in the diffusion setting.

nodes.name: Generator matrix (Q-matrix)
nodes.description: The matrix Q with off-diagonal entries qᵢⱼ ≥ 0 (transition rates) and diagonal entries qᵢᵢ = −Σⱼ≠ᵢ qᵢⱼ, satisfying P(t) = e^{tQ}; the infinitesimal description of a continuous-time Markov chain.

nodes.name: Inspection paradox (waiting time paradox)
nodes.description: At a random time t, the inter-renewal interval containing t is stochastically longer than a typical inter-renewal interval, because longer intervals are more likely to contain t; E[γ(t)] → (E[X²])/(2E[X]) > E[X]/2.

nodes.name: Method of generating functions
nodes.function_signature: (Recurrence or convolution equation) → (Closed-form or asymptotic solution)
nodes.description: Translates a recurrence or convolution equation into an algebraic or functional equation for the generating function, solves it, then extracts coefficients.

nodes.name: First-step analysis
nodes.function_signature: (Markov chain, quantity of interest) → (System of linear equations)
nodes.description: Conditions on the first transition of a Markov chain to derive a system of linear equations for hitting probabilities, expected hitting times, or other quantities.

nodes.name: Inversion formula for characteristic functions
nodes.description: F(b) − F(a) = lim_{T→∞} (1/2π) ∫_{−T}^{T} (e^{−ita} − e^{−itb})/(it) φ(t) dt at continuity points a,b of F; recovers the distribution from its characteristic function.

nodes.name: Uniqueness theorem for characteristic functions
nodes.description: Two probability distributions on ℝ are identical if and only if their characteristic functions are identical; φ_X = φ_Y implies X =ᵈ Y.

nodes.name: Gamma distribution
nodes.description: The continuous distribution with density f(x) = β^α x^{α−1} e^{−βx}/Γ(α) for x > 0, generalizing the exponential (α=1) and chi-squared (β=1/2, α=k/2) distributions.

nodes.name: Beta distribution
nodes.description: The continuous distribution on [0,1] with density f(x) = x^{α−1}(1−x)^{β−1}/B(α,β); conjugate prior for the Bernoulli parameter and the distribution of order statistics from the uniform.

nodes.name: Cauchy distribution
nodes.description: The distribution with density f(x) = 1/(πγ(1+((x−x₀)/γ)²)); a stable distribution of index 1 having no finite moments, and the ratio of two independent standard normals.

nodes.name: Continuous uniform distribution
nodes.description: The distribution on [a,b] with constant density f(x) = 1/(b−a); the maximum-entropy distribution on a bounded interval.

nodes.name: Exponential family of distributions
nodes.description: A parametric family with densities f(x|θ) = h(x) exp(η(θ)·T(x) − A(θ)); encompasses normal, exponential, gamma, Poisson, binomial, and many other standard distributions.

nodes.name: F-distribution (Fisher–Snedecor)
nodes.description: The distribution of (U/d₁)/(V/d₂) where U ~ χ²(d₁) and V ~ χ²(d₂) are independent; fundamental in analysis of variance and F-tests.

nodes.name: Lognormal distribution
nodes.description: The distribution of e^X where X ~ N(μ,σ²); equivalently, Y has a lognormal distribution if log Y is normally distributed.

nodes.name: Pareto distribution
nodes.description: The power-law distribution with survival function P(X > x) = (x_m/x)^α for x ≥ x_m; the prototypical heavy-tailed distribution, arising in the study of income and city sizes.

nodes.name: Weibull distribution
nodes.description: The distribution with CDF F(x) = 1 − exp(−(x/λ)ᵏ) for x ≥ 0; generalizes the exponential (k=1) and models failure times with increasing (k>1) or decreasing (k<1) hazard rates.

nodes.name: Logistic distribution
nodes.description: The distribution with CDF F(x) = 1/(1 + e^{−(x−μ)/s}) and bell-shaped density similar to the normal but with heavier tails.

nodes.name: Order statistics
nodes.description: The values X_{(1)} ≤ X_{(2)} ≤ ⋯ ≤ X_{(n)} obtained by sorting a random sample; the joint density of all order statistics from a continuous distribution with density f is n! ∏ f(x_{(i)}).

nodes.name: Marginal distribution
nodes.description: The distribution of a subset of random variables obtained by integrating (or summing) the joint distribution over the remaining variables: f_X(x) = ∫ f_{X,Y}(x,y) dy.

nodes.name: Edgeworth expansion
nodes.description: A refinement of the CLT giving P((Sₙ−nμ)/(σ√n) ≤ x) = Φ(x) + n^{−1/2} p₁(x)φ(x) + n⁻¹ p₂(x)φ(x) + ⋯ where pₖ are polynomials in the cumulants; provides higher-order corrections to the normal approximation.

nodes.name: Saddlepoint approximation
nodes.function_signature: (MGF or CGF of distribution) → (Accurate density/tail approximation)
nodes.description: Approximates the density of Sₙ/n at x by (2πnK''(ŝ))^{−1/2} exp(n(K(ŝ)−ŝx)) where ŝ solves K'(ŝ)=x; yields relative error O(1/n) uniformly in x, far superior to Edgeworth expansions in tails.

nodes.name: Cramér's decomposition theorem
nodes.description: If X + Y is normally distributed and X, Y are independent, then both X and Y are normally distributed; the normal distribution is indecomposable among non-degenerate laws.

nodes.name: Raikov's theorem
nodes.description: If X + Y has a Poisson distribution and X, Y are independent, then both X and Y have Poisson distributions; the Poisson analogue of Cramér's decomposition theorem.

nodes.name: Key renewal theorem
nodes.description: If F is non-lattice with mean μ and z is directly Riemann integrable, then ∫₀^∞ z(t−x)dU(x) → (1/μ)∫₀^∞ z(t)dt as t → ∞; the continuous-time sharpening of the Blackwell renewal theorem.

nodes.name: Age (backward recurrence time)
nodes.description: δ(t) = t − S_{N(t)}, the elapsed time since the last renewal before time t; the backward analogue of the excess life γ(t).

nodes.name: Equilibrium (stationary) renewal distribution
nodes.description: F_e(x) = (1/μ)∫₀ˣ (1−F(t))dt, the distribution whose use as the first inter-arrival time makes the renewal process stationary; also the asymptotic excess-life distribution.

nodes.name: Renewal reward theorem
nodes.description: If rewards Rₙ with E[|Rₙ|] < ∞ accrue at renewal epochs with mean inter-renewal time μ, then the long-run average reward rate converges to E[R]/μ a.s.

nodes.name: Abelian theorem for Laplace transforms
nodes.description: If f(t) ~ Ct^{ρ} as t → ∞, then its Laplace transform satisfies f̂(s) ~ CΓ(ρ+1)/s^{ρ+1} as s → 0⁺; transfers asymptotic information from the original function to the transform.

nodes.name: Regularly varying function
nodes.description: A measurable function f: (0,∞) → (0,∞) satisfying f(tx)/f(x) → t^ρ for every t > 0 as x → ∞, for some ρ ∈ ℝ (the index of regular variation); includes slowly varying functions (ρ=0) as a special case.

nodes.name: Feller semigroup
nodes.description: A strongly continuous positive contraction semigroup {Tₜ} on C₀(E) (continuous functions vanishing at infinity) that maps C₀(E) into itself; the semigroup generated by a Feller process.

nodes.name: Diffusion process
nodes.description: A continuous-path strong Markov process whose generator is a second-order differential operator L = (1/2)σ²(x)d²/dx² + b(x)d/dx; the continuous analogue of a random walk.

nodes.name: Esscher transform (exponential tilting)
nodes.function_signature: (Distribution F, parameter θ) → (Tilted distribution F_θ)
nodes.description: Defines a new probability measure dF_θ(x) = e^{θx} dF(x)/M(θ) where M(θ) = E[e^{θX}] is the MGF; shifts the mean of the distribution and is used for large-deviation estimates and option pricing.

nodes.name: Lévy's inequality
nodes.description: For independent symmetric random variables X₁,…,Xₙ with partial sums Sₖ, P(max_{1≤k≤n} |Sₖ| ≥ λ) ≤ 2P(|Sₙ| ≥ λ); a maximal inequality exploiting symmetry.

nodes.name: Occupation time
nodes.description: The total time a stochastic process spends in a given set: Γ_A(t) = ∫₀ᵗ 1_{X_s ∈ A} ds (continuous time) or Σₖ₌₀ⁿ 1_{Xₖ ∈ A} (discrete time).

nodes.name: Local time for random walk
nodes.description: L(x,n) = #{0 ≤ k ≤ n : Sₖ = x}, the number of visits to site x by the random walk up to time n; for the simple symmetric walk, the arc-sine law governs the fraction of time spent positive.

nodes.name: Resolvent of a Markov process
nodes.description: R_λ f(x) = E_x[∫₀^∞ e^{−λt} f(X_t) dt], the Laplace transform of the semigroup; satisfies the resolvent equation R_λ − R_μ = (μ−λ)R_λ R_μ and determines the process uniquely.

nodes.name: Lévy–Khintchine triplet
nodes.description: The triple (γ, σ², ν) where γ ∈ ℝ is the drift, σ² ≥ 0 the Gaussian variance, and ν a Lévy measure, uniquely characterizing an infinitely divisible distribution via its Lévy–Khintchine exponent.

nodes.name: Compound Poisson representation of infinitely divisible laws
nodes.description: Every infinitely divisible distribution is a weak limit of compound Poisson distributions; equivalently, its Lévy–Khintchine exponent can be approximated by compound Poisson exponents.

nodes.name: Maximal coupling
