nodes.description: A coupling (X,Y) of distributions μ and ν that maximizes P(X=Y), achieving P(X≠Y) = ‖μ−ν‖_{TV}; optimal for bounding total variation distance.

nodes.name: Symmetrization inequality
nodes.description: P(|Sₙ − ESₙ| > t) ≤ 2P(|S̃ₙ| > t/2) where S̃ₙ = Σ(Xᵢ − X'ᵢ) is the symmetrized sum with independent copies X'ᵢ; reduces tail bounds to the symmetric case.

nodes.name: Record values
nodes.description: X_{n} is an upper record if X_{n} > max(X₁,…,X_{n−1}); for i.i.d. continuous observations, record times form a renewal process with E[number of records in n trials] = Σₖ₌₁ⁿ 1/k ~ ln n.

nodes.name: Characteristic function inversion formula on a lattice
nodes.description: For a lattice distribution with span h, P(X = a+kh) = (h/2π) ∫_{−π/h}^{π/h} e^{−it(a+kh)} φ(t) dt; the discrete analogue of the Fourier inversion formula.

nodes.name: Type (convergence of types)
nodes.description: Two distributions F and G are of the same type if G(x) = F(ax+b) for constants a > 0, b; the convergence-of-types theorem states that if (Sₙ−bₙ)/aₙ →ᵈ F and (Sₙ−b'ₙ)/a'ₙ →ᵈ G with F non-degenerate, then F and G are of the same type.

nodes.name: Classification of stable laws (Lévy)
nodes.description: Every stable distribution is characterized by four parameters: index α ∈ (0,2], skewness β ∈ [−1,1], scale γ > 0, and location δ ∈ ℝ, with characteristic exponent −γ^α|t|^α(1−iβ sgn(t)tan(πα/2)) + iδt.

nodes.name: Operator stable distribution
nodes.description: A distribution μ on ℝᵈ such that for each n there exist matrices Aₙ and vectors bₙ with μⁿ = μ ∘ Aₙ⁻¹ * δ_{bₙ}; the multivariate generalization of stable laws where scalar normalization is replaced by linear operators.

nodes.name: Subexponential distribution
nodes.description: A distribution F on [0,∞) with P(X₁+X₂ > x)/P(X₁ > x) → 2 as x → ∞ (for i.i.d. X₁,X₂ ~ F); the tail of the sum is dominated by the maximum, implying P(Sₙ > x) ~ nP(X > x).

nodes.name: Self-decomposable distribution
nodes.description: A distribution μ is self-decomposable (class L) if for every c ∈ (0,1) there exists a distribution μ_c with μ = (μ scaled by c) * μ_c; equivalently, it is the limit law of normed sums of independent (not necessarily identically distributed) random variables.

nodes.name: Ehrenfest urn model (diffusion model)
nodes.description: A Markov chain on {0,1,…,N} modeling diffusion: at each step, one of N balls is chosen uniformly and moved to the other urn, so the chain transitions from k to k+1 with probability (N−k)/N and to k−1 with probability k/N.

nodes.name: Ruin probability on the half-line
nodes.description: For a random walk with negative drift, the probability P(sup_{n≥0} Sₙ ≥ x) of ever exceeding level x, which decreases exponentially in x when the adjustment coefficient exists: P(Sₙ ≥ x for some n) ≤ e^{−Rx}.

nodes.name: Fourier analysis on locally compact abelian groups
nodes.description: The extension of Fourier analysis to locally compact abelian groups via the dual group Ĝ: the Fourier transform of a measure μ is μ̂(χ) = ∫ χ(x) dμ(x), and convolution of measures corresponds to pointwise multiplication of transforms.

nodes.name: Domain of normal attraction
nodes.description: A distribution F belongs to the domain of normal attraction of a stable law G_α if (S_n − bn)/n^{1/α} →ᵈ G_α with the specific normalization n^{1/α}; a strict subset of the full domain of attraction requiring regular tail behavior.

nodes.name: n-step transition probability
nodes.description: The probability p^{(n)}(x,y) = P_x(X_n = y) of reaching state y from state x in exactly n steps; the (x,y)-entry of P^n.

nodes.name: Initial distribution of a Markov chain
nodes.description: A probability measure μ on the state space E that, together with the transition matrix P, uniquely determines the law of the Markov chain.

nodes.function_signature: (Transition matrix P, initial distribution μ) → (Probability measure on E^ℕ)
nodes.name: Canonical construction of a Markov chain
nodes.description: Constructs the Markov chain on the canonical path space Ω = E^ℕ with coordinate maps X_n(ω) = ω_n, using the Kolmogorov extension theorem to build the unique measure P_μ.

nodes.name: Accessibility (leads to) in a Markov chain
nodes.description: State y is accessible from state x (written x → y) if p^{(n)}(x,y) > 0 for some n ≥ 0; the fundamental asymmetric reachability relation on the state space.

nodes.name: Closed (absorbing) set in a Markov chain
nodes.description: A nonempty subset C of the state space is closed if p(x,y) = 0 for all x ∈ C, y ∉ C; equivalently, C is absorbing — once the chain enters C it never leaves.

nodes.name: Solidarity of period
nodes.description: All states in the same communication class have the same period; hence the period is a class property, and one may speak of the period of an irreducible chain.

nodes.name: Cyclic decomposition of a periodic chain
nodes.description: For an irreducible chain of period d, the state space decomposes into d cyclic classes C_0, ..., C_{d-1} such that from any state in C_r the chain moves to C_{r+1 mod d} in one step.

nodes.name: Essential and inessential states
nodes.description: A state x is essential if for every state y accessible from x, x is also accessible from y; otherwise x is inessential (transient).

nodes.name: First return time decomposition
nodes.description: The first return probabilities f^{(n)}(x,x) = P_x(T_x = n) satisfy the renewal equation p^{(n)}(x,x) = Σ_{k=1}^n f^{(k)}(x,x) p^{(n-k)}(x,x), linking n-step return probabilities to first return probabilities.

nodes.name: Recurrence criterion via Green function
nodes.description: A state x is recurrent if and only if G(x,x) = Σ_{n=0}^∞ p^{(n)}(x,x) = ∞, and transient if and only if G(x,x) < ∞.

nodes.name: Solidarity of positive/null recurrence
nodes.description: Positive recurrence and null recurrence are class properties: if one state in a communication class is positive (resp. null) recurrent, then all states in the class are.

nodes.name: Chung-Fuchs theorem
nodes.description: A random walk on ℝ^d with mean-zero i.i.d. increments is recurrent if d ≤ 2 and transient if d ≥ 3; recurrence is determined by the integrability of Re(1/(1-φ(t))) near 0, where φ is the characteristic function.

nodes.name: Number of visits to a transient state
nodes.description: For a transient state x, the total number of visits N_x started from x has a geometric distribution with parameter f(x,x) = P_x(T_x < ∞); hence E_x[N_x] = G(x,x) = 1/(1 - f(x,x)).

nodes.name: Invariant measure for a Markov chain
nodes.description: A σ-finite measure μ on the state space satisfying μP = μ; generalizes the stationary distribution to the σ-finite setting, essential for null recurrent chains.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of invariant measure for irreducible recurrent chains
nodes.description: An irreducible recurrent Markov chain admits a unique (up to scalar multiples) invariant measure μ, given by μ(y) = E_x[Σ_{k=0}^{T_x-1} 1_{X_k = y}] for any reference state x.

nodes.name: Ratio limit theorem (Chung-Erdős-Orey form)
nodes.description: For an irreducible recurrent chain, p^{(n)}(x,y)/p^{(n)}(x,z) → μ(y)/μ(z) as n → ∞ along multiples of the period, where μ is the invariant measure.

nodes.name: Cesàro convergence for Markov chains
nodes.description: For an irreducible positive recurrent chain with stationary distribution π, (1/n) Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} p^{(k)}(x,y) → π(y) as n → ∞, regardless of periodicity.

nodes.name: Orey's convergence theorem
nodes.description: For an irreducible, aperiodic, positive recurrent Markov chain, ‖P^n(x,·) − π(·)‖_{TV} → 0 as n → ∞ for all x; convergence to stationarity holds in total variation distance.

nodes.name: Doeblin's condition
nodes.description: There exist n₀ ≥ 1, ε > 0, and a probability measure φ such that P^{n₀}(x,A) ≥ εφ(A) for all states x and measurable sets A; a strong uniform mixing condition ensuring geometric ergodicity.

nodes.function_signature: (General Markov chain) → (Ergodic classes + transient set)
nodes.name: Doeblin decomposition
nodes.description: Decomposes the state space into at most countably many ergodic classes plus a transient set; every initial distribution eventually concentrates on the ergodic classes.

nodes.name: Geometric ergodicity
nodes.description: An ergodic Markov chain is geometrically ergodic if ‖P^n(x,·) − π(·)‖_{TV} ≤ C(x)ρⁿ for some ρ < 1; exponential convergence to the stationary distribution in total variation.

nodes.name: Taboo probability
nodes.description: The taboo transition probability ₐp^{(n)}(x,y) = P_x(X_n = y, X_k ∉ A for 1 ≤ k ≤ n-1), the probability of going from x to y in n steps while avoiding set A.

nodes.name: Taboo Green function
nodes.description: The expected number of visits to y starting from x while avoiding set A: ₐG(x,y) = Σ_{n=0}^∞ ₐp^{(n)}(x,y); a restricted potential kernel fundamental to decomposition theorems.

nodes.name: Last exit decomposition
nodes.description: The Green function decomposes via the last visit to an intermediate state z: G(x,y) = Σ_z G(x,z)·f(z,y) using taboo probabilities; dually G(x,y) = Σ_z f(x,z)·G(z,y).

nodes.name: Harmonic function for a Markov chain
nodes.description: A function h: E → ℝ satisfying Ph = h, i.e., h(x) = Σ_y p(x,y)h(y) for all x; the discrete analogue of harmonic functions, with h(X_n) forming a martingale.

nodes.name: Liouville property for recurrent Markov chains
nodes.description: An irreducible recurrent Markov chain has no non-constant bounded harmonic functions; every bounded function h with Ph = h is constant.

nodes.function_signature: (MC, domain D, boundary function f) → (Harmonic function on D with boundary values f)
nodes.name: Discrete Dirichlet problem
nodes.description: Solves for the unique function h harmonic on D with h = f on ∂D via h(x) = E_x[f(X_{τ_{∂D}})]; the probabilistic solution of discrete boundary value problems.

nodes.name: Superharmonic functions and optional stopping
nodes.description: If h is superharmonic (Ph ≤ h) for a Markov chain, then h(X_n) is a supermartingale; optional stopping yields h(x) ≥ E_x[h(X_τ)] for stopping times τ.

nodes.name: Potential kernel (deviation matrix) for recurrent chains
nodes.description: The deviation matrix A(x,y) = Σ_{n=0}^∞ [p^{(n)}(x,y) − π(y)], measuring cumulative deviation from equilibrium; the analogue of the Green function in the recurrent setting.

nodes.name: Potential of a charge (recurrent chain)
nodes.description: For a signed measure ν with ν(E) = 0, the potential Uν(x) = Σ_y A(x,y)ν(y) where A is the deviation matrix; the discrete analogue of the potential of a balanced charge.

nodes.name: Green kernel for transient Markov chains
nodes.description: G(x,y) = Σ_{n=0}^∞ p^{(n)}(x,y) = E_x[number of visits to y], finite for transient chains; the kernel for the potential operator Gf(x) = Σ_y G(x,y)f(y).

nodes.name: Riesz decomposition for Markov chains
nodes.description: Every non-negative superharmonic function on a transient Markov chain decomposes uniquely as h = Gν + f where Gν is a potential (ν ≥ 0) and f is harmonic.

nodes.name: Excessive function (α-excessive)
nodes.description: A non-negative function f satisfying αPf ≤ f and α^n P^n f(x) → f(x) for all x; when α = 1, these are the non-negative superharmonic functions with a regularity condition.

nodes.name: Characterization of excessive functions
nodes.description: A non-negative function f is excessive iff Pf ≤ f and P^n f → f pointwise; equivalently, f is the pointwise limit of an increasing sequence of potentials.

nodes.name: Minimum principle for excessive functions
nodes.description: If an excessive function f dominates a potential g outside a finite set, then f ≥ g everywhere; the dual of the maximum principle for subharmonic functions.

nodes.name: Domination principle for potentials
nodes.description: If Gμ ≤ Gν on the support of μ, then Gμ ≤ Gν everywhere; the discrete analogue of the classical domination principle in potential theory.

nodes.name: Cone of excessive functions
nodes.description: The set of all excessive functions for a Markov chain, forming a convex cone closed under pointwise infima and increasing limits; the fundamental object of probabilistic potential theory.

nodes.name: Energy of a measure (discrete potential theory)
nodes.description: ℰ(μ) = ⟨μ, Gμ⟩ = Σ_{x,y} μ(x)G(x,y)μ(y), the mutual energy of measure μ under the Green kernel G of a transient chain.

nodes.name: Dirichlet form (discrete Markov chain)
nodes.description: The quadratic form ℰ(f,f) = (1/2) Σ_{x,y} π(x)p(x,y)(f(x)−f(y))² measuring energy dissipation; for reversible chains, connected to the spectral gap.

nodes.name: Capacity of a set (discrete Markov chain)
nodes.description: Cap(A) = Σ_{x∈A} e_A(x) where e_A is the equilibrium measure; measures the ease with which the chain hits A and characterizes transience vs. recurrence.

nodes.name: Equilibrium measure (discrete potential theory)
nodes.description: The unique measure e_A on A such that Ge_A(x) = P_x(T_A < ∞) for transient chains; the charge distribution on A generating the hitting probability as its potential.

nodes.name: Equilibrium potential (discrete Markov chain)
nodes.description: h_A(x) = P_x(T_A < ∞) = Ge_A(x); an excessive function equal to 1 on A, the unique smallest excessive function dominating 1_A.

nodes.name: Capacity and transience criterion
nodes.description: A state is transient if and only if it has positive capacity; a Markov chain is transient iff Cap({x}) > 0 for some (hence all, in the irreducible case) states.

nodes.name: Energy principle (discrete potential theory)
nodes.description: The energy ℰ(μ) = ⟨μ, Gμ⟩ is minimized over probability measures on A by the normalized equilibrium measure; the minimum equals 1/Cap(A).

nodes.function_signature: (Excessive function f, set A) → (Réduite R_A f)
nodes.name: Balayage (sweeping) for Markov chains
nodes.description: Sweeps an excessive function f onto a set A, producing the réduite R_A f(x) = E_x[f(X_{T_A})], the smallest excessive function dominating f on A.

nodes.type_signature: (MC, excessive f, set A) → Excessive function
nodes.name: Réduite (reduced function) for Markov chains
nodes.description: R_A f(x) = inf{g(x) : g excessive, g ≥ f on A}, the smallest excessive function that dominates f on A; equals E_x[f(X_{T_A})].

nodes.name: Balayage of a measure (discrete potential theory)
nodes.description: The swept measure μ^A representing the distribution of the chain started with measure μ and stopped upon hitting A.

nodes.name: Balayage principle for Markov chains
nodes.description: For every excessive function f and set A, the réduite R_A f is excessive, equals f on A (up to a polar set), and is harmonic on A^c.

nodes.name: Hunt's balayage theorem
nodes.description: Every excessive function is the supremum of potentials of measures it dominates; gives a complete representation theory for the cone of excessive functions.

nodes.name: Continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC)
nodes.description: A continuous-time stochastic process (X_t)_{t≥0} on a countable state space satisfying the Markov property with time-homogeneous transition rates given by a Q-matrix.

nodes.name: Transition semigroup of a CTMC
nodes.description: The family {P(t)}_{t≥0} of transition matrices satisfying P(s+t) = P(s)P(t), P(0) = I, encoding transition probabilities of a continuous-time Markov chain.

nodes.name: Holding time of a CTMC
nodes.description: The time spent in state i before jumping, exponentially distributed with rate q_i = -q_{ii}; the memoryless property ensures the Markov property in continuous time.

nodes.name: Jump chain (embedded chain) of a CTMC
nodes.description: The discrete-time Markov chain recording successive states visited by the CTMC, with transition probabilities p̃(i,j) = q_{ij}/q_i; together with holding times, determines the CTMC.

nodes.name: Minimal solution of the Kolmogorov equations
nodes.description: The smallest non-negative solution to both Kolmogorov equations, constructed via successive approximations; honest iff no explosion occurs.

nodes.name: Explosion of a CTMC
nodes.description: The event that infinitely many jumps occur in finite time (ζ = lim J_n < ∞); when explosion occurs, the minimal chain is dishonest (Σ_y p_t(x,y) < 1).

nodes.name: Non-explosion criterion for CTMCs
nodes.description: A CTMC is non-explosive if Σ_n 1/q_{Y_n} = ∞ a.s.; sufficient conditions include uniform boundedness of rates or existence of a Lyapunov function f with Qf ≤ cf.

nodes.function_signature: (CTMC with bounded rates) → (Poisson-subordinated discrete chain)
nodes.name: Uniformization of a CTMC
nodes.description: Represents a CTMC with bounded rates as P(t) = e^{-qt} Σ (qt)^n/n! · P̃^n where P̃ = I + Q/q; reduces analysis to a Poisson-subordinated discrete chain.

nodes.name: Resolvent as λ-potential kernel
nodes.description: R_λ(x,y) = ∫_0^∞ e^{-λt} p(t,x,y) dt; the λ-potential kernel generalizing the Green function, with R_λ f = E_x[∫_0^∞ e^{-λt} f(X_t) dt].

nodes.name: λ-excessive function
nodes.description: A non-negative function f with e^{-λt} P_t f ≤ f for all t ≥ 0 and e^{-λt} P_t f → f as t ↓ 0; the natural class for resolvent potential theory.

nodes.name: Resolvent characterization of λ-excessive functions
nodes.description: A non-negative function f is λ-excessive iff αR_{λ+α} f ↑ f as α → ∞; equivalently, f is the pointwise supremum of λ-potentials.

nodes.name: Potential operator for continuous-time processes
nodes.description: Gf(x) = E_x[∫_0^∞ f(X_t) dt] = lim_{λ↓0} R_λ f(x); the continuous-time analogue of the discrete Green kernel, defined for transient processes.

nodes.name: Recovery of semigroup from resolvent
nodes.description: The transition semigroup is uniquely determined by the resolvent family via P_t f = lim (nR_{n/t})^{[nt]} f or Laplace inversion; content of the Hille-Yosida generation theorem.

nodes.name: Recurrence and transience for CTMCs
nodes.description: A CTMC state is recurrent if ∫_0^∞ p_t(x,x) dt = ∞ (returns a.s.) and transient if the integral is finite; recurrence/transience are class properties.

nodes.name: Invariant measure for a CTMC
nodes.description: A σ-finite measure π satisfying πQ = 0, equivalently πP(t) = π for all t ≥ 0; unique up to scalar for irreducible recurrent CTMCs.

nodes.name: Ergodic theorem for CTMCs
nodes.description: For an irreducible positive recurrent CTMC with stationary distribution π, (1/t)∫_0^t f(X_s) ds → Σ_x f(x)π(x) a.s. and p_t(x,y) → π(y) as t → ∞.

nodes.name: Green function for continuous-time processes
nodes.description: G(x,y) = ∫_0^∞ p_t(x,y) dt = E_x[total time at y]; the continuous-time Green function, finite when the process is transient.

nodes.name: Riesz decomposition for continuous-time processes
nodes.description: Every non-negative excessive function for a transient process decomposes uniquely as f = Gμ + h where Gμ is a potential and h is harmonic.

nodes.name: Capacity for continuous-time processes
nodes.description: Cap(A) = sup{μ(A) : supp(μ) ⊂ A, Gμ ≤ 1}; measures the size of A from the process's perspective, related to hitting probabilities and equilibrium measures.

nodes.name: Hunt process
nodes.description: A strong Markov process with right-continuous paths and quasi-left-continuity; the standard framework for probabilistic potential theory, generalizing Feller processes.

nodes.name: Quasi-left-continuity
nodes.description: For every increasing sequence of stopping times T_n ↑ T, X_{T_n} → X_T a.s. on {T < ∞}; prevents jumps at predictable times and is the key regularity assumption for Hunt processes.

nodes.name: Additive functional
nodes.description: A non-decreasing right-continuous process A_t with A_0 = 0 satisfying A_{t+s} = A_t + A_s ∘ θ_t; the building block for time changes and Revuz correspondence.

nodes.name: Revuz measure
nodes.description: The unique σ-finite measure μ_A associated to a positive continuous additive functional via lim_{t↓0} (1/t) E_m[∫_0^t f(X_s) dA_s] = ∫ f dμ_A.

nodes.name: Revuz correspondence
nodes.description: A bijection between positive continuous additive functionals (up to equivalence) and smooth measures via the Revuz measure; a cornerstone connecting additive functionals, Dirichlet forms, and measures.

nodes.name: Fine topology
nodes.description: The coarsest topology making all excessive functions continuous; the natural topology for potential theory, in which thin sets are precisely those of capacity zero.

nodes.function_signature: (MarkovProcess X_t, continuous additive functional A_t) → (New MarkovProcess Y_s = X_{τ_s})
nodes.name: Time change of a Markov process
nodes.description: Defines Y_s = X_{τ_s} where τ_s = inf{t : A_t > s}; the time-changed process is again a strong Markov process with transformed generator and state space.

nodes.function_signature: (MarkovProcess X_t, multiplicative functional M_t) → (Subprocess)
nodes.name: Killing and subprocess construction
nodes.description: Constructs a subprocess by killing X_t via a multiplicative functional M_t, yielding semigroup P̃_t f(x) = E_x[M_t f(X_t)]; amounts to modifying the generator by a killing rate.

nodes.function_signature: (MC, regeneration point) → (Renewal equation/asymptotics)
nodes.name: Renewal argument for Markov chains
nodes.description: Exploits regenerative structure at return times to a recurrent state, reducing long-run averages and limit theorems to renewal theory.

nodes.function_signature: (MC, recurrent state x) → (Cycle decomposition)
nodes.name: Cycle trick for Markov chains
nodes.description: Decomposes the trajectory into i.i.d. excursions from a reference state, enabling the law of large numbers, CLT, and large deviations for additive functionals.

nodes.function_signature: (Two MC copies, Doeblin condition) → (Coupling time bound)
nodes.name: Doeblin's coupling method
nodes.description: Runs two copies of a Markov chain exploiting Doeblin's condition to ensure coalescence in bounded expected time; yields geometric convergence bounds.

nodes.function_signature: (MC, Lyapunov function V, drift condition) → (Positive recurrence/Geometric ergodicity)
nodes.name: Lyapunov function method (Foster's criterion)
nodes.description: Establishes positive recurrence or geometric ergodicity via a Lyapunov function V with PV ≤ V − ε outside a finite set; the drift condition PV ≤ λV + b·1_C with λ < 1 gives geometric ergodicity.

nodes.name: Foster-Lyapunov criterion for geometric ergodicity
nodes.description: An irreducible aperiodic chain is geometrically ergodic if PV ≤ λV + b·1_C for V ≥ 1, λ < 1, b < ∞, and finite C; the convergence rate depends on λ.

nodes.function_signature: (MC, forbidden set A) → (Restricted transition analysis)
nodes.name: Taboo probability technique
nodes.description: Analyzes the chain via transition probabilities conditioned on avoiding a set, yielding restricted Green functions and decomposition formulas for passage times and potentials.

nodes.name: Harris recurrence
nodes.description: An irreducible chain on a general state space is Harris recurrent if every set A with ψ(A) > 0 is visited infinitely often a.s., where ψ is the irreducibility measure; the correct generalization of recurrence to uncountable spaces.

nodes.function_signature: (MC, positive harmonic function h) → (h-transformed MC)
nodes.name: Doob's h-transform
nodes.description: Defines the transformed kernel P^h(x,y) = h(y)p(x,y)/h(x), yielding a new Markov chain; used to condition on events of probability zero such as never hitting a set.

nodes.name: Martin boundary
nodes.description: A compactification of the state space via the Martin kernel K(x,y) = G(x,y)/G(x₀,y); boundary points represent extremal harmonic functions and classify all positive harmonic functions.

nodes.name: Martin representation theorem
nodes.description: Every positive harmonic function h for a transient chain has a unique representation h(x) = ∫_{∂_m} K(x,ξ) dν_h(ξ) over the minimal Martin boundary; the probabilistic Poisson integral formula.

nodes.name: Convergence parameter
nodes.description: R = sup{r ≥ 0 : Σ_n r^n p^{(n)}(x,y) < ∞}; the radius of convergence of the Green function series, independent of x,y for irreducible chains, classifying the chain as R-recurrent or R-transient.

nodes.name: R-recurrence and R-transience
nodes.description: An irreducible chain is R-recurrent if Σ_n R^n p^{(n)}(x,y) = ∞ and R-transient if finite, where R is the convergence parameter; generalizes ordinary recurrence and determines existence of R-invariant measures.

nodes.name: Solidarity theorem (general form)
nodes.description: For an irreducible chain, the convergence parameter R and the R-recurrence/R-transience classification are the same for all pairs (x,y); a unifying solidarity result encompassing period, recurrence, and convergence parameter.

nodes.name: Birth-death chain (discrete time)
nodes.description: A discrete-time Markov chain on ℕ with transitions only to nearest neighbors: p(n,n+1) = p_n, p(n,n−1) = q_n; the simplest non-trivial class admitting explicit formulas for hitting times, stationary distributions, and spectral properties.

nodes.function_signature: (Set of return times {n : p^{(n)}(x,x) > 0}) → (Period d = gcd)
nodes.name: Subadditive argument for period
nodes.description: Uses closure under addition of {n : p^{(n)}(x,x) > 0} and supermultiplicativity of transition probabilities to establish periodicity results and solidarity of period.

nodes.name: Wiener test (discrete potential theory)
nodes.description: A point z is regular for the discrete Dirichlet problem iff Σ_n Cap(A_n ∩ D^c)/Cap(A_n) = ∞ for annuli A_n around z; the discrete analogue of Wiener's regularity criterion.

nodes.name: Markov kernel (transition kernel on measurable space)
nodes.description: A function P: X × B(X) → [0,1] such that P(x, ·) is a probability measure for each x and P(·, A) is measurable for each A; the general-state-space analogue of a transition probability matrix.

nodes.name: φ-irreducibility (general state space)
nodes.description: A Markov chain with kernel P on measurable space (X, B(X)) is φ-irreducible if there exists a non-trivial σ-finite measure φ such that for every x ∈ X and every A with φ(A) > 0, there exists n ≥ 1 with P^n(x, A) > 0.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of maximal irreducibility measure
nodes.description: For a φ-irreducible chain, there exists a unique (up to equivalence) maximal irreducibility measure ψ such that every other irreducibility measure is absolutely continuous with respect to ψ.

nodes.name: Small set (Meyn-Tweedie)
nodes.description: A set C ∈ B(X) is (ν_m, m)-small for kernel P if P^m(x, A) ≥ ν_m(A) for all x ∈ C and A ∈ B(X), where ν_m is a non-trivial measure; the existence of small sets is the key structural property of φ-irreducible chains.

nodes.name: Petite set
nodes.description: A set C is petite if there exists a probability distribution a on ℤ₊ and a non-trivial measure ν_a such that the sampled kernel K_a(x, ·) = Σ_n a(n) P^n(x, ·) ≥ ν_a(·) for all x ∈ C; every small set is petite, and petite sets are the natural class for drift criteria.

nodes.name: Sampled chain (sampling distribution)
nodes.description: Given kernel P and a probability distribution a on ℤ₊, the sampled kernel K_a = Σ_n a(n) P^n averages transition probabilities over the sampling distribution; used to regularize periodicity and define petite sets.

nodes.name: Atom (general state space Markov chain)
nodes.description: A set α ∈ B⁺(X) is an atom for the kernel P if there exists a non-trivial measure ν such that P(x, ·) = ν(·) for all x ∈ α; the chain regenerates at each visit to α, enabling renewal-theoretic arguments.

nodes.name: Minorization condition
nodes.description: There exist a set C, an integer m ≥ 1, a constant δ > 0, and a probability measure ν such that P^m(x, B) ≥ δ ν(B) for all x ∈ C and B ∈ B(X); the fundamental condition enabling regeneration and coupling constructions for general state spaces.

nodes.name: Aperiodicity (φ-irreducible chain)
nodes.description: A φ-irreducible chain is aperiodic if the gcd of {n ≥ 1 : C is (ν_n, n)-small for some ν_n} equals 1 for some small set C; equivalently, the chain has period d = 1 in the general state space sense.

nodes.name: T-chain
nodes.description: A Markov chain whose sampled kernel K_a for some sampling distribution a has a non-trivial continuous component: K_a(x, ·) ≥ T(x, ·) where T(x, ·) is a non-trivial kernel with x ↦ T(x, A) lower semicontinuous for all A; T-chains have every compact set petite.

nodes.name: e-chain (equicontinuous chain)
nodes.description: A Markov chain on a topological state space such that the family of transition kernels {P^n(x, ·) : n ≥ 0} is equicontinuous at every x in the weak topology; e-chains are T-chains with strong structural properties including uniqueness of invariant measures on compact sets.

nodes.name: Feller property (Markov chain on topological space)
nodes.description: A Markov chain has the (weak) Feller property if Pf is continuous whenever f is bounded and continuous; equivalently, P(x, ·) is weakly continuous in x.

nodes.name: Strong Feller property
nodes.description: A Markov kernel P has the strong Feller property if Pf is continuous for every bounded measurable f; implies that the chain has a transition density with respect to some reference measure and ensures absolute continuity of P(x, ·) in x.

nodes.name: Skeleton chain
nodes.description: The discrete-time chain (X_{nδ})_{n≥0} obtained by sampling a continuous-time process at intervals of length δ; used to transfer discrete-time results (φ-irreducibility, drift criteria) to continuous-time settings.

nodes.name: Occupation measure (Markov chain)
nodes.description: The random measure η_n = (1/n) Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} δ_{X_k} recording the empirical fraction of time spent in each set; its almost-sure convergence to the invariant probability is the content of the ergodic theorem for Markov chains.

nodes.name: Recurrence-transience dichotomy (general state space)
nodes.description: A φ-irreducible chain is either Harris recurrent or transient; there is no intermediate behavior, paralleling the classical result for countable chains.

nodes.name: Positive Harris recurrence
nodes.description: A Harris recurrent chain is positive Harris recurrent if it admits a finite invariant measure (equivalently, an invariant probability measure π); this is the correct notion ensuring both the ergodic theorem and convergence in total variation for general state space chains.

nodes.name: Kac's theorem (general state space)
nodes.description: For a positive Harris recurrent chain with invariant probability π and a set A with π(A) > 0, the expected return time satisfies E_π[τ_A | X_0 ∈ A] = 1/π(A).

nodes.name: Foster's drift criterion for recurrence (general state space)
nodes.description: A φ-irreducible chain is Harris recurrent if there exists a petite set C and a function V ≥ 0 with V(x) → ∞ as x leaves compact sets such that PV(x) ≤ V(x) for all x ∉ C.

nodes.name: Drift criterion for transience
nodes.description: A φ-irreducible chain is transient if there exists a non-negative function V, a set A with ψ(A) > 0, and ε > 0 such that PV(x) ≥ V(x) + ε for all x ∉ A and V is bounded on A.

nodes.name: Foster's drift criterion for positive recurrence (general state space)
nodes.description: A φ-irreducible aperiodic chain is positive Harris recurrent if there exists a petite set C, a function V ≥ 1, and ε > 0 such that PV(x) ≤ V(x) − ε for x ∉ C and V is bounded on C.

nodes.name: Ergodicity (Meyn-Tweedie sense)
nodes.description: A positive Harris recurrent, aperiodic chain is ergodic: ‖P^n(x, ·) − π(·)‖_{TV} → 0 as n → ∞ for all x.

nodes.name: Uniform ergodicity
nodes.description: A chain is uniformly ergodic if sup_x ‖P^n(x, ·) − π(·)‖_{TV} → 0 as n → ∞ at geometric rate; equivalently, the entire state space is a small set, or Doeblin's condition holds.

nodes.name: Geometric ergodicity (general state space, V-norm)
nodes.description: A φ-irreducible aperiodic chain is V-geometrically ergodic if there exist r > 1 and V ≥ 1 such that ‖P^n(x, ·) − π(·)‖_V ≤ V(x)r^{−n}; characterized by the drift condition PV ≤ λV + b·1_C with λ < 1.

nodes.name: V-norm (f-norm) for measures
nodes.description: For a measurable function V ≥ 1 and a signed measure μ, the V-norm is ‖μ‖_V = sup{|∫ f dμ| : |f| ≤ V}; the natural norm for measuring convergence rates in ergodic theorems, with V = 1 recovering total variation.

nodes.name: Subgeometric ergodicity
nodes.description: A chain is subgeometrically ergodic if ‖P^n(x, ·) − π(·)‖_V ≤ V(x) r(n) where r(n) → 0 slower than any geometric rate; arises from drift conditions PV ≤ V − φ(V) + b·1_C with concave φ.

nodes.name: Polynomial ergodicity
nodes.description: A chain is polynomially ergodic of order β > 0 if ‖P^n(x, ·) − π(·)‖_V = O(n^{−β}) as n → ∞; corresponds to drift conditions with φ(v) = cv^{1−1/α} and arises in heavy-tailed models and random walks.

nodes.name: Drift criterion for geometric ergodicity (general state space)
nodes.description: A φ-irreducible aperiodic chain is geometrically ergodic in the V-norm if and only if there exist V ≥ 1, λ ∈ (0,1), b < ∞, and a petite set C such that PV(x) ≤ λV(x) + b·1_C(x).

nodes.name: Drift criterion for subgeometric ergodicity
nodes.description: If PV ≤ V − φ(V) + b·1_C for a petite set C, V ≥ 1, and a concave non-decreasing function φ with φ(v)/v → 0, then the chain is subgeometrically ergodic at rate determined by the inverse of φ.

nodes.name: Law of large numbers for Harris recurrent chains
nodes.description: For a positive Harris recurrent chain with invariant probability π and f ∈ L¹(π), (1/n) Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} f(X_k) → π(f) almost surely for every initial condition.

nodes.name: Central limit theorem for Harris recurrent chains
nodes.description: For a geometrically ergodic chain with invariant probability π and f with π(f²) < ∞, n^{1/2}((1/n) Σ f(X_k) − π(f)) converges in distribution to N(0, σ²_f).

nodes.name: Law of the iterated logarithm for Harris chains
nodes.description: For a geometrically ergodic Harris chain with π(|f|^{2+δ}) < ∞, limsup |Σ(f(X_k) − π(f))| / √(2nσ²_f log log n) = 1 almost surely, provided σ²_f > 0.

nodes.name: Asymptotic variance (Markov chain CLT)
nodes.description: The quantity σ²_f = lim n · Var_π((1/n) Σ f(X_k)) = π((f − π(f))²) + 2 Σ_{k≥1} π((f − π(f)) P^k(f − π(f))); determines the CLT scaling.

nodes.name: Kendall's theorem (uniform ergodicity characterization)
nodes.description: An irreducible aperiodic chain is uniformly ergodic if and only if the whole state space is petite (or small), equivalently if a Doeblin-type minorization condition holds on all of X.

nodes.name: Harris' ergodic theorem
nodes.description: If a φ-irreducible, aperiodic chain is positive Harris recurrent with invariant probability π, then ‖P^n(x, ·) − π‖_{TV} → 0 as n → ∞ for every x.

nodes.name: Comparison theorem for drift functions
nodes.description: If two kernels P₁, P₂ share the same small set structure and P₁V ≤ P₂V pointwise for a Lyapunov function V, then ergodicity properties established for P₂ transfer to P₁.

nodes.name: Multiplicative mean drift criterion (geometric case)
nodes.description: For a φ-irreducible chain, if E[V(X_{n+1})/V(X_n) | X_n = x] ≤ λ < 1 for x outside a petite set C with V bounded on C, then the chain is geometrically ergodic.

nodes.name: Doeblin-minorization equivalence for uniform ergodicity
nodes.description: A φ-irreducible aperiodic chain is uniformly ergodic if and only if it satisfies a uniform minorization P^m(x, ·) ≥ δν(·) for all x (Doeblin's condition); equivalently, X is a small set.

nodes.name: Moment bounds from drift conditions
nodes.description: If PV ≤ λV + b·1_C for a geometrically ergodic chain, then π(V) < ∞ and sup_n E_x[V(X_n)] ≤ λ^n V(x) + b/(1−λ); drift conditions yield explicit moment bounds.

nodes.name: Stochastic monotonicity (Markov chain)
nodes.description: A Markov chain on an ordered state space is stochastically monotone if x ≤ y implies P(x, ·) ≤_{st} P(y, ·) in the stochastic order; enables construction of monotone couplings.

nodes.name: Iterated function system (IFS) as Markov chain
nodes.description: A Markov chain X_{n+1} = f_{θ_{n+1}}(X_n) where (θ_n) are i.i.d.; the transition kernel P(x, A) = ∫ 1_A(f_θ(x)) μ(dθ) arises in random dynamical systems, MCMC, and stochastic approximation.

nodes.name: Compact sets are petite for T-chains
nodes.description: If the chain is a T-chain, then every compact subset of the state space is petite; bridges the topological and measure-theoretic structures in the Meyn-Tweedie framework.

nodes.name: V-uniform ergodicity
nodes.description: A chain is V-uniformly ergodic if sup_{x: V(x)<∞} ‖P^n(x, ·) − π(·)‖_V / V(x) → 0 as n → ∞; a refinement of geometric ergodicity where convergence is uniform over level sets of V.

nodes.name: Irreducibility plus strong Feller implies Harris recurrence
nodes.description: If a Markov chain on a locally compact space is φ-irreducible, has the strong Feller property, and admits a reachable compact set, then it is a T-chain; combined with a drift condition, this ensures Harris recurrence.

nodes.name: Ergodic decomposition for general Markov chains
nodes.description: A φ-irreducible chain that is not Harris recurrent decomposes into a maximal Harris recurrent absorbing set H and a transient complement; the absorbing set carries the unique invariant measure.

nodes.name: Expected number of visits (general state space)
nodes.description: For a transient chain, E_x[Σ_{n=0}^∞ 1_A(X_n)] = G(x, A) defines the Green kernel; for recurrent chains, G(x, A) = ∞ for all A with ψ(A) > 0.

nodes.name: Nonlinear state space model as Markov chain
nodes.description: The model X_{n+1} = f(X_n, W_{n+1}) with observations Y_n = g(X_n, V_n), where (W_n), (V_n) are i.i.d. noise sequences; the hidden state (X_n) is a Markov chain whose stability determines filter convergence.

nodes.name: Stability criterion for Markov chains from SDEs
nodes.description: For X_{n+1} = f(X_n, W_{n+1}) where f satisfies E[V(f(x, W))] ≤ λV(x) + b, the chain is geometrically ergodic; applies the Meyn-Tweedie drift framework to discrete-time samplings of SDEs.

nodes.name: Lyapunov criterion for continuous-time chains (generator form)
nodes.description: For a non-explosive continuous-time Markov process with generator L, if LV(x) ≤ −cV(x) + b·1_C(x) for a petite set C and V ≥ 1, then the process is positive Harris recurrent and ergodic.

nodes.name: Basic adjoint relationship (Revuz measure)
nodes.description: For a Harris recurrent chain with invariant measure π and a set A, E_A[Σ_{k=0}^{τ_A-1} 1_B(X_k)] = π(B)/π(A) for all B; establishes the Revuz correspondence between additive functionals and measures.

nodes.name: Resolvent characterization of recurrence (general state space)
nodes.description: A φ-irreducible chain is recurrent if and only if R_λ(x, A) → ∞ as λ ↑ 1 for all A with ψ(A) > 0; the potential kernel U = Σ_n P^n is infinite on ψ-positive sets.

nodes.name: Convergence parameter characterization of R-transience
nodes.description: For R-transient chains, the R-resolvent Σ_n R^n P^n(x, A) < ∞ characterizes transient behavior; R-recurrence is equivalent to existence of an R-invariant measure.

nodes.name: MCMC ergodicity via Meyn-Tweedie theory
nodes.description: A Metropolis-Hastings chain targeting π is Harris ergodic if the proposal is φ-irreducible and aperiodic and a suitable Lyapunov drift condition holds; the standard framework for verifying MCMC convergence.

nodes.name: f-modulated drift criterion
nodes.description: If PV ≤ V − f + b·1_C for V ≥ 1, f ≥ 1, and a petite set C, then the chain is positive Harris recurrent with π(f) < ∞; simultaneously establishes recurrence and integrability of f under π.

nodes.name: Explicit total variation convergence bound via drift and minorization
nodes.description: Given a drift condition PV ≤ λV + b·1_C and minorization P^m(x, ·) ≥ δν(·) on C, ‖P^n(x, ·) − π‖_{TV} ≤ (1 − δ)^{⌊n/m⌋} V(x) + residual; provides computable non-asymptotic bounds.

nodes.name: Splitting construction for continuous-time chains
nodes.description: Extends Nummelin splitting to continuous-time Markov processes by applying the splitting to the skeleton chain at a suitably chosen sampling rate δ > 0.

nodes.name: Accessible set (general state space)
nodes.description: A set A ∈ B(X) is accessible from x if P^n(x, A) > 0 for some n ≥ 1; the chain is φ-irreducible if every ψ-positive set is universally accessible.

nodes.name: Absorbing set (general state space)
nodes.description: A set H ∈ B(X) is absorbing if P(x, H) = 1 for all x ∈ H; the maximal Harris component is always absorbing, and the chain restricted to an absorbing set inherits φ-irreducibility.

nodes.name: Taboo kernel (general state space)
nodes.description: The kernel _A P^n(x, B) = P_x(X_n ∈ B, X_k ∉ A for 1 ≤ k ≤ n) giving transition probabilities conditional on avoiding set A for n steps; used in passage time and renewal decompositions.

nodes.name: Nummelin splitting technique
nodes.function_signature: (φ-irreducible chain with small set C) → (Split chain on augmented space with atom)
nodes.description: Augments the state space by introducing a binary auxiliary variable at visits to a small set C, using the minorization P^m(x, ·) ≥ ν_m(·) to construct an artificial atom α in the split chain.

nodes.name: Regeneration technique (for general state space chains)
nodes.function_signature: (Harris recurrent chain, atom or split chain) → (i.i.d. excursion blocks)
nodes.description: Decomposes the sample path into independent identically distributed excursion blocks between successive regeneration times at an atom; reduces limit theorems to the i.i.d. case.

nodes.name: Coupling construction for general state space chains
nodes.function_signature: (Two copies of Harris chain, minorization on small set C) → (Coupling time τ with P(τ > n) → 0)
nodes.description: At visits to the small set C, attempts to couple two copies using the minorization measure; succeeds with probability δ at each attempt, giving geometric tail bounds on coupling time.

nodes.name: Monotone coupling (stochastically ordered chains)
nodes.function_signature: (Stochastically monotone chain) → (Coupled pair with X_n ≤ Y_n a.s.)
nodes.description: Constructs a coupling (X_n, Y_n) of two copies of a stochastically monotone chain such that if X_0 ≤ Y_0 then X_n ≤ Y_n for all n a.s.; yields bounds on convergence rates.

nodes.name: Conditional expectation as L² projection
nodes.description: E[X | G] is the orthogonal projection of X onto L²(G) in the Hilbert space L²(Ω, F, P); it minimizes E[(X − Y)²] over all G-measurable Y.

nodes.name: Stochastic process
nodes.description: A family of random variables {X_t : t ∈ T} defined on a probability space (Ω, F, P) taking values in a measurable state space (E, ℰ), indexed by a totally ordered set T.

nodes.name: Natural filtration
nodes.description: The filtration F_t^X = σ(X_s : s ≤ t) generated by the process X, the smallest filtration to which X is adapted.

nodes.name: Predictable process
nodes.description: A process H measurable with respect to the predictable σ-algebra P generated by all left-continuous adapted processes; in discrete time, H_n is F_{n-1}-measurable.

nodes.name: Predictable σ-algebra
nodes.description: The σ-algebra P on Ω × [0,∞) generated by all left-continuous adapted processes, or equivalently by sets of the form (s,t] × A with A ∈ F_s and {0} × A with A ∈ F_0.

nodes.name: Optional σ-algebra
nodes.description: The σ-algebra O on Ω × [0,∞) generated by all right-continuous adapted processes (equivalently, all càdlàg adapted processes); contains the predictable σ-algebra.

nodes.name: Stopped σ-algebra
nodes.description: For a stopping time τ, F_τ = {A ∈ F : A ∩ {τ ≤ t} ∈ F_t for all t ≥ 0}, the σ-algebra of events determined by time τ.

nodes.name: Stopped process
nodes.description: The process X^τ_t = X_{t ∧ τ} obtained by freezing X at the stopping time τ; if X is a martingale (submartingale, supermartingale) then so is X^τ.

nodes.name: Submartingale
nodes.description: An adapted integrable process (X_t) satisfying E[X_t | F_s] ≥ X_s for all s ≤ t; equivalently, a process whose conditional expected future value is at least as large as the present value.

nodes.name: Right-continuous martingale
nodes.description: A continuous-time martingale with right-continuous sample paths (and left limits, i.e., càdlàg); the standard regularity assumption for continuous-time martingale theory.

nodes.name: Usual conditions (conditions habituelles)
nodes.description: A filtration (F_t) satisfies the usual conditions if it is right-continuous (F_t = F_{t+} = ∩_{s>t} F_s) and complete (F_0 contains all P-null sets). Required for the general theory of processes.

nodes.name: Existence of càdlàg modification
nodes.description: A right-continuous submartingale (or supermartingale) with respect to a filtration satisfying the usual conditions admits a càdlàg modification; in particular, every martingale under the usual conditions has a càdlàg version.

nodes.name: Class (D) process
nodes.description: A process X is of class (D) if the family {X_τ : τ a finite stopping time} is uniformly integrable; the strongest uniform integrability condition on a process, implying closure in L¹.

nodes.name: Class (DL) process
nodes.description: A process X is of class (DL) if for each t > 0, the family {X_τ : τ a stopping time with τ ≤ t} is uniformly integrable; weaker than class (D), sufficient for the Doob–Meyer decomposition on each [0,t].

nodes.name: Predictable quadratic variation (angle bracket process)
nodes.description: The unique predictable increasing process ⟨M⟩ such that M² − ⟨M⟩ is a local martingale; for continuous local martingales, ⟨M⟩ = [M]. Determines the law of the martingale via Lévy's characterization.

nodes.name: Semimartingale
nodes.description: A càdlàg adapted process X that decomposes as X = M + A where M is a local martingale and A is an adapted process of locally bounded variation; the most general class of stochastic integrators.

nodes.name: Markov process (general state space)
nodes.description: A stochastic process (X_t)_{t≥0} on a measurable state space (E, ℰ) with transition semigroup (P_t) satisfying E_x[f(X_{t+s}) | F_t] = P_s f(X_t) a.s. for all bounded measurable f; the general continuous-time formulation including non-countable state spaces.

nodes.name: Feller process
nodes.description: A strong Markov process whose transition semigroup (P_t) maps C_0(E) into C_0(E) and is strongly continuous; equivalently, a process whose semigroup is a Feller semigroup. Admits càdlàg paths.

nodes.name: Resolvent operator (of a semigroup/generator)
nodes.description: R_λ = ∫_0^∞ e^{-λt} T_t dt = (λI − A)^{-1} where A is the infinitesimal generator; the family {R_λ}_{λ>0} satisfies the resolvent equation R_λ − R_μ = (μ − λ)R_λ R_μ and determines the semigroup uniquely.

nodes.name: Resolvent equation
nodes.description: The resolvent operators satisfy R_λ − R_μ = (μ − λ)R_λ R_μ for all λ, μ > 0; a fundamental algebraic identity characterizing resolvent families and equivalent to the semigroup property.

nodes.name: Positive maximum principle
nodes.description: A linear operator A on C_0(E) satisfies the positive maximum principle if whenever f ∈ D(A) attains its supremum at x₀ with f(x₀) ≥ 0, then Af(x₀) ≤ 0. Characterizes generators of Feller semigroups (via Hille–Yosida–Ray).

nodes.name: Martingale problem (Stroock–Varadhan)
nodes.type_signature: (Operator A, initial distribution μ) → Prob(C([0,∞), E))
nodes.description: A probability measure P on path space solves the martingale problem for (A, μ) if the initial distribution is μ and f(X_t) − ∫_0^t Af(X_s) ds is a P-martingale for all f in the domain of A. Well-posedness implies the Markov property.

nodes.name: Poisson process as a Markov/Lévy process
nodes.description: The Poisson process N_t with rate λ is simultaneously a Markov process (with generator Af(n) = λ[f(n+1) − f(n)]), a Lévy process (stationary independent increments), and a counting process with N_t − λt a martingale.

nodes.name: Compound Poisson process
nodes.description: The process X_t = Σ_{k=1}^{N_t} Y_k where N_t is Poisson(λt) and Y_k are i.i.d. with distribution F, independent of N; a Lévy process with finitely many jumps in each interval and Lévy measure ν = λF.

nodes.name: Construction of Brownian motion via Kolmogorov extension
nodes.description: Brownian motion is constructed by specifying consistent finite-dimensional Gaussian distributions (BM has independent N(0, t−s) increments), applying the Kolmogorov extension theorem to get a process, then using the Kolmogorov–Čentsov theorem to obtain a continuous modification.

nodes.name: Generator of Brownian motion
nodes.description: The infinitesimal generator of Brownian motion on ℝ^d is A = (1/2)Δ (half the Laplacian), with domain containing C²_c(ℝ^d); the Feller semigroup is P_t f(x) = ∫ f(y) (2πt)^{-d/2} e^{-|x-y|²/(2t)} dy.

nodes.name: Path properties of Brownian motion
nodes.description: Sample paths of Brownian motion are a.s. continuous, nowhere differentiable, have unbounded variation on every interval, and are Hölder continuous of order α < 1/2 but not α ≥ 1/2.

nodes.name: Right-continuous filtration
nodes.description: A filtration (F_t)_{t≥0} is right-continuous if F_t = F_{t+} := ∩_{s>t} F_s for all t ≥ 0; a key component of the usual conditions, ensuring the débuts of right-continuous adapted processes are stopping times.

nodes.name: Début theorem
nodes.description: If (F_t) satisfies the usual conditions and A is a progressively measurable set in Ω × [0,∞), then the début D_A(ω) = inf{t ≥ 0 : (ω, t) ∈ A} is a stopping time. Applies in particular to hitting times of closed sets by càdlàg adapted processes.

nodes.name: Section theorem
nodes.description: For a measurable set H in the optional (resp. predictable) σ-algebra on Ω × [0,∞), and for every ε > 0, there exists a stopping time (resp. predictable time) T with [T] ⊂ H and P(π(H)) ≤ P(T < ∞) + ε, where π(H) is the projection onto Ω.

nodes.name: Optional projection
nodes.description: For a bounded measurable process Y, its optional projection °Y is the unique optional process satisfying °Y_T = E[Y_T | F_T] a.s. on {T < ∞} for every stopping time T.

nodes.name: Predictable projection
nodes.description: For a bounded measurable process Y, its predictable projection ^pY is the unique predictable process satisfying ^pY_T = E[Y_T | F_{T-}] a.s. on {T < ∞} for every predictable time T.

nodes.name: Compensator (dual predictable projection)
nodes.description: The unique predictable increasing process Ã such that A − Ã is a local martingale, where A is an adapted increasing process (or the increasing part of a submartingale). Generalizes the Doob–Meyer decomposition to the predictable projection framework.

nodes.name: Lévy–Itô decomposition
nodes.description: Every Lévy process X_t decomposes as X_t = bt + σW_t + ∫_{|x|<1} x Ñ(t,dx) + ∫_{|x|≥1} x N(t,dx) where W is Brownian motion, N is the Poisson random measure of jumps, and Ñ is its compensated version. The decomposition is canonical and unique.

nodes.name: Poisson random measure
nodes.description: A random counting measure N on [0,∞) × E such that N(A) is Poisson(ν(A)) for measurable A, and N(A₁), …, N(Aₖ) are independent for disjoint Aᵢ. The jump measure of a Lévy process is a Poisson random measure with intensity dt × ν(dx).

nodes.name: Markov semigroup on a Banach space
nodes.description: A strongly continuous semigroup (T_t) of positive contractions on a Banach lattice (typically C_0(E) or L^p) satisfying T_t 1 ≤ 1 (sub-Markov) or T_t 1 = 1 (Markov); the functional-analytic framework for Markov processes.

nodes.name: Core of a generator
nodes.type_signature: Generator A → Dense subspace D₀ ⊂ D(A)
nodes.description: A subspace D₀ of the domain D(A) of a semigroup generator A such that A is the closure of A|_{D₀}; the generator is uniquely determined by its action on any core. For Feller semigroups, C²_c often serves as a core.

nodes.name: Generator of a diffusion process
nodes.description: The infinitesimal generator of an Itô diffusion dX_t = b(X_t)dt + σ(X_t)dW_t is the second-order operator Af(x) = (1/2)Σ_{ij} a_{ij}(x) ∂²f/∂x_i∂x_j + Σ_i b_i(x) ∂f/∂x_i where a = σσᵀ.

nodes.name: Itô diffusion
nodes.description: The solution X_t of the SDE dX_t = b(X_t)dt + σ(X_t)dW_t; under Lipschitz conditions on b, σ, the solution exists, is unique, and is a strong Markov process with continuous paths and generator L = (1/2)σ²∂² + b∂.

nodes.name: Stochastic exponential (Doléans-Dade exponential)
nodes.description: For a semimartingale M, the unique solution Z_t = ℰ(M)_t of dZ = Z_{-} dM with Z_0 = 1; for continuous M, ℰ(M)_t = exp(M_t − (1/2)⟨M⟩_t). Used in Girsanov's theorem and change-of-measure arguments.

nodes.name: Novikov's condition
nodes.description: If M is a continuous local martingale with E[exp((1/2)⟨M⟩_∞)] < ∞, then the stochastic exponential ℰ(M) is a uniformly integrable martingale. Ensures that the Girsanov change of measure defines a true probability measure.

nodes.name: Multiplicative functional
nodes.description: A non-negative adapted process M_t satisfying M_0 = 1 and M_{t+s} = M_t · (M_s ∘ θ_t) a.s. for all s, t ≥ 0, where θ_t is the shift operator. Used to construct killed processes and subprocesses via the Feynman–Kac formula.

nodes.name: Killed process
nodes.description: The process obtained by sending the Markov process to a cemetery state ∂ at a rate determined by a multiplicative functional or killing measure κ; the semigroup becomes P̃_t f(x) = E_x[M_t f(X_t)] where M_t is the survival probability to time t.

nodes.name: Coupling technique
nodes.function_signature: (Two probability measures μ, ν) → (Joint construction bounding d(μ,ν))
nodes.description: Constructs two random variables (X, Y) on a common probability space with marginals μ and ν to bound distances; the coupling inequality gives ‖μ−ν‖_{TV} ≤ P(X ≠ Y). Applied to convergence rates for Markov chains and comparison arguments.

nodes.name: Optional stopping technique
nodes.function_signature: (Martingale/supermartingale M, stopping time τ) → (Identity or inequality for E[M_τ])
nodes.description: Applies the optional stopping theorem or optional sampling theorem to a (super)martingale at carefully chosen stopping times to derive identities or bounds; a workhorse technique for computing hitting probabilities, expected hitting times, and ruin probabilities.

nodes.name: Martingale method
nodes.function_signature: (Problem involving a Markov process) → (Solution via martingale construction)
nodes.description: Embeds the problem into martingale theory by constructing a martingale from the Markov process (e.g., via the generator: f(X_t) − ∫_0^t Af(X_s) ds), then applies martingale convergence, maximal inequalities, or optional stopping to deduce the desired conclusion.

nodes.name: Semigroup method
nodes.function_signature: (Markov process / PDE) → (Solution via C₀-semigroup and generator analysis)
nodes.description: Studies Markov processes or evolution equations through the associated C₀-semigroup {T_t} and its generator A, using Hille–Yosida theory, resolvent analysis, and perturbation theory to establish existence, uniqueness, and properties of solutions.

nodes.name: Localization via stopping times
nodes.function_signature: (Local property via τₙ ↑ ∞) → (Global property)
nodes.description: Reduces problems involving local martingales or locally bounded processes to bounded/integrable ones by stopping at an increasing sequence τₙ ↑ ∞, proving the result for stopped processes, then passing to the limit.

nodes.name: Generator characterization technique
nodes.function_signature: (Operator A satisfying conditions) → (A generates a Feller/C₀ semigroup)
nodes.description: Identifies the Markov process by characterizing its generator: verifies the positive maximum principle, density of the domain, and range condition, then applies the Hille–Yosida or Lumer–Phillips theorem to conclude A generates the desired semigroup.

nodes.name: Doob–Meyer technique
nodes.function_signature: (Submartingale / semimartingale) → (Predictable compensator + local martingale)
nodes.description: Decomposes a submartingale of class (DL) into a local martingale plus a predictable increasing process (the compensator), enabling separate analysis of the martingale and drift parts. The continuous-time analogue of the Doob decomposition.

nodes.name: Change of measure (Girsanov) technique
nodes.function_signature: (Process under P, Radon–Nikodym derivative L_t) → (Process under Q = L·P)
nodes.description: Changes the probability measure via a positive martingale density process L_t to simplify the process dynamics; under Q the drift changes while the martingale part is preserved. Girsanov's theorem gives the explicit transformation for semimartingales.

nodes.name: Lyapunov function technique (for Markov processes)
nodes.function_signature: (Markov process, Lyapunov function V, generator A) → (Stability / recurrence conclusion)
nodes.description: Establishes recurrence, positive recurrence, or ergodicity of a Markov process by finding a function V ≥ 1 with AV ≤ −cV + b·1_K outside a compact set K, so that V(X_t) is (approximately) a supermartingale ensuring return to K.

nodes.name: Potential-theoretic technique for Markov processes
nodes.function_signature: (Markov process, excessive/harmonic functions) → (Structural conclusions)
nodes.description: Analyzes a Markov process through its potential kernel, excessive functions, and harmonic functions; uses the Riesz decomposition, maximum principles, and balayage to study hitting times, recurrence, and boundary behavior.

nodes.name: Conditional dominated convergence theorem
nodes.description: If X_n → X a.s. and |X_n| ≤ Y with E[Y] < ∞, then E[X_n | G] → E[X | G] a.s. and in L¹; the dominated convergence theorem lifted to conditional expectations.

nodes.name: Conditional Fatou's lemma
nodes.description: If X_n ≥ 0 are integrable, then E[lim inf X_n | G] ≤ lim inf E[X_n | G] a.s.; the conditional version of Fatou's lemma.

nodes.name: Martingale Lᵖ convergence theorem
nodes.description: If (M_n) is a martingale bounded in Lᵖ for some p > 1, then M_n → M_∞ a.s. and in Lᵖ. The converse also holds: an Lᵖ-convergent martingale is bounded in Lᵖ.

nodes.name: Dambis–Dubins–Schwarz theorem
nodes.description: Every continuous local martingale M with ⟨M⟩_∞ = ∞ a.s. can be represented as a time-changed Brownian motion: M_t = B_{⟨M⟩_t} where B is a Brownian motion with respect to the time-changed filtration. The fundamental connection between continuous martingales and Brownian motion.

nodes.name: Occupation times formula
nodes.description: For a continuous semimartingale X with local time L^a_t, ∫_0^t f(X_s) d⟨X⟩_s = ∫_{-∞}^{∞} f(a) L^a_t da for every non-negative Borel function f; converts time integrals along the process into space integrals against local time.

nodes.name: Local time of a continuous semimartingale
nodes.description: A jointly measurable process L^a_t measuring the time density of the semimartingale X at level a up to time t; defined via the occupation times formula or as L^a_t = lim_{ε→0} (1/2ε) ∫_0^t 1_{|X_s - a| < ε} d⟨X⟩_s. Continuous in t, càdlàg in a.

nodes.name: Tanaka's formula
nodes.description: |B_t − a| = |a| + ∫_0^t sgn(B_s − a) dB_s + L^a_t, where L^a_t is the local time of Brownian motion at level a. Shows that |B_t − a| is a submartingale and provides the canonical construction of local time.

nodes.name: Entrance boundary (Feller classification)
nodes.description: A boundary point of a one-dimensional diffusion that can be reached from the interior in finite time and from which the process can enter the interior, but cannot be reached from outside. Characterized by the convergence/divergence of integrals involving the scale function and speed measure.

nodes.name: Exit boundary (Feller classification)
nodes.description: A boundary point of a one-dimensional diffusion that can be reached from the interior in finite time but from which the process cannot re-enter; characterized by convergence of the scale function integral and divergence of the speed measure integral at the boundary.

nodes.name: Speed measure of a one-dimensional diffusion
nodes.description: The unique (up to scalar) σ-finite measure m on the state interval (l,r) such that the generator of the diffusion acts as Af = (1/2)(d/dm)(df/ds) where s is the scale function. Determines the time scale of the diffusion and appears in the spectral theory.

nodes.name: Scale function of a one-dimensional diffusion
nodes.description: A continuous strictly increasing function s on the state interval (l,r) such that s(X_t) is a local martingale; equivalently, s'(x) = exp(−∫^x 2b(y)/σ²(y) dy) for a diffusion with drift b and diffusion coefficient σ. In natural scale (s(x) = x), the process has no drift.

nodes.name: Feller boundary classification for one-dimensional diffusions
nodes.description: Classification of each boundary point of a one-dimensional diffusion into four types — regular, exit, entrance, or natural — based on convergence of integrals involving the scale function and speed measure. Regular boundaries are both entrance and exit; natural boundaries are inaccessible.

nodes.name: Column Space (Range)
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ ℂ^{m×n} → col(A) = {Ax : x ∈ ℂ^n} ⊆ ℂ^m
nodes.description: The subspace of ℂ^m spanned by the columns of A, equal to the image (range) of the linear map x ↦ Ax.

nodes.name: Row Space
nodes.description: The subspace of ℂ^n spanned by the rows of A, equivalently the column space of the conjugate transpose A*.

nodes.name: Null Space (Kernel)
nodes.description: The subspace of ℂ^n consisting of all vectors mapped to zero by A.

nodes.name: Rank of a Matrix
nodes.description: The dimension of the column space of A, equivalently the number of nonzero singular values.

nodes.name: Unitary Matrix
nodes.description: A square complex matrix whose columns form an orthonormal basis of ℂ^m; equivalently Q* = Q⁻¹, preserving inner products and 2-norms.

nodes.name: Conjugate Transpose (Adjoint)
nodes.description: The matrix obtained by transposing A and taking complex conjugates of all entries; satisfies ⟨Ax, y⟩ = ⟨x, A*y⟩.

nodes.name: Frobenius Norm
nodes.description: The entrywise 2-norm of a matrix, equal to the square root of the sum of squared singular values: ‖A‖_F = (σ₁² + ⋯ + σ_r²)^{1/2}.

nodes.name: Matrix Operator Norm (Induced Norm)
nodes.description: The norm on matrices induced by vector norms on domain and codomain; the 2-norm equals the largest singular value σ₁.

nodes.name: Submultiplicativity of Matrix Norms
nodes.description: For any operator norm (and the Frobenius norm), the norm of a product is at most the product of the norms.

nodes.name: Singular Values
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ ℂ^{m×n} → σ₁ ≥ σ₂ ≥ ⋯ ≥ σ_p ≥ 0, p = min(m,n)
nodes.description: The nonnegative square roots of the eigenvalues of A*A, ordered decreasingly; they measure the semiaxes of the image of the unit ball under A.

nodes.name: Reduced (Thin) SVD
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ ℂ^{m×n} (m ≥ n) → A = Û Σ̂ V*,  Û ∈ ℂ^{m×n}, Σ̂ ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, V ∈ ℂ^{n×n}
nodes.description: The economy-size singular value decomposition retaining only the first n left singular vectors, reducing storage from O(m²) to O(mn).

nodes.name: Eckart–Young–Mirsky Theorem
nodes.type_signature: inf_{rank(B)≤k} ‖A − B‖₂ = σ_{k+1},  inf_{rank(B)≤k} ‖A − B‖_F = (σ_{k+1}² + ⋯ + σ_r²)^{1/2}
nodes.description: The best rank-k approximation to A in the 2-norm or Frobenius norm is the truncated SVD A_k = ∑_{i=1}^{k} σᵢ uᵢ vᵢ*.

nodes.name: Moore–Penrose Pseudoinverse
nodes.description: The unique matrix satisfying the four Penrose conditions (AA⁺A=A, A⁺AA⁺=A⁺, (AA⁺)*=AA⁺, (A⁺A)*=A⁺A); computable via SVD as A⁺ = VΣ⁺U*.

nodes.name: Orthogonal Projector
nodes.type_signature: P ∈ ℂ^{m×m}, P² = P, P* = P
nodes.description: An idempotent Hermitian matrix projecting onto a subspace S along S⊥; satisfies ‖P‖₂ = 1 (unless P = 0) and range(P) = S.

nodes.name: QR Factorization
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ ℂ^{m×n} (m ≥ n) → A = QR, Q ∈ ℂ^{m×m} unitary, R ∈ ℂ^{m×n} upper triangular
nodes.description: Decomposition of a matrix into a unitary factor Q and an upper triangular factor R; unique (up to signs) when A has full column rank and diagonal entries of R are positive.

nodes.name: Upper Triangular Matrix
nodes.type_signature: R ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, r_{ij} = 0 for i > j
nodes.description: A square matrix with all entries below the main diagonal equal to zero; its eigenvalues are the diagonal entries.

nodes.name: Lower Triangular Matrix
nodes.type_signature: L ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, l_{ij} = 0 for i < j
nodes.description: A square matrix with all entries above the main diagonal equal to zero.

nodes.name: Householder Reflector
nodes.description: A unitary Hermitian matrix that reflects vectors across the hyperplane orthogonal to v; used to zero out subdiagonal entries column by column.

nodes.name: Least Squares Problem
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ ℂ^{m×n}, b ∈ ℂ^m → x* = argmin_x ‖Ax − b‖₂
nodes.description: The problem of finding x minimizing the 2-norm of the residual Ax − b, arising when the system Ax = b is overdetermined (m > n).

nodes.name: Normal Equations
nodes.description: The n×n system whose solution gives the least squares minimizer; equivalent to projecting b onto col(A), but squaring the condition number makes direct solution ill-advised.

nodes.name: Conditioning of Ax = b
nodes.description: The relative error in the solution of Ax = b is bounded by κ(A) = ‖A‖‖A⁻¹‖ times the relative perturbation in data, so κ(A) measures sensitivity of linear systems.

nodes.name: Machine Epsilon
nodes.description: The smallest positive floating-point number such that fl(1 + ε) > 1; equivalently half the spacing between 1 and the next representable number (ε_mach ≈ 1.11 × 10⁻¹⁶ in IEEE double).

nodes.name: Fundamental Axiom of Floating-Point Arithmetic
nodes.description: Every elementary floating-point operation (+ − × ÷) produces a result that is the exact result rounded: the relative error of each operation is at most machine epsilon.

nodes.name: Backward Stability
nodes.description: A numerical algorithm is backward stable if for every input x, its computed output f̃(x) is the exact answer to a nearby problem f(x + δx) with ‖δx‖/‖x‖ = O(ε_mach).

nodes.name: Backward Stability Implies Forward Accuracy
nodes.description: If an algorithm is backward stable and the problem has condition number κ, then the relative forward error is at most O(κ · ε_mach).

nodes.name: Accuracy = Condition × Stability
nodes.description: The central principle of numerical analysis: the accuracy achievable by an algorithm is the product of the problem's condition number and the algorithm's backward error.

nodes.name: Backward Stability of Householder QR
nodes.description: Householder triangularization is backward stable: the computed factors Q̃, R̃ are the exact QR factors of a matrix A + δA with ‖δA‖/‖A‖ = O(ε_mach).

nodes.name: LU Factorization
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ ℂ^{n×n} → A = LU, L lower triangular, U upper triangular
nodes.description: Decomposition of a square matrix into a product of a lower triangular matrix L and an upper triangular matrix U; exists without pivoting when all leading principal minors are nonzero.

nodes.name: Partial Pivoting
nodes.type_signature: At step k, swap rows to place max_{i≥k} |a_{ik}| on the diagonal
nodes.description: Row interchange strategy in Gaussian elimination that selects the largest magnitude entry in the current column as pivot, ensuring |l_{ij}| ≤ 1 in L.

nodes.name: Permutation Matrix
nodes.description: A matrix with exactly one entry of 1 in each row and column and 0s elsewhere, representing a permutation of coordinates; orthogonal and its inverse is its transpose.

nodes.name: Growth Factor
nodes.description: The ratio of the largest entry encountered during Gaussian elimination to the largest entry of the original matrix; controls the backward error of LU factorization.

nodes.name: Backward Stability of GEPP
nodes.description: Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting is backward stable provided the growth factor ρ is moderate; in practice ρ = O(1) for virtually all matrices.

nodes.name: Hermitian Positive Definite Matrix
nodes.description: A Hermitian matrix all of whose eigenvalues are strictly positive; equivalently x*Ax > 0 for every nonzero vector x.

nodes.name: Cholesky Factorization
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ ℂ^{n×n} HPD → A = R*R, R upper triangular with positive diagonal
nodes.description: The unique decomposition of a Hermitian positive definite matrix into the product of an upper triangular matrix and its conjugate transpose; costs (1/3)n³ flops, half that of LU.

nodes.name: Hessenberg Matrix
nodes.type_signature: H ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, h_{ij} = 0 for i > j + 1
nodes.description: An upper Hessenberg matrix has zeros below the first subdiagonal; a natural intermediate form for eigenvalue computation since it preserves eigenvalues under unitary similarity and enables O(n²) QR steps.

nodes.name: Tridiagonal Matrix
nodes.description: A matrix with nonzero entries only on the main diagonal and the two adjacent diagonals; arises from Hessenberg reduction of Hermitian matrices and enables O(n) per QR step.

nodes.name: Givens Rotation
nodes.type_signature: G(i,j,θ) ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, orthogonal, differs from I only in rows/columns i,j
nodes.description: A rotation in the (i,j)-plane by angle θ that selectively zeros a single matrix entry; used in QR factorization of Hessenberg matrices and in Jacobi eigenvalue iterations.

nodes.name: Bidiagonal Matrix
nodes.type_signature: B ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, b_{ij} = 0 for j ∉ {i, i+1}
nodes.description: A matrix with nonzero entries only on the main diagonal and the first superdiagonal; the intermediate form in SVD computation.

nodes.name: Sparse Matrix
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ ℂ^{n×n} with O(n) nonzero entries
nodes.description: A matrix in which most entries are zero, typically with O(n) nonzeros; enables matrix-vector products in O(n) time, making Krylov methods practical for large systems.

nodes.name: Preconditioner
nodes.type_signature: M ≈ A, M⁻¹ easy to apply → solve M⁻¹Ax = M⁻¹b
nodes.description: A matrix M approximating A such that M⁻¹A has clustered spectrum or small condition number, transforming the original system into one for which Krylov methods converge rapidly.

nodes.name: Wilkinson Shift
nodes.type_signature: μ = eigenvalue of trailing 2×2 block of H closer to h_{nn}
nodes.description: The shift strategy for QR iteration that selects the eigenvalue of the trailing 2×2 submatrix of H closer to h_{nn}; guarantees at least quadratic convergence for Hermitian matrices and cubic in practice.

nodes.name: Ritz Values and Vectors
nodes.type_signature: θ_i = eigenvalues of H_k ∈ ℂ^{k×k} (Arnoldi projection)
nodes.description: The eigenvalues of the projected Hessenberg matrix H_k obtained from Arnoldi iteration; they approximate eigenvalues of A, with extremal eigenvalues typically converging first.

nodes.name: Incomplete LU (ILU) Preconditioner
nodes.type_signature: A ≈ LU with fill restricted to sparsity pattern S
nodes.description: An approximate LU factorization that discards fill-in entries outside a prescribed sparsity pattern, yielding a sparse triangular preconditioner applicable in O(nnz) operations.

nodes.name: Incomplete Cholesky Preconditioner
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ HPD → A ≈ R*R with fill restricted to pattern S
nodes.description: The symmetric positive definite analogue of ILU: an approximate Cholesky factor with fill limited to a sparsity pattern, preserving positive definiteness under mild conditions.

nodes.name: Domain Decomposition Preconditioner
nodes.type_signature: Ω = ∪ Ωᵢ → M⁻¹ via local solves on Ωᵢ
nodes.description: Decomposes the computational domain into overlapping or non-overlapping subdomains, solves local subproblems independently or with interface coupling, and assembles a global preconditioner.

nodes.name: Convergence of Krylov Methods via Polynomial Approximation
nodes.description: The error of a Krylov method after k steps is bounded by the best polynomial approximation to zero on the spectrum, connecting iterative solver convergence to approximation theory.

nodes.name: GMRES Convergence Bound
nodes.description: GMRES convergence is governed by how well polynomials of degree k bounded by 1 at the origin can be made small on the spectrum (or field of values) of A.

nodes.name: Lanczos–Gauss Quadrature Connection
nodes.type_signature: e₁ᵀ f(T_k) e₁ = Gauss quadrature of bᵀ f(A) b / ‖b‖²
nodes.description: The k-step Lanczos approximation to bᵀf(A)b equals a k-point Gauss quadrature rule for the Riemann–Stieltjes integral ∫f(λ)dμ(λ) defined by the spectral measure of A with respect to b.

nodes.name: CG–Lanczos Equivalence
nodes.type_signature: CG iterates ↔ Lanczos vectors for A ∈ HPD
nodes.description: The conjugate gradient method applied to Ax = b produces iterates equivalent to the Lanczos process applied to A with starting vector b; the CG residuals are scalar multiples of the Lanczos vectors.

nodes.name: CG Convergence Bound
nodes.description: The A-norm of the error in conjugate gradients after k iterations is bounded by 2((√κ(A) − 1)/(√κ(A) + 1))^k, where κ(A) = λ_max/λ_min is the spectral condition number.

nodes.name: Faber–Manteuffel Theorem
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ ℂ^{n×n} → short-recurrence optimal Krylov method exists ⟺ A is normal (or A = αI + βN, N normal)
nodes.description: A short-recurrence Krylov method minimizing a norm of the residual at each step can exist only for matrices that are normal (up to a shift and scaling), explaining why GMRES needs long recurrences for general A.

nodes.name: Bauer–Fike Theorem
nodes.type_signature: min_{λ ∈ σ(A)} |μ − λ| ≤ κ_p(V) ‖E‖_p, where (A+E)v = μv
nodes.description: For a diagonalizable matrix A = VDV⁻¹, every eigenvalue μ of A + E satisfies min_λ|μ − λ| ≤ κ(V)‖E‖, quantifying eigenvalue sensitivity via the eigenvector condition number.

nodes.name: Cauchy Interlacing Theorem
nodes.type_signature: A ∈ ℂ^{n×n} Hermitian, B principal (n−1)×(n−1) submatrix → λ₁(A) ≥ λ₁(B) ≥ λ₂(A) ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_{n−1}(B) ≥ λ_n(A)
nodes.description: The eigenvalues of a principal submatrix of a Hermitian matrix interlace with the eigenvalues of the full matrix.

nodes.name: Classical Gram–Schmidt (CGS)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{m×n}) → (Q ∈ ℂ^{m×n} orthonormal, R ∈ ℂ^{n×n} upper triangular)
nodes.description: Orthogonalizes columns of A by subtracting projections onto all previously computed basis vectors simultaneously; numerically unstable due to cancellation.

nodes.name: Modified Gram–Schmidt (MGS)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{m×n}) → (Q ∈ ℂ^{m×n} orthonormal, R ∈ ℂ^{n×n} upper triangular)
nodes.description: Orthogonalizes columns of A by sequentially projecting out each new basis vector from all remaining columns, yielding improved numerical stability over CGS.

nodes.name: Householder Triangularization
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{m×n}) → (Q ∈ ℂ^{m×m} unitary, R ∈ ℂ^{m×n} upper triangular)
nodes.description: Computes the QR factorization by applying a sequence of Householder reflectors to introduce zeros below the diagonal; costs 2mn² − (2/3)n³ flops and is backward stable.

nodes.name: Least Squares via QR Factorization
nodes.description: Solves the least squares problem by computing the reduced QR factorization A = Q̂R̂ and back-substituting; backward stable and O(2mn² − (2/3)n³) flops.

nodes.name: Least Squares via SVD
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{m×n}, b ∈ ℂ^m) → (x* = A⁺b = VΣ⁺U*b)
nodes.description: Solves the least squares problem using the pseudoinverse from the SVD; most robust method, especially for rank-deficient problems.

nodes.name: Back Substitution
nodes.function_signature: (R ∈ ℂ^{n×n} upper triangular, b ∈ ℂ^n) → (x: Rx = b)
nodes.description: Solves an upper triangular system by computing x_n, x_{n−1}, ..., x_1 sequentially in O(n²) flops; backward stable.

nodes.name: Forward Substitution
nodes.function_signature: (L ∈ ℂ^{n×n} lower triangular, b ∈ ℂ^n) → (x: Lx = b)
nodes.description: Solves a lower triangular system by computing x_1, x_2, ..., x_n sequentially in O(n²) flops.

nodes.name: Gaussian Elimination with Partial Pivoting (GEPP)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, b ∈ ℂ^n) → (PA = LU, x = U⁻¹L⁻¹Pb)
nodes.description: Computes PA = LU by choosing the largest-magnitude pivot in each column, then solves via forward and back substitution; costs (2/3)n³ flops and is backward stable in practice.

nodes.name: Cholesky Algorithm
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n} HPD) → (R ∈ ℂ^{n×n} upper triangular, A = R*R)
nodes.description: Computes the Cholesky factor by a modified form of Gaussian elimination exploiting symmetry; no pivoting needed, always stable, and costs (1/3)n³ flops.

nodes.name: Hessenberg Reduction
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}) → (Q*AQ = H, H upper Hessenberg, Q unitary)
nodes.description: Reduces A to upper Hessenberg form via n−2 Householder reflectors applied from left and right; costs (10/3)n³ flops for general A, (4/3)n³ for Hermitian A yielding tridiagonal T.

nodes.name: Power Iteration
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, v₀) → (λ₁ dominant eigenvalue, v₁ eigenvector)
nodes.description: Iterates v^{(k+1)} = Av^{(k)}/‖Av^{(k)}‖ to converge to the eigenvector of the largest-magnitude eigenvalue; convergence rate is |λ₂/λ₁|.

nodes.name: Inverse Iteration
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, shift μ) → (eigenvalue nearest μ, eigenvector)
nodes.description: Applies power iteration to (A − μI)⁻¹ to find the eigenvalue closest to a given shift μ; converges as |λ_nearest − μ|/|λ_next − μ| per step.

nodes.name: Rayleigh Quotient Iteration
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n} Hermitian, v₀) → (eigenvalue λ, eigenvector v)
nodes.description: Inverse iteration with the shift updated to the Rayleigh quotient ρ(v^{(k)}) = (v^{(k)*}Av^{(k)})/(v^{(k)*}v^{(k)}) at each step; achieves cubic convergence for Hermitian matrices.

nodes.name: QR Algorithm (Unshifted)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}) → (eigenvalues on diagonal of limit matrix)
nodes.description: Iterates A^{(k+1)} = R^{(k)}Q^{(k)} where A^{(k)} = Q^{(k)}R^{(k)} is a QR factorization; equivalent to simultaneous iteration with identity matrix, converging to Schur form under eigenvalue separation.

nodes.name: Shifted QR Algorithm
nodes.function_signature: (H ∈ ℂ^{n×n} Hessenberg) → (Schur form T = Q*HQ)
nodes.description: QR iteration with shifts μ^{(k)} chosen to accelerate convergence; each step factors H − μI = QR then forms H_new = RQ + μI, achieving quadratic or cubic convergence per eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Simultaneous Iteration (Subspace Iteration)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, initial subspace V₀ ∈ ℂ^{n×p}) → (p dominant eigenvalues and eigenvectors)
nodes.description: Block generalization of power iteration: multiply a block of vectors by A and orthogonalize at each step to converge to the dominant invariant subspace.

nodes.name: Implicit QR Step (Francis Algorithm)
nodes.function_signature: (H ∈ ℝ^{n×n} Hessenberg, shifts μ₁, μ₂) → (H̃ similar Hessenberg)
nodes.description: Performs a QR step implicitly without forming Q and R: introduces a bulge in H via the implicit Q theorem and chases it down the subdiagonal, enabling real arithmetic with complex conjugate shift pairs.

nodes.name: Deflation in Eigenvalue Computation
nodes.description: When a subdiagonal entry of a Hessenberg matrix becomes negligible, decouple the problem into two independent smaller eigenvalue problems.
