nodes.name: Jacobi Eigenvalue Algorithm
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℝ^{n×n} symmetric) → (eigenvalues, eigenvectors)
nodes.description: Diagonalizes a real symmetric matrix by iteratively applying plane (Givens) rotations to zero out the largest off-diagonal entry; converges unconditionally with ultimate quadratic rate.

nodes.name: Divide-and-Conquer Eigenvalue Algorithm
nodes.function_signature: (T ∈ ℝ^{n×n} symmetric tridiagonal) → (all eigenvalues and eigenvectors)
nodes.description: Splits a tridiagonal matrix into two half-sized tridiagonals plus a rank-one correction, recurses, then merges via the secular equation; O(n² to n³) depending on deflation.

nodes.name: Bisection for Symmetric Tridiagonal Eigenvalues
nodes.function_signature: (T ∈ ℝ^{n×n} symmetric tridiagonal, interval [a,b]) → (eigenvalues in [a,b])
nodes.description: Counts eigenvalues in an interval using the Sturm sequence property of LDLT factorizations of T − μI, then bisects to isolate each eigenvalue to prescribed accuracy.

nodes.name: MRRR Algorithm (Multiple Relatively Robust Representations)
nodes.function_signature: (T ∈ ℝ^{n×n} symmetric tridiagonal) → (all eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors in O(n²))
nodes.description: Computes all eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix in O(n²) time by choosing locally well-conditioned LDLT representations near each eigenvalue cluster.

nodes.name: SVD Algorithm (Golub–Kahan)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{m×n}) → (U, Σ, V: A = UΣV*)
nodes.description: Computes the SVD by first reducing A to bidiagonal form via Householder reflectors, then applying implicit shifted QR to the bidiagonal matrix to converge to Σ.

nodes.name: Bidiagonalization (Golub–Kahan)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{m×n}) → (U*AV = B, B bidiagonal, U, V unitary)
nodes.description: Reduces A to upper bidiagonal form by alternating Householder reflectors on the left and right; costs 4mn² − (4/3)n³ flops when m ≫ n.

nodes.name: Arnoldi Iteration
nodes.description: Builds an orthonormal basis of the Krylov subspace K_k(A,b) and a (k+1)×k upper Hessenberg matrix H̃_k via modified Gram-Schmidt; foundation of GMRES and non-Hermitian eigenvalue methods.

nodes.name: Implicitly Restarted Arnoldi (IRAM / ARPACK)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, k desired eigenvalues, p extra) → (k eigenvalues and eigenvectors)
nodes.description: Runs Arnoldi to length k+p, then applies p implicit QR shifts to filter out unwanted Ritz values, effectively restarting with an improved Krylov basis; the algorithm underlying ARPACK/eigs.

nodes.name: GMRES (Generalized Minimal Residual)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, b ∈ ℂ^n) → (x_k ∈ x_0 + K_k(A,r_0) minimizing ‖b − Ax‖₂)
nodes.description: At step k, finds the vector in the affine Krylov subspace x_0 + K_k(A, r_0) that minimizes the 2-norm of the residual; implemented via Arnoldi plus a least squares solve, applicable to general nonsymmetric systems.

nodes.name: Lanczos Iteration
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n} Hermitian, b ∈ ℂ^n, k) → (Q_k, T_k: AQ_k = Q_k T_k + β_{k+1} q_{k+1} e_k*)
nodes.description: The specialization of Arnoldi to Hermitian matrices producing a symmetric tridiagonal matrix T_k via a three-term recurrence; costs only O(n) per step but suffers from loss of orthogonality in finite arithmetic.

nodes.name: BiCG (Biconjugate Gradient)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, b ∈ ℂ^n) → (approximate solution x_k)
nodes.description: Extends CG to nonsymmetric systems by running coupled Lanczos-type recurrences with A and A*; generates biorthogonal residual sequences but may break down and does not minimize a norm.

nodes.name: CGS (Conjugate Gradient Squared)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, b ∈ ℂ^n) → (approximate solution x_k)
nodes.description: Applies the BiCG polynomial twice without requiring A*, squaring the convergence rate but also amplifying irregular convergence behavior.

nodes.name: BiCGSTAB (Bi-Conjugate Gradient Stabilized)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, b ∈ ℂ^n) → (approximate solution x_k)
nodes.description: Stabilized variant of BiCG due to van der Vorst that avoids the irregular convergence of CGS by combining a BiCG step with a minimization step; does not require A*.

nodes.name: QMR (Quasi-Minimal Residual)
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, b ∈ ℂ^n) → (approximate solution x_k with quasi-minimal residual)
nodes.description: Based on the Lanczos biorthogonalization, applies a quasi-minimization of the residual norm to obtain smooth convergence behavior; more robust against breakdown than BiCG.

nodes.name: Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient
nodes.function_signature: (A ∈ HPD, M ∈ HPD preconditioner, b) → (x: Ax = b)
nodes.description: Applies CG to the preconditioned system M⁻¹Ax = M⁻¹b (in implicit form preserving symmetry via M = CC*) with convergence governed by κ(M⁻¹A) instead of κ(A).

nodes.name: Chebyshev points of the second kind
nodes.description: The set of n+1 points x_j = cos(jπ/n), j=0,...,n in [-1,1], the projections onto the real axis of equispaced points on the upper unit semicircle.

nodes.name: Chebyshev three-term recurrence
nodes.description: The Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind satisfy T_0=1, T_1=x, and T_{k+1}(x)=2x T_k(x) − T_{k-1}(x) for k≥1.

nodes.name: Chebyshev orthogonality
nodes.description: The Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind are orthogonal on [-1,1] under the weight (1−x²)^{-1/2}, with ⟨T_j,T_k⟩=0 for j≠k and ⟨T_k,T_k⟩=π (k=0) or π/2 (k≥1).

nodes.name: Chebyshev series
nodes.type_signature: (f on [-1,1]) -> (coefficients {a_k} and series Σ a_k T_k)
nodes.description: The expansion f(x)=Σ a_k T_k(x) of a function on [-1,1] in Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind, with coefficients a_k=(2/π)∫_{-1}^1 f(x)T_k(x)(1−x²)^{-1/2}dx (a_0 halved).

nodes.name: Equivalence of Chebyshev and Fourier cosine series
nodes.type_signature: (f on [-1,1]) -> (even periodic g(θ)=f(cos θ) with identical coefficients)
nodes.description: Under x=cos θ the Chebyshev series of f on [-1,1] coincides with the Fourier cosine series of the even 2π-periodic function f(cos θ), making the two theories interchangeable.

nodes.name: Chebyshev projection (truncated Chebyshev series)
nodes.description: The degree-n polynomial f_n=Σ_{k=0}^n a_k T_k obtained by truncating the Chebyshev series, equal to the orthogonal projection of f onto P_n in the Chebyshev-weighted L² inner product.

nodes.name: Aliasing of Chebyshev coefficients
nodes.type_signature: (f, n+1 Chebyshev points) -> (interp coeff c_k = Σ_{aliased j} a_j)
nodes.description: On the n+1 Chebyshev points T_k is indistinguishable from T_m whenever k≡±m (mod 2n), so the interpolation coefficient equals the sum of the true Chebyshev coefficients of all modes aliased to that index, c_k=a_k+Σ a_{2mn±k}.

nodes.name: Barycentric interpolation formula
nodes.function_signature: (nodes x_j, values f_j, weights w_j, eval x) -> (p(x))
nodes.description: An algorithm evaluating the degree-n polynomial interpolant as p(x)=(Σ_j w_j f_j/(x−x_j))/(Σ_j w_j/(x−x_j)) using barycentric weights w_j=1/∏_{k≠j}(x_j−x_k).

nodes.name: Barycentric weights for Chebyshev points
nodes.description: The closed-form barycentric weights w_j=(−1)^j δ_j (δ_j=1/2 at the two endpoints, 1 otherwise) for interpolation at Chebyshev points of the second kind, enabling O(n) evaluation.

nodes.name: Numerical stability of the barycentric formula
nodes.type_signature: (barycentric eval in floating point) -> (backward stable result, error ~ eps·Λ_n)
nodes.description: The second barycentric interpolation formula with Chebyshev weights is backward stable in floating-point arithmetic, evaluating polynomial interpolants with relative accuracy governed by the Lebesgue constant rather than the ill-conditioning of explicit Lagrange or Newton forms.

nodes.name: Bernstein ellipse
nodes.description: For ρ>1 the open region E_ρ in ℂ bounded by the image of the circle |z|=ρ under the Joukowski map x=(z+z^{-1})/2, an ellipse with foci ±1 and semiaxis sum ρ.

nodes.name: Joukowski map
nodes.description: The conformal map x=(z+z^{-1})/2 sending circles |z|=ρ to Bernstein ellipses and the unit circle to [-1,1], underlying the transfer between Laurent/Fourier and Chebyshev analysis.

nodes.name: Chebyshev coefficient decay for bounded-variation functions
nodes.description: If f has bounded variation V on [-1,1] then its Chebyshev coefficients satisfy |a_k|≤2V/(πk) for k≥1.

nodes.name: Chebyshev coefficient decay for differentiable functions
nodes.type_signature: (f with f^{(ν)} BV, variation V) -> (|a_k| = O(k^{-ν-1}))
nodes.description: If f,...,f^{(ν-1)} are absolutely continuous and f^{(ν)} has bounded variation V on [-1,1], then |a_k|≤2V/(πk(k-1)...(k-ν))=O(k^{-ν-1}).

nodes.name: Chebyshev coefficient decay for analytic functions
nodes.description: If f is analytic in the Bernstein ellipse E_ρ with |f|≤M there, then its Chebyshev coefficients satisfy |a_k|≤2M ρ^{-k}, decaying geometrically.

nodes.name: Geometric convergence of Chebyshev approximation for analytic functions
nodes.description: If f is analytic in E_ρ with |f|≤M, its degree-n Chebyshev projection and interpolant satisfy ‖f−p_n‖_∞≤2Mρ^{-n}/(ρ−1) (with an extra factor for the interpolant), i.e. convergence at the geometric rate ρ^{-n}.

nodes.name: Algebraic convergence of Chebyshev approximation for differentiable functions
nodes.description: If f has a ν-th derivative of bounded variation V on [-1,1], its degree-n Chebyshev projection and interpolant satisfy ‖f−p_n‖_∞≤C_ν V n^{-ν}, giving algebraic convergence of order ν.

nodes.name: Estimate of optimal Chebyshev convergence rate ρ
nodes.description: The geometric convergence factor ρ equals the parameter of the largest Bernstein ellipse to which f extends analytically; equivalently 1/ρ=limsup|a_k|^{1/k}, relating coefficient decay to the region of analyticity.
aliases: Root test for Chebyshev convergence rate

nodes.name: Lebesgue constant (interpolation operator norm)
nodes.description: The norm Λ_n=‖L_n‖ of the polynomial interpolation operator on a given node set, equal to the maximum over the interval of the sum of absolute values of the Lagrange cardinal functions, quantifying error amplification.

nodes.name: Lebesgue constant for Chebyshev points
nodes.description: The Lebesgue constant for polynomial interpolation in Chebyshev points grows only logarithmically, Λ_n~(2/π)log(n+1)+O(1), so Chebyshev interpolation is well-conditioned and near-optimal.
aliases: Logarithmic growth of Chebyshev Lebesgue constant

nodes.name: Lebesgue constant for equispaced points
nodes.description: The Lebesgue constant for polynomial interpolation in equally spaced points grows exponentially, Λ_n~2^n/(e n log n), quantifying the instability behind the Runge phenomenon.
aliases: Exponential growth of equispaced Lebesgue constant

nodes.name: Lebesgue constant interpolation error bound
nodes.description: Polynomial interpolation error obeys ‖f−L_n f‖_∞≤(1+Λ_n)E_n(f), bounding the interpolant in terms of the best approximation via the interpolation Lebesgue constant.

nodes.name: Conditioning of polynomial interpolation
nodes.type_signature: (node set, data perturbation δ) -> (interpolant perturbation ≤ Λ_n ‖δ‖)
nodes.description: The sensitivity of a polynomial interpolant to perturbations of the data values is governed by the Lebesgue constant, so Chebyshev-point interpolation is stable (logarithmic) while equispaced interpolation is exponentially ill-conditioned.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of best polynomial approximation
nodes.description: For each f∈C([-1,1]) and n≥0 there exists a unique best (minimax) degree-n polynomial approximant in the supremum norm, via compactness and the Haar property of {1,x,...,x^n}.

nodes.name: de la Vallée Poussin lower bound (alternation lemma)
nodes.description: If a polynomial p∈P_n produces an error f−p that alternates in sign at n+2 points x_i, then min_i|f(x_i)−p(x_i)| is a lower bound for the minimax error E_n(f).
aliases: de la Vallée Poussin lower bound

nodes.name: Haar condition (Haar/Chebyshev system)
nodes.type_signature: (n-dim function space on [a,b]) -> (unique interpolation at any n distinct points)
nodes.description: A finite-dimensional space of continuous functions on an interval in which every nonzero element has at most n−1 zeros (equivalently any n points admit unique interpolation), guaranteeing existence and uniqueness of the best minimax approximant.

nodes.name: Linear approximation scheme
nodes.type_signature: (f, finite-dim linear space V) -> (best/near-best element of V)
nodes.description: An approximation in which the approximant is drawn from a fixed finite-dimensional linear subspace (polynomials, trigonometric polynomials, fixed-knot splines), so the set of approximants is closed under linear combination.

nodes.name: Nonlinear approximation
nodes.type_signature: (f, nonlinear family such as R_{mn}) -> (best/near-best approximant)
nodes.description: An approximation drawn from a set that is not a linear subspace (rational functions of fixed type, free-knot splines, sums of exponentials), so approximants are not closed under addition.

nodes.name: Node polynomial
nodes.description: The monic polynomial ℓ(x)=∏_{k=0}^n(x−x_k) whose roots are the interpolation nodes, governing interpolation error through the Hermite/Cauchy formula.

nodes.name: Hermite integral formula (Cauchy interpolation error formula)
nodes.type_signature: (f analytic, node polynomial ℓ, contour Γ) -> (f(x)−p(x) = (1/2πi)∮_Γ (ℓ(x)/ℓ(t))(f(t)/(t−x))dt)
nodes.description: The polynomial interpolation error equals (1/2πi)∮_Γ [ℓ(x)/ℓ(t)] f(t)/(t−x) dt over a contour Γ enclosing the nodes and x but inside the region of analyticity of f.

nodes.name: Potential theory of polynomial approximation
nodes.function_signature: (node density measure μ on [-1,1]) -> (potential u_μ(z)=∫log|z−t|dμ(t) governing convergence)
nodes.description: The framework identifying (1/n)log|ℓ(z)| with the logarithmic potential of the limiting node-density measure, so interpolation/approximation convergence rates are read off from level curves of that potential.

nodes.name: Green's function of the complement with logarithmic pole
nodes.type_signature: (compact E, point ∞) -> (g_E: ℂ\E → ℝ, harmonic, g_E|_E=0, g_E~log|z|−log cap at ∞)
nodes.description: The Green's function g_E(z) of the complement of a compact set E with pole at infinity: harmonic off E, vanishing on E, with g_E(z)=log|z|−log cap(E)+o(1) at infinity; its level curves are the convergence contours of interpolation.

nodes.name: Convergence rate from Green's function
nodes.type_signature: (f analytic up to level curve g_E=ρ) -> (‖f−p_n‖_∞ ~ exp(−nρ))
nodes.description: For nodes distributed according to the equilibrium measure, polynomial interpolants of f converge geometrically at rate exp(−g_E(z)) inside the largest level curve of the Green's function within which f is analytic.

nodes.name: Equispaced equilibrium potential
nodes.type_signature: (uniform density on [-1,1]) -> (potential u(z) with non-degenerate level curves through ±1)
nodes.description: The logarithmic potential of the uniform (Lebesgue) density on [-1,1], whose level curves pass through ±1 (not the interval itself), explaining via potential theory why equispaced interpolation diverges except for functions analytic in a large lens-shaped region.

nodes.name: Impossibility of stable high-order equispaced approximation
nodes.description: Any method reconstructing analytic functions from n+1 equispaced samples that converges geometrically must be exponentially ill-conditioned, and any well-conditioned method converges at best root-exponentially.

nodes.name: Interlacing of orthogonal polynomial roots
nodes.description: All roots of any orthogonal polynomial are real, simple, and lie in the support interval, and the roots of p_n and p_{n+1} strictly interlace.

nodes.name: Colleague matrix
nodes.type_signature: (p = Σ a_k T_k) -> (matrix A from recurrence, eig(A)=roots(p))
nodes.description: The Chebyshev-basis analogue of the companion matrix: a tridiagonal-plus-rank-one matrix built from the Chebyshev three-term recurrence whose eigenvalues are the roots of a polynomial given by its Chebyshev coefficients.

nodes.name: Rootfinding via eigenvalues (colleague/companion method)
nodes.function_signature: (polynomial coefficients) -> (roots as eigenvalues of colleague/companion matrix)
nodes.description: Computing all roots of a polynomial by forming its colleague (Chebyshev) or companion (monomial) matrix and numerically computing the matrix eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Maximal algebraic degree of exactness (Gauss optimality)
nodes.type_signature: (n-point rule) -> (max degree of exactness = 2n−1, attained only by Gauss)
nodes.description: No n-point quadrature rule can be exact for all polynomials of degree 2n, and the Gauss rule (nodes at orthogonal-polynomial roots) uniquely attains exactness through degree 2n−1.

nodes.name: Golub-Welsch algorithm
nodes.function_signature: (recurrence coefficients of orthogonal family) -> (Gauss nodes=eig(Jacobi matrix), weights from eigenvectors)
nodes.description: Computing Gauss quadrature nodes and weights as the eigenvalues and squared first eigenvector components of the symmetric tridiagonal Jacobi matrix formed from the three-term recurrence coefficients.

nodes.name: Comparable accuracy of Clenshaw-Curtis and Gauss quadrature
nodes.description: For functions of finite smoothness or analyticity, n-point Clenshaw-Curtis quadrature achieves accuracy essentially as good as n-point Gauss quadrature despite being exact only to degree n, because the relevant aliasing errors are small.
aliases: Trefethen's observation on Clenshaw-Curtis vs Gauss

nodes.name: Carathéodory-Fejér (CF) approximation
nodes.function_signature: (f ∈ C([-1,1]), degree n) -> (near-best degree-n approximant via Hankel SVD)
nodes.description: A near-best polynomial/rational approximation method computing an SVD of a Hankel matrix of Chebyshev coefficients and reading the near-minimax approximant from the dominant singular vector.

nodes.name: CF singular value / Hankel eigenvalue identity
nodes.type_signature: (Hankel matrix H of Chebyshev coefficients of f) -> (σ_{n+1}(H) ≈ E_n(f))
nodes.description: For an analytic function the (n+1)st singular value of the Hankel matrix of Chebyshev coefficients essentially equals the best degree-n approximation error E_n(f), so the CF approximant's error and the best error agree to many digits.
aliases: Hankel singular value = best approximation error

nodes.name: AAK (Adamyan-Arov-Krein) theory
nodes.type_signature: (Hankel operator with symbol f, type (m,n)) -> (best meromorphic approximation error = (n+1)st singular value)
nodes.description: The distance in sup-norm from a bounded analytic function (Hankel symbol) to the rational functions of type (m,n) equals a singular value of the associated Hankel operator, attained by a specific Schmidt vector.

nodes.name: Rational best approximation of type (m,n)
nodes.description: The rational function p/q with deg p≤m, deg q≤n minimizing the sup-norm error to a continuous function on an interval, characterized by an equioscillation whose length depends on the defect.

nodes.name: Rational equioscillation characterization theorem
nodes.type_signature: (f, r ∈ R_{mn} with defect d) -> (r best iff ≥ m+n+2−d alternations)
nodes.description: A rational function r∈R_{mn} is the best sup-norm approximation to f iff the error f−r equioscillates between extrema at least m+n+2−d times, where d is the defect of r.

nodes.name: Defect of a rational approximant
nodes.type_signature: (reduced r=p/q ∈ R_{mn}) -> (defect d = min(m−deg p, n−deg q))
nodes.description: The nonnegative integer d=min(m−deg p, n−deg q) measuring how far a reduced rational p/q falls short of fully using the available degrees in type (m,n), entering the equioscillation count.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of rational best approximation
nodes.type_signature: (f ∈ C([a,b]), type (m,n)) -> (existence and uniqueness of best r*)
nodes.description: On a real interval the best sup-norm rational approximation of given type to a continuous function exists and is unique, despite R_{mn} being non-convex and approximants possibly degenerate.

nodes.name: Root-exponential convergence of rational approximation
nodes.type_signature: (f with branch/corner singularity, type (n,n)) -> (best error = O(exp(−C√n)))
nodes.description: For functions with branch-point or corner singularities (such as |x|), rational best approximations converge at the root-exponential rate exp(−C√n), strictly faster than any polynomial rate, by clustering poles near the singularity.

nodes.name: Pole clustering near singularities
nodes.function_signature: (singularity location, rational degree n) -> (poles clustered exponentially toward singularity)
nodes.description: The construction principle that good rational approximants of functions with singularities place poles in a geometrically clustered arrangement approaching the singular point, enabling root-exponential accuracy.

nodes.name: Newman's theorem (rational approximation of |x|)
nodes.type_signature: (|x| on [-1,1], rational degree n) -> (best error E_{nn}(|x|) of order exp(−√n))
nodes.description: |x| on [-1,1] can be approximated by rationals of degree n with error between (1/2)exp(−√n) and 3exp(−√n), establishing root-exponential convergence far beyond the O(1/n) polynomial rate.

nodes.name: Newman's construction (Newman points)
nodes.type_signature: (degree n) -> (Newman rational r_n with poles clustered near 0)
nodes.description: The explicit rational r(x)=x(p(x)−p(−x))/(p(x)+p(−x)) with p(x)=∏(x+ξ^k), ξ=exp(−1/√n), giving geometrically clustered approximation of |x|.

nodes.name: Stahl's theorem (sharp |x| and exp rational rates)
nodes.type_signature: (|x| or e^x, type (n,n)) -> (sharp asymptotic minimax error constants)
nodes.description: Stahl's sharp asymptotics: best rational approximation error to |x| on [-1,1] satisfies E_{nn}~8exp(−π√n), and best rational approximation of e^x on (−∞,0] decays at the geometric Halphen constant rate ~1/9.28903 per degree.

nodes.name: Zolotarev's first problem (best rational approximation of sign)
nodes.type_signature: (sign(x) on [-1,-a]∪[a,1], type (n,n)) -> (best rational via Jacobi elliptic functions)
nodes.description: The best rational approximation of given type to sign(x) on two intervals symmetric about the origin, solved explicitly by Zolotarev via Jacobi elliptic functions, with exponential convergence ~exp(−cn/log(1/a)).

nodes.name: Zolotarev problems (elliptic extremal rational functions)
nodes.type_signature: (two disjoint real intervals, degree n) -> (explicit extremal rational functions and minimax error)
nodes.description: A family of four classical extremal problems solved by Zolotarev giving rational functions best separating/approximating on disjoint intervals, with explicit Jacobi-elliptic-function solutions and spectral/matrix-sign applications.

nodes.name: Chebyshev-Padé (Clenshaw-Lord) approximation
nodes.type_signature: (Chebyshev series of f, type (m,n)) -> (rational r=p/q matching Chebyshev coefficients through order m+n)
nodes.description: The rational approximation analogous to Padé but matching the Chebyshev series of f on [-1,1] rather than its Taylor series, giving rationals well-suited to approximation on an interval.

nodes.name: Convergence of Padé approximants and pole detection
nodes.type_signature: (meromorphic f, diagonal (n,n) sequence) -> (convergence off poles, denominator zeros → poles of f)
nodes.description: Padé approximants of a meromorphic function converge to it in regions avoiding its singularities, with denominator roots converging to the true poles, providing analytic continuation beyond the radius of convergence (subject to spurious Froissart poles).

nodes.name: Analytic continuation via rational approximation
nodes.function_signature: (local series/samples of analytic f) -> (rational approximant valid on a larger domain / singularity locations)
nodes.description: Using Padé or rational approximants computed from local data (Taylor/Chebyshev coefficients or samples) to extend a function analytically beyond its original domain or radius of convergence and locate its singularities.

nodes.name: Froissart doublets (spurious poles)
nodes.type_signature: (rational approximant from noisy data) -> (spurious pole-zero pairs with near-cancelling residues)
nodes.description: Near-coincident pole-zero pairs of a Padé or rational approximant that arise from noise or rounding and do not correspond to true singularities, signaling overfitting in rational approximation.

nodes.name: Quasimatrix
nodes.type_signature: ([a,b] × {1..n}) -> (object with n function-columns admitting linear-algebra operations)
nodes.description: A matrix-like object continuous in one dimension and discrete in the other — a finite collection of functions of a continuous variable treated as the columns of an ∞-by-n matrix, supporting QR and SVD.

nodes.name: Chebfun (numerical function representation)
nodes.type_signature: (f on [a,b]) -> (Chebyshev interpolant to ~machine eps with arithmetic/rootfinding/integration operators)
nodes.description: A representation of a function on an interval by an adaptively chosen Chebyshev interpolant of degree sufficient to capture it to machine precision, enabling numerical computation with functions as if they were vectors.

nodes.name: Chebfun adaptive degree selection (chopping)
nodes.function_signature: (f, tolerance ~ eps) -> (minimal degree n and coefficients with negligible tail)
nodes.description: Choosing the polynomial degree for a chebfun by sampling at successively doubled Chebyshev grids and truncating once the tail of the Chebyshev coefficients falls below a relative machine-epsilon threshold.

nodes.name: Spectral differentiation matrix
nodes.type_signature: (N+1 grid points) -> (dense (N+1)×(N+1) matrix D, D f(x_j) ≈ f'(x_j))
nodes.description: The dense matrix D mapping the vector of function values at (typically Chebyshev) grid points to the values of the interpolating polynomial's derivative at those same points.

nodes.name: Chebyshev differentiation matrix entries formula
nodes.type_signature: (Chebyshev points x_j, j=0..N) -> (entries D_{ij}, diagonal by negative sum)
nodes.description: The explicit entries D_{ij}=(c_i/c_j)(−1)^{i+j}/(x_i−x_j) for i≠j of the Chebyshev spectral differentiation matrix, with diagonal entries determined by the negative-row-sum trick.

nodes.name: Spectral accuracy (spectral convergence)
nodes.type_signature: (f analytic in Bernstein ellipse, N grid points) -> (error = O(ρ^{-N}) for some ρ>1)
nodes.description: For analytic functions the error of a spectral (Chebyshev) method decays geometrically (root-exponentially or faster) with the number of grid points, faster than any fixed algebraic power of 1/N.

nodes.name: Spectral collocation method for differential equations
nodes.function_signature: (linear ODE/BVP Lu=f with BCs on [-1,1]) -> (discrete system in powers of D on grid values, solved by linear algebra)
nodes.description: Solving boundary value problems by replacing derivatives with spectral differentiation matrices, imposing boundary conditions by deleting/modifying rows and columns, and solving the resulting dense linear system.

nodes.name: Affine set
nodes.description: A set that contains the entire line through any two of its points, i.e. is closed under affine combinations (coefficients summing to one).

nodes.name: Affine hull
nodes.type_signature: subset of R^n → affine subset of R^n
nodes.description: The set of all affine combinations of points of a given set, equivalently the smallest affine set containing it.

nodes.name: Convex set
nodes.description: A set that contains the line segment between any two of its points, i.e. is closed under convex combinations.

nodes.name: Convex hull
nodes.type_signature: subset of R^n → convex subset of R^n
nodes.description: The set of all convex combinations of points of a given set, equivalently the smallest convex set containing it.

nodes.name: Convex cone
nodes.description: A set closed under all conic (nonnegative) combinations of its points, equivalently closed under nonnegative scaling and addition.

nodes.name: Conic hull
nodes.type_signature: subset of R^n → convex cone in R^n
nodes.description: The set of all conic combinations (nonnegative-coefficient combinations) of points of a given set, the smallest convex cone containing it.

nodes.name: Hyperplane
nodes.type_signature: {x in R^n : a^T x = b}, a ≠ 0
nodes.description: The codimension-one affine set of points satisfying a single nontrivial linear equation a^T x = b.

nodes.name: Halfspace
nodes.type_signature: {x in R^n : a^T x ≤ b}, a ≠ 0
nodes.description: The convex set of points satisfying a single nontrivial linear inequality a^T x ≤ b, one of the two regions a hyperplane divides space into.

nodes.name: Euclidean ball
nodes.description: The convex set of points within Euclidean distance r of a center x_c.

nodes.name: Ellipsoid (set)
nodes.description: The convex set obtained by an invertible linear image of a Euclidean ball, parameterized by a center x_c and positive-definite shape matrix P.

nodes.name: Second-order (norm) cone
nodes.description: The convex cone of vector–scalar pairs whose vector part has Euclidean norm bounded by the scalar part, also called the ice-cream or Lorentz cone.

nodes.name: Polyhedron
nodes.description: The solution set of finitely many linear inequalities and equalities, equivalently an intersection of finitely many halfspaces and hyperplanes.

nodes.name: Simplex
nodes.description: The convex hull of k+1 affinely independent points, the simplest bounded polyhedron of a given affine dimension.

nodes.name: Positive semidefinite cone
nodes.description: The convex cone of symmetric n×n positive semidefinite matrices within the space of symmetric matrices.

nodes.name: Intersection preserves convexity
nodes.description: The intersection of any collection of convex sets is convex.

nodes.name: Affine image and preimage preserve convexity
nodes.description: The image and the inverse image of a convex set under an affine map are convex.

nodes.name: Perspective function
nodes.function_signature: (point (x,t) with t>0) → (x/t in R^n)
nodes.description: The map P(x,t)=x/t on the domain t>0 whose image and inverse image preserve convexity of sets.

nodes.name: Linear-fractional function
nodes.function_signature: (x with c^T x + d > 0) → ((Ax+b)/(c^T x + d))
nodes.description: The composition of an affine map with a perspective function, f(x)=(Ax+b)/(c^T x+d), which preserves convexity of sets on its domain.

nodes.name: Separating hyperplane theorem
nodes.description: Any two disjoint convex sets can be separated by a hyperplane with one set in each closed halfspace.

nodes.name: Dual cone
nodes.type_signature: K^* = {y : y^T x ≥ 0 for all x in K}
nodes.description: The set of vectors making a nonnegative inner product with every element of a cone K, itself always a closed convex cone.

nodes.name: Self-dual cones
nodes.description: The nonnegative orthant, the second-order cone, and the positive semidefinite cone each equal their own dual cone.

nodes.name: Proper cone
nodes.description: A convex cone that is closed, solid (nonempty interior), and pointed (contains no line).

nodes.name: Generalized inequality
nodes.description: The partial order x ⪯_K y defined by y − x ∈ K for a proper cone K, generalizing componentwise and matrix inequalities.

nodes.name: Minimum and minimal elements
nodes.description: For a generalized inequality, a minimum element is comparable to and below all others, while a minimal element has no other element strictly below it.

nodes.name: Dual characterization of minimal elements
nodes.description: A point is minimal for ⪯_K if it minimizes λ^T x over the set for some strictly dual-feasible λ ≻_{K^*} 0 (with a converse for minimum elements).

nodes.name: Convex function
nodes.description: A function whose domain is convex and which satisfies f(θx+(1−θ)y) ≤ θf(x)+(1−θ)f(y) for all θ in [0,1].

nodes.name: Concave function
nodes.description: A function whose negative is convex, equivalently satisfying the reversed convexity inequality.

nodes.name: Extended-value extension
nodes.function_signature: (convex f on dom f) → (f : R^n → R ∪ {+∞})
nodes.description: Extending a convex function to all of R^n by assigning value +∞ outside its domain, simplifying handling of domains in convexity statements.

nodes.name: First-order condition for convexity
nodes.description: A differentiable function on a convex domain is convex iff f(y) ≥ f(x) + ∇f(x)^T(y−x) for all x, y in the domain.

nodes.name: Second-order condition for convexity
nodes.description: A twice-differentiable function on a convex domain is convex iff its Hessian is positive semidefinite (∇²f ⪰ 0) throughout the domain.

nodes.name: Epigraph
nodes.type_signature: {(x,t) : x in dom f, f(x) ≤ t}
nodes.description: The set of points lying on or above the graph of a function, which is convex iff the function is convex.

nodes.name: Nonnegative weighted sum and integral preserve convexity
nodes.description: A nonnegative weighted sum, or weighted integral, of convex functions is convex.

nodes.name: Composition with an affine map preserves convexity
nodes.description: If f is convex then g(x)=f(Ax+b) is convex.

nodes.name: Pointwise maximum and supremum preserve convexity
nodes.description: The pointwise maximum of finitely many, or supremum of an arbitrary family of, convex functions is convex.

nodes.name: Scalar composition rules
nodes.description: Conditions on the monotonicity and convexity of h and g under which the composition f(x)=h(g(x)) of scalar functions is convex.

nodes.name: Vector composition rules
nodes.description: Conditions on h and the component functions g_i under which the composition f(x)=h(g_1(x),...,g_k(x)) is convex.

nodes.name: Partial minimization preserves convexity
nodes.description: If f(x,y) is jointly convex and C is convex, then g(x)=inf_{y in C} f(x,y) is convex in x.

nodes.name: Perspective of a function
nodes.function_signature: (convex f, point (x,t) with t>0) → (t f(x/t))
nodes.description: Forming g(x,t)=t f(x/t) from a function f, which is convex whenever f is convex.

nodes.name: Quasiconvex function
nodes.description: A function on a convex domain all of whose sublevel sets are convex, equivalently f(θx+(1−θ)y) ≤ max{f(x),f(y)}.

nodes.name: First-order condition for quasiconvexity
nodes.description: A differentiable f on a convex domain is quasiconvex iff f(y) ≤ f(x) implies ∇f(x)^T(y−x) ≤ 0.

nodes.name: Log-concave and log-convex functions
nodes.description: A positive function is log-concave (log-convex) if its logarithm is a concave (convex) function.

nodes.name: K-convex function
nodes.description: A vector-valued function convex with respect to a generalized inequality ⪯_K, satisfying f(θx+(1−θ)y) ⪯_K θf(x)+(1−θ)f(y).

nodes.name: Standard-form optimization problem
nodes.description: The canonical statement of minimizing an objective f_0 subject to inequality constraints f_i ≤ 0 and equality constraints h_j = 0.

nodes.name: Convex optimization problem (standard form)
nodes.type_signature: min f_0(x) s.t. f_i(x) ≤ 0, a_j^T x = b_j
nodes.description: A standard-form problem with convex objective and convex inequality constraint functions and affine equality constraints.

nodes.name: Optimality condition for convex problems
nodes.description: For a convex problem with differentiable objective, a feasible x is optimal iff ∇f_0(x)^T(y−x) ≥ 0 for every feasible y.

nodes.name: Equivalence transformations
nodes.function_signature: (optimization problem) → (equivalent reformulated problem)
nodes.description: Reformulations such as variable change, constraint substitution, slack variables, or epigraph form that preserve a problem's solution set.

nodes.name: Quasiconvex optimization via bisection
nodes.function_signature: (quasiconvex problem, tolerance) → (optimal value via convex feasibility subproblems)
nodes.description: Solving a quasiconvex problem by bisecting on the objective value and checking convex feasibility of each sublevel set.

nodes.name: Linear-fractional program
nodes.type_signature: min (c^T x + d)/(e^T x + f) s.t. linear constraints
nodes.description: A quasiconvex program minimizing a ratio of affine functions over a polyhedron, reducible to a linear program.

nodes.name: Quadratic program (QP)
nodes.type_signature: min (1/2)x^T P x + q^T x s.t. Gx ⪯ h, Ax = b, P ⪰ 0
nodes.description: A convex problem minimizing a convex quadratic objective subject to affine inequality and equality constraints.

nodes.name: Quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP)
nodes.type_signature: min convex quadratic s.t. convex quadratic ≤ 0, Ax = b
nodes.description: A convex problem with a convex quadratic objective and convex quadratic inequality constraints.

nodes.name: Second-order cone program (SOCP)
nodes.type_signature: min f^T x s.t. ||A_i x + b_i||_2 ≤ c_i^T x + d_i, Fx = g
nodes.description: A convex problem minimizing a linear objective subject to second-order cone constraints.

nodes.name: Robust linear program
nodes.type_signature: min c^T x s.t. a_i^T x ≤ b_i for all a_i in uncertainty set
nodes.description: A linear program with constraints required to hold for all parameter values in an uncertainty set, reducing (e.g. for ellipsoidal uncertainty) to an SOCP.

nodes.name: Geometric program (GP)
nodes.description: An optimization problem in posynomial and monomial functions that becomes convex under a logarithmic change of variables and objective.

nodes.name: Semidefinite program (SDP)
nodes.type_signature: min c^T x s.t. x_1 F_1 + ... + x_n F_n + G ⪯ 0, Ax = b
nodes.description: A convex problem minimizing a linear objective subject to a linear matrix inequality (matrix-valued affine constraint in the PSD cone).

nodes.name: Conic (cone) program
nodes.type_signature: min c^T x s.t. Fx + g ⪯_K 0, Ax = b
nodes.description: A convex problem in conic form with a linear objective and a generalized inequality constraint with respect to a proper cone K, generalizing LP, SOCP, and SDP.

nodes.name: Vector (multicriterion) optimization
nodes.description: An optimization problem whose objective is vector-valued and minimized with respect to a generalized inequality induced by a proper cone.

nodes.name: Pareto optimal point
nodes.type_signature: feasible x with f_0(x) minimal wrt ⪯_K
nodes.description: A feasible point of a vector optimization problem whose achieved objective value is minimal, i.e. no feasible point does at least as well in every component and strictly better in some.

nodes.name: Scalarization
nodes.function_signature: (vector optimization problem, weight λ ≻_{K^*} 0) → (scalar problem min λ^T f_0)
nodes.description: Finding Pareto optimal points by minimizing the scalar objective λ^T f_0(x) for dual-feasible weight vectors λ ≻_{K^*} 0.

nodes.name: Lagrangian
nodes.type_signature: L(x,λ,ν) = f_0(x) + Σ λ_i f_i(x) + Σ ν_j h_j(x)
nodes.description: The weighted sum of the objective and constraint functions of an optimization problem, with Lagrange multipliers λ and ν on the constraints.

nodes.name: Lagrange dual function
nodes.description: The infimum of the Lagrangian over x, a concave function of the multipliers that lower-bounds the optimal value for λ ⪰ 0.

nodes.name: Lagrange dual problem
nodes.description: The convex problem of maximizing the Lagrange dual function over nonnegative inequality multipliers, yielding the best lower bound on the primal optimal value.

nodes.name: Weak duality
nodes.description: The optimal value of the dual problem is always a lower bound on the optimal value of the primal problem, for any problem.

nodes.name: Duality gap
nodes.description: The nonnegative difference between the primal and dual optimal values; zero exactly when strong duality holds.

nodes.name: Strong duality
nodes.description: The condition that the dual optimal value equals the primal optimal value (zero duality gap), which holds for convex problems under a constraint qualification.

nodes.name: Slater's condition
nodes.description: A constraint qualification stating that strict feasibility of a convex problem (a point strictly satisfying the nonlinear inequalities) implies strong duality.

nodes.name: Geometric/epigraph interpretation of duality
nodes.function_signature: (primal problem) → (supporting-hyperplane view of the value function)
nodes.description: Interpreting the dual function and duality gap via supporting hyperplanes of the set of achievable constraint–objective value pairs.

nodes.name: Complementary slackness
nodes.description: At a primal–dual optimal pair with zero duality gap, each inequality multiplier and its constraint cannot both be nonzero (active).

nodes.name: Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions
nodes.description: The system of primal feasibility, dual feasibility, complementary slackness, and stationarity of the Lagrangian that is necessary, and for convex problems sufficient, for optimality.

nodes.name: Max-min (saddle-point) interpretation of duality
nodes.description: Expressing primal and dual optimal values as inf-sup and sup-inf of the Lagrangian, with strong duality corresponding to a saddle point.

nodes.name: Strong max-min equality (Sion's minimax theorem)
nodes.description: For a function convex in one argument and concave in the other over suitable convex sets, the order of inf and sup can be exchanged.

nodes.name: Theorems of alternatives via duality
nodes.function_signature: (system of inequalities) → (dual feasibility certificate of infeasibility)
nodes.description: Deriving theorems of alternatives by applying Lagrange duality to a feasibility problem so that exactly one of a primal system and a dual system is solvable.

nodes.name: Sensitivity (shadow price) interpretation
nodes.description: Under strong duality and differentiability, optimal dual variables equal the negative partial derivatives of the optimal value with respect to constraint right-hand sides.

nodes.name: Perturbation and global sensitivity analysis
nodes.function_signature: (constraint perturbations (u,v)) → (bounds on perturbed optimal value p*(u,v))
nodes.description: Using optimal dual variables to bound how the optimal value changes under tightening or loosening of the constraints.

nodes.name: Duality for generalized inequalities
nodes.description: The extension of Lagrange duality to problems with generalized-inequality constraints, using dual-cone multipliers λ ⪰_{K^*} 0.

nodes.name: SDP and cone program duality
nodes.description: The explicit primal–dual pair and strong-duality conditions for semidefinite and conic programs, with matrix or cone-valued dual variables.

nodes.name: Norm approximation problem
nodes.description: The problem of minimizing the norm of the residual Ax − b, whose form (LP, QP, etc.) depends on the chosen norm.

nodes.name: Chebyshev (minimax) approximation
nodes.description: Norm approximation in the ℓ∞ norm, minimizing the largest residual magnitude, expressible as a linear program.

nodes.name: Penalty function approximation
nodes.type_signature: min Σ φ(r_i), r = Ax − b
nodes.description: Minimizing a sum of a convex penalty function applied to each residual (e.g. quadratic, ℓ1, deadzone, or Huber penalty).

nodes.name: Regularized (Tikhonov) approximation
nodes.description: A bi-objective approximation that trades off residual norm against a regularization term penalizing the solution size; the squared-ℓ2 case is Tikhonov regularization.

nodes.name: Robust least squares
nodes.type_signature: min sup_{A in uncertainty set} ||Ax − b||_2
nodes.description: Least-squares approximation minimizing the worst-case residual over uncertainty in the data matrix A, reducible to an SOCP or SDP.

nodes.name: Maximum likelihood estimation as a convex problem
nodes.description: Formulating maximum likelihood estimation as maximizing a concave log-likelihood, hence a convex optimization problem, for log-concave models.

nodes.name: MAP estimation as a convex problem
nodes.description: Maximum a posteriori estimation cast as maximizing a concave log-posterior (log-likelihood plus log-prior) when the posterior is log-concave.

nodes.name: Optimal experiment design
nodes.type_signature: min (over measurement fractions) scalar of error covariance
nodes.description: Choosing measurement proportions to minimize a scalar measure (D-, A-, or E-optimality) of the estimation error covariance, formulated as an SDP or logdet program.

nodes.name: Chebyshev center
nodes.type_signature: center of the largest ball inscribed in a polyhedron
nodes.description: The center of the largest Euclidean ball contained in a convex set, computable by linear programming for a polyhedron.

nodes.name: Maximum volume inscribed ellipsoid
nodes.type_signature: max log det B s.t. ellipsoid {Bu + d : ||u|| ≤ 1} ⊆ C
nodes.description: The largest-volume ellipsoid contained in a convex set, found by a convex logdet maximization program.

nodes.name: Minimum volume enclosing (Löwner-John) ellipsoid
nodes.type_signature: min log det A^{-1} s.t. set ⊆ {x : ||Ax + b|| ≤ 1}
nodes.description: The smallest-volume ellipsoid containing a given set, the Löwner-John ellipsoid, found by a convex logdet program or SDP.

nodes.name: Linear discrimination
nodes.type_signature: find (a,b) : a^T x_i − b > 0, a^T y_j − b < 0
nodes.description: Finding a separating hyperplane that strictly classifies two point sets, a linear-programming feasibility problem.

nodes.name: Support vector machine
nodes.type_signature: min (1/2)||a||^2 + C Σ u_i s.t. margin/slack constraints
nodes.description: Robust linear discrimination maximizing the classification margin (with slack penalties for nonseparable data), a convex quadratic program.

nodes.name: Projection onto a convex set
nodes.type_signature: min ||x − x_0|| s.t. x in C
nodes.description: Finding the point of a convex set nearest to a given point, a convex problem (QP or SOCP depending on the norm and set).

nodes.name: Floor planning (placement)
nodes.type_signature: convex/geometric program over cell positions and sizes
nodes.description: Arranging non-overlapping rectangular cells to minimize bounding-box area subject to placement constraints, formulated as a convex (geometric-programming) problem under a fixed relative ordering.

nodes.name: Strong convexity
nodes.description: The assumption that a function's Hessian is bounded below by a positive multiple of the identity, giving a quadratic lower bound used in convergence analysis.

nodes.name: Line search (exact and backtracking)
nodes.function_signature: (point x, descent direction Δx) → (step size t > 0)
nodes.description: Choosing the step length along a descent direction, either by exact minimization or by backtracking (Armijo) until sufficient decrease is achieved.

nodes.name: Gradient descent method
nodes.function_signature: (differentiable f, start x_0) → (minimizing sequence)
nodes.description: A descent method that at each step moves along the negative gradient direction Δx = −∇f(x) with a line search.

nodes.name: Steepest descent method
nodes.function_signature: (differentiable f, norm, start x_0) → (minimizing sequence)
nodes.description: A descent method using the normalized direction of steepest decrease with respect to a chosen norm, of which gradient descent is the Euclidean-norm case.

nodes.name: Newton step and Newton decrement
nodes.description: The Newton search direction obtained from the Hessian and gradient, together with the Newton decrement that measures proximity to optimality and serves as a stopping criterion.

nodes.name: Newton's method (damped and pure)
nodes.function_signature: (twice-differentiable f, start x_0) → (minimizing sequence)
nodes.description: An affine-invariant descent method using the Newton step with a damped (line-search) phase followed by quadratically convergent pure Newton steps near the optimum.

nodes.name: Self-concordant function
nodes.description: A convex function whose third derivative is bounded by its second derivative to the 3/2 power (and its multidimensional restriction along lines), the Nesterov-Nemirovski property enabling complexity bounds independent of constants.

nodes.name: Convergence analysis for self-concordant functions
nodes.description: A bound on the number of Newton iterations to minimize a self-concordant function that depends only on the initial gap and the Newton tolerance, free of unknown problem constants.

nodes.name: Newton system via factorization and structure
nodes.function_signature: (Newton system ∇²f Δx = −∇f) → (step Δx)
nodes.description: Computing the Newton step by Cholesky or other factorization of the Hessian, exploiting sparsity or block structure for efficiency.

nodes.name: KKT system (Newton system for equality constraints)
nodes.description: The block matrix linear system whose solution gives the Newton step for an equality-constrained minimization.

nodes.name: Newton's method with equality constraints
nodes.function_signature: (equality-constrained problem, feasible start) → (minimizing sequence)
nodes.description: Newton's method for minimizing a function subject to affine equality constraints, generating feasible iterates by solving the KKT system at each step.

nodes.name: Infeasible-start Newton method
nodes.function_signature: (equality-constrained problem, possibly infeasible start) → (minimizing sequence)
nodes.description: A Newton method that uses the combined primal–dual residual and need not start at a feasible point, attaining feasibility and optimality together.

nodes.name: Newton step via elimination
nodes.function_signature: (KKT system) → (step Δx)
nodes.description: Solving the equality-constrained Newton/KKT system by eliminating variables to reduce it to a smaller positive-definite system.

nodes.name: Logarithmic barrier function
nodes.description: A smooth convex function that grows to infinity as x approaches the boundary of the inequality-feasible set, used to approximate indicator constraints.

nodes.name: Central path
nodes.description: The curve of minimizers, parameterized by t > 0, of the objective plus a scaled logarithmic barrier, converging to an optimal point as t → ∞.

nodes.name: Central path suboptimality bound
nodes.description: A central path point is no more than m/t suboptimal, where m is the number of inequality constraints, via an associated dual feasible point.

nodes.name: Barrier method (SUMT)
nodes.function_signature: (convex problem, strictly feasible start) → (approximately optimal point)
nodes.description: An interior-point method that solves a sequence of barrier-augmented problems along the central path with geometrically increasing t, also known as the sequential unconstrained minimization technique.

nodes.name: Barrier method convergence and complexity
nodes.description: A bound on the number of centering steps, and hence Newton iterations, the barrier method needs to reach a given accuracy, polynomial for self-concordant barriers.

nodes.name: Phase I (finding a strictly feasible point)
nodes.function_signature: (constraints) → (strictly feasible point or certificate of infeasibility)
nodes.description: An auxiliary optimization that minimizes the maximum constraint violation to compute a strictly feasible starting point for an interior-point method.

nodes.name: Primal-dual interior-point method
nodes.function_signature: (convex problem, start) → (approximately optimal primal–dual pair)
nodes.description: An interior-point method that updates primal and dual variables simultaneously by solving the perturbed KKT (modified Newton) equations, without an explicit inner centering loop.

nodes.name: Surrogate duality gap
nodes.description: A computable gap used in primal–dual methods that equals the actual duality gap when the iterates are primal and dual feasible.

nodes.name: Generalized-inequality interior-point methods
nodes.function_signature: (SOCP/SDP, strictly feasible start) → (approximately optimal point)
nodes.description: Extensions of barrier and primal–dual interior-point methods to cone programs using generalized logarithmic (e.g. −log det) barriers for the second-order and PSD cones.

nodes.name: Schur complement
nodes.function_signature: (block matrix [[A,B],[B^T,C]] with A ≻ 0) → (S = C − B^T A^{-1} B)
nodes.description: The matrix S = C − B^T A^{-1} B obtained by eliminating a block from a partitioned matrix, used in factorization and elimination.

nodes.name: Schur complement characterization of positive semidefiniteness
nodes.description: For A ≻ 0, the block matrix is positive semidefinite iff its Schur complement is, converting nonlinear matrix inequalities into linear matrix inequalities.

nodes.name: Convexity of the matrix-fractional function
nodes.description: The matrix-fractional function x^T Y^{-1} x is jointly convex in x and the positive-definite matrix Y.

nodes.name: Concavity of log-determinant
nodes.description: The function log det X is concave on the cone of symmetric positive-definite matrices.

nodes.name: Entropy H(X)
nodes.type_signature: discrete RV X with pmf p → R_{≥0}
nodes.description: The expected value −Σ p(x) log p(x) of the self-information of a discrete random variable, measuring its average uncertainty in bits.

nodes.name: Joint entropy H(X,Y)
nodes.description: The entropy −ΣΣ p(x,y) log p(x,y) of a pair of random variables treated as a single vector-valued variable.

nodes.name: Conditional entropy H(Y|X)
nodes.description: The expected entropy −ΣΣ p(x,y) log p(y|x) of Y averaged over the conditioning variable X.

nodes.name: Mutual information I(X;Y)
nodes.description: The relative entropy D(p(x,y)‖p(x)p(y)) between the joint distribution and the product of marginals, equal to H(X)−H(X|Y).

nodes.name: Conditional mutual information I(X;Y|Z)
nodes.description: The expected reduction in uncertainty about X from knowing Y, given Z, equal to H(X|Z)−H(X|Y,Z).

nodes.name: Mutual information–entropy relations
nodes.description: The identities I(X;Y)=H(X)−H(X|Y)=H(Y)−H(Y|X)=H(X)+H(Y)−H(X,Y) and I(X;X)=H(X).

nodes.name: Chain rule for entropy
nodes.description: The joint entropy decomposes as H(X_1,...,X_n)=Σ_i H(X_i | X_{i−1},...,X_1).

nodes.name: Chain rule for mutual information
nodes.description: The mutual information decomposes as I(X_1,...,X_n; Y)=Σ_i I(X_i; Y | X_{i−1},...,X_1).

nodes.name: Chain rule for relative entropy
nodes.description: The joint relative entropy decomposes as D(p(x,y)‖q(x,y))=D(p(x)‖q(x))+D(p(y|x)‖q(y|x)).

nodes.name: Information inequality (Gibbs' inequality)
nodes.description: Relative entropy is nonnegative, D(p‖q) ≥ 0, with equality if and only if p=q.

nodes.name: Nonnegativity of mutual information
nodes.description: I(X;Y) ≥ 0 with equality if and only if X and Y are independent.

nodes.name: Conditioning reduces entropy
nodes.description: H(X|Y) ≤ H(X), with equality iff X and Y are independent; conditioning never increases entropy on average.

nodes.name: Uniform distribution maximizes entropy
nodes.description: For a finite alphabet of size m, H(X) ≤ log m with equality iff X is uniformly distributed.

nodes.name: Independence bound on entropy
nodes.description: H(X_1,...,X_n) ≤ Σ_i H(X_i), with equality iff the X_i are mutually independent.

nodes.name: Log-sum inequality
nodes.description: For nonnegative a_i, b_i, Σ a_i log(a_i/b_i) ≥ (Σ a_i) log((Σ a_i)/(Σ b_i)), with equality iff a_i/b_i is constant.

nodes.name: Convexity of relative entropy
nodes.description: D(p‖q) is jointly convex in the pair (p,q).

nodes.name: Concavity of entropy
nodes.description: H(p) is a concave function of the probability distribution p.

nodes.name: Concavity/convexity of mutual information
nodes.description: For fixed p(y|x), I(X;Y) is concave in p(x); for fixed p(x), I(X;Y) is convex in p(y|x).

nodes.name: Data-processing inequality
nodes.description: If X→Y→Z form a Markov chain then I(X;Y) ≥ I(X;Z); no processing of Y can increase its information about X.

nodes.name: Fano's inequality
nodes.description: For an estimate X̂ of X from Y with error probability P_e, H(P_e)+P_e log(|X|−1) ≥ H(X|Y), lower-bounding the error probability by the conditional entropy.

nodes.name: L1 bound on entropy difference
nodes.description: If the L1 distance between two distributions p and q on an alphabet of size m is at most 1/2, then |H(p)−H(q)| ≤ −‖p−q‖_1 log(‖p−q‖_1/m).

nodes.name: Asymptotic Equipartition Property (AEP)
nodes.description: For i.i.d. X_1,...,X_n ~ p, −(1/n) log p(X_1,...,X_n) → H(X) in probability.

nodes.name: Typical set A_ε^{(n)}
nodes.description: The set of sequences whose empirical entropy rate −(1/n) log p(x^n) is within ε of H(X), i.e. whose probability is near 2^{−nH}.

nodes.name: Properties of the typical set
nodes.description: The typical set has probability near 1, has at most 2^{n(H+ε)} elements, at least (1−ε)2^{n(H−ε)} elements, and each member has probability near 2^{−nH}.

nodes.name: AEP-based source coding bound
nodes.description: i.i.d. sequences can be encoded with about nH(X) bits using roughly n(H+ε) bits per typical sequence and a negligible-probability overflow code.

nodes.name: Smallest high-probability set B_δ^{(n)}
nodes.description: A minimum-cardinality set carrying probability at least 1−δ, whose size to first order in the exponent equals that of the typical set (≈ 2^{nH}).

nodes.name: Entropy rate H(𝒳)
nodes.description: The per-symbol limit H(𝒳)=lim_{n→∞} (1/n) H(X_1,...,X_n) of the entropy of a stationary stochastic process.

nodes.name: Equivalence of entropy-rate definitions
nodes.description: For a stationary process the limit H'=lim H(X_n | X_{n−1},...,X_1) exists and equals the entropy rate H(𝒳).

nodes.name: Entropy rate of a Markov chain
nodes.description: For a stationary Markov chain with stationary distribution μ and transition matrix P, the entropy rate is H(𝒳)=−Σ_{ij} μ_i P_{ij} log P_{ij}.

nodes.name: Entropy rate of a hidden Markov / functions of Markov chains
nodes.description: For a function Y_i=φ(X_i) of a stationary Markov chain, the entropy rate is squeezed between H(Y_n|Y_{n−1},...,Y_1,X_1) and H(Y_n|Y_{n−1},...,Y_1), both converging to it.

nodes.name: Markov chains and the second law
nodes.description: For a Markov chain, relative entropy D(μ_n‖μ'_n) to any other distribution evolving under the same transition decreases with time, and H(X_n) increases toward stationarity for a doubly stochastic chain.

nodes.name: Prefix (instantaneous) code
nodes.description: A code in which no codeword is a prefix of any other, so each symbol is decodable as soon as its codeword ends.

nodes.name: Entropy bound on expected codeword length
nodes.description: The expected length L of any prefix D-ary code satisfies L ≥ H_D(X), with equality iff the lengths are l_i=−log_D p_i.

nodes.name: Shannon code lengths
nodes.description: The codeword-length assignment l_i=⌈log(1/p_i)⌉ which satisfies Kraft and achieves expected length within one bit of entropy.

nodes.name: Optimal code length bound (H ≤ L < H+1)
nodes.description: The minimum expected length L* of a prefix code satisfies H_D(X) ≤ L* < H_D(X)+1, and block coding drives the per-symbol length to the entropy rate.

nodes.name: Penalty for using the wrong code
nodes.description: Using a code optimal for q to encode a source p costs an extra D(p‖q) bits per symbol over the entropy, i.e. expected length is between H(p)+D(p‖q) and H(p)+D(p‖q)+1.

nodes.name: Huffman coding
nodes.function_signature: (source pmf, D-ary alphabet) → (optimal prefix code)
nodes.description: A bottom-up algorithm that builds an optimal prefix code by repeatedly merging the least probable symbols into a combined symbol.

nodes.name: Optimality of Huffman codes
nodes.description: The Huffman code achieves the minimum expected codeword length over all prefix (hence all uniquely decodable) codes for a given source.

nodes.name: Shannon–Fano–Elias coding
nodes.function_signature: (source pmf) → (prefix code)
nodes.description: A coding scheme using the rounded cumulative distribution function F̄(x) truncated to ⌈log(1/p(x))⌉+1 bits to assign prefix-free codewords.

nodes.name: Arithmetic coding
nodes.function_signature: (source sequence, model) → (codeword in [0,1))
nodes.description: A coding technique that represents an entire sequence by an interval of the unit line determined by cumulative probabilities, encoded by a single number.

nodes.name: Competitive optimality of Shannon code
nodes.description: For Shannon code lengths l(x), no other uniquely decodable code l'(x) can satisfy l'(x) < l(x)−c with probability exceeding 2^{−c+1}; the Shannon code is essentially uncrushable.

nodes.name: Horse race / gambling model
nodes.type_signature: outcomes with probabilities p_i and odds o_i
nodes.description: A repeated investment model in which a gambler distributes wealth across m outcomes with win probabilities p_i and payoff odds o_i.

nodes.name: Doubling rate W(b,p)
nodes.description: The expected logarithmic growth rate W(b,p)=Σ p_i log(b_i o_i) of wealth per race under bet allocation b.

nodes.name: Kelly (proportional) gambling optimality
nodes.description: The doubling rate is maximized by proportional betting b_i=p_i, yielding optimal doubling rate W*(p)=Σ p_i log o_i − H(p).

nodes.name: Conservation theorem (gambling)
nodes.description: For uniform fair odds o_i=m, the sum of the doubling rate and the entropy is constant: W*(p)+H(p)=log m.

nodes.name: Value of side information in gambling
nodes.description: The increase ΔW in doubling rate due to side information Y equals the mutual information I(X;Y) between the horse race outcome and the side information.

nodes.name: Doubling rate of dependent horse races
nodes.description: For a sequence of races, the growth-rate-optimal wealth grows as 2^{nW*} where the per-race doubling rate relates to the entropy rate via W*=Σ log o − H(𝒳) for fair uniform odds.

nodes.name: Entropy of English
nodes.description: The estimated entropy rate of English (about 1.3 bits/letter) obtained via models and Shannon's guessing/gambling estimation games.

nodes.name: Discrete memoryless channel (DMC)
nodes.type_signature: (input alphabet X, transition p(y|x), output alphabet Y)
nodes.description: A channel specified by a conditional distribution p(y|x) that acts independently on each transmitted symbol.

nodes.name: Channel capacity C
nodes.description: The maximum mutual information C=max_{p(x)} I(X;Y) over input distributions, the information capacity of the channel.

nodes.name: Binary symmetric channel (BSC)
nodes.description: A binary-input binary-output channel that flips each bit independently with probability p, having capacity 1−H(p).

nodes.name: Binary erasure channel (BEC)
nodes.description: A binary-input channel that erases each symbol with probability α and otherwise transmits it correctly, having capacity 1−α.

nodes.name: Symmetric and weakly symmetric channels
nodes.type_signature: channel with permuted rows/columns of transition matrix
nodes.description: A channel whose transition-matrix rows are permutations of one another (and columns sums equal), for which capacity equals log|Y|−H(row) achieved by the uniform input.

nodes.name: Jointly typical set A_ε^{(n)}
nodes.description: The set of pairs (x^n,y^n) that are individually typical and whose joint empirical entropy is near H(X,Y).

nodes.name: Joint AEP
nodes.description: Jointly typical pairs have probability near 1, number about 2^{nH(X,Y)}, and an independently drawn pair is jointly typical with probability about 2^{−nI(X;Y)}.

nodes.name: Channel code (M, n)
nodes.description: An encoding of M messages into length-n channel inputs together with a decoding rule, with rate R=(log M)/n bits per channel use.

nodes.name: Channel coding theorem (achievability)
nodes.description: For any rate R < C there exist codes with maximal error probability tending to 0; all rates below capacity are achievable.

nodes.name: Converse to the channel coding theorem
nodes.description: Any sequence of (2^{nR},n) codes with error probability tending to 0 must have R ≤ C; capacity is the supremum of achievable rates.

nodes.name: Random coding argument
nodes.function_signature: (rate R<C) → (code with small average error)
nodes.description: A proof method that generates a codebook at random from p(x), bounds the expected error probability, and concludes a good code exists.

nodes.name: Jointly typical decoding
nodes.function_signature: (received y^n, codebook) → (decoded message or error)
nodes.description: A decoder that declares the unique codeword jointly typical with the received sequence, erring only on atypicality or collision.

nodes.name: Feedback capacity theorem
nodes.description: Feedback does not increase the capacity of a discrete memoryless channel: C_FB=C.

nodes.name: Source–channel separation theorem
nodes.description: A source of entropy rate H can be transmitted reliably over a channel of capacity C iff H < C, and separate optimal source and channel coding is asymptotically optimal.

nodes.name: Zero-error capacity
nodes.description: The largest rate at which messages can be sent over a channel with exactly zero probability of error, related to the independence number of the channel's confusability graph.

nodes.name: Differential entropy h(X)
nodes.type_signature: continuous RV with density f → R ∪ {±∞}
nodes.description: The quantity h(X)=−∫ f(x) log f(x) dx, the continuous analogue of entropy for a random variable with density f.

nodes.name: Differential entropy of uniform and Gaussian
nodes.description: The uniform on [0,a] has differential entropy log a, and the N(0,σ²) Gaussian has differential entropy (1/2) log(2πeσ²).

nodes.name: AEP for differential entropy
nodes.description: For i.i.d. continuous X_i with density f, −(1/n) log f(X^n) → h(X), and the typical set has volume about 2^{nh(X)}.

nodes.name: Relation of differential to discrete entropy
nodes.description: The entropy of an n-bit quantization of a continuous X satisfies H(X^{Δ}) ≈ h(X)+n, so differential entropy is discrete entropy minus the log of the quantization step.

nodes.name: Joint and conditional differential entropy
nodes.description: The differential entropies h(X,Y)=−∫ f log f and h(X|Y)=h(X,Y)−h(Y) defined for jointly continuous variables.

nodes.name: Continuous relative entropy and mutual information
nodes.description: The relative entropy D(f‖g)=∫ f log(f/g) and mutual information I(X;Y)=h(X)−h(X|Y) for continuous variables, both nonnegative.

nodes.name: Entropy of the multivariate Gaussian
nodes.description: A multivariate normal with covariance K has differential entropy (1/2) log((2πe)^n |K|).

nodes.name: Gaussian maximizes differential entropy
nodes.description: Among all densities with a given covariance K, the multivariate Gaussian uniquely maximizes differential entropy.

nodes.name: Hadamard's inequality (via entropy)
nodes.description: For a positive-definite covariance matrix K, |K| ≤ Π K_{ii}, derived from the independence bound on differential entropy.

nodes.name: Gaussian channel
nodes.description: A continuous channel adding independent Gaussian noise of power N to the input, typically under an input power constraint E[X²] ≤ P.

nodes.name: Capacity of the Gaussian channel
nodes.description: The power-constrained Gaussian channel has capacity C=(1/2) log(1+P/N) bits per transmission, achieved by Gaussian inputs.

nodes.name: Sphere-packing argument
nodes.function_signature: (power P, noise N, n) → (number of distinguishable codewords)
nodes.description: A geometric heuristic counting how many noise spheres of radius √(nN) pack into a signal sphere of radius √(n(P+N)), yielding 2^{nC} codewords.

nodes.name: Capacity of the band-limited Gaussian channel
nodes.description: A band-limited channel of bandwidth W with power P and noise spectral density N_0/2 has capacity W log(1+P/(N_0 W)) bits per second.

nodes.name: Parallel Gaussian channels capacity
nodes.description: For k independent Gaussian channels under a total power constraint, capacity is Σ (1/2) log(1+P_i/N_i) maximized over a power allocation summing to P.

nodes.name: Water-filling power allocation
nodes.function_signature: (noise levels N_i, total power P) → (optimal powers P_i)
nodes.description: The optimal allocation P_i=(ν−N_i)^+ that pours power into the lowest-noise channels up to a common water level ν.

nodes.name: Capacity with colored Gaussian noise
nodes.description: For a Gaussian channel with non-white noise of covariance K_Z, capacity is obtained by water-filling over the eigenvalues of the noise covariance under a power constraint.

nodes.name: Gaussian channel with feedback
nodes.description: For the colored Gaussian channel feedback increases capacity by at most half a bit and at most a factor of two; for the memoryless (white) Gaussian channel feedback does not increase capacity.

nodes.name: Rate-distortion function R(D)
nodes.type_signature: (source p(x), distortion d, level D) → R_{≥0}
nodes.description: The minimum mutual information R(D)=min_{p(x̂|x): E d(X,X̂) ≤ D} I(X;X̂) needed to describe a source within average distortion D.

nodes.name: Distortion measure d(x,x̂)
nodes.description: A nonnegative function quantifying the cost of representing source symbol x by reconstruction x̂ (e.g. Hamming or squared-error).

nodes.name: Rate-distortion theorem
nodes.description: The operational rate-distortion function (minimum rate for distortion ≤ D) equals the information rate-distortion function R(D)=min I(X;X̂).

nodes.name: Rate-distortion of a Bernoulli source
nodes.description: A Bernoulli(p) source under Hamming distortion has R(D)=H(p)−H(D) for 0 ≤ D ≤ min(p,1−p) and 0 beyond.

nodes.name: Rate-distortion of a Gaussian source
nodes.description: A N(0,σ²) source under squared-error distortion has R(D)=(1/2) log(σ²/D) for D ≤ σ² and 0 for D ≥ σ².

nodes.name: Rate-distortion for parallel Gaussian sources (reverse water-filling)
nodes.description: For independent Gaussian sources under total squared-error distortion, the optimal distortion allocation D_i=min(λ,σ_i²) gives reverse water-filling, allocating no rate to low-variance components.

nodes.name: Convexity and monotonicity of R(D)
nodes.description: The rate-distortion function R(D) is a nonincreasing convex function of the distortion level D.

nodes.name: Blahut–Arimoto algorithm
nodes.function_signature: (channel or source, constraint) → (capacity or R(D))
nodes.description: An alternating-minimization iteration that computes channel capacity or the rate-distortion function by treating them as a double minimization over two distributions.

nodes.name: Capacity / R(D) as double optimization
nodes.description: Both channel capacity and the rate-distortion function can be written as a minimization of relative entropy over two distributions, justifying the Blahut–Arimoto alternating scheme.

nodes.name: Strong typicality / method of types (preview)
nodes.description: Sequences classified by their empirical type (histogram) so that the probability of a type and the number of sequences of a type are governed by entropy and relative entropy exponents.

nodes.name: Binary entropy function H(p)
nodes.description: The entropy −p log p −(1−p) log(1−p) of a Bernoulli(p) variable, a concave function peaking at p=1/2.

nodes.name: Type (empirical distribution) of a sequence
nodes.type_signature: x^n in X^n → P_{x^n} on X
nodes.description: The empirical probability distribution P_{x^n} of a length-n sequence, recording the relative frequency of each symbol of the alphabet.

nodes.name: Polynomial bound on the number of types
nodes.description: The number of distinct types of length-n sequences over an alphabet of size |X| is at most (n+1)^{|X|}, polynomial in n.

nodes.name: Method of types
nodes.function_signature: (i.i.d. sequence problem) → (combinatorial count over type classes)
nodes.description: A combinatorial proof technique that partitions sequences by their type and replaces probability calculations with counting over the polynomially many type classes.

nodes.name: Probability of a sequence under Q in terms of type
nodes.description: Under i.i.d. distribution Q, the probability of a sequence of type P equals 2^{-n(H(P)+D(P||Q))}, depending on the sequence only through its type.

nodes.name: Size of a type class
nodes.description: The number of sequences of type P satisfies (n+1)^{-|X|} 2^{nH(P)} ≤ |T(P)| ≤ 2^{nH(P)}, so to first order |T(P)| ≈ 2^{nH(P)}.

nodes.name: Probability of a type class under Q
nodes.description: Under i.i.d. Q the probability of type class T(P) satisfies (n+1)^{-|X|}2^{-nD(P||Q)} ≤ Q^n(T(P)) ≤ 2^{-nD(P||Q)}, decaying like 2^{-nD(P||Q)}.

nodes.name: Universal source code via types
nodes.description: A fixed-rate block code that encodes all sequences whose type has entropy below the rate R, achieving asymptotically optimal compression without knowing the source distribution.

nodes.name: I-projection (relative-entropy projection)
nodes.type_signature: (distribution Q, convex set E) → P* in E
nodes.description: The distribution P* in a set E minimizing the relative entropy D(P||Q), the closest distribution in E to Q in the Kullback–Leibler sense.

nodes.name: Conditional limit theorem
nodes.description: Conditioned on the empirical distribution lying in a convex set E, the marginal distribution of a single coordinate converges to the I-projection P* of Q onto E.

nodes.name: Pythagorean theorem for relative entropy
nodes.description: For the I-projection P* of Q onto a convex set E, every P in E satisfies D(P||Q) ≥ D(P||P*) + D(P*||Q).

nodes.name: Large deviation theory
nodes.function_signature: (rare-event set, distribution) → (exponential decay rate)
nodes.description: The study of exponential decay rates of probabilities of rare events, identifying the rate as a relative-entropy (or rate-function) minimization over the event.

nodes.name: Binary hypothesis testing problem
nodes.description: The decision problem of choosing between two candidate distributions P_1 and P_2 for observed data, with error probabilities of type I (alpha) and type II (beta).

nodes.name: Likelihood ratio test
nodes.description: The optimal test deciding between two hypotheses by comparing the ratio of their likelihoods to a threshold T.

nodes.name: Chernoff–Stein lemma
nodes.description: For fixed type I error bounded by epsilon, the best achievable exponent of the type II error is the relative entropy D(P_1||P_2), i.e. beta_n ≈ 2^{-nD(P_1||P_2)}.

nodes.name: Chernoff information
nodes.description: The quantity C(P_1,P_2) = -min_{0≤λ≤1} log Σ P_1^λ(x) P_2^{1-λ}(x), the best achievable exponent of the overall (Bayesian) probability of error in binary hypothesis testing.

nodes.name: Bayesian probability of error exponent
nodes.description: The minimal Bayesian probability of error in deciding between P_1 and P_2 from n i.i.d. samples decays with exponent equal to the Chernoff information C(P_1,P_2), independent of the priors.

nodes.name: Relative entropy and Fisher information (local approximation)
nodes.description: For nearby parameters, the relative entropy between f(·;θ) and f(·;θ+dθ) is to second order (1/2) J(θ) dθ^2, making Fisher information the local curvature of the KL divergence.

nodes.name: Score function
nodes.description: The derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to the parameter, whose expectation is zero and whose variance is the Fisher information.

nodes.name: Maximum entropy principle
nodes.description: The principle of choosing, among all distributions satisfying given constraints, the one of maximum (differential) entropy as the least-biased model.

nodes.name: Maximum entropy distribution
nodes.description: The entropy-maximizing distribution under moment constraints, which has exponential-family form f*(x)=exp(λ_0+Σ λ_i r_i(x)) with multipliers fixing the moments.

nodes.name: Maximum entropy theorem
nodes.description: The distribution of exponential-family form matching given moment constraints uniquely maximizes differential entropy among all distributions meeting those constraints.

nodes.name: Burg's maximum entropy theorem
nodes.description: Among all stationary processes with prescribed autocorrelation values R_0,...,R_p, the one of maximum entropy rate is the p-th order Gauss–Markov (autoregressive) process matching those correlations.

nodes.name: Maximum entropy spectral estimation
nodes.description: The spectral density estimate obtained by maximizing entropy rate subject to known autocorrelations, yielding an all-pole (autoregressive) spectrum.

nodes.name: Existence of maximum entropy distribution
nodes.description: A maximum entropy distribution of the exponential form exists matching the constraints precisely when such an exponential-form distribution is normalizable and satisfies them; otherwise the supremum is not attained.

nodes.name: Universal source coding
nodes.type_signature: (unknown source class) → code achieving entropy rate
nodes.description: Lossless coding that asymptotically achieves the entropy rate of an unknown source drawn from a known class, without prior knowledge of the source statistics.

nodes.name: Minimax redundancy
nodes.description: The smallest worst-case excess of expected code length over entropy, minimized over codes and maximized over sources in the class, characterizing the price of universality.

nodes.name: Redundancy of a code
nodes.type_signature: (code, source θ) → expected length minus entropy
nodes.description: The expected per-symbol excess of a code's length over the source entropy, equal to the relative entropy between the true distribution and the coding distribution.

nodes.name: Lempel–Ziv (LZ78) coding
nodes.function_signature: (data string) → (parsed phrase / pointer stream)
nodes.description: A universal compression algorithm that incrementally parses the input into distinct phrases, each the shortest new string, coded as a pointer to a previous phrase plus a new symbol.

nodes.name: Lempel–Ziv (LZ77) sliding-window coding
nodes.function_signature: (data string, window) → (offset, length, symbol) triples
nodes.description: A universal compression algorithm that encodes the next text segment as a pointer (offset and match length) into a sliding window of recently seen text.

nodes.name: LZ78 phrase / dictionary tree
nodes.description: The dictionary of distinct phrases produced by incremental LZ78 parsing, whose count c(n) controls the codeword length.

nodes.name: Optimality of LZ78
nodes.description: For a stationary ergodic source, the compression rate of LZ78 converges almost surely to the entropy rate, making it asymptotically optimal without knowledge of the source.

nodes.name: Optimality of sliding-window (LZ77) coding
nodes.description: Sliding-window Lempel–Ziv compression achieves the entropy rate of a stationary ergodic source as the window size grows, using recurrence-time properties of the source.

nodes.name: Bound on number of distinct LZ phrases
nodes.description: The number c(n) of distinct phrases in the LZ78 parsing of a length-n string satisfies c(n) ≤ n/((1-ε_n) log n), the key combinatorial bound for proving optimality.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov complexity
nodes.description: The length of the shortest binary program that makes a universal computer output the string x and halt, the algorithmic measure of descriptive complexity.

nodes.name: Conditional Kolmogorov complexity
