nodes.description: The length of the shortest program that outputs x given the string y (and its length) as additional input to the universal computer.

nodes.name: Universality (invariance) of Kolmogorov complexity
nodes.description: For any other computer A there is a constant c_A such that K_U(x) ≤ K_A(x) + c_A, so complexity relative to a universal machine is machine-independent up to an additive constant.

nodes.name: Upper bound on Kolmogorov complexity
nodes.description: For any string, K(x | ℓ(x)) ≤ ℓ(x) + c and K(x) ≤ ℓ(x) + 2 log ℓ(x) + c, so complexity is at most the length plus a small description of the length.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov complexity and entropy
nodes.description: For an i.i.d. source with entropy H, the expected Kolmogorov complexity per symbol of a length-n sequence converges to H, linking algorithmic and Shannon information.

nodes.name: Universal probability
nodes.description: The probability that a universal computer fed random program bits outputs x, dominating every computable distribution up to a multiplicative constant.

nodes.name: Universal probability ≈ 2^{-K(x)}
nodes.description: The universal probability of a string and its Kolmogorov complexity satisfy log(1/P_U(x)) = K(x) + O(1), so the most likely program is essentially the shortest one.

nodes.name: Incompressible sequence
nodes.description: A finite string whose Kolmogorov complexity is at least its length (no shorter description exists), of which most strings of each length are examples.

nodes.name: Algorithmically random (infinite) sequence
nodes.type_signature: infinite binary sequence with K(x_1..x_n) ≥ n - c
nodes.description: An infinite sequence all of whose prefixes are essentially incompressible, the algorithmic notion of randomness (Martin-Löf / Kolmogorov).

nodes.name: Chaitin's Omega
nodes.description: The halting probability of a universal prefix machine fed random bits, a well-defined real number that is algorithmically random and noncomputable.

nodes.name: Noncomputability of Kolmogorov complexity
nodes.description: There is no algorithm that computes K(x) for all strings x; the complexity function is uncomputable, related to the undecidability of the halting problem.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov sufficient statistic
nodes.type_signature: (string x) → finite set / model S* with x ∈ S*
nodes.description: The smallest finite-complexity description (model) S* containing x relative to which the remaining bits of x are random, separating structure from noise in a single string.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov structure function
nodes.type_signature: (x, complexity bound k) → log|S| over sets S∋x with K(S)≤k
nodes.description: The function giving, for each model-complexity budget k, the smallest log-cardinality of a set containing x describable in ≤ k bits, tracing the structure/randomness trade-off.

nodes.name: Occam's razor (algorithmic form)
nodes.description: The principle, justified by universal probability, that the shortest computable explanation consistent with the data should be preferred because it has the highest a priori probability.

nodes.name: Universal gambling scheme
nodes.function_signature: (sequence) → bets via universal probability
nodes.description: A betting strategy that distributes wealth across all programs proportional to 2^{-ℓ(p)}, guaranteeing capital growth tied to the Kolmogorov complexity of the realized sequence.

nodes.name: Network information theory
nodes.description: The study of information flow in networks with multiple senders and receivers, characterizing achievable rate regions rather than single capacities.

nodes.name: Multiple-access channel (MAC)
nodes.description: A channel with several independent senders and one receiver, modeled by a single conditional distribution of the output given all the inputs.

nodes.name: Multiple-access channel capacity region
nodes.description: The set of achievable rate pairs (R_1,R_2) for the MAC, the closure of the convex hull of all rates satisfying R_1 ≤ I(X_1;Y|X_2), R_2 ≤ I(X_2;Y|X_1), and R_1+R_2 ≤ I(X_1,X_2;Y) for some product input distribution.

nodes.name: Gaussian multiple-access channel capacity
nodes.description: The capacity region of the Gaussian MAC with powers P_1,P_2 and noise N, given by R_i ≤ C(P_i/N) per user and R_1+R_2 ≤ C((P_1+P_2)/N) jointly, with C(x)=(1/2)log(1+x).

nodes.name: Successive cancellation (onion-peeling) decoding
nodes.function_signature: (MAC output, ordered users) → decoded messages
nodes.description: A decoding strategy that decodes one user's message, subtracts its effect, and decodes the next, achieving corner points of the multiple-access capacity region.

nodes.name: Broadcast channel
nodes.description: A channel with one sender and several receivers, each receiving a possibly different output of a single transmitted signal.

nodes.name: Degraded broadcast channel
nodes.description: A broadcast channel in which the receivers can be ordered so that the worse receiver's output is a degraded (further-processed) version of the better receiver's output.

nodes.name: Capacity region of the degraded broadcast channel
nodes.description: The achievable rate region for a degraded broadcast channel, R_1 ≤ I(X;Y_1|U), R_2 ≤ I(U;Y_2), achieved by superposition coding over an auxiliary variable U.

nodes.name: Superposition coding
nodes.function_signature: (two messages, auxiliary codebook) → layered codeword
nodes.description: An encoding that superimposes a fine codeword for the strong receiver on a coarse cloud-center codeword for the weak receiver, achieving the degraded broadcast region.

nodes.name: Gaussian broadcast channel capacity
nodes.description: The capacity region of the degraded Gaussian broadcast channel, obtained by splitting power αP and (1−α)P between the two users with superposition coding.

nodes.name: Slepian–Wolf rate region
nodes.description: The achievable rate region for separate lossless encoding of correlated sources, the pentagon defined by R_1 ≥ H(X|Y), R_2 ≥ H(Y|X), R_1+R_2 ≥ H(X,Y).

nodes.name: Transmission of correlated sources over a MAC
nodes.description: A sufficient condition for sending correlated sources over a multiple-access channel, in which the source correlation can be exploited and source–channel separation generally fails.

nodes.name: Relay channel
nodes.description: A channel with a sender, a receiver, and an intermediate relay node that helps convey the message by transmitting based on its own received signal.

nodes.name: Capacity of the degraded relay channel
nodes.description: The capacity of a degraded relay channel, C = max min{I(X,X_1;Y), I(X;Y_1|X_1)}, achieved by block-Markov decode-and-forward coding.

nodes.name: Interference channel
nodes.description: A channel with two sender–receiver pairs in which each receiver wants only its own sender's message while suffering interference from the other transmission.

nodes.name: Capacity of the strong-interference Gaussian interference channel
nodes.description: For strong interference, the Gaussian interference channel capacity region coincides with that of the corresponding compound multiple-access channel, since each receiver can decode both messages.

nodes.name: Gelfand–Pinsker theorem (channel with side information)
nodes.description: The capacity of a channel with state known noncausally at the encoder is C = max [I(U;Y) − I(U;S)] over auxiliary U and encoding x(u,s).

nodes.name: Writing on dirty paper (Costa)
nodes.description: For a Gaussian channel with additive Gaussian interference known at the transmitter, the capacity equals that of the interference-free channel, so the known interference costs nothing.

nodes.name: Gelfand–Pinsker binning
nodes.function_signature: (message, known state) → codeword via auxiliary bins
nodes.description: An encoding that organizes auxiliary codewords into bins per message and chooses within a bin one jointly typical with the known state, the dual of Slepian–Wolf binning.

nodes.name: Failure of source–channel separation in networks
nodes.description: Unlike the point-to-point case, separately optimal source coding and channel coding are not in general optimal for networks, as exhibited by correlated sources over a MAC.

nodes.name: Gaussian multiuser channels
nodes.description: The family of additive white Gaussian noise network models (MAC, broadcast, relay, interference) used to obtain explicit multiuser capacity regions.

nodes.name: Stock market (price relative vector)
nodes.description: A model of m stocks given by a random vector X of price relatives, where X_i is the ratio of end-of-day to start-of-day price of stock i.

nodes.name: Portfolio
nodes.description: An allocation of wealth across stocks given by a probability vector b, where b_i is the fraction invested in stock i.

nodes.name: Doubling rate
nodes.type_signature: (portfolio b, distribution F) → W(b,F) = E[log b^T X]
nodes.description: The expected logarithm of the wealth relative b^T X of a portfolio, the exponential growth rate of wealth under repeated reinvestment.

nodes.name: Log-optimal portfolio
nodes.description: The portfolio b* maximizing the expected log wealth (doubling rate), which maximizes the long-run growth rate of capital.

nodes.name: Kuhn–Tucker characterization of the log-optimal portfolio
nodes.description: A portfolio b* is log-optimal iff E[X_i / (b*^T X)] ≤ 1 for every stock, with equality for every stock held with positive weight.

nodes.name: Competitive optimality of the log-optimal portfolio
nodes.description: For the log-optimal portfolio b* and any other portfolio b, the probability that b does at least as well as b* by a factor t is at most 1/t, so b* is competitively optimal.

nodes.name: Expected-ratio bound for log-optimal wealth
nodes.description: For the log-optimal portfolio b* and any portfolio b, E[(b^T X)/(b*^T X)] ≤ 1, the key inequality underlying competitive optimality.

nodes.name: Side information increases growth rate by mutual information
nodes.description: The increase in the optimal doubling rate of a stock market due to side information Y is at most the mutual information I(X;Y) between the market and the side information.

nodes.name: Asymptotic optimality of log-optimal investment (AEP for investment)
nodes.description: For a stationary ergodic market, the wealth of the log-optimal (causal) portfolio strategy grows to first order in the exponent like 2^{nW*}, and no causal strategy does better.

nodes.name: Universal portfolio
nodes.function_signature: (past price relatives) → next-day portfolio (Bayesian mixture)
nodes.description: Cover's causal investment strategy that performs a wealth-weighted average over all constant-rebalanced portfolios, achieving the same exponential growth as the best constant portfolio chosen in hindsight.

nodes.name: Constant rebalanced portfolio
nodes.description: An investment strategy that rebalances to the same fixed proportion vector b every trading period regardless of past prices.

nodes.name: Asymptotic optimality of the universal portfolio
nodes.description: The universal portfolio's wealth is within a polynomial factor of the best constant rebalanced portfolio in hindsight, so it achieves the same growth-rate exponent without knowing the future.

nodes.name: Entropy power
nodes.description: The variance of a Gaussian having the same differential entropy per dimension as X, the quantity through which entropy and second-moment inequalities connect.

nodes.name: Entropy power inequality (EPI)
nodes.description: For independent random vectors X and Y, the entropy power of the sum dominates the sum of entropy powers: 2^{(2/n)h(X+Y)} ≥ 2^{(2/n)h(X)} + 2^{(2/n)h(Y)}.

nodes.name: Fisher information (of a random vector under translation)
nodes.description: The translation Fisher information of a random vector, the expected squared gradient of its log density, central to the Fisher information and entropy-power chain.

nodes.name: Fisher information inequality
nodes.description: For independent random vectors X and Y, the reciprocal Fisher information is superadditive: 1/J(X+Y) ≥ 1/J(X) + 1/J(Y).

nodes.name: Cramér–Rao (estimation form) via Fisher information
nodes.description: The Fisher information of a random variable is at least the reciprocal of its variance, J(X) ≥ 1/var(X), with equality for the Gaussian.

nodes.name: de Bruijn's identity
nodes.description: The rate of change of the differential entropy of X + √t Z (Z standard Gaussian) with respect to t equals half the Fisher information: (d/dt) h(X+√t Z) = (1/2) J(X+√t Z).

nodes.name: Minkowski determinant inequality
nodes.description: For positive-definite K_1 and K_2, |K_1+K_2|^{1/n} ≥ |K_1|^{1/n} + |K_2|^{1/n}, the determinant analogue of the entropy power inequality.

nodes.name: Szász's inequality
nodes.description: A chain of inequalities relating the determinant of a positive-definite matrix to the geometric means of the determinants of its principal submatrices of each order, following from subset-entropy inequalities.

nodes.name: Han's inequality (subset entropy inequality)
nodes.description: The average of the entropies of all size-k subsets of a set of random variables, normalized by k, is nonincreasing in k, so larger subsets give smaller per-variable entropy.

nodes.name: Han's inequality for relative entropies
nodes.description: The analogue of Han's inequality for relative entropy, in which averaged subset relative entropies are monotone, used to derive determinant inequalities for ratios of distributions.

nodes.name: Subset inequalities for determinants
nodes.description: A family of inequalities, generalizing Hadamard and Szász, bounding the determinant of a covariance matrix by symmetric functions of the determinants of its principal submatrices.

nodes.name: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality (covariance form)
nodes.description: For random variables with finite second moments, (E[XY])^2 ≤ E[X^2]E[Y^2], used to bound covariances and underlie the Cramér–Rao bound.

nodes.name: Invariant σ-algebra of a measure-preserving transformation
nodes.description: For a measure-preserving map T on (Ω,F,P), the sub-σ-field 𝓘 = {A ∈ F : T⁻¹A = A} of T-invariant events, whose triviality (mod P) characterizes ergodicity of T.

nodes.name: σ-algebra generated by a random variable
nodes.description: For a measurable map X : (Ω,F) → (S,𝓢), the smallest sub-σ-field σ(X) = X⁻¹(𝓢) = {X⁻¹(B) : B ∈ 𝓢} making X measurable, encoding exactly the information carried by X.

nodes.name: Stieltjes measure function
nodes.description: A nondecreasing right-continuous function F : ℝ → ℝ that induces a unique Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure μ on (ℝ,𝓑) via μ((a,b]) = F(b) − F(a).

nodes.name: Feller's converse to the central limit theorem
nodes.description: For a uniformly asymptotically negligible triangular array whose row sums converge to a standard normal, the Lindeberg condition is necessary, i.e. asymptotic normality with negligible summands forces Lindeberg's condition to hold.

nodes.name: Esseen's smoothing inequality
nodes.description: Bounds the sup-norm distance between two distribution functions (one with bounded density) by an integral of the difference of their characteristic functions over a finite frequency window plus a remainder, supplying the analytic engine for Berry–Esseen-type rates.

nodes.name: Lindeberg replacement (swapping) method
nodes.function_signature: (Sum of independent summands, smooth test function f) → (CLT error bound via term-by-term Gaussian substitution)
nodes.description: Proves a central limit theorem by replacing the summands one at a time with matching-moment Gaussians and Taylor-expanding a smooth test function, telescoping the total error into a sum of small third-order remainders.

nodes.name: Standard machine (measure-theoretic bootstrap)
nodes.function_signature: (Property verified for indicators) → (Property for all integrable measurable functions)
nodes.description: Establishes a linear/monotone identity or inequality for general measurable functions by proving it first for indicator functions, then extending by linearity to simple functions, by monotone convergence to nonnegative measurable functions, and finally by difference to integrable functions.

nodes.name: Mixing implies ergodicity
nodes.description: Any (strongly or weakly) mixing measure-preserving transformation is ergodic, since asymptotic independence P(A ∩ T⁻ⁿB) → P(A)P(B) forces every invariant set to have measure 0 or 1.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov cycle condition
nodes.description: An irreducible positive-recurrent Markov chain with stationary distribution is reversible if and only if for every finite cycle x₀ → x₁ → … → xₙ = x₀ the product of forward transition probabilities equals the product of the reverse transition probabilities.

nodes.name: Multiplication (fundamental counting) principle
nodes.function_signature: (stages s_1,...,s_k with n_1,...,n_k choices each) → (total number of outcomes n_1·n_2·…·n_k)
nodes.description: The number of ways to perform a sequence of independent choices equals the product of the number of options available at each stage.

nodes.name: Ordered samples with replacement
nodes.description: The set of ordered r-tuples drawn with repetition allowed from n distinct objects, of which there are exactly n^r.

nodes.name: Ordered samples without replacement (permutations of r from n)
nodes.description: The set of ordered r-tuples of distinct elements chosen from n objects, of which there are exactly the falling factorial (n)_r = n!/(n−r)!.

nodes.name: Combinations with repetition (stars and bars)
nodes.function_signature: (n cell types, r indistinguishable items) → (number of unordered selections C(n+r−1, r))
nodes.description: A bijective counting technique placing r identical items into n categories by arranging r stars and n−1 bars, giving C(n+r−1, r) multisets.

nodes.name: Occupancy (balls in cells) model
nodes.description: The combinatorial probability model in which r balls are distributed among n cells, parametrizing classical distinguishability and exclusion assumptions.

nodes.name: Maxwell–Boltzmann statistics
nodes.description: The occupancy scheme in which r distinguishable balls are placed independently and uniformly into n cells, yielding n^r equally likely arrangements.

nodes.name: Boole's inequality (subadditivity)
nodes.description: The probability of a finite or countable union of events is at most the sum of their individual probabilities.

nodes.name: Multinomial theorem
nodes.description: The expansion of (x_1+…+x_m)^n as a sum over compositions of n of multinomial-coefficient-weighted monomials.

nodes.name: Probability of realizing exactly m of N events
nodes.description: The inclusion-exclusion-type formula expressing P(exactly m of N events occur) as an alternating sum of the binomial-weighted symmetric sums S_m, S_{m+1}, ….

nodes.name: Returns to the origin (u_{2n})
nodes.description: The probability u_{2n} that a simple symmetric random walk is back at the origin after 2n steps, equal to C(2n,n)2^{-2n}.

nodes.name: Iterated generating functions for branching processes
nodes.description: The generating function of the n-th generation size in a Galton–Watson process is the n-fold functional composition of the offspring generating function.

nodes.name: Sparre Andersen fluctuation theorem
nodes.description: A distribution-free combinatorial identity stating that for exchangeable increments the law of the number of positive partial sums equals the law of the index of the first maximum, underpinning random-walk fluctuation theory.

nodes.name: Independent increments process
nodes.description: A stochastic process whose increments over disjoint time intervals are mutually independent random variables.

nodes.name: Stationary increments
nodes.description: A stochastic process for which the distribution of an increment X_{t+h}−X_t depends only on the length h and not on the time t.

nodes.name: Bessel function densities
nodes.description: Probability densities expressed through modified Bessel functions, arising e.g. as first-passage densities of random walks and as laws of sums of independent exponential or noncentral chi-square variables.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov canonical representation
nodes.description: The canonical representation of the characteristic function of an infinitely divisible law with finite variance via a drift and a finite spectral measure K(dx), the finite-second-moment specialization of the Lévy–Khinchine formula.

nodes.name: Index of stability α
nodes.description: The exponent α ∈ (0,2] characterizing a stable distribution through the scaling relation of sums of i.i.d. copies and governing its tail behavior.

nodes.name: Types of distributions (affine equivalence)
nodes.description: The equivalence classes of distribution functions under affine transformations X ↦ aX+b (a>0), within which location and scale vary but shape is fixed.

nodes.name: Duality lemma for random walks
nodes.function_signature: (partial sums S_1,...,S_n of i.i.d. increments) → (equality in law with the reversed-order partial sums)
nodes.description: The time-reversal identity that the partial sums (S_1,…,S_n) have the same joint law as the reversed walk, relating first-passage and ladder events to maxima.

nodes.name: Transitive closure TC(x)
nodes.description: The smallest transitive set containing x as a subset, obtained by iterating union over ω.

nodes.name: Burali-Forti paradox
nodes.description: The class Ord of all ordinals is not a set; assuming it were yields an ordinal strictly greater than every ordinal.

nodes.name: Ordinal arithmetic
nodes.description: Addition, multiplication, and exponentiation of ordinals defined by transfinite recursion; associative but non-commutative.

nodes.name: Cantor normal form
nodes.description: Every ordinal α has a unique representation α=ω^{β₁}k₁+···+ω^{βₙ}kₙ with β₁>···>βₙ and positive integers kᵢ.

nodes.name: Epsilon numbers (ε-numbers)
nodes.description: Fixed points of ordinal exponentiation, i.e. ordinals ε satisfying ω^ε=ε, with ε₀ the least such ordinal.

nodes.name: Order type
nodes.description: The unique ordinal order-isomorphic to a given well-ordered set, given by the Mostowski collapse of its ∈-relation.

nodes.name: Rank function
nodes.description: The function assigning to each set x the least ordinal α with x∈V_{α+1}, measuring its position in the cumulative hierarchy.

nodes.name: ∈-induction (Foundation induction)
nodes.description: Proving a property holds of all sets by showing it holds of x whenever it holds of all elements of x, justified by Foundation.

nodes.name: Well-founded relation
nodes.description: A binary relation R on a class such that every nonempty subset has an R-minimal element, equivalently admits no infinite R-descending chain.

nodes.name: Well-founded recursion
nodes.function_signature: (WellFoundedRelation, G) → Function
nodes.description: Defining a function uniquely along a set-like well-founded relation by specifying its value at x in terms of its values at R-predecessors of x.

nodes.name: Hereditarily small sets H(κ)
nodes.description: The set of all sets whose transitive closure has cardinality strictly less than κ; H(κ) models ZFC minus Power Set for regular κ.

nodes.name: Aleph function ℵ_α
nodes.description: The order-isomorphism enumerating the infinite cardinals (initial ordinals) in increasing order, with ℵ₀ the least.

nodes.name: Initial ordinal
nodes.description: An ordinal not equinumerous with any smaller ordinal; the initial ordinals are exactly the cardinal numbers.

nodes.name: Cardinal arithmetic
nodes.description: Sum, product, and exponentiation of cardinals defined via cardinality of disjoint union, Cartesian product, and function space.

nodes.name: Hessenberg's theorem (κ²=κ)
nodes.description: Every infinite cardinal κ satisfies κ·κ=κ, proved via the Gödel pairing well-ordering of κ×κ.

nodes.name: Gödel pairing function
nodes.description: A definable well-ordering of Ord×Ord whose restriction to κ×κ is a bijection onto κ for every infinite cardinal κ.

nodes.name: Cofinality cf(α)
nodes.description: The least order type (equivalently least cardinality) of an unbounded subset of a limit ordinal α.

nodes.name: Regular cardinal
nodes.description: A cardinal κ with cf(κ)=κ, i.e. not the union of fewer than κ sets each of size less than κ.

nodes.name: Singular cardinal
nodes.description: A cardinal κ with cf(κ)<κ, i.e. expressible as a union of fewer than κ smaller sets.

nodes.name: Successor cardinals are regular
nodes.description: Under AC, every successor cardinal ℵ_{α+1} is regular.

nodes.name: Continuum function
nodes.description: The cardinal exponential κ↦2^κ giving the size of the power set; 2^{ℵ₀}=𝔠 is the continuum.

nodes.name: Hausdorff formula
nodes.description: For all α,β: ℵ_{α+1}^{ℵ_β}=ℵ_α^{ℵ_β}·ℵ_{α+1}, reducing successor-cardinal exponentiation.

nodes.name: Gimel function ℷ(κ)
nodes.description: The function ℷ(κ)=κ^{cf(κ)}; all cardinal exponentiation reduces to gimel values and the continuum function.

nodes.name: Beth function ℶ_α
nodes.description: The hierarchy ℶ₀=ℵ₀, ℶ_{α+1}=2^{ℶ_α}, ℶ_λ=sup_{α<λ}ℶ_α of iterated power-set cardinals.

nodes.name: Generalized Continuum Hypothesis (GCH)
nodes.description: The assertion 2^{ℵ_α}=ℵ_{α+1} for every ordinal α, equivalently ℶ_α=ℵ_α for all α.

nodes.name: Tukey's lemma
nodes.description: Every nonempty family of finite character has a maximal element under inclusion; equivalent to the Axiom of Choice.

nodes.name: Trichotomy of cardinals
nodes.description: For any sets X,Y either |X|≤|Y| or |Y|≤|X|; this comparability of all cardinals is equivalent to AC.

nodes.name: Ideal (set-theoretic)
nodes.description: A family of subsets closed downward and under finite unions and not containing the whole set; the dual notion to a filter.

nodes.name: κ-complete filter
nodes.description: A filter closed under intersections of fewer than κ of its members.

nodes.name: Principal vs non-principal ultrafilter
nodes.description: A principal ultrafilter is the set of all supersets of a fixed point; a non-principal one contains the cofinite filter (Fréchet filter).

nodes.name: Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem
nodes.description: Every proper filter on a set (or Boolean algebra) extends to an ultrafilter; weaker than full AC.

nodes.name: Complete Boolean algebra
nodes.description: A Boolean algebra in which every subset has a least upper bound (and dually a greatest lower bound).

nodes.name: Regular open algebra RO(P)
nodes.description: The complete Boolean algebra of regular open subsets of a topological space (or separative poset), serving as its canonical Boolean completion.

nodes.name: Closed unbounded (club) set
nodes.description: A subset of a regular uncountable cardinal κ that is unbounded and closed under suprema of its bounded subsets.

nodes.name: Club filter
nodes.description: The κ-complete normal filter on a regular uncountable κ generated by the closed unbounded subsets of κ.

nodes.name: Normal filter
nodes.description: A filter on a cardinal closed under diagonal intersection △_{α<κ}C_α; for the club filter this is equivalent to closure under regressive-function fibers.

nodes.name: Intersection of clubs is club
nodes.description: The intersection of fewer than κ club subsets of a regular uncountable κ is again club, so the club sets generate a κ-complete filter.

nodes.name: Tree (set-theoretic)
nodes.description: A partially ordered set (T,<) in which the predecessors of every node are well-ordered by <.

nodes.name: Branch, level, and height of a tree
nodes.description: A branch is a maximal chain, the α-th level is the set of nodes whose predecessors have order type α, and the height is the supremum of the levels.

nodes.name: Aronszajn tree
nodes.description: A κ-tree of height κ all of whose levels have size <κ and which has no branch of length κ.

nodes.name: Existence of an Aronszajn tree
nodes.description: An ℵ₁-Aronszajn tree exists in ZFC.

nodes.name: Suslin tree
nodes.description: An ℵ₁-tree with no uncountable chain and no uncountable antichain, equivalently a ccc Aronszajn tree.

nodes.name: Suslin's problem (Suslin Hypothesis)
nodes.description: The question whether every ccc dense complete linear order without endpoints is isomorphic to ℝ; SH asserts that it is.

nodes.name: Equivalence of Suslin tree and Suslin line
nodes.description: A Suslin line exists if and only if a Suslin tree exists.

nodes.name: Kurepa tree / Kurepa's hypothesis
nodes.description: An ℵ₁-tree with countable levels and at least ℵ₂ uncountable branches; Kurepa's Hypothesis asserts one exists.

nodes.name: Special Aronszajn tree
nodes.description: An Aronszajn tree that is the union of countably many antichains, equivalently admitting an order-preserving map into ℚ.

nodes.name: Partition calculus (arrow notation)
nodes.description: The notation κ→(λ)^n_m meaning every m-coloring of the n-element subsets of κ has a homogeneous subset of order type λ.

nodes.name: Square principle □_κ (Jensen)
nodes.description: The existence of a coherent sequence ⟨C_α:α<κ⁺⟩ of clubs C_α⊆α with otp(C_α)≤κ and coherence under limit points, holding in L.

nodes.name: Club principle ♣
nodes.description: A guessing principle giving a sequence ⟨A_α⟩ of cofinal subsets A_α⊆α such that every uncountable X⊆ω₁ contains some A_α; a weakening of ◊.

nodes.name: ◊ implies CH
nodes.description: The diamond principle ◊ on ω₁ implies the Continuum Hypothesis.

nodes.name: Singular Cardinal Hypothesis (SCH)
nodes.description: The assertion that for every singular κ with 2^{cf(κ)}<κ one has κ^{cf(κ)}=κ⁺.

nodes.name: Lévy hierarchy (Σ_n/Π_n)
nodes.description: The classification of set-theoretic formulas by the number of alternations of bounded-then-unbounded quantifiers into Σ_n, Π_n, Δ_n classes.

nodes.name: Absoluteness
nodes.function_signature: (Formula, TransitiveModels) → PreservedTruthValue
nodes.description: The method of showing a formula's truth is preserved between transitive models; Δ₀ formulas are absolute and Σ₁ formulas are upward absolute.

nodes.name: Elementary submodel method
nodes.function_signature: H(θ) → CountableElementarySubmodel
nodes.description: Taking a countable elementary submodel M≺H(θ) and applying its Mostowski collapse as a core tool for combinatorial set theory.

nodes.name: Skolem functions / Skolem hull
nodes.function_signature: (Structure, Set) → ElementarySubstructure
nodes.description: Closing a set of parameters under definable Skolem witnessing functions to obtain an elementary substructure.

nodes.name: Gödel operations 𝒢₁–𝒢₁₀
nodes.function_signature: Sets → Set
nodes.description: A finite list of ten basic finitary set operations whose closure yields exactly the Σ₀-definable (rudimentary) functions used to build L.

nodes.name: Constructible well-ordering <_L
nodes.description: The canonical Σ₁-definable well-ordering of the constructible universe L obtained from the stagewise construction of the L_α.

nodes.name: AC holds in L
nodes.description: The constructible universe L satisfies the Axiom of Choice via the definable global well-ordering <_L.

nodes.name: Relative constructibility L[A]
nodes.description: The smallest inner model of ZF closed under the definable-power-set operation relativized to a predicate A.

nodes.name: Constructible closure L(A)
nodes.description: The smallest inner model of ZF containing the set A (and its transitive closure) as an element.

nodes.name: ◊ holds in L (Jensen)
nodes.description: V=L implies the diamond principle ◊_κ on every regular uncountable κ, proved via condensation.

nodes.name: □_κ holds in L (Jensen)
nodes.description: V=L implies Jensen's square principle □_κ for every uncountable cardinal κ, proved by fine-structure methods.

nodes.name: Kurepa tree exists in L
nodes.description: V=L (via ◊⁺) implies the existence of a Kurepa tree.

nodes.name: Rudimentary functions
nodes.function_signature: Sets → Set
nodes.description: The class of functions generated by the Gödel operations and closed under composition and bounded quantification, used to define the J-hierarchy.

nodes.name: Jensen J-hierarchy J_α
nodes.description: A refinement of the constructible hierarchy built by rudimentary closure, satisfying smooth condensation at every level.

nodes.name: Σ_n-projectum ρ_n
nodes.description: For a fine-structural level, the least ordinal ρ such that some Σ_n-definable (with parameters) subset of ρ is not a member of the level.

nodes.name: Fine-structural condensation
nodes.function_signature: Σ_n-Submodel → J-level
nodes.description: The principle that Σ_n-elementary submodels of J-levels collapse to J-levels, refining Gödel's condensation lemma.

nodes.name: Silver indiscernibles
nodes.description: A closed unbounded class of ordinal order-indiscernibles for L that generate L via Skolem functions; they exist iff 0# exists.

nodes.name: 0# exists implies V≠L
nodes.description: If 0# exists then every uncountable cardinal is inaccessible (indeed indiscernible) in L, so V≠L.

nodes.name: Covering lemma implies SCH
nodes.description: If 0# does not exist, Jensen's covering lemma holds and implies the Singular Cardinal Hypothesis.

nodes.name: Notion of forcing
nodes.description: A separative partial order (P,≤,𝟙) of conditions used to extend a ground model by a generic filter.

nodes.name: Dense and predense sets
nodes.description: A subset D of a forcing poset is dense if every condition has an extension in D, and predense if every condition is compatible with a member of D.

nodes.name: Compatible and incompatible conditions
nodes.description: Two conditions are compatible if they have a common extension and incompatible otherwise; an antichain is a set of pairwise incompatible conditions.

nodes.name: Rasiowa–Sikorski lemma
nodes.description: For any countable family of dense subsets of a poset there is a filter meeting every member of the family.

nodes.name: P-names
nodes.function_signature: (Poset) → Name
nodes.description: Hereditarily P-labeled sets that name potential elements of a forcing extension and are interpreted via a generic filter G.

nodes.name: Canonical names (x̌, Ġ)
nodes.function_signature: (GroundSet) → Name
nodes.description: The check-name x̌ denoting a ground-model set x and the name Ġ denoting the generic filter in the forcing extension.

nodes.name: Forcing relation p⊩φ
nodes.description: The relation holding when p∈P forces φ, i.e. φ is true in M[G] for every generic G containing p.

nodes.name: Definability lemma (forcing)
nodes.description: For each formula φ the forcing relation p⊩φ is definable in the ground model.

nodes.name: Truth lemma
nodes.description: For a generic G, M[G]⊨φ if and only if some condition p∈G forces φ.

nodes.name: Forcing theorem (fundamental)
nodes.description: The Definability and Truth lemmas together reduce truth in M[G] to a ground-model-definable forcing relation.

nodes.name: Ground model definability
nodes.description: The ground model M is definable, with a parameter, inside any of its set-generic extensions (Laver–Woodin).

nodes.name: Separativity / separative quotient
nodes.function_signature: Poset → SeparativePoset
nodes.description: Replacing a forcing poset by its separative quotient, densely embeddable into the regular open completion / a complete Boolean algebra.

nodes.name: Cohen forcing
nodes.function_signature: Fn(I,2) → CohenReal
nodes.description: Forcing with finite partial functions Fn(I,2) to adjoin a new real (or I-many mutually generic Cohen reals).

nodes.name: Countable chain condition (ccc)
nodes.description: A forcing poset has the ccc if every antichain in it is countable.

nodes.name: ccc forcing preserves cardinals
nodes.description: A ccc forcing notion preserves all cardinals and cofinalities of the ground model.

nodes.name: Cohen forcing is ccc
nodes.description: The poset Fn(I,2) satisfies the countable chain condition, proved via the Δ-system lemma.

nodes.name: Nice names
nodes.function_signature: (ccc poset, GroundSet) → Name
nodes.description: Antichain-indexed names for subsets of a ground-model set, used to count the subsets appearing in a ccc extension.

nodes.name: Con(ZFC)⟹Con(ZFC+¬CH) (Cohen)
nodes.description: Forcing with Fn(ω₂×ω,2) over a model of ZFC yields a ccc extension in which 2^{ℵ₀}=ℵ₂, so ¬CH is consistent.

nodes.name: Boolean-valued universe V^B
nodes.description: The hierarchy of B-valued names with each formula assigned a truth value ‖φ‖∈B, an alternative formulation of forcing.

nodes.name: Boolean truth value ‖φ‖
nodes.function_signature: Formula → CompleteBooleanAlgebra
nodes.description: The recursively defined element of a complete Boolean algebra B giving the degree of truth of a formula in V^B.

nodes.name: Mixing lemma
nodes.description: Given a maximal antichain {b_i} and names {ẋ_i}, there is a single name ẋ with b_i≤‖ẋ=ẋ_i‖ for all i.

nodes.name: Maximum principle (forcing)
nodes.description: If ‖∃x φ(x)‖=b in V^B then there is a name ẋ with ‖φ(ẋ)‖=b.

nodes.name: Lévy collapse Coll(ω,κ)
nodes.function_signature: Cardinal → CollapsingForcing
nodes.description: Forcing with finite (or appropriate) conditions that collapses a cardinal κ, or all cardinals below λ, to ω.

nodes.name: <κ-closed forcing
nodes.description: A forcing notion in which every descending sequence of length <κ has a lower bound.

nodes.name: <κ-closed forcing adds no new <κ-sequences
nodes.description: A <κ-closed forcing adds no new sequences of length <κ, hence preserves H_κ and all cardinals up to κ.

nodes.name: κ-cc / κ-Knaster
nodes.description: A poset is κ-cc if all its antichains have size <κ, and κ-Knaster if every κ-sized subset has a κ-sized pairwise-compatible subset.

nodes.name: κ-cc forcing preserves cardinals ≥κ
nodes.description: A κ-cc forcing notion preserves all cardinals and cofinalities greater than or equal to κ.

nodes.name: Product forcing lemma
nodes.description: G×H is P×Q-generic over M iff G is P-generic over M and H is Q-generic over M[G], and then M[G×H]=M[G][H].

nodes.name: Two-step iteration P∗Q̇
nodes.function_signature: (P, P-name Q̇) → Poset
nodes.description: The forcing that first forces with P and then with a P-name Q̇ for a poset, realized by ordered pairs of conditions.

nodes.name: Martin's Axiom MA_κ
nodes.description: For every ccc poset and every family of at most κ dense sets there is a filter meeting all of them.

nodes.name: Martin's Axiom (MA)
nodes.description: The assertion that MA_κ holds for every κ<2^{ℵ₀}.

nodes.name: MA_{ℵ₀} is a theorem of ZFC
nodes.description: Martin's Axiom for countably many dense sets is provable in ZFC, being exactly the Rasiowa–Sikorski lemma.

nodes.name: Con(MA+¬CH) (Solovay–Tennenbaum)
nodes.description: A finite-support ccc iteration of length ω₂ forces MA together with 2^{ℵ₀}=ℵ₂.

nodes.name: Finite-support iteration
nodes.function_signature: ⟨P_α,Q̇_α⟩ → IterationLimit
nodes.description: An iterated forcing construction in which conditions have finite support, used to obtain ccc-preserving limits.

nodes.name: FS iteration of ccc is ccc
nodes.description: A finite-support iteration of ccc forcing notions is itself ccc, proved via the Δ-system lemma.

nodes.name: MA_{ℵ₁} implies ¬CH
nodes.description: Martin's Axiom for ℵ₁ dense sets implies 2^{ℵ₀}>ℵ₁, refuting the Continuum Hypothesis.

nodes.name: Con(SH) (Solovay–Tennenbaum)
nodes.description: Suslin's Hypothesis is consistent with ZFC, obtained from a model of MA+¬CH which kills all Suslin trees.

nodes.name: MA and additivity of measure/category
nodes.description: Under MA_κ the union of at most κ Lebesgue-null (resp. meager) sets of reals is null (resp. meager).

nodes.name: Countable-support iteration
nodes.function_signature: ⟨P_α,Q̇_α⟩ → ProperIterationLimit
nodes.description: An iterated forcing construction with countable support, the standard framework for iterating proper forcings.

nodes.name: Properness preserved under CS iteration
nodes.description: Countable-support iterations of proper forcing notions are proper (Shelah).

nodes.name: Mahlo cardinal
nodes.description: A regular cardinal κ for which the set of inaccessible cardinals below κ is stationary in κ.

nodes.name: Weakly compact cardinal
nodes.description: An inaccessible cardinal κ with the tree property, equivalently satisfying κ→(κ)²₂ or Π¹₁-indescribability.

nodes.name: Tree property characterization of weak compactness
nodes.description: For an inaccessible κ, weak compactness is equivalent to the tree property and to the partition relation κ→(κ)²₂.

nodes.name: Normal measure
nodes.description: A κ-complete nonprincipal ultrafilter on a measurable cardinal κ closed under diagonal intersections; equivalently the constant function is least nontrivial in the ultrapower.

nodes.name: Ultrapower Ult(V,U)
nodes.function_signature: (Class, κ-complete U) → (TransitiveModel, j)
nodes.description: Forming V^κ/U and collapsing the well-founded structure to a transitive inner model M with elementary embedding j:V→M.

nodes.name: Measurable cardinals and elementary embeddings
nodes.description: κ is measurable iff there is a nontrivial elementary embedding j:V→M into a transitive class with critical point κ.

nodes.name: Iterated ultrapowers
nodes.function_signature: (Model, Measure) → CommutativeSystemOfEmbeddings
nodes.description: Repeatedly taking ultrapowers by images of a measure to produce a directed system of elementary embeddings and iterates.

nodes.name: Ramsey cardinal
nodes.description: A cardinal κ satisfying the partition relation κ→(κ)^{<ω}_2.

nodes.name: Erdős cardinal κ→(α)^{<ω}
nodes.description: For an ordinal α, the least cardinal κ(α) satisfying the partition relation κ→(α)^{<ω}_2.

nodes.name: Ehrenfeucht–Mostowski models
nodes.function_signature: (OrderIndiscernibles) → ElementarySubmodel
nodes.description: Building elementary submodels generated over a set of order-indiscernibles via Skolem functions, the engine producing sharps.

nodes.name: κ→(ω₁)^{<ω} implies 0# exists
nodes.description: The existence of an Erdős/Ramsey-type cardinal with κ→(ω₁)^{<ω} yields uncountably many indiscernibles for L, hence 0#.

nodes.name: Strongly compact cardinal
nodes.description: A cardinal κ such that every κ-complete filter on any set extends to a κ-complete ultrafilter.

nodes.name: Huge cardinal
nodes.description: A cardinal κ admitting an elementary embedding j:V→M with critical point κ and ^{j(κ)}M⊆M.

nodes.name: Extenders
nodes.function_signature: (Embedding) → SystemOfUltrafilters
nodes.description: Coherent systems of ultrafilters coding a (possibly strong) elementary embedding, generalizing normal measures.

nodes.name: Vopěnka's principle
nodes.description: Every proper class of first-order structures of the same type contains two members one of which elementarily embeds into the other.

nodes.name: Proper forcing
nodes.description: A forcing notion preserving stationary subsets of [λ]^ω for all λ; equivalently generic conditions exist over countable elementary submodels.

nodes.name: Cantor space 2^ω
nodes.description: The space of infinite binary sequences with the product topology, a compact perfect totally disconnected Polish space.

nodes.name: Baire space homeomorphic to the irrationals
nodes.description: The Baire space ω^ω is homeomorphic to the space of irrational reals, via continued fractions.

nodes.name: Universality of Baire space
nodes.description: Every nonempty Polish space is a continuous image of the Baire space ω^ω.

nodes.name: Tree on a set and its body [T]
nodes.description: A set of finite sequences closed under initial segments; its body [T] of infinite branches is the corresponding closed subset of the product space.

nodes.name: Well-founded tree and its rank
nodes.description: A tree with no infinite branch, to which well-founded recursion assigns an ordinal rank.

nodes.name: Borel hierarchy (Σ⁰_α,Π⁰_α,Δ⁰_α)
nodes.description: The transfinite stratification of the Borel sets of a Polish space by iterated countable unions and complements.

nodes.name: Borel codes
nodes.function_signature: BorelSet → Real
nodes.description: Real-number codes for Borel sets making Borel relations definable and absolute between transitive models.

nodes.name: Property of Baire
nodes.description: A set has the Baire property if it differs from an open set by a meager set; the BP sets form a σ-algebra closed under the Suslin operation.

nodes.name: Suslin operation 𝒜
nodes.function_signature: (Sequences of sets) → AnalyticSet
nodes.description: The operation 𝒜_s A_s=⋃_f⋂_n A_{f↾n} on a Suslin scheme that generates the analytic sets from closed sets.

nodes.name: Coanalytic set Π¹₁
nodes.description: The complement of an analytic set; the first level of the projective hierarchy dual to Σ¹₁.

nodes.name: Cantor–Bendixson derivative and rank
nodes.function_signature: ClosedSet → (PerfectKernel, Ordinal)
nodes.description: The iterated removal of isolated points from a closed set, stabilizing at a countable ordinal rank and leaving the perfect kernel.

nodes.name: Perfect set property (PSP)
nodes.description: A set of reals has the PSP if it is either countable or contains a nonempty perfect subset.

nodes.name: Analytic sets have the perfect set property
nodes.description: Every uncountable analytic set contains a nonempty perfect subset.

nodes.name: Analytic sets are Lebesgue measurable
nodes.description: Every Σ¹₁ set is Lebesgue measurable.

nodes.name: Analytic sets have the Baire property
nodes.description: Every Σ¹₁ set has the property of Baire.

nodes.name: Universal analytic set
nodes.description: A single Σ¹₁ subset of (ω^ω)² that is universal for all Σ¹₁ subsets of ω^ω, witnessing Σ¹₁≠Π¹₁.

nodes.name: Π¹₁ norm / rank
nodes.function_signature: Π¹₁ set → (Element → Ordinal<ω₁)
nodes.description: A regular Π¹₁-norm assigning each member the ordinal rank of an associated well-founded tree, all below ω₁.

nodes.name: Σ¹₁-boundedness theorem
nodes.description: A Σ¹₁ subset of the well-founded trees has ranks bounded below ω₁.

nodes.name: Projective hierarchy (Σ¹_n,Π¹_n,Δ¹_n)
nodes.description: The hierarchy of pointclasses with Σ¹₁ the analytic sets, Π¹_n the complements, and Σ¹_{n+1} the projections of Π¹_n sets.

nodes.name: Projective hierarchy is proper
nodes.description: For each n there is a universal Σ¹_n set, and the projective hierarchy is strictly increasing.

nodes.name: Uniformization
nodes.description: Selecting for a relation R⊆X×Y a function with graph in R, with the graph required to lie in a given pointclass.

nodes.name: Σ¹₂-uniformization (Novikov–Kondô–Addison)
nodes.description: Every Σ¹₂ relation can be uniformized by a Σ¹₂ function.

nodes.name: Prewellordering property
nodes.description: A pointclass Γ has the prewellordering property if every Γ set admits a Γ-norm; Π¹₁ and Σ¹₂ have it.

nodes.name: Scale property
nodes.description: A set has a scale if there is a sequence of norms with a convergence/lower-semicontinuity property enabling uniformization.

nodes.name: Periodicity theorems (Moschovakis)
nodes.description: Under determinacy the prewellordering and scale properties propagate up the projective hierarchy in a periodic pattern.

nodes.name: Shoenfield tree
nodes.function_signature: Σ¹₂ set → Tree on ω×ω₁
nodes.description: A tree on ω×ω₁ whose projection is a given Σ¹₂ set, reducing membership to well-foundedness and giving Shoenfield absoluteness.

nodes.name: Σ¹₂ well-ordering under V=L
nodes.description: If V=L there is a Σ¹₂ well-ordering of the reals, yielding a Δ¹₂ non-Lebesgue-measurable set.

nodes.name: Constructible reals ℝ∩L
nodes.description: The reals belonging to L, a Σ¹₂ set which under V=L equals all reals.

nodes.name: Infinite game G(A) and strategy
nodes.description: A two-player perfect-information game on ω where players alternately play naturals, I winning iff the resulting real lies in A; a strategy is a function dictating moves.

nodes.name: Determinacy of a set Det(A)
nodes.description: The property that one of the two players has a winning strategy in the game G(A).

nodes.name: Gale–Stewart theorem
nodes.description: Every open game and every closed game (on a tree) is determined.

nodes.name: Unraveling / covering technique
nodes.function_signature: (Game, Tree) → ClopenGameOnLargerTree
nodes.description: Lifting a game to an auxiliary tree on which the payoff set becomes clopen, the key device in Martin's proof of Borel determinacy.

nodes.name: AD implies all sets Lebesgue measurable
nodes.description: Under the Axiom of Determinacy every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable.

nodes.name: AD implies the Baire property for all sets
nodes.description: Under the Axiom of Determinacy every set of reals has the property of Baire, via the Banach–Mazur game.

nodes.name: AD implies perfect set property for all sets
nodes.description: Under the Axiom of Determinacy every uncountable set of reals contains a perfect subset.

nodes.name: Banach–Mazur game
nodes.function_signature: (Set A) → comeagerness criterion
nodes.description: An infinite game in which players choose decreasing basic open sets, characterizing comeagerness and the Baire property of A.

nodes.name: Analytic determinacy
nodes.description: Every analytic (Σ¹₁) game is determined; this is equivalent to the existence of sharps for all reals and follows from a measurable cardinal (Martin, Harrington).

nodes.name: Sharps and analytic determinacy equivalence
nodes.description: The existence of x# for every real x is equivalent to the determinacy of all analytic games (Harrington–Martin).

nodes.name: Homogeneously Suslin set / homogeneous tree
nodes.function_signature: (Tree, system of measures) → DeterminedSet
nodes.description: A tree carrying a coherent commuting system of countably complete measures whose projection is a homogeneously Suslin (hence determined) set.

nodes.name: Martin–Steel theorem (projective determinacy)
nodes.description: n Woodin cardinals with a measurable above imply Π¹_{n+1}-determinacy; infinitely many Woodins imply full projective determinacy.

nodes.name: PD implies regularity for all projective sets
nodes.description: Projective Determinacy implies every projective set is Lebesgue measurable, has the Baire property and the perfect set property, and projective relations can be uniformized.

nodes.name: AD equiconsistent with infinitely many Woodins
nodes.description: Con(ZF+AD) is equivalent to Con(ZFC+there are infinitely many Woodin cardinals) (Woodin).

nodes.name: Wadge reducibility / Wadge hierarchy
nodes.description: A≤_W B iff A=f^{-1}(B) for a continuous f; under determinacy the induced degrees form a nearly well-ordered hierarchy.

nodes.name: Solovay's model construction via Lévy collapse
nodes.function_signature: (Inaccessible κ) → ModelOfZF+DC
nodes.description: Lévy-collapsing an inaccessible cardinal to ω₁ and passing to the L(ℝ) of the extension to obtain a ZF+DC model in which all sets are Lebesgue measurable, Baire, and have the PSP.

nodes.name: Inaccessible necessary for all sets Lebesgue measurable (Shelah)
nodes.description: If every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable (with DC) then ω₁ is inaccessible in L, so an inaccessible cardinal is needed for Solovay's model.

nodes.name: Transitive set
nodes.description: A set X every element of which is also a subset of X, so that membership never escapes X.

nodes.name: Δ₀ (bounded) formula
nodes.type_signature: first-order formula with only bounded quantifiers ∀x∈y, ∃x∈y
nodes.description: A first-order set-theoretic formula all of whose quantifiers are bounded, hence absolute between any transitive model and the universe.

nodes.name: Relativization φᴹ
nodes.function_signature: (formula φ, transitive class/set M) → (formula φᴹ with all quantifiers restricted to M)
nodes.description: The syntactic operation restricting every quantifier of a formula φ to range over a class or set M, expressing truth-in-M inside the ambient universe.

nodes.name: ◊⁺ (diamond-plus)
nodes.type_signature: ⟨A_α : α<ω₁⟩ with A_α ⊆ P(α) countable, guessing every X⊆ω₁ with a club on a club
nodes.description: A strengthening of ◊ assigning to each α<ω₁ a countable family A_α⊆P(α) such that for every X⊆ω₁ there is a club C with X∩α and C∩α both in A_α for all α∈C.

nodes.name: ◊⁺ implies a Kurepa tree (Jensen)
nodes.description: The principle ◊⁺ implies the existence of a Kurepa tree, a tree of height ω₁ with countable levels and at least ℵ₂ cofinal branches.

nodes.name: First-order signature (language)
nodes.description: A specification of constant symbols, function symbols, and relation symbols together with their arities, fixing the non-logical vocabulary of a first-order language.

nodes.name: L-structure
nodes.description: A nonempty set M together with interpretations of each constant, function, and relation symbol of a signature L as actual elements, functions, and relations on M.

nodes.name: L-term
nodes.description: A syntactic expression built from variables and constant symbols by repeated application of function symbols of the signature L.

nodes.name: L-formula
nodes.description: A well-formed syntactic expression built from atomic formulas (equalities and relation symbols applied to terms) using Boolean connectives and quantifiers over variables.

nodes.name: Tarski satisfaction relation
nodes.description: The recursively defined relation specifying when an L-structure M with a variable assignment makes an L-formula true, giving the semantics of first-order logic.

nodes.name: L-embedding
nodes.description: An injective map between L-structures preserving the interpretation of all constants, functions, and relations (and their negations on atomic formulas).

nodes.name: Substructure / extension
nodes.description: An L-structure M whose domain is a subset of N closed under N's functions and constants, with all symbols interpreted as restrictions of N's interpretations.

nodes.name: L-theory
nodes.description: A set of L-sentences (closed formulas), the models of which are the L-structures satisfying every sentence in the set.

nodes.name: Logical consequence (semantic entailment)
nodes.description: The relation holding when every model of a theory T also satisfies the sentence φ.

nodes.name: Axiomatizable theory
nodes.description: A theory closed under logical consequence that is the set of consequences of some (often finite or recursive) set of axioms.

nodes.name: Definable function and definable closure
nodes.description: A function whose graph is a definable set, and the definable closure dcl(A) consisting of all elements that are the unique realization of some formula over A.

nodes.name: Henkin construction
nodes.function_signature: (consistent L-theory T) → (term model M ⊨ T)
nodes.description: Expand T to a maximal consistent theory with witnessing constants for every existential sentence, then build a model out of equivalence classes of closed terms.

nodes.name: Tarski–Vaught test
nodes.description: A substructure M of N is an elementary substructure iff for every formula φ(x,b) with parameters in M that has a solution in N, it already has a solution in M.

nodes.name: Tarski's elementary chain theorem
nodes.description: The union of an elementary chain of L-structures is an elementary extension of each member of the chain.

nodes.name: Diagram lemma
nodes.description: Models of the atomic (elementary) diagram of M correspond exactly to L-structures admitting an embedding (elementary embedding) of M.

nodes.name: Elementary diagram
nodes.description: The set of all L_M-sentences true in M after adjoining a new constant for each element of M; its models are the elementary extensions of M.

nodes.name: Upward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem
nodes.description: Any infinite structure has elementary extensions of every cardinality κ ≥ max(|M|,|L|).

nodes.name: Löwenheim–Skolem–Tarski theorem
nodes.description: A first-order theory with an infinite model has a model of every cardinality κ ≥ |L|+ℵ₀.

nodes.name: Dense linear order without endpoints (DLO)
nodes.description: The complete ℵ₀-categorical theory of a dense linear order having no least and no greatest element.

nodes.name: Robinson's test for model completeness
nodes.type_signature: (∀ M,N ⊨ T, M⊆N: ∃-formulas preserved up) ⟹ T model complete
nodes.description: A theory is model complete iff every embedding between its models preserves existential formulas, equivalently every formula is equivalent to an existential one.

nodes.name: Quantifier elimination test
nodes.description: A theory admits quantifier elimination iff for any two models with a common substructure A, a primitive existential formula realized in one over A is realized in the other (a back-and-forth/substructure-completeness criterion).

nodes.name: Completeness and decidability of ACF_p
nodes.description: For each fixed characteristic, the theory of algebraically closed fields is complete and decidable, a consequence of its quantifier elimination.

nodes.name: Lefschetz principle
nodes.description: A first-order sentence holds in the complex field iff it holds in every algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (and in characteristic p for all large p), by completeness of ACF.

nodes.name: Ax's theorem (injective endomorphisms are surjective)
nodes.type_signature: f: V→V injective polynomial map ⟹ surjective
nodes.description: Every injective polynomial map of an algebraic variety over an algebraically closed field to itself is surjective, proved by transfer from finite fields.

nodes.name: Completeness and decidability of RCF
nodes.description: The theory of real closed ordered fields is complete and decidable, following from Tarski's quantifier elimination for RCF.

nodes.name: Hilbert's 17th problem (model-theoretic form)
nodes.description: Every positive semidefinite rational function over a real closed field is a sum of squares of rational functions, derived via the model completeness of RCF.

nodes.name: Quantifier elimination for Presburger arithmetic
nodes.description: The first-order theory of the additive integers admits quantifier elimination in the language expanded by congruence-mod-n predicates.

nodes.name: Omitting Types Theorem
nodes.type_signature: non-isolated type p ⟹ ∃ countable M omitting p
nodes.description: A countable theory has a countable model omitting any given non-isolated (non-principal) partial type, generalizable to countably many such types.

nodes.name: Isolated (principal) type
nodes.description: A complete type generated by a single formula φ, i.e. an isolated point of the Stone space of types, realized in every model containing A.

nodes.name: Prime model
nodes.description: A model of a complete theory that elementarily embeds into every other model of the theory.

nodes.name: Atomic model
nodes.description: A model in which every tuple realizes an isolated (principal) complete type over the empty set.

nodes.name: Prime ⟺ countable atomic
nodes.description: For a complete countable theory, a model is prime iff it is countable and atomic, and such a model is unique up to isomorphism when it exists.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of prime/atomic models
nodes.description: A complete countable theory has a (unique up to isomorphism) prime model iff the isolated types are dense in every Stone space Sₙ(∅).

nodes.name: Uniqueness of saturated models
nodes.type_signature: two κ-saturated models of card κ ⟹ isomorphic
nodes.description: Any two saturated models of a complete theory having the same cardinality are isomorphic, proved by a back-and-forth argument.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of homogeneous models
nodes.type_signature: same card + same realized types ⟹ isomorphic
nodes.description: Two homogeneous models of the same cardinality realizing exactly the same types are isomorphic.

nodes.name: Universal model
nodes.description: A model into which every model of the theory of cardinality at most |M| elementarily embeds.

nodes.name: Monster model
nodes.description: A very large saturated and strongly homogeneous model serving as a universal domain inside which all small models and all types under study are realized.

nodes.name: Ehrenfeucht–Mostowski type (EM-type)
nodes.type_signature: Φ: order type ↦ type of indiscernibles
nodes.description: The complete type, indexed by increasing tuples, shared by an order-indiscernible sequence, determining a functor from linear orders to models.

nodes.name: Existence of indiscernibles
nodes.type_signature: any infinite (M, I) ⟹ ∃ indiscernible J realizing EM-type
nodes.description: For any theory with infinite models and any infinite linear order, there is a model containing a sequence of order-indiscernibles, obtained via Ramsey's theorem and compactness.

nodes.name: Few types over EM models
nodes.description: A model generated as the Skolem hull of order-indiscernibles realizes only few types over itself, used to control the number of types and models.

nodes.name: Vaughtian pair
nodes.description: A pair of models M ≺ N with M ≠ N but having the same infinite solution set for some formula φ, witnessing a two-cardinal phenomenon.

nodes.name: Uncountably categorical theories have no Vaughtian pairs
nodes.description: An uncountably categorical complete theory admits no Vaughtian pairs, a key step in the proof of Morley's theorem.

nodes.name: Morley degree
nodes.description: For a definable set of finite Morley rank, the maximum number of disjoint definable subsets of the same rank, measuring multiplicity at that rank.

nodes.name: Totally transcendental theory
nodes.type_signature: every formula has ordinal Morley rank
nodes.description: A theory in which every definable set has an ordinal-valued Morley rank, equivalent to ω-stability for countable languages.

nodes.name: ω-stable ⟹ totally transcendental
nodes.description: An ω-stable theory is totally transcendental, so every definable set carries a well-defined Morley rank and degree.

nodes.name: Definability of types (and heirs)
nodes.description: In a stable (in particular ω-stable) theory, every type over a model is definable, giving canonical extensions (heirs and coheirs) to larger sets.

nodes.name: Uncountably categorical ⟹ ω-stable
nodes.description: Every uncountably categorical countable complete theory is ω-stable, a central lemma in Morley's categoricity theorem.

nodes.name: ω-stable group / group of finite Morley rank
nodes.description: A group definable in an ω-stable theory, whose definable subsets carry Morley rank and degree, modeling algebraic-group-like behavior.

nodes.name: Descending chain condition on definable subgroups
nodes.type_signature: no infinite descending chain of definable subgroups
nodes.description: In an ω-stable (finite Morley rank) group there is no infinite strictly descending chain of definable subgroups, yielding a connected component.

nodes.name: Connected component G⁰
nodes.description: The smallest definable subgroup of finite index in a group of finite Morley rank, normal in G, called the connected component.

nodes.name: Generic type of a group
nodes.description: A type of an element of a finite-Morley-rank group whose Morley rank equals that of the whole group, invariant under translation in the connected case.

nodes.name: Stabilizer of a type
nodes.description: The definable subgroup of group elements fixing the (translated) type p, central to analyzing generic data in finite-Morley-rank groups.

nodes.name: Zilber indecomposability theorem
nodes.type_signature: family of indecomposable Xᵢ ∋ 1 ⟹ ⟨Xᵢ⟩ definable connected
nodes.description: In a group of finite Morley rank, the subgroup generated by a family of definable indecomposable subsets each containing the identity is definable and connected, an analogue of indecomposable algebraic subsets generating subgroups.

nodes.name: Macintyre's theorem
nodes.description: Every infinite ω-stable field is algebraically closed.

nodes.name: ω-stable division rings are commutative
nodes.description: An infinite division ring whose theory is ω-stable is commutative, hence an algebraically closed field.

nodes.name: Algebraic closure gives a pregeometry
nodes.description: On a strongly minimal set, the model-theoretic algebraic closure operator satisfies finite character, monotonicity, idempotence, and exchange, forming a pregeometry.

nodes.name: Exchange property for acl (Steinitz exchange)
nodes.description: In a strongly minimal theory, if a is algebraic over B together with c but not over B alone, then c is algebraic over B and a, the abstract Steinitz exchange axiom.

nodes.name: Pregeometry (combinatorial geometry)
nodes.description: A set with a closure operator satisfying reflexivity, monotonicity, finite character, idempotence, and the exchange property, abstracting linear/algebraic dependence (a matroid-like structure).

nodes.name: Dimension and independence in a pregeometry
nodes.description: The common cardinality of any maximal independent (closure-free) subset of a set, well-defined by the exchange property and additive over closures.

nodes.name: Dimension determines the model
nodes.description: Two models of a strongly minimal theory are isomorphic iff their associated pregeometries have the same dimension, the mechanism behind uncountable categoricity.

nodes.name: Trivial (degenerate) geometry
nodes.description: A pregeometry in which the closure of any set is the union of the closures of its points, exhibiting no nontrivial dependence.

nodes.name: Locally modular geometry
nodes.type_signature: modularity of cl over a point
nodes.description: A pregeometry that becomes modular after localizing at a single point, equivalently dim(A∪B)+dim(A∩B)=dim(A)+dim(B) for closed sets with nonempty intersection.

nodes.name: Locally modular ⟺ no definable field
nodes.description: A non-trivial strongly minimal set is non-locally-modular iff it interprets an infinite field (an algebraically closed field), linking geometry to definable algebraic structure.

nodes.name: Zilber's trichotomy conjecture
nodes.type_signature: strongly minimal ⟹ trivial / modular group / ACF
nodes.description: The conjecture that every strongly minimal set is either trivial, the geometry of a modular group (vector-space-like), or interprets an algebraically closed field; true for Zariski geometries, false in general.

nodes.name: Locally modular ⟹ group-based geometry
nodes.description: A non-trivial locally modular strongly minimal set interprets an abelian group whose geometry is essentially that of a vector space over a division ring (group configuration / 1-basedness).

nodes.name: Model completeness of ACF
nodes.description: The theory of algebraically closed fields is model complete: every embedding between algebraically closed fields is elementary, equivalently a Nullstellensatz statement.

nodes.name: Robinson's test application to ACF/RCF
nodes.description: A model-complete theory with a model embedding into every model (e.g. the prime field) is complete, used to derive completeness of ACF_p and RCF.

nodes.name: Signature
nodes.type_signature: L = (constants, function symbols with arities, relation symbols with arities)
nodes.description: A signature (language) is a set of constant symbols, function symbols, and relation symbols each equipped with an arity.

nodes.name: Domain (universe)
nodes.description: The domain or universe of a structure is the underlying set on which its functions and relations are defined.

nodes.name: Cardinality of a structure
nodes.description: The cardinality of a structure is the cardinality of its domain.

nodes.name: Term
nodes.description: A term is a syntactic expression built from variables and constants by repeated application of function symbols.

nodes.name: Term function (value of a term)
nodes.description: The term function is the map sending an assignment of domain elements to variables to the value the term takes under that assignment in the structure.

nodes.name: Homomorphism
nodes.type_signature: h : A → B preserving functions and relations
nodes.description: A homomorphism is a map between structures of the same signature that commutes with all function symbols and preserves all relation symbols.

nodes.name: Isomorphism
nodes.type_signature: f : A → B bijective with f, f^{-1} embeddings
nodes.description: An isomorphism is a bijective homomorphism whose inverse is also a homomorphism, so it preserves and reflects all functions and relations.

nodes.name: Substructure generated by a set
nodes.type_signature: ⟨X⟩_A = smallest substructure of A containing X
nodes.description: The substructure generated by a subset X is the smallest substructure containing X, consisting of all values of terms with parameters in X.

nodes.name: Reduct and expansion
nodes.description: A reduct is a structure obtained by forgetting some symbols of the signature, and its expansion is a structure on the same domain interpreting additional symbols.

nodes.name: Diagram (atomic/literal)
nodes.type_signature: Diag(A) = set of atomic and negated-atomic sentences true in A_A
nodes.description: The diagram of a structure is the set of all atomic and negated atomic sentences with parameters that hold in the structure expanded by names for its elements.

nodes.name: Canonical (term) structure
nodes.description: A canonical or term structure is a structure whose elements are equivalence classes of closed terms, used in Henkin-style constructions.

nodes.name: First-order formula
nodes.description: A first-order formula is a syntactic expression built from atomic formulas using boolean connectives and quantification over individual variables.

nodes.name: Atomic formula
nodes.description: An atomic formula is a relation symbol or equality applied to terms, with no connectives or quantifiers.

nodes.name: Free and bound variables
nodes.description: A variable occurrence is bound if it lies within the scope of a quantifier binding it and free otherwise.

nodes.name: Sentence
nodes.description: A sentence is a first-order formula with no free variables.

nodes.name: Parametrically definable set
nodes.type_signature: {ā ∈ A^n : A ⊨ φ(ā,b̄)} for parameters b̄
nodes.description: A parametrically definable set is the solution set in a structure of a formula allowing parameters from the domain.

nodes.name: Theory of a structure Th(A)
nodes.description: The theory of a structure is the set of all first-order sentences true in it.

nodes.name: Elementary equivalence
nodes.description: Two structures are elementarily equivalent when they satisfy exactly the same first-order sentences.

nodes.name: Elementary embedding
nodes.type_signature: f : A → B with A ⊨ φ(ā) ⟺ B ⊨ φ(f ā)
nodes.description: An elementary embedding is a map between structures that preserves the truth of all first-order formulas with parameters.

nodes.name: Elementary Diagram Lemma
nodes.type_signature: B ⊨ ElDiag(A) ⟺ ∃ elementary embedding A → B↾L
nodes.description: The elementary diagram lemma states that models of the elementary diagram of a structure correspond exactly to its elementary extensions (up to elementary embedding).

nodes.name: Back-and-forth equivalence (potential isomorphism)
nodes.type_signature: A ≅_p B via a nonempty set of partial isomorphisms with back-and-forth property
nodes.description: Back-and-forth equivalence (potential isomorphism) holds between two structures when there is a nonempty family of partial isomorphisms closed under extending any member by one element on either side.

nodes.name: Cantor's theorem on DLO
nodes.type_signature: any two countable DLOs are isomorphic
nodes.description: Cantor's theorem states that any two countable dense linear orders without endpoints are isomorphic.

nodes.name: Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé game
nodes.description: The Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé game is a two-player game of n rounds in which Duplicator must maintain a partial isomorphism against Spoiler's element choices in two structures.

nodes.name: Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé theorem
nodes.description: The Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé theorem states that Duplicator has a winning strategy in the n-round game exactly when the two structures agree on all sentences of quantifier rank at most n.

nodes.name: Quantifier rank
nodes.description: The quantifier rank of a formula is the maximal depth of nesting of quantifiers occurring in it.

nodes.name: Hintikka formulas
nodes.type_signature: φ^n_ā : formula of quantifier rank n describing the n-type of ā
nodes.description: Hintikka formulas are the finitely many formulas of a given quantifier rank that completely describe a tuple up to back-and-forth equivalence of that rank.

nodes.name: Age of a structure
nodes.type_signature: Age(A) = { finitely generated B : B embeds in A } (up to iso)
nodes.description: The age of a structure is the class of all finitely generated structures that embed into it.

nodes.name: Hereditary property (HP)
nodes.type_signature: B ∈ K and A embeds in B ⟹ A ∈ K
nodes.description: A class has the hereditary property when it is closed under taking finitely generated substructures.

nodes.name: Joint embedding property (JEP)
nodes.description: A class has the joint embedding property when any two of its members embed into a common member.

nodes.name: Amalgamation property (AP)
nodes.type_signature: A↪B, A↪C ⟹ ∃D with B↪D, C↪D agreeing on A
nodes.description: A class has the amalgamation property when any two extensions of a common member can be embedded into a single member compatibly over that member.

nodes.name: Fraïssé limit
nodes.type_signature: unique countable ultrahomogeneous M with Age(M) = K
nodes.description: The Fraïssé limit of a suitable class is the unique countable ultrahomogeneous structure whose age is that class.

nodes.name: Ultrahomogeneous structure
nodes.type_signature: every iso between finitely generated substructures extends to an automorphism
nodes.description: A structure is ultrahomogeneous when every isomorphism between finitely generated substructures extends to an automorphism of the whole structure.

nodes.name: Fraïssé's theorem
nodes.type_signature: K with HP,JEP,AP,countably many iso types ⟹ unique Fraïssé limit
nodes.description: Fraïssé's theorem states that a countable class closed under isomorphism with HP, JEP, and AP has a unique countable ultrahomogeneous structure as its limit.

nodes.name: Weak homogeneity
nodes.type_signature: finite partial isos extend one element at a time
nodes.description: Weak homogeneity is the property that any isomorphism between finitely generated substructures can be extended to include any one further element.

nodes.name: The random graph (Rado graph)
nodes.description: The random graph is the unique countable graph that is the Fraïssé limit of all finite graphs and satisfies the extension property.

nodes.name: Extension property (graphs)
nodes.type_signature: ∀ disjoint finite U,V ∃z adjacent to all of U, none of V
nodes.description: The extension property states that for any two disjoint finite sets of vertices there is another vertex joined to all of the first set and none of the second.

nodes.name: ℵ₀-categoricity of the random graph
nodes.description: The theory of the random graph is ℵ₀-categorical, having a unique countable model up to isomorphism.

nodes.name: Orbit and stabiliser
nodes.type_signature: orbit G·a, stabiliser G_a = {g : g·a = a}
nodes.description: For a group acting on a structure, the orbit of an element is its image set under the group and the stabiliser is the subgroup fixing it.

nodes.name: Permutation group topology
nodes.type_signature: basic open sets = cosets of pointwise stabilisers of finite tuples
nodes.description: The topology of pointwise convergence on a permutation group has as basic open sets the cosets of pointwise stabilisers of finite tuples.

nodes.name: Closed-subgroup characterization of automorphism groups
nodes.type_signature: G ≤ Sym(Ω) closed ⟺ G = Aut(A) for some structure A on Ω
nodes.description: A subgroup of the symmetric group on a set is the automorphism group of some structure exactly when it is closed in the topology of pointwise convergence.

nodes.name: k-homogeneity / k-transitivity
nodes.type_signature: G acts transitively on k-tuples (of distinct elements)
nodes.description: A permutation group is k-transitive when it acts transitively on ordered k-tuples of distinct elements, and k-homogeneous when transitive on k-element subsets.

nodes.name: Imaginary elements
nodes.type_signature: classes ā/E for ∅-definable equivalence relations E
nodes.description: Imaginary elements are equivalence classes of definable equivalence relations on tuples, adjoined to a structure to name quotients.

nodes.name: Small index property
nodes.type_signature: every subgroup of index < 2^ℵ0 is open
nodes.description: A countable structure has the small index property when every subgroup of its automorphism group of index less than the continuum is open.

nodes.name: Interpretation Γ
nodes.type_signature: Γ : A ⤳ B via definable domain, relations, and quotient
nodes.description: An interpretation of one structure in another is given by a definable subset, definable relations on it, and a definable equivalence relation whose quotient recovers the target structure.

nodes.name: Coordinate map
nodes.description: The coordinate map of an interpretation is the definable surjection from the interpreting definable set onto the domain of the interpreted structure.

nodes.name: Reduction of theories via interpretation
nodes.function_signature: (interpretation Γ : A⤳B, Th(A)) → (decision/transfer for Th(B))
nodes.description: Interpretation reduces questions about the interpreted structure (such as decidability or definability) to corresponding questions about the interpreting structure.

nodes.name: A^eq / M^eq construction
nodes.type_signature: A^eq = A with all imaginary sorts adjoined
nodes.description: The A^eq construction expands a structure by adding a sort for every ∅-definable equivalence relation together with the canonical projection maps.

nodes.name: Elimination of imaginaries
nodes.type_signature: every imaginary is interdefinable with a real tuple
nodes.description: A theory eliminates imaginaries when every definable equivalence class has a definable canonical representative as a tuple of real elements.

nodes.name: Pseudo-elementary class (PC)
nodes.type_signature: reducts of models of a theory in a larger signature
nodes.description: A pseudo-elementary class is the class of reducts to a signature of the models of a theory in a larger signature.

nodes.name: Word construction interpreting groups/fields
nodes.function_signature: (combinatorial/word data) → (interpreted group or field)
nodes.description: The word construction interprets a group or field inside a structure by encoding its elements and operations as definable words or coordinate tuples.

nodes.name: Gödel completeness theorem
nodes.description: The completeness theorem states that a first-order sentence is a semantic consequence of a theory if and only if it is provable from it.

nodes.name: Direct and reduced product
nodes.description: The direct product of structures is their coordinatewise product, and the reduced product modulo a filter identifies tuples agreeing on a set in the filter.

nodes.name: Compactness via ultraproducts
nodes.function_signature: (finitely satisfiable theory T) → (model of T as ultraproduct)
nodes.description: This technique proves the compactness theorem by building a model of a finitely satisfiable theory as an ultraproduct of models of its finite subsets.

nodes.name: Diagonal embedding into an ultrapower
nodes.description: The diagonal embedding sends each element of a structure to the class of the constant sequence, giving an elementary embedding into any ultrapower.
