nodes.name: Łoś–Tarski preservation theorem
nodes.type_signature: φ preserved under substructures ⟺ φ equivalent to a universal sentence
nodes.description: The Łoś–Tarski theorem states that a first-order sentence is preserved under substructures if and only if it is logically equivalent to a universal sentence.

nodes.name: Chang–Łoś–Suszko theorem
nodes.type_signature: φ preserved under unions of chains ⟺ equivalent to ∀∃ sentence
nodes.description: The Chang–Łoś–Suszko theorem states that a sentence is preserved under unions of chains if and only if it is equivalent to a universal-existential (∀∃) sentence.

nodes.name: Lyndon's preservation theorem
nodes.type_signature: φ preserved under surjective homomorphisms ⟺ equivalent to a positive sentence
nodes.description: Lyndon's theorem states that a sentence is preserved under surjective homomorphisms if and only if it is logically equivalent to a positive sentence.

nodes.name: Craig interpolation theorem
nodes.type_signature: φ ⊨ ψ ⟹ ∃θ in common language with φ⊨θ⊨ψ
nodes.description: The Craig interpolation theorem states that whenever one sentence implies another there is an interpolant in their common language implied by the first and implying the second.

nodes.name: Beth definability theorem
nodes.description: The Beth definability theorem states that a relation implicitly definable in a theory is explicitly definable by a formula in the remaining language.

nodes.name: Realizing and omitting types
nodes.type_signature: A realizes p if some ā satisfies all of p; omits p otherwise
nodes.description: A structure realizes a type when some tuple satisfies every formula in it and omits the type when no tuple does.

nodes.name: Countably saturated model
nodes.type_signature: realizes every type over every finite parameter set
nodes.description: A countably (ℵ₀-) saturated model is one realizing every complete type over each of its finite parameter subsets.

nodes.name: ℵ₀-categorical theory
nodes.type_signature: T has exactly one countable model up to isomorphism
nodes.description: A theory is ℵ₀-categorical when all of its countable models are isomorphic.

nodes.name: Oligomorphic permutation group
nodes.type_signature: finitely many orbits on A^n for each n
nodes.description: A permutation group is oligomorphic when it has only finitely many orbits on n-tuples for every natural number n.

nodes.name: Existentially closed structure
nodes.type_signature: every existential formula solvable in an extension is already solvable in A
nodes.description: A structure is existentially closed in a class when every existential formula with parameters that has a solution in some extension already has a solution in it.

nodes.name: Inductive theory
nodes.type_signature: models closed under unions of chains; axiomatized by ∀∃ sentences
nodes.description: A theory is inductive when the union of any chain of its models is again a model, equivalently when it is axiomatizable by universal-existential sentences.

nodes.name: Existence of existentially closed models
nodes.type_signature: every model of an inductive theory extends to an e.c. model
nodes.description: Every model of an inductive theory embeds into an existentially closed model of the same theory.

nodes.name: Model companion / model completion
nodes.type_signature: T* mutually model-consistent with T and model-complete
nodes.description: The model companion of a theory is a model-complete theory with the same universal consequences, and is a model completion when it additionally has amalgamation over models of the base.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of the model companion
nodes.type_signature: if a model companion exists it is unique and axiomatizes the e.c. models
nodes.description: A theory has at most one model companion, and when it exists it is exactly the theory of the existentially closed models.

nodes.name: Quantifier elimination
nodes.type_signature: every formula equivalent mod T to a quantifier-free formula
nodes.description: A theory has quantifier elimination when every formula is equivalent modulo the theory to a quantifier-free formula in the same free variables.

nodes.name: Model-complete with prime model implies QE
nodes.type_signature: T model-complete + prime model ⟹ T has quantifier elimination
nodes.description: A model-complete theory that has a model embeddable in every model (a prime model) admits quantifier elimination.

nodes.name: Nullstellensatz via model completeness
nodes.function_signature: (model completeness of ACF) → (Hilbert Nullstellensatz)
nodes.description: This technique derives Hilbert's Nullstellensatz from the model completeness of algebraically closed fields by transferring solvability up to an extension field.

nodes.name: Kaiser hull
nodes.type_signature: largest inductive theory with the same e.c. models as T
nodes.description: The Kaiser hull of a theory is the set of all ∀∃ sentences holding in every existentially closed model, i.e. the largest inductive theory with the same existentially closed models.

nodes.name: Stability via type-counting
nodes.type_signature: T is λ-stable if |S_n(A)| ≤ λ for all |A| ≤ λ
nodes.description: A theory is λ-stable when over every parameter set of size at most λ there are at most λ complete types.

nodes.name: Stable / superstable / ω-stable hierarchy
nodes.description: A theory is stable if it is λ-stable for some λ, superstable if λ-stable for all large λ, and ω-stable if ℵ₀-stable, forming a strict hierarchy.

nodes.name: Order property
nodes.description: A theory has the order property when some formula defines an infinite linear order on a sequence of tuples in some model.

nodes.name: Indiscernible sequence
nodes.type_signature: (a_i)_{i∈I}: tp(a_{i_1},...,a_{i_n}) depends only on the order of indices
nodes.description: An indiscernible sequence is an order-indexed family of tuples such that any two increasing tuples of the same length have the same type.

nodes.name: Set indiscernibles
nodes.type_signature: (a_i): tp of any n distinct elements is the same regardless of order
nodes.description: A set of indiscernibles is a family of elements such that every n-element subset realizes the same type irrespective of ordering.

nodes.name: Ramsey / Erdős–Rado theorem
nodes.type_signature: large enough sets admit monochromatic homogeneous subsets for finite colourings
nodes.description: The Ramsey and Erdős–Rado theorems guarantee that any finite colouring of the finite subsets of a sufficiently large set has an infinite homogeneous subset.

nodes.name: EM model / functor
nodes.type_signature: linear order I ↦ EM(I): model generated by indiscernibles indexed by I
nodes.description: The Ehrenfeucht–Mostowski functor sends a linear order to the model generated by an indiscernible sequence of that order type realizing a fixed EM-type.

nodes.name: EM construction technique
nodes.function_signature: (EM-type, linear order I) → (model with prescribed automorphisms/indiscernibles)
nodes.description: The Ehrenfeucht–Mostowski construction builds models with many automorphisms and few types by generating them from indiscernible sequences indexed by a chosen linear order.

nodes.name: Forking
nodes.type_signature: p(x) over B forks over A⊆B if it implies a disjunction of dividing formulas over A
nodes.description: Forking is a notion of dependence under which an extension of a type adds essential new information relative to a smaller parameter set.

nodes.name: Heir and coheir (non-forking extensions)
nodes.type_signature: heir/coheir: finitely-satisfiable / definable extensions of a type
nodes.description: An heir of a type is a coheir-dual extension that is finitely satisfiable in (resp. definable over) the original parameter set, giving canonical non-forking extensions.

nodes.name: Prime model over a set (t.t.)
nodes.type_signature: prime model of T containing A, existing for totally transcendental T
nodes.description: For a totally transcendental theory, the prime model over a parameter set is the least elementary extension containing that set, embedding elementarily into every other model containing it.

nodes.name: Partial computable function
nodes.description: A partial function on the naturals whose graph is the set of input-output pairs realized by some Turing machine (defined exactly where the machine halts).

nodes.name: Total computable function
nodes.description: A total function on the naturals computed by a Turing machine that halts on every input.

nodes.name: Primitive recursion schema
nodes.description: The function-building rule defining f(x,0)=g(x) and f(x,n+1)=h(x,n,f(x,n)), one of the closure operations generating the primitive recursive functions.

nodes.name: μ-operator (unbounded minimization)
nodes.description: The search operator producing g(x)=the least y with f(x,y)=0 (undefined if none exists), whose addition to the primitive recursive base yields exactly the partial recursive functions.

nodes.name: Partial recursive functions
nodes.description: The smallest class of partial functions containing the basic functions (zero, successor, projections) and closed under composition, primitive recursion, and the μ-operator.

nodes.name: Register machine
nodes.description: An abstract computing device with finitely many unbounded-integer registers manipulated by increment/decrement-and-jump instructions, an alternative model defining exactly the computable functions.

nodes.name: Church–Turing Thesis
nodes.description: The informal claim that every function effectively calculable by an algorithm is computable by a Turing machine (equivalently, is partial recursive).

nodes.name: Computability Thesis (Soare)
nodes.description: Soare's reformulation asserting that the intuitively computable functions coincide with the Turing-computable functions, motivating the terminology 'computable/c.e.' in place of 'recursive'.

nodes.name: Oracle Turing machine
nodes.description: A Turing machine equipped with a query tape that may consult an oracle set A for membership answers during its computation, the device underlying relative computability.

nodes.name: Use function
nodes.description: The function u(e,x,s) giving the largest oracle argument queried during the halting computation of Φ_e^A(x) (by stage s), bounding which oracle bits affect the output.

nodes.name: Gödel number / index
nodes.description: A natural number coding a Turing machine (or partial recursive program) under a fixed effective enumeration, so that e is an index for the e-th partial computable function φ_e.

nodes.name: Turing jump A′
nodes.description: The halting set relativized to oracle A, A′={e : Φ_e^A(e)↓}, the canonical operator strictly raising Turing degree.

nodes.name: Arithmetical hierarchy
nodes.description: The classification of subsets of ℕ by the number of alternating number quantifiers prefixing a computable matrix, with Σ0_n existential-leading, Π0_n universal-leading, and Δ0_n their intersection.

nodes.name: Many-one (m) reducibility
nodes.description: A≤_m B iff there is a total computable f with x∈A ⟺ f(x)∈B for all x.

nodes.name: One-one (1) reducibility
nodes.description: A≤_1 B iff there is a total computable injection f with x∈A ⟺ f(x)∈B for all x.

nodes.name: Truth-table (tt) reducibility
nodes.description: A≤_tt B iff there is a total computable procedure assigning to each x a finite Boolean truth-table condition on B-membership of finitely many points that decides x∈A (a total, hence everywhere-converging, Turing reduction).

nodes.name: Weak truth-table (wtt) reducibility
nodes.description: A≤_wtt B iff A≤_T B via an oracle reduction whose use is bounded by a computable function of the input.

nodes.name: Simple set
nodes.description: A c.e. set whose complement is infinite yet contains no infinite c.e. subset (Post's first weakening of completeness).

nodes.name: Immune set
nodes.description: An infinite set containing no infinite computably enumerable subset.

nodes.name: Productive set
nodes.description: A set A with a total computable productive function p such that whenever W_e⊆A then p(e)∈A∖W_e, witnessing that A is not c.e. in an effective way.

nodes.name: Creative set
nodes.description: A computably enumerable set whose complement is productive; equivalently a many-one complete c.e. set such as K.

nodes.name: Diagonal halting set K0
nodes.description: The set K0={⟨e,x⟩ : Φ_e(x)↓} of pairs encoding a machine and an input on which it halts, a c.e. many-one complete set.

nodes.name: Hypersimple set
nodes.description: A c.e. set whose complement is hyperimmune, i.e. its principal (enumeration-ordered) function is not dominated by any computable function.

nodes.name: Hyperimmune set
nodes.description: An infinite set whose principal function (listing its elements in increasing order) is not majorized by any computable function.

nodes.name: Hyperhypersimple set
nodes.description: A c.e. set whose complement cannot be covered by any uniformly computable array of finite sets meeting it in exactly one block each (strengthening hypersimplicity).

nodes.name: Maximal set
nodes.description: A c.e. set whose complement is infinite and cannot be split into two infinite pieces by any c.e. set, i.e. it is a coatom in the lattice of c.e. sets modulo finite difference.

nodes.name: Stage approximation Φ_{e,s}^A(x)
nodes.description: The s-step truncation of the oracle computation Φ_e^A(x), which converges iff the full computation halts within s stages, providing the computable approximations used in priority constructions.

nodes.name: Enumeration Theorem
nodes.description: There is a single partial computable function (universal function) that, given an index e and input x, simulates φ_e(x).

nodes.name: Kleene Normal Form Theorem
nodes.description: Every partial computable function can be written as U(μs.T(e,x,s)) for a fixed primitive recursive Kleene T-predicate and primitive recursive output U, using a single application of the μ-operator.

nodes.name: c.e. = Σ0_1 characterization
nodes.description: A set is computably enumerable iff it is the domain of a partial computable function iff it is the projection of a computable relation iff it is definable by a single existential number quantifier over a computable matrix.
aliases: Σ01 normal form for c.e. sets

nodes.name: Post's Complementation Theorem
nodes.type_signature: A computable ⟺ A and ℕ∖A both c.e.
nodes.description: A set is computable (decidable) if and only if both it and its complement are computably enumerable.
aliases: Post's theorem (computable iff c.e. and co-c.e.)

nodes.name: Recursion Theorem with parameters
nodes.description: A uniform (parametrized) version of Kleene's recursion theorem producing a computable function of the parameters that returns fixed-point indices uniformly.

nodes.name: Myhill Isomorphism Theorem
nodes.type_signature: A≤_1 B ∧ B≤_1 A ⟹ A≡ B (computable permutation)
nodes.description: Two sets that are one-one reducible to each other are computably isomorphic, i.e. there is a computable permutation of ℕ carrying one onto the other.

nodes.name: Myhill characterization of creative sets
nodes.description: The creative sets are exactly the many-one complete c.e. sets, and all are computably isomorphic to the halting set K.

nodes.name: m-completeness of K
nodes.description: Every computably enumerable set many-one reduces to the halting set K, so K is m-complete (indeed 1-complete) among c.e. sets.

nodes.name: Jump Theorem
nodes.type_signature: A<_T A′; A≤_T B ⟹ A′≤_m B′; A′ is Σ0_1(A)-complete
nodes.description: The Turing jump satisfies A<_T A′ strictly, is monotone (A≤_T B implies A′≤_m B′ hence A′≤_T B′), and A′ is c.e. in and complete for A.

nodes.name: Post's Theorem
nodes.description: Connects the arithmetical hierarchy to iterated jumps: a set is Σ0_{n+1} iff it is c.e. in the n-th jump 0^{(n)}, and Δ0_{n+1} comprises exactly the sets Turing-below 0^{(n)}.

nodes.name: Hierarchy Theorem (arithmetical hierarchy is proper)
nodes.description: For every n the arithmetical hierarchy is strict, with Σ0_n, Π0_n, and Δ0_n all distinct, witnessed by the n-th jump.

nodes.name: Shoenfield Limit Lemma
nodes.type_signature: A≤_T 0′ ⟺ A(x)=lim_s g(x,s) for computable g
nodes.description: A set (or function) is Turing reducible to 0′ if and only if it is the pointwise limit of a computable sequence of approximations; equivalently A is Δ0_2.

nodes.name: Modulus Lemma
nodes.type_signature: A≤_T ∅′ with c.e. approx ⟹ ∃ modulus m≤_T A
nodes.description: If A has a computable approximation converging to a Δ0_2 set, then any function dominating its modulus of convergence computes A; in particular every c.e. set has a modulus of its enumeration of the same Turing degree.

nodes.name: Existence of a simple set (Post)
nodes.description: Post constructed a computably enumerable set that is simple, hence c.e., noncomputable, and not many-one complete, advancing toward Post's problem.

nodes.name: Productive sets are not c.e.
nodes.description: A productive set cannot be computably enumerable, since its productive function effectively escapes every candidate enumeration W_e⊆A.

nodes.name: Relativization principle
nodes.type_signature: Theorem(∅) ⟹ Theorem(A) for all oracles A
nodes.description: The meta-principle that results proved about computable functions and c.e. sets remain valid uniformly when all notions are relativized to an arbitrary oracle A.

nodes.name: Dovetailing
nodes.function_signature: (countably many computations) → (single fair interleaved enumeration)
nodes.description: A scheduling method that runs infinitely many partial computations together by advancing each one finitely at successive stages, ensuring every computation that halts is eventually seen.

nodes.function_signature: (ℕ×ℕ) → ℕ
nodes.name: Pairing function / coding of tuples
nodes.description: A computable bijection ⟨·,·⟩:ℕ²→ℕ (e.g. Cantor's polynomial) with computable inverses, extended to code finite tuples and sequences as single numbers.

nodes.function_signature: (requirement list) → (set built by stages with movable markers)
nodes.name: Construction by stages with movable markers
nodes.description: A method that builds a c.e. set or function in stages, tracking the current candidate witness for each requirement by a marker that is moved (released) when its requirement is reinjured or refined.

nodes.name: Permitting method
nodes.function_signature: (c.e. set C, requirement) → (object ≤_T C built only when C permits)
nodes.description: A construction technique that makes a built set computable in a given c.e. set C by only acting on a requirement at a stage when C newly enumerates a small element ('permits' the change).

nodes.name: Reduction to K (proving undecidability)
nodes.function_signature: (problem P) → (m-reduction K≤_m P proving P undecidable)
nodes.description: A proof method establishing undecidability of a set P by exhibiting a computable many-one reduction from the halting set K (or another known undecidable set) to P.

nodes.name: Computable approximation (Δ0_2 method)
nodes.function_signature: (Δ0_2 object A) → (computable sequence A_s with lim_s A_s = A)
nodes.description: The technique of representing a Δ0_2 set or function as the limit of a computable stagewise approximation, the workhorse behind Limit-Lemma and injury constructions.

nodes.name: Turing equivalence (≡_T)
nodes.description: The equivalence relation A≡_T B holding when A≤_T B and B≤_T A, i.e. each set computes the other.

nodes.name: Turing degree
nodes.description: An equivalence class of subsets of ℕ under Turing equivalence, representing a level of relative computability.

nodes.name: Degree structure D
nodes.description: The upper semilattice of all Turing degrees partially ordered by relative computability, with least element 0, join operation, and the jump operator.

nodes.name: Join of degrees (a∨b)
nodes.description: The least upper bound of two Turing degrees, computed by the degree of the disjoint sum A⊕B={2x:x∈A}∪{2x+1:x∈B}.

nodes.name: Degree 0
nodes.description: The least Turing degree, consisting precisely of the computable (decidable) sets.

nodes.name: Degree 0′ (zero jump)
nodes.description: The Turing degree of the halting problem, the jump of 0 and the greatest c.e. degree.

nodes.name: Jump hierarchy (0,0′,0″,…)
nodes.description: The strictly increasing sequence of iterated jumps of 0, giving canonical representatives 0^{(n)} of degrees high in the arithmetical hierarchy.

nodes.name: c.e. degrees R
nodes.description: The substructure of Turing degrees containing a computably enumerable set, an upper semilattice with least element 0 and greatest element 0′.

nodes.name: Low set / degree
nodes.description: A set (or degree) whose jump is as low as possible, A′≡_T 0′, so it computes nothing extra at the jump level.

nodes.name: Low_n degree
nodes.description: A degree whose n-th jump equals 0^{(n)}, generalizing lowness to higher jumps.

nodes.name: High set / degree
nodes.description: A degree below 0′ whose jump is as high as possible, A′≡_T 0″, so it computes a function dominating all computable functions.

nodes.name: High_n degree
nodes.description: A degree below 0′ whose n-th jump is maximal, A^{(n)}≡_T 0^{(n+1)}.

nodes.name: High/Low hierarchy
nodes.description: The classification of c.e. (or Δ0_2) degrees by how their iterated jumps compare to the corresponding jumps of 0, forming nested Low_n and High_n classes.

nodes.name: Superlow degree
nodes.description: A degree whose jump is truth-table (not merely Turing) equivalent to 0′, a uniform strengthening of lowness.

nodes.name: Hyperimmune-free degree
nodes.type_signature: a≠0 with every f≤_T a dominated by a computable g
nodes.description: A nonzero degree every function of which is majorized by a computable function (equivalently, every f≤_T a is computably dominated).

nodes.name: Hyperimmune degree
nodes.type_signature: a computing a function dominating no computable g
nodes.description: A degree that computes a function not majorized by any computable function (i.e. computes a hyperimmune set's principal function).

nodes.name: GL1 degree (generalized low 1)
nodes.description: A degree satisfying the generalized lowness condition a′≡_T a∨0′, the relativized analogue of lowness not requiring a≤_T 0′.

nodes.name: GL2 degree (generalized low 2)
nodes.description: A degree satisfying a″≡_T (a∨0′)′; the complement GL2̄ (a not GL2) marks degrees of strong domination/escape properties.

nodes.name: Minimal degree
nodes.description: A nonzero Turing degree with no degree strictly between it and 0, an atom of the degree ordering.

nodes.name: 1-generic set / degree
nodes.type_signature: G meeting/avoiding every Σ0_1 set of conditions
nodes.description: A set G that is Cohen-generic for one-quantifier (Σ0_1) conditions: for each c.e. set of strings, G either meets it or has an initial segment with no extension in it.

nodes.name: n-generic set / degree
nodes.description: A set generic for arithmetical conditions of complexity Σ0_n, refining 1-genericity up the hierarchy.

nodes.name: Ershov hierarchy
nodes.description: The fine classification of Δ0_2 sets by the number (and ordinal type) of mind-changes allowed in a computable approximation, with the finite levels being the n-c.e. sets.

nodes.name: n-c.e. set
nodes.description: A set admitting a computable approximation A_s that changes its decision on each x at most n times (1-c.e. = c.e.).

nodes.name: d.c.e. set / degree
nodes.description: A difference of two computably enumerable sets (the 2-c.e. sets), and the degrees they realize.

nodes.name: e-state
nodes.type_signature: finite binary string over requirements R_0..R_{e}
nodes.description: In the maximal/dense-set constructions, the binary vector recording which of the first e c.e. sets a given element currently belongs to, maximized to push the construction toward a coatom complement.

nodes.name: Post's Problem
nodes.description: The question, solved affirmatively by Friedberg and Muchnik, of whether there exists a computably enumerable set whose Turing degree is strictly between 0 and 0′.

nodes.name: Kleene–Post Theorem
nodes.description: There exist Turing degrees a and b below 0′ that are incomparable, constructed by the finite extension method (though not necessarily c.e.).

nodes.name: Existence of incomparable c.e. degrees
nodes.description: There are computably enumerable sets of incomparable Turing degree, the content of the Friedberg–Muchnik solution to Post's problem realized within R.

nodes.name: Low Basis Theorem (Jockusch–Soare)
nodes.type_signature: every nonempty Π0_1 class has a low member
nodes.description: Every nonempty Π0_1 class (e.g. the paths of an infinite computable binary tree) contains a member of low Turing degree.

nodes.name: Hyperimmune-free Basis Theorem
nodes.type_signature: every nonempty Π0_1 class has a hyperimmune-free member
nodes.description: Every nonempty Π0_1 class contains a member of hyperimmune-free (computably dominated) degree.

nodes.name: Minimal Pair Theorem (Lachlan–Yates)
nodes.description: There exist nonzero computably enumerable degrees a and b whose only common lower bound is 0, a minimal pair in R.

nodes.name: Existence of a minimal degree (Spector)
nodes.description: Spector proved, by forcing with computable perfect trees, that minimal Turing degrees exist.

nodes.name: Exact Pair Theorem
nodes.type_signature: ideal I countable ⟹ ∃ a,b with I={c:c≤a ∧ c≤b}
nodes.description: Every countable ideal of Turing degrees has an exact pair: two degrees whose set of common lower bounds is exactly that ideal.

nodes.name: Embedding lattices into the c.e. degrees
nodes.description: Every finite (indeed countable) distributive lattice embeds, preserving join and meet, into the upper semilattice of computably enumerable degrees.

nodes.name: Nondistributivity of the c.e. degrees (Lachlan)
nodes.type_signature: R is not a distributive lattice
nodes.description: Lachlan showed the c.e. degrees fail distributivity by embedding the nonmodular/nondistributive five-element lattices, so R is not a distributive lattice.

nodes.name: Nondiamond Theorem (Lachlan)
nodes.type_signature: the four-element Boolean lattice does not embed into R preserving 0 and 1
nodes.description: Lachlan proved that the diamond lattice cannot be embedded into the c.e. degrees preserving both least and greatest elements (0 and 0′).

nodes.name: Robinson Low Splitting / interpolation
nodes.type_signature: low c.e. degrees split below any c.e. degree with interpolation
nodes.description: Robinson's theorem providing splitting of c.e. degrees by low c.e. degrees together with an interpolation/density property, refining Sacks splitting with lowness control.

nodes.name: Friedberg Jump Inversion Theorem
nodes.type_signature: ∀ c≥0′ ∃ a with a′≡_T a∨0′≡_T c
nodes.description: For every degree c≥0′ there is a degree a whose jump is c (and a∨0′=c), so the jump operator maps onto the cone above 0′.

nodes.name: Finite-injury priority method
nodes.function_signature: (priority-ranked requirement list) → (c.e. set/degree, each requirement injured finitely often)
nodes.description: A stagewise construction satisfying ranked requirements R_0,R_1,… in which lower-priority requirements may injure higher ones only finitely often, so each is eventually permanently satisfied.

nodes.name: Priority requirements and injury
nodes.function_signature: (competing requirements) → (priority ordering + injury bookkeeping)
nodes.description: The bookkeeping framework assigning a fixed priority order to requirements and declaring a requirement 'injured' when a higher-priority action undoes its current strategy, forcing it to restart.

nodes.name: Kleene–Post finite extension method
nodes.function_signature: (requirements) → (set built by finite initial-segment extensions, oracle 0′)
nodes.description: A forcing-style construction building characteristic functions by successive finite extensions, each diagonalizing one requirement, with the whole construction computable in 0′.

nodes.name: Length-of-agreement function
nodes.function_signature: (Φ_e^A, B, s) → ℓ(e,s)
nodes.description: The measure ℓ(e,s) of the longest initial segment on which a candidate reduction Φ_e^A agrees with target B at stage s, used to detect when a requirement appears satisfied.

nodes.name: Restraint function
nodes.function_signature: (requirement, stage) → ℕ
nodes.description: A function r(e,s) imposing a stagewise lower bound below which a strategy protects its computations, preventing lower-priority requirements from enumerating small elements that would injure it.

nodes.name: Hat trick
nodes.function_signature: (true-stage enumeration) → (corrected ('hatted') approximation Â_s)
nodes.description: A bookkeeping device in infinite-injury arguments that replaces A_s by the 'hatted' approximation reflecting only changes below the current restraint at true stages, taming nonmonotone injury.

nodes.name: Infinite-injury priority method
nodes.function_signature: (requirements possibly injured ∞ often along a tree) → (construction guided by the true path)
nodes.description: A priority construction in which requirements may be injured infinitely often, organized on a tree of strategies so that along the true path each requirement is met.

nodes.name: Tree of strategies
nodes.function_signature: (requirement guesses) → (tree of nodes, true path)
nodes.description: A tree whose nodes are strategy versions parametrized by finitely many guesses about the outcomes of higher-priority requirements, with the correct guesses lying on the true path.

nodes.name: True path
nodes.type_signature: infinite branch of the strategy tree
nodes.description: The leftmost path through the tree of strategies visited infinitely often, along which every requirement's correct guesses are realized.

nodes.name: Thickness Lemma
nodes.function_signature: (c.e. set A piecewise-thick over columns) → (B≤_T A built thick on required columns)
nodes.description: A lemma/technique in infinite-injury constructions guaranteeing a built c.e. set contains 'thick' (cofinite) portions of prescribed columns of a given set, used to control its degree.

nodes.name: Pinball machine
nodes.function_signature: (elements as balls + gates by priority) → (controlled enumeration into target)
nodes.description: A visualization/technique for 0‴ and density constructions in which elements ('balls') roll past priority-ordered 'gates' that hold or release them, regulating when they enter the constructed set.

nodes.name: 0‴-priority argument
nodes.function_signature: (requirements with two-level infinite injury) → (construction verified using 0‴)
nodes.description: A higher-level priority construction whose verification requires three jumps of bookkeeping (a tree-of-trees), e.g. in Lachlan's nondistributivity and density refinements.

nodes.name: Minimal pair construction
nodes.function_signature: (two c.e. sets A,B) → (common computations preserved so any C≤A,≤B is computable)
nodes.description: The technique of building two c.e. sets while preserving, for each potential common reduction, agreement that forces any set computable from both to be computable.

nodes.name: Spector's construction (tree forcing)
nodes.function_signature: (nested computable perfect trees) → (minimal-degree real on the intersection)
nodes.description: A forcing construction with a descending sequence of computable perfect (Spector) trees, each splitting or forcing total/partial behavior, yielding a real of minimal degree.

nodes.name: Cohen forcing in arithmetic
nodes.function_signature: (finite conditions / dense sets for arithmetic formulas) → (n-generic real)
nodes.description: The use of finite binary strings as Cohen forcing conditions to build generic reals deciding arithmetical statements, producing n-generic sets and degrees.

nodes.name: Induction principle on wffs
nodes.function_signature: Wff → Property

nodes.name: Truth table method
nodes.function_signature: Wff → BooleanFunction

nodes.name: Substitution of a term for a variable
nodes.function_signature: (Formula,Var,Term) → Formula

nodes.name: Generalization on constants
nodes.function_signature: Proof(c) → Proof(forall x)

nodes.name: Alphabetic variant (bound-variable renaming)
nodes.function_signature: Formula → AlphaEquivFormula

nodes.name: Reduction many-sorted to one-sorted
nodes.function_signature: ManySortedTheory → OneSortedTheory

nodes.name: Sentence symbol
nodes.description: Atomic propositional symbols A_n forming the alphabet of sentential logic.

nodes.name: Sentential well-formed formula
nodes.description: Strings built from sentence symbols and connectives by the formation rules.

nodes.name: Unique readability (sentential)
nodes.description: Every sentential wff has a unique parse tree / decomposition.

nodes.name: Truth assignment
nodes.description: A function assigning truth values to sentence symbols.

nodes.name: Extended truth assignment
nodes.description: Unique extension of a truth assignment to all wffs respecting connectives.

nodes.name: Tautology
nodes.description: A wff true under every truth assignment.

nodes.name: Tautological implication
nodes.description: Sigma tautologically implies tau iff every assignment satisfying Sigma satisfies tau.

nodes.name: Tautological equivalence
nodes.description: Two wffs with identical truth values under all assignments.

nodes.name: Functional completeness
nodes.description: Every boolean function is realized by a wff over a complete connective set.

nodes.name: Normal forms (DNF/CNF)
nodes.description: Every wff is equivalent to one in disjunctive and conjunctive normal form.

nodes.name: Compactness (sentential)
nodes.description: A set of wffs is satisfiable iff every finite subset is satisfiable.

nodes.name: Decidability of tautologies
nodes.description: There is an effective procedure deciding whether a wff is a tautology.

nodes.name: Switching circuits
nodes.description: Application of sentential logic to boolean/switching circuit design.

nodes.name: Variable assignment
nodes.description: Function assigning domain elements to first-order variables.

nodes.name: Logical implication and validity
nodes.description: Gamma logically implies phi iff every model of Gamma models phi; validity is implication from empty set.

nodes.name: Substitution lemma
nodes.description: Satisfaction of phi(x/t) relates to satisfaction of phi under modified assignment.

nodes.name: Homomorphism theorem
nodes.description: Homomorphisms preserve satisfaction of quantifier-free formulas; isomorphisms preserve all.

nodes.name: Logical axiom groups
nodes.description: The six groups of logical axioms (tautologies, quantifier, equality, etc.).

nodes.name: Deducibility relation
nodes.description: Gamma proves phi via logical axioms and modus ponens.

nodes.name: Generalization theorem
nodes.description: If Gamma proves phi and x not free in Gamma, then Gamma proves forall x phi.

nodes.name: Soundness theorem
nodes.description: Every deducible formula is logically implied (provability implies validity).

nodes.name: Consistency
nodes.description: A theory is consistent iff it does not prove a contradiction.

nodes.name: Lindenbaum lemma
nodes.description: Every consistent set extends to a maximal consistent set.

nodes.name: Enumerability of theorems
nodes.description: The set of theorems of an effectively axiomatized theory is recursively enumerable.

nodes.name: Prenex normal form
nodes.description: Every formula is equivalent to one with all quantifiers in front.

nodes.name: Skolem normal form
nodes.description: Equisatisfiable universal form obtained by introducing Skolem functions.

nodes.name: Herbrand normal form
nodes.description: Dual Skolemization yielding existential/Herbrand form.

nodes.name: Language of number theory
nodes.description: Language with 0, S, +, *, < for arithmetic.

nodes.name: Standard structure N
nodes.description: The standard model of arithmetic on the natural numbers.

nodes.name: Robinson arithmetic Q
nodes.description: Finitely axiomatized weak arithmetic Q.

nodes.name: Numeral
nodes.description: Term S...S0 representing a natural number.

nodes.name: Definable relation in N
nodes.description: A relation defined by a first-order formula over the standard model.

nodes.name: Representability theorem
nodes.description: Every recursive function/relation is representable in Q.

nodes.name: Godel beta function
nodes.description: Beta function coding finite sequences by arithmetic means.

nodes.name: Recursiveness of syntax
nodes.description: Syntactic relations (proof, substitution) are primitive recursive after arithmetization.

nodes.name: Fixed-point (diagonal) lemma
nodes.description: For each phi(x) there is a sentence sigma with proves sigma<->phi(#sigma).

nodes.name: Undecidability of arithmetic
nodes.description: True arithmetic / Q is undecidable.

nodes.name: Church's theorem
nodes.description: The set of valid first-order sentences is undecidable.

nodes.name: Essential undecidability
nodes.description: A theory all of whose consistent extensions are undecidable.

nodes.name: Decidable and undecidable theories
nodes.description: Classification of theories by decidability.

nodes.name: Hilbert-Bernays derivability conditions
nodes.description: The three derivability conditions on the provability predicate.

nodes.name: Godel second incompleteness theorem
nodes.description: No consistent effective theory extending Q proves its own consistency.

nodes.name: Incompleteness applications to set theory
nodes.description: Consequences of incompleteness for ZF/ZFC.

nodes.name: Second-order language
nodes.description: Language permitting quantification over relations and functions.

nodes.name: Standard (full) second-order semantics
nodes.description: Semantics where second-order variables range over the full power set.

nodes.name: Categoricity in second-order logic
nodes.description: Second-order axioms (e.g. PA2) are categorical.

nodes.name: Failure of compactness/completeness (SOL)
nodes.description: Full second-order logic lacks compactness and a complete proof system.

nodes.name: General (Henkin) structures
nodes.description: Second-order structures with restricted relation domains.

nodes.name: Completeness for general semantics
nodes.description: Second-order logic with Henkin semantics is complete.

nodes.name: Many-sorted logic
nodes.description: First-order logic with multiple sorts of variables.

nodes.name: Topological dynamical system (cascade)
nodes.description: A pair consisting of a compact metric space together with a continuous self-map (discrete time, a cascade) or continuous flow, generating orbits under iteration.

nodes.name: Topological transitivity
nodes.description: A system is topologically transitive if for every pair of nonempty open sets U,V there exists n with fⁿ(U)∩V≠∅, equivalently it has a dense orbit on a complete separable space.

nodes.name: Topological mixing
nodes.description: A system is topologically mixing if for every pair of nonempty open sets U,V there exists N such that fⁿ(U)∩V≠∅ for all n≥N.

nodes.name: Minimality (topological)
nodes.description: A topological system is minimal if every orbit is dense, equivalently the only closed invariant subsets are ∅ and X.

nodes.name: Nonwandering set Ω(f)
nodes.description: The set of points x such that every neighborhood U of x satisfies fⁿ(U)∩U≠∅ for some n>0, a closed invariant set containing all recurrent behavior.

nodes.name: Chain recurrent set / ε-chains
nodes.description: The set of points x admitting, for every ε>0, a periodic ε-pseudo-orbit (ε-chain) from x to itself, where each successive jump is within ε of the true image.

nodes.name: Birkhoff recurrence theorem
nodes.description: Every topological dynamical system on a nonempty compact metric space contains a nonempty minimal closed invariant subset, hence a recurrent (almost periodic) point.

nodes.name: Topological entropy via spanning/separated sets (Bowen–Dinaburg)
nodes.description: The exponential growth rate of the minimal cardinality of (n,ε)-spanning sets (equivalently maximal (n,ε)-separated sets) measuring orbit complexity at finite resolution.

nodes.name: Topological entropy via open covers (Adler–Konheim–McAndrew)
nodes.type_signature: h_top(f) = sup_U lim_n (1/n) log N(⋁_{i<n} f^{-i}U)
nodes.description: The supremum over open covers U of the exponential growth rate of the minimal cardinality of subcovers of the joined cover ⋁ f^{-i}U, the original definition of topological entropy.

nodes.name: Periodic orbit growth rate p_n(f)
nodes.description: The sequence counting the number of fixed points of fⁿ (periodic points of period dividing n), whose exponential growth rate bounds topological entropy from below.

nodes.name: Artin–Mazur zeta function
nodes.description: The formal power series generating function exponentiating the periodic-point counts p_n(f), encoding the dynamical periodic structure of f.

nodes.name: Rationality of the zeta function for subshifts of finite type
nodes.description: For a topological Markov chain with transition matrix A, the Artin–Mazur zeta function equals the reciprocal of det(I−zA), hence is rational.

nodes.name: Li–Yorke theorem (period three implies chaos)
nodes.description: A continuous interval map possessing a periodic point of period three has periodic points of every period and an uncountable scrambled set exhibiting Li–Yorke chaos.

nodes.name: Denjoy inequality
nodes.description: For a C² (or bounded-variation-derivative) circle diffeomorphism with irrational rotation number, the total variation of log of the derivative of fⁿ over a fundamental domain is uniformly bounded by V(log Df').

nodes.name: Denjoy counterexample
nodes.type_signature: (C¹ circle diffeo, irrational ρ, not minimal)
nodes.description: A C¹ (but not C²) circle diffeomorphism with irrational rotation number that is not topologically conjugate to a rotation, possessing a wandering interval and a Cantor minimal set.

nodes.name: Poincaré classification theorem for circle homeomorphisms
nodes.type_signature: ρ(f)∈ℚ ⟺ ∃ periodic orbit; ρ irrational, minimal ⇒ conjugate to R_ρ
nodes.description: An orientation-preserving circle homeomorphism has a periodic orbit iff its rotation number is rational, and if the rotation number is irrational and the map is minimal it is topologically conjugate to the rigid rotation by that number.

nodes.name: Rationality of rotation number iff periodic orbit
nodes.description: An orientation-preserving circle homeomorphism has rotation number p/q in lowest terms iff it has a periodic orbit of period q.

nodes.name: Morse–Smale system
nodes.type_signature: (f: M→M, Ω(f) finite hyperbolic, transverse W^s,W^u)
nodes.description: A diffeomorphism (or flow) whose nonwandering set consists of finitely many hyperbolic periodic orbits whose stable and unstable manifolds intersect transversally, the simplest structurally stable systems.

nodes.name: Expanding map of the circle E_m
nodes.description: The degree-m self-cover of the circle multiplying the angle by an integer m of absolute value at least 2, the canonical uniformly expanding example with topological entropy log|m|.

nodes.name: Doubling map
nodes.description: The angle-doubling self-map of the circle, a degree-two expanding map measure-preserving for Lebesgue and conjugate to the one-sided full 2-shift.

nodes.name: Linear toral automorphism (cat map)
nodes.description: The automorphism of the torus induced by an integer matrix A of determinant ±1, hyperbolic (Anosov) when A has no eigenvalue on the unit circle, the Arnold cat map being the SL(2,ℤ) case [[2,1],[1,1]].

nodes.name: Circle rotation R_α
nodes.description: Rigid rotation of the circle by angle α, which is minimal and uniquely ergodic iff α is irrational and periodic iff α is rational.

nodes.name: Full shift σ on Σ_N
nodes.description: The left-shift on the space of bi-infinite (or one-sided) sequences over an N-symbol alphabet, the universal model of symbolic dynamics with topological entropy log N.

nodes.name: Topological Markov chain / subshift of finite type Σ_A
nodes.description: The shift restricted to the closed invariant set of sequences whose successive symbol transitions are permitted by a 0–1 transition matrix A, the basic building block of hyperbolic symbolic dynamics.

nodes.name: Spectral decomposition for topological Markov chains
nodes.type_signature: Σ_A irreducible ⇒ disjoint cyclically permuted topologically mixing components
nodes.description: An irreducible topological Markov chain decomposes into finitely many disjoint closed sets cyclically permuted by σ on each of which a power of σ is topologically mixing.

nodes.name: Cylinder set (symbolic dynamics)
nodes.description: The set of sequences agreeing with a prescribed finite word on a fixed block of coordinates, the basic clopen sets generating the topology and Borel structure of a shift space.

nodes.name: Inclination lemma (λ-lemma)
nodes.type_signature: (p hyperbolic, D ⋔ W^s(p)) ⇒ fⁿ(D) → W^u(p) in C¹
nodes.description: If a disk D transversally intersects the stable manifold of a hyperbolic fixed point, its forward iterates accumulate in the C¹ topology on the unstable manifold of that point.

nodes.name: Anosov flow
nodes.description: A smooth flow whose tangent bundle splits continuously and invariantly into uniformly contracting stable, flow-direction, and uniformly expanding unstable subbundles.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic linear map
nodes.description: An invertible linear operator with no eigenvalue of modulus one, so that ℝⁿ splits into complementary contracting and expanding invariant subspaces.

nodes.name: Unstable subspace E^u
nodes.description: The maximal invariant subspace on which a hyperbolic linear map (or the differential of a hyperbolic system) is uniformly expanding, spanned by generalized eigenspaces for eigenvalues of modulus greater than one.

nodes.name: Local product structure
nodes.description: The property of a locally maximal hyperbolic set that nearby points x,y have a unique intersection of the local stable manifold of x with the local unstable manifold of y lying in the set, giving it a local product of stable and unstable coordinates.

nodes.name: Expansiveness
nodes.description: A homeomorphism is expansive if there is a constant c such that any two distinct points are eventually separated by more than c under forward or backward iteration.

nodes.name: Cone criterion (cone field) for hyperbolicity
nodes.function_signature: (invariant stable/unstable cone fields with expansion/contraction) → (uniform hyperbolicity of Λ)
nodes.description: A method establishing hyperbolicity of an invariant set by exhibiting continuous fields of stable and unstable cones that are mapped strictly inside themselves by Df⁻¹ and Df respectively with uniform expansion.

nodes.name: Adapted (Lyapunov) norm
nodes.function_signature: (hyperbolic splitting, ε>0) → (norm making contraction/expansion strict at first step)
nodes.description: A reparametrized Riemannian metric, equivalent to the original, in which the contraction on E^s and expansion on E^u of a hyperbolic system become immediate (one-step), eliminating the bounding constant C.

nodes.name: Graph transform method
nodes.function_signature: (Lipschitz section graph near hyperbolic set) → (contracted iterate converging to invariant manifold)
nodes.description: The Hadamard contraction-mapping argument that constructs stable and unstable manifolds as fixed points of the operator sending the graph of a Lipschitz function to the graph of its image under f.

nodes.name: Structural stability of expanding maps (Shub)
nodes.type_signature: (f expanding on M, g C¹-close) ⇒ g topologically conjugate to f
nodes.description: Every C¹ expanding endomorphism of a compact manifold is structurally stable and topologically conjugate to a fixed expanding linear model on an infranilmanifold (Shub's theorem).

nodes.name: Anosov structural stability theorem
nodes.type_signature: (f Anosov, g C¹-close) ⇒ ∃ homeomorphism h: h∘g=f∘h
nodes.description: Every Anosov diffeomorphism is structurally stable: any C¹-small perturbation is topologically conjugate to it via a homeomorphism close to the identity.

nodes.name: Hölder continuity of the hyperbolic splitting
nodes.description: For a hyperbolic set of a C¹⁺ᵅ diffeomorphism the stable and unstable subbundles depend Hölder-continuously on the base point, even when they fail to be C¹.

nodes.name: No-cycle condition
nodes.type_signature: no chain Ω_i → Ω_j → … → Ω_i among basic sets
nodes.description: The requirement that the basic sets in Smale's spectral decomposition admit no cyclic chain of heteroclinic connections, equivalently they can be totally ordered by the relation of stable/unstable intersection.

nodes.name: Ω-stability theorem
nodes.description: An Axiom A diffeomorphism satisfying the no-cycle condition is Ω-stable: any C¹-nearby diffeomorphism is topologically conjugate to it on its nonwandering set.

nodes.name: Strong transversality condition
nodes.description: The condition that all stable and unstable manifolds of an Axiom A system intersect transversally, characterizing (with Axiom A) C¹ structural stability via the Robbin–Robinson–Mañé theorem.

nodes.name: C¹ structural stability theorem (Robbin–Robinson–Mañé)
nodes.type_signature: C¹ structurally stable ⟺ Axiom A + strong transversality
nodes.description: A C¹ diffeomorphism is C¹ structurally stable if and only if it satisfies Axiom A together with the strong transversality condition.

nodes.name: Filtration (dynamical)
nodes.function_signature: (f: M→M) → (nested family M_1⊂…⊂M_k of f-trapping submanifolds isolating basic sets)
nodes.description: A nested sequence of compact submanifolds with boundary, each mapped into its own interior, used to isolate the chain components/basic sets of a system and order them.

nodes.name: Markov partition for hyperbolic sets
nodes.function_signature: (locally maximal hyperbolic set Λ) → (finite cover by rectangles with Markov boundary property)
nodes.description: A finite cover of a hyperbolic set by proper rectangles (products of stable and unstable pieces) whose boundaries map compatibly so that itineraries give a semiconjugacy to a subshift of finite type.

nodes.name: Existence of Markov partitions (Sinai–Bowen)
nodes.type_signature: (Λ locally maximal hyperbolic) ⇒ ∃ Markov partitions of arbitrarily small diameter
nodes.description: Every locally maximal hyperbolic set admits finite Markov partitions of arbitrarily small diameter, yielding a finite-to-one symbolic coding by a subshift of finite type (Sinai for Anosov, Bowen for Axiom A).

nodes.name: Smale solenoid attractor
nodes.description: The hyperbolic attractor obtained as the nested intersection of images of a solid torus under an embedding wrapping it twice (or k times) around longitudinally, locally a product of a Cantor set and an arc.

nodes.name: DA (derived from Anosov) attractor
nodes.type_signature: modify cat map at fixed point ⇒ hyperbolic attractor
nodes.description: A hyperbolic attractor produced by altering a toral Anosov automorphism near a fixed point so the fixed point becomes a repeller, yielding a non-invertible-on-its-basin attracting basic set.

nodes.name: Plykin attractor
nodes.type_signature: hyperbolic attractor in the plane/sphere with 1-dim unstable
nodes.description: A planar (or 2-sphere) hyperbolic attractor with one-dimensional unstable foliation locally homeomorphic to the product of a Cantor set and an interval, the lowest-dimensional orientable example.

nodes.name: Absolute continuity of stable/unstable foliations
nodes.type_signature: holonomy of W^s, W^u maps null sets to null sets
nodes.description: For a C¹⁺ᵅ (partially) hyperbolic system the stable and unstable foliations are absolutely continuous, i.e. their holonomy maps preserve sets of measure zero, the key analytic input to the Hopf ergodicity argument.

nodes.name: Hopf argument
nodes.function_signature: (absolutely continuous stable/unstable foliations + Birkhoff averages constant along leaves) → (ergodicity)
nodes.description: The method proving ergodicity of a volume-preserving hyperbolic system by showing Birkhoff averages are constant along stable and unstable leaves and using absolute continuity of these foliations to conclude they are a.e. constant.

nodes.name: Geodesic flow on negatively curved manifold is Anosov
nodes.type_signature: (M compact, sec(M)<0) ⇒ geodesic flow on T¹M is Anosov
nodes.description: The geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of a compact Riemannian manifold of negative sectional curvature is an Anosov flow, with stable/unstable bundles tangent to the horosphere foliations (Anosov's theorem).

nodes.name: Ergodicity of volume-preserving Anosov systems
nodes.description: A C¹⁺ᵅ Anosov diffeomorphism or flow preserving a smooth volume is ergodic, mixing, and in fact Bernoulli with respect to that volume.

nodes.name: Livšic theorem
nodes.type_signature: (f transitive Anosov, φ Hölder, Σ_{periodic} φ = 0) ⇒ φ = u∘f − u, u Hölder
nodes.description: For a transitive hyperbolic system, a Hölder cocycle that sums to zero over every periodic orbit is a Hölder coboundary, i.e. cohomologous to zero.

nodes.name: Cohomological equation / coboundary (dynamics)
nodes.description: The equation expressing an observable φ as the coboundary of a transfer (transformation) u under the dynamics f, central to questions of cohomology and equivalence of cocycles.

nodes.name: Rationality/meromorphy of the zeta function for Axiom A systems
nodes.description: For an Axiom A diffeomorphism the Artin–Mazur zeta function is rational (via Markov partitions), and the associated Ruelle dynamical zeta function for flows is meromorphic.

nodes.name: Smale's differentiable dynamics program
nodes.function_signature: (generic smooth system) → (hyperbolic theory: Axiom A, spectral decomposition, stability)
nodes.description: The overarching synthesis organizing hyperbolic dynamics around horseshoes, Axiom A, the spectral decomposition, structural and Ω-stability, and symbolic coding via Markov partitions.

nodes.name: Unique ergodicity
nodes.description: The property that a topological system admits exactly one invariant Borel probability measure, which is then automatically ergodic.

nodes.name: Unique ergodicity criterion
nodes.type_signature: (uniform convergence of (1/n)Σ φ∘fⁱ to a constant ∀φ∈C(X)) ⟺ unique ergodicity
nodes.description: A continuous system is uniquely ergodic if and only if for every continuous function the Birkhoff averages converge uniformly to a constant (equivalently to the integral against the unique invariant measure).

nodes.name: Koopman operator
nodes.function_signature: (measure-preserving f) → (unitary U_f φ = φ∘f on L²(μ))
nodes.description: The composition operator U_f φ = φ∘f induced on L²(μ) by a measure-preserving transformation, an isometry (unitary if invertible) translating dynamical properties into spectral properties.

nodes.name: Spectral characterization of weak and strong mixing
nodes.type_signature: weak mixing ⟺ Koopman operator has no nonconstant eigenfunctions; mixing ⟺ correlations →0
nodes.description: A measure-preserving system is weakly mixing iff its Koopman operator has continuous spectrum on the orthocomplement of constants (no nonconstant L² eigenfunctions), and strongly mixing iff all correlation coefficients tend to zero.

nodes.name: Discrete (pure point) spectrum
nodes.type_signature: L²(μ) = closed span of eigenfunctions of U_f
nodes.description: The property of a measure-preserving system that the eigenfunctions of its Koopman operator span L²(μ), characterizing systems measurably isomorphic to rotations on compact groups.

nodes.name: Halmos–von Neumann theorem
nodes.type_signature: discrete spectrum ⟺ conjugate to compact group rotation; isomorphism ⟺ same eigenvalue group
nodes.description: An ergodic system has discrete spectrum iff it is measurably isomorphic to an ergodic rotation on a compact abelian group, and two such systems are isomorphic iff their groups of eigenvalues coincide.

nodes.name: Rank-one system
nodes.description: A measure-preserving transformation built by a cutting-and-stacking construction from a single Rokhlin tower at each stage, the simplest class of ergodic systems and a rich source of generic examples.

nodes.name: Rigidity (measurable)
nodes.description: The property of a measure-preserving system that some sequence of iterates of its Koopman operator converges strongly to the identity, the opposite extreme from mixing.

nodes.name: Entropy of a partition H(ξ)
nodes.description: The Shannon entropy of a finite or countable measurable partition ξ, the average information gained by learning which atom of ξ a point lies in.

nodes.name: Conditional entropy of partitions H(ξ|η)
nodes.description: The average residual information in partition ξ given knowledge of partition η, the basic quantity from which Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy is built.

nodes.name: Metric (Kolmogorov–Sinai) entropy h_μ(f)
nodes.description: The supremum over finite partitions of the asymptotic per-step entropy of refinements under f, an isomorphism invariant measuring the exponential rate of information production of a measure-preserving system.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov–Sinai (Sinai) generator theorem
nodes.description: If a finite-entropy partition ξ generates the σ-algebra under f (its iterated refinements separate points mod 0), then the entropy of the system equals the entropy relative to that single partition.

nodes.name: Abramov formula
nodes.type_signature: h(special flow) = h(base map)/∫ roof dμ
nodes.description: The entropy of a suspension (special) flow equals the entropy of its base transformation divided by the integral of the roof (return-time) function, and analogously for induced maps.

nodes.name: Suspension (special) flow
nodes.type_signature: (base map T, roof r) ↦ flow on {(x,s): 0≤s≤r(x)}/(x,r(x))∼(Tx,0)
nodes.description: The flow obtained from a base transformation T and a positive roof function r by flowing upward at unit speed in the mapping torus and identifying the top of each fiber with the base point of its T-image.

nodes.name: K-system (Kolmogorov automorphism)
nodes.description: A measure-preserving transformation admitting an exhaustive and trivial-tail generating sub-σ-algebra, equivalently having completely positive entropy; K-systems are mixing of all orders.

nodes.name: Bernoulli automorphism
nodes.description: A measure-preserving system isomorphic to a two-sided Bernoulli shift on an independent identically distributed product space, the most random class of dynamical systems.

nodes.name: Measure of maximal entropy
nodes.description: An invariant probability measure whose metric entropy attains the topological entropy, the equilibrium state for the zero potential and unique for many hyperbolic and expansive systems.

nodes.name: Variational principle for topological pressure
nodes.description: The topological pressure of a continuous potential φ equals the supremum over invariant measures of metric entropy plus the integral of φ, generalizing the variational principle for entropy (φ=0).

nodes.name: Equilibrium state
nodes.description: An invariant measure realizing the supremum in the variational principle for the pressure of a potential φ, the dynamical analogue of a Gibbs state in statistical mechanics.

nodes.name: Gibbs measure (for a Hölder potential)
nodes.description: An invariant measure whose cylinder masses are comparable, up to a uniform constant, to exp(S_nφ − nP(φ)), the unique equilibrium state of a Hölder potential on a mixing hyperbolic system.

nodes.name: Measurable partition (Rokhlin theory)
nodes.function_signature: (Lebesgue space, measurable partition ξ) → (factor space, family of conditional measures on atoms)
nodes.description: Rokhlin's framework treating a partition into possibly uncountably many atoms as a measurable object dual to a sub-σ-algebra, equipped with a canonical system of conditional (disintegrated) measures on its atoms.

nodes.name: Conditional measures (disintegration)
nodes.function_signature: (measure μ, measurable partition ξ) → (family {μ_C} of measures on atoms with μ = ∫ μ_C dμ̄)
nodes.description: The canonical decomposition of a measure on a Lebesgue space into conditional probability measures supported on the atoms of a measurable partition, integrating back to the original measure.

nodes.name: Lebesgue space (Lebesgue probability space mod 0)
nodes.description: A probability space isomorphic mod null sets to an interval carrying Lebesgue measure together with at most countably many atoms.

nodes.name: Gauss measure
nodes.description: The probability measure dμ = (1/ln 2)·dx/(1+x) on [0,1) that is invariant under the Gauss (continued-fraction) map.

nodes.name: Induced (first-return) transformation T_A
nodes.description: For a measure-preserving T and a positive-measure set A, the map T_A(x)=T^{n_A(x)}(x) sending x to its first return to A, which preserves the normalized restriction of m to A.

nodes.name: First return-time function n_A
nodes.description: The function assigning to x∈A the least integer n≥1 with T^n x ∈ A, finite a.e. by Poincaré recurrence.

nodes.name: Kakutani–Rokhlin tower (skyscraper) construction
nodes.function_signature: (base map S on A, height/return function n) → (measure-preserving transformation T on the tower over A)
nodes.description: A method that builds a measure-preserving transformation by stacking iterates of a base map according to a return/height function over a base set.

nodes.name: Bernoulli shift
nodes.type_signature: (Π Y, B, Πp) → (Π Y, B, Πp)
nodes.description: The coordinate shift on a one- or two-sided product probability space equipped with the product measure of a fixed probability vector (p_0,…,p_{k-1}).

nodes.name: Markov shift
nodes.description: The coordinate shift on a sequence space whose measure is determined by a stochastic matrix P and a stationary probability vector p with pP=p.

nodes.name: Two-sided shift map σ
nodes.description: The coordinate-shift homeomorphism (σx)_n = x_{n+1} on a bi-infinite sequence space, preserving any shift-invariant measure.

nodes.name: Endomorphism/automorphism of a compact group (as m.p.t.)
nodes.description: A continuous surjective group homomorphism of a compact group, which preserves the normalized Haar measure.

nodes.name: Automorphism/endomorphism of the torus (matrix m.p.t.)
nodes.description: The map T(x)=Ax mod 1 on the n-torus induced by an integer matrix A, preserving Lebesgue measure (an automorphism when det A = ±1).

nodes.name: Isomorphism mod 0 (measure-theoretic isomorphism)
nodes.description: An invertible measure-preserving map between full-measure invariant subsets that conjugates two systems, the basic equivalence relation of ergodic theory.

nodes.name: Measure-algebra isomorphism (conjugacy of measure algebras)
nodes.description: A measure-preserving Boolean σ-algebra isomorphism between the measure algebras of two systems that intertwines the induced maps.

nodes.name: Spectral isomorphism (unitary equivalence of Koopman operators)
nodes.type_signature: W U_{T_1} = U_{T_2} W, W unitary
nodes.description: Existence of a unitary operator intertwining the Koopman operators of two systems, an equivalence strictly weaker than isomorphism mod 0.

nodes.name: Conjugacy implies spectral isomorphism
nodes.description: Measure-theoretically isomorphic systems have unitarily equivalent Koopman operators, while the converse fails.

nodes.name: Point spectrum (eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of U_T)
nodes.description: The set of λ for which the Koopman operator has a nonzero eigenfunction f with f∘T = λf a.e.

nodes.name: Eigenvalues of modulus one with constant-modulus eigenfunctions
nodes.description: For an ergodic transformation every eigenvalue has modulus one, eigenfunctions have constant modulus a.e., and the eigenvalues form a subgroup of the circle with eigenfunctions of distinct eigenvalues orthogonal.

nodes.name: Weak-mixing product characterization (T×T ergodic)
nodes.type_signature: T weak-mixing ⟺ T×T ergodic ⟺ T×T weak-mixing
nodes.description: A transformation is weak-mixing if and only if its Cartesian square is ergodic, equivalently the square is itself weak-mixing.

nodes.name: Weak-mixing ⇔ continuous spectrum (no nonconstant eigenfunctions)
nodes.type_signature: T weak-mixing ⟺ 1 is the only (simple) eigenvalue of U_T
nodes.description: A transformation is weak-mixing if and only if the constants are the only eigenfunctions of its Koopman operator, i.e. U_T has continuous spectrum on the orthocomplement of constants.

nodes.name: Weak-mixing equivalent to all powers ergodic
nodes.description: A transformation is weak-mixing if and only if every power Tⁿ is ergodic, and then every power is itself weak-mixing.

nodes.name: Koopman–von Neumann lemma
nodes.description: A bounded nonnegative sequence has Cesàro averages tending to zero if and only if it converges to zero along a subsequence of density one.

nodes.name: Ergodicity criterion for group rotations
nodes.type_signature: rotation by a on G ergodic ⟺ {aⁿ} dense
nodes.description: Rotation by an element a of a compact group G is ergodic with respect to Haar measure if and only if the cyclic subgroup generated by a is dense in G.

nodes.name: Ergodicity criterion for toral automorphisms
nodes.type_signature: A ergodic ⟺ no eigenvalue of A is a root of unity
nodes.description: A toral endomorphism given by integer matrix A is ergodic with respect to Lebesgue measure if and only if no eigenvalue of A is a root of unity.

nodes.name: Ergodicity and mixing of Bernoulli and Markov shifts
nodes.description: Bernoulli shifts are strong-mixing, and a Markov shift is ergodic if and only if its stochastic matrix is irreducible (mixing if aperiodic).

nodes.name: Fekete subadditive sequence lemma
nodes.type_signature: a_{m+n} ≤ a_m + a_n ⟹ lim a_n/n = inf a_n/n
nodes.description: For a subadditive real sequence the limit of a_n/n exists and equals the infimum of a_n/n.

nodes.name: Entropy of a transformation with respect to a partition h(T,ξ)
nodes.description: The asymptotic per-step entropy of the iterated joins of a partition under T, whose limit exists by subadditivity.

nodes.name: Measure-theoretic entropy of a transformation h(T)
nodes.description: The supremum of h(T,ξ) over all finite measurable partitions, an isomorphism invariant of the system.

nodes.name: Entropy behaviour under powers and inverses
nodes.description: Measure-theoretic entropy scales linearly under iteration and is invariant under inversion of an invertible transformation.

nodes.name: Generator (one-sided/two-sided)
nodes.description: A finite measurable partition whose iterated T-preimages (one-sided, or two-sided for invertible T) generate the full σ-algebra mod 0.

nodes.name: Join (refinement) of partitions ξ∨η
nodes.description: The common refinement of two partitions whose atoms are the nonempty intersections of an atom of each.

nodes.name: Basic entropy (in)equalities for partitions
nodes.description: Entropy of partitions satisfies the chain rule H(ξ∨η)=H(η)+H(ξ|η), subadditivity, monotonicity, and concavity in the partition.

nodes.name: Pinsker σ-algebra
nodes.description: The largest T-invariant sub-σ-algebra on which the transformation has zero entropy.

nodes.name: Space M(X) of Borel probability measures
nodes.description: The convex set of Borel probability measures on a compact metric space, compact and metrizable in the weak* topology.

nodes.name: Space M(X,T) of T-invariant probability measures
nodes.description: The nonempty compact convex subset of M(X) consisting of the T-invariant Borel probability measures of a continuous system.

nodes.name: Ergodic measures are the extreme points of M(X,T)
nodes.description: The ergodic invariant measures are exactly the extreme points of M(X,T), which is a Choquet simplex.

nodes.name: Bowen (dynamical) metric d_n
nodes.description: The metric measuring the maximal separation of two orbit segments over n iterates, used to define (n,ε)-separated and spanning sets.

nodes.name: L^p mean ergodic theorem
nodes.type_signature: f∈L^p ⟹ A_n f → f* in L^p
nodes.description: For 1≤p<∞ and f∈L^p, the Birkhoff averages converge in L^p norm to the conditional expectation onto the invariant σ-algebra.

nodes.name: Upper semicontinuity of the entropy map and existence of equilibrium states
nodes.type_signature: μ ↦ h_μ(T) u.s.c. ⟹ equilibrium states exist
nodes.description: When the map μ↦h_μ(T) is upper semicontinuous on M(X,T) (e.g. for expansive systems) the supremum in the variational principle is attained, so equilibrium states exist for every continuous potential.

nodes.name: Khinchin and Lévy constants for continued fractions
nodes.type_signature: a.e. x: (∏ a_i)^{1/n} → K, (1/n)log q_n → L
nodes.description: For Lebesgue-almost every x the geometric mean of the continued-fraction partial quotients converges to Khinchin's constant and the denominators grow at the Lévy constant rate, via Birkhoff applied to the ergodic Gauss map.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue group as complete invariant for discrete spectrum
nodes.type_signature: ergodic discrete-spectrum T_1 ≅ T_2 ⟺ equal eigenvalue groups
nodes.description: For ergodic transformations with discrete spectrum the subgroup of the circle formed by the eigenvalues is a complete invariant up to isomorphism.

nodes.name: Galilean space-time structure
nodes.type_signature: AffineSpace4D with time projection and Euclidean fibers
nodes.description: A four-dimensional affine space equipped with a surjective time map to ℝ and a Euclidean metric on each simultaneity fiber, providing the kinematic arena of classical mechanics.

nodes.name: Galilean group
nodes.type_signature: Group of affine automorphisms preserving Galilean structure
nodes.description: The group of all affine transformations of Galilean space-time preserving the time intervals and the spatial Euclidean distance between simultaneous events.

nodes.name: Galileo's principle of relativity
nodes.description: The laws of mechanics are invariant under the Galilean group, so no inertial frame is physically distinguished from another.

nodes.name: Newton's equation of motion
nodes.description: The second-order differential equation positing that the acceleration of a point mass is determined by a force function of position, velocity, and time.

nodes.name: Newton's principle of determinacy
nodes.description: The initial positions and velocities of all points of a mechanical system uniquely determine its entire future and past motion.

nodes.name: Galilean invariance constraints on forces
nodes.description: Requiring Newton's equations to be Galilean-invariant forces the interaction to depend only on relative positions and relative velocities of the particles and to be invariant under rotations and time translations.

nodes.name: Conservative (potential) force field
nodes.description: A force field that is the negative gradient of a scalar potential function, so that work done is path-independent.

nodes.name: Conservation of momentum
nodes.description: For a closed system the total linear momentum is conserved, following from the translational invariance of the Lagrangian.

nodes.name: Conservation of angular momentum
nodes.description: For a system invariant under rotations the total angular momentum about the center is conserved, following from rotational invariance of the Lagrangian.

nodes.name: Period of one-dimensional motion (energy integral)
nodes.description: The period of oscillation of a one-degree-of-freedom conservative system expressed as an integral over the classically allowed region between turning points.

nodes.name: Reduction of the two-body problem (reduced mass)
nodes.description: The two-body problem with central interaction separates into free motion of the center of mass and motion of a single particle of reduced mass μ in a central field.

nodes.name: Reduction of central motion via angular momentum
nodes.function_signature: (central force motion in ℝ³) → (one-dimensional radial motion)
nodes.description: Uses conservation of angular momentum to confine motion to a plane and eliminate the angular variable, reducing a central-field problem to a single radial degree of freedom.

nodes.name: Effective potential
nodes.description: The sum of the true potential and the centrifugal term M²/(2μr²) governing the equivalent one-dimensional radial motion in a central field.

nodes.name: Orbit equation of central motion (quadrature)
nodes.description: The closed-form expression of the orbit shape φ(r) for central motion obtained by integrating the radial and angular equations.

nodes.name: Kepler's problem
nodes.description: The central-field problem with an inverse-square attractive force, whose bounded orbits are conics with the center of force at a focus.

nodes.name: Laplace–Runge–Lenz vector
nodes.description: A conserved vector specific to the inverse-square central field, pointing along the major axis and encoding the orientation and eccentricity of the orbit.

nodes.name: Analysis of fall to the center
nodes.function_signature: (central potential, energy, angular momentum) → (collision vs. bounded vs. escape verdict)
nodes.description: Determines whether a particle in a central field spirals into the center in finite time by comparing the potential's singularity with the centrifugal barrier.

nodes.name: Generalized (canonical) momentum
nodes.description: The momentum conjugate to a generalized coordinate, defined as the partial derivative of the Lagrangian with respect to the corresponding velocity.

nodes.name: Cyclic coordinates and Routh reduction
nodes.description: When a coordinate is cyclic (absent from the Lagrangian) its conjugate momentum is conserved, and Routh's procedure eliminates it to obtain a reduced Lagrangian system in the remaining coordinates.

nodes.name: Holonomic constraint
nodes.description: A constraint expressible as equations relating only the coordinates (and possibly time), confining motion to a submanifold of configuration space.

nodes.name: D'Alembert–Lagrange principle
nodes.description: The principle that the total virtual work of the constraint forces vanishes for all virtual displacements compatible with the constraints, yielding the equations of constrained motion.

nodes.name: Lagrangian mechanics on a manifold
nodes.description: The formulation of Lagrangian dynamics for a system whose configuration space is a smooth manifold, with the Lagrangian a function on the tangent bundle and motions the critical curves of the action.

nodes.name: Legendre transformation (Lagrangian to Hamiltonian)
nodes.description: Passes from the Lagrangian on the tangent bundle to the Hamiltonian on the cotangent bundle by replacing velocities with conjugate momenta via fiberwise convex duality.

nodes.name: Small oscillations / linearization about equilibrium
nodes.function_signature: (Lagrangian, stable equilibrium) → (linear system of coupled oscillators)
nodes.description: Approximates motion near a stable equilibrium by expanding the kinetic and potential energies to quadratic order, yielding a linear system of coupled harmonic oscillators.

nodes.name: Normal modes and characteristic frequencies
nodes.description: Small oscillations of a system about stable equilibrium decompose into independent harmonic normal modes whose characteristic frequencies are the roots of the generalized eigenvalue equation det(K - ω²M)=0.

nodes.name: Simultaneous diagonalization of two quadratic forms
nodes.function_signature: (positive-definite form T, symmetric form U) → (basis diagonalizing both)
nodes.description: Finds a single linear change of coordinates that simultaneously diagonalizes a positive-definite quadratic form and another symmetric form, used to decouple the kinetic and potential energies.

nodes.name: Parametric resonance
nodes.description: A system whose parameters vary periodically in time can be destabilized, with the trivial equilibrium becoming unstable when the driving frequency is near twice a natural frequency divided by an integer.

nodes.name: Rigid-body configuration space SO(3)
nodes.description: The configuration space of a rigid body fixed at a point is the rotation group SO(3), and of a free rigid body the group of orientation-preserving Euclidean motions.

nodes.name: Inertia tensor
nodes.type_signature: I : ℝ³ → ℝ³ symmetric positive operator
nodes.description: The symmetric positive operator on the body frame relating angular velocity to angular momentum, encoding the mass distribution of a rigid body.

nodes.name: Principal axes of inertia
nodes.description: The orthogonal eigenframe of the inertia tensor, in which the inertia operator is diagonal with the principal moments of inertia as eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Angular velocity in body and space frames
nodes.description: The angular velocity vector of a rotating rigid body expressed in the rotating body frame and in the fixed space frame, related by the body's current rotation.

nodes.name: Euler's equations for a rigid body
nodes.description: The equations of motion of a rigid body in the body frame, equating the rate of change of angular momentum plus its gyroscopic term to the applied torque.

nodes.name: Euler angles
nodes.description: A triple of angles parametrizing the orientation of a rigid body as a composition of three successive rotations, giving local coordinates on SO(3).

nodes.name: Poinsot's construction (inertia ellipsoid)
nodes.description: The free rotation of a rigid body is described geometrically as the inertia ellipsoid rolling without slipping on a fixed plane perpendicular to the conserved angular momentum.

nodes.name: Lagrange top (heavy symmetric top)
nodes.description: A heavy symmetric rigid body fixed at a point on its symmetry axis, an integrable case whose motion combines precession, nutation, and spin.

nodes.name: Stability of rotation about principal axes
nodes.description: Steady rotation of a free rigid body about the axes of largest and smallest moment of inertia is stable, while rotation about the intermediate axis is unstable.

nodes.name: Poincaré–Cartan integral invariant
nodes.description: The 1-form p dq - H dt whose integral around any closed curve in extended phase space is preserved by the Hamiltonian flow, characterizing the canonical structure.

nodes.name: Relative and absolute integral invariants
nodes.description: An integral over a cycle is an absolute integral invariant of a flow if preserved over arbitrary cycles and relative if preserved only over boundaries, with the canonical 1-form and symplectic form furnishing the basic Hamiltonian examples.

nodes.name: Separation of variables in the Hamilton–Jacobi equation
nodes.function_signature: (separable Hamiltonian, coordinate choice) → (complete integral as sum of single-variable terms)
nodes.description: Seeks a complete integral of the Hamilton–Jacobi equation as a sum of functions each depending on one coordinate, reducing the PDE to decoupled quadratures and exhibiting the system as integrable.

nodes.name: Euler equations on a Lie algebra
nodes.description: The generalization of the rigid-body and ideal-fluid equations as the flow on the dual of a Lie algebra generated by a left-invariant quadratic energy via the coadjoint action.

nodes.name: Geodesics on Lie groups (hydrodynamics analogy)
